# Garuda-purana 1

## Chapter 1

## \|\| 1.1 \|\|

*oṃ ajamajaramanantaṃ jñānarūpaṃ mahāntaṃ śivamamalamanādiṃ bhūtadehādihīnam \|*  
*sakalakaraṇahīnaṃ sarvabhūtasthitaṃ taṃ harimamalamamāyaṃ sarvagaṃ vanda ekam \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. I Salute the One Supreme, without birth, decay or end, identical with knowledge, great, auspicious free from impurities, without beginning, devoid of elemental body and actions, stationed in all creatures, Hari, freed from impurity and illusion and present everywhere.

## \|\| 1.2 \|\|

*namasyāmi hariṃ rudraṃ brahmāṇaṃ ca gaṇādhipam \|*  
*devīṃ sarasvatīṃ caiva manovākkarmabhiḥ sadā \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. With mind, speech and actions I do always salute Hari, Rudra, Brahma, the lord of Ganas and the goddess Sarasvati.

## \|\| 1.3-4 \|\|

*sūtaṃ paurāṇikaṃ śāntaṃ sarvaśāstraviśāradam \|*  
*viṣṇubhaktaṃ mahātmānaṃ naimiśāraṇyamāgatam \|\| 3 \|\|*

*tīrthayātrāprasaṅgena upaviṣṭaṃ śubhāsane \|*  
*dhyāyantaṃ viṣṇumanaghaṃ tamabhyarcyāstuvankavim \|\| 4 \|\|*

3-4. Having adored and lauded the poet Suta, well-versed in Puranas, of a quiet nature, the master of all scriptures, devoted to Visnu and high-souled when he came to the forest of Naimisa while making a pilgrimage to sacred shrines and seated on a holy seat was meditating on the sinless Visnu.

## \|\| 1.5 \|\|

*śaunakādyā mahābhāgā naimiṣīyāstapodhanāḥ \|*  
*munayo ravisaṅkāśāḥ śāntā yajña parāyaṇāḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. The great Rsis, баипака and others, dwelling in the forest of Naimisi, having asceticism for their wealth, of quescent souls, effulgent like the sun and ever engaged in the celebration of sacrifices, said.

## \|\| 1.6 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*sūta ! jānāsi sarvaṃ tvaṃ pṛcchāmastvāmato vayam \|*  
*devatānāṃ hi ko deva īśvaraḥ pūjya eva kaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. The Rsis said — О Suta, thou art informed of every thing and therefore we ask you — "Amongst the celestials who is Isvara and who is worthy of adorations? Who should be meditated on?

## \|\| 1.7-8 \|\|

*ko dhyeyaḥ ko jagatsraṣṭā jagatpātti ca hanti kaḥ \|*  
*kasmātpravartate dharmo duṣṭahantā ca kaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*tasya devasya kiṃ rūpaṃ jagatsargaḥ kathaṃ mataḥ \|*  
*kairvrataiḥ sa tu tuṣṭaḥ syātkena yogena vāpyate \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. Who is the creator of tlie universe? Who protects it and who destroys it? From whom proceeds religion? Who suppresses the wicked? With what vowed observances is he pleased? By what yoga can he be obtained?

## \|\| 1.9 \|\|

*avatārāśca ke tasya kathaṃ vaṃśādisambhavaḥ \|*  
*varṇāśramādidharmāṇāṃ kaḥ pātā kaḥ pravartakaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. What are his incarnations and what is his family? Who has instituted the various castes and orders and who protects them?

## \|\| 1.10 \|\|

*etatsarvaṃ tathānyacca brūhi sūta ! mahāmate ! \|*  
*nārāyaṇakathāḥ sarvāḥ kathayāsmākamuttamāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. О Suta, О thou of great intellect, do thou describe unto us, all this and every thing else, the most excellent themes about Narayana.,

## \|\| 1.11 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*purāṇaṃ gāruḍaṃ vakṣye sāraṃ viṣṇukathā śrayam \|*  
*garuḍoktaṃ kaśyapāya purā vyāsācchrutaṃ mayā \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Suta said — I will describe the Garuda Purana, the essence of all accounts relating to Visnu. Formerly Garuda described it to Kasyapa and I myself had heard it from Vyasa.

## \|\| 1.12 \|\|

*eko nārāyaṇo devo devānāmīśvareśvaraḥ \|*  
*paramātmā paraṃ brahma janmādyasya yato bhavet \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. The Lord Narayana alone is the lord of all the lords of the deities, the great soul and the great Brahma; from him proceeds birth etc,

## \|\| 1.13 \|\|

*jagato rakṣaṇārthāya vāsudevo 'jaro 'maraḥ \|*  
*sa kumārādirūpeṇa avatārānkarotyajaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. For the protection of the universe Vasudeva, without birth and death, assumes various incarnations by his body, namely that of Koumara and others.

## \|\| 1.14 \|\|

*hariḥ sa prathamaṃ devaḥ kaumāraṃ sargamāsthitaḥ \|*  
*cacāra duścaraṃ brahman brahmacaryamakhaṇḍitam \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Having undertaken the inarnation of Koumara and lived in the celestial region the first deity Hari, out any break.

## \|\| 1.15 \|\|

*dvitīyaṃ tu bhavāyāsya rasātalagatāṃ mahīm \|*  
*uddhariṣyannupādatte yajñeśaḥ saukaraṃ vapuḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Secondly having assumed the Boar-form the lord of sacrifices, for the general well-being, released and held up the earth sunk deep under the nether region.

## \|\| 1.16 \|\|

*tṛtīyamṛṣisargaṃ tu devarṣitvamupetya saḥ \|*  
*tantraṃ sātvatamācaṣṭe naiṣkarmyaṃ karmaṇāṃ yataḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Thirdly for the creation of the Rsis, he, assuming the form of a Brahma Rsis, performed Sattvik (pervaded by the quality of goodness) actions from Which alone proceed desireless actions.

## \|\| 1.17 \|\|

*naranārāyaṇo bhūtvā turye tepe tapo hariḥ \|*  
*dharmasaṃ rakṣaṇārthāya pūjitaḥ sa surāsuraiḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Then for protecting righteousness, Hari, assuming the form of Nara-Narayana, practised hard penances. He was then adored by the celestials and Asuras.

## \|\| 1.18 \|\|

*pañcamaḥ kapilo nāma siddheśaḥ kālaviplutam \|*  
*provāca sūraye sāṅkhyaṃ tattvagrāmavi nirṇayam \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. His fifth incarnation was Kapila, the lord of Siddhas1 who expoimded unto the celestials the Sankhya2, which ascertains the Tattvas or elementary particles which had been lost in time.

## \|\| 1.19 \|\|

*ṣaṣṭhamatrerapatyatvaṃ dattaḥ prāpto 'nasūyayā \|*  
*ānvīkṣikīmalarkāya prahlādādibhya ūcivān \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. In his sixth incarnation he was born as the son of Atri and communicated, to Alarka, Purahlada and o!hers, the knowledge of Anvsiki (metaphysics) obtained by him from Anasuya.

## \|\| 1.20 \|\|

*tataḥ sapta ākūtyāṃ ruceryajño 'bhyajāyata \|*  
*sutrāmādyaiḥ suragaṇairyaṣṭvā svāyambhuvāntare \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. His seventh incarnation, in the Svayambhuva Manvantara, was Yajna, the will- begotten child of Akuti, who performed sacrifices in the company of the celestials.

## \|\| 1.21 \|\|

*aṣṭame merudevyāṃ tu nābherjāta urukramaḥ \|*  
*darśayanvartma nārīṇāṃ sarvāśramanamaskṛtam \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. In his eighth incarnation be was born as the powerful son of Nabhi from Merudevya. Adored of all the orders he pointed out to men the real road.

## \|\| 1.22 \|\|

*ṛṣibhiryācito bheje navamaṃ pārthivaṃ vapuḥ \|*  
*dugdhairmahauṣadhairviprāstena saṃjīvitāḥ prajāḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Solicited by Rsis he assumed the body of Prthu as his ninth incarnation and the Brahmanas and other creatures were revived by him with the milk of herbs.

## \|\| 1.23 \|\|

*rūpaṃ sa jagṛhe mātsyaṃ cākṣuṣāntarasaṃplave \|*  
*nāvyāropya mahīmayyāmapādvaivasvataṃ manum \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. When the Earth was submerged under water in the end of the Caksusa Manvantara he assumed the form of a Fish and saved the Manu Vaivasvata by placing him on a boat.

## \|\| 1.24 \|\|

*surāsurāṇāmudadhiṃ mathnatāṃ mandarācalam \|*  
*dadhre kamaṭharūpeṇa pṛṣṭha ekādaśe vibhuḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. In his eleventh incarnation the Lord, in the shape of a tortoise, held on his back the mount Mandara with which the celestials and Asuras churned the ocean.

## \|\| 1.25 \|\|

*dhānvantaraṃ dvādaśamaṃ trayodaśamameva ca \|*  
*āpyāyatsurānanyānmohinyā mohayaṃstriyā \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. In his twelfth increantion as well as in the thirteenth in the form of a woman he stupified the Asuras and pleased the celestials.

## \|\| 1.26 \|\|

*caturdaśaṃ nārasiṃhaṃ caitya (vaira) daityendramūrjitam \|*  
*dadāra karajairugrairerakāṃ kaṭakudyathā \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Assuming the form of a man-lion in his fourteenth incarnation he subdued the Daitya chief by sutting his entrails with the fierce claws.

## \|\| 1.27 \|\|

*pañcadaśaṃ vāmanako bhūtvāgādadhvaraṃ baleḥ \|*  
*pāda trayaṃ yācamānaḥ pratyāditsustriviṣṭapam \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Assuming the form of a dwarf in his fifteenth incarnation he went to the Sacrifice of Bali and praying for room for his three feet obtained it.

## \|\| 1.28 \|\|

*avatāre ṣoḍaśame paśyanbrahmadruho nṛpān \|*  
*triḥ saptakṛtvaḥ kupito niḥ kṣattrāmakaronmahīm \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Beholding the kings aggrandise the Brahmanas in his sixteenth incarnation, he, filled with anger, divested the earth of the Ksatriyas for twenty one times.

## \|\| 1.29 \|\|

*tataḥ saptadaśe jātaḥ satyavatyāṃ parāśarāt \|*  
*cakre vedataroḥ śākhāṃ dṛṣṭvā puṃso 'lpamedhasaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. In his seventeenth incarnation he was begotton on Satyavatl by Parasara (as Veda- Vyasa); and seeing the feeble intellect of the people he divided the Vedas.

## \|\| 1.30 \|\|

*naradevatvamāpannaḥ surakāryacikīrṣayā \|*  
*samudranigrahādīni cakre kāryāṇyataḥ param \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Then for accomplishing the work of the celestials he was born as a king (Rama), built a bridge over the ocean and performed other feats.

## \|\| 1.31 \|\|

*ekonaviṃśe viṃśatime vṛṣṇiṣu prāpya janmanī \|*  
*rāmakṛṣṇāviti bhuvo bhagavānaharadbharam \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. In his nineteenth and twentieth incarnations the Lord was born as Rama and Krsna and relieved the earth of her burden.

## \|\| 1.32 \|\|

*tataḥ kalestu sandhyānte saṃmohāya suradviṣām \|*  
*buddho nāmrā jinasutaḥ kīkaṭeṣu bhaviṣyati \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Then at the junction of the Kali Yuga, for stupefying the enemies of the celestials he was born as Buddha, the son of Jina.

## \|\| 1.33 \|\|

*atha so 'ṣṭamasandhyāyāṃ naṣṭaprāyeṣu rāñjasu \|*  
*bhavitā viṣṇuyaśaso nāmnā kalkī jagatpatiḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. In the period of the eighth junction (change of cycles), when all the kings will be on the verge of destruction (change of cycles), when all the kings will be on the verge of destruction, he will be born as Visnujasa's son Kalki, the lord of the world.

## \|\| 1.34 \|\|

*avatārā hyasaṃkhyeyā hareḥ sattvanidherdvijāḥ \|*  
*manuvedavido hyādyāḥ sarve viṣṇukalāḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Innumerable are the incarnation of Hari, the mine of Sattva, О twice-born ones. The prime Manus, the knowers of the Vedas, are all said to have originated from Visnu.

## \|\| 1.35 \|\|

*tasmātsargādayo jātāḥ saṃpūjyāśca vratādinā \|*  
*purāṇaṃ gāruḍaṃ vyāsaḥ purāsau me 'bravīdidam \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. From them proceeded the work of creation. And they should be adored with vowed observances and other rites. This Garuda Purana consisting of right thousand and eight hundred verses Vyasa formerly narrated to me.

## Chapter 2

## \|\| 2.1 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ \|*  
*kathaṃ vyāsena kathitaṃ purāṇaṃ gāruḍaṃ tava \|*  
*etatsarvaṃ samākhyāhi paraṃ viṣṇukathāśrayam \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. The Rsis said — Why did Vyasa describe to you the Garuda Purana? Do thou describe thus the. most excellent theme relating to Visnu

## \|\| 2.2-4 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*ahaṃ hi munibhiḥ sārdhaṃ gato badarikāśramam \|*  
*tatra dṛṣṭo mayā vyāso dhyāyamānaḥ pareśvaram \|\| 2 \|\|*

*taṃ praṇamyopaviṣṭo 'haṃ pṛṣṭavānhi munīśvaram \|*  
*sūta uvāca \|*  
*vyāsa brūhi hare rūpaṃ jagatsargādikaṃ tataḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*manye dhyāyasi taṃ yasmāttasmājjānāsi taṃ vibhum \|*  
*evaṃ pṛṣṭo yathā prāha tathā viprā?nibodhata \|\| 4 \|\|*

2-4. The Suta said — In the company of the ascetics I had gone to the hermitage of Badarika. There I saw Vyasa meditating on the great Isvara. Having bowed unto him I took my seat and accosted that foremost of ascetics saying — "О Vyasa, relate unto me the form of Hari from which has emanated the creation of the universe. Methinks, while thou dost meditate on the Lord' thou must be knowing it." Hear, О Vipras, what he did relate on being thus accosted by me.

## \|\| 2.5 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca \|*  
*śṛṇu sūta ! pravakṣyāmi purāṇaṃ gāruḍaṃ tava \|*  
*saha nāradadakṣādyairbrahmā māmuktavānyathā \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Vyasa said — Hear, О Suta, I will recount the Purana Garuda which Brahma described to me in the company of Narada, Daksa and others.

## \|\| 2.6 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*dakṣanāradamukhyaistu yuktaṃ tvāṃ kathamuktavān \|*  
*brahmā śrīgāruḍaṃ puṇyaṃ purāṇaṃ sāravācakam \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. The Suta said — How did Brahma relate the sacred Purana Garuda, describing the true essence, unto thee when united with Dak§a, Narada and other.

## \|\| 2.7 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca \|*  
*ahaṃ hi nārado dakṣo bhṛgvādyāḥ praṇipatya tam \|*  
*sāraṃ brūhīti papracchurbrahmāṇaṃ brahmalokagam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Vyasa said — Having saluted Brahma who was residing in the Brahmaloka, myself, Daksa, Narada, Bhrgu and others said to him. "Describe unto us the quintessence (of the sacred lore)."

## \|\| 2.8 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*purāṇaṃ gāruḍaṃ sāraṃ rudraṃ ca māṃ yathā \|*  
*suraiḥ sahābravīdviṣṇustathāhaṃ vyāsa vacmite \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Brahma said — О Vyasa, I will recount to you, the Garu4a Purana, the cream of sacred learning which Visnu described to me and Rudra formerly while in the company of other celestials.

## \|\| 2.9 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca \|*  
*kathaṃ rudraṃ suraiḥ sārdhamabravīdvai hariḥ purā \|*  
*purāṇaṃ gāruḍaṃ sāraṃ brūhi brahmanmahārthakam \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Vyasa said: — О Brahman, describe to me the Garuda Purana, pregnant with great significance, the essence of all, which Hari formerly described to Rudra while in the company of other celestials.

## \|\| 2.10 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ahaṃ gato 'driṃ kailāsamindrādyairdaivataiḥ saha \|*  
*tatra dṛṣṭo mayā rudro dhyāyamānaḥ paraṃ padam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Brahma said: — With Indra and other celestials I had gone to the mount Kailasa. There I was Rudra engaged in the meditation of the great station.

## \|\| 2.11-13 \|\|

*pṛṣṭo namaskṛtaḥ kiṃ tvaṃ devaṃ dhyāyasi śaṅkara? \|*  
*tvatto nānyaṃ paraṃ devaṃ jānāmi brūhi māṃ tataḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*sārātsārataraṃ tattvaṃ śrotukāmaḥ suraiḥ saha \|*  
*rudrauvāca \|*  
*ahaṃ dhyāyāmi taṃ viṣṇuṃ paramātmānamīśvaram \|\| 12 \|\|*

*sarvadaṃ sarvagaṃ sarvaṃ sarvaprāṇihṛdisthitam \|*  
*bhasmoddhūlitadehastu jaṭāmaṇḍalamaṇḍitaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

11-13. Having saluted him I addressed him, saying — "O Sankara, on what art thou meditating? Save thee, I do not know of a greater deity. Do thou therefore describe unto me \[the subject of thy meditation\] the quintessence \[of the sacred learning\] who, along with the celestials, am anxious to listen to it. " Rudra said: — I meditate on Visnu, the great soul, the Demiurgus, who gives all, who is present everywhere and who resides in the hearts of all creatures.

## \|\| 2.14 \|\|

*viṣṇorārādhanārthaṃ me vratacaryā pitāmaha \|*  
*tameva gatvā pṛcchāmaḥ sāraṃ yaṃ cintayāmyaham \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. О grand-father, my body is besmeared with ashes and my hairs have been clotted. All my vowed observances are intended for the adoration of Visnu. I will describe him unto you, the essence of all, on whom I meditate.

## \|\| 2.15-16 \|\|

*viṣṇuṃ jiṣṇuṃ padmanābhaṃ hariṃ dehavivarjitam \|*  
*śuciṃ śuciṣadaṃ haṃsaṃ tatpadaṃ parameśvaram \|\| 15 \|\|*

*yuktā sarvātmanātmānaṃ taṃ devaṃ cintayāmyaham \|*  
*yasminviśvāni bhūtāni tiṣṭhanti ca viśanti ca \|\| 16 \|\|*

15-16. I meditate on the deity Hari, Visnu, Jisnu, who is lotus-naveiled and shorn of a body; who is purity, the source of purity; who is the impersonal self and the individual soul; who is the great lShvara and unites all souls with himself. In him exist all the world and elements and into him they enter.

## \|\| 2.17 \|\|

*guṇabhūtāni bhūteśe sūtre maṇigaṇā iva \|*  
*sahasrākṣaṃ sahasrāṅghriṃ sahasroruṃ varānanam \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. All the gums (qualities) and elements exist, in that lord of elements as pearls are strung by a thread. He has a thousand eyes, a thousand heads, a thousand thighs and a most beautiful face.

## \|\| 2.18 \|\|

*aṇīyasāmaṇīyāṃsaṃ sthaviṣṭhaṃ ca sthavīyasām \|*  
*garīyasāṃ gariṣṭhaṃ ca śreṣṭhaṃ ca śreyasāmapi \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. He is the minutest of the minute, the firmest, of the firm, the heaviest of the heavy and the best of all that is good.

## \|\| 2.19 \|\|

*yaṃ vākyeṣvanuvākyeṣu niṣatsūpaniṣatsu ca \|*  
*gṛṇanti satyakarmāṇaṃ satyaṃ satyeṣu sāmasu \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. In the words, letters, principal and minor sacred lores and in the true Saman he is lauded as truth and the author of true deeds.

## \|\| 2.20 \|\|

*purāṇa puruṣaḥ prokto brahmā prokto dvijātiṣu \|*  
*kṣaye saṅkarṣaṇaḥ proktastamupāsyamupāsmahe \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. He is called the ancient Purusa and Brahma amongst the twice-born. He is called Sankarsana in destruction.

## \|\| 2.21 \|\|

*yasmiṃllokāḥ sphurantīme jale śakunayo yathā \|*  
*ṛtamekākṣaraṃ brahma yattatsadasataḥ param \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. I therefore adore him in whom all these worlds shine us the Shakuna fishes in the water. He is the divine law, the word (Om), Brahma, the that, the existent and non-existent and the supreme.

## \|\| 2.22-23 \|\|

*arcayanti ca yaṃ devā yakṣarākṣasapannagāḥ \|*  
*yasyāgnirāsyaṃ dyaurmūrdhā khaṃ nābhiścaraṇau kṣitiḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*candrādityau ca nayane taṃ devaṃ cintayāmyaham \|*  
*yasya trilokī jaṭhare masya kāṣṭhāśca bāhavaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

22-23. The celestials, the Yaksas, the Raksasas and the Pannagas adore him. Fire is his mouth, the heaven is his head, the sky is his navel and the earth is his feet and the sun and moon are his two eyes. I meditate on him.

## \|\| 2.24-27 \|\|

*yasyocchvāsaśca pavanaḥ taṃ devaṃ cintayāmyaham \|*  
*yasya keśeṣu jīmūtā nadyaḥ sarvāṅgasandhiṣu \|\| 24 \|\|*

*kukṣau samudrāścatvārastaṃ devaṃ cintayāmyaham \|*  
*paraḥ kālātparo yajñātparaḥ sadasataścayaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*anādirādi rviśvasya taṃ devaṃ cintayāmyaham \|*  
*manasaścandramā yasya cakṣuṣośca divākaraḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*mukhādagniśca saṃjajñe taṃ devaṃ cintayāmyaham \|*  
*padybhāṃ yasya kṣitirjātā śrotrābhyāṃ ca tathā diśaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

24-27. I meditate on that deity whose breaths are the wind, in whose belly the three worlds exist and whose anus are the hairs are the clouds, and in the joints of whose body are the four oceans. I meditate on that deity who is above time, who is above sacrifices, who is above the existent and non-existent and who is the beginning and end of the universe. I meditate on that deity from who mind emanates the moon, from whose eyes the sun and from whose mouth the fire.

## \|\| 2.28-29 \|\|

*mūrdhabhāgāddivaṃ yasya taṃ devaṃ cintayāmyaham \|*  
*sargaśca pratisargaśca vaṃśo manvantarāṇi ca \|\| 28 \|\|*

*vaṃśānucaritaṃ yasmāttaṃ devaṃ cintayāmyaham \|*  
*yaṃ dhyāyāmyahametasmādūjāmaḥ sāramīkṣitum \|\| 29 \|\|*

28-29. I meditate on that deity from whose feet the earth is produced, from whose ears the directions and from whose head the Div. (celestial region). I meditate on that deity from whom have proceeded the works of principal and minor creations, the various races, Manvantaras, and histories of the families. We will proceed to him, to witness the trtle essence, on whom I do meditate.

## \|\| 2.30 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ityukto 'haṃ purā rudraḥ śvetadvīpanivāsinam \|*  
*stutvā praṇamya taṃ viṣṇuṃ śrotukāma sthitaḥ suraiḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Brahma said: — I was thus formerly addressed by Rudra. Having lauded and saluted Visnu, the dweller of the white island (Shveta-dvipa) we sat calmly desirous of listening to (the subject).

## \|\| 2.31 \|\|

*asmākaṃ madhyato rudra uvāca parameśvaram \|*  
*sārāntsārataraṃ viṣṇuṃ pṛṣṭavāṃstaṃ praṇamya vai \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. From amongst us Rudra said to Visnu, the great Isvara — "Describe to us the most essential of all essence; we salute thee".

## \|\| 2.32 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*yathā papraccha māṃ vyāsa stathāsau bhagavān bhavaḥ \|*  
*papraccha viṣṇuṃ devādyaiḥ śṛṇvatāmamaraiḥ saha \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. What, О Vyasa, you have asked me the Lord Bhava asked Visnu in the hearing of myself and other celestials.

## \|\| 2.33 \|\|

*rudra uvāca \|*  
*hare kathaya deveśa ! devadevaḥ ka īśvaraḥ \|*  
*ko dhyeyaḥ kaśca vai pūjyaḥ kairvratai stuṣyate paraḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Rudra said: — О Hari, О king of goods, tell us who is the god of goods; who is Isvara; who should be meditated on; who should be adored; with what vowed observances, the great is propitiated?

## \|\| 2.34 \|\|

*kairdharmaiḥ kaiśca niyamaiḥ kayā vā dharmapūjayā \|*  
*kenācāreṇa tuṣṭaḥ syātkiṃ tadrūpaṃ ca tasya vai \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. ith what religious observances, with what process of self-restraint, with what form of adoration and with what sort of conduct is He pleased?

## \|\| 2.35-36 \|\|

*kasmāddevājjagajjātaṃ jagatpālayate cakaḥ \|*  
*kīdṛśairavatāraiśca kasminyāti layaṃ jagat \|\| 35 \|\|*

*sargaśca pratisargaśca vaṃśo manvantarāṇi ca \|*  
*kasmāddevātpravartante kasmimannetatpratiṣṭhitam \|\| 36 \|\|*

35-36. What is his form? From what deity the universe has emanated and who protects it? What are his incarnations? In whom the world is dissolved? From what delay proceed the works of principal and minor creations, the various families and Manvantaras? In whom do all these exist?

## \|\| 2.37-39 \|\|

*etatsarvaṃ hare ! brūhi yaccānyadapi kiñcana \|*  
*parameśvaramāhātmyaṃ yuktayogādikaṃ tathā \|\| 37 \|\|*

*tathāṣṭādaśa vidyāśca harī rudraṃ tato 'bravīt \|*  
*hariruvāca \|*  
*śṛṇu rudra ! pravakṣyāmi brahmaṇā ca suraiḥ saha \|\| 38 \|\|*

*ahaṃ hi devo devānāṃ sarvalokeśvareśvaraḥ \|*  
*ahaṃ dhyeyaśca pūjyaśca stutyohaṃ statibhiḥ suraiḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

37-39. Do thou describe all this and every thing else, О Hari. Then Hari described to Rudra the glories of the great Isvara, the Yoga and eighteen sorts of learning. Hari said — Hear, О Rudra, I will describe it, along with Brahma and other celestials. I am the god of gods, the lord of all the worlds. I am the object of meditation and adoration and am lauded by the celestials with panegyric verses.

## \|\| 2.40 \|\|

*ahaṃ hi pūjito rudra ! dadāmi paramāṃ gatim \|*  
*niyamaiśca vrataistuṣṭa ācāreṇa ca mānavaiḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. When I am worshipped by men with self restraint, vowed observances and good conduct О Rudra, I grant them the most excellent stage.

## \|\| 2.41 \|\|

*jagatsthiterahaṃ bījaṃ jagatkartā tvahaṃ śiva ! \|*  
*duṣṭanigrahakartā hi dharmagoptā tvahaṃ hara ! \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. I am the seed of the preservation of the world and I am also the destroyer of the universe, О Shiva. О Нага, I am also the suppressor of the wicked and the protector of religion.

## \|\| 2.42 \|\|

*avatāraiśca matsyādyaiḥ pālayāmyakhilaṃ jagat \|*  
*ahaṃ mantrāśca mantrārthaḥ pūjādhyānaparo hyaham \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. With fish and other incarnations I do protect the earth. I am the import of the mystic formula and am engaged in adoration and meditation.

## \|\| 2.43 \|\|

*svargādīnāṃ ca kartāhaṃ svargādīnyahameva ca \|*

43\. I am the creator of heaven and I am myself the heaven etc.

## \|\| 2.44 \|\|

*jñātā śrotā tathā mantā vaktā vaktavyameva ca \|*

44\. I am the knower, the hearer, the speaker and the object of speech. I am all and the deity identical with all. I am the source of worldly enjoyments and emancipation.

## \|\| 2.45 \|\|

*dhyānaṃ pūjopahāro 'haṃ maṇḍalānyahameva ca \|*  
*itihāsānyahaṃ rudra ! sarvavedā hyahaṃ śiva ! \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. I am the presents of meditation and adoration:, I am the Mandalas, the Itihasas, O. Rudra. О 5iva, I am all the deities.

## \|\| 2.46 \|\|

*sarvajñānānyahaṃ śambho ! brahmātmāhamahaṃ śiva ! \|*  
*ahaṃ brahmā sarvalokaḥ sarvadevātmako hyaham \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. O Sambhu, I am all the forms of knowledge I am at one with Brahma, О Shiva. I am Brahma, all the regions, and identical with all the deities.

## \|\| 2.47 \|\|

*ahaṃ sākṣātsadācāro dharmo 'haṃ vaiṣṇavo hyaham \|*

47\. I am the personification of righteous conduct and the religion of Visnu. I am the Varnas (castes) and ASramas (orders) and I am the ancient religion.

## \|\| 2.48 \|\|

*yamo 'haṃ niyamo rudra ! vratāni vividhāni ca \|*  
*ahaṃ sūryastathā candro maṅgalādīnyahaṃ tathā \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. I am the process of regulation that of self- restraint and tile various vowed observances, O Rudra. I am the sun, the moon, and all the auspicious things.

## \|\| 2.49 \|\|

*purā māṃ garuḍaḥ pakṣī tapasārādhayadbhuvi \|*  
*tuṣṭa ūce varaṃ brūhi matto vavre varaṃ sa tu \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Formerly with assceticism the bird Garuda had worshipped me on earth. Pleased with him I asked him to pray for a boon; and he too prayed for a boon.

## \|\| 2.50-53 \|\|

*garuḍa uvāca \|*  
*mama mātā ca vinatā nāgairdāsīkṛtā hare \|*  
*yathāhaṃ deva tāñjitvā cāmṛtaṃ hyānayāmi tat \|\| 50 \|\|*

*dāsyādvimokṣayiṣyāmi yathāhaṃ vāhanastava \|*  
*mahābalo mahāvīryaḥ sarvajño nāgadāraṇaḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

*purāṇasaṃhitākartā yathāhaṃ syāṃ tathā kuruṃ \|*  
*viṣṇuruvāca \|*  
*yathā tvayoktaṃ garuḍa tathā sarvaṃ bhaviṣyati \|\| 52 \|\|*

*nāgadāsyānmātaraṃ tvaṃ vinatāṃ mokṣayiṣyasi \|*  
*devādīnsakalāñjitvā cāmṛtaṃ hyānayiṣyasi \|\| 53 \|\|*

50-53. Garuda said: — О Hari, my mother Vinata — had been made a slave, by the Nagas. Do thou so order, that I may bring ambrosia after vanquishing the celestials, that I may release her from slavery and that I may be thy carrier. Do thou so order that I may be highly powerful, greatly strong, onmiscient, the aftlictor of the Nagas, and the author of Purans and Samhitas. Visnu said: — What you have said, О Garuda, will all be accomplished. You will release you mother Vinata from the Nagas. Having vanquished all the deities and others you will bering ambrosia.

## \|\| 2.54-55 \|\|

*mahābalo vāhanastvaṃ bhaviṣyasi viṣārdanaḥ \|*

*yaduktaṃ matsvarūpaṃ ca tava cāvirbhaviṣyati \|*  
*gāruḍaṃ tava nāmnā talloke khyātiṃ gamiṣyati \|\| 55 \|\|*

54-55. You will be the highly powerful carrier. By my favour you will be jthe author of the Purana, describing my glories and forms. By your name it will be celebrated on the earth as Garuda.

## \|\| 2.56 \|\|

*yathāhaṃ devadevānāṃ śrīḥ khyāto vinatāsuta \|*  
*tathā khyātiṃ purāṇeṣu gāruḍaṃ gāruḍaiṣyati \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. О son of Vinata, as I am the God of gods and Sri is celebrated so the Garuda Purana will be celebrated amongst all the Puranas.

## \|\| 2.57 \|\|

*yathāhaṃ kīrtanīyo 'tha tathā tvaṃ garuḍātmanā \|*  
*māṃ dhyātvā pakṣimukhyedaṃ purāṇaṃ gada gāruḍam \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. As I am worthy of being lauded so thou shalt be. Meditating on me by your mind do you describe this Garuda Purana by your bird mouth."

## \|\| 2.58 \|\|

*ityukto garuḍo rudra ! kaśyapāyāha pṛcchate \|*  
*kaśyapo gāruḍaṃ śrutvā vṛkṣaṃ dagdhamajīvayat \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. Thus accosted, О Rudra, Garuda described it to Kasyapa. Hearing the Garuda Purana Kasyapa revived the burnt tree.

## \|\| 2.59 \|\|

*svayaṃ cānyamanā bhūtvā vidyayānyānya jīvayat \|*  
*yakṣi oṃuṃsvāhājāpī vidyayaṃ gāruḍī parā \|*  
*garuḍoktaṃ gāruḍaṃ hi śṛṇu rudra ! madātmakam \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. Hearing yourself with fixed attention do you revive others with your learning. "The bird, Ош, Um, Swaha" — This is the great learning of Garuda. Hear, О Rudra, the great Garuda Purana narrated by Garuda.

## Chapter 3

## \|\| 3.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*iti rudrābjajo viṣṇoḥ śuśrāva brahmaṇo muniḥ \|*  
*vyāso vyāsādahaṃ vakṣyehaṃ te śaunaka naimiṣe \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Suta said — Thus did Rudra bear it from Visnu; Brahma from Rudra; from Brahma the ascetic Vyasa; and myself from Vyasa. And I relate it to you. О Sounaka, in the forest of Naimisa.

## \|\| 3.2-3 \|\|

*munīnāṃ śṛṇvatāṃ madhye sargādyaṃ devapūjanam \|*  
*tīrthaṃ bhuvanakośaṃ ca manvantaramihocyate \|\| 2 \|\|*

*varṇāśramādidharmāśca dānarājādidharmakāḥ \|*

2-3. In the assemblage of the ascetics have been described by me, the creation and the adoration of the deities, the various sacred sbrines, the wealth of the world and the Manvantaras; the duties of the various Varnas (castes) and Asramas (orders); the gifts, the regal duties, the laws, vowed observances, families and the medical science with a diagnosis of diseases; the various auxiliary sciences, the universal dissolution; religious profit, desire, worldly profit and the most excellent knowledge.

## \|\| 3.4 \|\|

*aṅgāni pralayo dharmakāmārthajñānamuttamam \|*

4\. The illusory deeds, and those beyond the range of illusion, of Visnu have all been narrated in Garuda Purana.

## \|\| 3.5 \|\|

*purāṇe gāruḍe sarvaṃ garuḍo bhagavānatha \|*  
*vāsudevaprasādena sāmarthyātiśayairyutaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. This Garuda is Bhagavan1 By the favour of Vasudeva he has been endued with great strength.

## \|\| 3.6-9 \|\|

*bhutvā harervāhanaṃ ca sargādīnāṃ ca kāraṇam \|*  
*devānvijitya garuḍo hyamṛtāharaṇaṃ tathā \|\| 6 \|\|*

*cakre kṣudhā hṛtaṃ yasya brahmāṇḍamudare hareḥ \|*  
*yaṃ dṛṣṭvā smṛtamātreṇa nāgāndīnāṃ ca saṃkṣayaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*kaśyapo gāruḍādvṛkṣaṃ dagdhaṃ cājīvayadyataḥ \|*  
*garuḍaḥ sa haristena proktaṃ śrīkaśyapāya ca \|\| 8 \|\|*

*tacchrīmadrāruḍaṃ puṇyaṃ sarvadaṃ paṭhatastava \|*  
*vakṣye vyāsaṃ namaskṛtya śṛṇu śaunaka tadyathā \|\| 9 \|\|*

6-9. Having become the carrier of Hari be is the instrument of creation etc. Having vanquished the celestials Garuda brought ambrosia, by which the appetite of the universe, lying in the belly of Hari, was appeased. His very sight or recollection destroys the serpents. Through Garuda Kasyapa revived all the burnt trees. Garuda is Hari. He related it unto Казуара. The auspicious Garuda Purana, when read, gives piety and all objects. Hear, О Sounaka, how Hari describe it unto Rudra.

## Chapter 4

## \|\| 4.1 \|\|

*rudra uvāca \|*

1\. Rudra said — О Janarddana, do thou described the primary and secondary creations, the families, Manvantaras as, well as the histories of the families.

*hariruvāca \|*

*naranārāyaṇo devo vāsudevo nirañjanaḥ \|*

*tasmāhuddhirmanastasmāttataḥ khaṃ pavana stataḥ \|*

7\. From him emanate the intellect, mind, the Tattvas (principles) ether, air, fire, water and earth.

## \|\| 4.8 \|\|

*aṇḍo hiraṇmayo rudra tasyāntaḥ svayameva hi \|*  
*śarīragrahaṇaṃ pūrvaṃ sṛṣṭyarthaṃ kurute prabhuḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. О Rudra, He is the golden egg and is himself his own end. The Lord assumes a body for the purposes of creation.

## \|\| 4.9 \|\|

*brahmā caturmukho bhūtvā rajomātrādhikaḥ sadā \|*

## \|\| 4.10 \|\|

*aṇḍasyāntarjagatsarvaṃ sadevāsuramānuṣam \|*

## \|\| 4.11 \|\|

*apasaṃhriyate cānte saṃhartā ca svayaṃ hara \|*

11\. As Creator he creates the universe; as Visnu he protects it; and he destroys it in the end. Hari himself is the destroyer, Having assumed the body of Brahma Hari creates the universe and as Visriu he protects it.

## \|\| 4.12 \|\|

*rudrarūpī ca kalpānte jagatsaṃharate 'khilam \|*

## \|\| 4.13 \|\|

*daṃṣṭūyoddharati jñātvā vārahīmāsthitastanūm \|*

13\. He, assuming the form of a boar, held up with his tusks the earth sunk under water. Hear, О Sankara, I will describe all in short beginning with the first creation of the deity.

## \|\| 4.14 \|\|

*(1)prathamo mahataḥ sargo virūpo brahmaṇastu saḥ \|*  
*(2) nanmātrāṇāṃ dvitīyastu bhūtasargo hi sa smṛtaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

## \|\| 4.15 \|\|

*(3)vaikārikastṛtīyastu sargastvaindriyakaḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*ityeṣa prākṛtaḥ sargaḥ sambhūto buddhipūrvakaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

## \|\| 4.16 \|\|

*(4)mukhyasargaścaturthastu mukhyā vai sthāvarāḥ smṛtāḥ \|*  
*(5)tiryaksrotāstu yaḥ proktastiryagyonyaḥ sa ucyate \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. The tourth is the primary creation and all the stationery bodies are known as primary creations. The next is Tiryyakasrotas1 who are otherwise called Tiryyakjollya i.e. beasts etc.

## \|\| 4.17 \|\|

*(6) tadūrdhvastotasāṃ ṣaṣṭho devasargastu sa smṛtaḥ \|*  
*(7) tator'vāksrotasāṃ sargaḥ saptamaḥ sa tu mā nuṣaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. The sixth is the Urdhasrotasa2 which is called the creation of the celestials. The seventh is the creation of Arvakasrotas3 or human beings.

## \|\| 4.18 \|\|

*(8)aṣṭamo 'nugrahaḥ sargaḥ sāttvikastāmasastu saḥ \|*  
*pañcaite vaikṛtāḥ sargāḥ prākṛtāstu trayaḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. The eighth is the creation of Anugrahas4 pervaded by the qualities of Sattva (goodness) and Sattva (ignorance). These are the five orders of the Vaikarika (organic) creation. There are three orders of the elementary and organic creation.

## \|\| 4.19 \|\|

*prākṛto vaikṛtaścāpi (9) kaumāro navamaḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*sthāvarāntāḥ surādyāstu prajā rudra ! caturvidhāḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Koumara makes the ninth. О Rudra, there are four orders of creation beginning with the celestials and ending with the stationery creation.

## \|\| 4.20-22 \|\|

*brahmaṇaḥ kurvataḥ sṛṣṭiṃ jajñire mānasāḥ sutāḥ \|*  
*tato devāsurapitṝnmānuṣāṃśca catuṣṭayam \|\| 20 \|\|*

*sisṛkṣurambhāṃsyetāni svamātmānamayūyujat \|*  
*vyaktātmanastamomātrādudriktāstatprajāpateḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*sisṛkṣerjaghanātpūrvamasurā jajñire tataḥ \|*  
*utsasarja tatastāṃ tu tamomātrātmikāṃ tanūm \|\| 22 \|\|*

20-22. While engaged in the work of creation Brahma first procreated his mind-born sons. Then desirous of creating the tour classes of beings, viz. the celeslials, Asuras, Pitrs and human beings, all, going under the name of Amba he adored his own self,5 as the lord of beings, although himself of unfettered soul, concentrated his soul, being desirous of creating, passion overspread him and first from forth his hips came out the Asuras,

## \|\| 4.23 \|\|

*tamomātrā tanustyaktā śaṅkarābhūdvibhāvarī \|*

23\. And then he renounced his person surcharged with Tama or darkness; and his darkness, on being renounced by him, О Sankara, was converted into Night, Having assumed another body he became desirous of creating and felt delight,

## \|\| 4.24-38 \|\|

*sattvodriktāstu mukhataḥ saṃbhūtā brahmaṇo hara ! \|*

*etān grāmyānpaśūnprāhurāraṇyāṃśca nibodha me \|*  
*śvāpadaṃ dvikhuraṃ hastivānarāḥ pakṣipañcamāḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

*audakāḥ paśavaḥ ṣaṣṭhāḥ saptamāśca sarīsṛpāḥ \|*  
*pūrvādibhyo mukhebhyastu ṛgvedādyāḥ prajajñire \|\| 34 \|\|*

*āsyādvai brāhmaṇā jātā bāhubhyāṃ kṣattriyāḥ smṛtāḥ \|*  
*ūrubhyāṃ tu viśaḥ sṛṣṭāḥ śūdraḥ padybhāma jāyata \|\| 35 \|\|*

*brahmaloko brāhmaṇānāṃ śākraḥ kṣattriyajanmanām \|*  
*mārutaṃ ca viśāṃ sthānaṃ gāndharvaṃ śūdrajanmanām \|\| 36 \|\|*

*brahmacārivratasthānāṃ brahmalokaḥ prajāyate \|*  
*prājāpatyaṃ gṛhasthānāṃ yathāvihitakāriṇām \|\| 37 \|\|*

*sthānaṃ saptaṛṣīṇāṃ ca tathaiva vanavāsinām \|*  
*yatīnāmakṣayaṃ sthānaṃ yadṛcchāgāmināṃ sadā \|\| 38 \|\|*

24-38. Then О Нага, came out from the mouth of Brahma, the celestials surcharged with the justity of Sattva (goodness). On being renounced by him his body, surcharged with the quality of Sattva, was converted into Day. Therefore it is that the Asuras are powerful in the night and the celestials during the day. He then assumed a person fraught with the quality of goodness and then sprang from him the ancestors. And that body, on being renounced by him, became Twilight remaining between day and night, Then having assumed a body fraught with the quality of Rajas (darkness) he created human beings, And on being renouned by him that form became moon-light which is termed Prak-sandhya.1 Moonlight, Night, Day and Twilight are his bodies. And then he assumed another body fraught with the quality of darkness and thereat sprung hunger from his and from hunger wrath. Brahma then creater Raksasas exercised with hunger. (Those that said 'Save him') are called Raksasa and those (diat said 'We shall eat him up) are called Yaksas from Yaksana eating, And from the movement. (Sarpana) of his hairs sprang the serpents. Waxing worm he generated some beings of warthful temper. Q sinless, then die Gandharvas came out singing. All these beings were created by him. He created goats from his mouth, the kine from his belly and sides; me horses, elephants, asses and camels from his feet, and medicinal herbs furnished with fruits and roots from the hairs of his body. Fair complexioned male sheep, horses, mules and asses are called gramya or household animals. Hear, I will describe the wild ones, (They are) the beasts of prey, the cloven-hoofed, elephants, monkeys, and fifthly, birds and sixthly, acquatic animals and seventhly, reptiles. From his eastern and other mouths he created the Rk and other Vedas. The Brahmanas originated from his mouth, die Ksatriyas from his arms, me Vaisyas from his thighs and the Sudras form his feet. The region of Brahma is for the Brahmanas, that of Sakra for me Ksatriyas, mat of Marut (windgod) for die Vaiiyas and that Gandharvas for the Sudras. Those practising the Brahmacarya injunctions attain the region of Brahma. The householders, performing duly their duties, repair to die region of die Creator, Those, living in me forest, acquire the region of me seven Rsis. The sphere of me Yatis, going at will, is die eternal region.

Hari said: — Having created me world and all orders of beings the Lord created his mind- begotten sons for multiplying his creation; namely Dharma, Rudra, Manu, Sanaka, Sana tana, Bhrgu, Sanatkumara, Ruci, Suddha, Marici, Atri, Angira, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu, Narada and the Patris Varhisadas.

5-6. The Lotus-sprung deity, from his right thumb, created Daksa endued with four forms and his wife from his left thigh, Daksa begat on her beautiful daughters. He gave them away unto the sons of Brahma and conferred Sati on Rudra.

7-8. Numberless, highly powerful sons were born unto Rudra. He conferred the auspicious Khyati, matchless in beauty, on Bhrgu. Bhrgu begat on her Dhata and Vidhata. He also begat Shrj who was Narayaria's wifi.

## \|\| 5.9 \|\|

*dhātāvidhātroste bhārye tayorjātau sutāvubhau \|*

*smṛteścāṃṅgirasaḥ putrāḥ prasūtāḥ kanyakāstathā \|*

## \|\| 5.14-16 \|\|

*prītyāṃ pulastyabhāryāyāṃ dattolistatsuto 'bhavat \|*

14-16. Pulastya begat on Priti Dottoli, Three sons, Karman, Arthavira and Sahisnu were begat on his wife Sumati the sixty thousand ^sis of controlled passions by name Valakhilyas. They were all of the height of a thumb and effugent like the burning sun.

*ūrjāyāṃ tu vasiṣṭasya saptājāyanta vai sutāḥ \|*

## \|\| 5.19-21 \|\|

*tasmātsvāhā sutāṃllebhe trīnudāraujaso hara ! \|*

19-21. Daksa conferred Suha on the fire-god who had assumed a body. О Нага, from him Suaha obtained three highly effulgent sons viz. Pavaka, Pavamana and Suci, all eaters of water. 37-38. Gourl became Sambhu's wife whose sons were Vinayaka and Kumara. Rudra, the powerful master of Bhrngl, was by nature wrathful. He destroyed Daksa's sacrifice and imprescated a curse on him, saying, "You will be born as a man, in the family of Dhruva.

## Chapter 6

## \|\| 6.1 \|\|

*hariruvāca \|*

*ripoḥ putrastathā śrīmāṃścākṣuṣaḥ kīrtito manuḥ \|*  
*rurustasya sutaḥ śrīmānaṅgastasyāpi cātmajaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. His son was known as tlie beautiful Manu Caksusa. His son was Ruru whose son was the beautiful Anga.

*aṅgasya veṇaḥ putrastu nāstiko dharmavarjitaḥ \|*

5\. Anga's son was Vena who was an atheist and an irreligious person. Vena, the perpetrator of iniquities, was killed by the Rsis with Kusa.

## \|\| 6.6-7 \|\|

*ūruṃ mamanthuḥ putrārthe tato 'sya tanayo 'bhavat \|*

*tato 'sya dakṣiṇaṃ pāṇiṃ mamanthuḥ sahasā dvijāḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

6-7. They then churned his thigh for a son and thereat sprang a son, grsatly dwarfish and black. They then said "sit down, sit down" and he was called Nisada dwelling on the mount Vindhya. Then the twice-born once suddenly churned his right thigh.

## \|\| 6.8-9 \|\|

*tasmāttasya suto jāto viṣṇormānasarūpadhṛk \|*  
*puthurityevanāmā sa veṇaputro divaṃ yayau \|\| 8 \|\|*

*dudoha pṛthivīṃ rājā prajānāṃ jīvanāya hi \|*  
*antardhānaḥ pṛthoḥ putro tahavirdhānastadātmajaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

8-9. From there sprange a son assuming the mental form of Visnu, by name Prthu. By that son Vena repaired to the celestial region. They king milched the earth, for giving life to his subjects. Prthu's son was Antarddhana whose son again was Havirdhana.

## \|\| 6.10 \|\|

*prācīnavaharstetputraḥ pṛthivyāmekarāḍ babhau \|*

10\. His son Praclnavarhl became the Lord Paramount of the world.

## \|\| 6.11 \|\|

*tasmātsuṣāva sāmudrī daśa prācīnabarhiṣaḥ \|*  
*sarve prācetasā nāma dhanurvedasya pāragāḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Не espoused the daughter of the ocean of salt rater and begat on her ten Praclnavarhls who were called Pracetas and were masters of the science of archery.

## \|\| 6.12 \|\|

*apṛthagadharṃmacaraṇāste 'tapyanta mahattapaḥ \|*  
*daśavarṣasahasrāṇi samudrasalileśayāḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. They all practised the same religious austerities and remained immersed in the bed of the deep for ten thousand years.

## \|\| 6.13 \|\|

*prajāpatitvaṃ saṃprāpya bhāryā teṣāṃ ca māriṣa \|*  
*abhavaddhavaśāpena tasyāṃ dakṣo 'bhavattataḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. They attained to the dignity of the Patriarchs; and their wife was Marlsa. of her was born Daksa by the impecation of Bhava.

## \|\| 6.14 \|\|

*asṛjanmanasā dakṣaḥ prajāḥ pūrvaṃ caturvodhāḥ \|*  
*nāvardhanta ca tāstasya apadhyātā hareṇa tu \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. As before Daksa against created four classes of beings from his mind. Obstructed by Нага they did not multiply.

## \|\| 6.15 \|\|

*maithunena tataḥ sṛṣṭiṃ kartumaicchatprajāpatiḥ \|*  
*asikrīmāvahadbhāryāṃ vīraṇasya prajāpateḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. The Patriarch then desired to carry on the work of creation by sexual intercourse. He then poused Asiknl, the daughter of the Patriarch Varuna.

## \|\| 6.16 \|\|

*tasya putrasahasraṃ tu vairaṇyāṃ samapadyata \|*  
*nāradoktā bhuvaścāntaṃ gatā jñātuṃ ca nāgatāḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. He begat on the daughter of Varuna a thousand sons. The end of the earth being decribed by Narada they went there to learn it and did not return.

## \|\| 6.17 \|\|

*dakṣaputrasahasraṃ ca teṣu naṣṭeṣu sṛṣṭavān \|*  
*śavalāśvāste 'pi gatā bhrātṝṇāṃ padavīṃ hara ! \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. On their being lost Daksa created another thusand, named ^aklasva, who also followed the foot steps of their brothers, О Нага.

## \|\| 6.18 \|\|

*dakṣaḥ kruddhaḥ śaśāpātha nāradaṃ janma cāpsyasi \|*  
*nārado hyabhavatputraḥ kaśyapasya muneḥ punaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Worked up with anger Daksa cursed Narada saying "You will obtain a birth" and he was again born as the son of the ascetic Kasyapa.

## \|\| 6.19 \|\|

*yajñe dhvaste 'tha dakṣo 'pi śaśāprograṃ maheśvaram \|*  
*stutvātvāmupacāraiśca pūjayiṣyanti śaṅkara \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. On his sacrifice being destroyed Daksa imprecated the terrific Mahesvara, saying, "Having worshipped thee with necessary articles the twice-born will leave them aside.

## \|\| 6.20 \|\|

*janmāntare 'pi vaireṇa te vinaśyanti śaṅkara ! \|*  
*tasmādvairaṃ na kartavyaṃ kadācidapi kenacit \|*  
*asiknyāṃ (mahiṣyāṃ) janayāmāsa dakṣo duhitaro hyatha \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Even in another birth, your hostilities will not terminate, О Sankara."

## \|\| 6.21-22 \|\|

*ṣaṣṭiṃ kanyā rūpayutā dve caivāṅgirase dadau \|*  
*dve prādātsa kṛśāśvāya daśa dharṃmāya cāpyatha \|\| 21 \|\|*

*caturdaśa kaśyapāya aṣṭāviṃśātimindave \|*  
*pradadau bahuputrāya suprabhāṃ bhāminīṃ tathā \|\| 22 \|\|*

21-22. Daksa begat on Asikni sixty beautiful daughters. He gave away two of them unto Angiras. He conferred two on Krsasva, ten on Dharma, thirteen on Kasyapa and twenty-seven on Indu. He conferred Suprabha and Bhaminl on Vahuputra.

## \|\| 6.23-25 \|\|

*manoramāṃ bhānumatīṃ viśālāṃ bahudāmatha \|*  
*dakṣaḥ prādānmahādeva ! catasro 'riṣṭanemaye (ne) \|\| 23 \|\|*

*sa kṛśāśvāya ca prādātsuprajāṃ ca tathā jayām \|*  
*arundhatī vasuryār(jā) mī lambā bhānurmarudvatī \|\| 24 \|\|*

*saṅkalpā ca muhūrtā ca sādhyā viśvā ca tā daśa \|*

*oṃ hrūṃ śikhāyai namaḥ \|*  
*oṃ hraiṃ kavacāya namaḥ \|*  
*oṃ hrauṃ netratrayāya namaḥ \|*  
*oṃ hraḥ astrāya namaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Om, Hrim, salutation unto Sarasvatl. Om, Hram, salutation unto her heart. Om, Hrim, salutation unto her head. Om, Hrum, salutation unto her hairs. Om, Hram, salutation unto her amulet. Om, Hrum, salutation unto her three eyes. Om, Hrah, salutation unto the weapons.

## \|\| 7.9 \|\|

*śraddhā ṛddhiḥ kalā medhā tuṣṭiḥ puṣṭiḥ prabhā matiḥ \|*  
*oṃ hrīṅkārādyā namo 'ntāśca sarasvatyāśca śaktayaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Sradha, Hrddhi, Kala, Medha, Tusti, Prabha, Mati, these energies of Sarasvati, should be adored with mantrams beginning with Om and ending with Namah.

## \|\| 7.10 \|\|

*kṣetrapālāya namaḥ \|*  
*oṃ gurubhyo namaḥ \|*  
*oṃ paramagurubhyo namaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Om salutation unto the Ksetrapalas. Om salutation unto the preceptors. Om salutation unto the great Guru.

## \|\| 7.11 \|\|

*padmasthāyāḥ sarasvatyā āsanādyaṃ prakalpayet \|*  
*sūryādīnāṃ svakairprantraiḥ pavitrārohaṇaṃ tathā \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. He should then dedicate seats and other offerings to Sarasvati standing on a lotus. The sacred Arohana (installation of the image) of Surya (sun) and other deities should be performed with their respective mantrams.

## Chapter 8

## \|\| 8.1 \|\|

*hariruvāca \|*  
*bhūmiṣṭhe maṇḍape snātvā maṇḍale viṣṇumarcayet \|*  
*pañcaraṅgikacūrṇena vajranābhaṃ tu maṇḍalam \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Hari said — Having bathed in the Mandapa (temple) built on earth one should adore Visnu in Mandala (circular figure).

## \|\| 8.2 \|\|

*ṣoḍaśaiḥ koṣṭhakaistatra saṃmitaṃ rudra? kārayet \|*  
*caturthapañcakoṇeṣu sūtrapātaṃ tu kārayet \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. With powers of five colours, this circular figure, Vajranabha, should be drawn. О Rudra sixteen rooms should be drawn there. In the fourth and fifth corners strings should be placed.

## \|\| 8.3 \|\|

*koṇasūtrādubhayataḥ koṇā ye tatra saṃsthitāḥ \|*  
*teṣu caiva prakurvīta sūtrapātaṃ vicakṣaṇaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. The strings in the corner should be extended to both the other corners. A man, well versed in all these rites, should thus place strings in all the corners.

## \|\| 8.4 \|\|

*tadanantarakoṇeṣu evameva hi kārayet \|*  
*prathamā nābhiruddiṣṭā madhye rekhāprasaṃgame \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Similarly he should deal with interior comers. The first should be placed in the centre and then al the junction of the lines in the middle.

## \|\| 8.5 \|\|

*antareṣu ca sarveṣu aṣṭau caiva tunābhayaḥ \|*  
*pūrvamadhyamanābhi bhyāmathaṃ sūtraṃ tu bhrāmayet \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. In all the interior parts dlere are eight centres. The centres of the eastern and central figures should be connected widl a string.

## \|\| 8.6 \|\|

*antarā sa dvijaśreṣṭhaḥ pādonaṃ bhrāmayeddhara ! \|*  
*anena nābhisūtrasya karṇikāṃ bhrāmayecchiva ! \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. О Нага, the foremosst of the twice-born should draw the base in the interior parts. О Siva, connected widl it the pericarps of the central string should be drawn.

## \|\| 8.7 \|\|

*karṇikāyā dvibhāgena kesarāṇi vicakṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*tadagreṇa sadā vidvāndalānyeva samālikhet \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. On two sides of the pericarps an expert should draw the filaments. A learned man should draw petals on their heads.

## \|\| 8.8 \|\|

*sarveṣu nābhikṣetraṣu mānenānena suvrata ! \|*  
*padmāni tāni kurvīta deśikaḥ para mārthavit \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. О thou of firm vows, a worshipper, conversant widl the knowledge of the true object, should draw figures of lotuses in all the centres.

## \|\| 8.9 \|\|

*ādisūtravibhāgena dvārāṇi parikalpayet \|*  
*dvāraśobhāṃ tathā tatra tadardhena tu kalpayet \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. With the division of the first string one should draw the doors. With the half he should make decorations for the same.

## \|\| 8.10 \|\|

*karṇikāṃ pītavarṇena sitaraktādikesaraiḥ \|*  
*antaraṃ nīlavarṇena dalāni asitena ca \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. The pericarp should be drawn with yellow colour, the filaments with dark blue, the inside violet and the petals with crimson.

## \|\| 8.11-12 \|\|

*kṛṣṇavarṇena rajasā caturaśraṃ prapūrayet \|*  
*dvārāṇi śuklavarṇena rekhāḥ pañca ca maṇḍale \|\| 11 \|\|*

*sitā raktā tathā pītā kṛṣṇā caiva yathākramam \|*  
*kṛtvaiva maṇḍalañcādau nyāsaṃ kṛtvārcayeddharim \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12. The tour parts should be filled up with black powder, the doors with white powder and the five ines of the Mandala in order with crimson, yellow and dark-blue. Having performed Nyasa:assignment of the limbs he should adore Hari in the five Mandala.

## \|\| 8.13 \|\|

*hṛnmadhye tu nyasedviṣṇuṃ kaṇṭhe saṅkarṣaṇaṃ tathā \|*  
*pradyumnaṃ śirasi nyasya śikhāyāmaniruddhakam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. He should assign his heart to Visnu, the middle part to Sankarsana, the head to Pradyumna and the tuft of hair on the head to Aniruddha.

## \|\| 8.14 \|\|

*brahmāṇaṃ sarvagātreṣu karayoḥ śrīdharaṃ tathā \|*  
*ahaṃ viṣṇuriti dhyātvā karṇikāyāṃ nyaseddharim \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. His entire body should be assigned to Brahma and the fingers to Sridhara. Meditating "I am Visnu" he should perform the Nyasa of Hari in the pericarps.

## \|\| 8.15-16 \|\|

*nyasetsaṅkarṣaṇaṃ pūrve pradyumnaṃ caiva dakṣiṇe \|*  
*aniruddhaṃ paścime ca brihmāṇaṃ cottare nyaset \|\| 15 \|\|*

*śrīdharaṃ rudrakoṇeṣu indrādīndikṣu vinyaset \|*  
*tato 'bhyarcya ca gandhādyaiḥ prāpnuyātparamaṃ padam \|\| 16 \|\|*

15-16. He should perform the Nyasa of Sankarsana in the east, that of Pradyumna in the south, that of Aniruddha in the west, that of Brahma in the north that of Sridhara, Indra and other deities in Rudra and other corners. Having adored them with scents and other articles a worshipper attains to the great station.1

## Chapter 9

## \|\| 9.1 \|\|

*hariruvāca \|*  
*samaye (yā) dīkṣitaḥ śiṣyo baddhanetrastu vāsasā \|*  
*aṣṭāhutiśataṃ tasya mūlamantreṇa homayet \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Hari said: — Being initiated in proper time and having his eyes covered with a cloth a disciple should offer one hundred and eight oblations with the principal mantram.

## \|\| 9.2 \|\|

*dviguṇaṃ putrake homaṃ triguṇaṃ sādhake matam \|*  
*nirvāṇadeśike rudra ! caturguṇamudāhṛtam \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Rudra twice the number should be offered in a Putraka Нота1, thrice the number in Sadhaka2 and four times the number in Nirvanadesika.3

## \|\| 9.3 \|\|

*guruviṣṇudvijastrīṇāṃ hantā badhyastva(śca)dīkṣitaiḥ \|*  
*atha dīkṣāṃ pravakṣyāmi dharmādharmakṣayaṅkarīm \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. A destroyer of a preceptor, Visnu's image, Brahmana and a woman deserves death at the hands of those who are not initiated. I will describe his DIksa or initiation destructive of virtue and sin.

## \|\| 9.4 \|\|

*upaveśya bahiḥ śiṣyāndhāraṇaṃ teṣu kārayet \|*  
*vāyavyā kalayā rudra śoṣyamāṇānvicintayet \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Having caused his disciples to sit outside he should make them concentrte their minds.

## \|\| 9.5 \|\|

*āgreyyā dahyamānāṃśca plāvitānambhasā punaḥ \|*  
*tejastejāsi taṃ jīvamekīkṛtya samākṣipet \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. О Rudra, he should consider sprinkled with water. Uniting the sentiency with fire he should consign it to fire.

## \|\| 9.6 \|\|

*prāṇavaṃ cintayevdyomni śarīre 'nyattu kāraṇam \|*  
*ekaikaṃ yo jayettatra kṣetrajñaṃ dehakāraṇāt \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Не should meditate on Pranava the instrument of all, in the sky and in the body. He should next unite it with Ksetrajna4 for its being the cause of the body.

## \|\| 9.7 \|\|

*utpādya yojayetpaścādekaikaṃ vṛṣabhadhvaja \|*  
*maṇḍalādiṣvaśaktastu kalpayitvār'cayeddharim \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Then imagining all the 6aktis or female energies of the deity in the various Mandala he should adore Hari.

## \|\| 9.8 \|\|

*caturdvāraṃ bhavettacca brahmatīrthādanukramāt \|*  
*hastaṃ padmaṃ samākhyātaṃ patrāṇyaṅgulayaḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. There should be four doors in order of Brahma Tirtha (shrine) and others. The head is the lotus; the fingers are fihnents.

## \|\| 9.9-10 \|\|

*karṇikā talahastantu nakhānyasya tu kesarāḥ \|*  
*tatrārcayeddhariṃ dhyātvā sūryandvagnayantareva ca \|\| 9 \|\|*

*taṃ hastaṃ pātayenmūrdhni śiṣyasya tu samāhitaḥ \|*  
*haste viṣṇuḥ sthito yasmādviṣṇuhastastatastvayam \|*  
*naśyanti sparśanāttasya pātakānyakhilāni ca \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. Then meditating there on Hari, the sun and fire, he, with a controlled mind, should place it on the head of the disciple, for in the hand is stationed Visnu, his own hand being that of Visnu, and with its touch the entire collection of sins is dissipated.

## \|\| 9.11 \|\|

*guruḥ śiṣyaṃ samabhyarcya netre baddhe tu vāsasā \|*  
*devasya pramukhaṃ kṛtvā puṣpamevārpayettataḥ \|*  
*puṣpaṃ nipatitaṃ yatra mūrdhno devasya śārṅgiṇaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Having adored the disciple, covered his eyes with a piece of cloth, and placed him in front of the deity the preceptor should throw flowers there. He should throw flowers where the head of the deity, the holder of Sharnga bow is.

## \|\| 9.12 \|\|

*tannāma kārayettasya strīṇāṃ nāmāṅkitaṃ svayam \|*  
*śūdrāṇāṃ dāsasaṃyuktaṃ kārayettu vicakṣaṇaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. He should mention his name as well as those of his wives. In the case of a 6udra, an expert preceptor should mention the name of his master.

## Chapter 10

## \|\| 10.1 \|\|

*hariruvāca \|*  
*r śyādipūjāṃ pravarśyāmi sthaṇḍilādiṣu siddhaye \|*  
*śrīṃ hrīṃ mahālakṣmyai namaḥ \|*  
*śrāṃ śrīṃ śrūṃ śraiṃ śrauṃ śraḥ kramāddhṛdayaṃ ca śiraḥ śikhām \|*  
*kavacaṃ netramastraṃ ca āsanaṃ mūrtimarcayet \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Hari said: — I will describe the adoration of Sri and other deities in Sthandilas1 for the attainment of Siddhis2. Om, Srim, salutation unto the great Laksmi. Sram. Srim, Srum, Sroum, Sr a. He should gradually worship the heart, head, the tuft of hair, amulet, the eyes, the seat and the image.

## \|\| 10.2-4 \|\|

*maṇḍale padmagarbhe ca caturdvāri rajo 'nvite \|*  
*catuḥ ṣaṣṭyantamaṣṭādi khākṣe khākṣyādi maṇḍalam \|\| 2 \|\|*

*khākṣīndusūryagaṃ sarvaṃ khādivedenduvartanāt \|*  
*lakṣmīmaṅgāni caikasminkoṇe durgāṃ gaṇaṃ gurum \|\| 3 \|\|*

*kṣetrapālamathāgnyādau homāñjuhāva kāmabhāk \|*  
*oṃ ghaṃ ṭaṃ ḍaṃ haṃ śrīmahālakṣmyai namaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

2-4. One who wishes to attain his desired-for objects should offer oblations to the Mandala, the sun, moon, Laksmi and her limbs in our comer, Durga, Gana, preceptor and Kstrapala (Visnu) in the Mandala having the figure of a lotus drawn inside it, four doors painted with dust and sixty four comers. With the mantram, "Om, Gham, Tam, Dam, Ham, salutation unto the great Laksmi" he should adore Laksmi together with all the members of the family as narrated before.

## \|\| 10.5 \|\|

*anena pūjayellakṣmīṃ pūrvoktaparivārakaiḥ \|*  
*oṃ saiṃ sarasvatyai namaḥ \|*  
*oṃ hrīṃ saiṃ sarasvatyai namaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Om, Soum, salutation unto Sarasvatl. Om, Hrim, Soun, salutation unto Sarasvatl.

## \|\| 10.6 \|\|

*oṃ hrīṃ vadavadavāgvādinisvāhā oṃ hrīṃ sarasvatyai namaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Om, Hrim, say, say. О goddess of speech, Swaha. Om, Hrim, salutation unto Sarasvati.

## Chapter 11

## \|\| 11.1 \|\|

*hariruvācaṃ \|*  
*navavyūhārcanaṃ vakṣye yaduktaṃ kaśyapāya hi \|*  
*jīvamutkṣipya mūrdhanyaṃ nābhyāṃ vyomniniveśayet \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. I will now describe the mode of adorning the nine Vyuhas as narrated unto Kasyapa. Having drawn up the vital breath through the head one should place it in the sky through the navel.

## \|\| 11.2 \|\|

*tatoramiti bījena dahedbhūtātmakaṃ vapuḥ \|*  
*yamityanena bījena tacca sarva vināśayet \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Then with the mantram Ram he should consume the body identical with the up-going vital air. And he should destroy all with the mantram Yam.

## \|\| 11.3 \|\|

*lamityanena bījena plāvayetsacarācaram \|*  
*vamityanena bījena cintayedamṛtaṃ tataḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. With the mantram Lam he should overflood the entire world mobile and immobile. Then with the mantramVam he should meditate on ambrosia.

## \|\| 11.4 \|\|

*tato budvudamadhye tu pītavāsāścaturbhujaḥ \|*  
*ahaṃ matastathātmānaṃ dhyānena paricintayet \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Thereupon by dhyana (meditation) he should think of the four-armed deity, clad in a yellow raiment, in the middle of the bubble, as well as of his bathing.

## \|\| 11.5 \|\|

*mantranyāsaṃ tataḥ kuryāttrividhaṃ karadehayoḥ \|*  
*dvādaśākṣarabījena uktabījairanantaram \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. He should next perform the three-fold mantra-nyasa3 ceremony of the fingers and body.

## \|\| 11.6 \|\|

*ṣaḍaṅgena tataḥ kuryātsākṣādyena harirbhavet \|*  
*dakṣiṇāṅguṣṭhamārabhya madhyāṅguṣṭhandale nyaset \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. After the recitation of this mantram, with one composed of twelve letters, he should make assignment of six limbs so that Hari himself might appear there.

## \|\| 11.7-8 \|\|

*madhye bījadvayaṃ nyasya nyasedaṅge tataḥ punaḥ \|*  
*hṛcchirasi śikhāvarṃmavakkrākṣyudahapṛṣṭhataḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*bāhvośca karayorjānvoḥ pādayoścāpi vinyaset \|*  
*padmākārau karau kṛtvā madhye 'ṅguṣṭhaṃ niveśayet \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. Beginning with the thumb of the right hand he should assign the middle finger to the petal. Having assigned the two BTJas in the middle he should assign them to the other limbs viz, heart, head, the crown of the head where lies the tuft of hair, mouth, eyes, belly, back, arms, hands, thighs and feet. Having converted the hand into the shape of a lotus he should place the thumb in the middle.

## \|\| 11.9 \|\|

*cintayettatra sarveśaṃ paraṃ tattvamanāmayam \|*  
*kramāccaitāni bījāni tarjanyādiṣu vinya set \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. And there he should meditate on the Lord of all, the great undecaying Principle. Then in order he should assign all the other mantrams to fore and other fingers.

## \|\| 11.10 \|\|

*tato mūrdhākṣivakkreṣu kaṇṭhe ca hṛdaye tathā \|*  
*nābhau guhye tathā jānvoḥ pādayorvinyasetkramāt \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. He should then in order make assignment of the head, eyes, mouth, throat, heart, navel, buttock, thighs and feet.

## \|\| 11.11 \|\|

*pāṇyoḥ ṣaḍaṅgabījāni nyasya kāye tato nyaset \|*  
*aṅguṣṭhādikaniṣṭhāntaṃ vinyasedvījapañcakam \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Having assigned the mantrams of six limbs or parts to the plams he should assign others to the body. He should assign the five mantrams to the five fingers beginning with the thumb and ending with the youngest.

## \|\| 11.12-13 \|\|

*karamadhye netrabījamaṅganyāsa'pyayaṃ kramaḥ \|*  
*hṛdaye hṛdayaṃ nyasya śiraḥ śirasi vinyaset \|\| 12 \|\|*

*śikhāyāṃ tu śikhāṃ nyasya kavacaṃ sarvatastanau \|*  
*netraṃ netre vidhātavyamastrañca karayordvayoḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

12-13. He should assign the mantram of the eye to the hand and then make assignment of other limbs. Having assigned heart to the heart he should assign head to the head, Shikha (tuft of hair) to the Shlkha and amulet to the entire body. Eyes should be assigned to the eyes and the weapon to the two hands.

## \|\| 11.14-15 \|\|

*tenaiva ca diśo baddhā pūjā vidhimathācaret \|*  
*hṛdaye cintayetpūrvaṃ yogapīṭhaṃ samāhitaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*dharma jñanaṃ ca vairāgyamaiśvaryaṃ ca yathākramam \|*  
*āgneyādau ca pūrvādāvadharmādīṃśca vinyaset \|\| 15 \|\|*

14-15. Having bound all the quarters with the weapon to the two hands. Having bound all the quarters with the weapon he should commence the rite of adoration. First of all with a controlled mind he should meditate on Yogapitha (the seat of yoga) in his heart, and in due order on religion, knowledge, assign iniquity etc. to the north-east and east.

## \|\| 11.16 \|\|

*ebhiḥ paricchannatanuṃ pīṭhabhūtaṃ tadātmakam \|*  
*anantaṃ vinsetpaścātpūrvakāyonnataṃ sthitam \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. The body, free of all these sins, should be then converted into FItha seat). He should afterwards assign Ananta.

## \|\| 11.17-18 \|\|

*tato vidyātsarojātaṃ dalāṣṭasamadigdalam \|*  
*sitābjaṃ śatapatrāḍhyaṃ viprakīrṇordhakarṇikam \|\| 17 \|\|*

*dhyātvā vedādinā paścātsūryasomānalātmanām \|*  
*maṇḍalāni kramādevamuparyupari cintayet \|\| 18 \|\|*

17-18. Having meditated first, by means of the Vedas etc. on learning, the eight quarters of a hundred petals covered with filaments he should meditate on Mandala identical with the sun, moon and fire and then think of the deity on one above the other.

## \|\| 11.19 \|\|

*tataḥ pūrvādidiksaṃsthāḥ śaktīḥ keśavagocarāḥ \|*  
*vimalādyā nyasedaṣṭau navamīṃ karṇikāgatām \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. He should then perform the assignment of eight energies of Kesava stationed in the east and of the ninth in the pericarp.

## \|\| 11.20 \|\|

*evaṃ dhyātvā samabhyarcya yogapīṭhamanantaram \|*  
*manasāvāhya tatreśaṃ hariṃ śārṅgaṃ nyasetpunaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Having thus meditated on and adored the Yogapitha, he should invoke the lord.thereof. Hari, the hlder of 6arnga bow and assign him there.

## \|\| 11.21-22 \|\|

*hṛdayādīni pūrvādicaturdigdalayogataḥ \|*  
*madhye netraṃ tu koṇeṣu astramantraṃ nyasettataḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*saṅkarṣaṇādibījāni pūrvādikramayogataḥ \|*  
*dvāri pūrve pare caiva vainateyaṃ tu vinyaset \|\| 22 \|\|*

21-22. He should assign heart etc. to the lotuses of the four quarters, east etc., the eye in the middle mantrams of Sankarsana and c. to the east and other quarters and Vinata's son to the eastern and western doors and the discus Sudarsana of a thousand rays to the southern gate.

## \|\| 11.23-24 \|\|

*sudarśanaṃ sahasrāraṃ dakṣiṇe dvāri vinyaset \|*  
*śriyaṃ dakṣiṇato nyasya lakṣmīmuttaratastathā \|\| 23 \|\|*

*dvāryattare gadāṃ nyasya śaṅkhaṃ koṇeṣu vinyaset \|*  
*devadakṣiṇataḥ śārṅgaṃ vāme caiva sudhīrnyaset \|\| 24 \|\|*

23-24. He should assign Sri to the south, Laksmi to the north, the club to the northern gate and the conch-shell to the corners. An intelligent worshipper should place the Sarhga bow either on the right or on the left of the deity.

## \|\| 11.25 \|\|

*tadvatkhaṅgaṃ tathā cakraṃ nyasetpārśvadvayordvayam \|*  
*tato 'ntarlokapālāṃśca svadigbhedena vinyaset \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Similarly conch-shell and discus should be placed on both the sides. According to the distinction of their respective quarters all the guardian deities thereof should be assigned.

## \|\| 11.26 \|\|

*vajrādīnyāyudhānyeva tathaiva viniveśayet \|*  
*ūrghvaṃ brihma tathānantamadhaśca paricintayet \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. In the same way the various weapons, such as thunder-bolt etc., should be assigned. He should meditate on Brahma upwards and Ananta downwards.

## \|\| 11.27 \|\|

*sarvaṃ dhyātveti saṃpūjya mudrāḥ sandarśayettataḥ \|*  
*añjaliḥ prathamā mudrā kṣipraṃ devaprasādhanī \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Having meditated on the adored them all he should display Mudra.1 Anjali (the folding of palms) is the first Mudra which speedily secures the favour of the deity.

## \|\| 11.28 \|\|

*vandanī hṛdayāsaktātsārdhaṃ dakṣiṇatonnatā \|*  
*ūrdhāṅguṇṭho vāmamuṣṭirdakṣiṇāṅguṣṭhabandhanaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Vandam the next when it is placed on the breast with the right hand raised half-way up. Urdhvangustha (thumb raised up) is formed by the clasping of the fist on the left hand with the thumb of the right hand.

## \|\| 11.29 \|\|

*savyasya tasya cāṅguṣṭho yaḥ sa uddhaḥ prakīrtitaḥ \|*  
*tisraḥ sādhāraṇā hyetā mūrtibhedena kalpitāḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. In this the thumb of the left hand should be raised up. These are the three ordinary forms arranged according to the difference of the forms of the idols.

## \|\| 11.30 \|\|

*kaniṣṭhādipramokeṇa aṣṭau mudrā yathākramam \|*  
*aṣṭānāṃ pūrvabījānāṃ kramaśastvavadhārayet \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. With the intertwining of the youngest finger eight Mudras are formed in order. These should be formed with the recitation of the first eight mantrams.

## \|\| 11.31 \|\|

*aṅguṣṭhena kaniṣṭhāntaṃ nāmayitvāṅgulitrayam \|*  
*mudreyaṃ narasiṃhasya nyubjaṃ kṛtvā karadvayam \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. With the thumb the three sucessive fingers ending with the youngest should be bent. Then the two hands should be bent. This is the Mudra of Narasithha (man-lion).

## \|\| 11.32 \|\|

*savyahastaṃ tathottānaṃ kṛtvordhaṃ bhrāmayecchanaiḥ \|*  
*navamīyaṃ smṛtā mudrā varāhābhimatā sadā \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Having raised up the left hand he should whirl it. This is the Mudra approved of Varaha (the boar-form).

## \|\| 11.33 \|\|

*muṣṭidvayamathottānamṛjvaikaikena mocayet \|*  
*utkuñcayetsarvamuktā aṅgamudreyamucyate \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Having raised up the two fists he should straighten the fingers of the one and then bend all of them. This Mudra is called Anga.

## \|\| 11.34 \|\|

*muṣṭidvayamatho baddhā evamevānupūrvaśaḥ \|*  
*daśānāṃ lokapālānāṃ mudrāśca kramayogataḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Having intertwined in order two fists the Mudras for the ten guardian deities of the quarters should be formed.

## \|\| 11.35 \|\|

*suramādyaṃ dvitīyaṃ ca upāntyañcāntyameva ca \|*  
*vāsudevo balaḥ kāmo hyaniruddho yathākramam \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. The first vowel, the second, the last but one and the last should be in order assigned to Vasudeva, Bala, Kama and Aniruddha.

## \|\| 11.36 \|\|

*praṇavastatsadityetad huṃ kṣaiṃ bhūriti mantrakāḥ \|*  
*nārāyaṇastathā brahmā viṣṇuḥ siṃho varāharāṭ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. "Om, Tatsat, Hum, Ksroum, Bhuh)" г э the mantrams for Narayana, Brahma, Visnu, the man-lion and Boar forms.

## \|\| 11.37 \|\|

*sitāruṇaharidrābhā nīlaśyāmallohitāḥ \|*  
*meghāgnimadupiṅgābhā varṇato navanāmakāḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. White, red, green, violet, blue, dark-blue, crimson, cloud-colour, fire-colour, honey- colour and twany colour are the nine names.

## \|\| 11.38-39 \|\|

*kaṃ ṭaṃ paṃ śaṃ garutmānsyājjaṃ khaṃ vaṃ ca sudarśanam \|*  
*ṣaṃ caṃ phaṃ ṣaṃ gadādevī vaṃ laṃ maṃ kṣaṃ ca śaṅkhakam \|\| 38 \|\|*

*ghaṃ ḍhaṃ bhaṃ haṃ bhavecchrīśca gaṃ jaṃ vaṃ śaṃ ca puṣṭikā \|*  
*ghaṃ vaṃ ca vanamālā syācchrī vatsaṃ daṃ saṃ bhavet \|\| 39 \|\|*

38-39. Kam, Tam, Pam, Sam, Garutman. Jam, Kham, Bam, Sudarsana. Kham, Cham, pham, Sam, the club. Vam, Lam, Mam, Ksam, conch- shell. Gham, Dham, Vam, Bham, Hain, Sri. Gam, Jam, Dam, Vam, Sam, nourishment. Dham, Vam, the garland of the forest flowers. Dam, Sam, is for the mystric mark Srivatsa.

## \|\| 11.40 \|\|

*chaṃ ḍaṃ paṃ yaṃ kaustubhaḥ proktaścānanto hyahameva ca \|*  
*ityaṅgāniyathāyogaṃ devadevasya vai daśā \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Cham, Dam, Pam, Yam is for the jewel Koustava. He should then say "I am Ananta". These are the ten limbs of the Lord of gods.

## \|\| 11.41 \|\|

*garuḍo 'mbujasaṃkāśo gadā caivāsitākṛtiḥ \|*  
*puṣṭiḥ śirīṣapuṣpābhā lakṣmīḥ kāñcanasannibhā \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Garuda is smoke-coloured. The club is white. Push (nourishment) is of the colour of a Sirisa flower. LaksmI is the gold-hued.

## \|\| 11.42 \|\|

*pūrṇacandranibhaḥ śaṅkhaḥ kaustubhastvaruṇadyutiḥ \|*  
*cakraṃ sūryasahasrābhaṃ śrīvatsaḥ kundasannibhaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. The conch-shell is effulgent like the fullmoon. Srivatsa is of the colour of a Kunda flower.

## \|\| 11.43-44 \|\|

*pañcavarṇanibhā mālā hyananto meghasannibhaḥ \|*  
*vidyudrūpāṇi cāstrāṇi yāni noktāni varṇataḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

*arghyapādyādi vai dadyātpuṇḍarīkākṣavidyayā \|\| 44 \|\|*

43-44. The garland is f five colours. Ananta is of the colour of is cloud. All the weapons described before are of the lightnings. According to the light of the science of the lotus-eyed deity one should offer Arghya, Padya (water for washing feet) etc.

## Chapter 12

## \|\| 12.1 \|\|

*hariruvāca \|*  
*pūjānukramasiddhyarthaṃ pūjānukrama ucyate \|*  
*oṃ nama ityādau saṃsmṛtiḥ paramātmanaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Hari said: I will describe the order of adoration for achieving the success thereof. The recollection of the great soul should be made with mantras,"Om, Salutation, etc."

## \|\| 12.2 \|\|

*yaṃ raṃ vaṃ lamiti kāyaśuddhiḥ \|*  
*oṃ nama iti caturbhujātmanirmāṇam \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. With the mantram "Yam, Vam, Lam, Ram" the purification of the body should be performed. With the mantram "Om salutation" the image of the four-armed deit should be made. With the three sorts of the making of idols should be made. Then follows the adoration of Yoga-pitha satione in the heart.

## \|\| 12.4 \|\|

*namaste puṇḍarīkākṣa namaste viśvabhāvana \|*  
*subrahmaṇya namaste 'stu mahāpuruṣa pūrvaja \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Salutration unto thee, О thou having lotus eyes; salutation unto thee О creator of the universe, О Subrahmanya; salutation unto thee, О great Purusa. О thou the first, born.

## \|\| 12.5-6 \|\|

*homakarṇaṇi caiteṣāṃ svāhāntamupakalpayet \|*  
*evaṃ japtvā vidhānena śatamaṣṭottaraṃ tathā \|\| 5 \|\|*

*arghaṃ dattvā jitaṃ tena praṇāmaṃ ca punaḥ punaḥ \|*  
*tato 'gnāvapi sampūjyaṃ taṃ yajeta yathāvidhi \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. In Нота rites this mantram ending with the wor.d Swaha should be recited. Having duly recited this mantram one hundred and eight times the worshipper should offer Arghya and bow unto the Deity again and again. Afterwards having worshipped the fire he should duly adore with his own mantram Acyuta the god of gods.

## \|\| 12.7-8 \|\|

*devadevaṃ svabījena aṅgādibhirathācyutam \|*  
*pūrvamullikhya cābhyukṣya praṇavena tu mantravit \|\| 7 \|\|*

*bhrāmayitvānalaṃ kuṇḍe pūjayecca śubhaiḥ phalaiḥ \|*  
*pūrvaṃ tatsakalaṃ dhyātvā maṇḍale manasā nyaset \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. Having first lighted fire, fed it and whirled it one, conversant with mantrams, should adore it in the Kunda with auspicious reslults. Having first meditated on all he should assign his mind to the Mandala.

## \|\| 12.9-10 \|\|

*vāsudevākhyatattvena hutvā cāṣṭottaraṃ śatam \|*  
*saṃkarṣaṇādibījena yajetṣaṭkaṃ tathaiva ca \|\| 9 \|\|*

*trayantrayaṃ tathāṅgānāmekaikāndikpatīṃstathā \|*  
*pūrṇāhutiṃ tathaivānte dadyātsamyagupasthitaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. Then with the Tattva called Vasudeva he should offer one hundred and eight oblations. Then with Sankarsana and other mantrams he should offer six adorations, three each time to his limbs as well as to the guardian deities of the quarters. Then is the end he should offer Purnahuti.

## \|\| 12.11 \|\|

*vāgatīte pare tattve ātmānaṃ ca layaṃ nayet \|*  
*upaviśya punarmudrāṃ darśayitvā nametpunaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Then he should immerse his own self in the great principle which is beyond the range of speech. Then taking his seat, making again Mudras he should again bow.

## \|\| 12.12 \|\|

*nityamevaṃvidhaṃ homaṃ naimitte dviguṇaṃ bhavet \|*  
*gacchagaccha paraṃ sthānaṃ yatra devo nirañjanaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. This is the daily Нота rite; the occasional one requires double the rituals.

## \|\| 12.13-14 \|\|

*gacchantu devatāḥ sarvāḥ svasthānasthitihetave \|*  
*sudarśanaḥ śrīhariśca acyutaḥ sa trivikramaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*caturbhujo vāsudevaḥ ṣaṣṭhaḥ pradyumna eva ca \|*  
*saṃkarṣaṇaḥ pūruṣo 'tha navavyūho daśātmakaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

13-14. (He should then say) "Go, go to that great region where dwells the deity who is devoid of passions. Mayall the deities repair to their respective quarters." Sudargana, Sri, Hari, Acyuta, Trivikrama (three footsteps), Caturbhuja (four-arms), Vasudeva, the sixth Pradyumma, Sankarsana, Purusa are the nine Vyuhas.

## \|\| 12.15 \|\|

*aniruddho dvādaśātmā atha ūrdhamanantakaḥ \|*  
*ete ekādibhiścakrairvijñeyā lakṣitāḥ surāḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Then comes Aniruddha and Ananta. With all these Cakras the gods are known and marked. And they are worshipped in a house along with the Raksasa and Danavas.

## \|\| 12.16 \|\|

*cakrāṅkitaiḥ pūjitaḥ syāndrṛhe rakṣetsadānaraiḥ \|*  
*oṃ cakrāya svāhā.oṃ vicakrāya svāhā.oṃ sucakrāya svāhā.oṃ mahācakrāya svāhā.oṃ mahācakrāya asurāntakṛt huṃ phaṭ oṃ huṃ sahasrāra huṃ phaṭ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Om Cakraya Swaha, am Vicakraya Swaha, am Sucakraya Swaha, Om Mahacakraya Swaha, am, the remover of the Asuras, Hum, Phat, Om, Hum of thousand flames, Hum, Phat.

## \|\| 12.17 \|\|

*dvārakācakrapūjeyaṃ gṛhe rakṣākarī śubhā \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. This adoration of the discus at the door of the house is auspicious. It gives also protection.

## Chapter 13

## \|\| 13.1 \|\|

*hariruvāca \|*  
*pravakṣyāmyadhunā hyetadvaiṣṇavaṃ pañjaraṃ śubham \|*  
*namonamaste movidaṃ cakraṃ gṛhya sudarśanam \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Hari said: — I will now describe the most auspicious mantram of Visnu called Panjara.l Salutation unto thee, О Govinda. Take up thy discus, Sudarsana.

## \|\| 13.2 \|\|

*prācyāṃ rakṣasva māṃ viṣṇo ! tvāmahaṃ śaraṇaṃ gataḥ \|*  
*gadāṃ kaumodakīṃ gṛhṇa padmanābha namo 'sta te \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. And protect me in the west, a Visnu. I have taken refuge with thee. Take up thy club KoumodakI, О lotus-na veiled deity, salutation unto thee.

## \|\| 13.3-13 \|\|

*yāmyāṃ rakṣasva māṃ viṣṇo ! tvāmahaṃ śaraṇaṃ gataḥ \|*  
*halamādāya saunande namaste puruṣottama \|\| 3 \|\|*

*pratīcyāṃ rakṣa māṃ viṣṇo ! tvāmaha śaraṇaṃ gataḥ \|*  
*musalaṃ śātanaṃ gṛhya puṇḍarīkākṣa rakṣa mām \|\| 4 \|\|*

*uttarasyāṃ jagannātha ! bhavantaṃ śaraṇaṃ gataḥ \|*  
*khaḍgamādāya carṃmātha astraśāstrādikaṃ hare ! \|\| 5 \|\|*

*namaste rakṣa rakṣoghna ! aiśānyāṃ śaraṇaṃ gataḥ \|*  
*pāñcajanyaṃ mahāśaṅkhamanughoṣyaṃ ca paṅkajam \|\| 6 \|\|*

*pragṛhya rakṣa māṃ viṣṇo āgnyeyyāṃ rakṣa sūkara \|*  
*candrasūryaṃ samāgṛhya khaḍgaṃ cāndramasaṃ tathā \|\| 7 \|\|*

*nairṛtyāṃ māṃ ca rakṣasva divyamūrte nṛkesarin \|*  
*vaijayantīṃ smapragṛhya śrīvatsaṃ kaṇṭhabhūṣaṇam \|\| 8 \|\|*

*vāyavyāṃ rakṣa māṃ deva hayagrīva namo 'stu te \|*  
*vainateyaṃ samāruhya tvantarikṣe janārdana ! \|\| 9 \|\|*

*māṃ rakṣasvājita sadā namaste 'stvaparājita \|*  
*viśālākṣaṃ samāruhya rakṣa māṃ tvaṃ rasātale \|\| 10 \|\|*

*akūpāra namastubhyaṃ mahāmīna namo 'stu pte \|*  
*karaśīrṣādyaṅgulīṣu satya tvaṃ bāhupañjaram \|\| 11 \|\|*

*kṛtvā rakṣasva māṃ viṣṇo namaste puruṣottama \|*  
*etaduktaṃ śaṅkarāya vaiṣṇavaṃ pañjaraṃ mahat \|\| 12 \|\|*

*purā rakṣārthamīśānyāḥ kātyāyanyā vṛṣadhvaja \|*  
*nāśāyāmāsa sā yena cāmarānmahiṣāsuram \|\| 13 \|\|*

3-13. Protect me in the south, О Visnu, I have taken refuge with thee. Salutation unto thee, О Purusottama. Taking up thy plugh-share Sunanda, protect me in the east, О Visnu, I have taken refuge with thee. Taking up thy mace Satana, О thou having lotus eyes, protect me in the north, О lord of the universe, I have taken refuge with thee. О Hari, taking up thy sword, leathern fence, and other weapons, protect me, О destroyer of Raksasas. I bow unto thee, I am under thy protection. Taking up thy great conch shell Pancajanya and thy lotus Anudbodha, protect me, О Visnu, О Boar, in the south-east. Taking up the sun, and moon as well as the sword Candramasu do thou protect me in the south wear, О thou of a calestial form, Oman- lion. Taking up Vaijayanti2 and 6rivatsa, the ornament of thy throat do thou protect me in the north-west, О god, О Hayagnva. I bow unto thee. О Janarddana, having ridden Vinata's son do thou protect me in the sky, О thou unvanquished by the Raksasa. I bow unto thee, О thou never defeated. Having ridden Visalaksa3 do thou protect me in the nether region, О tortoise,4 salutation unto thee. Salutation unto thee, О great fish. О truth, making thy Bahupanjaram in the hand, and fingers, do thou protect me, О Visnu. Salutation unto thee, О Purusottama. This great Visnu Panjara was thus described unto Йапкага, who again described it unto Katyayani. By this she killed the immortal Asura Mahisa.

## \|\| 13.14 \|\|

*dānavaṃ raktabījaṃ ca anyāṃśca surakaṇṭakān \|*  
*etajjapannaro bhaktyā śatrūnvijayate sadā \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. The Danava Raktabija and other thorns of the relestials. By reciting it with rever- sential faith a man always destroys his enemies.

## Chapter 14

## \|\| 14.1 \|\|

*hariruvāca \|*  
*atha yogaṃ pravakṣyāmi bhuktimuktikaraṃ param \|*  
*dhyāyibhiḥ procyate dhyeyo dhyānena harirīśvaraḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Hari said: — I will how describe the great Yoga which give emancipation and enjoyment. The Dhyayins (yogins) hold that the Lord Hari alone to be meditated on.

## \|\| 14.2 \|\|

*tacchṛṇuṣva maheśāna sarvapāpavināśanam \|*  
*viṣṇuḥ sarveśvaro 'nantaḥ ṣaḍbhirbhūparivarjitaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Therefore, listen to it, О great Isana. Visnu, the lord of all, is the destroyer of sins, without end and devoid of feet and body.

## \|\| 14.3 \|\|

*vāsudevo jagannātho brahmātmāsmyahameva hi \|*  
*dehidehasthito nityaḥ sarvadehavivarjitaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. He is Vasudeva, the lord of the universe and identical with Brahmana. Although he daily assumes various bodies he is (in south) devoid of them all.

## \|\| 14.4 \|\|

*dehadharṃmavihīnaśca kṣarākṣaravivarjitaḥ \|*  
*ṣaḍvidheṣu sthito draṣṭā śrotā ghrātā hyatīndriyaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. He is shorn of the natural functions of the body and is devoid of death and decay, stationed in the six fold objects he is seer, hearer and smeller and is (at the same time) above the reach of organs.

## \|\| 14.5 \|\|

*taddharṃmarahitaḥ sraṣṭā nāmagotravivarjitaḥ \|*  
*mantā manaḥ sthito devo manasā parivarjitaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. He is devoid of the functions of senses, the creator and has no name or family.

## \|\| 14.6 \|\|

*manodharṃmavihīnaśca vijñānaṃ jñānameva ca \|*  
*boddhā buddhisthitaḥ sākṣī sarvajño buddhivarjitaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. The deity is in the mind but does not himself possess it. He is devoid of mental faculties, discriminative knowledge and knowledge. He perceives all by intellect, is stationed it, the witness of all and omniscient; (and at the same time) he is devoid of intellect.

## \|\| 14.7 \|\|

*buddhidharṃmavihīnaśca sarvaḥ sarvagato manaḥ \|*  
*sarvaprāṇivinirmuktaḥ prāṇadharṃmavivarjitaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. He is devoid of the functions of intellect, is all, present every where, and is in the mind of all. He is freed from vital airs and is devoid of their actions.

## \|\| 14.8 \|\|

*prāṇaprāṇo mahāśānto bhayena parivarjitaḥ \|*  
*ahaṅkārādihīnaśca taddharṃmaparivarjitaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. But he is the vital principle of all creatures, of a quiescent soul and divorced from fear. He is shorn of Ahankara (egoism) and other principles and devoid of their natural actions.

## \|\| 14.9 \|\|

*tatsākṣī tanniyantā ca paramānandarūpakaḥ \|*  
*jāgratsvapnasuṣuptisthastatsākṣī tadvivarjitaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. But he is their witness, the ordainer thereof and of the form of great felicity. He is the witness of the various states of waking, dreamless sleep and dreaming sleep and himself is above them all.

## \|\| 14.10 \|\|

*turīyaḥ paramo dhātā dṛgrūpo guṇavarjitaḥ \|*  
*mukto buddho 'jaro vyāpī satya ātmāsmyahaṃ śivaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. But he is Tuny a,2 the great ordainer, of the form of the quarter and devoid of gunas (qualities). He is emancipated, enlightened, 1 undecaying, all pervading, all-auspicious and always present in self.

## \|\| 14.11 \|\|

*evaṃ ye mānavā vijñā dhyāyantīśaṃ paraṃ padam \|*  
*prāpnuyuste ca tadrūpaṃ nātra kāryā vicāraṇā \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Understanding this the men, who meditate on this great Is (God), attain to his form. There is no need of ascertaining actions in this matter.

## \|\| 14.12 \|\|

*iti dhyānaṃ samākhyātaṃ tava śaṅkara suvrata \|*  
*paṭhedya etatsatataṃ viṣṇulokaṃ sa gacchati \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. О Sankara, О thou of good vows, I have thus described the Dhyana. He, who always regads, it attains to the region of Visnu.

## Chapter 15

## \|\| 15.1 \|\|

*rudra uvāca \|*  
*saṃsārasāgarāddhorāmucyate kiṃ japanprabho \|*  
*narastanme paraṃ japyaṃ pathaya tvaṃ janārdana \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Rudra said: — О Lord, О Janarddana, do thou describe unto me the Great Being by reciting whose name a man may cross the dreadful mean of Samsara.

## \|\| 15.2-3 \|\|

*hariruvāca \|*  
*pareśvaraṃ paraṃ brahma paramātmānamavyayam \|*  
*viṣṇuṃ nāmasahasreṇa stuvanmukto bhavennaraḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*yatpa vitraṃ paraṃ japyaṃ kathayāmi vṛṣadhvaja ! \|*  
*śṛṇuṣvāvahito bhūtvā sarvapāpavināśanam \|\| 3 \|\|*

2-3. Hari said: — Reciting the thousand names of Visnu, the Demiurgus, the great Brahmana, the Absolute. Undecaying Self, a man attains to emancipation. О bull-emblemed deity, hear with fixed attention, I will describe this sacred and great object of recitation (Japa) which destroys all sins.

## \|\| 15.4 \|\|

*oṃ vāsudevo mahāviṣṇurvāmano vāsavo vasuḥ \|*  
*bālacandra nibho bālo balabhadro balādhipaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. He is Vasudeva, the great Visnu, Vamana (Dwart),2 Vasava, Vasu, effulgent like the newly risen sun, and the highly powerful Balabhadra.

## \|\| 15.5 \|\|

*balibandhanakṛdvedhā (11)vareṇyo vedavitkiviḥ \|*  
*vedakartā vedarūpo vedyo vedapariplutaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. He fettered (the Asura) Bali, is the all- knower, the worshipful knower of the Vedas and the poet. He is the creator of the Vedas, of the form of tbe Vedas, worthy of being known and filled with the Vedas.

## \|\| 15.6 \|\|

*vedāṅgavettā vedeśo(20) balādhāro balārdanaḥ \|*  
*avikāro vareśaśca varuṇo varuṇādhipaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*
