*oṃ hāṃ hīṃ hūṃ haiṃ hauṃ haḥ śivasūryāya namaḥ \|*  
*oṃ haṃ khakholkāya sūryamūrtaye namaḥ \|*  
*oṃ hrāṃ hrīṃ saḥ sūryāya namaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Then having placed near the sun he should adore him with Surya (sun) mantrams. \[It is\] Om, Ham, Him, Hum, Haim, Houm, Hah salutation onto Shiva Surya. Om, Ham salutation unto Khaholka, the form of the sun. Om, Hram, Hrim, Sah, salutation unto the sun.

## \|\| 23.8 \|\|

*daṇḍine piṅgale tvātibhūtāni ca tataḥ smaret \|*  
*agnayādau vimaleśānamārādhya paramaṃ sukham \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. In the same way \[the attendants of the sun\] Dandina and Pingala should be remembered. Then in the south-east and other comers of the mystic diagram Vimala, Isa and other powers of the sun should e adored with great felicity.

## \|\| 23.9 \|\|

*yajetpadmāṃ ca rāṃ dīptāṃ rīṃ sūkṣmāṃ rūṃ jayāṃ ca reṃ \|*  
*bhadrāṃ ca raiṃ vibhūtiṃ roṃ vimalāṃ raumamodhi (rodhi) kām \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Then he should adore Padma with the mantram Ram, Diptawith the Rim, Suksma with Rum Jaya with Rem, Bhadra with Raim, Bibhuti with Rom and Vimala with Roum.

## \|\| 23.10 \|\|

*raṃ vidyutāṃ ca pūrvādau rā (raṃ) madhye sarvatomukhīm \|*  
*arkāsanaṃ sūryamūrteṃ hrāṃ hrūṃ (hrīṃ) saḥ sūryamarcayet \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. He should adore lightnings with Ram, in the east and other quaters, Ram in the middle and Ran on all sides. He should adore the seat of the sun, the fom, of the sun itself withthe mantram "Hram, Hrum, Sah".

## \|\| 23.11 \|\|

*oṃ āṃ hṛdarkāya ca śiraḥ śikhā ca bhūrbhuvaḥ svarom \|*  
*jvālinīṃ hraṃ kavacasya cāstraṃ rājñāṃ ca dīkṣitām \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Om and am are the mantrams for the heart of the sun and his head and tuft of hair. Roum is for heaven, sky and earth. The burning mantram Hum is for the coat of mail: astram is for the initiated queen. The worshipper should adore all in the heart of the sun.

## \|\| 23.12-13 \|\|

*yajetsūryahṛdā sarvānsoṃ somaṃ maṃ ca maṅgalam \|*  
*baṃ budhaṃ bṛṃ bṛhaspatiṃ bhaṃ bhārgavaṃ śaṃ śanaiścaram \|\| 12 \|\|*

*raṃ rāhuṃ kaṃ yajetketuṃ oṃ tejaścaṇḍamarcayet \|*  
*sūryamabhyarcya cācamya kaniṣṭhāto 'ṅgakāṃnyaset \|\| 13 \|\|*

12-13. Som is the mantram for Soma, Mam for Mahgala, Bam for Budha, Brm for Brhaspati, Bham for Bhargava, Jum for 6ani and ram for Rahu. With Ram one should adore Ketu and with Om the solar disc. Having adored the sun and insed his mouth wirh water he should assign all the figers beginning with the youngest.

## \|\| 23.14 \|\|

*hāṃ hṛcchiro hūṃ śikhā haiṃ varṃma hauṃ caiva netrakam \|*  
*ho 'straṃ śaktisthitiṃ kṛtvā bhūtaśuddhiṃ punarnyaset \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Ham, Him is the mantram for the head, Hum for Shikha (tuft of hair), Haim for coat of mail, Houm for eyes and Hos for the weapon. Having thus placed the Sakti he should pertorm again the nyasa of bhuta-suddhi (purification of elements).

## \|\| 23.15-18 \|\|

*arghyapātraṃ tataḥ kṛtvā tadadbhiḥ prokṣayedyajet \|\| 15 \|\|*

*ātmānaṃ padmasaṃsthaṃ ca hauṃ śivāya tato bahiḥ \|*  
*dvāre nandimahākālau gaṅgā ca yamunātha gauḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*śrīrastraṃ vāstvadhipatiṃ brahmāṇaṃ ca gaṇaṃ gurum \|*  
*śaktyanantau yajenmadhye pūrvādau dharṃmakādikam \|\| 17 \|\|*

*adharṃmādyaṃ ca vahnyādau madhye padmasya karṇike \|*  
*vāmājyeṣṭhā ca pūrvādau raudrī kālī ca pūrṣadaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

15-18. Then making a vessel of arghya, he should sprinkle it with water and then adore the self as being stationed in the lotus, in the exterior with the mantram "Salutation unto Shiva," then Nandi and Mahakala at the gate, then Ganga, Yamuna, the goddess of speech, (the mystic mark) Shrivatsa, the presiding goddess of the land, Brahma, Gana, the preceptor. &akti and Ananta in the middle pericarp, Dharma (Ihe god of virtues and others, in the east and other sides, the god of sin (Adharma) and other in the south-east pericarp, Varna and Jyestha in the middle pericarp; Roudri, Kali and Shivasita in the easternn pericarp of the lotus of the heart.

## \|\| 23.19 \|\|

*oṃ hauṃ kalavikariṇyai balavikariṇī tataḥ \|*  
*balapramathinī sarvabhūtānāṃ damanī tataḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Then the BalavikarinI should be adored with the mantram "Om, Houm, saluation unto Kalavikarini". The goddess of strength, which subdues all creatures, should be next adored.

## \|\| 23.20 \|\|

*manonmanī yajedetāḥ paṭhimadhye śivāgrataḥ \|*  
*śivāsanaṃ mahāmūrti mūrtimadhye śivāya ca \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Then in the Pitha before Siva ManonmanI should be adored. He should then make a seat for Shiva and his great image. He should invoke the spirit of Shiva with in the image.

## \|\| 23.21-23 \|\|

*āvāhanaṃ sthāpanaṃ ca sannidhānaṃ nirodhanam \|*  
*sakalīkaraṇaṃ mudrādarśanaṃ cārghyapādyakam \|\| 21 \|\|*

*ācāmābhyaṅgamudvartaṃ snānaṃ nirṃmathanaṃ caret \|*  
*vastraṃ vilepanaṃ puṣpaṃ dhūpaṃ dīpaṃ caruṃ dadet \|\| 22 \|\|*

*ācāmaṃ mukhavāsaṃ ca tāmbūlaṃ hastaśodhanam \|*  
*chatracāmarapāvitraṃ paramīkaraṇaṃ caret \|\| 23 \|\|*

21-23. He should then peroform the rites of sthapanam (installation of the image), Sannidhana, Nirodha, Sakallkarana, Mudra, Aghya, Padya, Acama, Abhyanga, Udvarta, Snana (bathing) and Nirmahcana (rubbing) Next he should offer raiments, unguents, flowers, incense, lamps, caru (a kind of food) water for rinsing mouth, delightful habitation, betel, imbrella, chowries, and sacred thread.

## \|\| 23.24 \|\|

*rūpakpena caikāhajapo jāpyasamarpaṇam \|*  
*stutirnatirhṛdādyaiśca jñeyaṃ nāmāṅga pūjanam \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. He should then imagine the form of one God, recite his name and dedicate it to him. With eulogy, bowing and \[meditation in the\] heart this adoration of Namanga (Name and limbs) should be finished.

## \|\| 23.25-27 \|\|

*agnīśarakṣo vāyavye madhye pūrvāditantrakam \|*  
*indrādyāṃśca yajeccaṇḍaṃ tasmai nirmālyamarpayet \|\| 25 \|\|*

*guhāyātiguhyagoptā tvaṃ gṛhāṇāsmatkṛtaṃ japam \|*  
*siddhirbhavatu me deva tatprasādāttvayi sthitiḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*yatkiñcitkriyate karma sadā sukṛtaduṣkṛtam \|*  
*tanme śivapadasthasya rudra kṣapaya śaṅkara \|\| 27 \|\|*

25-27. Agnisa should be placed in the north-west. He should then adore Indra and other deities and Canda and dedicate to them offerings, saying "Thou art the mysterious of the mysterious and the protector. Do thou accept this my recitation. О god, may I, by thy favour and on thy being present here, attain succes.

## \|\| 23.28-29 \|\|

*śivo dātā śivo bhoktā śivaḥ sarvamidaṃ jagat \|*  
*śivo jayati sarvatra yaḥ śivaḥ so 'hameva ca \|\| 28 \|\|*

*yatkṛtaṃ yatkariṣyāmi tatsarvaṃ sukṛtaṃ tava(tastavam) \|*  
*tvaṃ trātā viśvanetā ca nānyonātho 'stimeśiva \|\| 29 \|\|*

28-29. O god! О thou the giver of fame! do thou destroy all my actions, good or ba whatever I have done who am of the dignity of Shiva. Siva is the giver, Siva is enjoyer and Siva is the entire universe. Siva is victorious everywhere. I am myself Siva. О Siva! thou art the saviour and the learder of the universe. Save thee I have no other lord."

## \|\| 23.30 \|\|

*athānyena prakāreṇa śivapūjāṃ vadāmyaham \|*  
*gaṇaḥ sarasvatī nandī mahākālo 'thagaṅgayā \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. i shall now describe another method of the adoration of Siva. Gana, Sarasvatl, Nandi, Mahakala, Ganga, Yamuna, and the presiding deity of the house-all these should be assigned to the eastern gate.

## \|\| 23.31-34 \|\|

*pavanāstraṃ vāstvadhipo dvāri pūrvāditastvime \|*  
*indrādyāḥ pūjanīyāśca tattvāni pṛthivī jalam \|\| 31 \|\|*

*tejo vāyurvyoma gandho rasarūpe ca śabdakaḥ \|*  
*sparśo vāk pāṇi pādaṃ ca pāyūpasthaṃ śrutitvacam \|\| 32 \|\|*

*cakṣurjihvā ghrāṇamano buddhiścāhaṃ prakṛtyapi \|*  
*pumānnāgo buddhividye kalā kālo niyatyapi \|\| 33 \|\|*

*māyā ca śuddha vidyā ca īśvaraśca sadāśivaḥ \|*  
*śaktiḥ śivaśca tāñjñātvā mukto jñānī śivo bhavet \|\| 34 \|\|*

31-34. They should be adored Indra and other deities, earth, water, fire, air, sky, smell, taste, form sound, touch, speech, hand feet, the organ of generation, ear, skin tongue, nose, mind, egoism, nature, man, anger, malice, learning, proper time, improper time, fate, illusion, pure learning, Isvara (creator) and Sadasiva, Sakti and Siva.

## \|\| 23.35-37 \|\|

*yaḥ śivaḥ sa harirbrahmā so 'haṃ brahmāsmi śaṅkara \|\| 35 \|\|*

*bhūtaśuddhiṃ pravakṣyāmi yayā śuddhaḥ śivo bhavet \|*  
*hṛtpadme sadyomantraḥ syānnivṛttiśca kalā iḍā \|\| 36 \|\|*

*piṅgalā dve ca nāḍyau tu prāṇo 'pānaśca mārutau \|*  
*indro deho brahmahetuścaturastraṃ ca maṇḍalam \|\| 37 \|\|*

35-37. Having known all these he should become wise and liberated. He who is Siva is Hari and Brahma and I am Brahman due to liberation. I shall explain the purification of elements, through which a man being purified becomes Siva. The mantra is in the lotus of the heart. The return is immediate. These two are are the Nadis, (nerves) Ida7 and Pingala.8 The two Prana and Арапа in the square Mandala (diagram) shall be the bodies of Indra and Brahma.

## \|\| 23.38-40 \|\|

*vaktreṇa lāñchitaṃ vāyumekoddhātaguṇāḥ śarāḥ \|*  
*tdṛtsthānasādṛśyarutaṃ śatakoṭipravistaram \|\| 38 \|\|*

*oṃ hrīṃ pratiṣṭhāyai hrūṃ hraḥ phaṭ \|*  
*oṃ hrīṃ hrūṃ vidyāyai hraṃ hraḥ phaṭ \|*  
*caturaśītikoṭīnāmucchrayaṃ bhūmitantrakam \|\| 39 \|\|*

*tanmadhye bhavavṛkṣaṃ ca ātmānaṃ ca vicintayet \|*  
*adhomukhīṃ tataḥ pṛthvīṃ tattacchudhdaṃ bhaveddhruvam \|\| 40 \|\|*

38-40. The mandala is marked by Vajra1 and illuminated. The arrows are the quality of single stroke. The quiver in the place of heart is spacious and contains hundred chambers. От Hrlm Pratisthdyai Hum Hah Phat; Orii Hrdm Vidyayai Hram Hah Phat. The Bhumi Tantra is Eightyfour crores in height. In its centre he shoulf contemplate the Bhavavrksa (the tree of worldly existence) and the soul. The Earth should then be thought of as with a face downwards, Then everything should be made pure.

## \|\| 23.41 \|\|

*vāmā devī pratiṣṭhā ca suṣumnā dhārikā tathā \|*  
*samānodānavaruṇā devatā viṣṇu kāraṇam \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Varna Devi is the Pratistha (base). Susumna\]2 is dharikd (the supporting prop). The deities are Samana, Udana and Varum. Visnu is the cause.

## \|\| 23.42 \|\|

*addhātāśca guṇā vedāḥ śvetaṃ dhyānaṃ tathaiva ca \|*  
*evaṃ kuryātkaṇṭhapadmamardhacandrākhyamaṇḍalam \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Udghatas (beginnings) are four timzes. The dhyana is Shveta (white). The lotus of the neck should be made thus. The mandala (diagram) shall be called Ardhachandra (Crescent moon).

## \|\| 23.43 \|\|

*padmāṅkitaṃ dviviṃśatikakoṭivistīrṇamau smaret \|*  
*caturnavatyucchrayaṃ ca ātmānaṃ ca adhomukham \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Marked by a lotus it shall extend to two hundred crores. The Atman nintyfour (times) in height shall be thought of as with face downwards.

## \|\| 23.44 \|\|

*tālusthānaṃ ca padmaṃ ca aghoro vidyayānvitaḥ \|*  
*nābhyo(ḍyo) ṣṭhayorhastijihvādhyāno nāgognidevatā \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. There are places and lotuses. The Aghora (non-terrific) shall be accompanied by learning. Ndga (Serpent) and the deity of fire are to be contemplated as the tongue of an elephant with the lips in the centre.

## \|\| 23.45 \|\|

*rudrahetustriruddhātāstriguṇā raktavarṇakam \|*  
*jvālākṛte trikoṇaṃ ca catuḥ koṭiśatāni ca \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Rudra is the cause. The Udgitha is for three times. Its colour is that of blood. It is in the form of a blaze, trainangular in shape. Its altitude and width are four hundred crores.

## \|\| 23.46-48 \|\|

*vistīrṇaṃ ca samutsedhaṃ rudratattvaṃ vicintayet \|*  
*lalāṭe vai tatpuruṣaḥ śāntiryaḥ śādvalaṃ budhāḥ (vṛṣā) \|\| 46 \|\|*

*kūrmaśca kṛkaro vāyurdeva īśvarakāraṇam \|*  
*dviruddhāto guṇau dvau ca dhūmraṣaṭkoṇamaṇḍalam \|\| 47 \|\|*

*bindvaṅkitaṃ cāṣṭakoṭivistīrṇaṃ cocchrayastathā \|*  
*caturdaśādhikaṃ koṭivāyutattvaṃ vicintayet \|\| 48 \|\|*

46-48. Rudra Tattva should should be contemplated thus. It is in the forehead that the Purusa has his Sakti, A grassy place with tortoise and partridge, О scholars. Vayu is the deity. Igvara is the cause. The Vayu Tattva should be contemplated as extending to fourteen crores. Udgitha is for two times. The mandala is haxagonal in shape called Vrsa. It is marked by a dot. The width and the altitude are eighy crores.

## \|\| 23.49 \|\|

*dvādaśati sarasije śāntya tītāstatheśvarāḥ \|*  
*kuhūśca śaṅkhinī nāḍyo devadatto dhanañjayaḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. In a lotus of twelve ends the Isvaras are beyond. Sdnti (peace) Kuhu, Sahkhini, Devadatta and Dhananjaya are Nadls,

## \|\| 23.50 \|\|

*śikhaiśānakāraṇaṃ ca sadāśiva iti smṛtaḥ \|*  
*guṇa ekastathoddhātaḥ śuddhasphaṭikavatsmaret \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. The cause is Sikhesa and Sadasiva. The Udghdta is fore once only. It should be remembered as resembling bright glass.

## \|\| 23.51 \|\|

*ṣoḍaśakoṭivistīrṇaṃ pañcaviṃśatikocchrayam \|*  
*vartulaṃ cintayevdyoma bhutaśuddhirudāhṛtā \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. The width is sixteen crores. The altitude is twenty five crores. Thus the abode should be contemplated as circular in shape. Bhuta Suddhi has been explained thus.

## \|\| 23.52 \|\|

*guṇayo gururbojaguruḥ śaktayanantau ca dharṃmakaḥ \|*  
*jñānavairāgyamaiśvaryaistataḥ pūrvādipatrake \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. Ganaguru, Bijaguru, Sakti, Atlanta, Dharmaka, Jnana, Vairagya, Aisvarya — all these are in the petals beginning with that in the east.

## \|\| 23.53 \|\|

*adhordhvavadane dve ca padmakarṇikakesaram \|*  
*vāmādyā ātmavidyā ca sadā dhyāyecchivākhyakam \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Both of them are prone-faced and supinefaced. The pericarp and filaments of the lotus are contemplated. One should always contemplate the Atmavidya (study of soul) and those others beginning with Vama.

## \|\| 23.54 \|\|

*tattvaṃ śivāsane mūrtirhe hauṃ vidyādehāya namaḥ \|*  
*baddhapadmāsanāsīnaḥ sitaḥ ṣoḍaśavārṣikaḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. The Tattva named Siva should be thought of in the seat of Shiva. The Murti is Ho Haum. Obeisance to Vidyadeha. Lord Shiva is seated in the pose Padmasana, white in colour and sixteen years old.

## \|\| 23.55 \|\|

*pañcavaktraḥ karāgraiḥ svairdaśabhiścaiva dhārayan \|*  
*abhayaṃ prasādaṃ śaktiṃ śūlaṃ khaṭvāṅgamīśvaraḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. He has five faces. Of his ten hands, the five on the right carry Abhaya, Prasada, Sakti, Sula (trident) and Khalvahga.

## \|\| 23.56 \|\|

*dakṣaiḥ karairvāmakaiśca bhujaṅgaṃ cākṣasūtrakam \|*  
*ḍamarukaṃ nīlotpalaṃ bījapūrakamuttamam \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. And the left ones carry Serpent, Akssutra drums, blue lotus and the pomegrate.

## \|\| 23.57 \|\|

*icchājñānakriyāśaktistrinetro hi sadāśivaḥ \|*  
*evaṃ śivārcanadhyānī sarvadā kālavarjitaḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Sadasiva is three-eyed. He has iccha sakti (will-power), Jnanasakti (knowledge-power), and Kriyasakti (Action-power). A person who worships Siva like this and contemplates thus will be devoid of Kala (become deathless).

## \|\| 23.58 \|\|

*ihāhorā vacāreṇa trīṇi varṣāṇi jīvati \|*  
*dinadvayasya cāreṇa jīvedvarṣadvayaṃ naraḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. If one circle of worship is completed in a day and night, the worshipper shall live for three years, if in two days, he shall live for two years.

## \|\| 23.59 \|\|

*dinatrayasya cāreṇa varṣamekaṃ sa jīvati \|*  
*nākāle śītale mṛtyuruṣṇe caiva tu kārake \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. If in three days he shall live for one year. He will never have premature death or death due to cold or heat.

## Chapter 24

## \|\| 24.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*vakṣye gaṇādikāḥ pūjāḥ sarvadā svargadāḥ parāḥ \|*  
*gaṇāsanaṃ gaṇamūrti gaṇādhipatimarcayet \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Suta said: I will now describe the most excellent adoration of Ganas1 which gives all and even heaven. The worshipper should adore the seats of Ganas, the images of Ganas and the lord of Ganas.

## \|\| 24.2 \|\|

*gāmādihṛdayādyaṅgaṃ durgāyā gurupādukāḥ \|*  
*durgāsanaṃ ca tanmūrtiṃ hrīṃ durge rakṣaṇīti ca \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Heart and other limbs shold be assigned to Druga. The sandals of the preceptor, the seat of Druga and her image should be adored with the mantram: — "Hrim, О Durga, protect."

## \|\| 24.3-4 \|\|

*tdṛdādikaṃ nava śaktyo rudracaṇḍā pracaṇḍayā \|*  
*caṇḍogrā caṇḍanāyikā caṇḍā caṇḍavatī kramāt \|\| 3 \|\|*

*caṇārūpā caṇḍikākhyā durgedurge 'tha rakṣiṇi \|*  
*vajrakhaḍgādikā mudrāḥ śivādyā vahnideśataḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

3-4. Then assignment should be made to the eight Saktis, called Candikas, viz Rudracanda, Pracanda, Candogra, Candanayika, Canda, Candavati and Candarupa with the mantram О Durga, О Durga, О protectress. Then Vajra, Khadga and other Mudras of Siva should be adored in the south-east.

## \|\| 24.5 \|\|

*sadāśivamahāpretapadmāsana mathāpi vā \|*  
*aiṃ klīṃ (hrīṃ) saustripurāyai namaḥ \|*  
*oṃ hrāṃ hrīṃ kṣeṃ kṣaiṃ strīṃ skīṃ roṃ spheṃ sphīṃ śāṃ padmāsanaṃ ca mūrtiṃ ca tripurātdṛdayādikam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Then Sadasiva the lord of goblins and the lotus seat \[should be adored.\] Em, Klim, salutation unto Sonstripura. Om, Hram, Hrim, Ksem, Ksaim, Strim, Skom, Rom, Sphem, Sphom, the lotus seat and the heart etc. of Tripura.

## \|\| 24.6-10 \|\|

*pīṭhāmbuje tu brāhayādīrbrahmāṇī ca maheśvarī \|*  
*kaumārī vaiṣṇavī pūjyā vārāhī cendradevatā \|\| 6 \|\|*

*cāmuṇḍā caṇḍikā pūjyā bhairavākhyāṃstato yajet \|*  
*asitāṅgoruruścaṇḍaḥ krodha unmattabhairavaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*kapālī bhīṣaṇaścaiva saṃhāraścāṣṭa bhairavāḥ \|*  
*ratiḥ prītiḥ kāmadevaḥ pañca bāṇāśca yoginī \|\| 8 \|\|*

*vaṭukaṃ durgayā vighnarājo guruśca kṣetrapaḥ \|*  
*padmagarbhe maṇḍale ca trikoṇe cintayeddhṛdi \|\| 9 \|\|*

*śuklāṃ varadākṣasūtrapustābhayasamanvitām \|*  
*lakṣajapyācca homācca tripurā siddhidā bhavet \|\| 10 \|\|*

6-10. Then in the lotus pTtha (altar) should be adored BrahmanI, Mahesvari, Koumarl, Vaisnavi, Indradevata Camunda and Candika. Then the Bhairavas should be adored. Asitanga, Ruru, Canda, Krodha, Unmatabhairava, Kapall, Bhlsana, and Samhara, are the eight Bhairavas. He should meditate in his heart, in a mandala (diagram) with a lotus inside in and having three corners, on Rati, Prlti, Kamadeva, the five arrows, Yoginl, Valuka, Durga, Vighnaraja, Guru (preceptor) and Ksatrapa. By reciting this mantram for a lac of times and by offering oblations to the fire Tripura gives Siddhi.

## Chapter 25

## \|\| 25.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*

1\. Suta said: — Em, Krlm, Srim, Sphem Ksoum, I adore the paduka (shoe), of Aannta Sakti.

*oṃ hraṃ kālāgnirudrapādukāṃ pūjayāmi namaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Em, Hrim, Srim Phrom, Ksoum, I adore the Paduka of Adhara-shakti, salutation.

## \|\| 25.3 \|\|

*oṃ hrīṃ huṃ hāṭakeśvaradevapādukāṃ pūjayāmi namaḥ \|*  
*oṃ hrīṃ śeṣabhaṭṭārakapādukāṃ pūjayāmi namaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Om, Hrim, I dore the Paduka of Katagni Rudra, salutation, Om, Hrim, Hum, I adore the Paduka of Hatakesvara, salutation.

## \|\| 25.4 \|\|

*oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ pūthivītatsavarṇabhuvanadvīpasamudradiśāmanantākhyamāsanaṃ padmāsanaṃ pūjayāmi namaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Om, Hrim, $rim, I adore the seat called Ananta, having the earth, insular continents and the oceans on all sides, salutation.

## \|\| 25.5 \|\|

*hrīṃ śrīṃ nivṛttyādi kalā pṛthivyāditattva manantādibhuvanamoṅkārādivarṇam \|*  
*hakārādinavātmakapadaḥ sadyodātādimantraḥ hrāṃ hṛdayādyaṅgaḥ \|*  
*evaṃ mantramaheśvara siddhavidyātmakaḥ parāmṛtārṇavaḥ sarvabhūto diksamastaṣaḍaṅgaḥ sadāśivārṇavapayaḥ pūrṇodadhipakṣaśrīmānāspadātmakaḥ vidyomāpūrṇajñatvakartṛtvalakṣaṇajyeṣṭhācakrarudraśaktyātmakakarṇi kaḥ \|*  
*navaśaktiśivādibhirmūlamaṇḍalatrayakujātmakotpannāpadmāsanapādukāṃ pūjayāmi namaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Hrim, Srlm, Nivrtti and other Kalas. Earth and other elements. Ananta and other worlds. Omkar and other letters. The nine syllables Hakara etc. Sadyajata and other Mantrams. Ham, the heart and other limbs. This is the mantram of Mahesvara. It is identical with the most consummate learning and it the ocean of great ambrosia.

Lam salutation unto the soles of the hands. Vam, salutation unto the back of hands,

2\. Then Deha (body) Nyasa. Kam, salutation unto Manivandha. Em, Hrim, Shrim, salutation unto Karaskara. He should consecrate the hands with Hum Hum, effulgent like the great fire.

## Chapter 27

## Chapter 28

## \|\| 28.1-2 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*gopālapūjāṃ vakṣyāmi bhuktimuktipradāyinīm \|*  
*dvāre dhātā vidhātā ca gaṅgāyamunayā saha \|\| 1 \|\|*

*śaṅkhapadmanidhī caiva sāraṅgaḥ śarabhaḥ śriyā \|*  
*pūrve bhadraḥ subhadro dvau dakṣe caṇḍapracaṇḍakau \|\| 2 \|\|*

1-2. Suta said: — I will now describe the adoration of Gopala which yeilds emancipation and enjoyment. In the door Dhata, Vidhata, Ganga with Yamuna, the Nidhis 6ankha and Padma, Sarahga, 6arabha and Shri should be adored. In the east should be adored Bhadra and Subhadra, in the south Canda and Pracanda.

## \|\| 28.3 \|\|

*paścime balaprabalau jayaśca vijayo yajet \|*  
*uttare śrīścaturdvāre gaṇo durgā sarasvatī \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. In the west Vala, and Pravala and Jaya and Vijaya in the north. In the four doors Sri, Gana? Durga and Sarasvatl should be adored.

## \|\| 28.4 \|\|

*kṣetrasyāgnyādikoṇeṣu dikṣu nāradapūrvakam \|*  
*siddho gururnalakūvaraṃ koṇe bhagavataṃ yajet \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. In the south-east and other corners of the field Narada, Siddhas, the preceptor, Nalakuvara should be adored.

## \|\| 28.5-6 \|\|

*pūrve viṣṇuṃ viṣṇutapo viṣṇuśaktiṃ samarcayet \|*  
*tato viṣṇuparīvāraṃ madhye śaktiṃ ca kūrṃmakam \|\| 5 \|\|*

*anantaṃ pṛthivīṃ dharmaṃ jñānaṃ vairāgyamagnitaḥ \|*  
*aiśvaryaṃ vāyupūrvaṃ ca prakāśātmānamuttare \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. In the east the worshipper should adore Visnu, his ascetcism and power. Then in the middle he should adore the family of Visnu, the 6aktis, the tortoise, Ananta, earth, religion, knowledge and disassociation from the world. He should adore prosperity in the south-east and the manifest self in the north.

## \|\| 28.7 \|\|

*sattvāya prakṛtātmane rajase moharūpiṇe \|*  
*tamase kanda padmāya yajetkaṃ kākatattvakam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. He should then adore the Sattva guna identical with Prakrti (nature), and Rajas identical with Moha (stupefaction) and Tamas, the lotus and the principle of egoism, learning, the great principle and the solar and lunar discs.

## \|\| 28.8-9 \|\|

*vidyātattvaṃ paraṃ tattva sūryeduvahnimaṇḍalam \|*  
*vimalādyā āsanaṃ ca prācyāṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ prapūjayet \|\| 8 \|\|*

*gopījanavallabhāya svāhānto manurucyate \|*  
*aṅgāni yathā-āca kraṃ ca sucakraṃ ca vicakraṃ ca tathaica \|\| 9 \|\|*

8-9. Then in the east he should adore Vimala and other seats with the man trams 6rlm, Hrlm, salutation unto the dearest lord of milik-men, Svaha. This is the mantram. In the eastern corners of the diagrm of the heart he should adore his weapons viz Acakra, Sucakra, Vicakra, the discus Sudarsana, which protects the three worlds and destroys the Asuras.

## \|\| 28.10-11 \|\|

*trailokyarakṣakaṃ cakramasurārisudarśanam \|*  
*hṛdādipūrvakoṇaṣu astraṃ śaktiṃ ca pūrvataḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*rukmiṇī satyabhāmā ca sunandā nāgnajityapi \|*  
*lakṣmaṇā mitravindā ca jāmbavatyā śuśīlayā \|\| 11 \|\|*

10-11. Then in the east he should adore the Shaktis namely Rukmini, Satyabhama, Sunanda, Nagnajitl, Laksmana, Mitravrnda, Jambavati and Susita.

## \|\| 28.12 \|\|

*śaṅkhacakragadāpadmaṃ musalaṃ śārṅgamarcayet \|*  
*khaṅgaṃ pāśāṅkuśaṃ prācyāṃ śrīvatsaṃ kaustubhaṃ yajet \|*  
*mukuṭaṃ valamālāṃ ca aindrādyāndhvajamukhyakān \|*  
*kumudādyānviṣvaksenaṃ śriyā kṛṣṇaṃ sahārcayet \|*  
*japyāddhyānātpūjanācca sarvānkāmānavānpuyāt \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Then in the east he should also adore his conch shell, discus, club, lotus, mace, the Sarnga bow, sword, noose, goad, the mystic mark 6rivatsa, and the jewel Koustabha. He should then adore his crown, garland of wild flowers, his Indra and other flags, Kumudas, Visvaksena and Krsna along with 6rya. By reciting his name and adoring him one attains all desired for objects.

## Chapter 29

## \|\| 29.1 \|\|

*hariruvāca \|*  
*trailokyamohinīṃ vakṣye puruṣottamamukhyakām \|*

1\. Hari said: — I will now describe the Trailokyamohini rite (fascinating the three worlds) of the foremost of male beings, its adoration and the mantram called Shrldhara which yeilds religious profit, desire and wives.

## \|\| 29.2 \|\|

*oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ hrūṃ oṃ namaḥ \|*  
*puruṣottama apratirūpa lakṣmīnivāsa jagatkṣobhaṇa sarvastrīhṛdayadāraṇa tribhuvanamadonmādanakara surāsuramanuja suṃdarī janamanāṃsi tāpayatāpaya śoṣayaśoṣaya mārayamāraya stambhayastambhaya drāvayadrāvaya ākarṣaya ākarṣaya.paramasubhaga sarvasaubhāgyakara sarvakāmaprada amukaṃ hanahana cakreṇa gadayā khaḍgena sarvabāṇairbhidhibhindhi pāśena kuṭṭakuṭṭa aṅkuśena tāḍayatāḍaya turuturu kiṃ tiṣṭhasi tārayatāraya yāvatsamīhitaṃ me siddhaṃ bhavati hrīṃ (hrūṃ) phaṭ namaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Ош, Hrim, Shrim, Klim, Hum, От, Namah: О foremost of male-beings! О thou of an incomparable form! О thou the abode of the goddess of prosperity! О thou the agitator of the entire universe! О thou who rivest the hearts of all women! О thou who maddenst the three worlds! Distress the hearts of all beautiful women amongst me celestials and Asuras; dry them up, strike them, check them, melt them and attract memory of great auspiciousness! О thou of good luck! О thou the giver of all desired for object! destroy such and such person with thy discus, club or sword. Cut him with all thy weapons, strike him with thy goad, inflict him. Why dost thou wait. Save me, save me, so long my Siddhi is not perfected. Hum, phat salutation.

## \|\| 29.3 \|\|

*oṃ śrīṃ (śrīḥ) śrīdharāya trailokyamohanāya namaḥ \|*  
*klīṃ puruṣottamāya trailokyamohanāya namaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Srim, salutation unto the holder of Sri and the enchanter of the three worlds. Klim, salutation unto the foremost of male beings, the enchanter of the three worlds.

## \|\| 29.4 \|\|

*oṃ viṣṇave trailokyamohanāya namaḥ \|*  
*oṃ śrīṃ klīṃ trailokyamohanāya vipṇave namaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Hum, salutation unto' Visnu, the enchanter of the three worlds. Om, 6rlm, Hrim, Klim, salutation unto Visnu, the enchanter of the three worlds.

## \|\| 29.5 \|\|

*trailokyamohanā mantrāḥ sarve sarvārthasādhakāḥ \|*  
*sarve cintyā pṛthag vāpi vyāsātsaṃkṣepato 'tha vā \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. All the Trailokyamohana mantrams are capable of securing the accomplishment of all objects. They may be meditated upon again separately and in brief.

## \|\| 29.6-7 \|\|

*āsanaṃ mūrtimantraṃ ca homādyaṅgaṣaḍaṅgakam \|*  
*cakraṃ gadāṃ ca khaḍgaṃ ca musalaṃ śaṃmakhaśarṅgakam \|\| 6 \|\|*

*śaraṃ pāśaṃ cāṅkuśaṃ ca lakṣmīgaruḍasaṃyutam \|*  
*viṣvaksenaṃ vistarādvānaraḥ sarvamavāpnuyāt \|\| 7 \|\|*

6-7. Having adored with mantrams me seat, the image, the six limbs, discus, club, sword, mace, conch-shell, the Sarnga, arrow, noose, goad, Laksmi, Garuda and Visvaksena one attains ot all.

Hear, hear, О Rudra. I will describe the principal mantram of the deity.

*hariruvāca \|*

4-6. Vasudeva is one, undecaying, peaceful, the great soul, eternal, unstained, a god, by his Maya (illusive power) Hari exists in five forms, viz. as Visnu who favours the creation and destroys rhe wicked, as Vasudeva, Sankarsana, Pradyumna and Aniruddha. in his own torm Narayana exists as five.

*ete mantrāḥ samākhyātāstava rudra samāsataḥ \|*

## \|\| 32.20-21 \|\|

*oṃ padmāya namaḥ \|*

20-21. Having made the assignment of limbs the worshipper should show all the Mudras. Having meditated as the self. Vasudeva and the Great Isvara a man should first worship the seat and then invoke the spirit. О owl-emblemed dity, Dhatri and Vidhatri should be adored in the door.

*garuḍaṃ pūjayedagre vāsudevasya śaṅkara \|*

*āvāhya maṇḍale devaṃ kṛtvā nyāsaṃ tu tasya ca \|*

## \|\| 32.29 \|\|

*snānaṃ vastraṃ tathācāmaṃ gandhaṃ puṣpaṃ ca dhūpakam \|*

*daṃ stotraṃ japetpaścādvāsudevamanusmaran \|*

*pradyumnāyādidevāyāniruddhāya namonamaḥ \|*

## \|\| 32.32 \|\|

*narapūjyāya kīrtyāya stutyāya varadāya ca \|*

32\. Salutation unto the lord of men. Salutation unto him who is adored by men, whose glories are described and sung by them, and who gives boons. Salutation unto the ancient who is without beginning and destruction.

## \|\| 32.33 \|\|

*sṛṣṭisaṃhārakartre ca brahmaṇaḥ pataye namaḥ \|*

## \|\| 32.34 \|\|

*kalikalmaṣahartre ca sureśāya namonamaḥ \|*

## \|\| 32.35 \|\|

*vahurūpāya tīrthāya triguṇāyāguṇāya ca \|*

## \|\| 32.36 \|\|

*mokṣadvārāya dharmāya nirmāṇāya namonamaḥ \|*

## \|\| 32.37 \|\|

*saṃsārasāgare ghore nimagnaṃ māṃ samuddhara \|*

37\. Do thou save me who am immersed in the dreadful deep of Sarhsara. O, lord of celestials! О lord of the universe! save thee there is no other saviour.

## \|\| 32.38 \|\|

*tvāmava sarvagaṃ viṣṇuṃ gato 'haṃ śaraṇaṃ gataḥ \|*  
*jñānadīpapradānena tamomuktaṃ prakāśaya \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. I seek refuge with thee, О Visnu! О thou omnipresent! By giving me the lamp of knowledge, do thou make me freed of ignorance.

## \|\| 32.39-40 \|\|

*evaṃ stuvīta deveśaṃ sarvakleśavināśanam \|*

*pañcatattvasamāyuktaṃ dhyāyodviṣṇuṃ naro hṛdi \|*  
*visarjayattatā devamiti pūjā prakīrtitā \|\| 40 \|\|*

39-40. This is the hymn of the king of gods dfructive of all sorts of afflictions. (Having chanted his glories with other Vedic hymns, О blue-throated deity!a man should meditate in his heart on Visnu with the five Tattvas. Afterwards he should, throwaway the image of the deity.

## \|\| 32.41 \|\|

*sarvakāmapradā śreṣṭhā vāsudevasya śaṅkara \|*  
*etatpūjanamātreṇa kṛtakṛtyo bhavennaraḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Thus, О Sankara, the most excellent adoration of Vasudeva is described which yields all desired-for objects. By offering this adoration a man becomes successful in all his objects.

## \|\| 32.42 \|\|

*idaṃ ca yaḥ paṭhedrudra pañcatattvārcanaṃ naraḥ \|*

42\. The man, who reads this adoration of the five Tattvas, who listens to it or makes others listen to it, repairs to the region of Visnu.

## \|\| 34.25 \|\|

*praṇavādyairnamo 'ntaiśca caturthyantaiśca nāmabhiḥ \|*  
*mantrairebhirmahādeva āsanaṃ paripūjayet \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. With the mantrams formed of their names in the dative form beginning with Pranava and ending with Names the worshipper, О Mahadeva, should adore the seat.

## \|\| 34.26 \|\|

*snānagandhapradānena puṣpadhūpapradānataḥ \|*  
*dīpanaivedyadānena āsanasyārcanaṃ śubham \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. The most auspicious adoration of the seat should be made with the offerings of bathing water, scents, flowers, incense, lamps and edibles.

## \|\| 34.27 \|\|

*kartavyaṃ vidhinānena iti te hara kīrtitam \|*  
*tataścāvāhayeddevaṃ hayagrīvaṃ sureśvaram \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. I have thus described the prescription, О Нага. He should next invoke the deity, Hayagrlva, the king of the celestials.

## \|\| 34.28-29 \|\|

*vāmanāsāpuṭenaiva āgacchantaṃ vicintayet \|*  
*āgacchataḥ prayogeṇa mūlamantreṇa śaṅkara \|\| 28 \|\|*

*āvāhanaṃ prakartavyaṃ devadevasya śaṅkhinaḥ \|*  
*āvāhyamaṇḍale tasya nyāsaṃ kuryādatandritaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

28-29. He should think of his arrival through the left nostril. The invocation rite of the god of gods, the holder of conch-shell, should be Having invoked his spirit in the mystic diagram a careful worshipper should perform the rite of Nyasa.

## \|\| 34.30 \|\|

*nyāsaṃ kṛtvā ca tatrasthaṃ cintayetparameśvaram \|*  
*hayagrīvaṃ mahādevaṃ surāsuranamaskṛtam \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Having performed the Nyasa he should meditate on the Great Kvara as being stationed there-the great deity Hayagrlva, adored of the celestials and Asuras.

## \|\| 34.31 \|\|

*indrādilokapālaiśca saṃyuktaṃ viṣṇumavyayam \|*  
*dyātvā pradarśayenmudrāḥ śaṅkhacakrādikāḥ śubhāḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Having meditated on the imdecaying Vi$nu accompanied by Indra and other guardian deities of the quarters he should make the Mudra Shankha, Cakra and others.

## \|\| 34.32 \|\|

*pādyārghyācamanīyāni tato dadyācca viṣṇave \|*  
*snāpayecca tato devaṃ padmanābhamanāmayam \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. He should next offer unto Visnu water for washing feet, Arghya and water for rinsing mouth. Then he should bathe the changeless, lotusmavelled deity.

## \|\| 34.33 \|\|

*devaṃ saṃsthāpya vidhivadvastraṃ dadyādvṛṣadhvaja \|*  
*tato hyācamanaṃ dadyādupavītaṃ tataḥ śubham \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Having duly placed the image of the deity, he should first dedicate to him, raiment, О bull- emblemed deity, then water for rinsing mouth and sacred thread.

## \|\| 34.34-35 \|\|

*tataśca maṇḍale rudra dhyāyeddevaṃ pareśvaram \|*  
*dhyātvā pādyādikaṃ bhūyo dadyāddevāya śaṅkara \|\| 34 \|\|*

*dadyādbhairavadevāya mūlamantreṇa śaṅkara \|*  
*oṃ kṣāṃ hṛdayāya namaḥ anena hṛdayaṃ yajet \|\| 35 \|\|*

34-35. Thereupon in the mystic diagram, О Rudra, he should meditate on the Great Isvara. Having meditated on him, О Sankara, he should again offer unto him water for washing feet and other articles, He should offer these with the principal mantram, О Йапкага. With mantram "Om, Ksam, salutation unto, the heart" he should adore the heart.

## \|\| 34.36 \|\|

*oṃ kṣīṃ śirase namaśca śirasaḥ pūjanaṃ bhavet \|*  
*oṃ kṣūṃ śikhāyai namaśca śikhāmetena pūjayet \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. With the mantram "Om, Kslm, salutation unto the head/' he should adore the head. With the mantram "Om Ksum, salutation unto the tuft of hair", he should adore &ikha.

## \|\| 34.37 \|\|

*oṃ kṣaiṃ kavacāya namaḥ kavacaṃ paripūjayet \|*  
*oṃ kṣaiṃ netrāya namaśca netraṃ cānena pūjayet \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. With mantram om saim, solutation unto the coat of manl. With the mantram "Om, Ksoum, salutation unto the eye" he should adore the eye.

## \|\| 34.38-39 \|\|

*oṃ kṣaḥ astrāya nama iti astraṃ cānena pūjayet \|*  
*hṛdayaṃ ca śiraścaiva śikhāṃ ca kavacaṃ tathā \|\| 38 \|\|*

*pūrvādiṣu pradeśeṣu hyetāstu paripūjayet \|*  
*koṇeṣvastraṃ yajedrudra netraṃ madhyai prapūjayet \|\| 39 \|\|*

38-39. With the mantram "Om, Ksah, salutation unto the weapon" he should adore the weapon. In the eastern and other sides he should adore the heart, the heart, the tuft of hair and the coat of mail. О Rudra, in the corner of the diagram he should adore the weapon and the eye in the centre.

## \|\| 34.40 \|\|

*pūjayetparamāṃ devīṃ lakṣmīṃ lakṣmīpradāṃ śubhām \|*  
*śaṅkhaṃ padmaṃ tathā cakraṃ gadāṃ pūrvāditor'cayet \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. In the eastern side he should adore the conch-shell, the lotus, the discus and the club.

## \|\| 34.41 \|\|

*khaḍgaṃ ca musalaṃ pāśamaṅkuśaṃ saśaraṃ dhanuḥ \|*  
*pūjayetpūrvato rudra ebhirmantraiḥ svanāmakaiḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. О Rudra, again in the eastern side with those mantrams describing their names, he should adore the sword, mace, noose, and the bow with the arrows.

## \|\| 34.42 \|\|

*śrīvatsaṃ kaustubhaṃ mālāṃ tathā pītāmbaraṃ śubham \|*  
*pūjayetpūrvato rudra śaṅkhacakragadādharam \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. О Rudra, he should next adore in the east, the mystic mark Shrivatsa, Koustabha, garland, the sacred yellow raiment ass well as the holder of conch-shell, discus and club.

## \|\| 34.43-44 \|\|

*brahmāṇaṃ nāradaṃ siddhaṃ guruṃ paraguruṃ tathā \|*  
*gurośca pāduke tadvatparamasya gurostathā \|\| 43 \|\|*

*indraṃ savāhanaṃ cātha parivārayutaṃ tathā \|*  
*agniṃ yamaṃ nirṛtiṃ ca varuṇaṃ vāyumeva ca \|\| 44 \|\|*

43-44. He should next adore Brahma, Narada, Siddhas, the great preceptor, the shoes of the preceptor, those of the great preceptor, Indra, his carrier and the entire family, Agni, Yama, Nirrti, Varuna, Vayu,

## \|\| 34.45 \|\|

*somamīśānamevaṃ vai brahmāṇaṃ paripūjayet \|*  
*pūrvādikordhvaparyantaṃ pūjayedvṛṣabhadhvaja \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Soma, Tsana, and Nagas, from the east upwards, О bull emblemed deity.

## \|\| 34.46 \|\|

*vajraṃ śaktiṃ tathā daṇḍaṃ khaṅgaṃ pāśaṃ dhvajaṃ gadām \|*  
*triśūlaṃ cakrapadme ca āyudhānyatha pūjayet \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. He should next adore thunderbolt, 6akti, rod, sword, noose, standard, club, trident, discus, lotus and other weapons.

## \|\| 34.47 \|\|

*viṣvaksenaṃ tato devamaiśānyāṃ diśi pūjayet \|*  
*ebhirmantrairnamo 'ntaiśca praṇavādyairvṛṣadhvaja \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. In the north-east corne; he should worship Visvaksena, with these mantrams beginning with Om and ending with Namah (salutation) О bull-emblemed deity.

## \|\| 34.48 \|\|

*pūjā kāryā mahādeva hyanantasya vṛṣadhvaja \|*  
*devasya mūlamantreṇa pūjā kāryā vṛṣadhvaja \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. О Mahadeva, О bull-emblemed deity, adoration of the deity Ananta should be made with the principal mantram.

## \|\| 34.49 \|\|

*gandhaṃ puṣpaṃ tathā dhūpaṃ dīpaṃ naivedyameva ca \|*  
*pradakṣiṇaṃ namaskāraṃ japyaṃ tasmai samarpayet \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. He should next offer scents, flowers, incense, lamps, and edibles. He should circumambulate the deity, bow unto him and recite his name.

## \|\| 34.50 \|\|

*stuvīta cānyā stutyā praṇavādyairvṛṣadhvaja \|*  
*oṃ namo hayaśirase vidyādhyakṣāya vai namaḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. With the following hymn beginning with am he. should chant his glories, О bull-emblemed deity. Om. Namah, salutation into Hayasira, the master of learning.

## \|\| 34.51-52 \|\|

*namo vidyāsvarūpāya vidyādātre namonamaḥ \|*  
*namaḥ śāntāya devāya triguṇāyātmane namaḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

*surāsuranihantre ca sarvaduṣṭavināśine \|*  
*sarvalokādhipataye brahmarūpāya vai namaḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

51-52. Salutation again and again unto him of the from of learning, and the giver of the same. Salutation unto the deity of a quiescent soul, identical with three gunas, the destroyer of the celestials and Asuras and of all wicked beings. Salutation unto him of the from of Brahmana, the lord of all the worlds.

## \|\| 34.53-54 \|\|

*namaśceśvaravandyāya śaṅkacakradhāraya ca \|*  
*nama ādyāya dāntāya sarvasattvahitāya ca \|\| 53 \|\|*

*triguṇāyāguṇāyaiva brahmaviṣṇusvarūpiṇe \|*  
*kartre hartre sureśāya sarvagāya namonamaḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

53-54. Salutation unto him adored of Isvara, the holder of conchshell and discus. Salutation unto the first cause, who is self-controlled, devoted to the well-being of all creatures, invested with three gunas, devoid of them, identical with Brahma and Visnu, the creator, destroyer, the king of the celestials and present everywhere.

## \|\| 34.55-56 \|\|

*ityevaṃ saṃstavaṃ kṛtvā devadevaṃ vicintayet \|*  
*hṛtpadme vimale rudra śaṅkhacakragadādharam \|\| 55 \|\|*

*sūryakoṭipratīkāśaṃ sarvāvayavasundaram \|*  
*hayagrīvomahīśeśaṃ paramātmānamavyayam \|\| 56 \|\|*

55-56. Having recited this hymn, О Rudra, a worshipper should meditate in his pure lotus of the heart, on the god of gods, the holder of conchshell, discus and club, effeulgent like a million suns, perfectly beautiful Hayagrlva, the undecaying impersonal self.

## \|\| 34.57 \|\|

*iti te kathitā pūjā hayagrīvasya śaṅkara \|*  
*yaḥ paṭhetparayā bhaktyā sa gacchetparamaṃ padam \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. О Sankara, I have thus described unto thee the adoration of Hayargriva. He, who reads it with great reverence, attains to the most exalted station.

## Chapter 35

## \|\| 35.1 \|\|

*hariruvāca \|*  
*nyāsādikaṃ pravakṣyāmi gāyattryāḥ śṛṇu śaṅkara \|*  
*viśvāmitraṛṣiścaiva savitā cātha devatā \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Hari said: — I will now describe the nyasa and the metre of Gayatrl. Visvamitra is the Rsi thereof and Savita (the Sun) is the god.

## \|\| 35.2 \|\|

*brahmaśīrṣā rudraśikhā viṣṇorhṛdayasaṃśritā \|*  
*viniyogaikanayanā kātyāyanasagotrajā \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. She has Bramana for her head, Rudra for the flame and is stationed in the heart of Visnu. She has application for her one eye and is born in the race of Katyayana.

## \|\| 35.3 \|\|

*trailokyacaraṇā jñeyā pṛthivīkukṣisaṃsthitā \|*  
*evaṃ jñātvā tu gāyattrīṃ japeddvādaśalakṣakam \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. She is known as having she three worlds for her feet and is placed in the belly of earth.

## \|\| 35.4 \|\|

*tripadāṣṭākṣarā jñeyā catuṣpādā ṣaḍakṣarā \|*  
*jepa ca tripadā groktā arcane ca catuṣpadā \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. It consists of three words and eight letters and again of four words and six letters. The one of three words should be used for the purposes of recitation and that of four words for the purposes of adoration.

## \|\| 35.5 \|\|

*nyāse jape tathā dhyāne agnikārye tathārcane \|*  
*gāyattrīṃ vinyasennityaṃ sarvapāpagraṇāśinīm \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. In the rites of Nyasa, recitation, meditation, adoration and fire a worshipper should daily use Gayatrl destructive of all sins.

## \|\| 35.6-10 \|\|

*pādāṃsuṣṭhe gulphamadhye jaṅghayorviddhi jānunoḥ \|*  
*ūrvorguhye ca vṛṣaṇe nāḍyāṃ nābhau tanūdare \|\| 6 \|\|*

*stanayorhṛdi kaṇṭhauṣṭhamukhe tāluni cāṃsayoḥ \|*  
*netre bhuvārlalāṭe ca pūrvasyāṃ dakṣiṇottare \|\| 7 \|\|*

*paścame mūrdhni cākāraṃ nyasedvarṇānvadāmyaham \|*  
*indranīlaṃ ca vahniṃ ca pītaṃ śyāmaṃ ca kāpilam \|\| 8 \|\|*

*śvetaṃ vidyutprabhaṃ tāraṃ kṛṣṇaṃ raktaṃ krameṇa tat \|*  
*śyāmaṃ śuklaṃ tathā pītaṃ śvetaṃ vai padmarāgavat \|\| 9 \|\|*

*śaṅkhavarṇaṃ pāṇḍuraṃ ca raktaṃ cāsavasannibham \|*  
*arkavarṇasamaṃ saumyaṃ śaṅkhābhaṃ śvetameva ca \|\| 10 \|\|*

6-10. One should assign it to the toes of the feet, insteps, knee-joints, organ of exeretion, scrotum, tubes, navel, belly, breast, heart, throat mouth, palate, eyes, eye-brows, forehead, in the east, south, north west and head. The colour of saphire, the colour of fire, yellow, dark-blue, twany-colour, that of white, that of lightning, dark, crimson, that of conch-shell, grey, that of wine, and sun \[constitute it\].

## \|\| 35.11 \|\|

*yadyatspṛśati hastena yacca paśyati cakṣuṣā \|*  
*pūtaṃ bhavati tatsarvaṃ gāyattryā na paraṃ viduḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. All articles which he touches with his hands or sees with his eyes become purified. There is nothing superior to Gayatri.

## Chapter 36

## \|\| 36.1 \|\|

*hariruvāca \|*  
*sandhyāvidhiṃ pravakṣyāmi śṛṇu rudrāghanāśanam \|*  
*prāṇāyāmatrayaṃ kṛtvā sandhyāsnānamupakramet \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Hari said: — Hear, О Rudra, I will now describe the rites of Sandhya which destroy all sins. Having practised Praijayama, (suppression of vital airs), thrice the worshipper should bathe at the period of conjunction.

## \|\| 36.2 \|\|

*sapraṇavāṃ savyāhṛtiṃ gāyattrīṃ śirasā saha \|*  
*triḥ paṭhedāyatapraṇaḥ prāṇāyāmaḥ sa ucyate \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. That process of Yoga is called Pranayama in which a man, having controlled his vital breath, reads thrice the Gayatri with Pranava and Vyarhrti.

## \|\| 36.3 \|\|

*manovākrāyajaṃ doṣaṃ prāṇāyāmairdaheddvijaḥ \|*  
*tasmātsarveṣu kāleṣu prāṇāyāmaparo bhavet \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. By the yogic process of Pranayama a twice- born one destroys the impurities of the mind, speech and body and therefore practises it during all hours of the day.

## \|\| 36.4 \|\|

*sāyamagniśca metyuktā prātaḥ sūryetyapaḥ pibet \|*  
*āpaḥ punantu madhyāhne upaspṛśya yathāvidhi \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Then reciting the mantram "Sayam Agni (fire in the evening)" as well as "Pratah Surya (the sun in the morning)" he should drink water.

## \|\| 36.5 \|\|

*āpohiṣṭhetyṛcā kuryānmārjanaṃ tu kuśodakaiḥ \|*  
*praṇavena tu saṃyuktaṃ kṣipedvāri padepade \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Then duly touching water in the noon and by reciting the Rk 'Apohistha' he should rub his body with the water of KuSa blades. Then adding to this mantram Pranava he should sprinkle water at every step.

## \|\| 36.6 \|\|

*rajastamaḥ svamohotthāñjāgratsvapnasuṣuptijān \|*  
*vāṅmanaḥ karmajāndoṣānnavaitānnavabhirdahet \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. With nine he should destroy the nine-fold impurities originating from Rajas (darkness), Tamas (ingnorance),Moha (stupefaction), from waking state, dreaming state and that of dreamless sleep, those originating from speech, mind and action.

## \|\| 36.7 \|\|

*samuddhṛtyodakaṃ pāṇau japtvā ca drupadāṃ kṣipet \|*  
*tripaḍaṣṭau dvādaśadhā vartayedaghamarpaṇam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Taking up water in his two palms and reciting the Gayatri he should throw it quickly thrice, six, eight or twelve.times. It destroys all sins.

## \|\| 36.8 \|\|

*udutyañcitramityābhyāmupatiṣṭheddivākaram \|*  
*divā rātrau ca yatpāpaṃ sarvaṃ naśyati tatkṣaṇāt \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. He should stand facing the sun and recite it. It destroys immeditately all sins which a man commits day and night.

## \|\| 36.9 \|\|

*pūrvasaṃdhyāṃ japaṃstiṣṭhetpaścimāmupaviśya ca \|*  
*mahāvyāhṛtisaṃyuktāṃ gāyattrīṃ praṇavānvitām \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Sitting in the west he should recite the first Sandhya-the Gayatri, consisting of the great Vyarhrti and Pranava.

## \|\| 36.10 \|\|

*daśabhirjanmajanitaṃ śatena tu purā kṛtam \|*  
*triyugaṃ tu sahasreṇa gāyattrī hanti duṣkṛtam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Gayatri destroys sins, committed before in ten or a hundred births, and in three or a thousand yugas (cycles).

## \|\| 36.11 \|\|

*raktā bhavati gāyattrī sāvitrī śuklavarṇikā \|*  
*kṛṣṇā sarasvatī jñeyā saṃdhyātrayamudāhṛtam \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Gayatrl is Crimson-coloured and Savitri is white-hued and Sarasvatl is dark-blue. These are called the three Sandhyas.

## \|\| 36.12-13 \|\|

*oṃ bhūrvinyasya hṛdaye oṃ bhuvaḥ śirasi nyaset \|*  
*oṃ svariti śikhāyāṃ ca gāyattryāḥ prathamaṃ padam \|\| 12 \|\|*

*vinyasetkavace vidvāndvitīyaṃ netrayornyaset \|*  
*tṛtīyenāṅgavinyāsaṃ caturthaṃ sarvato nyaset \|\| 13 \|\|*

12-13. Having assigned the letters Om, bhur to the heart he should assign От, bhuvah to the head and От, Swar to the tuft of hair on the head. A learned man should assign the first word of the Gayatrl to the coat of mail, the second to the eyes, the third to the limbs and the fourth to every where.

## \|\| 36.14 \|\|

*saṃdhyākāle tu vinyasya japedvai vedamātaram \|*  
*śivastasyāstu sarvāhne prāṇāyāmaparaṃ nyaset \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Having made this assignment at the period of junction he should recite the mother of the Vedas.

## \|\| 36.15-18 \|\|

*tripadā yā tu gāyattrī brahmaviṣṇumaheśvarī \|*  
*viniyogamṛṣicchando jñātvā tu japamārabhet \|\| 15 \|\|*

*sarvapāpavinirmukto brahmalokamavāpnuyāt \|*  
*parorajasi sāvadoṃ turīyapadamīritam \|\| 16 \|\|*

*taṃ hanti sūryaḥ sandhyāyāṃ nopāstiṃ kurute tu yaḥ \|*  
*turīyasya padasyāpi ṛṣirnirmala eva ca \|\| 17 \|\|*

*chandastu devī gāyattrī paramātmā ca devatā \|\| 18 \|\|*

15-18. This Gayatrl consists of three padas and is identical with Brahma, Visnu and Mahesvara. Having learnt its application, saintly author and verse one should begin it recitation. Being shorn of all forms of sins he repairs to the region of Brahma.

## Chapter 37

## \|\| 37.1 \|\|

*hariruvāca \|*  
*gāyattrī paramā devī bhuktimuktipradā ca tām \|*  
*yo japettasya pāpānivinaśyanti mahāntyapi \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Hari said: — The great goddess Gayatrl gives enjoyment and emancipation. He who recites it has even mighty iniquities dissipated.

## \|\| 37.2-4 \|\|

*gāyattrīkalpamākhyāsye bhuktimuktipradaṃ ca tat \|*  
*aṣṭottaraṃ sahasraṃ vā athavāṣṭaśataṃ japet \|\| 2 \|\|*

*trisandhyaṃ brahmalokīsyācchataṃ japtvā jalaṃ pibet \|*  
*saṃdhyāyāṃ sarvapāpaghnīṃ devīmāvāhya pūjayet \|\| 3 \|\|*

*bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ svamantreṇa yutāṃ dvādaśanāmabhiḥ \|*  
*gāyatryai namaḥ \|*  
*sāvitryai sarasvatyai namonamaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

2-4. I will now describe the Gayatrl Kalpa which yields enjoyment and emancipation. Having recited it one thousand and eight times or one hundred and eight times at three periods of junction one repairs to the region of Brahma. Then after reciting it a hundred times he should drink water. Having invoked the spirit of the goddess having twelve names who destroys all sins at the period of conjunction he should adore her, with her won mantram "Bhur, Bhuvas, Svaha." Om, salutation unto Gayatrl. Om, salutation unto Savitri.

## \|\| 37.5 \|\|

*vedamātre ca sāṃkṛtyai brahmāṇī kauśikī kramāt \|*  
*sādhvyai sarvārthasādhinyai sahasrākṣyai ca bhūrbhuvaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Om, salutation unto Sarasvatl, unto the mother of the Vedas, Sangkriti, Brahman! and Kousikl. He should assign the mantram "Bhur, Bhuvas" to Sadhya, having a thousand eyes, who accomplishes all objects.

## \|\| 37.6 \|\|

*svarevaṃ juhuyā dagnau samidājyaṃ haviṣyakam \|*  
*aṣṭottarasahasraṃ vāpyathavāṣṭaśanta ghṛtam \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. With the man tram "Swar" he should offer unto fire, one thousand and eight or one hundred and eight times, sacrificial twig butter and Havi.

## \|\| 37.7-8 \|\|

*dharmakāmādisiddhyarthaṃ juhuyātsarvakarmasu \|*  
*pratimāṃ candanasvarṇanirmitāṃ pratipūjya ca \|\| 7 \|\|*

*yathā lakṣaṃ tu japtavyaṃ payomūlaphalārśanaiḥ \|*  
*ayutadvayahomena sarvakāmānavāpnuyāt \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. He should make all these oblations for attaining success in religious rites, personal undertakings and all other works. Having adored an image, made of sandal-wood or gold, recited the name a lac of times, lived on water, roots and fruits and performed two Ayutas of Homas a person attains to all desired-for objects.

## \|\| 37.9 \|\|

*uttare śikhare jātā bhūmyāṃ parvata vāsinī \|*  
*brahmaṇā samanujñātā gaccha devi yathāsukham \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. О goddess, ordered by Brahma, do thou, at thy pleasure, repair to the land situated on the northern summit.

## Chapter 38

## \|\| 38.1 \|\|

*hariruvāca \|*  
*navamyādau yajeddurgāṃ hrīṃ durge rakṣiṇīti ca \|*  
*mātarmātarvare durge sarvakāmārthasādhani \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Hari said: — A worshipper should adore Durga in a Navami and other days with the mantram: — "Hrim, О Durga! Protect me, О mother, О foremost of mothers, О thou who dost grant all desired for objects."

## \|\| 38.2-3 \|\|

*anena balidānena sarvakāmānprayaccha me \|*  
*gaurī kālī umā durgā bhadrā kāntiḥ sarasvatī \|\| 2 \|\|*

*maṅgalā vijayā lakṣmīḥ śivā nārāyaṇī kramāt \|*  
*mārge tṛtīyāmārabhya pūjayenna viyogabhāk \|\| 3 \|\|*

2-3. Being gratified with this offering do thou give me all desired-for object Gaurl, Kali, Uma, Durga, Bhadra, Kanti, Sarasvati, Mangala Vinaya, Laksmi, Shiva, Narayani — he who adores all these in order beginning with the third day of the dark or light fomight, does not suffer from separation.

*aṣṭādaśabhujāṃ kheṭakaṃ ghaṇṭāṃ darpaṇaṃ tarjanīm \|*

4-6. Не should then meditate, with mantrams, on her having eighteen arms, on Khetaka, hell, mirror, the fore-finger, bow, standard, axe damaru (a small drum), noose, 3akti, mace, dart skull, goad made of adamant, arrow, a discus and probe. I will now describe the recitation of the names of the auspicious goddess.

7\. Om, salutation unto the auspicious goddess Camunda, living in the cremation ground, having a skull in her hand, seated on the back of a huge goblin, having a garland of huge conveyances, the night of death, encircled by a number of Ganas, having a huge mouth and many arms, armed with a bell, a small drum and Kinikini and laughing aloud with the sound of Kilikili, Hum. \[Salutation unto her\], making enough of loud sound, having her body covered all over with the skin of an elephant, as well as blood and flesh, having a tongue hanging down, a great RaksasI, having hideous teeth, laughing aloud, effulgent like lightining, having terrific eyes. Hili, Hili, do thou put thy tongue into thy mouth. Hum, salutation unto thy tongue Trini, О thou having a face covered with frowns, О thou having an auspicious seat, wearing a garland of skulls, (around the neck), braided licks, crown and the moon (on the head) and laughing alod Kili Kill Hum, Hum, О thou having terrific teeth, О thou who dost dissipate all obstacles, do thou make me accomplish this work, Do it! Do it! Kaha! Kaha! do thou make me enter with the goad. Vahga! Vanga! make me tremble! make me tremble. Go! Go! guide me! guide me! О thou fond of blood, flesh and wine, kill, kill, grind, cut, cut, strike, strike, make my body strong as an adamant. Destroy all the wicked beings of the three worlds. Make be possess every thing that is taken or not taken. Make me walk! Dance! Dance! Bind! Bind! Jump! О thou having eyes entered into sockets! О thou having hairs tied up! О thou having the face of an Uluka! О thou wearing a garland of hands! burn, burn, rot, rot, take, take, make me enter this mystic diagram. Make me possessed by the energies of Brahma, Visnu, Rsi and Rudra. Kili, Kili, Khili, Khili, Mili, Mili, Cili, Cili, О thou having a good appearance! О thou having thy body encircled by a black serpent! О thou having all the planets in thee! О thou having elongated lips! О thou having a nose sunk between the two eye-brows! О thou having a grim face! О thou, having twany coloured braids! О Brahml! break, break, burn, burn, О thou having a death-like face! Khala, Khala, strike down, strike down. О thou having red shot eyes, roll them, strike, strike the ground. Take, take, open up your eyes, open. Break, break feet, take, take. Display, display, the Mudras hum, hum, phat, rive, rive, cut as under with the trident. Kill, kill with the trident, strike, strike with the rod. Cut, cut, with the Shakti; wound, wound with discus. Bit, bit, with the teeth. Strike with a stick. Strike, strike with the goad. Take, take the head suffering from fever coming every day, every second da:', every third day and every founh day. Release me, release me from the she goblins, Skandas and evil stars. Lala, Lala, raise up, raise up the earth. Strike down, strike down. Take, take Brahmana. Come come, Mahesvari. Come, come, Kaumari. Come, come, Varahl, come, come Aindrl Come, Come, Camunda. Come, come Vaisnavi Come, come, NarasimhI. Come, come, Shivadutl. Come, come, Kapalinl. Come, come, Revatl. Come, come, SuskrevatL Come, come Akasa Revatl. Come come, О thou ranging on the mount Himalaya. Come, come, О thou ranging on the mount Kailasa. Come, come, cut open this great mantram. Kili, Kili, О thou having Bimva-like lips, О thou of a dreadful form, О Camunda, О thou originating from the anger of Rudra, thou who dost destroy the Asuras and range in the sky, bind, bind the time with thy noose. Enter, enter into this mystic diagram. Strike, strike, take, take, bind, bind the mouth. Bind the eyes, bind the feet, bind the hands and feet, bind, bind all the evil stars. Bind, bind all the directions. Bind, bind, all the opposite directions. Bind, bind the up and down. Bind, bind with the ashes, drinks, earth and sessamum seeds. Possess, possess, strike, О Camunda. Kili, Kili, Viche, Hum, Phat, Svaha.

## \|\| 38.8 \|\|

*aṣṭottarapadānāṃ hi mālā mantramayī japaḥ \|*  
*ekaikrapadamaṣṭasahasradhā trimadhurāktatilāṣṭasahasrahāmeḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. This is the recitation of the Mula mantram consisting of one thousand and eight letters. Each word should be recited eight thousand times. With sessamum seeds mixed with sugar, honey and clarified butter eight thousand Homas should be performed.

## \|\| 38.9 \|\|

*mahāmāṃsena-trimadhurāktena aṣṭottarasahsatraṃ ca ekaikaṃ ca padaṃ yajet \|*  
*tilāṃstrimadhurāktāṃśca sahasraṃ cāṣṭa homayet \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. With human flesh, suger, honey and clarified butter one should recite a word one thousand and eight times. With sessamum seeds, sugar, honey and clarified butter he should perform one thousand and eight Homas.

## \|\| 38.10 \|\|

*mahāmāṃsaṃ trimadhurādatha vā sarvakarmakṛt \|*  
*vārisarṣapabhasmādikṣepādyuddhādike jayaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Or with human flesh, honey, sugar and clarified butter he should perform all the rites. By throwing water, sessamum seeds and ashes one achieves victory in battle etc.

## \|\| 38.11 \|\|

*aṣṭāviṃśabhujā dhyeyā aṣṭādaśabhujāthavā \|*  
*dvādaśāṣṭabhujā vāpi dhyeyā vāpi caturbhujā \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. The goddess should be meditated on as having twenty-eight arms, eighteen arms, twelve arms or four arms.

## \|\| 38.12-13 \|\|

*asikheṭānvitau hastau gadādaṇḍayutau parau \|*  
*śaracāpayutau cānyau khaḍgamudrarasaṃyutau \|\| 12 \|\|*

*khaṅkhaghaṇṭānvitau cānyau dhvajadaṇḍayutau parau \|*  
*anyau paraśucakrāḍhyau ḍamarudarpaṇānvitau \|\| 13 \|\|*

12-13. Her two hands are adorned with sword and Kheta, the other two with club and rod, the other two with arrow and bow, the other two with dagger and mace, the other two with conchshell and bell, the other two with standard and rod', the other two with axe and discus, the other two with a small drum and mirror.

## \|\| 38.14-15 \|\|

*śaktihastāśritau cānyau raṭoṇī musalānvitau \|*  
*pāśatomarasaṃyuktau ḍhakrāpaṇavasaṃyutau \|\| 14 \|\|*

*tarjayantī pareṇaiva anyaṃ kalakaladhvanim \|*  
*abhayasvastikādyau ca mahiṣaghnī ca siṃhagā \|\| 15 \|\|*

14-15. The other hands are endued with 6akti, mace, noose, Tomara, durm and Pnava. With the other hand she is striking a drum and making a sound. She gives protection, kills the buffaloe-faced domon, and rides a lion.

## \|\| 38.16 \|\|

*jaya tvaṃ kila bhūteśe sarvabhūtasamāvṛte \|*  
*rakṣa māṃ nijabhūtebhyo valiṃ gṛhṇa namo 'stu te \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Victory unto thee, О queen of ghosts and others encircled by goblins. Save me from thy goblins and accept my sacrifice. Salutation unto thee.

## Chapter 39

## \|\| 39.1 \|\|

*rudra uvāca \|*

1\. Rudra said: — О Janarddana, do thou describe, again in brief, the adoration of the deity, the sun, another form of Visnu, which yields emancipation and enjoyment.

## \|\| 39.2 \|\|

*vāsudeva uvāca \|*

Оm, Om, salutation unto Vimala. am, am, salutation unto Sara, am, am, saluttion unto Adhara. Om, am, salutation unto Paramamukha. These Vimala and other should be adored in the south-east and other corners.

He should then adore adore DTpti and others as well as Sarvatomukhin inside the diagram. Om. Yam, salutation unto DIpta. Om, VinI, salutation unto Bhadra. Om, Vaim, salutation unto Jaya. ## \|\| 39.5 \|\|

*oṃ arkāsanāya namaḥ \|*

With, this mantram a worshipper should invoke life in the image of the sun, install it, and perform the rite of Sannidhapanan (bringing near). ## Chapter 40

## \|\| 40.1 \|\|

*śaṅkara uvāca \|*  
*māheśvarīṃ ca me pūjāṃ vada śaṅkhagadādhara \|*  
*yāṃ jñātvā mānavāḥ siddhiṃ gacchanti parameśvara \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Sankara said: — О Sankara, describe unto me the adoration of Mahesvari, by knowing which, О great God, men attain to Siddhi.

## \|\| 40.2-3 \|\|

*hariruvāca \|*  
*śṛṇu māheśvarīṃ pūjāṃ kathyamānāṃ vṛṣadhvaja \|*  
*ādau snātvā tathācamya hyāsane copaviśya ca \|\| 2 \|\|*

*nyāsaṃ kṛtvā maṇḍale vai pūjayacce maheśvaram \|*  
*mantrairetairmaheśāna parivārayutaṃ haram \|\| 3 \|\|*

2-3. Hari said: — Hear, О bull-emblemed deity, I will describe the adoration of Mahesvari. Having bathed first, then rinsed his mouth, taken his seat and performed Nyasa a worshipper should adore Mahesavara in the mystic diagram together with her family, with the following mantrams, О grat Isana.

## \|\| 40.4 \|\|

*oṃ hāṃ śivāsanadevatā āgacchateti \|*  
*anenāvāhayedrudra devatā āsanasya yāḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. With the mantram, "O Ye presiding deities of diva's seat, come here" he should, О Rudra, invoke the presiding deities of the seat.

Om, Ham, salutation unto Sajani. Om, Ham, salutation unto Kriya. Om, Ham, salutation into Vrddhi. Om, Ham, salutation unto Karya. Om, Hum, salutation unto Dhatri. Om, Ham, salutation unto Bhramanl. Om. Ham salutation unto Mohinl. Om, Ham, salutation unto Tvara. О bull-emblemed deity these thirteen are known as the Kalas or pass of Vamadeva.

10\. Om, Ham, salutation unto Tatpurusa. Om, Ham, salutation unto Vrtti. am, Ham, salutation unto Pratistha. Om, Ham, salutation unto Madya. Om, Ham, salutation unto Shanti. О bull-emblemed deity, these four are known as the Kalas or parts of Tatpurusa.

11\. Om, Hum, salutation unto Aghora. Om, Ham, salutation unto Uma. Om, Ham, salutation unto Ksma, (forgiveness). Om, Ham, salutation unto Nidra (sleep). Om, Ham, salutation unto Vyadhi (disease). Om, Ham, salutation unto Ksudha (hunger). Om, Hum, salutation unto Trsna (thirst). О Нага, these are the eight terrific parts of Aghora.

Om, Ham, salutation unto Yama, the lord of departed spirits, am, Ham, salutation unto Nairrta, the lord of Raksas. Om, Ham, salutation unto Varuna, the lord of waters. ## \|\| 40.14-19 \|\|

*āvāhanaṃ sthāpanaṃ sannidhānaṃ ca śaṅkara \|*  
*sannirodhaṃ tathā kuryātsakalīkaraṇaṃ tathā \|\| 14 \|\|*

*tattvanyāsaṃ ca mudrāyā darśanaṃ dyānameva ca \|*  
*pādyamācamanaṃ hyarghyaṃ puṣpāṇyabhyaṅgadānakam \|\| 15 \|\|*

*tata udvartanaṃ snānaṃ sugandhaṃ cānulepanam \|*  
*vastrālaṃ kārabhogāṃśca hyaṅganyāsaṃ ca dhūpakam \|\| 16 \|\|*

*dīpaṃ naivedyadānaṃ ca hastodvartanameva ca \|*  
*pādyārghyācamanaṃ gandhaṃ tāmbūlaṃ gītavādanam \|\| 17 \|\|*

*nṛtyaṃ chatrā dikaraṇaṃ mudrāṇāṃ darśanaṃ tatā \|*  
*rūpaṃ dhyānaṃ japañcātha ekavadbhāva eva ca \|\| 18 \|\|*

*mūlamantreṇa vai kuryājjapapūjāsamarpaṇam \|*  
*māheśī kathitā pūjā rudra pāpavināsinī \|\| 19 \|\|*

14-19. О Shankara, a worshipper should thus perform the rites of invocation, installation, making near, concentration and Sakalikarana, and next the assignment of Tattvas, the is playing of Mudras and meditation. He should next dedicate water for washing feet, that for rinsing mouth, Arghya, flowers, water for bathing, scents, unguents, raiments, ornaments, objects of enjoyment, incense, stamps, food. He should also propitiate the deity with water for washing feet, water for rinsing mouth, scents, betel, umbrella and Mudras. He should meditate on the form and reef the name and dedicate the adoration and recitation was the principal mantram. О Rudra, I have thus described the adoration of Mahesi which destroys alol sins.

## Chapter 41

## \|\| 41.1 \|\|

*vāsudeva uvāca \|*  
*oṃ viśvāvasurnāma gandharvaḥ kanyānāmadhipatirlabhāmi te kanyāṃ samutpādya tasmai viśvavāsave svāhā \|*  
*strīlābho mantrajāpyācca kālarātriṃ vadāmyaham \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Vasudeva said: — Om, there is Gandharva, by name Visvavasu, the master of maidens. I will secure him for you. "Having begotten maidens. Unto Visvasu, Svaha." This is the recitation of the mantram for obtaining wives. I will describe the night of death.

## \|\| 41.2 \|\|

*oṃ namo bhagavati ṛkṣakarṇi caturbhuje ūrdhvakeśi trinayane kālarātri mānuṣāṇāṃ vasārudhirabhojane amukasya prāptakālasya mṛtyuprade huṃ phaṭ hanahana dahadaha māṃsarudhiraṃ pacapaca ṛkṣapatni svāhā \| na tithirna ca nakṣatraṃ nopavāso vidhīyate \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Om. salutation unto the auspicious goddess, having ears like those of a bear and four arms. О thou having hairs, tied up! О thou, having three eyes! This is the night of death for men in the matter of feeding upon marrow and blood. May deadlapproach such and such person who has come to the proper time. Ham, phat, kitt, kitt, kitt, bum, bum, flesh and blood, раса, раса, Riksapatni (wife of the bear) Svaha. There is no restriction for the observance of lunar days, stars, or fasting.

## \|\| 41.3 \|\|

*kruddho raktena saṃmārjya karau tābhyāṃ pragṛhya ca \|*  
*pradoṣe saṃjapelliṅgamāmapātraṃ ca mārayet \|*  
*oṃ namaḥ sarvatoyantrāṇyetadyathā jambhani mohani sarvaśatruvidāriṇi rakṣarakṣa māmamukaṃ sarvabhayopadravebhyaḥ svāhā \|*  
*śukre naṣṭe mahādeva vakṣye 'haṃ dvijapādiha \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. A worshipper should rub his hands with blood and then take up all articles with them. Early in the morning he should recite the name of the phallic emblem and strike it with a mango leaf. Om, salutation unto all the weapons, so that, О Jambhani, О thou who charmest all, О thou who dost destroy all the enemies, protect me, such and such a person, from all fears and calamities, Svaha. On the destruction of Sukra, О Mahadeva, I described it which saves all the twice-born.

## Chapter 42

## \|\| 42.1 \|\|

*hariruvāca \|*  
*pavitrāropaṇaṃ vakṣye sivasyāśivanāśanam \|*  
*ācāryaḥ sādhakaḥ kuryātputrakaḥ samayī hara \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Hari said: — I will now describe the eternal rite of Shiva called Pavitrarohana1 which, О Нага, a priest a worshipper or his son or a person, observant of a vow, should perform.

## \|\| 42.2 \|\|

*saṃvatsarakṛtāṃ pūjāṃ vighneśo harate 'nyathā \|*  
*āṣāḍhe śrāvaṇe māghe kuryādbhādrapade 'pi vā \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Having performed the adoration extending over full one year one should perform this rite in the month of Asada, 6ravana, Magha or Bhadrapada.

## \|\| 42.3 \|\|

*sauvarṇaraupyatāmraṃ ca sūtraṃ kārpāsikaṃ kramāt \|*  
*jñeyaṃ kujādau saṃgrāhyaṃ kanyayā kartitaṃ ca yat \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. He should first of all procure a thread made of gold, silver, copper or of cotton spun by a maiden.

## \|\| 42.4 \|\|

*triguṇaṃ triguṇīkṛtya tataḥ kuryātpavitrakam \|*  
*granthayo vāmadevena satyena kṣālayecchiva \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Having made nine folds of this thread he should perform the rite of Pavitrakam. With the Vamadeva mantram he should make the Granthis (knots).

## \|\| 42.5-7 \|\|

*aghoreṇa tu saṃśodhya baddhastatpuruṣādbhavet \|*  
*dhūpayedīśamantreṇa tantudevā iti (me) smṛtāḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*oṃ kāraścandramā vahnirbrahnā nāgaḥ śikhidhvajaḥ \|*  
*ravirviṣṇuḥ śivaḥ proktaḥ kramāttantuṣu devatāḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*aṣṭottaraśataṃ kuryātpañcāśatpañcaviṃśatim \|*  
*rudro 'ttamādi vijñeyaṃ mānaṃ ca granthayo daśa \|\| 7 \|\|*

5-7. With the Satya mantram, О Siva, he should wash the thread, with the Aghora man tram he should purify it, with the Tatpurusa mantram he should tie it and with Isa mantram he should place incense. The following are known as Tantudevas or deities of the thread viz., Omkara, Candrama, Vanhi, Brahma, Naga, 3ikhidhvaja, Ravi, Visnu and Shiva. The length of the sacrificial thread, О Rudra, should be either one hundred and eight fingers in length or fifty or twenty five. There are ten Granthis" or knots.

## \|\| 42.8-11 \|\|

*caturaṅgulāntarāḥ syurgranthināmāni ca kramāt \|*  
*prakṛtiḥ pauruṣī vīrā caturtho cāparājitā \|\| 8 \|\|*

*jayā ca vijayā rudrā ajitā ca sadāśivā \|*  
*manonmanī sarvamukhī dvyaṅgulāṅgulato 'thavā \|\| 9 \|\|*

*rañjayetkuṅkumādyaistu kuryādrandhaiḥ pavitrakam \|*  
*saptamyāṃ vā trayodaśyāṃ śuklapakṣe tathetare \|\| 10 \|\|*

*kṣīrādibhiśca saṃsnāpya liṅgaṃ gandhādibhiryajet \|*  
*dadyādrandhapavitraṃ tu ātmane brahmaṇe hara \|\| 11 \|\|*

8-11. And the interstice between one Granthi and the other should be four fingers; or it may be two fingers or one. \[The names of the ten Granthis are: — Prakrti, Pourusi, Vira, Aparajita, Jaya, Vijaya, Rudra, Manonmani and Sarvatamukhi. On the seventh or the thirteenth day of the light fortnight one should dye it with saffron and perform the Pavitraka rite with scents. Having sprinkled the phallic emblem with thickened milk he should rub it with scents and dedicate the sacred perfumeries to the self- the Brahmana.

## \|\| 42.12 \|\|

*puṣpaṃ gandhayutaṃ dadyānmūleneśānagocare \|*  
*pūrve ca daṇḍakāṣṭhaṃ tu uttare cāmalakīphalam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. He should place scented flowers at the foot of the image of Isana, sticks for cleansing teeth in the east and fruits of emblic myrobalam in the north.

## \|\| 42.13-14 \|\|

*mṛttikāṃ paścime dadyāddakṣiṇe bhasma bhūtayaḥ \|*  
*nairṛtehyaguruṃ dadyācchikhāmantreṇa mantravit \|\| 13 \|\|*

*vāyavyāṃ sarṣapaṃ dadyātkavacena vṛṣadhvaja \|*  
*gṛhaṃ saṃveṣṭya sūtreṇa dadyādrandhapavitrakam \|\| 14 \|\|*

13-14. He should place earth in the west and ashes in the south. One, conversant with mantrams, should place, with 3ikha mantram, Aguru in the south-east corner and sessamum seeds with the Kavaca mantram, О bull-emblemed deity. Having encircled the house with a thread he should offer sacred scents.

## \|\| 42.15 \|\|

*homaṃ kṛtvā gneya dattvā dadyādbhūtabaliṃ tathā \|*  
*āmantrito 'si deveśa gaṇaiḥ sārdhaṃ maheśvara \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Then after offering oblations of fire he should place offerings for pernicious spirits. О king of goods. О Mahesvara, thou hast been invited with thy ganas (goblins).

## \|\| 42.16-17 \|\|

*prātastvāṃ pūjayiṣyāmi atra sannihito bhava \|*  
*nimantryānena tiṣṭhettu kurvan gītādikaṃ niśi \|\| 16 \|\|*

*mantritāni pavitrāṇi sthāpayeddevapārśvataḥ \|*  
*snātvādityaṃ caturdaśyāṃ prāgrudraṃ ca prapūjayet \|\| 17 \|\|*

16-17. Do thou come near, I will adore thee in the morning. Having thus invited the deity he should the night in singing and place, by the side of the image, sacred articles inspired with mantrams. Having sprinkled the sun with water on the fourteenth day of the durk fortnight he should adore Rudra.

## \|\| 42.18 \|\|

*lalāṭasthaṃ viśvarūpaṃ dhyātvātmānaṃ prapūjayet \|*  
*astreṇa prokṣitānyevaṃ hṛdayenārcitānyatha \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. He should first meditate on self in the form of the universe, as being stationed on the fore head and then adore it. He should sprinkle it with water with the astra mantram and adore it with the Hrdaya mantram.

## \|\| 42.19-20 \|\|

*saṃhitāmantritānyeva dhūpitāni samarpayet \|*  
*śivatattvātmakaṃ cādau vidyātattvātmakaṃ tataḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

*ātmatattvātmakaṃ paścāddevakākhyaṃ tator'cayet \|*  
*oṃ hauṃ hauṃ śivatattvāya namaḥ \|*  
*oṃ hīṃ(hīḥ) vidyātattvāya namaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

19-20. He should next dedicate incense inspired with mantrams. He should first of all adore Shiva Tattva, then Vidya Tattva and next Atma Tattva. Om, Houm, salutation unto Shiva Tattva (essence of Shiva). Om, Him. salutation unto the essential spirit of learning.

## \|\| 42.21-23 \|\|

*oṃ hāṃ (hauḥ) ātmatattvāya namaḥ \|*  
*oṃ hāṃ hīṃ hūṃ kṣaiṃ sarvatattvāya namaḥ \|*  
*kālātmanā tvayā deva yaddṛṣṭaṃ māmake vidhau \|\| 21 \|\|*

*kṛtaṃ kliṣṭaṃ samutsṛṣṭaṃ hutaṃ gupta ca yatkṛtam \|*  
*sarvātmanātmanā śambho pavitreṇa tvadicchayā \|\| 22 \|\|*

*pūrayapūraya makhavrataṃ tanniyameśvarāya sarvatattvātmakāya sarvakāraṇapālitāya oṃ hāṃ hīṃ hūṃ haiṃ hauṃ śivāya namaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

21-23. Om, Ham, salutation unto the essence of self. Om. Ham, Him. Hain, Kosum salutation unto the essence of all. О God! О Shambhu! whatever, thou, indentical with time, hast seen in me, whatever I have done, have offered as oblations to fire, whatever I have created, have all been done by me, by the will, for the rite of Pavitrakam. Om, fulfil my vow of sacrifice. Om, Ham, Him, Hum. Haim, Houm, salutation unto Shiva, the lord of observances, identical with all essences and the cause of all.

## \|\| 42.24-25 \|\|

*pūrvairanena yo dadyātpavitrāṇāṃ catuṣṭayam \|*  
*dattvā vahneḥ (vare) pavitraṃ ca gurave dakṣiṇāṃ diśet \|\| 24 \|\|*

*baliṃ dattvā dvijān bhojya caṇḍaṃ prācyai visarjayet \|\| 25 \|\|*

24-25. With this mantram.the four offerings of a Pavitraka rite should be made. Having offered Pavitrakam to the fire one should make presents unto the preceptor, offer food, feed the Brahmanas, worship Canda and then perform the Visarjana (life-destroying) rite.

## Chapter 43

## \|\| 43.1-2 \|\|

*hariruvāca \|*  
*pavitrāropaṇaṃ vakṣye bhuktimuktipradaṃ hareḥ \|*  
*purā devāsure yuddhe brahmādyāḥ śaraṇaṃ yayuḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*viṣṇuśca teṣāṃ devānāṃ dhvajaṃ graiveyakaṃ dadau \|*  
*etau dṛṣṭvā vinaṅkṣyanti dānavānabravīddhariḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

1-2. Hari said: — I will now describe the Pavitrarohana rite of Hari which yields emancipation and enjoyment. Formerly in the war between the gods and Danavas. the celestials, headed by Brahma, sought refuge with Visnu who conferred on them the standerd Graiveyaka. Seeing them Hari said that they would overcome the Danavas.

## \|\| 43.3-4 \|\|

*viṣṇūkte hyabravīnnāgo vāsukeranujastadā \|*  
*vṛṇīta ca vapitrākhyaṃ varaṃ cedaṃ vṛṣadhvaja \|\| 3 \|\|*

*graiveyaṃ haridattaṃ tu mannāmnā khyātimeṣyati \|*  
*ityukte tena te devāstannāmnā tadvaraṃ viduḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

3-4. On Visnu saying so, the Naga, Vasuki's younger brother, said: — О bull-emblemed deity, I pray from thee this boon, called Pavitraka. so dlat the Graiveya, conferred by Hari. may pass by my name". On his thus addressing the Devas they conferred on him, the same boon.

## \|\| 43.5 \|\|

*prāvṛṭkāle tu ye martyā nārciṣyanti pavitrakaiḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ sāṃvatsarī pūjā viphalā ca bhaviṣyati \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. The mortals, who worship me with the Pavitraka rite during the rainy season, have their adoration extending over full one year rendered useless.

## \|\| 43.6 \|\|

*tasmātsarveṣu deveṣu pavitrāropaṇaṃ kramāt \|*  
*pratipatpaurṇamāsyāntā yasya yā tithirucyate \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. The Pavitrarohana rite of all the deities should be celebrated in order on the lunar days respectively reserved for them, beginning with the first day after the full moon.

## \|\| 43.7-8 \|\|

*dvādaśyāṃ viṣṇave kāryaṃ śukle kṛṣṇe 'tha vā hara \|*  
*vyatīpāte 'yane caiva candarasūryagrahe śiva \|\| 7 \|\|*

*viṣṇave vṛddhikārye ca gurorāgamane tathā \|*  
*nityaṃ pavitramuddiṣṭaṃ prāvṛṭkāle tvavaśyakam \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. On the twelfth day of the dark or light fortnight the one for Visnu should be performed. It is always necessary to perform the Pavitra rite during the rainy season, preference being always given to a Vyatipata1 day, to a solar or lunar eclipse, to a day when the Vrddhi rite of Visnu is performed or when the precepter comes.

## \|\| 43.9-10 \|\|

*kauśeyaṃ paṭṭasūtraṃ vā kārpāsaṃ kṣaumameva vā \|*  
*kuśasūtra dvijānāṃ syādrājñā kauśeyapaṭṭakam \|\| 9 \|\|*

*vaiśyānāṃ cīraṇaṃ kṣaumaṃ śūdrāṇāṃ śaṇavalkajam \|*  
*kārpāsaṃ padmajaṃ caiva sarveṣāṃ śastamīśvara \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. The sacred thread should be made of either red silk, silk fibres, cotton or linen. The twice- born should offer a thread made of Kusa reeds, the kings that made of silk, the Vaisyas that of wool and the Sudras that made of new barks. О Is vara! one, made of cotton or of fibres of a lotus, is preferable unto all castes..

## \|\| 43.11-12 \|\|

*brāhmaṇyā kartitaṃ sūtraṃ triguṇaṃ triguṇīkṛtam \|*  
*oṃ kāro 'tha śivaḥ somo hyagnirbrahyā phaṇī raviḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*vighneśo viṣṇurityete sthitāstantuṣu devatāḥ \|*  
*brahmā viṣṇuśca rudraśca trisūtre devatāḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12. Three knots of three folds each should be made of a thread spun by a Brahmana. A worshipper should next recite the names of the presiding gods of the threas beginning with Om. They are Siva, Soma, Agni, Brahma, PhanI, Ravi, Ganesa and Visnu. Brahma, Visnu and Rudra are the three presiding gods of the three threads.

## \|\| 43.13-14 \|\|

*sauvarṇe rājate tāmre vaiṇave mṛnmaye nyaset \|*  
*aṅguṣṭhena catuḥ ṣaṣṭiḥ śreṣṭhaṃ madhyaṃ tadardhataḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*tadardhā tu kaniṣṭhā syātsūtramaṣṭottaraṃ śatam \|*  
*uttamaṃ madhyamaṃ caiva kanyasaṃ pūrvavatkramāt \|\| 14 \|\|*

13-14. One should keep the thread in a golden vessel, or in one made of silver, or of copper, or of bamboo or of earth. The size of the best vessel should be sixty four fingers in circumference, that of the middling one its half, and that of the youngest the its half again. The best thread must be one hundred and eight fingers in length, the middling one its half, and the youngest its half, again.

## \|\| 43.15 \|\|

*uttamoṃ'guṣṭhamānena madhyamo madhyamena tu \|*  
*kanyase ca kaniṣṭhena aṅgulyā granthayaḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. The best knot should be of the size of a knot of the thumb; the middling one of that of the middle finger and the smallest one of that of the youngest finger.

## \|\| 43.16 \|\|

*vimāne sthaṇḍile caiva etatsāmānyalakṣaṇam \|*  
*śivoddhṛtaṃ pavitraṃ tu pratimāyāṃ ca kārayet \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. The measurement of the sacrificial alter must be guided by these general characteristics. The sacrificial thread must be placed on the idol (of Visnu) which should be of the size of that of Shiva.

## \|\| 43.17-18 \|\|

*hṛnnābhirū(ru) rumāne ca jānubhyāmavalambinī \|*  
*aṣṭottarasahasreṇa catvāro granthayaḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*ṣaṭtriṃ(ḍviṃ) śacca caturviśaddvādaśa granthayo 'thavā \|*  
*uttamādiṣu vijñeyāḥ parvabhirvā pavitrakam \|\| 18 \|\|*

17-18. It must pass through breast, navel, thigh and hang up to the knee-joints. With a thread measuring one thousand and eight fingers in length should be formed four, thirty-six, twenty four and twelve knots severally, each being of the size of a finger knot

## \|\| 43.19 \|\|

*carcitaṃ kuṅkumenaiva haridrācandanena vā \|*  
*sopavāsaḥ pavitrantu pātrasthamadhivāsayet \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. It should be then dyed with saffron, turmeric or sandal. After fasting a worsipper should place the sacred thread on a vessel and perform the initiatory rite of consecration.

## \|\| 43.20 \|\|

*aśvatthapatrapuṭake aṣṭadikṣu niveśitam \|*  
*daṇḍakāṣṭhaṃ kuśāgraṃ ca pūrve saṅkarṣaṇena tu \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Then in vessels made of fig leaves it should be placed in the eight quarters. Twigs and Kusa blades should be dedicated to Shankarsana in the east.

## \|\| 43.21-22 \|\|

*rocanākuṅkumenava pradyumnena tu dakṣiṇe \|*  
*yuddhārtho phalasiddhyarthamaniruddhena paścime \|\| 21 \|\|*

*candanaṃ nīlayuktaṃ ca tilabhasmākṣataṃ tathā \|*  
*āgneyādiṣu koṇeṣur śyādīnāṃ tu kramānnyaset \|\| 22 \|\|*

21-22. Rocana (yellow figment) and saffron should be dedicated to Pradyumna in the south. A person, who is about to undertake a war and seeks for victory, should dedicate to Aniruddha in the west, sandal, blue colour, sessamum seeds, ashes and aksata. In the south-east and other comers he should make assignment of Shri and other goddesses.

## \|\| 43.23 \|\|

*pavitraṃ vāsudevena abhimantrya sakṛtsakṛt \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā punaḥ prapūjyātha vastreṇācchādya yatnataḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Having then inspired the sacred thread widl Vasudeva mantrams, looked at it again and worshipped it he should cover it with a piece of cloth.

## \|\| 43.24-25 \|\|

*devasya purataḥ sthāpyaṃ pratimāmaṇḍalasya vā \|*  
*paścime dakṣiṇe caiva uttare pūrvavatkramāt \|\| 24 \|\|*

*brāhmādīṃścāpi saṃsthāpya kalaśaṃ cāpi pūjayet \|*  
*astreṇa maṇḍalaṃ kṛtvā naivedyañca samarpayet \|\| 25 \|\|*

24-25. He should then place it before the image of the deity or the luystic diagram. Having placed duly as before Brahmanas in the west, south and north he should worship the pitchers. Then having drawn the mystic diagram with a weapon he should place the offerings.

## \|\| 43.26 \|\|

*adhivāsya pavitraṃ tu trisūtreṇa navena vā (ca) \|*  
*vedikāṃ veṣṭayitvā tu ātmānaṃma kalaśaṃ ghṛtam \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Having thus performed the Adhivasa rite of the sacred thread he should encircle the altar with three or nine threads and then connect his own body and the pitchers with it.

## \|\| 43.27-28 \|\|

*agnikuṇḍaṃ vimānaṃ ca maṇḍapaṃ gṛhameva ca \|*  
*sūtramekaṃ tu saṃgṛhya dadyāddevasya mṛrdhāni \|\| 27 \|\|*

*dattvā paṭhedimaṃ mantraṃ pūjayitvā maheśvaram \|*  
*āvāhito 'si deveśa pūjārthaṃ parameśvara \|\| 28 \|\|*

27-28. Connecting the well of sacred fire, the pedastal, the awning and the temple with one thread he should place it on the head of the deity. Having thus offered the thread and worshipped the great god the worshipper should recite the following mantram. "O King of gods! О Graeat Isvara! I have invoked thy presence here for adoring thee.

## \|\| 43.29-30 \|\|

*tatprabhāter'cayiṣyāmi sāmagyāḥ sannidhau bhava \|*  
*ekarātraṃ trirātraṃ vā adhivāsya pavitrakam \|\| 29 \|\|*

*rātrau jāgaraṇaṃ kṛtvā prātaḥ saṃpūjya keśavam \|*  
*āropayetkrameṇaiva jyeṣṭhamadhyakanīyasam \|\| 30 \|\|*

29-30. I will adore thee in the morning. Do thou come near these articles/' Having performed the Adhivasa rite of the sacred thread for one of three nights a worshipper should keep up the night and adore Kesava in the morning. He should next place (on die image) the biggest, middling and the smallest threads.

## \|\| 43.31 \|\|

*dhūpayitvā pavitraṃ tu mantreṇaivābhimantrayet \|*  
*prajaptagranthikaṃ caiva pūjayetkusumādibhiḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Then having incensed the sacred thread he should inspire it with mantrarris. Having recited die names of the knots he should adore them with flowers and other articles.

## \|\| 43.32-33 \|\|

*gāyattryā cārcitaṃ tena devaṃ saṃpūjya dāpayet \|*  
*samaṃ putrakalatrādyaiḥ sūtrapucchaṃ tu dhārayet \|\| 32 \|\|*

*viśuddhagranthikaṃ ramyaṃ mahāpātakanāśanam \|*  
*sarvapāpakṣayaṃ deva tavāgre dhārayāmyaham \|\| 33 \|\|*

32-33. Then having recited the Gayatrl he should adore the deity with the following mantram. May my sons and wife hold this thread. О god, I hold before thee this purified and beautiful knot destructive of the greatest iniquity and of all sort of sins.

## \|\| 43.34-35 \|\|

*evaṃ dhūpādinābhyarcya madhyamādīntsamarpayet \|*  
*pavitraṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ tejaḥ sarvapātakanāśanam \|\| 34 \|\|*

*dharmakāmārthasiddhyarthaṃ svakaṇṭhe dhārayāmyaham \|*  
*vanamālāṃ samabhyarcya svena mantreṇa dāpayet \|\| 35 \|\|*

34-35.
