33\. Svadhyaya is the recitation of Vedic Mantrams. And with the concentration of mind one should adore Hari. Asana (yoga posture) consists of Padma and other, and Pranayama is the suppression of vital airs.

## \|\| 49.34 \|\|

*mantradhyāna to garbho viparīto hyagarbhakaḥ \|*  
*evaṃ dvidhā tridhāpyuktaṃ puraṇātpūrakaḥ sa ca \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Inhaling the breath and sending it with Mantrams and meditation, either twice or thrice, is called Puraka.

## \|\| 49.35-36 \|\|

*kumbhako niścalatvācca recanādrecakastridhā \|*  
*laghurdvādaśamātraḥ syāccaturviṃśatikaḥ paraḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

*ṣaṭtriṃśanmātrikaḥ śreṣṭhaḥ pratyāhāraśca rodhanam \|*  
*brahmātmacintā dhyānaṃ syāddhāraṇā manaso dhṛtiḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

35-36. Absolute suspension of breath is called Kumbhaka. Expiration by one nostril is called Recaka. The withdrawal of the organs of senses from external objects is called Pratyahara. Dhyana is the meditation on self and Brahma. The steadying of the mind is called Dharana.

## \|\| 49.37-38 \|\|

*ahaṃ brahmetyavasthānaṃ samādhirbrahmaṇaḥ sthitiḥ \|*  
*ahamātmā paraṃ brahma satyaṃ jñānamanantakam \|\| 37 \|\|*

*brahma vijñānamānandaḥ sa tattvamasi kevalam \|*  
*ahaṃ brahmāsmyahaṃ brahma aśarīramānindriyam \|\| 38 \|\|*

37-38. The state of mind in which one's soul is absolutely immersed in Brahma and when he thinks "I am Brahma" is called Samadhi. I am Self, the Para-Brahma, ever existent, full of knowledge and without end. The bliss of knowing Brahma us realized when on understands Tattvamasi3. I am Brahma, am without body and organs of senses.

## \|\| 49.39 \|\|

*ahaṃmanobuddhimahadahaṅkārādivarjitam \|*  
*jāgratsvapnasuṣuptyādiyuktajyotistadīyakam \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. I am devoid of mind, intellect and egoism. I am the light in three states of wakefulness, dreaming sleep, and dream less sleep.

## \|\| 49.40 \|\|

*nityaṃ śuddhaṃ buddhamuktaṃ satyamānandamadvayam \|*  
*yo 'sāvādityapuruṣaḥ so 'sāvahamakhaṇḍitam \|*  
*iti dhyāyanvimucyet brāhmaṇo bhavabandhanāt \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. I am eternal, pure, enlightened, existent, blissful and without second. I am that Prime Purusa. I am that undivided, portionless Purusa. A Brahmana, thus meditating, is freed from the fetters of the world.

## Chapter 50

## \|\| 50.1 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ahanyahani yaḥ kuryātkriyāṃ sa jñānamāpnuyāt \|*  
*brāhme muhūrte cotthāya dharmamarthaṃ ca cintayet \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Brahma said: — He who performs religious rites daily attains to Jnana (knowledge). Having got up from bed at the Brahma-muhurta1 he should meditate on religious profit and worldly profit.

## \|\| 50.2-3 \|\|

*cintayeddhṛdi padmasthamānandamajaraṃ harim \|*  
*uṣaḥ kāle tu saṃprāpte kṛtvā cāvaśyakaṃ budhaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*strāyānnadīṣu śuddhāsu śaucaṃ kṛtvā yathāvidhi \|*  
*prataḥ snānena pūyante ye 'pi pāpakṛto janāḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

2-3. He should also meditate, in the lotus of his heart, on blissful and undecaying Hari. When the dawn approaches a learned man, having performed the necessary rites, should repair to a river of pure water for bathing, and perform there duly the purificatory rite. Even sinful wights are sanctified by morning ablutions.

## \|\| 50.4 \|\|

*tasmātsarvaprayatnena prātaḥ snānaṃ samācaret \|*  
*prātaḥ snānaṃ praśaṃsanti dṛṣṭādṛṣṭaṣṭakaraṃ hi tat \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Therefore with every possibie care a person should bathe early in the morning. Wise men speak highly of morning ablutions \[in consequence of their yielding fruits\] seen and unseen.

## \|\| 50.5 \|\|

*sukhātsuptasya satataṃ lālādyāḥ saṃstravanti hi \|*  
*ato naivācaretkarmāṇyakṛtvā snānamāditaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. When a person sleeps at ease saliva and other impurities come out. Therefore without bathing first no one should perform a religious rites.

## \|\| 50.6 \|\|

*alakṣmīḥ kālakarṇo ca duḥ svapnaṃ durvicintitam \|*  
*prataḥ snānena pāpāni dhūyante nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Poverty, misfortune, bad dreams, and anxious thoughts — all these sins are forsooth destroyed by morning ablutions.

## \|\| 50.7 \|\|

*na ca snānaṃ vinā puṃsāṃ prāśastyaṃ karma saṃsmṛtam \|*  
*home japye viśeṣeṇa tasmātsnānaṃ samācaret \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. It is not proper for persons to perform religious rites without bathing. Particularly in Нота and Japa one must bathe.

## \|\| 50.8-9 \|\|

*aśaktāvaśiraskaṃ tu snānamasya vidhīyate \|*  
*ārdreṇa vāsasā vāpi mārjanaṃ kāyikaṃ smṛtam \|\| 8 \|\|*

*brāhmamāgneyamuddiṣṭaṃ vāyavyaṃ divyameva ca \|*  
*vāruṇaṃ yaugikaṃ tadvatṣaḍaṅgaṃ snānamācaret \|\| 9 \|\|*

8-9. He shuld sprinkle his head with water and rub his body with a piece of wet cloth. He should perform the six forms of bathing, viz., Brahma, Agneya, Vayavya, Divya, Varuna and Yougika.

## \|\| 50.10 \|\|

*brāhmaṃ tu mārjanaṃ mantraiḥ kuśaiḥ sodakabindubhiḥ \|*  
*āgreyaṃ bhasmanā'pādamastakāddehadhūnanam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. The Brahma form of bathing consists in rubbing the body with drops of waterpured through Kusa reeds and accompained with Mantrams. Agneya form consists is besmearing the body, from head to foot, with ashes.

## \|\| 50.11 \|\|

*gavāṃ hi rajasā proktaṃ vāyavyaṃ snānamuttamam \|*  
*yattu sātapavarṣeṇa snānaṃ taddivyamucyate \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. The most excellent form of bathing, namely, Vayavya, consists in rubbing on the body the powder of cow-dung. Bathing in the sun-shine is called Divya.

## \|\| 50.12 \|\|

*vāruṇaṃ cāvagāhaṃ ca mānarsa tvātmavedanam \|*  
*yaugikaṃ snānamākhyātaṃ yogena haricintanam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Varuna consists in plunging into water and knowing the self in mind. Meditation on Hari by means of Yoga is called Yougika form of bathing.

## \|\| 50.13 \|\|

*ātmatīrthamiti khyātaṃ sevitaṃ brahmavādibhiḥ \|*  
*kṣīravṛkṣasamudbhūtaṃ mālatīsambhavaṃ śubham \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. It is the shrine of self resorted to by Brahmavadins. With his face directed towards either the north or the east a person should cleanse his teeth with the twigs either of Ksira, Malatl, Bilva or Karavlra trees.

## \|\| 50.14-15 \|\|

*apāmārgaṃ ca vilvaṃ ca karavīraṃ ca dhāvane \|*  
*udaṅmukhaḥ prāṅmukho vā bhakṣayeddantadhāvanam \|\| 14 \|\|*

*prakṣālya bhuktvā tajjahyācchucau deśe samāhitaḥ \|*  
*snātvā santarpayeddevānṛṣīnpitṛgaṇāṃstathā \|\| 15 \|\|*

14-15. Standing on a purified spot he should wash his teeth and mouth and then throw the stick away. Afterwards having bathed he should offer libations of water to the celestials, Rsis and the departed manes.

## \|\| 50.16-17 \|\|

*ācamya vidhivannityaṃ punarācamya vāgyataḥ \|*  
*saṃmārjya mantrai rātmānaṃ kuśaiḥ sodakabindubhaiḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*āpohiṣṭhāvyāhṛtibhiḥ sāvitryā vāruṇaiḥ śubhaiḥ \|*  
*oṅkāravyāhṛtiyutāṃ gāyattrīṃ vedamātaram \|\| 17 \|\|*

16-17. Having rinsed his mouth he should do it again observing silence. Having sprinked his body with drops of water through Kusa reeds and with Mantrams; Apohistha,Vyarhrti and the auspicious Varuni and having recited the Gayatrl, consisting of Om and Vyarhrti, the mother of the Vedas, he should offer libations of water to the sun with his mind fixed in him.

## \|\| 50.18-20 \|\|

*japtvā jalāñjaliṃ dadyādbhāraskaraṃ prati tanmanāḥ \|*  
*prākkūleṣu tataḥ sthitvā darbheṣu susamāhitaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*prāṇāyāmaṃ tataḥ kṛtvā dhyāyetsandhyāmiti śrutiḥ \|*  
*yā sandhyā sā jagatsūtirmāyātītā hi niṣkalā \|\| 19 \|\|*

*aiśvarī kevalā śaktistattvatrayasamudbhavā \|*  
*dhyātvā raktāṃ sitāṃ kṛṣṇāṃ gāyattrīṃ vai japedvudhaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

18-20. Thereupon sitting on Kusa-grass in the morning, controlling his mind and suppressing his vital air he should meditate on Sandhya Mantrams. She, who is Sandhya, is the mother of the universe, beyond illusion, sinless, divine and sprung from three-fold energies. Having thus meditated a learned man should recite crimsoncoloured, white and bark-blue Gayatrl.

## \|\| 50.21-22 \|\|

*prāṅmukhaḥ satataṃ vipraḥ sandhyopāsanamācaret \|*  
*sandhyāhīno 'śucirnityamanarhaḥ sarvakarmasu \|\| 21 \|\|*

*yadanyatkurute kiñcinna tasya phalabhāgbhavet \|*  
*ananyacetasaḥ santo brāhmaṇā vedapāragāḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

21-22. With his face directed towards the earth a Brahmana should always perform his Sandhya rites. He, who does not make Sandhya worship, is impure and is not competent to pertorm any action. And he does not reap the fruit of anything else he does. Having duly adored Sandhya, the pure and self-controlled Brahmanas, the masters of the Vedas, attain to the most excellent region.

## \|\| 50.23-24 \|\|

*upāsya vidhivatsandhyāṃ prāptāḥ pūrvaparāṃ gatim \|*  
*yo 'nyatra kurute yatnaṃ dharma kārye dvijottamaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

*vihāya sandhyāpraṇatiṃ sa yāti narakāyutam \|*  
*tasmātsarvaprayatnena sandhyopāsanamācaret \|\| 24 \|\|*

23-24That best of the twice-born, who, neglecting the Sandhya rites, tries to perform any other religious ceremony, goes to a mullion of hells. Therefore with every possible care on should perform the Sandhya rites.

## \|\| 50.25-26 \|\|

*upāsito bhavettena devo yogatanuḥ paraḥ \|*  
*sahasraparamāṃ nityāṃ śatamadhyāṃ daśāvarām \|\| 25 \|\|*

*gāyattrīṃ vai japedvidvānprāṅmukhaḥ prayataḥ śuciḥ \|*  
*athopatiṣṭhedādityamudayasthaṃ samāhitaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

25-26. By doing so one gets the most excellent celestial and Yoga body. A learned man, controlling his senses, purif iying his own body and mind, and sitting with his face towards the east, should recite the Gayatrl, a thousand, hundred or tefi times. Having controlled his mind, he should sit facing the rising sun.

## \|\| 50.27-28 \|\|

*mantraistu vividhaiḥ sauraiḥ ṛgyajuḥsāmasaṃjñitaiḥ \|*  
*upasthāya mahāyogaṃ devadevaṃ divākaram \|\| 27 \|\|*

*kurvīta praṇatiṃ bhūmau mūrdhānamabhimantritaḥ \|*  
*oṃ khakholkāya śāntāya kāraṇatrayahetave \|\| 28 \|\|*

27-28. With many potent Mantrams, belongiong to the Юс Yayus and Sama Veda, he should adore and salute the Sun, the god of gods, touching the ground with his head, saying "am, salutation, I dedicate my self unto Khakholka, the cause of the three-fold causes, unto him of the form of knowledge.

## \|\| 50.29-30 \|\|

*nivedayāmi cātmānaṃ namaste jñānarūpiṇe \|*  
*tvameva brahma paramamāpo jyotī raso 'mṛtam \|\| 29 \|\|*

*bhūrbhuvaḥ svastvamoṅkāraḥ sarvo rudraḥ sanātanaḥ \|*  
*etadvai sūryahṛdayaṃ japtvā stavanamuttamam \|\| 30 \|\|*

29-30. Thou art Brahma, the great water, fire and juice. Thou art earth, heaven and sky, am and the eternal Rudra." Having recited mentally this most excellent hymn in the morning and noon one should bow unto the Sun.

## \|\| 50.31-32 \|\|

*prātaḥ kāle ca madhyāhne namaskuryāddivākaram \|*  
*athāgamya gṛhaṃ vipraḥ (paścāt) samācamya yathāvidhi \|\| 31 \|\|*

*prajvālya vahniṃ vidhivajjuhuyājjātavedasam \|*  
*ṛtvik putro 'tha patnī vā śiṣyo vāpi sahodaraḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

31-32. Then returing to his house and rinsing his mouth duly with water a Brahmana should light up (himself) the sacred fire and offer oblations unto it. With the permission of the sacrificer, his priest, son, wife, pupil or brother may also offer oblations.

## \|\| 50.33-34 \|\|

*prāpyānujñāṃ viśeṣeṇa juhuyādvā yathāvidhi \|*  
*vinā ma (ta) ntreṇa yatkarma nāmutreha phalapradam \|\| 33 \|\|*

*daivatāni namaskuryādupahārānnivedayet \|*  
*guruṃ caivāpyupāsīta hitaṃ cāsya samācaret \|\| 34 \|\|*

33-34. Any religious rite, that is performed withut Mantrams, yields no fruit in this world. He should bow unto the deities and dedicate unto them offerings. He should adore his preceptor and do what is conducive to his well-being.

## \|\| 50.35 \|\|

*vedābhyāsaṃ tataḥ kuryātprayatnācchaktito dvijaḥ \|*  
*japedvādhyāpayecchiṣyāndhārayedvai vicārayet \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. A twice born should afterwards, according to his power, study the Vedas with proper care; he should recite the Mantrams, teach his pupils, conceive the meaning and discuss the same.

## \|\| 50.36 \|\|

*avekṣeta ca śāstrāṇi dharmādīni dvijottamaḥ \|*  
*vaidikāṃścaiva nigamānvedāṅgāni ca sarvaśaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. That best of the twice-bron should also read the Dharma 6astras (Religious Codes), me Vedic texts and me Vedangas.

## \|\| 50.37 \|\|

*upayādīśvaraṃ caiva yogakṣemaprāsiddhaye \|*  
*sādhayedvividhānarthānkuṭumbārthaṃ tato dvijaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. For making his Yoga successful me twice- born should approach the Deity and afterwards do various works, tor his relatives.

## \|\| 50.38 \|\|

*tato madhyāhnasamaye snānārthaṃ mṛdamāharet \|*  
*puṣpākṣatāṃstilakuśān gomayaṃ śuddhameva ca \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Thereupon in the noon he should collect, for the purpose of bathing, earth, flowers, dried paddy, sessamum seeds, sacrificial grass, and the pure cow-dung.

## \|\| 50.39 \|\|

*nadīṣu devakhāteṣu taḍāgeṣu saraḥ su ca \|*  
*snānaṃ samācarennaiva parakīye kadācana \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. He should bathe in a river, in a tank dedicated to a deity, in a pool or in a pond (of his own) hut he should never bathe (in a well or tank) belonging to another person,

## \|\| 50.40-42 \|\|

*pañca piṇḍānanuddhṛtya snānaṃ duṣyanti nityaśaḥ \|*  
*mṛdaikayā śiraḥ kṣālyaṃ dvābhyāṃ nābhestathopari \|\| 40 \|\|*

*adhaśca tisṛbhiḥ kṣālyaṃ pādau ṣaṭbhistathaiva ca \|*  
*mṛttikā ca samuddiṣṭā vṛddhāmalakamātnikā \|\| 41 \|\|*

*gomayasya pramāṇaṃ tu tenāṅgaṃ lepayettataḥ \|*  
*prakṣālyācamya vidhivattataḥ snāyātsamāhitaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

40-42. If he does not offer five pindas every day his bathing becomes impure. The head should be washed once with earth, the navel twice, the part beneath it duice, and the feet six times. Earth should be of me quantity of a ripe Myrobalam; cowdung should also be of me same quantity. He should then besmear his body with it. Having washed his body and rinsed his mouth, he should bathe with a controlled mind.

## \|\| 50.43 \|\|

*lepayitvā tu tīrasthastalliṅgaireva mantrataḥ \|*  
*abhimantrya jalaṃ mantrairāliṅgairvāruṇaiḥ śubhaiḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Then coming on the shore, he should besmr his body with earth, reciting the Linga Mantrams. He should then inspire the water wim me auspicious Varuna Mantrams.

## \|\| 50.44-45 \|\|

*tnānakāle smaredviṣṇamāpo nārāyaṇo yataḥ \|*  
*prekṣya oṅkāramādityaṃ trirnimajjejjalāśaye \|\| 44 \|\|*

*ācāntaḥ punarācāmenmantreṇānena mantravit \|*  
*antaścarasi bhūteṣu guhāyāṃ viśvatomukhaḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

44-45. At me time of baming he should mink of the Narayana form of Visnu in the water. Having looked at the sun with Om, he should thrice plunge himself into me water and again rinse his mouth with the following mantram. "Thou rangest in the mind of creatures and art the mounth of the universe.

## \|\| 50.46 \|\|

*tvaṃ yajñastvaṃ vaṣaṭkāra āpo jyotī raso 'mṛtam \|*  
*drupadāṃ vā trirabhyasyevdyāhṛtipraṇavānvitām \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Thou art Yama, Vasatkara, water, fire juice and ambrosia". He should repeat thrice the Drupada Mantram consisting of Vyahrti and Pranava.

## \|\| 50.47-48 \|\|

*sāvitrīṃ vā jape dvidvāṃstathā caivāghamarṣaṇam \|*  
*tataḥ saṃmārjanaṃ kuryādāpohiṣṭhāmayobhuvaḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

*idamāpaḥ pravahatavyāhṛtibhistathaiva ca \|*  
*tato 'bhimantritaṃ topamāpo hiṣṭhādimantrakaiḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

47-48. The learned worshipper should next recite the Savitri Mantram destructive of sins. Thereupon he should cleanse the earm with me Apohistha Mantram, with the Mantram "flow pure water? and with Vyahrti. He should next inspire water wim Apohifha Mantram.

## \|\| 50.49 \|\|

*antarjalamavāṅmagno japettriraghamarṣaṇam \|*  
*drupadāṃ vātha sāvitrariṃ tadviṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padam \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. He should next repeat mrice the Mantram " Antarjalamavarimagnon" destructive of all sins, or Drupada of Savitri, me most excellent region of Visnu.

## \|\| 50.50 \|\|

*āvartayedvā praṇavaṃ devadevaṃ ramareddharim \|*  
*apaḥ pāṇau samādāya japtvā vai mārjane kṛte \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. He should next recite Pranava and meditate on Hari me god of gods. Taking up water in his hands and reciting the Mantram, he should sprinkle the head therewith, and would mus be freed off all sins.

## \|\| 50.51-53 \|\|

*vinyasya mūrdhni tattoyaṃ mucyate sarvapātakaiḥ \|*  
*sandhyāmupāsya cācamya saṃsmarennityamīśvaram \|\| 51 \|\|*

*athopatiṣṭhedādityamūrdhvapuṣpānvitāñjalim \|*  
*prakṣipyālokayeddevamudayantaṃ na śakyate \|\| 52 \|\|*

*udutyaṃ citramityevaṃ taccakṣuriti mantrataḥ \|*  
*haṃsaḥ śuciṣadetena sāvitryā ca viśeṣataḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

51-53. Having made the Sandhya adorations and rinsed his mouth, he should daily meditate on the God, and sit facing the sun, placing his palms full of flowers on the crown of his head. Throwing them he should look at the god stationed on the rising mountain (i. e. the rising sun) with the Mantram. Thou art the eye, ever pure, supreme soul and existent, or particularly with the Savitri or other Vedic Mantrams.

## \|\| 50.54-55 \|\|

*anyaiḥ saurairvaidikaiśca gāyattrīṃ ca tato japet \|*  
*mantrāṃśca vividhānpaścātprākkūle ca kaśāsane \|\| 54 \|\|*

*tiṣṭhaṃśca vīkṣyamāṇor'kaṃ japaṃ kuryātsamāhitaḥ \|*  
*sphaṭikābjākṣarudrākṣaiḥ putrajīvasamudbhavaiḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

54-55. He should next repeat Gayatri and various other mantrams. Sitting on a seat of Kusa grass with his face towards the east he should look at the sun and repeat prayers with a controlled mind. The garland of beads should either be made of crystal, lotus, Rudraksa or Putranjlva.

## \|\| 50.56 \|\|

*kartavyā tvakṣālā syādantarā tatra sā smṛtā \|*  
*yadi syātklinnavāsā vai vārimadhyagataścaret \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. If his cloth be tattered he should stand in the water and perform his adorations.

## \|\| 50.57 \|\|

*anyathā ca śucau bhūmyāṃ darbheṣu ca samāhitaḥ \|*  
*pradakṣiṇaṃ samāvṛtya namaskṛtya tataḥ kṣitau \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Else he should sit, with a controlled mind, on Kusa grass spread on a sanctified spot. Then going round, he should bow touching the ground with his head.

## \|\| 50.58-59 \|\|

*ācamya ca yathāśāstraṃ śaktyā svādhyāyamācaret \|*  
*tataḥ santarpayeddevānṛṣīnpitṛgaṇāṃstathā \|\| 58 \|\|*

*ādāvoṅkāramuccārya namo 'nte tarpayāmi ca \|*  
*devānbrahmaṛṣīṃścaiva tarpayedakṣatodakaiḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

58-59. Then rinsing his mouth as sanctioned by the Shastras" he should read the Vedas according to his power. Afterwards he should offer libations of water for the gods, Rsis and the departed manes with the prayer "Om, salutatin unto you all, I offer these libations of water." He should dedicate libations of water and fried paddy unto the celestials, and Brahma Rsis.

## \|\| 50.60-65 \|\|

*pitṝndevānmunīn bhaktyā svasūtroktavidhānataḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

*devarṣoṃstarpayeddhīmānudakāñjalibhiḥ pitṝt \|*  
*yajñopavītī devānāṃ nivītī ṛṣitarpaṇe \|\| 61 \|\|*

*prācīnāvītī pitrye tu tena tīrthena bhārata \|*  
*niṣpīḍya snānavastraṃ vai samācamya ca vāgyataḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

*svairmantrairarcayeddevānpuṣpaiḥ patraistathāmbubhiḥ \|*  
*brahmāṇaṃ śaṅkaraṃ sūryaṃ tathaiva madhusūdanam \|\| 63 \|\|*

*anyāṃścābhimatāndevān bhaktyā cākrodhano hara ! \|*  
*pradadyādvātha puṣpādi sūktena puruṣeṇa tu \|\| 64 \|\|*

*āpo vā devatāḥ sarvāstena samyak samarcitāḥ \|*  
*dhyātvā praṇavapūrvaṃ vai devaṃ vārisamāhitaḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

60-65. He should dedicate offerings reverentially unto the departed manes, gods and ascetics according to the prescription of his own Religious Code. He should gratify the celestial saints and the departed manes with palmfuls of water. Sacrificial threads are also offered to the gods along with water, Nivita (the Brahminical thread suspended round the neck) to the Rsis and Praclnavltins (the sacrificial thread worn over the right arm and passing under the left) to the departed manes. Pressing the water out of the cloth after bathing, rinsing his mouth and observing silence, he should adore the deities with flowers, leaves and water, and Sua Mantrams. О wrathful Нага, \[he should adore\] Brahma, Sankara, the sungod, the slayer of Madhu (Visnu) and various other approved deities. With the Purusa Sukta Mantram he should dedicate flowers and other offerings; or he should adore all the deities with water only. Controlling his mind he should meditate on the deity repeating Om.

## \|\| 50.66 \|\|

*namaskāreṇa puṣāpāṇi vinyasedvai pṛthakpṛthak \|*  
*narte hyārādhanātpuṇyaṃ vidyate karma vaidikam \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. Then saluting him he should keep flowers and other offerings in separate places. Without adoration no Vedic rite becomes consecrated.

## \|\| 50.67 \|\|

*tasmāttatrādimadhyānte cetasā dhārayeddharim \|*  
*tadviṣṇoriti mantreṇa sūktena puruṣeṇa tu \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. Therefore in the beginning, middle and end of every rite, one should mentally meditate on Hari. With the Mantram "Thou art Visnu" and the hymn of the Purusa-Sukta, one should dedicate his self unto Visnu of pure effulgence.

## \|\| 50.68-69 \|\|

*nivedayecca ātmānaṃ viṣṇave 'malatejase \|*  
*tadādhyātmamanāḥ śāntastadviṣṇoriti mantrataḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

*aprete saśirā vetiyajetvā puṣpake harim \|*  
*devayajñaṃ pitṛyajñaṃ tathaiva ca \|*  
*mānuṣaṃ brahmayajñaṃ ca pañca yajñānsamācaret \|\| 69 \|\|*

68-69. Having all his mental faculties tranquilized and his mind fixed on the deity, he should, with the Mantram, "Thou art Visnu", perform the five sacrifices, namely that for the deities, that for the evil spirits, that for the departed manes, that for men and that for Bramha.

## \|\| 50.70 \|\|

*yadi syāttarpaṇādarvāgbrayajñaṃ kuto bhavet \|*  
*kṛtvā manuṣyayajñaṃ vai tataḥ svādhyāyamācaret \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. Without the offering of libations of wdter Brahma Yajna is not finished. After celebrating the sacritice for men(Manusyajna) one should read the Vedas.

## \|\| 50.71 \|\|

*vaiśvadevastu kartavyo devayajñaḥ sa tu smṛtaḥ \|*  
*bhūtayajñaḥṛ sa vai jñeyo bhūtebhyo yastvayaṃ baliḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. In a sacrifice for the gods offerings should be made to that class gods called Visvedevas. In Bhiitayajna animals should be sacrified for the evil spirits.

## \|\| 50.72-73 \|\|

*śvabhyaśca śvapacebhyaśca patitādibhya eva ca \|*  
*dadyādbhūmau bahistvannaṃ pakṣibhyaśca dvijottamaḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

*ekaṃ tu bhojayedvipraṃ pitṝnuddiśya sattamāḥ \|*  
*nityaśrāddhaṃ taduddiśya pitṛyajño gatipradaḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

72-73. The foremost of the twice-born should next offer food to the dogs, the degraded caste people, outcastes and birds, on the grounds outside the house. In honour of the departed manes the best of sacrificers should feed at least one Brahmana. He should perform the daily sraddha in their honour. Such a Pitryajha yields blessed regions.

## \|\| 50.74 \|\|

*uddhṛtya vā yathāśakti kiñcidannaṃ samāhitaḥ \|*  
*vedatattvārthaviduṣe dvijāyaivopapādayet \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. Then with a controlled mind he should, conmmensurate with his means, take up a portion of food and offer it to a Brhamana well- read in the Vedas.

## \|\| 50.75 \|\|

*pūjayedatithiṃ nityaṃ namasyedarcayoddvijam \|*  
*manovākkarmabhiḥ śāntaṃ svāgataiḥ svagṛhaṃ tataḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. He should daily treat his guests hospitably and welcome a Brahmana who comes to his house and adore him with mind, words and deeds.

## \|\| 50.76 \|\|

*bhikṣāmāhurgrāsamātramannaṃ tatsyāccaturguṇam \|*  
*puṣkalaṃ hantakāraṃ tu taccaturguṇamucyate \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. A mouthful of food is called Bhiksa (alms) and enough is given when four times as much is distributed.

## \|\| 50.77 \|\|

*godohamātrakālaṃ vai pratīkṣyo hyatithiḥ svayam \|*  
*abhyāgatānyathāśakti pūjayedatithiṃ tathā \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. A guest should wait for the period that is necessary for milching a cow. One should, as much as lies in his power, treat uncalled-for guests hospitably.

## \|\| 50.78 \|\|

*bhikṣāṃ vai bhikṣave dadyādvidhivadbrahyacāriṇe \|*  
*dadyādannaṃ yathāśakti arthibhyo lobhavarjitaḥ \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. One should daily offer alms to a mendicant, and food to a Brahmacarin (religious student) and to beggars what they want proportionate to his means, and being himself freed from avarice.

## \|\| 50.79-80 \|\|

*bhuñjati bandhubhiḥ sārdhaṃ vāgyato 'nnamakutsayan \|*  
*akṛtvā tu dvijaḥ pañca mahāyajñān dvijottamaḥ \|\| 79 \|\|*

*bhuñjate cetsa mūḍhātmā tiryagyoniṃ ca gacchati \|*  
*vedābhyāso 'nvahaṃ śaktyā mahāyajñakriyākṣamāḥ \|\| 80 \|\|*

79-80. He should next take food in the company of his friends. The foolish Brahmana, who takes his food without celebrating these five sacrifices, is born in a degraded caste. Those, who are competent to celebrate a great sacrifice, should study the Veda.

## \|\| 50.81-82 \|\|

*nāśayantyāśu pāpāni devānāmarcanaṃ tathā \|*  
*yo mohādatha vālasyādakṛtvā devatārcanam \|\| 81 \|\|*

*bhuṅkte sa yāti narakāntsūṃkareṣveva jāyate \|*  
*aśaucaṃ saṃpravakṣyāmi aśuciḥ pātakī sadā \|\| 82 \|\|*

81-82. The adoration of a god dissipates speedily all sins. He, who, either out of ignorance or laziness, takes his food without worshipping the deity, goes to hell and is born as a hog. I will now describe what is impurity. An impure man is visited by sins.

## \|\| 50.83 \|\|

*aśaucaṃ caiva saṃsargācchuddhiḥ saṃsargavarjanāt \|*  
*daśāhaṃ prāhurāśaucaṃ sarveviprā vipaścitaḥ \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. Impurity is generated either by associating with impure persons or avoiding the company of pious men. The learned Brahmanas speak of ten sorts of impurity.

## \|\| 50.84 \|\|

*mṛteṣu vātha jāteṣu brāhmaṇānāṃ dvijottama \|*  
*ādantajananāt sadya ācūḍādekarātrakam \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. The Brahmanas are impure if any person dies in their family or any child is born. When a child dies before teething the period of impurity is immediately over; it lasts for a day before the solemnization of the rite of tonsure.

## \|\| 50.85 \|\|

*trirātramaupanayanāddaśarātramataḥ param \|*  
*kṣattriyo dvādaśahena daśabhiḥ pañcabhirviśaḥ \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. It lasts for three days before the rite of wearing sacred thread is not performed. After that it lasts for ten nights. For the Kastriyas the period consists of twelve days and for the Vaisyas fifteen days.

## \|\| 50.86 \|\|

*śudhyenmāsena vai śūdro yatīnāṃ nāsti pātakam \|*  
*rātribhirmāsatulyābhirgarbhastrāveṣu śaucakam \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. A Sudra is cleansed from impurity after a month. For a Yati there is no impurity. For abhortion it lasts either for a night or for a month.

## Chapter 51

## \|\| 51.1 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*athātaḥ saṃpravakṣyāmi dānadharmamanuttamam \|*  
*arthānāmucite pātre śraddhayā pratipādanam \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Brahma said: — I will now describe the most excellent rules of making charities. Wealth should be respectfully given to a worthy person.

## \|\| 51.2 \|\|

*dānaṃ tu kathitaṃ tajjñairbhuktimuktiphalapradam \|*  
*nyāyenopārjayedvittaṃ dānabhogaphalaṃ ca tat \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Charity yields enjoyment and emancipation. Riches, acquired by fair means, when given away in charities, yeild the fruits of enjoyment.

## \|\| 51.3 \|\|

*adhyāpanaṃ yājanaṃ ca vṛttamāhuḥ pratigraham \|*  
*kusīdaṃ kṛṣivāṇijyaṃ kṣattravṛtto 'tha varjayet \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Teaching, officiating as priests and accepting presents are the duties of the Brahmanas. Usury, agriculture and trade are the duties of the VaiSyas. When charity is made to a worthy person it is called Sattvik (v. one pervaded by the quality of goodness).

## \|\| 51.4 \|\|

*yaddīyate tu pātrebhyastaddānaṃ parikīrtitam \|*  
*nityaṃ naimittikaṃ kāmyaṃ vimalaṃ dānamīritam \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Besides there are various other forms of charity, viz,, Nitya (daily), Naimittika (occasional), Kamya (made with the desire of fruits) and Vimala (pure, or disinterested).

## \|\| 51.5 \|\|

*ahanyahani yatkiñciddīyate 'nupakāriṇe \|*  
*anuddiśya phalaṃ tasmādbrāhmaṇāya tu nityaśaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Whatever is daily given to persons who have done us no good or to the Brahmanas without any expectation for fruits it is called Nitya.

## \|\| 51.6 \|\|

*yattu pāpopaśāntyai ca dīyate vidupāṃ kare \|*  
*naimittikaṃ taduddiṣṭandānaṃ sadbhiranuṣṭhitam \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Whatever is given to a learned person for the expiatin of sins or for averting evils, is called Naimittika. Such charities are made by pious men.

## \|\| 51.7 \|\|

*apatyavijayaiśvaryasvargārthaṃ yatpradīyate \|*  
*dānaṃ tatkāmyamākhyātamṛṣibhirdharmācintakaiḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Whatever is given for having children, a children, achieving victory, or attaining heaven, is called hy the Rsis, well read in the Religious Code, Kamya.

## \|\| 51.8 \|\|

*īśvaraprīṇanārthāya brahmāvitsupradīyate \|*  
*cetasā sattvayuktena dānaṃ tadvimalaṃ śivam \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. With a mind pervaded by the quality of Sattva (goodness) when a man makes presents to persons conversant with the knowledge of Brahma, only with the object of pleasing God such a gifr is called Vimala.

## \|\| 51.9 \|\|

*ikṣubhiḥ santatāṃ bhumiṃ yavagodhūmaśālinīm \|*  
*dadāti vedaviduṣe sa na bhūyo 'bhijāyate \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. If a man gives lands abounding in barley and corns and outskirted on all sides with sugarcane plants, he is never born again.

## \|\| 51.10 \|\|

*bhūmidānātparaṃ dānaṃ na bhūtaṃ na bhaviṣyati \|*  
*vidyāṃ dattvā brāhmaṇāya brahmaloke mahīyate \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. There never had been nor there will be any charity superior to the giving away of lands. By giving education", unto the Brahmanas one becomes glorified in the region of Brahma.

## \|\| 51.11 \|\|

*dadyādaharahastāstu śraddhayā brahmacāriṇe \|*  
*sarvapāpavinirmukto brahmasthānamavāpnuyāt \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. By giving reverentially food unto the Brahmacarins one, freed off of all sins, attains to the region of Brahma.

## \|\| 51.12-20 \|\|

*vaiśākhyāṃ paurṇamāsyāṃ tu brāhmaṇānsapta pañca ca \|*  
*upoṣyābhyarcayedvidvānmadhunā tilasarpiṣā \|\| 12 \|\|*

*gandhādibhiḥ samabhyarcya vācayedvā svayaṃ vadet \|*  
*prīyatāṃ dharmarājeti yathā manasi vartate \|\| 13 \|\|*

*yāvajjīvaṃ kṛtaṃ pāpaṃ tatkṣaṇādeva naśyati \|*  
*kṛṣṇājine tilānkṛtvā hiraṇyamadhusarpiṣā \|\| 14 \|\|*

*dadāti yastu viprāya sarvaṃ tarati duṣkṛtam \|*  
*ghṛtānnamudakaṃ caiva vaiśākhyāṃ ca viśeṣataḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*nirdiśya dharmarājāya viprebhyo mucyate bhayāt \|*  
*dvādaśyāmarcayedviṣṇumupoṣyāghapraṇāśanam \|\| 16 \|\|*

*sarvapāpavinirmukto naro bhavati niścitam \|*  
*yo hi yāṃ devatāmicchetsamārādhayituṃ naraḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*brāhmaṇānpūjayeddatnādbhojayedyoṣitaḥ surān \|*  
*santānakāmaḥ satataṃ pūjayedvai purandaram \|\| 18 \|\|*

*brahmavarcasakāmastu brāhmaṇānbrahmaniścayāt \|*  
*ārogyakāmo 'tha raviṃ dhanakāmo hutāśanam \|\| 19 \|\|*

*karmaṇāṃ siddhikāmastu pūjayedvai vināyakam \|*  
*bhogakāmo hi śaśinaṃ balakāmaḥ samīraṇam \|\| 20 \|\|*

12-20. If a person, after fasting on the full-moon dayin month of Vaisakha (March-April), adores twelve Brahmanas with honey and cakes of sessamum seeds or with scents or with sweet and moral words, all the sins, committed by him all through his life, are immediately dissipated. Having placed sessamum seeds, gold, honey and sarpl on skin of a black antelope he, who makes them over to a Brahmana, crosses over all his iniquities. He, who specially in the month of Vaisaka treats the Brahmanas with clarified butter, bolied rice and water in honour of Dharmaraja, becomes freed from all fear. It on the twelfth day of a fortnight a person adores Visnu who destroys all sins he forsooth becomes freed form all sins. Whatever deity a man wishes to adore, he must beforehand worship the Brahmanas and feed the women and celestials. He, who wishes to recover from a disease, must worship the Sun; while one, wishing for riches, should worship the fire-God. One, wishing for success in all his undertakings, should worship Vinayaka and one, wishing for enjoyments, should worship the moon. One, wishing for strength, should adore the Wind-god.

## \|\| 51.21 \|\|

*mumukṣuḥ sarvasaṃsārātprayatnenārcayeddharim \|*  
*akāmaḥ sarvakāmo vā pūjayettu gadādharam \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. And he, who wishes for emancipation from worldly fetters, should with every care adore Hari. He. who does not desire for any thing or he, who desires for every thing, should adore Gadadhara.

## \|\| 51.22 \|\|

*vāridastṛptimāpnoti sukhamakṣayyamannadaḥ \|*  
*tilapradaḥ prajāmiṣṭāṃ dīpadaścakṣuruttamam \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. The giver of ware attains to gratification. The giver of boiled rice enjoys happiness. The giver of sessamum seeds obtains good offspring and the giver of lamps most excellent eyes.

## \|\| 51.23 \|\|

*bhūmidaḥ sarvamāpnoti dīrghamāyurhiraṇyadaḥ \|*  
*gṛhado 'gryāṇi veśmāni rūpyado rūpamuttamam \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. One, who gives away lands, attains to all while the giver of gold acquires longevity. The giver of houses attains to the most exalted station in the world and the giver of silver a most handsome appearance.

## \|\| 51.24 \|\|

*vāsodaścāndrasālokyamaśvisālokyamaśvadaḥ \|*  
*anaḍuddaḥ śriyaṃ puṣṭāṃ godo bradhnasya viṣṭapam \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. The giver of dwelling houses attains to the region of the moon and the giver of horses to that of Asvins. The giver of bulls attains prosperity while the giver of kine attains to the region of Brahma.

## \|\| 51.25 \|\|

*yānaśayyāprado bhāryāmaiśvaryamabhayapradaḥ \|*  
*dhānyadaḥ śāvataṃ saukhyaṃ brahmado brahma śāśvatam \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. He, who gives conveyances and beddings, obtains a wife, and the giver of protection attains wealth. The giver of corns enjoys eternal happiness; while the giver of Brahma (knowledge of) attains to the neighbourhood of Brahma.

## \|\| 51.26 \|\|

*vedavitsu dadajjñānaṃ svargaloke mahīyate \|*  
*gavāṃ ghāsapradānena sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Imparting knowledge on the knowers of the Vedas one become glorified in the celestial region. By giving grass to the kine one becomes freed from all sins.

## \|\| 51.27-32 \|\|

*indhanānāṃ pradānena dīptāgnirjāyate naraḥ \|*  
*auṣadhaṃ snehamāhāraṃ rogirogapraśāntaye \|\| 27 \|\|*

*dadāno rogarahitaḥ sukhī dīrghāyureva ca \|*  
*asipatravanaṃ mārgaṃ kṣuradhārāsamanvitam \|\| 28 \|\|*

*tīkṣṇā tapaṃ ca taraticchatropānatprado naraḥ \|*  
*yadyadiṣṭatamaṃ loke yaccāsya dayitaṃ gṛhe \|\| 29 \|\|*

*tattadguṇavate deyaṃ tadevākṣayamicchatā \|*  
*ayena viṣuve caiva grahaṇe candrasūryayoḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

*saṃkrāntyādiṣu kāleṣu dattaṃ bhavati cākṣayam \|*  
*prayāgādiṣu tīrtheṣu gayāyāṃ ca viśeṣataḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*dānadharmātparo dharmo bhūtānāṃ nahe vidyate \|*  
*svargāyurbhūtikāmena dānaṃ pāpopaśāntaye \|\| 32 \|\|*

27-32. By giving sacrificial fuels a man becomes effulgent like fire. By giving to the diseased, for the removal of his ailments, medicines, attendance and food one becomes freed from diseases, enjoys happiness and lives long. By giving away umbrellas one passes unscathed through a road of Asipatra leaves, sharp as razor and does not suffer from the fierce ravs of the sun. He, who wishes things never to end, must give away unto qualified persons the various desired-for objects of the world and whatever is most favourite unto him in the house. If any thing is given away in charity during the equinox, the solar and lunar eclipses and on the. last day of a month it becomes never exhausted. There is no religious rite for a man to perform in this world superior to the making of charities in Prayaga (Allahabad) and and various other sacred places and especialty in Gaya where charities are made for attaining heaven and averting evils.

## \|\| 51.33 \|\|

*dīyamānaṃ tu yo mohādgoviprāgnisureṣu ca \|*  
*nivārayati pāpātmā tiryagyoniṃ vrajennaraḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. The sinful person, who prevents a Brahmana from worshipping sacred fire and celebrating sacrifices, goes to hell.

## \|\| 51.34 \|\|

*yastu durbhikṣavelāyāmannādyaṃ na prayacchati \|*  
*mriyamāṇeṣu vipreṣu brahmahā sa tu garhitaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. He, who does nor give food during a famine, becomes the hateful destroyer of the Brahmanas on account of their meeting with death (for his negligence).

## Chapter 52

## \|\| 52.1 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi prāyaścittavidhiṃ dvijāḥ \|*  
*brahmahā ca surāpaśca steyī ca gurutalpagaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Brahma said: — I will describe the regulations of Praya&ntta or penances. The principal sinners are those who kill Brahmanas, those who drink spirituous liquors, those who comm it thefts and those who violate the beds of their preceptors.

## \|\| 52.2 \|\|

*pañca pātakinastvete tatsaṃyogī ca pañcamaḥ \|*  
*upapāpāni gohatyāprabhṛtīni surā jaguḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. And the fifth class of sinners are those who associate with all those people. The minor sins, as described by the celestials, are the slaughtering of kine, etc.

## \|\| 52.3-4 \|\|

*brahmahā dvādaśābdāni kuṭīṃ kṛtvā vane vaset \|*  
*kuryādanaśanaṃ vātha bhṛgoḥ patanameva ca \|\| 3 \|\|*

*jvalantaṃ vā viśedagniṃ jalaṃ vā praviśetsvayam \|*  
*brāhmaṇārthe gavārthe vā samyak prāṇānparityajet \|\| 4 \|\|*

3-4. One, committing the sin of Brahmanicide, should make a cottage in a forest and live there for twelve years; or he should fast or level the summit of a mountain; or he should himself either enter imo tire or water. For the Brahmanas or the kine, he should entirely give up his life.

## \|\| 52.5 \|\|

*dattvā cānnaṃ ca viduṣe brahmahatyāṃ vyapohati \|*  
*aśvamedhāvabhṛthake snātvā vā mucyate dvijaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. By giving food fo the learned one may expatiate the sin of Brahmanicide. By performing a horse-sacrifice or bathing in a sacred shrine, one is freed from the sin.

## \|\| 52.6 \|\|

*sarvasvaṃ vā vedavide brāhmaṇāya pradāpayet \|*  
*sarasvatyāstaraṅgiṇyāḥ saṅgame lokaviśrute \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Or he should make over his all to a Brahmana, well read in the Vedas.

## \|\| 52.7-9 \|\|

*śuddhe triṣavaṇasnātastrirātropoṣito dvijaḥ \|*  
*setubandhe naraḥ snātvā mucyate brahmahatyayā \|\| 7 \|\|*

*kapālamocane snātvā vārāṇasyāṃ tathaiva ca \|*  
*surāpastu surāṃ pītvā agnivarṇāṃ dvijottamaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*payo ghṛtaṃ vā gomūtraṃ tasmātpāpātpramucyate \|*  
*suvarṇasteyī muktaḥ syānmusalena hato nṛpaiḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

7-9. A twice bron one should bathe thrice a day at the sacred and celebrated confluence of all the streams of the river Sarasvatl and fast for three nights. By bathing at the Setuvandha1, at Kapalmocana and Benares, one is freed from the sin of Brahmanicide. The twice-born, who has drunk spirituous liquor, is freed from the sin by drinking, hot as fire, wine, milk, clarified butter and cow's urine. By being killed by a king with a mace the stealer of gold is freed from the sin.

## \|\| 52.10-18 \|\|

*cīravāsā dvijo 'raṇye caredbrahmahaṇavratam \|*  
*gurubhāryāṃ samāruhya brāhmaṇaḥ kāmamohitaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*avagūhetstriyaṃ taptāṃ dīptāṃ kārṣṇāyasīṃ kṛtām \|*  
*gurvaṅganāgāminaśca careyurbahmahavratam \|\| 11 \|\|*

*cāndrāyaṇāni vā kuryātpañca catvāri vā punaḥ \|*  
*patitena ca saṃsargaṃ kurute yastu vai dvijaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*sa tatpāpāpanodārthaṃ tasyaiva vratamācaret \|*  
*taptakṛcchraṃ caredvātha saṃvatsaramatandritaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*sarvasvadānaṃ vidhivatsarvapāpaviśodhanam \|*  
*cāndrāyaṇaṃ ca vidhinā kṛtaṃ caivātikṛcchrakam \|\| 14 \|\|*

*puṇyakṣetre gayādau ca gamanaṃ pāpanāśanam \|*  
*amāvasyāṃ tithiṃ prāpya yaḥ samārādhayedbhavam \|\| 15 \|\|*

*brāhmaṇān bhojayitvā tu sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate \|*  
*upoṣitaścaturdaśyāṃ kṛṣṇapakṣe samāhitaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*yamāya dharmarājāya mṛtyave cāntakāya ca \|*  
*vaivasvatāya kālāya sarvabhūtakṣayāya ca \|\| 17 \|\|*

*pratyekaṃ tilasaṃyuktāndadyātsapta jalāñjalīn \|*  
*snātvā nadyāṃ tu pūrvāhne mucyate sarvapātakaiḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

10-18. For expiating the sin of Brahmanicide, a twice-born one should, clad in bark, live in the forest. A Brahmana, who possessed by lust, knows his preceptor's wife, is to embrace the heated figure of a woman made of black iron. Or he may observe the penance of Brahmanicide or perform the Candrayana2 vow. A Brahmana, who keeps company with degraded people, should perform the following penance for cleansing himself of the sin. He should undergo hardships without any sleep for one full year and duly give away his every thing. This will destroy all sins. Due celebration of Candrayana accompanied with all possible hardships and the visiting of sacred places, such as Gaya, also leads to the destruction of the sin. Не. who on an Amavasya day adores Bhava and feeds the Brahmanas, is also freed off of all sins. If one, bathing in a river in the forenoon and fasting on the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight, offers seven handfuls or water with sessamum seeds to Yama, Dharmaraja, Mrtyu, Anantaka, Vaivasvata, Kala and Sarvabhuta Kahaya (the destroyer and all creatures) he becomes freed from all sins.

## \|\| 52.19 \|\|

*brahmacaryamadhaḥ śayyāmupavāsaṃ dvijārcanam \|*  
*vrateṣveteṣu kurvīta śāntaḥ saṃyatamānasaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Having controlled his intellectual and mental faculties he should observe the vow of celibacy, sleep on earth, fast and adore ilie twice-born.

## \|\| 52.20 \|\|

*paṣṭhyāmupoṣito devaṃ śuklapakṣe samāhitaḥ \|*  
*saptamyāmarcayedbhānuṃ mucyate sarvapātakaiḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. On the sixth day from the full moon he should, with a controlled mind, adore the deity (Visnu), and on the seventh day, ilie sun-god. He would thus be freed off of all sins.

## \|\| 52.21 \|\|

*ekādaśyāṃ nirāhāraḥ samabhyarcya janārdanam \|*  
*dvādaśyāṃ śuklapakṣasya mahāpāpaiḥ pramucyate \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Having fasted and adored Janarddana on the eleventh and the twelfth days of the light fort night, one becomes freed from all great sins.

## \|\| 52.22 \|\|

*tapo japastīrthasevā devabrāhmaṇapūjanam \|*  
*grahaṇādiṣu kāleṣu mahāpātakanāśanam \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Recitation, visiting the sacred shrines and the worship of the deities and Brahmanas during an eclipse also destroys sins.

## \|\| 52.23 \|\|

*yaḥ sarvapāpayukto 'pi puṇyatīrtheṣu mānavaḥ \|*  
*niyamena tyajetprāṇānmucyate sarvapātakaiḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Even if visited by all sorts of sins, a man duly renounces his life at a sacred shrine he becomes freed from them all.

## \|\| 52.24 \|\|

*brahmaghnaṃ vā kṛtaghnaṃ vā mahāpātakadūṣitam \|*  
*bhartāramuddharennārī praviṣṭā saha pāvakam \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. If a woman enters into fire with her husband, she reclaims him, even if he be guilty of Brahmanicide, ingratitude or of other vile iniquities.

## \|\| 52.25 \|\|

*pativratā tu yā nārī bhartuḥ śuśrūṣaṇotsukā \|*  
*na tasyā vidyate pāpamiha loke paratra ca \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. he chaste woman, who is always anxious to serve her husband, is visited by no sin either in this world or in the next.

## \|\| 52.26 \|\|

*tathā rāmasya subhagā sītā trailokyaviśrutā \|*  
*patnī dāśaratherdevī vijigye rākṣaseśvaram \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. As it is said that the lucky wife of Rama, the son of Dasratha, SIta, celebrated in ilie world, defeated ilie king of Raksasas.

## \|\| 52.27 \|\|

*phalgutīrthādiṣu snātaḥ sarvācāraphalaṃ labhet \|*  
*ityāha bhagavānviṣṇuḥ purā mama yatavratāḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. By bathing in the sacred Phalgu river one reaps the fruit of all the religious rites. Formerly ilius did the divine Visnu speak to me, О ye of controlled actions.

## Chapter 53

## \|\| 53.1-5 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ brahmābravīcchrutvā hareraṣṭanidhīṃstathā \|*  
*tatra padmamahāpadmau tathā makarakacchapau \|\| 1 \|\|*

*mukundaku(na) ndau nīlaśca śaṅkhaścaivāparo nidhiḥ \|*  
*satyāmṛddhau bhavantyete svarūpaṃ kathayāmyaham \|\| 2 \|\|*

*padmena lakṣitaścaiva sāttviko jāyate naraḥ \|*  
*dākṣiṇyasāraḥ puruṣaḥ suvarṇādikasaṃgraham \|\| 3 \|\|*

*rupyādi kuryāddadyāttu yatidaivādiyajvanām \|*  
*mahāpadmāṅkito dadyāddhanādyaṃ dhārmikāya ca \|\| 4 \|\|*

*nīdhī padmamahāpadmau sāttvikau puruṣau smṛtī \|*  
*makareṇāṅkitaḥ khaḍgabāṇakuntādisaṃgrahī \|\| 5 \|\|*

1-5. Suta said: — Thus did Brahma describe the eight Nidhis1 as the had heard from Visnu. They are Padma, Mahapadma, Makara, Kacchapa, Mukunda, Nanda and Nila. And the other Nidhi is iaankha. I will now describe their characteristic marks. A person, bearing the mark of Padma, becomes Sattvika (pervaded by the quality of goddess). He is compassionate by nature, collects gold, silver, etc., and dedicates them to Yatis. celestials and ascetics. I Divine trasures of Kubera nine of which arc enumerated viz,, the Padma. Maha-padma, Sankha, Makara, Kaechapa, Mukunda. Nanda, Nila and Kharba: their nature is not exactly defined though some of them appears to be precious gems. According to the Tilntrik system they are personified and worshipped as demigods attendant either upon Kubera or upon LaksmI. A person, bearing the mark Mahapadma, gives away wealth unto the pious. Persons, bearing the marks of Padma and Mahapadma Nidhis, are called Sattvika. A person,,bearing the mark of Makara, becomes the collector of swords, arrows and lances.

## \|\| 53.6 \|\|

*dadyācchrutāya maitrīṃ ca yāti nityaṃ ca rājabhiḥ \|*  
*dravyārthaṃ śatruṇā nāśaṃ saṃgrāme cāpi saṃvrajet \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. He gives away wealth unto persons, well- read in Shrutis and contracts friendship with kings. He also destroys his enemies in battle.

## \|\| 53.7-9 \|\|

*makaraḥ kacchapaścaiva tāmasau tu nidhī smṛtau \|*  
*kacchapī viśvasennaiva na bhuṅkena (nā) dadāti ca \|\| 7 \|\|*

*nidhānamurvyāṃ kurute nidhiḥ sopyekapūruṣaḥ \|*  
*rājasenamukundena lakṣitā rājyasaṃgrahī \|\| 8 \|\|*

*bhuktabhogo gāyanebhyo dadyādveśyādikāsu ca \|*  
*rajastamomayo nandī ādhāraḥ syātkulasya ca \|\| 9 \|\|*

7-9. Makara and Kacchapa are the two Tamasik (pervaded by the quality of ignorance) Nidhis. One, bearing the mark of Kacchapa, does not confide in anyone and does not eat; nor does he give anything to anyone. That singular person, bearing the mark of this Nidhi, fills the earth with treasures. A person, bearing the mark of the Rajasik (pervaded by the quality of darkness) Nidhi Mukunda, becomes the collector of kingdoms. He enjoys freely and liberally and makes presents to the songsters and prostitutes.

## \|\| 53.10 \|\|

*stutaḥ prīto bhavati vai bahubhāryā bhavanti ca \|*  
*pūrvamitreṣu śaithilyaṃ prītimanyaiḥ karoti ca \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. A person, bearing the mark of Nanda pervaded by the qualities of, darkness and ignorance, becomes the support" of his family, always chased with eulogy and the husband of many wives. He loses affection for his former friends and finds delight in new ones.

## \|\| 53.11 \|\|

*nīlana cāṅkitaḥ sattvatejasā saṃyuto bhavet \|*  
*vastradhānyādisaṃgrāhī taḍāgādi karoti ca \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. One, bearing the mark of Nila, is endued with the virtues of Sattva guna. He collects clothes and corns and digs tanks, etc.

## \|\| 53.12 \|\|

*tripū(pau) ruṣo nidhiścaiva āmrārāmādi kārayet \|*  
*ekasya syānnidhiḥ śaṅkhaḥ svayaṃ bhuṅkte dhanādi(nta)kam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. The Niddhi Shankha is selfish and himself squanders away his money. His relatives live on a very wretched fare and do not put on beautiful raiments.

## \|\| 53.13 \|\|

*kadannabhukparijano na ca śobhanavastradhṛk \|*  
*svapoṣaṇaparaḥ śaṅkhī dadyātparanare vṛthā \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. One, bearing the mark of iSankha, is always busy with seeking his own pleasure and does not give his money to anyone else.

## \|\| 53.14 \|\|

*miśrāvalokanānmiśrasvabhāvaphaladāyinaḥ \|*  
*nidhīnāṃ rūpamuktaṃ tu hariṇāpi harādike \|*  
*harirbhuvanakośādi yathovāca tathā vade \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. The characters of these Nidhis were thus described by Hari unto Нага and others. I describe the treasures of the world as recounted by Hari.

## Chapter 54

## \|\| 54.1-4 \|\|

*hariruvāca \|*  
*agnīdhraścāgnibāhuśca bapuṣmāndhyutimāṃstathā \|*  
*medhāmedhātithirbhavyaḥ śabalaḥ putra eva ca \|\| 1 \|\|*

*jyotiṣmāndaśamo jātaḥ putrā hyete priyavratāt \|*  
*medhāgnibāhuputrāstu trayo yogaparāyaṇāḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*jātismarā mahābhāgā nairājyāya mamo daṣuḥ \|*  
*vibhajya sapta dvīpāni saptānāṃ pradadau nṛpaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*yojanānāṃ pramāṇena pañcāśatkoṭirāplutā \|*  
*jalopari mahī yātā maurivāste sarijjale \|\| 4 \|\|*

1-4. Hari said: — Agnidhra, Agnivahu, Vapusman, Dyutiman, Medhatithi, Bhavya, Cabbala, Putra, and the tenth Jyotisman — these were the sons of Priyavrata. Medha and Agnivahu had three sons each, who were given to Yoga, were great, had the recollection of their pristine births and fixed their minds on the kingdom. Having divided-the earth into seven insular continents the king conferred them on his seven sons. The earth is situated on the water like unto a boat and is five hundred koti yojanas in dimension.

## \|\| 54.5 \|\|

*jambūplakṣāhvayau dvīpau śālmalaścāparo hara \|*  
*kuśaḥ krauñcastathā śākaḥ puṣkaraścaiva saptamaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. О Нага, the two insular continents are Jambu and Plaksa. The next is Salmala. The others are Kusa, Krounca and Йака. The seventh is Puskara.

## \|\| 54.6 \|\|

*ete dvīpāḥ samudraistu sapta saptabhirāvṛtāḥ \|*  
*lavaṇekṣusurāsarpirdādhidugdhajalaiḥ samam \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. All these islands are each girt by seven oceans. They are Lavana, Iksu, Sura, Sarpi, Dadhi, Dugdha, and water.

## \|\| 54.7 \|\|

*dvīpāttu dviguṇo dvīpaḥ samudraśca vṛṣadhvaja \|*  
*jambūdvīpe sthito merurlakṣayojanavistṛtaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Each ocean is double in dimension than the island it encircles, О blue-emblemed deity. In the insular continent of Jambu is situate the mount Meru extending over a lakh of Yojanas.

## \|\| 54.8 \|\|

*caturaśītisāhasrairyojanairasya cocchrayaḥ \|*  
*praviṣṭaḥ ṣoḍaśādhastāddvatriṃśanmūrdhni vistṛtaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Its summit is eighty four thousand Yojanas in height. Its base is sixteen thousand Yojanas and is of the shape of a pericarp of a lotus.

## \|\| 54.9-10 \|\|

*adhaḥ ṣoḍaśasāhasraḥ karṇikākārasaṃsyitaḥ \|*  
*himavānhemakūṭaśca niṣadhaścāsya dakṣiṇe \|\| 9 \|\|*

*nīlaḥ śvetaśca śṛṅgī ca uttare varṣaparvatāḥ \|*  
*plakṣādiṣu narā rudra ye vasanti sanātanāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. The boundary mountains Himavan, Hemakuta and Nisadha are situate on its south, while Nila, 6veta and Srngl mountains are situate in the north. О Rudra, the persons, who live in the insular continent of Plaksa, are immortal.

## \|\| 54.11-13 \|\|

*śaṅkarātha na teṣvasti yugāvasthā kathañcana \|*  
*jambūdvīpeśvarātputrā hyagrīdhnādabhavannava \|\| 11 \|\|*

*nābhiḥ kiṃpuruṣaścaiva harivarṣamilā vṛtaḥ \|*  
*ramyo hiraṇmayākhyaśca kururbhadrāśva eva ca \|\| 12 \|\|*

*ketumālo nṛpastebhyastatsaṃjñān khaṇḍakāndadau \|*  
*nābhestu merudevyāṃ tu putro 'bhūdṛṣabho hara \|\| 13 \|\|*

11-13. О Sankara, there is no division of Yugas (cycles) in all these islands. Agnidhra, the king of the insular continent Jambu, hadining sons, viz. Nabhi, Kimpurusa, Harivarsa, Havrta, Ramya, Hiranvan, 6astha, Kurubhadrasva and Ketumala. The king divided his kingdom into nine parts and conferred them on all his sons. Nabhi begat on Merudevya a son by name Rs abha.

## \|\| 54.14 \|\|

*tatputro bharato nāma śālagrāme sthito vratī \|*  
*sumatirbharatasyābhūttatputrastaijaso 'bhavat \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. His son, the ascetic Bharata lived in Shalagrama. Bharata's son was Sumati whose son was Tejasa.

## \|\| 54.15 \|\|

*indradyumnaśca tatputraḥ parameṣṭhī tataḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*pratīhāraścatatputraḥ pratihartā tadātmajaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. His son was Indradyumna, whose son was known as Paramesthi. The latter's son was Pratihara whose son was Pratiharta.

## \|\| 54.16 \|\|

*sutastasmādathai jātaḥ prastārastatsuto vibhuḥ \|*  
*pṛthuśca tatsuto nakto naktasyāpi gayaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. He begat a son by name Prastara whose son was the powerful Prthu. His son was Nakta whose son was Gaya.

## \|\| 54.17 \|\|

*naro gayasya tanayastatputrobhudvirāḍagataḥ \|*  
*tato dhīmānmahātejā bhauvanastasya cātmajaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Gaya's son was Nara whose son was Buddhirata. His son was the intelligent and highly powerful Bhouvana.

## \|\| 54.18 \|\|

*tvaṣṭā tvaṣṭuśca virajā rajastasyāpyabhūtsutaḥ \|*  
*śatajidrajasastasya viṣvagjyotiḥ sutaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. He had four sons, viz., Tvasta, Tvastu, Viraja and Rajas. Raja's son was Satajit whose son was Visvakjyot.

## Chapter 55

## \|\| 55.1-2 \|\|

*hariruvāca \|*  
*madhye tvilāvṛto varṣo bhadrāśvaḥ pūrvato 'dbhutaḥ \|*  
*pūrvadakṣaiṇato varṣo hiraṇvānvṛṣabhadhvaja \|\| 1 \|\|*

*tataḥ kimpuruṣo varṣo merordakṣiṇataḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*bhārato dakṣiṇe prokto harirdakṣiṇapāścime \|\| 2 \|\|*

1-2. Hari said: — In the centre is situate the kingdom of Ilavrta; while that to Bhadrasva is situate in the east. In the south-east in situate Hiranvanvarsa, О bull-emblemed deity, Kimpurusa Varsa is situate in the south of the mount Meru. Bharata Varsa is situate in the south, while Hari in the south-west. mRnA TU\|cb: 4f^Emhrlttl

## \|\| 55.3 \|\|

*paścime ketumālaśca ramyakaḥ paścimottare \|*  
*uttare ca kurorvarṣaḥ kalpavṛkṣasamāvṛtaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Ketumala is situate in the west, while Ramyaka, in the north-west. In the north is situate Kuruvarsa covered with Kalpa trees.

## \|\| 55.4-5 \|\|

*siddhiḥ svābhāvikī rudra ! varjayitvā tu bhāratam \|*  
*indradvīpaḥ kaśerumāṃstāmravarṇo gabhastitamān \|\| 4 \|\|*

*nāgadvīpaḥ kaṭāhaśca siṃhalo vāruṇastathā \|*  
*ayaṃ tunavamasteṣāṃ dvīpaḥ sāgarasaṃvṛtaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. О Rudra, except Bharata Varsa, Siddhi is naturally obtainable every where. Indradvipa, Kserumana, Tamravarna, Gabhastiman, Naga- dvlpa, Kataha, Simhala and Varina — these are the nine inlands each encircled by an ocean.

## \|\| 55.6 \|\|

*pūrve kirātāstasyāste paścime yavanāḥ sthitāḥ \|*  
*andhrā dakṣiṇato rudra ! turaṣkāstvapi cottare \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. The Kiratas live in the east, the Yavanas in the west, the Andhras in the south, and the Turaskas in the north.

## \|\| 55.7-8 \|\|

*brāhmaṇāḥ kṣattriyā vaiśyāḥ sūdrāścāntaravāsinaḥ \|*  
*mahendro malayaḥ sahyaḥ śuktimānṛkṣaparvataḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*vindhyaśca pāriyātraśca saptātra kulaparvatāḥ \|*  
*vedasmṛtir narmadā ca varadā surasā śivā \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. The Brahmanas, K?atriyas, VaiSyas and Sudras live in the central group of the islands. Mahendra, Malaya, Sahya, fsuktimana, Riksa, Vindhya, Paribhadra, — all these are the seven boundary mountains. Vedasmrti, Narmadam, Varada, Surasa, Siva.

## \|\| 55.9-11 \|\|

*tāpī payoṣṇī sarayūḥ kāverī gomatī tathā \|*  
*godāvarī bhīmarathī kṛṣṇaveṇī mahānadī \|\| 9 \|\|*

*ketumālā tāmraparṇo candrabhāgā sarasvatī \|*  
*ṛṣikulyā ca kāverī mattagaṅgā payasvinī \|\| 10 \|\|*

*vidarbhā ca śatadrūśca nadyaḥ pāpaharāḥ śubhāḥ \|*  
*āsāṃ pibanti salilaṃ madhyadeśādayo janāḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

9-11. Tapi, Payosni, Sarayu, Kaveri, Gomati, Godavari, Bhimarathi, Krsnavarna, Mahanadi, Ketumala, Tamraparni, Candrabhaga, Saras- vati, Rsikulya, Mattaganga, Payasvini. Vidarbha and Satadru — these are the sacred rivers destructive of all sins. The inhabitants of the central countries drink the water of all these rivers.

## \|\| 55.12 \|\|

*pāñcālāḥ kuravo matsyā yaudheyāḥ sapaṭaccarāḥ \|*  
*kuntayaḥ śūrasenāśca madhyadeśajanāḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Pancalas, Kurus, Matsyas, Youdheyas, Sapatacaras, Kuntis and 6tirasenas, are the the clans who inhabit the central countries.

## \|\| 55.13-14 \|\|

*vṛṣadhvaja ! janāḥ pādmāḥ sūtamāgadhacedayaḥ \|*  
*kāśaya (ṣāyā) śca videhāśca pūrvasyāṃ kosalāstathā \|\| 13 \|\|*

*kaliṅgavaṅgapuṇḍrāṅgā vaidarbhā mūlakāstathā \|*  
*vindhyāntarnilayā deśāḥ pūrvadakṣiṇataḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

13-14. О bull-emblemed deity, the Padmas, Sutas, Magadhas, Cedis, KaSayas, Videhas live in the eastern countries. Kosalas, Kalihgas, Vartgas, Pundrangas, Mulakas as well as those living around the Vindhya ranges are said to inhabit south-eastern countries.

## \|\| 55.15 \|\|

*pulandāśmakajīmūtanayarāṣṭranivāsinaḥ \|*  
*karṇār(nā)ṭakambojaghaṇā dakṣiṇāpathavāsinaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. The inhabitants of Pulinda, ASmaka and Jimutanaya as-well as Kambojas, Kanatas and Ghafas are called Southerners.

## \|\| 55.16 \|\|

*ambaṣṭhadraviḍā lāṭāḥ kāmbhojā strīmukhāḥ śakāḥ \|*  
*ānartavāsinaścaiva jñeyā yakṣiṇapaścime \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. The people of Ambastha, Dravi4a, Lata, Kamboja, Strimukha, бака, and Anartha are said to inhabit south-western, countries.

## \|\| 55.17 \|\|

*strīrājyāḥ saindhavā mlecchā nāsti kā yavanāstathā \|*  
*paścimena ca vijñeyā māthurā naiṣadhaiḥ saha \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Strairajyas, Saindhavas, Mlecchas and the godless Yavanas together with Naisadhas and the people of Mathura are known as inhabiting the western countries.

## \|\| 55.18 \|\|

*māṇḍavyāśca tuṣārāśca mūlikāśvamukhāḥ khaśāḥ \|*  
*mahākeśā mahānāsā deśāstūttarapaścime \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Mandavya, Tusara, Mulika, Musa, Kosa, Mahakesa, Mahanada are the countries lying in the north-west.

## \|\| 55.19 \|\|

*lamba (mpā) kā stananāgāśca mādragāndhārabāhlikāḥ \|*  
*himācalālayā mlecchā udīcīṃ diśamāśritāḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Lambakas, Tananagas, Madragandhara, Vahyikas are the Mlecchas living in the north beyond the Himalaya.

## \|\| 55.20 \|\|

*trigartanīlakolāta (bha) brahmaputrāḥ saṭaṅkaṇāḥ \|*  
*abhīṣāhāḥ sakāśmīrā udakparveṇa kīrtitāḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Trigarta, Nilakolabha, Brahmaputra, Sata ankana, Abhlsaha and Kasmira are all situated in the north.

## Chapter 56

## \|\| 56.1-2 \|\|

*hariruvāca \|*  
*sapta medhātitheḥ putrāḥ plakṣadvīpeśvarasya ca \|*  
*jyeṣṭhaḥ śāntabhavo nāma śiśirastadantaraḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*sukhodayastathā nandaḥ śivaḥ kṣemaka eva ca \|*  
*dhruvaśca saptamasteṣāṃ plakṣadvīpeśvarā hi te \|\| 2 \|\|*

1-2. Hari said: — Medatithi, the king of the insualr continent of Plaksa, had seven sons, viz,, the eldest Santabhava, Sisira, Sukhovaya, Nanda, Siva, Ksemaka and Dhruva. These seven were the kings of the insular continent Plaksa.

## \|\| 56.3 \|\|

*gomedaścaiva candraśca nārado dundubhistathā \|*  
*somakaḥ sumanāḥ śailo baibhrājaścātra saptamaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Gomeda, Candra, Narada, Dundubhi, Somaka, Sumana, and Saila were the seven sons of Vibhraja.

## \|\| 56.4 \|\|

*anutaptā śikhī caiva vipāśā tridivā kramuḥ \|*  
*amṛtā sukṛtā caiva saptaitāstatra nimnagāḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Anutapta, Sikhi, Vipasa, Tridiva, Krama, Amrta and Sukrta were the seven rivers.

## \|\| 56.5-8 \|\|

*vapuṣmāñchālmalasyeśastatsutā varṣanāmakāḥ \|*  
*śveto 'tha haritaścaiva jīmūto rohitastathā \|\| 5 \|\|*

*vaidyuto mānasaścaiva saprabhaśācapi saptamaḥ \|*  
*kumudaśconnato droṇo mahiṣo 'tha balāhakaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*krauñcaḥ kakudmānhyete vai girayaḥ saritastvimāḥ \|*  
*yonitoyā vitṛṣṇā ca candrā śukla vimocanī \|\| 7 \|\|*

*vidhṛtiḥ saptamī tāsāṃ smṛtāḥ pāpapraśāntidāḥ \|*  
*jyotiṣmataḥ kuśadvīpe sapta putrāḥ śṛṇuṣvatān \|\| 8 \|\|*

5-8. Vapusman was the king of the insular continem Salmala. His sons were called Varsas. They were Sveta, Harita, Jimuta, Rohita, Vaidyuta. Manasa and Saprabha, Kumuda, Unnata, Drona, "Mahisa, Valahaka, Krounca and Kakudman, these seven were the mountains. The rivers were Yoni, Toya, Vitrsna, Candra, Sukla and Vimocanl; the seventh was Vidhrit; and they all afforded release from sins. Jyotisman, the king of the insular continent Kusa, had seven Sons. Hear their names.

## \|\| 56.9 \|\|

*udbhido veṇumāṃścaiva dvairatho lambano dhṛtiḥ \|*  
*prabhākaro 'tha kapilastannāmā varṣapaddhatiḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. They were Udbhida, Venuman, Dvairatha, Lambana, Dhrti, Prabhakara and Kapila.

## \|\| 56.10 \|\|

*vidrumo hemaśailaśca dyutimānpuṣpavāṃstathā \|*  
*kuśeśayo hariścaiva saptamo mandarācalaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. The moimtains were Vidruma, Hemasaila, Dyutiman. Puspaman, Kusesaya, Hari and the munt Mandara.

## \|\| 56.11 \|\|

*dhūtapāpā śivā caiva pavitrā sanmatistathā \|*  
*vidyudabhrā mahī cānyā sarvapāpaharāstvimāḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. The rivers were Dhutapapa, Siva, Pavitra, Sammati Vidyudambha, Mahikasa. They were all destructive of all sins.

## \|\| 56.12-16 \|\|

*krauñcadvīpe dyutimataḥ putrāḥ sapta mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*kuśalo mandagaścoṣṇaḥ pīvaro 'thondhakārakaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*muniśca dundubhiścaiva saptaite tatsutā hara \|*  
*krauñcaśca vāmanaścaiva tṛtīyaścāndha (tha) kārakaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*divāvṛtpañcamaścānyo dundubhiḥ puṇḍarīkavān \|*  
*gaurī kumudvatī caiva sandhyā rātrirmanojavā \|\| 14 \|\|*

*khyātiśca puṇḍarīkā ca saptaitā varṣanimnagāḥ \|*  
*śākadvīpeśvarādbhavyātsapta putrāḥ prajajñire \|\| 15 \|\|*

*jaladśca kumāraśca sukumāroruṇī bakaḥ \|*  
*kusumodaḥ samodārkiḥ saptamaśca mahādrumaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

12-16. Dyutiman had seven high-souled sons in the insular continent of Krounca, Kusala, Mandaga, Usna, Pivara, Andhakaraka, Muni and Dun-dubhi; these seven were his sons, О Нага. The seven mountains were Krounca, Vamana, the third Andhakaraka, Devavrta, Mahasaila, Dundubhi and Pandarikavan. Gaurl, Kumudvati, Sandhya, Ratri, Manojava, Khyatl and Pundarika-these seven were the boundary rivers. The king of the insular continent of Shaka begat seven, sons, viz., Jalada, Kumara, Sukumara, Masibaka, Kusumoda, SamodarkI and the seventh Mahadruma.

## \|\| 56.17 \|\|

*sukumārī kumārī ca nalinī dhenukā ca yā \|*  
*ikṣuśca veṇukā caiva gabhastī saptamī tathā \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Sukumari, Kumarl, Nalinl, Dhenuka, Iksu, Velnuka and Gabhasti were the seven rivers.

## \|\| 56.18 \|\|

*śabalātpuṣkareśācca mahāvīraśca dhātakiḥ \|*  
*abhūdvarṣadvayaṃ caiva mānasottaraparvataḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Zavala, the king of Puskara, begat the great hero Dhatakl. The two Varsas were situate on the mount Manasottara.

## \|\| 56.19 \|\|

*yojanānāṃ sahasrāṇi ūrdhvaṃ pañcāśaducchritaḥ \|*  
*tāvaccaiva ca vistīrṇaḥ sarvataḥ parimaṇḍalaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. It was a thousand Yojanas in height. Its summit was five hundred yojanas high and its extent an all sides, was the same.

## \|\| 56.20-21 \|\|

*svādūdakenodadhinā puṣkaraḥ pariveṣṭitaḥ \|*  
*svādūdakasya purato dṛśyate lokasaṃsthitiḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*dviguṇā kāñcanī bhūmiḥ sarvajantuvivarjitā \|*  
*lokālokastataḥ śailo yojanāyutāvistṛtaḥ \|*  
*tamasā parvato vyāptastamo 'pyaṇḍakaṭāhataḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

20-21. The insular continent of Puskara is encircled on allies by the ocean of sweet water. Before the sweet waler is seen the country inhabited by people; the gold fields, shorn of all animals, constitute Ihe half of the continent. The mountain is Lokaloka, one Ayuta of yojanas in extent. One part of this mountain is enshrouded with darkness and the other part is free from it.

## Chapter 57

## \|\| 57.1-2 \|\|

*hariruvāca \|*  
*saptatistu sahasrāṇi bhūmyucchrāyo 'pi kathyate \|*  
*daśasāhasramekaikaṃ pātālaṃ vṛṣabhadhvaja \|\| 1 \|\|*

*atalaṃ vitalaṃ caiva nitalaṃ ca gabhastimat \|*  
*mahākhyaṃ sutalaṃ cāgryaṃ pātālaṃ cāpi saptamam \|\| 2 \|\|*

1-2. Hari said: — Twenty seven thousand yojanas is the exlent of the earth and ten thousand and one is thai of the nether region. О bull-emblemed deity, Atala, Vitala, Nitala, Gabhastiman, Mahaksya, Sutala and Agra are the seven Patalas.

## \|\| 57.3 \|\|

*kṛṣṇā śuklāruṇā pītā śarkarā śailakāñcanā \|*  
*bhūyastatra daiteyā vasanti ca bhujaṅgamāḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Krsna (dark-blue), ^uklarna (white as sun), Pita (yellow), багкага and Sailakancana are the lands Ihere where the Daityas and serpents reside.

## \|\| 57.4-7 \|\|

*raudre tu puṣkaradvīpe narakāḥ santi tāñchṛṇu \|*  
*rauravaḥ sūkaro rodhastālo vinaśanastathā \|\| 4 \|\|*

*mahājvālastaptakumbho lavaṇo 'thi vimohitaḥ \|*  
*rudhirākhyo vaitaraṇī kṛmiśaḥ kṛmibho janaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*asipatravanaḥ kṛṣṇo nānābhakṣaśca dāruṇaḥ \|*  
*tathā pūyavahaḥ pāpo vahnijvālastvadhaḥ śirāḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*saṃdaṃśaḥ kṛṣṇasūtraśca tamaścāvīcireva ca \|*  
*śvabhojano 'thāpratiṣṭhoṣṇavīcirnarakāḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

4-7. In the terrific insular continent of Puskara are situate the hells. Hear their names. They are Rourava, Sukara, Rodha, Tala, Visasana, Mahajvala, Taptakumbha, Lavana, Vimdhita, Rudhira, VaitaranI, Krmisa, Krmibhojana, Asipatravana, Krsna, the terrific hell Nabhaksa, Puyavaha, Papa, Vanhijvala, Krsnsutra, Tama, Avici, 6vabhojana, Apratista, Usavicl.

## \|\| 57.8 \|\|

*pāpinasteṣu pacyante viṣaśastrāgnidāyinaḥ \|*  
*uparyupari vai lokā rudra ! bhūtādayaḥ sthitāḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. The sinners who administer poison, use weapons and set fire, are wasted there. О Rudra, the various lokas or regions are situate one over another.

## \|\| 57.9-10 \|\|

*vārivahnyanilākāśairvṛtaṃ bhūtādinā ca tat \|*  
*tadaṇḍaṃ mahatā rudra ! pradhānena ca veṣṭitam \|\| 9 \|\|*

*aṇḍaṃ daśaguṇaṃ vyāptaṃ nārāyaṇaḥ sthitaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. The various elements are also situate in this order. О Rudra, the egg is encircled by the principle of greatness and that again by water, fire and ether covering the space ten times dlat occupied by the egg.

## Chapter 58

## \|\| 58.1 \|\|

*hariruvāca \|*  
*vakṣye pramāṇasaṃsthāne sūryādīnāṃ śṛṇuṣva me \|*  
*yojānānāṃ sahasrāṇi bhāskarasya ratho nava \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Hari said: — Hear, I will now describe the position and the dimension of the sun and other planets. The sun has nine cars, each a thousand yojanas in dimension.

## \|\| 58.2-3 \|\|

*īṣādaṇḍastathaivāsya dviguṇo vṛṣabhadhvaja \|*  
*sārdhakoṭistathā sapta niyutānyadhikāni ca \|\| 2 \|\|*

*yojanānāṃ tu tasyākṣastatra cakraṃ pratiṣṭhitam \|*  
*trinābhimati pañcāre ṣaṇneminyakṣayātmake \|\| 3 \|\|*

2-3. Twice this number is the dimension of its plough, О bull-emblemed deity. Half a koh and seven Niyuta of yojanas is the dimension of its Aksa (part of wheel), where the wheel is placed. It has three naves and six Nemis (circumference).

## \|\| 58.4 \|\|

*saṃvatsaramaye kṛtsnaṃ kālacakraṃ pratiṣṭhitam \|*  
*catvāriṃśatsahasrāṇi dvitīyo 'kṣo vivasvataḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. This wheel goes one round within one full year. The second Aksa of the car of Vivasvan is forty thousand yojanas in dimension.

## \|\| 58.5-6 \|\|

*pañcānyāni tu sārdhāni syandanasya vṛṣadhvaja \|*  
*akṣapramāṇamubhayoḥ pramāṇaṃ tu yugārdhayoḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*hrasvo 'kṣastadyugārdhena dhruvādhāre rathasya vai \|*  
*dvitīye 'kṣe tu taccakraṃ saṃsthitaṃ mānasācale \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. The five others have each half the same dimension. О bull-emblemed deity. The extent of each of the two Aksas is half a yoga (cycle); the smaller Aksa, of the car, with half the cycle is stationed in the polar star. And the second wheel is stationed in the mount Manasa.

## \|\| 58.7 \|\|

*gāyattrī sabṛhatyuṣṇigjagatītriṣṭubeva ca \|*  
*anuṣṭuppaṅktirityuktāśchandāṃsi harayo raveḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Gayatri, Samvrhatl, Usnic, Jagati, Trstup, Anustup, and Pankti-these metres are the the horses of the sun.

## \|\| 58.8-10 \|\|

*dhātā kratusthalā caiva pulastyo vāsukistathā \|*  
*rathakṛdgrāmaṇīrhetistumburuścaitramāsake \|\| 8 \|\|*

*aryamā pulahaścaiva rathojāḥ puñjikasthalā \|*  
*prahetiḥ kacchanīraśca nāradaścaiva mādhave \|\| 9 \|\|*

*mitro 'tristakṣako rakṣaḥ pauruṣeyo 'tha menakā \|*  
*hāhā rathasvanaścaiva jyeṣṭhe bhāno rathe sthitāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

8-10. Dhata, Kratusthala. Pulastya, Vasuki, Rathakrt. Agramam, Heti and Tumbhru reside in the solar disc in the month of Caitra, Aryama, Pulaha, Rathoujas, Punjikasthala, Praheti, Kaccha, NIra and Narada in the month of Vaisaka. Mitra, Atri, Taksaka, Raksa, Pouruseya, Menaka, Haha, Rathasvana reside on the car of the sun in the month of Jyestha.

## \|\| 58.11 \|\|

*varuṇo vasiṣṭho rambhā sahajanyā kuhūrbudhaḥ \|*  
*rathacitrastathā śukro vasantyāṣāḍhasaṃjñite \| \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Varuna, Vasistha, Rambha, Sajanya, Kuhu, Budha, Rathacitra and Shukra live in the month of Asadha.

## \|\| 58.12 \|\|

*indro viśvāvasuḥ srota(śrotra) elāpatrastathāṅgirāḥ \|*  
*pramlocā ca nabhasyete sarpāścārke tu santi vai \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Indra, Visvavasu, Srota, Elapatra, Angira, Pramloca and Nabha-these serpents live in the month of Havana.

## \|\| 58.13 \|\|

*vivasvānugrasenaśca bhṛgurāpūraṇastathā \|*  
*anumlocāśaṅkhapālau vyāghro bhādrapade tatā \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Vivasvan, Ugrasena, Bhrgu, Apurana, Anumloca, Shankhapala and Vyagra live in the month of Bhadrapada.

## \|\| 58.14 \|\|

*pūṣā ca surucirdhātā gautamo 'tha dhanañjayaḥ \|*  
*suṣeṇo 'nyo dhṛtācī ca vasantyāśvayuje ravau \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Pusa, Suruci, Dhata, Goutama, Dhananjaya, Susena, GhrtacI live in the sun in the month of Asvina.

## \|\| 58.15 \|\|

*viśvāvasurbharadvājaḥ parjanyairāvatau tadā \|*  
*viśvācī senajiccāpaḥ (pi) kārtike cādhikāriṇaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Visvavasu, Bharadvaja, Parjanya, Airavata. Visvaci, Senajit, and Apa — these are entitled to live in the month of Kartika.

## \|\| 58.16 \|\|

*aṃśuśca kāśyapastārkṣyo mahāpadmastathorvaśī \|*  
*citrasenastathā vidyunmārgaśīrṣādhikāriṇaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Ansu, Kasyapa, Tarksya, Mahapadma, UrvasI, Citrasena, and Vidyut live in tile month of Agrahavana.

## \|\| 58.17 \|\|

*kraturbhargastathorṇāyuḥ sphūrjaḥ karkoṭakastathā \|*  
*ariṣṭanemiścaivānyā pūrvacittivarrātsarāḥ \|*  
*pauṣamāse vasantyete sapta bhāskaramaṇḍale \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Kratu, Bharga, Urnayu, Sphurja, Bharga, Urnayu, Karkot, Aristanemi, Purvacitti, and the most excellent Apsarasa live in the solar disc in the month of Pousa.

## \|\| 58.18 \|\|

*tvaṣṭātha jamadagniśca kambalo 'tha tilottamā \|*  
*brahmāpeto 'tha ṛtajiddhṛtarāṣṭraśca saptamaḥ \|*  
*māghamāse vasantyete sapta bhāskaramaṇḍale \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Tvasta, Jamadagni. Kamsala, Tilottama, Brahmapeta, Ritajit and Dhrtarastra live in the solar disc in the month of Magha.

## \|\| 58.19 \|\|

*viṣṇuraśvataro rambhā sūryavarcāśca satyajit \|*  
*viśvāmitrastathā rakṣo yajñāpeto hi phālgune \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Visru, Asvatara, Rambha, Suryavarcca, Satyajit, Visvamitra, Raksa and Yajnapeta live in the month of Phalguna.

## \|\| 58.20 \|\|

*saviturmaṇḍale brahmanviṣṇuśaktyupabṛṃhitāḥ \|*  
*stuvanti munayaḥ sūryaṃ gandharvairgoyate puraḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. О Brahman, the solar disc is pervaded by the energies of Visnu. The ascetics laud the sun and the Gandharvas sing before.

## \|\| 58.21 \|\|

*nṛtyantyo 'psaraso yānti sūryasyānuniśācarāḥ \|*  
*vahanti pannagā yakṣaiḥ kriyate 'bhīṣusaṃgrahaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. The Apsaras dance and the night-rangers follow the sun. The Pannagas carry (the vehicle) and the Yaksas collect the bridles.

## \|\| 58.22-23 \|\|

*bālakhilyāstathaivainaṃ parivārya samāsate \|*  
*rathastricakraḥ somasya kundābhāstasya vājinaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*vāmadakṣiṇato yuktā daśa tena caratyasau \|*  
*vārya (yva) granidravyasambhūto rathaścandrasutasyaca \|\| 23 \|\|*

22-23. The Vajakhilya Rsis sit encircling him. The car of the moon has three wheels and the horses are white as Kunda flowers. It runs, drawn by ten horses, on the right and left. The car of the son of the moon (Budha) is made, of \[the essence of air and fire.

## \|\| 58.24-27 \|\|

*piśaṅgesturagairyuktaḥ so 'ṣṭābhirvāyuvegibhiḥ \|*  
*savarūthaḥ sānukarṣo yukto bhūmibhavairhayaiḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*sopāsaṃgapatākastu śukrasyāpi ratho mahān \|*  
*ratho bhūmisutasyāpi taptakāñcanasannibhaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*aṣṭāśvaḥ kāñcanaḥ śrīmān bhaumasyāpi ratho mahān \|\| 26 \|\|*

*padmarāgāruṇairaśvaiḥ saṃyukto vahnisaṃbhavaiḥ \|*  
*aṣṭābhiḥ pāṇḍarairyuktairvājibhiḥ kāñcane rathe \|\| 27 \|\|*

24-27. It is drawn by eight yellow-coloured steeds fleet as the wind. The great chariot of 3ukra has a Varutha2, Anukarsa3, is drawn by horses born of earth and adorned with flags. The huge chariot of Bhumi's (earth) son (Mars) is of the clour of molten gold and is drawn by eight steeds, of the colour of the filaments of a lotus and born of fire.

## \|\| 58.28-29 \|\|

*tiṣṭhaṃstiṣṭhati varṣaṃ vai rāśaurāśau bṛhaspatiḥ \|*  
*ākāśasambhavairaśvaiḥ śavalaiḥ syandanaṃ yutam \|\| 28 \|\|*

*samāruhya śanairyāti mandagāmī śanaiścaraḥ \|*  
*svarbhānosturagā hyaṣṭau bhṛṅgābhā dhūsaraṃ ratham \|\| 29 \|\|*

28-29. Jupiter resides for one year at every sign of a Zodiac sitting on his golden car drawn by eight yellowish-white horses. Riding a car drawn by horses of variegated colour and born of ether Saturn moves slowly on; Svarbhanu1 has eight horses of the colour of the earth and his car is grey-hued.

## \|\| 58.30-31 \|\|

*sakṛdyaktāstu bhūteśabahantyavirataṃ śiva \|*  
*tathā keturathasyāśvā aṣṭau te vātaraṃhasaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

*palāladhūmavarṇābhā lākṣārasanibhāruṇāḥ \|*  
*dvīpanadyadrayudanvanto bhuvanāniharestanuḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

30-31. О lord of goblins, yoked to his car they carry him, day and night. Rahu's car has eight horses, fleet as the wind and smoky-coloured and which have their tongues coated with saliva. On it he roams over the earth consisting of islands, rivers and mountains.

## Chapter 59

## \|\| 59.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*jyotiścakraṃ bhuvo mānamuktvā provāca keśavaḥ \|*  
*caturlakṣaṃ jyotiṣasya sāraṃ rudrāya sarvadaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Suta said: — Having learnt the solar system and the dimension of the earth Kesava communicated, unto Rudra, the essence of astronomy having four characteristic marks.

## \|\| 59.2-3 \|\|

*hariruvāca \|*  
*kṛttikāstvagnidevatyā rohiṇyo brahmaṇaḥ smṛtāḥ \|*  
*ilvalāḥ somadevatyā raudraṃ cārdramudāhṛtam \|\| 2 \|\|*

*punarvasustathādityastiṣyaśca gurudaivataḥ \|*  
*aśleṣāḥ sarpadevatyā maghāśca pitṛdevatāḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

2-3. Hari said: — Krttika (Gemini)2 is the planet ofthe fire god and Rohini (Cancer) is of Brahma. Ilvala (stars in the Orion's head) belonging to Soma and Ardra (Virgo) to Rudra Aditya (the sun) and Punarvasu (Libra) are the planets of the preceptor. Aslesa (Sagita) is the planet of the serpents while Magha (Capri) is that of the departed manes.

## \|\| 59.4 \|\|

*bhāgyāśca pūrvaphalgunya aryamā ca tathottaraḥ \|*  
*sāvitraśca tathā hastā citrā tvaṣṭā prakīrtitaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Purva Phalguni (Aquari) is the planet of good luck as well as the sun, Uttara-Phalguna (Pisces), Savitra (sun) Hasta3, Citra4 and Tvasta (sun).

## \|\| 59.5 \|\|

*svātī ca vāyudevatyā nakṣatraṃ parikīrtitam \|*  
*indrāgnidevatā proktā viśākhā vṛṣabhadhvaja \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Svati is known as the star of the wind-god and Visakha, О bull-emblemed deity, is that of Indra and Fire god.

## \|\| 59.6 \|\|

*maitramṛkṣamanūrādhā jyeṣṭhā śākraṃ prakīrtitam \|*  
*tathā nirṛtidevatyo mūlastajjñairudāhṛtaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Maitram, Iksam, Anuradha and Jyestha are the stars of 6akra. Miilas is the star of Nirrti.

## \|\| 59.7 \|\|

*āpyāstvāṣāṭhapūrvāstu uttarā vaiśvadevatāḥ \|*  
*brāhmaścaivābhijitproktaḥ śravaṇā vaiṣṇavaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Asadha Purva is that of water-god and Uttara is that of Visvadevatas. Abhijit is the star of Brahma and Havana is that of Visnu.

## \|\| 59.8 \|\|

*vāsavastu tathā ṛkṣaṃ dhaniṣṭhā procyate budhaiḥ \|*  
*tathā śatabhiṣā proktaṃ nakṣatraṃ vāruṇaṃ śiva \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Riksam is the star of Vasava, and Dhanistha is that of Budha; while the star 6atabhisa is that of Varuna.

## \|\| 59.9 \|\|

*ājaṃ bhādrapadā pūrvā ahirbrudhnyastathottarā \|*  
*pauṣṇaṃ ca revatī ṛkṣamaśvayukcāśvadaivatam \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Bhadrapada appears in the east, Ahirbbru- dhana in the north as wen as Pusya, Revati, Riksam, Asvayuk.

## \|\| 59.10-13 \|\|

*bharaṇyṛkṣaṃ tathā yāmyaṃ proktāste ṛkṣadevatāḥ \|*  
*brahmāṇī saṃsthitā pūrve pritapannavamītithau \|\| 10 \|\|*

*māheśvarī cottare ca dvitīyā daśāmītithau \|*  
*pañcamyāṃ ca trayodaśyāṃ vārāhī dakṣiṇe sthitā \|\| 11 \|\|*

*ṣaṣṭhyāṃ caiva caturdaśyāmindrāṇī paścime sthitā \|*  
*saptamyāṃ paurṇamāsyāṃ ca cāmuṇḍā vāyugocare \|\| 12 \|\|*

*aṣṭamyamāvāsyayoge mahālakṣmīśagocare \|*  
*ekādaśyāṃ tṛtīyāyāmagnikoṇe tu vaiṣṇavī \|\| 13 \|\|*

10-13. Bharani appears in the north. These are caned Riksa devatas. On the first and ninth day of the fortnight Brahmanl is stationed in the east, on the second and tenth day of the fortnight, Mahesvari is stationed in the north, on the fifth, and the thirteenth days. Varahl appears in the south, on the sixth, and the fourteenth days, Indram is stationed is the west on the seventh day and on the full-moon, day, Camunda appears in the northwest, on the eighth, and Amavasya day, Mahalaksmi is stationed in the north-east, on the eleventh, and third day of the fortnight, Vaisnavl appears in the south-east, on the twelfth.

## \|\| 59.14-15 \|\|

*dvādaśyāṃ ca caturthyāṃ tu kaumārī nairṛte tathā \|*  
*yoginīsuṃmukhenaiva gamanādi na kārayet \|\| 14 \|\|*

*aśvinīmaitrarevatyo mṛgamūlapunarvasu \|*  
*puṣyā hastā tathā jyeṣṭhā prasthāne śreṣṭhamucyate \|\| 15 \|\|*

14-15. And on the fourth day Koumari appears in the south-east. One should not leave his house for another place while Yoginl1 is in front. AsvinI, Revati, Mrgamula, Punarvasu, Pusya, Hasta and Jyestha are the most auspicious stars under whose auspices one should leave his house.

## \|\| 59.16-21 \|\|

*hastādipañcaṛkṣāṇi uttarātrayameva ca \|*  
*aśvinī rohiṇī puṣyā dhaniṣṭhā ca punarvasū \|\| 16 \|\|*

*vastraprāvaraṇe śreṣṭho nakṣatrāṇāṃ gaṇaḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*kṛttikā bharaṇyaśleṣā maghā mūlaviśākhayoḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*trīṇi.pūrvā tathā caiva adhovakrāḥ prakīrtitāḥ? \|*  
*eṣu vāpītaḍāgādikūpabhūmitṛṇāni ca \|\| 18 \|\|*

*devāgārasya khananaṃ nidhānakhananaṃ tathā \|*  
*gaṇitaṃ jyotiṣārambhaṃ khanibilapraveśanam \|\| 19 \|\|*

*kuryādadhogatānyeva anyāni ca vṛṣadhvaja \|*  
*revatī cāśvinī citrā svātī hastā punarvasū \|\| 20 \|\|*

*anurādhā mṛgo jyeṣṭhā ete pārśvamukhāḥ smṛtāḥ \|*  
*gajoṣṭrāśvabalīvardadamanaṃ mahiṣasya ca \|\| 21 \|\|*

16-21. The five Riksas, Hasta2 3 4 5 6 7, the three Uttaras, AsvinI, RohinI, Pusya, Dhanistha, Punarvasu are the stars most favourable for putting on new raiments. Krttika, BharanI, Aslesa, Magha, which are known to have their faces directed down wards, are favourable for digging tanks, wells and reservoirs of water and for cultivating lands and laying foundations of temples and dwelling houses. When these stars and others, О bull- emblemed deity, go down it is the best time to begin the study of Mathematics, Astronomy and enter imo mines, ditches, etc. When Revatl, Asvini, Citra, Svati, Hasta, Punarvasu, Anuradha, Mrga, Jyestha, all these lies sideways it is the the best time for taming elephants, camels, bulls and buffaloes.

## \|\| 59.22 \|\|

*bījānāṃ vapanaṃ kuryādgamanāgamanādikam \|*  
*cakrayantrarathānāṃ ca nāvādīnāṃ pravāhaṇam \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. For sowing seeds and for paying visits. The cows shuold also be tamed under the influence of these stars. The wheels and machineries of cars should be constructed and boats should be floated.

## \|\| 59.23-24 \|\|

*pārśveṣu yāni karmāṇi kuryādeteṣu tānyapi \|*  
*rohiṇyārdrāṃ tathā puṣyā dhaniṣṭhā cottarātrayam \|\| 23 \|\|*

*vāruṇaṃ śravaṇaṃ caiva nava cordhvamukhāḥ smṛtāḥ \|*  
*eṣu rājyābhiṣekaṃ ca paṭṭabandhaṃ ca kārayet \|\| 24 \|\|*

23-24. When Rohini, Ardra, Pusya, Dhanistha, the three Uttaras, Varuna, 6ravana, — these nine have their faces upwards it it the best time for installing asking in the kingdom, and putting on silk raiments.

## \|\| 59.25-28 \|\|

*ūrdhvamukhyānyucchritāni sarvāṇyeteṣu kārayet \|*  
*caturtho cāśubhā ṣaṣṭhī aṣṭamī navamī tathā \|\| 25 \|\|*

*amāvāsyā pūrṇimā ca tadvādaśī ca caturdaśī \|*  
*aśuklā pratipacchreṣṭhā dvitīyā candra sūnunā \|\| 26 \|\|*

*tṛtīyā bhūmiputreṇa caturtho ca śanaiścare \|*  
*gurau śubhā pañcamī syātṣaṣṭīmaṅgalaśukrayoḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

*saptamī somaputreṇa aṣṭamī kujabhāskarau \|*  
*navamī candravā(sau) reṇa daśamī tu gurau śubhā \|\| 28 \|\|*

25-28. The most inauspicious days are the fourth, sixth, eight, ninth and Amavasya. The full- moon, the twelfth, the fourteenth, and the first day of the dark fort-night, are most auspicious days as also the second day when presided over by the Moon's son (Mercury), the third, by the Earth's son (Mars) and the fourth, by Saturn. The fifth day of a formight is auspicious when it is presided over by Jupiter, the sixth day, when by Mars and Venus, the seventh day when by Mercury, the eighth wnen, by Mars, the ninth day, when by the Moon, and the tenth, when by Jupiter.

## \|\| 59.29-31 \|\|

*ekādaśyā guruśukrau dvādaśyāṃ ca punarbudhaḥ \|*  
*trayodaśī śukrabhaumau śanau śreṣṭhā caturdaśī \|\| 29 \|\|*

*paurṇamāsyapyamāvāsyā śreṣṭhā syācca bṛhaspatau \|*  
*dvādaśīṃ dahate bhānuḥ śaśī caikādaśīṃ dahet \|\| 30 \|\|*

*kujo dahecca daśāmīṃ navamīṃ ca budho dahet \|*  
*aṣṭamīṃ dahate jīvaḥ saptamīṃ bhārgavo dahet \|\| 31 \|\|*

29-31.
