The Jupiter is auspicious and pure on the eleventh day of a fort-ninght, the Mercury, on the twelfth day, the Venus, on the thirteenth day, the Saturn on the fourteenth day, and Jupiter is the most auspicious buth on the Amavasya and the full-moon day. The Sun bums the twelfth day of a fortnight, the Moon the eleventh day, the Mars, the tenth day, the Mercury, the ninth day, the JIva1, the eighth day, Bharagava (Venus), the seventh day.

## \|\| 59.32-35 \|\|

*sūryaputro dahetṣaṣṭhīṃ gamanādyāsu nāsti vai \|*  
*pratipannavamīṣveva caturdaśyaṣṭamīṣu ca \|\| 32 \|\|*

*budhavāreṇa prasthānaṃ dūrataḥ parivarjayet \|*  
*meṣe karkaṭake ṣaṣṭhī kanyāyāṃ mithune 'ṣṭamī \|\| 33 \|\|*

*vṛṣe kumbhe caturtho ca dvādaśī makare tule \|*  
*daśamī vṛścike siṃhe dhanurmone caturdaśī \|\| 34 \|\|*

*etā dagdhā na gantavyaṃ pīḍādiḥ kila mānavaiḥ \|*  
*viśākhātrayamāditye pūrvāṣāḍhātraye śaśī \|\| 35 \|\|*

32-35. And the Sun's son, the sixth. One should not leave his house on such a day.On the first, ninth, four tenth, and eighth day of a fortning, and on Wednesday one should postpone his departure for a distant country. The sixth day under the influence of Aries1 and Cancer, the eighth day of Virgo and Gemini, the fourth day of Taurus and Aquaris, the twelfth day of Capricomus and Libra, the tenth day of Libra and Scorpio and the fourteenth day of Sigattarius and Pisces are all inauspicious, and no man should leave his house on any these of days.

## \|\| 59.36-37 \|\|

*dhaniṣṭhātritayaṃ bhaume budhe vai revatītrayam \|*  
*rohiṇyāditrayaṃ jīve śukre puṣyātrayaṃ śiva \|\| 36 \|\|*

*śanivāre varjayecca uttarāphalgunītrayam \|*  
*eṣu yogeṣu cotpātamṛtyurogādikaṃ bhavet \|\| 37 \|\|*

36-37. When the three stars of Dhanistha are in conjunction with Mars, when the three stars of Revati are with Mercury, when the three stars of Visakha are with the sun, when the moon is in the three stars of Purvasadha, when the three stars of Rohini are in Pusya and when the three stars of Pusya are with Venus \[they always forebode evil.) One should avoid the three stars of Uttara Phalguna on Saturday. These conjunctions forebode calamities either ending in death or a fatal disease.

## \|\| 59.38-41 \|\|

*mūler'kaḥ śravaṇe candraḥ proṣṭhapadyuttare kujaḥ \|*  
*kṛttikāsu budhaścaiva gurau rudra punarvasuḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

*pūrvaphalgunī śukre ca svātiścaiva śanaiśvare \|*  
*etai cāmṛtayogāḥ syuḥ sarvakāryaprasādhakāḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

*kālaṃ pravadhyanni?śaktidā? neṣṭamanda? \|*  
*parvādistu jñeyaḥ kālaḥ kālaviśāradaiḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

*ekīkṛtyākṣarānmātraṃ nāmnoḥ strīpuṃsayostribhiḥ \|*

38-41. When the Sun is in conjunction with Mula, when the moon is with Havana, when Mars in with Purva and Uttara Bhadrapada, when Mercury is with Krttika when Jupiter is with Punarvasu, when Venus is with Purva Phalguna, when Saturn is with Svati these conjunctions are called Amrtayoga which yields success in all undertakings.

## \|\| 59.42 \|\|

*viṣkambhe ghaṭikāḥ pañca śūle sapta prakīrtitāḥ \|*

42\. Viskumbhayoga lasts for five hours. 6ula- yoga lasts for seven hours. Ganda and Atiganda, yogas, last for six hours, and Vyaghatavajra, for nine hours.

## \|\| 59.43 \|\|

*vyatīpāte ca parighe vaidhṛte ca dinedine \|*

44-45. The combination between Hasta and the Sun, Jupiter and Pusya, Mercury and Anuradha, Rohini and Saturn, Moon and Souma, Venus and Revati and Mars and Asvini is always auspicious. These combinations are called Siddhi yogas and they avert every form of calamity.

46-47. The combinations between the Sun and Bharani, the Moon and Citra, Mars, Uttara- Asada, Mercury and Dhanistha, Saturn and Revati are called, О Sambhu, Visa-yogas (poisonous combinations).

## \|\| 59.48-49 \|\|

*puṣyaḥ punarvasuścaiva revatī citrayā saha \|*

*kuryācchatabhiṣāyāṃ ca jātakarmādi mānavaḥ \|*  
*viśākhā cottarātrīṇi maghārdrā bharaṇī tathā \|*  
*āśleṣā kṛttikā rudra ! prasthāne maraṇapradāḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

48-49. When the combination takes place between Pusya, Punarvasu, Revafi, Citra, Havana, Dhanistha. Hasta, Asivini, Mrga, and ^atabhisa, a man should perform rites consequent upon the birth of a child. О Rudra, if a child. О Rudra, if a man kayes home for another place under the combination of any three planets of Vteakha, Uttara, Magha, Ardra, BharanI Aslesa and Krttika, he meets with death.

## Chapter 60

## \|\| 60.1-2 \|\|

*hariruvāca \|*  
*ṣaḍāditye daśā jñeyā some pañcadaśa smṛtāḥ \|*

1-2. Hari said: — The Dasa, or the maximum influence of the Sun lasts for six years, that of the Moon for fifteen years, that of Mars, for eight years, that of Mercury, for seventeen years, that of Saturn, for ten years, that of Jupiter, for nineteen years, that of Rahu, for twelve years, and that of Venus, for twenty one years.

## \|\| 60.3 \|\|

*raverdaśā duḥ khadā syādudveganṛpanāśakṛt \|*  
*vibhūtidā somadaśā sukhamiṣṭānnadā tathā \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. The influence of the Sun produces misery and anxiety and brings on the destruction of a king. The influence of the Moon yields wealth, happiness and savoury edibles.

## \|\| 60.4 \|\|

*duḥ khapradā kujadaśā rājyādeḥ syādvināśinī \|*  
*divyastrīdā budhadaśā rājyadā kośavṛddhidā \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. The influence of Mercury gives heavenly bride and kingdom and increases wealth.

## \|\| 60.5 \|\|

*śanerdaśā rājyanāśabandhuduḥ khakarī bhavet \|*  
*gurordaśā rājyadā syātsukhadharmādidāyinī \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. The influence of Saturn brings on the destruction of kingdoms and the misery of friends. The influence of Jupiter gives kingdom, happiness and virtue.

## \|\| 60.6 \|\|

*rāhordaśā rājyanāśavyādhidā duḥ khadā bhavet \|*  
*hastyaśvadā śukradaśā rājyastrīlābhadā bhavet \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. The influence of Rahu brings on the destruction of kingdoms, misery and diseases. The influence of Venus gives elephants, horses, kingdom and women.

## \|\| 60.7-9 \|\|

*meṣa aṅgārakakṣetraṃ vṛṣaḥ śukrasya kīrtitaḥ \|*

*sūryakṣetraṃ bhavetsiṃhaḥ kanyā kṣetraṃ budhasya ca \|*  
*bhārgavasya tulā kṣetraṃ vṛścikoṅgārakasya ca \|\| 8 \|\|*

*dhanuḥ sura guroścaiva śanermakarakumbhakau \|*  
*mīnaḥ suraguroścaiva grahakṣetraṃ prakīrtitam \|\| 9 \|\|*

7-9. The constellation of Aries is the houses of Mars; Tauras, is of Jupiter; Gemini, is of Mercury; Cancer, is of the Moon; Leo, of the sun; Virgo is of Mercury; Libra, is of Venus; Scorpio, is of Mars Sagittarius, is of Jupiter; Capricornus and Aquaris are the houses of Saturn; Pisces, is of Jupiter.

## \|\| 60.10 \|\|

*paurṇamāsyādvayaṃ tatra pūrvāṣāḍhādvayaṃ bhavet \|*  
*dvirāṣāḍhaḥ sa vijñeyo viṣṇuḥ svapiti karkaṭe \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. When tllere are two full-moon nights in one month, two Purva Asadhas and two Asdhas Visnu sleeps in Cancer.

## \|\| 60.11 \|\|

*aśvinī revatī citrā dhaniṣṭhā syādalaṅkṛtau \|*  
*mṛgāhikapimārjāraśvānaḥ sūkarapakṣiṇaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. The sars Asvini, Revafi, Citra, and Dhanistha are the most auspicious stars for starting for a new place. Deer, monkey, cat, dog, parrot, mungoose and mouse, when seen on the right side, are auspicious at tile time of departure.

## \|\| 60.12-13 \|\|

*nakulo mūṣakaścaiva yātrāyāṃ dakṣiṇe śubhaḥ \|*  
*viprakanyā śivā eṣāṃ śaṅkhabherīvasundharāḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*veṇustrīpūrṇakumbhāśca yātrāyāṃ darśanaṃ śubham \|*  
*jambūkoṣṭrakharādyāśca yātrāyāṃ vāmake śubhāḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

12-13. The daughter of a Brahmana, a dead body, conch-shell, bugle, earth, bamboo, a woman, a pitcher full of water are auspicious when seen at the time of departure. A jackal, camel, and ass the auspicious when seen on the left hand side at the time of departure.

## \|\| 60.14 \|\|

*kārpāsauṣadhitailaṃ ca pakrāṅgārabhujaṅgamāḥ \|*  
*muktakeśī raktamālyanagnādyaśubhamīkṣitam \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Cotton, oil of a medicinal plant, burning embers, snakes, a woman with dishevelled hairs, a garland of red flowers and a naked person are always inauspicious when seen.

## \|\| 60.15 \|\|

*hakrāya lakṣaṇaṃ vakṣye labhatpūrve mahāphalam \|*  
*āgneye śokasantāpau dakṣiṇe hānimāpnuyāt \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. I will now describe the characteristic marks of hiccough. When a man stands facing the east hiccough produces great fruits. When he faces the south-east it produces sorrow and anxiety.

## \|\| 60.16 \|\|

*nairṛtya śokasantāpau miṣṭānnaṃ caiva paścime \|*  
*artha prāpnoti vāyavye uttare kalahobhavet \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. When he faces the south it does unjury. When he faces the south-west it produces sorrow and anxiety. When he faces the west it gives sweet food. When he faces the north-west he obtains wealth. When he faces the north he enters on a quarrel.

## \|\| 60.17-20 \|\|

*īśāne maraṇaṃ proktaṃ hikkāyāścaphalāphalam \|*  
*vilikhya ravicakraṃ tu bhāskaro narasannibhaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*yasminnṛkṣe vasadbhānustadāndi trīṇi mastake \|*  
*trayaṃ vakre pradātavyamekaikaṃ skandhayornyaset \|\| 18 \|\|*

*ekaikaṃ bāhuyugme tu ekaika hastayordvayoḥ \|*  
*hṛdaye pañca ṛkṣāṇi ekaṃ nābhau pradāpayet \|\| 19 \|\|*

*ṛkṣamekaṃ nyasedguhye ekaikaṃ jānuke nyaset \|*  
*nakṣatrāṇi ca śeṣāṇi ravipāde niyojayet \|\| 20 \|\|*

17-20. When he faces the north-east he is doomed to die. These are the good and evil, fruits of hiccough. Having drawn the solar circle one should imagine it to be the figure of a man. He should next calculate in what stars the Sun resides. He should then attribute three stars to the head; another three, to the face; one, to each shoulder; one, to each arm; one, to each hand; five starwto the heart; one, to the navel; one, to the buttock; and one, to each knee-joint. The remaining stars should be assigned to the feet of the Sun.

## \|\| 60.21 \|\|

*caraṇasyena ṛkṣeṇa alpāyurjāyate naraḥ \|*  
*vidaśagamanaṃ jānau guhyasthe paradāravān \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. When one's presiding star is at the foot, the man be comes short-lived. When it is on the knee-joints, he goes to live in foreign countries. When it is on the buttock, he knows other people's wives.

## \|\| 60.22 \|\|

*nābhisthenālpasantuṣṭo hṛtsthena syānmaheśvaraḥ \|*  
*pāṇisthena bhaveccauraḥ sthānabhraṣṭo bhaveddhaja \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. When it is on the navel, he becomes contented with little. When it is on heart, he becomes Mahesvara. When it is on the hands, he becomes a heroe. When it is on the arms, he loses his position.

## \|\| 60.23 \|\|

*skandhasthite dhanapatirmukhe miṣṭānnamāpnuyāt \|*  
*mastake padṛvastraṃ syānnakṣatraṃ yadi sthitam \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. When it is on the mouth, he obtains dainty dishes. When it is on the head he obtains silk raiments.

## Chapter 61

## \|\| 61.1 \|\|

*hariruvāca \|*  
*saptamopacayādyasthaścandraḥ sarvatra śobhanaḥ \|*

1\. Hari said: — When the Moon is on the increase from its seventh digit it is always and everywhere favourable.

## \|\| 61.2 \|\|

*saṃpūjyamāno lokaistu guruvaddṛśyate śaśī \|*  
*candrasya dvādaśāvasthā bhavanti śṛṇu tā api \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. It should be adored by people and the Moon is seen like Jupiter. There are twelve Dasas or stages of the Moon. Hear them.

## \|\| 61.3-9 \|\|

*triṣutriṣu ca ṛkṣeṣu aśvinyādi vadāmyaham \|*  
*pravāsasthaṃ punardṛṣṭaṃ mṛtāvasthaṃ jayāvaham \|\| 3 \|\|*

*hāsyāvasthaṃ natā(krīḍā) vasthaṃ pramodāvasthameva ca \|*  
*viṣādāvasthabhogasthe jvarāvasthaṃ vyavasthitam \|\| 4 \|\|*

*kampā(nyā) vasthaṃ sukhāvasthaṃ dvādaśāvasthagaṃ bhavet \|*  
*pravāso hānimṛnyṛ ca jayo hāseratiḥ sukham \|\| 5 \|\|*

*śoko bhogo jvaraḥ kampaḥ sukhaṃ ceti kramātphalam \|*

*tṛtīye rājasanmānaṃ caturthe kalahāgamaḥ \|*  
*pañcamena mṛgāṅkena strīlābho vai tathā bhavet \|\| 7 \|\|*

*ghanadhānyāgamaḥ ṣaṣṭhe ratiḥ pūjā ca saptame \|*

*daśame kāryaniṣpattidhruvamekādaśe jayaḥ \|*

3-9. I will describe his station in every three stars beginning with Asvinl. The twelve stages are Pravasas (living in a foreing country), Punamasta (lost again), Mrta (dead), Jaya (success), Hasya (smiling), Krida (sporting), Pramoda (enjoying), Visada (sorrowing), Bhoga (enjoying), Jvara (decrepitude), Kampa (trembling) and Svastha (sound health). The Moon, in his condition of Pravasa, brings on injury and death, and in that of Jaya, merriment, sexual pleasure, and happiness, the other stages, viz,, бока, Bhoga, Jvara, Kampa and Sukha respectively produce their destined fruits. When the Moon resides in the first house of constellation at the time of birth he always gives satisfaction; when in the second, the person does not feel satiation; when in the third, the person enjoys royal honours; when in the fourth, he quarrels with other people; when the moon is in the fifth house the person obtains a good wife; when in the sixth, the person acquires wealth and corns; when in the seventh, he enjoys sexual pleasures and becomes the adored of all; when in the eighth there is danger to his life; when in the nimh. his wealth is accumulated; when in the tenth, he hrings his work to a successful close; when in the eleventh, he meets with success; when the Moon is in the twelfth house there is, forsooth, death for the man.

## \|\| 61.10 \|\|

*kṛttikādau ca pūrveṇa saptarkṣāṇi ca vai vrajet \|*  
*maghādau dakṣiṇe gacchedanurādhādi paścime \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Under the influence of the seven strs forming the constellation of Krttika it is better to start for the east. Under the influence of Magha it is better In start for the south; under the influence of Anuradha it is better to start for the west.

## \|\| 61.11-12 \|\|

*praśastā cottara yātrā dhaniṣṭhādiṣu saptasu \|*  
*aśvinī revatī citrā dhaniṣṭhā samalaṅkṛtau \|\| 11 \|\|*

*mṛgāśvicitrāpuṣyāśca mūlā hastā śubhāḥ sadā \|*  
*kanyāpradāne yātrāyāṃ pratiṣṭhādiṣu karmasu \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12. Under the influence of Dhanistha it is better to start for the north. Asvinl, Revati, Citra, Dhanistha, Mrgasiras, Pusya, Mula and Hasta are always tavourable in marriage, for giving away a daughter in marriage for going out on business, for consecrating temples and for other religious and social ceremonies.

## \|\| 61.13 \|\|

*śukracandrau hi janmasthau śubhadau ca dvitīyake \|*  
*śaśijñaśukrajīvāśca rāśau rāśau cātha tṛtīyake \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. It the Moon and Jupiter reside in the second house at the time of birth they are auspicious. The Moon, Jupiter and Pusya are auspicious when they live in the third house with Gemini.

## \|\| 61.14 \|\|

*bhaumamandaśaśāṅkārkā budhaḥ śreṣṭhaścaturthake \|*  
*śukrajīvau pañcame ca candraketusamāhitau \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Mars, Saturn, Moon, Sun and Mercury are most auspicious when they live in the fourth house.

## \|\| 61.15 \|\|

*mandākārai ca kujaḥ ṣaṣṭhe gurucandrau ca saptame \|*  
*jñaśukrāvaṣṭame śreṣṭhau navamastho guruḥ śubhaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Saturn, Sun and Mars are auspicious in the sixth house, while Jupiter and Moon in the seventh. Venus is most auspicious in the eighth house, while Jupiter in the ninth.

## \|\| 61.16 \|\|

*arkārkicandrā daśame grahā ekādaśe khilāḥ \|*  
*budho 'tha dvādaśe caiva bhārgavaḥ sukhado bhavet \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. The Sun and Moon are auspicious in the tenth house, while all the planets are auspicious in the eleventh house. Venus and Mercury are favourable in the twelfth house.

## \|\| 61.17-18 \|\|

*siṃhena makaraḥ śreṣṭhaḥ kanyayā meṣa uttamaḥ \|*  
*tulayā saha mīnastu kumbhena sahakarkaṭaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*dhanuṣā vṛṣabhaḥ śreṣṭho mithunena ca vṛścikaḥ \|*  
*etatṣaḍaṣṭakaṃ?prītyai bhavatyeva na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

17-18. The combinations, between Leo and Capri- comus, between Virgo and Aries, between Libra and Pisces, between Aquarius and Cancer, between Sagittaries and Taurus and between Gemini and Scorpio are most auspicious. These fourteen combinations always conduce to well being.

## Chapter 63

## \|\| 63.1-2 \|\|

*hariruvāca \|*  
*narastrīlakṣaṇaṃ vakṣye saṃkṣapācchṛṇu śaṅkara \|*  
*asvedinau mṛdutalau kamalodarasannibhau \|\| 1 \|\|*

*śliṣṭāṅgulī tāmranakhau sugulphau śirayojjhitau \|*

1-2. Hari said: — Hear, О Sankara, I will now describe in brief the characteristic marks of men and women. Tender plams like lotus petals4 and not perspiring, fingers adjoining each other, copper-coloured nails, beautiful ankles, well- formed head and feet, plump like a tortoise, mark out a man to be a king.

## \|\| 63.3-5 \|\|

*virūkṣapāṇḍuranakhau vakrau caiva śirānatau \|*

*duḥ khadāridyadau syātā nātra kāryāṃ vicāraṇā \|*  
*alparomayutā śreṣṭhā jaṅghā hastikaropamā \|\| 4 \|\|*

*romaikaikaṃ kūpake syādbhūpānāṃ tu mahātmanām \|*  
*dvedve romṇī paṇḍitānāṃ śrotriyāṇāṃ tathaiva ca \|\| 5 \|\|*

3-5. Yellow nails, rough face, high head, feet like winnowing baskets, and withered fingers of the feet, are the marks for sorrow and poverty. There is no doubt about it. Thighs like the trunks of elephants containing few hairs, and one hair in the navel are the marks for great kings. The learned men and persons conversant with Shrutis have two hairs each on their thighs.

## \|\| 63.6 \|\|

*romatrayaṃ daridrāṇāṃ rogī nirmāṃsajānukaḥ \|*

6\. Those, who are poor, have three hairs and diseased men have their knee-joints devoid of flesh. One, who has got a small genital organ, becomes a rich man with no issue.

## \|\| 63.7 \|\|

*sthūlaliṅgo daridraḥ syāddukhyekavṛṣṇī bhavet \|*  
*viṣamestrīcañcalo vai nṛpaḥ syādvṛṣaṇe same \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. One, who has got a big genital organ, becomes poor. One, who has got one scrotum, becomes poor. One, who has got unequal testes, gets a fickle wife. One, who has got equal testes, becomes a king.

## \|\| 63.8 \|\|

*pralambavṛṣaṇo 'lpāyurnirdravyaḥ kumaṇirbhavet \|*  
*pāṇḍurairmalinaiścaiva maṇibhiśca sukhī naraḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. One, with hanging testes, becomes shor-t- lived. One, having a bad wrist, becomes poor. With pale-coloured wrists a person becomes happy.

## \|\| 63.9 \|\|

*niḥ svāḥ saśabdamūtrāḥ syurnṛpā niḥśabdadhārayā \|*  
*bhogāḍhyāḥ samajaṭharā niḥ svāḥ syurghaṭasannibhāḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. An idigent person passes urine with great sound. Those, who pass urine without any sound, become kings. Those, who have even bellies, enjoy various pleasures of life. Those, who have bellies like post, become indigent.

## \|\| 63.10 \|\|

*sarpodarā daridrāḥ syū rekhābhiścāyurucyate \|*  
*lalāṭe yasya dṛśyante tisro rekhāḥ samāhitāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Those, who have serpentine bellies become poor. Liner marks indicate longevity. He, who has three lines on the forehead, becomes happy, gets sons, and lives for sixty years. One having two lines lives for forty years.

## \|\| 63.11 \|\|

*sukhī putrasamāyuktaḥ sa ṣaṣṭiṃ jīvate naraḥ \|*  
*catvāriṃśacca varṣāṇi dvirekhādarśanānnaraḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. One, who has a line on the fore-head extending to the ears, lives for twenty years. If one has three lines on the fore-head extending up to ears he lives for a hundred years.

## \|\| 63.12 \|\|

*viṃśatyabdaṃ tvekarekhā ākarṇāntāḥ śatāyuṣaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. One, having two lines, lives for seventy years. One, having three lines, lives for sixty years. The person, having two lines one clear and another indistinct, lives for twenty years.

## \|\| 63.13 \|\|

*saptatyāyurdvirekhā tu ṣaṣṭyāyustisṛbhirbhavet \|*  
*vyaktāvyaktābhī rekhābhirviṃśatyāyurbhavennaraḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. One, who has short lines, lives for forty years. The person, who has broken lines, meets with an accidental death.

## \|\| 63.14 \|\|

*catvāriṃśacca varṣāṇi hīnarekhastu jīvati \|*  
*bhinnābhiścaiva rekhābhirapamṛtyurnarasya hi \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. The person, on whose head are seen the marks of a trident of Pattika, is favoured with riches and children, and lives for a hundred years.

## \|\| 63.16 \|\|

*tarjanyā madhyamāṅgulyā āyūrekhā tu madhyataḥ \|*  
*saṃprāptā yā bhavedrudra ! sa jīveccharadaḥ śatam \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. The person, whose line of life passes through the middle and fore-fingers, lives for a hundred years, О Rudra.

## \|\| 63.17-18 \|\|

*prathamā jñānarekhā tu hyaṅguṣṭhādanuvartate \|*  
*madhyamāmūlagā rekhā āyūrekhā ataḥ param \|\| 17 \|\|*

*kaniṣṭhikāṃ samāśritya āyūrekhā samāviśet \|*  
*acchinnā vā vibhaktā vā sa jīveccharadaḥ śatam \|\| 18 \|\|*

17-18. The person, one whose palm the line of knowledge extends up to the thumb, and the line of life extends up to the foot of the middle fingers form the youngest in an unbroken and undivided condition, lives for a hundred years.

## \|\| 63.19 \|\|

*yasya pāṇitale rekhā āyustasya prakāśayet \|*  
*śatavarṣāṇi jīvecca bhogī rudra ! na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. The person, on whose palm the line of life appears in a distinct form, lives for a hundred years and becomes the happy recipient of all earthly blessings.

## \|\| 63.20 \|\|

*kaniṣṭhikāṃ samāśritya madhyamāyāmupāgatā \|*  
*ṣaṣṭhivarṣāyuṣaṃ kuryādāyūrekhā tu mānavam \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. The person, on whose palm the line of life extends also from the youngest to the middle finger, lives for eighty years.

## Chapter 64

## \|\| 64.1 \|\|

*hariruvāca \|*  
*yasyāstu kuñcitāḥ keśā mukhaṃ ca parimaṇḍalam \|*  
*nābhiśca dakṣiṇāvartā sā kanyā kulavardhinī \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Hari said: — The maiden, who has got curling locks, a round face and a deep navel, increases her family.

## \|\| 64.2 \|\|

*yā ca kāñcanavarṇābhā raktahastasaroruhā \|*  
*sahasrāṇāṃ tu nārīṇāṃ bhavetsāpi pativratā \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. A woman, whose colour is like that of gold, and whose hands are red, is called Padmini. Such a woman, born one in' a thousand, is personification of chastity.

## \|\| 64.3 \|\|

*vakrakeśā ca yā kanyā maṇḍalākṣī ca yā bhavet \|*  
*bhartā ca mriyate tasyā niyataṃ duḥ khabhāginī \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. The woman, who has uneven hairs and round eyes, becomes widowed, and is always unfortunate in her surroundings.

## \|\| 64.4 \|\|

*pūrṇacandramukhī kanyā bālasūryasamaprabhā \|*  
*viśālanetrā bimboṣṭhī sā kanyā labhate sukham \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. The maiden, who has a face like the full moon, is effulgent like the rising Sun, has expensive eyes and Vimba-like lips, enjoys happiness.

## \|\| 64.5 \|\|

*rekhābhirbahubhiḥ kleśaṃ svalpābhirdhanahīnatā \|*  
*raktābhiḥ sukhamāpnoti kṛṣṇābhiḥ preṣyatāṃvrajet \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Many lines indicate misery and dearth of the same signifies poverty. One, having crimsoncoloured lines, enjoys happiness, and one, having dark blue lines, becomes unchaste.

## \|\| 64.6 \|\|

*kārye ca mantrī satstrī syātsatī (khī) syātkaraṇeṣu ca \|*  
*streheṣu bhāryā mātā syādveśyā ca śayane śubhā \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. A wife is like a minister to her husband in works, a friend in enjoyments, a mother in affection, and a public women while on bed.

## \|\| 64.7 \|\|

*aṅkuśaṃ kuṇḍalaṃ cakraṃ yasyāḥ pāṇitale bhavet \|*  
*putraṃ prasūyate nārī narendraṃ labhate patim \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. The women, who has the marks of a goad, circle and discus on her plam, gives birth to a son and obtains a king as her husband.

## \|\| 64.8 \|\|

*yasyāstu romaśau pārśvau romaśau ca payodharau \|*  
*annatau cādharoṣṭhau ca kṣipraṃ mārayate patim \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. The women, whose two sides and breasts are covered with hairs and whose lips are high, soon destroys her husband.

## \|\| 64.9 \|\|

*yasyāḥ pāṇitale rekhā prākārastoraṇaṃ bhavet \|*  
*api dāsakule jātā rājñītvamupagacchati \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The woman, who has the marks of a wall or gateway on her palms, becomes a queen even if she is born as a maid servant.

## \|\| 64.10 \|\|

*udvṛttā kapilā yasya romarājī nirantaram \|*  
*api rājakule jātā dāsītvamupagacchati \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. One, who has rows of reddish and high hairs on her person, becomes a maid servant even if he is born in a royal family.

## \|\| 64.11-12 \|\|

*yasyā anāmikāṅguṣṭhau pṛthivyāṃ naiva tiṣṭhataḥ \|*  
*patiṃ mārayate kṣipraṃ svecchācāreṇa vartate \|\| 11 \|\|*

*yasyā gamanamātreṇa bhūmikampaḥ prajāyate \|*  
*patiṃ mārayate kṣipraṃ svecchācāreṇa vartate \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12. One, who has got her thumb and ringfinger of an unusually high stature, soon kills her husband and leads a loose life.

## \|\| 64.13 \|\|

*cakṣuḥ snehena saubhāgyaṃ dantasnehena bhojanam \|*  
*tvacaḥ snehena śāyyāṃ ca pādasnehena vāhanam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. One who is much heavy and who has thung walk kills her husband and be characterless. Oily eyes indicate good luck, oily teeth indicate good eating, oily skin indicates a good bed, and oily feet indicate conveyances.

## \|\| 64.14-16 \|\|

*snigdhonnatau tāmranakhau nāryāśca caraṇau śubhau \|*  
*matsyāṅkuśābjacihnau ca cakralāṅgalalakṣitau \|\| 14 \|\|*

*asvedinau mūdutalau praśastau caraṇau striyāḥ \|*  
*śubhe jaṅghe virome ca ūrū hastikaropamau \|\| 15 \|\|*

*aśvatthapatrasadṛśaṃ vipulaṃ guhyamuttamam \|*  
*nābhiḥ praśastā gambhīrā dakṣiṇāvartikā śubhā \|*  
*aromā trivalī nāryā hṛtstanau romavarjitau \|\| 16 \|\|*

14-16. The auspicious signs of women are cool and high breasts, copper-coloured nails, beautiful feet, marks of fish, goad, lotus, discus and plough-share on the soles and palms which do not perspire, a beautiful hip without hairs, thigh like the trunk of an elephant, most excellent and capacious buttock like a fig leaf, spacious and deep navel and chest and breast shorn of hairs.

## Chapter 65

## \|\| 65.1 \|\|

*hariruvāca \|*  
*samudroktaṃ pravakṣyāmi narastrīlakṣaṇaṃ śubham \|*  
*yena vijñātamātreṇa atītānāgatāpramā \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Hari said: — I will now describe the auspicious marks of men and women as described by Samudra (Palmistry) by knowing which one may without any labour calculate the past and future.

## \|\| 65.2-6 \|\|

*asvedinau mṛdutalau kamalodarasannibhau \|*  
*śleṣṭāṅgulī tāmranakhau pādāviṣṇau śirojjhitau \|\| 2 \|\|*

*kūrmonnatau gūḍhagulphau supārṣṇo nṛpateḥ smṛtau \|*  
*śū(sar) pākārau virūkṣau ca vakrau pādau śirālakau \|\| 3 \|\|*

*saṃśuṣkau pāṇḍuranakhau niḥ svasya viralāṅgulī \|*  
*mārgāyotkaṇṭakau pādau kaṣāyasadṛśau tathā \|\| 4 \|\|*

*vicchittidau ca vaṃśasya brahmanghau śaṅku (pakra) sannibhau \|*  
*agamyāgamane prītau jaṅghā viralaromikā \|\| 5 \|\|*

*mṛduromā samā jaṅghā tathā karikaraprabhā \|*  
*ūravo jānavastulyā nṛpasyopacitāḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

2-6. Unperspiring palms, lotus-like belly, fingers adjoining one another, copper-coloured nails, warm feet like tortoise, strong ankles and beautiful sides are the marks of a king. Rough, uneven feet like winnowing baskets, dry locks, twany coloured nails and distantly placed fingers are the marks of poverty. Well-formed and red feet, equal shanks without hairs, thighs like the trunks of elephants and equal knee joints are the characteristic marks of a king.

## \|\| 65.7 \|\|

*niḥ svasya sṛgālajaṅghā raumaikaikaṃ cakūpake \|*  
*nṛpāṇāṃ śrotriyāṇāṃ ca dvedve śriye ca dhīmatām \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. The indigent have shankles like those of a jackal and have hairs in the navel. The kings the 6rotriyas and the intelligent have two hairs each.

## \|\| 65.8 \|\|

*tryādyairniḥ svā mānavāḥ syurduḥ svabhājaśca ninditāḥ \|*  
*keśāśca vai kuñcitāśca pravāse mriyate naraḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Persons, having there hairs, become poor, miserable and are always objects of censure. A person, having curling hairs, dies in a foreign counrty.

## \|\| 65.9 \|\|

*nirmāṃsajānuḥ saubhāgyamalpairnimnai ratiḥ striyāḥ \|*  
*vikaṭaiśca daridrāḥ syuḥ samāṃsai rājyameva ca \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. A knee-joint without sufficient flesh indicates good luck (in a man). With a knee joint of insufficient flesh one knows degraded women. One, having beformed knee joints, becomes poor and one having plumps ones, obtains a kingdom.

## \|\| 65.10 \|\|

*mahadbhirāyurākhyātaṃ hyalpaliṅgo dhanī naraḥ \|*  
*apatyarahitaścaiva sthūlaliṅgo ghanojjhitaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. A person, having a short genital organ, lives long and becomes rich and has few offspring. One, having a huge genital organ, becomes proud of his wealth.

## \|\| 65.11 \|\|

*meḍhe vāmanate caiva sutārtharahito bhavet \|*  
*vakre 'nyathā putravāntsyāddāridrayaṃ vinatetvadhaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. When the left testes is swollen the person does not get sons. When the testes are uneven the person obtains sons; and when they are bent down it indicates poverty.

## \|\| 65.12 \|\|

*alpe tvatanayo liṅgeśirāle 'tha sukhī naraḥ \|*  
*sthūlagranthiyute liṅge bhavetputrādisaṃyutaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. When the genital organ is small a person obtains sons; when the head of the genital organ is plump the person becomes happy; when there are thick chords in the organ the person becomes happy.

## \|\| 65.13 \|\|

*kośagūḍhe dīrghairbhugnaiśca dhanavarjitaḥ \|*  
*balavānyuddhaśīlaśca laghuśektaḥ sa eva ca \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. When the testes are thick-set the person becomes a king; and when they are long and rugged the person becomes poor. One, who has a small testicle, becomes a strong and powerful warrior.

## \|\| 65.14 \|\|

*durbalastvekavṛṣaṇo viṣamābhyāñcalaḥ striyām \|*  
*samābhyāṃ kṣitipaḥ proktaḥ pralambena śatābdavān \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. One, who has got me teste, becomes weak; and one, who has got uneven testes, gets a fickle wife. One, who has got even restes, becomes a king; and one, who has got a long testicle, lives for a hundred years.

## \|\| 65.15 \|\|

*udvṛṃ (ddha) tābhyāṃ ca bahvāyū rūkṣairmaṇibhirīśvaraḥ \|*  
*pāṇḍarairmaṇibhirniḥ svā malinaiḥ sukhabhāginaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. One, who has got high wrists, lives for many years; one, who has got rugged wrists, becomes a master. With yellow-coloured wrists people become poor, and with dark wrists they enjoy happiness.

## \|\| 65.16-17 \|\|

*saśabdaniḥ śabdamūtrāḥ syudaṃridrāśca mānavāḥ \|*  
*ekadvitricatuḥ pañcaṣaḍbhirdhārābhireva ca \|\| 16 \|\|*

*dakṣiṇāvartacalitamūtrā bhiśca nṛpāḥ smṛtāḥ \|*  
*vikīrṇamūtrā niḥ svāśca pradhānasukhadāyikāḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

16-17. Persons, who pass urine either with or without any sound, become poor. When urine comes out in one, two, three, four, five, or six lines and passes towards the right, it indicates the signs of kinghood. Those, who pass urine in a scattered way, become indigent, those, who pass urine in a strong flow, become happy and obtain good wives.

## \|\| 65.18 \|\|

*ekadhārāśca vanitāḥ snigdhairmaṇibhirunnataiḥ \|*  
*samaiḥ strīratnadhanino madhye nimnaiśca kanyakāḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. When urine remains on an equal level a man obtains wife, gems and riches, and when it goes down he obtains maidens.

## \|\| 65.19 \|\|

*śuṣkairniśvā viśuṣkaiśca durbhagāḥ parikīrtitāḥ \|*  
*puṣpagandhe nṛpāḥ śukre madhugandhe dhanaṃ bahuḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. When the semen is dry a person becomes indigent and when there is scent of flower in the semen he becomes king. When there is smell of honey in it he acquires immense riches.

## \|\| 65.20 \|\|

*putrāḥ śukre matsyagandhe tanuśukre ca kanyakāḥ \|*  
*mahābhogī māṃsagandhe yajvā syānmadagandhini \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. When there is the smell of fish in the semen he gets a son. When semen is scanty he obtains maidens. When there is the small of meat he enjoys various luxuries of life; when there is the smell of wine he becomes a priest.

## \|\| 65.21 \|\|

*daridraḥ kṣāragandhe ca dīrghāyuḥ śīghramaithunī \|*  
*aśīghramaithunyalpāyuḥ sthūlasphik syāddhanojjhitaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. When there is smell of ashes he becomes poor. One, who finishes soon his sexual inter course, lives long. He, whose sexual intercourse lasts long, is short-lived.

## \|\| 65.22 \|\|

*māṃsalasphik sukhī syācca siṃhasphik bhūpatiḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*bhavetsiṃhakaṭī rājā niḥ svaḥ kapikaṭirnaraḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. One, having big buttocks, becomes proud of his wealth. One having fleshy buttocks becomes happy; and one having loinine buttocks becomes a king. One; having a monkey-like waist, becomes indigent.

## \|\| 65.23-24 \|\|

*sarpodarā daridrāḥ syuḥ piṭharaiśca ghaṭaiḥ samaiḥ \|*  
*dhanino vipulaiḥ pārśvairniḥ svā raktaiśca nimnagaiḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

*samakakṣāśca bhogāḍhyā nimnakakṣā dhanojjhitāḥ \|*  
*nṛpāśconnatakakṣāḥ syurjihnā viṣamakakṣakāḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

23-24. Persons, having serpentine bellies, become poor. Those, having pan or pot like bellies, become rich. People, having spacious arm-pits, become indigent; those, having equal arm-pits, enjoy various objects of life; those, who have hollowed arm-pits, become pround of wealth; those, who have elevated arm-pits, those, who have uneven arm-pits, and those, who have crooked arm-pits, become kinggf.

## \|\| 65.25 \|\|

*matsyodarā bahudhanā nābhibhiḥ sukhinaḥ smṛtāḥ \|*  
*vistīrṇābhirbahulābhirnimnābhiḥ kleśabhāginaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Those, who have got fish-like bellies and navels, become happy. Those, who have got capacious or low navels, are doomed to suffer

## \|\| 65.26 \|\|

*balimadhyagatā nābhiḥ śūlabādhāṃ karoti hi \|*  
*vāmāvartaśca sādhyaṃ vai medhāṃ dakṣiṇatastathā \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. If there is wrinkle inside a navel it brings on death at the stake for the person. If there is wrinkle on one side the man lives for ever.

## \|\| 65.27 \|\|

*pārśvāyatā cirāyurdā tūpaviṣṭā dhaneśvaram \|*  
*adho gavāḍhyaṃ kuryācca nṛpatvaṃ padmakarṇikā \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. If it is a equinoctial position he becomes the possessor of riches. If it is downwards he becomes the possessor of kine. If it is of the shape of a pericarp of a lotus he becomes a king.

## \|\| 65.28 \|\|

*ekabaliḥ śatāyuḥ syācchrībhogī dvivaliḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*trivaliḥ kṣmāpa ācārya ṛjubhirvālibhiḥ sukhī \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. If there is one wrinkle the person lives for a hundred years. If there are two he enjoys prosperity. If there are three wrinkles he becomes a preceptor. If the wrinkles are straight the person becomes happy.

## \|\| 65.29 \|\|

*agamyāgāmī jihmabalirbhūpāḥ pārśvaiśca māṃsalaiḥ \|*  
*mṛdubhiḥ susamaiścaiva dakṣiṇāvartaromabhiḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. If the wrinkle is awry he knows women unworthy of being known. If the arm-pits are fleshy, tender, even and covered with rows of hairs on the right side, the person becomes a king.

## \|\| 65.30 \|\|

*viparītaiḥ parapreṣyā nirdravyāḥ sukhavarjitāḥ \|*  
*anuddhataiścūcukaiśca bhavanti subhagā narāḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. If the rows of hairs tend towards the opposite direction the person becomes devoid of all objects and happiness. If the nipples of the breasts are not high the persons become very lucky.

## \|\| 65.31 \|\|

*nirdhanā viṣamairderghaiḥ pītopacitakairnṛpāḥ \|*  
*samonnataṃ ca hṛdayamakampaṃ māṃsalaṃ pṛthu \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. But if they are uneven, high and of yellow colour they become poor. The kings have high and fleshy chests which do not tremble, are sinewy and covered with strong hairs going downwards.

## \|\| 65.32 \|\|

*nṛpāṇāmadhamānāṃ ca khararomaśirālakam \|*  
*arthavānsamavakṣāḥ syātpīnairvakṣobhirūrjitaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. A rich man has an even chest. One, having plump chest, becomes very powerful.

## \|\| 65.33-34 \|\|

*vakṣobhirviṣamairniḥ svaḥ śastreṇanidhanāstathā \|*  
*viṣamairjatrubhirniḥ svā asthinaddhaiśca mānavāḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

*unnatairbhogino nimnairniḥ svāḥ pīnairdhanānvitāḥ \|*  
*niḥ svaścipiṭakaṇṭhaḥ syācchirāśuṣkagalaḥ sukhī \|\| 34 \|\|*

33-34. Persons, having uneven chests, become indigent and are killed by weapons. Persons, having rugged collar-bones, become indigent. Those, having elevated collar-bones, enjoy various objects of life; those, having depressed ones, become indigent; and those, having plump ones, become rich. One, who has a flat neck becomes indigent. He who has got the arteries of his neck, not very prominent, becomes happy.

## \|\| 65.35 \|\|

*śūraḥ syānmahiṣagrīvaḥ śāstrātto mṛgakaṇṭhakaḥ \|*  
*kambugrīvaśca nṛpatirlambakaṇṭho 'tibhakṣakaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Не. who his buffalo necked, becomes a hero. He who has a neck like that of a deer, masters the Holy Scriptures. One, who has a neck like a conch-shell, becomes a king; whereas one, who has a long neck, becomes a voracious eater.

## \|\| 65.36 \|\|

*aromaśā bhugnapṛṣṭhaṃ śubhaṃ cāśubhamanyathā \|*  
*kakṣāśvatthadalā śreṣṭhā sugandhirmṛgaromikā \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. A back, not covered with hairs and even in shape, always indicates auspiciousness, while of any other kind it is the forerunner of inauspiciousness.

## \|\| 65.37 \|\|

*anyathā tvarthahīnānāṃ dāridrayasya ca kāraṇam \|*  
*saṃmāsau caiva bhugnālpau śliṣṭau ca vipulau śubhau \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. The most auspicious arm-pit is that of the shape of a fig-leaf, which is covered with brown hairs and from which good smell comes out. Any other description is the mark of poverty. Fleshy, well-formed and well-joined anus are the most auspicious.

## \|\| 65.38 \|\|

*ājānulambitau bāhū vṛttau pīnau nṛpeśvare \|*  
*niḥ svānāṃ romaśau hrasvau śreṣṭhau karikara prabhau \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Well-rounded and fleshy arms, extending up to the knees, indicate the signs of royalty. Short arms, covered with hairs, indicate signs of poverty. Arms, like the trunks of elephants, are the best.

## \|\| 65.39 \|\|

*hastāṅgulaya eva syuvāyudvārayutāḥ śubhāḥ \|*  
*medhāvināṃ ca sūkṣmāḥ syurbhṛtyānāṃ cipiṭāḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Fingers of the hands, when straight, are most auspicious. Those of the intelligent are short and those of the servants are flat.

## \|\| 65.40 \|\|

*sthūlāṅgulībhirniḥ svāḥ syurnatāḥ syuḥ sukṛśaistadā \|*  
*kapitulyakarāḥ niḥ svā vyāghratulyakarairbalam \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. The indigent have either fat, crooked or bent and lean fingers. Those, who have hands like those of a monkey, become indigent. That like a tiger indicates strength.

## \|\| 65.41-42 \|\|

*pitṛvittavināśaśca nimnātkaratalānnarāḥ \|*  
*maṇibandhairnigūḍhaiśca suśliṣṭaiḥ śubhagandhibhiḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

*nṛpā hīnāḥ karacchaidaiḥ saśabdairdhanavarjitāḥ \|*  
*saṃvṛtaiścaiva nimnaiśca dhaninaḥ parikīrtitāḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

41-42. The depressed palm of a person indicates the destruction of his paternal property. The kings have well-formed, thick-set and sweet- scented wrists. Those, whose fingers make a sound when handled, become degraded and poor.

## \|\| 65.43 \|\|

*prottānaka radātāro viṣamairviṣamā narāḥ \|*  
*karaiḥ karatalaiścaiva lākṣābhairīśvarāstalaiḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Persons, who have uneven fingers, always pay taxes. Those, who have red hands and palms, become very rich.

## \|\| 65.44 \|\|

*paradāraratāḥ pītairūkṣairniḥ svā narā matāḥ \|*  
*tuṣatulyanakhāḥ klībāḥ kuṭilaiḥ sphuṭitairnarāḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Tho'Se, who have yellow-coloured and rough ones, become indigent and addicted to other people's wives. Those who have nails like husks, become eunuchs. Those, who have rugged and broken nails, become indigent.

## \|\| 65.45 \|\|

*niḥ svāśca kunakhaistadvadvivarṇaiḥ paratarkakāḥ \|*  
*tāmrairbhūpā dhanāḍhyāśca aṅguṣṭhaiḥ sayavaistathā \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Those, who have discoloured and disfigured nails, always pry into other's busi-ness. Those, who have copper-coloured nails, become kings. Those, who have the mark of a barley on their thumbs, become rich.

## \|\| 65.46 \|\|

*aṅguṣṭhamūlajaiḥ putrī syāddīrghāṅguliparvakaḥ \|*  
*dīrghāyuḥ subhagaścaiva nirdhano viralāṅguliḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. When there is such a mark at the foot of the thumb a person gets sons. If a person has long knots in the fingers he lives a long life and becomes lucky. He, who has disjoined fingers, becomes poor.

## \|\| 65.47 \|\|

*ghanāṅguliśca sadhanastisro rekhāścayasya vai \|*  
*nṛpateḥ karatalagā maṇibandhātsamutthitāḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. He, who has got close fingers, become a rich man. The person, on which plams three lines appear from the wrist, becomes a king. When the figures of two fishes appear on the palm the person becomes a great sacrificer.

## \|\| 65.48 \|\|

*yugamīnāṅkitanaro bhavetsatraprado naraḥ \|*  
*vajrākārāśca dhanināṃ matsyapucchanibhā budhe \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. The sign of a thunder-bolt appearing on the palm indicates the possession of riches. The sign of the tail of a fish indicates intellect.

## \|\| 65.49 \|\|

*śaṅkhātapatraśivikāgajapadmopamā nṛpe \|*  
*kumbhāṅkuśapatākābhā mṛṇālābhā nidhīśvare \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. The signs of conch-shell, umbrella, vehicle, elephant and lotus indicate royalty. The marks of a pitcher, goad, flag and lotus-stalk indicate the possession of gems.

## \|\| 65.50 \|\|

*dāmābhāśca gavāḍhyānāṃ svastikābhā nṛpeśvare \|*  
*cakrāsitomaradhanuḥ kuntābhā nṛpateḥ kare \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. The mark of a chord indicates the possession of kine; that of Svastika indicates royalty. The marks of discus, sword, Tomara, bow and teeth appear on the hands of a king.

## \|\| 65.51 \|\|

*alūkhalābhā yajñāḍhyā vedībhā cāgnihotriṇi \|*  
*vāpīdevakulyābhāstrikoṇābhāścadhārmike \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. The mark of a mortar appears on the palms of a person who celebrates sacrifices and that of a sacrificial altar appears on the palm of an Agnihotri. The marks of a tank and triangle indicate righteousness.

## \|\| 65.52-53 \|\|

*aṅguṣṭhamūlagā rekhāḥ putrāḥ sūkṣmāśca dārikāḥ \|*  
*pradeśinīgatā rekhā kaniṣṭhāmūlagāminī \|\| 52 \|\|*

*śatāyuṣaṃ ca kurute chinnayā taruto bhayam \|*  
*niḥ svāśca bahurekhāḥ syunirdravyāścibukaiḥ kṛśaiḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

52-53. Lines, origination from the root of the thumb, indicate the possession of sons and happiness. A line, extending from the tip of the thumb to-that of the fore-finger and originating from the root of the youngest finger, makes one live for a hundred years. When it is broken it indicates danger from a tree. Many lines indicate poverty.

## \|\| 65.54 \|\|

*māṃsalaiśca dhanopetā āraktairadharairnṛpāḥ \|*  
*bimbopamaiśca sphuṭitairoṣṭhairūkṣaiścakaṇḍitaiḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. A spare chin indicates want; while a fleshy one indicates riches. Red lips indicate royalty. Smiling and tender lips, resembling Bimba fruits, indicate the same. Those who have rugged lips become poor.

## \|\| 65.55 \|\|

*viṣamairdhanahīnāśca dantāḥ snigdhā ghanāḥ śubhāḥ \|*  
*tīkṣṇā dantāḥ samāḥ śreṣṭhā jihvā raktā samā śubhā \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Thick-set and cool teeth are the best. Sharp but even teeth are also most auspicious. Red tongue is also most auspicious.

## \|\| 65.56 \|\|

*ślakṣṇā dīrghā ca vijñeyā tālū śvete dhanakṣaye \|*  
*kṛṣṇe ca paruṣo vakraṃ samaṃ saumyaṃ ca saṃvṛtam \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. Blue and tall tongue is also the best and a white palate indicates the destruction of wealth. There arc two kinds of faces-dark and rough; tender and gentle.

## \|\| 65.57 \|\|

*bhūpānāmamalaṃ ślakṣṇaṃ viparītaṃ ca duḥ khinām \|*  
*mahā duḥ khaṃ durbhagāṇāṃ strīmukhaṃ putramāpnuyāt \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Clean and tender face indicates royalty and its opposite indicates poverty. A son, possessing the face of his mother, suffers great miseries.

## \|\| 65.58 \|\|

*āḍhyānāṃ vartulaṃ vakraṃ nirdravyāṇāṃ ca dīrghakam \|*  
*bhīruvakraḥ pāpakarmā dhūrtānāṃ caturaśrakam \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. A rich person has a round face and a poor man a tall one. The vicious have cowardly faces and the wicked cunning ones.

## \|\| 65.59 \|\|

*nimnaṃ vakramaputrāṇāṃ kṛpaṇānāṃ ca hrasvakam \|*  
*sampūrṇaṃ bhogināṃ kāntaṃ śmaśru snigdhaṃ śubhaṃ mṛdu \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. Those who have depressed faces get no sons. The misers have short faces. The happiest of men, who enjoys all the luxuries of life, has tender, thin and beautiful beards.

## \|\| 65.60 \|\|

*saṃhataṃ cāsphuṭitāgraṃ raktaśmaśruśca caurakaḥ \|*  
*raktālpaparuṣaśmaśrukarṇāḥ syuḥ pāpamṛtyavaḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. A thief has got thick, short and crimson- coloured heards. The, sinful persons have red and rugged heards.

## \|\| 65.61 \|\|

*nirmāṃsaiścipiṭairbhogāḥ kṛpaṇā hrasvakarṇakāḥ \|*  
*śaṅkukarṇāśca rājāno romakarṇā gatāyuṣaḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. The misers have short ears. Those who have got spear like ears become kings. Those, who have got hairs on their ears, die soon.

## \|\| 65.62 \|\|

*bṛhatkarṇāśca dhaninorājānaḥ parikīrtitāḥ \|*  
*karṇaiḥ snigdhāvanaddhaiśca vyālambairmāṃsalairnṛpāḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. Persons, having big ears, become kings and rich men. Persons, endued with hanging and fleshy ears, also become kings.

## \|\| 65.63 \|\|

*bhogī vai nimnagaṇḍaḥ syānmatrī sampūrṇagaṇḍakaḥ \|*  
*śukanāsaḥ sukhī syācca śuṣkanāso 'tijīvanaḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. One having depressed cheeks, enjoys all the luxuries of life. One, having well-formed cheeks, becomes a minister. One, having a nose like that of a parrot, becomes happy. One, who has got a thin nose, lives long.

## \|\| 65.64 \|\|

*chinnāgrakūpanāsaḥ syādagamyāgamane rataḥ \|*  
*dīrghanāse ca saubhāgyaṃ cauraścākuñcitendriyaḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. One, who has got a well-like nose with its tip broken, knows women unworthy of being known. One, who has got a long nose, enjoys good luck. A thief has got a flat nose.

## \|\| 65.65 \|\|

*mṛtyuścipiṭanāse syāddhīno bhāgyavatāṃ bhavet \|*  
*svalpacchidrau supuṭau ca avakrau ca nṛpeśvare \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. A flat nose also indicates death and misfortune. A straight nose, with beautiful tip and small nostrils, indicates the signs of royalty.

## \|\| 65.66 \|\|

*krūre dakṣiṇavakrā syādvalināṃ ca kṣutaṃ sakṛt \|*  
*syādviniṣpiṇḍitaṃ hrādi sānunādaṃ ca jīvakṛt \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. A little curve on the right side indicates crookedness. Continual sneezing indicates strength. A flat nose indicates the possession of delight and that with sound indicates the possessor as being the supporter of all creatures.

## \|\| 65.67 \|\|

*vakrāntaiḥ padmapatrābhairlocanaiḥ sukhabhāginaḥ \|*  
*mārjāralocanaiḥ pāpmā durātmā madhupiṅgalaiḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. Persons, having eyes like lotus-petals with a little curve at the comers, enjoy all the luxuries of life. Sinful persons have eyes like those of a cat and wicked wights have twany-coloured eyes.

## \|\| 65.68 \|\|

*krūrāḥ kekaranetrāśca haritākṣāḥ sakalmaṣāḥ \|*  
*jihyaiśca locanaiḥ śūrāḥ senānyo gajalocanāḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. The crooked are squint-eyed and the sinful persons have yellow-coloured eyes. The heroes have oblique eyes and the warriors have eyes like those of an elephant.

## \|\| 65.69 \|\|

*gambhīrākṣā īśvarāḥ syurmantriṇaḥ sthūlacakṣuṣaḥ \|*  
*nīlotpa lākṣā vidvāṃsaḥ saubhāgyaṃ śyāmacakṣuṣām \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. The kings have got grave eyes and the ministers fleshy ones. The learned have eyes like the petals of a red lotus; while the fortunate men have dark-blue eyes.

## \|\| 65.70 \|\|

*syātkṛṣṇatārakākṣāṇāmakṣṇāmutpāṭanaṃ kila \|*  
*maṇḍalākṣāśca pāpāḥ syurniḥ svāḥ syurdenalocanāḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. Dark blue pupils and the absence of eyelids indicate the destruction of the possessor. The sinful wights have round eyes and the indigent have poorly-looking eyes.

## \|\| 65.71 \|\|

*dṛk snigdhā vipulā bhoge alpāyuradhikonnatā \|*  
*viśālonnatā sukhinī daridrā viṣamabhruvaḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. Those, who have got cool skin, enjoy the various objects of life. Those, who have got elevated navels, live for a short time. Those, who have got capacious and elevated navels, become happy. Those, who have got uneven eye-brows, become poor.

## \|\| 65.72-74 \|\|

*ghanadīrghāsusaktabhrūrbālendūnnatasubhruvaḥ \|*  
*āḍhyo niḥ svaśca khaṇḍabhrṛrmadhye ca vinatabhruvaḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

*strīṣu gamyāsu saktāḥ syuḥ sutārthe parivarjitāḥ \|*  
*annatairvipulaiḥ śaṅkhairlalāṭairviṣamaistathā \|\| 73 \|\|*

*nirdhanā dhanavantaśca ardhendusadṛśairnarāḥ \|*  
*ācāryāḥ śuktiviśālaiḥ śirālaiḥ pāpakāriṇaḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

72-74. Long but unconnected eye-brows indicate riches. He, who has got creascent-shaped eyebrows, becomes rich. One, who has got a cut between the two eye-brows, becomes indigent. Those, who have got bent down eye brows, know women unworthy of being known. A high, capacious, conch-shell-like and rugged fore-head indicates poverty. Persons, having crescent-shaped foreheads, become rich. Persons, having sinew fore-heads, become sinners.

## \|\| 65.75 \|\|

*annatābhaiḥ śirābhiśca svastikābhirdhaneśvarāḥ \|*  
*nimnairlalāṭairbandhārhāḥ krūrakarmaratāstathā \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. Persons, having high and triangular foreheads, become the possessors of wealth. Persons, having depressed fore-heads, are addicted to wicked deeds and worthy of being slain.

## \|\| 65.76 \|\|

*saṃvṛtaiśca lalāṭaiśca kṛpaṇā unnatairnṛpāḥ \|*  
*anaśru snigdharuditamadīnaṃ śubhadaṃ nṛṇām \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. A round fore-head indicates miserliness. An elevated fore-head indicates royalty.

## \|\| 65.77-79 \|\|

*pracurāśrudīnaṃ rūkṣaṃ ca ruditaṃ ca sukhāvaham \|*  
*akampaṃ hasitaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ mīlitākṣamaghāvaham \|\| 77 \|\|*

*asakṛddhasitaṃ duṣṭaṃ sonmādasya hyanekadhā \|*  
*lalāṭopasṛtāstisro rekhāḥ syuḥ śatavarṣiṇām \|\| 78 \|\|*

*nṛpatvaṃ syāccatasṛbhirāyuḥ pañcanavatyatha \|*  
*arekheṇāyurnavatirvicchinnābhiśca puṃślalāḥ \|\| 79 \|\|*

77-79. A dry unperspiring for-head is not auspicious tor men. A sufficiently perspiring and rough fore-head indicates happiness. Untrembling and expensive fore-head is the best and expressive of happiness. A laughing and wicked fore-head indicates madness. Three lines on the fore-head indicate longevity for a hundred years. Four lines indicate royalty and longevity for ninety-five years. Absence of any line indicates longevity for ninety years. When the lines on the forehead are broken a man becomes licentious.

## \|\| 65.80 \|\|

*keśāntopagatābhiśca aśītyāyurnaro bhavet \|*  
*pañcabhiḥ saptabhiḥ ṣaḍbhiḥ pañcāśadvahubhistathā \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. If the lines extend up to hairs a person lives for eighty years. If there are five, seven or six lines, a person lives fifty years or more.

## \|\| 65.81 \|\|

*catvāriṃśacca vakrābhistriṃśadbhrūlagnagāmibhiḥ \|*  
*viṃśatirvāmavakrā bhirāyuḥ kṣudrābhiralpakam \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. If they are dark-blue in colour a man lives forty years; and if they extend up to the eyebrows the person lives thirty years. When there are twenty lines bending towards the left it indicates longevity and when there are short lines it indicates short life.

## \|\| 65.82 \|\|

*chatrākāraiḥ śirobhistu nṛpā nimnaśirā dhanī \|*  
*cipiṭaiśca piturmṛtyurgavādyāḥ parimaṇḍalaiḥ \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. An umbrella-like head indicates royalty, auspiciousness and riches. A bland head indicates the death of one's father while a circular head indicates riches.

## \|\| 65.83 \|\|

*ghaṭamūrdhā pāparucirdhanādyaiḥ parivarjitaḥ \|*  
*kṛṣṇairākuñcitaiḥ keśaiḥ snigdhairekaikasambhavaiḥ \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. A pitcher-like head indicates vile desire and poverty. Black, straight, thin and not too much hairs indicate royalty.

## \|\| 65.84-86 \|\|

*abhinnāgraiśca mṛdubhirna cātibahubhirnṛpāḥ \|*  
*bahumūlaiśca viṣamaiḥ sthūlāgraiḥ kapilaistathā \|\| 84 \|\|*

*niḥ svāścaivātikucilairghanairasita (dhika) mūrdhajaiḥ \|*  
*yadyadgātraṃ mahārūkṣaṃ śirālaṃ māṃsavarjitam \|\| 85 \|\|*

*tattatsyā daśubhaṃ sarvaṃ tato 'nyathā \|*  
*vipulastriṣu gambhīro dīrghaḥ sūkṣmaśca pañcasu \|\| 86 \|\|*

84-86. Hairs, having many roots, uneven, with gross tips, twany-coloured, bent down, thick and dark-blue also indicare signs of royalty. Highly rough, sinewy body, deviod of flesh, is most inauspicious. Any other description is auspicious.

## \|\| 65.87 \|\|

*ṣaḍunnataścaturhrasvo raktaḥ saptasvasau nṛpaḥ \|*  
*nābhiḥ svaraśca sasattvaṃ ca trayaṃ gambhīramīritam \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. For kings there are three deep, spacious and long marks, five very fine, six elevated, four short and seven crimson coloured. Navel, voice and understanding these three should be deep.

## \|\| 65.88 \|\|

*puṃsaḥ syādativistīrṇaṃ lalāṭaṃ vadanaṃ hyuraḥ \|*  
*cakṣuḥ kakṣā nāsikā ca ṣaṭ syur nṛpakṛkāṭikāḥ \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. Fore-head, face and chest should be broad. Eye, side, tooth, nose, mouth and back of the neck should be high.

## \|\| 65.89-90 \|\|

*unnatāni ca hrasvani jaṅghā grīvā ca liṅgakam \|*  
*pṛṣṭhaṃ catvāri raktāni karatālvadharā nakhāḥ \|\| 89 \|\|*

*netrāntapādajihvauṣṭhāḥ pañca sūkṣmāṇi santi vai \|*  
*daśanāṅguliparvāṇi nakhakeśatvacaḥ śubhāḥ \|\| 90 \|\|*

89-90. Shank, neck, genital organ and back-these four should be short. Palms, corners of the mouth, nails, corners of the eyes. feet, tongue and lips should be red. Teeth, knots of fingers, nails, hairs and skin- rhese five should be very fine.

## \|\| 65.91 \|\|

*dīrghāḥ stanāntaraṃ bāhudantalocananāsikāḥ \|*  
*narāṇāṃ lakṣaṇaṃ proktaṃ vadāmi strīṣu lakṣaṇam \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. The distance between breasts, arms, teeth, eyes and nose should be long. I have thus described the characteristic marks of men. I will now describe those of women.

## \|\| 65.92 \|\|

*rājñyāḥ snigdhau samau pādau talau tāmrau nakhau tathā \|*  
*śliṣṭāṅgulī connatāgrau tāṃ pāpya nṛpatirbhavet \|\| 92 \|\|*

92\. She, who has got cool and equal feet and palms, coppery nails, joining fingers with elevated tips, becomes a queen. One, obtaining her \[as a wife\] becomes a king.

## \|\| 65.93 \|\|

*nigūḍhagulphopacitau padmakāntitalau śubhau \|*  
*asvedinau mṛdutalau matsyāṅkuśaghvajāñcitau \|\| 93 \|\|*

93\. Well formed ankle, lotus-like, tender and unperspiring palms containing the marks fish, goad and flag single out a woman for a queen.

## \|\| 65.94 \|\|

*vajrābjahalacihnau ca dāsyāḥ pādau tato 'nyathā \|*  
*jaṅghe ca romarahite suvṛtte viśire śubhe \|\| 94 \|\|*

94\. The feet of a queen bear the marks of a thunderbolt, lotus and plough-share. Well- rounded hips, devoid of hairs and arteries, are most auspicious.

## \|\| 65.95 \|\|

*anulbaṇaṃ sandhideśaṃ samaṃ jānudvayaṃ śubham \|*  
*ūrū karikarākārāvaromau ca samau śubhau \|\| 95 \|\|*

95\. Well-formed joints and even knee-joints are most auspicious. Thighs, like the trunk of an elephant, even and without hairs, are most auspicious.

## \|\| 65.96-97 \|\|

*aśvatthapatrasadṛśaṃ vipulaṃ guhyamuttamam \|*  
*śroṇīlalāṭakaṃ strīṇāmūru kūrmonnataṃ śubham \|\| 96 \|\|*

*gūḍho maṇiśca śubhado nitambaśca guruḥ śubhaḥ \|*  
*vistīrṇamāṃsopacitā gambhīrā vipulā śubhā \|\| 97 \|\|*

96-97. A capacious buttock, like unto a fig-leaf, is most auspicious. Loins, fire-head and chest, when they are of the fonn of a tortoise, are most auspicious. Fleshy wrists and hips are most auspicious for women.

## \|\| 65.98-99 \|\|

*nābhiḥ pradakṣiṇāvartā madhyaṃ tribaliśobhitam \|*  
*aromaśau stanau pīnau ghanāvaviṣamau śubhau \|\| 98 \|\|*

*kaṭhinau romaśā śastā mṛdugrīvā ca kambubhā \|*  
*āraktāvadharau śreṣṭhau māṃsalaṃ vartulaṃ mukham \|\| 99 \|\|*

98-99. A navel, capacious, deep and fleshy with three wrinkles inside, is most auspicious. Even and pointed breasts without hairs are most auspicious. Red lips are most auspicious and round and fleshy mouth is the best.

## \|\| 65.100 \|\|

*kundapuṣpasamā dantā bhāṣitaṃ kokilāsamam \|*  
*dākṣiṇyayuktamaśaṭhaṃ haṃsaśabdasukhāvaham \|\| 100 \|\|*

100\. Teeth must be like Kunda flowers and speech must be sweet like the notes of a cuckoo. She should be able to adjustable and acts like a swan.

## \|\| 65.101 \|\|

*nāsā samā samapuṭā strīṇāṃ tu rucirā śubhā \|*  
*nīlotpalanibhaṃ cakṣurnāsālagnaṃ na lambakam \|\| 101 \|\|*

101\. Mercy, simplicity and even nose are the most beautiful marks for women.

## \|\| 65.102-103 \|\|

*na pṛthū bālendunibhe bhruvau cātha lalāṭakam \|*  
*śubhamardhendusaṃsthānamatuṅgaṃ syādalomaśam \|\| 102 \|\|*

*sumāṃsalaṃ karṇayugmaṃ samaṃ mṛdu samāhitam \|*  
*snigdhā nīlāśca mṛdavo mūrdhajāḥ kuñcitāḥ kacāḥ \|\| 103 \|\|*

102-103. Eyes like blue lotuses well attached to the nose, eye-brows not very plump and like unto the rising moon, fore-head not very elevated and without hairs, not very fleshy and tender ears of equal size, and tender, curling and dark hairs are the most auspicious marks.

## \|\| 65.104-108 \|\|

*strīṇāṃ samaṃ śiraḥ śreṣṭhaṃ pāde pāṇitale 'tha vā \|*  
*vājikuñjaraśrīvṛkṣayūpeṣuyavatomaraiḥ \|\| 104 \|\|*

*dhvajacāmaramālābhiḥ śailakuṇḍalavedibhiḥ \|*  
*śaṅkhātapatrapadmaiśca matsyasvastikasadrathaiḥ \|\| 105 \|\|*

*lakṣaṇairaṅkuśādyaiśca striyaḥ syū rājavallabhāḥ \|*  
*nigūḍhamaṇibandhau ca padmagarbhopamau karau \|\| 106 \|\|*

*na nimnaṃ nonnataṃ strīṇāṃ bhavetkaratalaṃ śubham \|*  
*rekhānvitaṃ tvavidhavāṃ kuryātsaṃbhoginīṃ striyam \|*  
*rekhā yā maṇibandhotthā gatā madhyāṅguliṃ kare \|\| 107 \|\|*

*gatā pāṇitale yā ca yordhvapādatale sthitā \|*  
*strīṇāṃ puṃsāṃ tathā sā syādrājyāya ca sukhāya ca \|\| 108 \|\|*

104-108. Well-formed head and soles or plams, bearing the marks of horse, elephant, tree, sacrificial stake, wheat, Tomara, flag, chowri, garland, hill, well, altar, conch-shell, umbrella, lotus, fish. Svastika, car and goad are the signs of royalty in Women. The auspicious marks in women are well- formed wrists and hands like lotuses and palms not depressed nor very elevated. Linear marks on the palms are the signs which show that a woman will not be widowed and enjoy her life. If a line rising from the wrist goes to the middle finger it indicates the possession of kingdom and happiness in women.

## \|\| 65.109 \|\|

*kaniṣṭhikāmūlabhavā rekhā kuryācchatāyuṣam \|*  
*pradeśinīmadhyamābhyāmantarālagatā satī \|\| 109 \|\|*

109\. A line originating from the root of the youngest tinger indicates life for a hundred years. If a line passes from the tip of the thumb to that of the fore-finger it indicates the shortness of life.

## \|\| 65.110 \|\|

*ūnā ūnāyuṣaṃ kuryādrekhāścāṅguṣṭhamūlagāḥ \|*  
*bṛhatyaḥ putrāstanvyastu pramadāḥ parikīrtitāḥ \|\| 110 \|\|*

110\. If a line originates from the foot of the thumb and is long it indicates the possession of sons; and if it is short it indicates the possession of women.

## \|\| 65.111 \|\|

*svalpāyuṣo bahu (laghu) cchinnā dīrghāchinnā mahāyuṣam \|*  
*śubhaṃ tu lakṣaṇaṃ strīṇāṃ proktaṃ tvaśubhamanyathā \|\| 111 \|\|*

111\. If that line is broken at many places in indicates the shortness of life; and if it is broken at a long interval it indicates longevity. These are the auspicious marks for women and others are inauspicious.

## \|\| 65.112 \|\|

*kaniṣṭhikānāmikā vā yasyā na spṛśate mahīm \|*  
*aṅguṣṭhaṃ vā gatātītya tarjanī kulaṭā ca sā \|\| 112 \|\|*

112\. The woman, whose youngest or ring finger does not touch the ground or whose thumb is bigger than the forefinger, becomes unchaste.

## \|\| 65.113 \|\|

*ūrdhvaṃ dvābhyāṃ piṇḍikābhyāṃ jaṅghe cātiśirālake \|*  
*romaśecātimāṃse ca kumbhākāraṃ tathodaram \|\| 113 \|\|*

113\. Elevated calves, sinewy, hairy or fleshy hips, pitcher-like belly, depressed and small buttock are the signs of misery.

## \|\| 65.114 \|\|

*vāmāvartaṃ nimnamalpaṃ duḥ khitānāṃ ca guhyakam \|*  
*grīvayā hrasvayā niḥ svā dīrghayā ca kulakṣayaḥ \|\| 114 \|\|*

114\. Short neck is the sign of poverty and a long one is the sign of the extinction of the family.

## \|\| 65.115-116 \|\|

*pṛthulayā pracaṇḍāśca striyaḥ syurnātra saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*kekare piṅgale netre śyāme lolekṣaṇā satī \|\| 115 \|\|*

*smite kūpe gaṇḍayośca sā dhruvaṃ vyabhicāriṇī \|*  
*pralambinī lalāṭe tu devaraṃ hanti cāṅganā \|\| 116 \|\|*

115-116. Fat women are forsooth terrific. Squint and twany-coloured eyes, dark-blue smiling looks, and smiling and depressed cheeks are the signs of unchastity. If a woman has a tall fore head she kills the younger brother of her husband.

## \|\| 65.117 \|\|

*udare śvaśuraṃ hanti patiṃ hanti sphicordvayoḥ \|*  
*yā tu romottarauṣṭhī syānna śubhā bhartureva hi \|\| 117 \|\|*

117\. If the belly is long she kills her father-inlaw and if the-hips are high she kills her husband. Hairy lips are most inauspicious for husbands.

## \|\| 65.118 \|\|

*stanau saromāvaśubhau karṇau ca viṣamau tathā \|*  
*karālā viṣamā dantāḥ kleśāya ca bhavanti te \|\| 118 \|\|*

118\. Hairy breasts, rugged ears, sharp and uneven teeth conduce to their miseries.

## \|\| 65.119 \|\|

*cauryāya kṛṣṇamāṃsāśca dīrghā bhurtuśca mṛtyave \|*  
*kravyādarūpairhastaiśca vṛkakākādisannibhaiḥ \|\| 119 \|\|*

119\. If the flesh is dark-blue it shows she will be a thief and if it is tough it indicates the death of her hushand and she acts like a crow and should not believe on them.

## \|\| 65.120 \|\|

*śirālairviṣamaiḥ śuṣkairvittahīnā bhavanti hi \|*  
*samunnatottareṣṭhī yā kalahe rūkṣabhāṣiṇī \|\| 120 \|\|*

120\. A sinewy, uneven and dry body indicate poverty. If the upper lip is high it shows she will be quarrel some and harsh-speeched.

## \|\| 65.121 \|\|

*strīṣu doṣā virūpāsu patrākāro guṇāstataḥ \|*  
*narastrīlakṣaṇaṃ proktaṃ vakṣye tajjñānadāyakam \|\| 121 \|\|*

121\. Want of accomplishments and an ugly feature are both short-comings in women. I have thus described the characteristic marks of men and women which confer wisdom on men.

*hariruvāca \|*

1\. Hari said: — It is better to adore a stone which has no characteristic marks than the one which has a circular mark on it.

*tricakro 'sāvacyutaḥ syāccatuścakraścaturbhujaḥ \|*

The next is Vasudeva, then Pradyumna, then Sankarsana and the eighth is Purusottama. Navavyuha is the tenth. Aniruddha is the eleventh, then Ekadasa and then Dvadasatma. Ananta is on the top of all the lines. Where there is 6alagrama stone there lives the lord of Dvaravatl (Visnu). Where is the meeting between these two there is forsooth emancipation.

*aṅgirāḥ śrīmukho bhāvaḥ yuvā dhātā tathaiva ca \|*  
*īśvaro bahudhānyaśca pramāthī vikramo viṣuḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*citrabhānuḥ svabānuśca tāraṇaḥ pārthivo vyayaḥ \|*

8-10. Prabhava, Vibhava, бикга, Pramoda, Prajapati, Angira, Shrlmukha, Bhava, Pusa, Dhata, Isvara, Vahudhanaya, Pramathi, Vikrama, Vidhu, Citrabhanu, Svarbhanu, Druna, Irarthiva. Vyaya, $arvajit, Sarvadhari. Virodhi, Vikrta, Khara.

*plavaṅgaḥ kīlakaḥ saumyaḥ sādhāraṇavirodhakṛt \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-14. Nandana, Vijaya, Jaya, Manmatha. Darmukha, Hemalamva, Vilamya, Vikara, 6arvarl, Plava, &ubhakrt, 6obhana, Krodha, Visvavasu, Parabhava, Plavanga, Kllaka, Soumya, Sadharama, Virodhakrt, Paridhara, Pramadi; Ananda, Raksasa, Nala, Pingala, Kalasiddharta, Durmati, Sumatl, Dundubhl, Rudhirodgarl, Raktaksa, Krodhana, Aksaya- are the names which indicate years to be either auspicious or inauspicious.

## \|\| 66.15 \|\|

*kālaṃ vakṣyāmi saṃsiddhyai rudra pañcasvarodayāt \|*  
*rājā sā(mā) jā udāsā ca pīḍā mṛtyustathaiva ca \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. О Rudra, I will now describe time leading to success according to the system of Pancasuara1 (five vowels). They are Raja, Saja, Saja, Udasa, PIda and Mrtyu.

## \|\| 66.16 \|\|

*ā ī ū ai au svarāṃśca likhetpañcāgnikoṣṭhake \|*  
*ūrdhvatiryaggatai rekhaiḥ ṣaḍvahnikramamāgataiḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. In (he figure of five fires one should write the vowels A, I, U, E, OU. Six fires should come from the lines drawn upwards or askance.

## \|\| 66.17-18 \|\|

*tithī ekā gnikoṣṭheṣu trayo rājātha sā (mā) jayāḥ \|*  
*udāsāmṛtyupīḍāśca kujaḥ somasutaḥ kramāt \|\| 17 \|\|*

*guruśukrau ca mandaśca ravicandrau yathoditam \|*  
*revatyādimṛgāntāśca ṛkṣāṇi prathamā kalā \|\| 18 \|\|*

17-18. In (he house of one fire the times Raja, Saja, Udasa, PIda and Mrtyu are in order presided over by Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, Saturn, the sun and the moon, the first division of the time is presided over by the stars beginning with Revatl and ending with Mrgasira.

## \|\| 66.19 \|\|

*pañcapañcānyatra bhāni caitrādya udayastathā \|*  
*dvādaśāhairdvayormāsanāmnorādyakṣaraṃ tathā \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Beginning with the month of Caitra each group of five stars appears. From the first letters of the names of the stars twelve days and two months are derived.

## \|\| 66.20 \|\|

*kalāliṅgā ca yā tiṣṭhetpañcamastasya vai mṛtiḥ \|*  
*kalā tithistathā vāro nakṣatraṃ māsameva ca \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. In the fifth house of the figure the characteristic marks of the various divisions of Time are found. Form the first letter of the name of any article pronounced by a party divisions of Time, the various Tithis, various days, stars and months are calculated.

## \|\| 66.21-23 \|\|

*nāmodayasya pūrvaṃ ca tathā bhavati nānyathā \|*

*kṣāmādyaṅgaśivāmīkṣā viṣagrahamatirhara \|*  
*trailokyamohanaṃ bījaṃ nṛsiṃhasya tu padma(nna)gam \|\| 22 \|\|*

*mṛtyuñjayo gaṇo lakṣmī rocanādyaistu lekhitaḥ \|*  
*bhūrje tu dhāritāḥ kaṇṭhe bāhau ceti jayādidāḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

21-23. The mantram is "Om, Ksoum, Shivaya Namah." It is called Trailokyamohana. It counteracts the influence of evil stars on mental faculties and yeilds success, when written on a Bhurja leaf with Gorocana and along with the names of Siva, Gana and Laksmi, it is placed on the neck or arms.

## Chapter 67

## \|\| 67.1 \|\|

*(iti jyotiḥ śāstraṃ samāptam) \|*  
*sūta uvāca \|*  
*hareḥ śrutvā haro gaurīṃ dehasthaṃ jñānamabravīt \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Suta said: — Now I shall narrate to you the science of divination which the god Harlearned from Hari and disclosed to his consort Gauri, and the data of which can be gathered from one's own internal system or organism.

## \|\| 67.2-8 \|\|

*kujo vahnī raviḥ pṛthvī saurirāpaḥ prakīrtitaḥ \|*  
*vāyusaṃsthāsthito rāhurdakṣarandhrāvabhāsakaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*guruḥ śukrastathā saumyaścandraścaiva caturthakaḥ \|*  
*vāmanāḍīṃ tu madhyasthāṃ kārayedātmanastathā \|\| 3 \|\|*

*yadācara ilāyuktastadā karmasamācaret \|*  
*sthānasevāṃ tathā dhyānaṃ vāṇijyaṃ rājadarśanam \|\| 4 \|\|*

*anyāni śubhakarmāṇi kārayeta prayatnataḥ \|*  
*dakṣanāḍīpravāhe tu śanirbhaumaśca saihikaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*inaścaiva tathāpye pāpānāmudayo bhavet \|*  
*śubhāśubhaviveko hi jñāyate tu svarodayāt \|\| 6 \|\|*

*dehamadhye sthitā nāḍyo bahurūpāḥ suvistarāḥ \|*  
*nābheradhastādyaḥ kandastvaṅkurāstatra nirgatāḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*dvisaptatisahasrāṇi nābhimadhye vyavasthite \|*  
*cakravacca sthitāstāstu sarvāḥ prāṇaharāḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

2-8. The Mars, the Fire-God, the Sun, the Earth, the Saturn, the Water-God and the Nodes (Rahu), should be deemed as seated in, or permeating with their respective influences, the air or the vital wind that blows through the right nostril of a man; whereas the Jupiter, the Venus, the Mercury and the Moon should be regarded as the presiding planets of the wind that escapes through his left nostril. Rites or incantations undertaken or practised for the acquisition of territories or a place in the king's service, as well as acts such as the first starting of a trade or the first interview of a king, and auspicious works in general, should be performed when the breath- wind would blow through one's left nostril. The Saturn, the Nodes, the Mars, the Sun, and the Planet of Water, should be deemed as ascendent when the process of respiration would be performed through the right nostril, and all baneful priniples should be likewise regarded as dominant with them. The good or evil fate of a man can be divined from the escapage of the breath-wind through the different nostrils as well as from the predominance of the concomitant principles (Svarodaya) in the diviner. Net works of nerves of varied shape and immense extensions run through the body in all directions. From the nerve-bulb or nerve ganglion alone, situated below the umbilicus, there branch out no less than seventy-two thousand nerves, rolled up in the form of a coil or wheel, each carrying away the stream of life in their course.

## \|\| 67.9-10 \|\|

*tāsāṃ madhye trayaḥ śreṣṭhā vāmadakṣaiṇamadhyamāḥ \|*  
*vāmā somātmikā proktā dakṣiṇā ravisannibhā \|\| 9 \|\|*

*madhyamā ca bhavedagniḥ phalantī kālapūriṇī \|*  
*vāmā hyamṛtarūpā ca jagadāpyāyane sthitā \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. Three out of these innumerable nerves, preeminently rank as the most important. These three (occult) nerves run below the spinal column of a man, the left one being called the Ida, and the right one, the Pingala. The central one of this nerve system is called the Susumna. The Moon is the presiding deity of the Ida or the left nerve, the Pingala or the right nerve is effulgent with the light of the sun, while the Susumna or the central one owns the Fire God as its tutelary divinity, and it the destroyer of all phenomenal life. The Ida or the left nerve flows with the stream of divine ambrosia and laves the shores of the organic world with a perpetual flow of lite.

## \|\| 67.11 \|\|

*dakṣiṇā raudrabhāgena jagacchoṣayate sadā \|*  
*dvayorvāhe tu mṛtyuḥ syātsarvakāryavināśinī \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. The Pingala or the right nerve is permeated with the essence of the god of destruction (Rudra) and carries within it the principle of universal dissolution. The concerted work of these two nerves (the left and the right) leads to death and ushers in an absolute breakdown of all undertakings.

## \|\| 67.12 \|\|

*nirgame tu bhavedvāmā praveśe dakṣaiṇā smṛtā \|*  
*iḍācāre tathā saumyaṃ candrasūryagatastathā \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Inspiration or taking ih of the breath wind is performed by means of the Ida, while respiration or the process of letting in out, is done with the help of the Pingala. All blissful or auspicious acts, should be undertaken when the vital energy of the doer would remain confined to the Ida, while all fatal, or harmful incantations should be practised when the same would be lodged in the Pingala.

## \|\| 67.13-14 \|\|

*kārayetkrūra karmāṇi prāṇe piṅgalasaṃsthite \|*  
*yātrāyāṃ sarvakāryeṣu viṣāpahāraṇe iḍā \|\| 13 \|\|*

*bhojane maithune yuddhe piṅgalā siddhidāyikā \|*  
*uccāṭamāraṇādyeṣu karmasveteṣu piṅgalā \|\| 14 \|\|*

13-14. Sojourn to a distant land and all processes for the elimination of poison from the human system, should be started under the auspices of the flowing of the vital stream through the Ida, while a predominance of the Pingala (flowing of the life stream through Pingala) in a man, should be deemed as the most auspicious occasion for taking his dinner, or visiting his wife, or tighting his antagonist. Similarly a predominance of the Pingala should be made use of, in practising incantations which are fatal in their effect or can send one' s adversary crazy from his household.

## \|\| 67.15 \|\|

*maithune caiva saṃgrāme bhojane siddhidāyikā \|*  
*śobhaneṣu ca kāryeṣu yātrāyāṃ viṣakarmaṇi \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. A battle, or a sexual intercourse, partaken of, entered into, or commenced during the assendency of the Pingala, is sure to be crowned with success.

## \|\| 67.16-17 \|\|

*śāntimuktyarthasiddhyai ca iḍā yojyā narādhipaiḥ \|*  
*dvābhyāṃ caiva pravāhe ca krūrasaumyavivarjane \|\| 16 \|\|*

*viṣavattaṃ tu jānīyātsaṃsmarettu vicakṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*saumyādiśubhakāryeṣu lābhādijayajīvite \|\| 17 \|\|*

16-17. Kings and crowned heads, should take advantage of such a state of the Ida, in undertaking all acts which tend to make men happy, as well as in commencing a sojourn to a distant country, or in practising venomous charms or those which bring about the fruition (realishation) of one' own speech.

## \|\| 67.18-19 \|\|

*gamanāgamane caiva vāmā sarvatra pūjitā \|*  
*yuddhādibhojane ghāte strīṇāṃ caiva tu saṃgame \|\| 18 \|\|*

*praśastā dakṣiṇā nāḍī praveśe kṣudrakarmaṇi \|*  
*śubhāśubhāni kāryāṇi lābhālābhau jayājayau \|\| 19 \|\|*

18-19. A simultaneous flowing of the life current through both of these occult nerves (Ida and Pingala) should be interpreted to indicate on occasion when charms of both blissful and fatal virtues, should not be practised, and such a state should be deemed as the equator of life.

## \|\| 67.20-26 \|\|

*jīvājīvāya yatpṛcchenna sidhyati ca madhyamā \|*  
*vāmācāre 'thavā dakṣe pratyaye yatra nāyakaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*tanusthaḥ pṛcchate yastu tatra siddhirna saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*vaicchando vāmadevastu yadā vahati cātmani \|\| 21 \|\|*

*tatra bhāge sthitaḥ pṛcchetsiddhirbhavati niṣphalā \|*  
*vāme vā dakṣiṇe vāpi yatra saṃkramate śivā \|\| 22 \|\|*

*ghore ghorāṇi kāryāṇi saumye vai madhyamāni ca \|*  
*prasthite bhāgato haṃse dvābhyāṃ vai sarvavāhinī \|\| 23 \|\|*

*tadā mṛtyuṃ vijānīyādyogī yogaviśāradaḥ \|*  
*yatrayatra sthitaḥ pṛcchedvāmadakṣiṇasaṃmukhaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*tatratatra samaṃ diśyādvātasyodayanaṃ sadā \|*  
*agrato vāmikā śreṣṭhā pṛṣṭhato dakṣiṇā śubhā \|\| 25 \|\|*

*vāmena vāmikā proktā dakṣiṇe dakṣiṇā śubhā \|*  
*vāme vāmā śubhe caiva dakṣiṇe dakṣiṇā śubhā \|\| 26 \|\|*

20-26. A predominance of the left occult nerve is the most auspicious occasion for the purposes of a journey and for practising all lucky incantations, as well as for undertaking all works of profit and victory and those that contribute to the preservation of health and life. Similarly an ascendency of the right occult nerve, Pihgala, should be deemed as the signal moment for starting on a military expedition, on for visiting the bed of a woman and for undertaking all monor acts in general.

## \|\| 67.27-32 \|\|

*jīvo jīvati jīvena yacchūnyaṃ tastvaro bhavet \|*  
*yatkiñcitkāryamuddiṣṭaṃ jayādiśubhalakṣaṇam \|\| 27 \|\|*

*tatsarvaṃ pūrṇanāḍyāṃ tu jāyate nirvikalpataḥ \|*  
*anyanāḍyādiparyantaṃ pakṣatrayamudāhṛtam \|\| 28 \|\|*

*yāvatṣaṣṭhī tu pṛcchāyāṃ pūrṇāyāṃ prathamo jayet \|*  
*riktāyāṃ tu dvitīyastu kathayettadaśaṅkitaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*vāmācārasamo vāyurjāyate karmasiddhidaḥ \|*  
*pravṛtte dakṣiṇe mārge viṣame viṣamākṣaram \|\| 30 \|\|*

*anyatra vāmavāhe tu nāma vai viṣamākṣaram \|*  
*tadāsau jayamāpnoti yodhaḥ saṃgrāmamadhyataḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*dakṣavātapravāhe tu yadi nāma samākṣaram \|*  
*jā(ja) yate nātra sandeho nāḍīmaghye tu lakṣayet \|\| 32 \|\|*

27-32. A battle should be commenced, when the general or the warrior leading the attack, would feel his vital wind blowing through the occult nerves of rthe Sun and the Moon, and a person with such a state of vital air, enquiring about the probable result of the battle, should be assured of the success of the, party on whose behalf he had consulted the diviner. Such a party is sure to conquer the whole country lying at the angle of the compass which the vital wind blows to, even if the lord of the celestials confronts his army as an opposing rival. The ten occult nerves, such as the Aries, etc., and which are arranged in both sides of a human frame, represent the Lagnas such as the Cara (mobile) the Sthira (fixed), etc.

## \|\| 67.33-39 \|\|

*piṅgalāntargate prāṇe śamanīyāhavaṃ jayet \|*  
*yāvannāḍyudayaṃ cārastāṃ diśaṃ yāvadāpayet \|\| 33 \|\|*

*na dātuṃ jāyate so 'pi nātra kāryā vicāraṇā \|*  
*atha saṃgrāmamadhye tu yatra nāḍī sadā vahet \|\| 34 \|\|*

*sā diśā jayamāpnoti śūnye bhaṅgaṃ vinirdiśet \|*  
*jātacāre jayaṃ vidyānmṛtake mṛtamādiśet \|\| 35 \|\|*

*jayaṃ parājayaṃ caiva yo jānāti sa paṇḍitaḥ \|*  
*vāme vā dakṣiṇe vāpi yatra sañcarate śivam \|\| 36 \|\|*

*kṛtvā tatpadamāpnoti yātrā santataśobhanā \|*  
*śaśisūryapravāhe tu sati yuddhaṃ samācaret \|\| 37 \|\|*

*yastu pṛcchati tatrasthaḥ sa sādhurjayatidhruvam \|*  
*yāṃ diśaṃ vahate vāyustāṃ diśaṃ yāvadājayaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

*jāyate nātra sandeha handro yadyagrataḥ sthitaḥ \|*  
*meṣyādyā daśa yā nāḍyo dakṣiṇā vāma saṃsthitāḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

33-39. The diviner or prophet should hold up his face, in the shape of a bell after the enquirer had finished putting his query, and he would take ill or let out his breath wind simultaneously with the inspiration or respiration of the enquirer. О Shiva, the five fundamental material principles of the universe, are situated in the right and left sides of a human organism. The predominance of the principles of fire in a human system, should be inferred from the escaping of the vital wind along the upper part of the nostril, while the ascendency of the water principle, should be judged its outflow, touching the bottom line of the nostril. In the same manner the escaping of the breath-wind in a slanting direction, would indicate the predominance of the principle of wind. The predominence of the earth priniciple would be indicated by the breath-wind keeping a middle path inside the nostril, while the predominance of the principle of sky shold be inferred from the outflow of the breath as stuffing the nostril and running in all directions.

## \|\| 67.40-43 \|\|

*caresthire tadvimārge tādṛśetādṛśe kramāt \|*  
*nirgame nirgamaṃ yāti saṃgrahe saṃgrahaṃ viduḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

*pṛcchakasya vacaḥ śrutvā ghaṇṭākāreṇa lakṣayet \|*  
*vāme vā dakṣiṇe vāpi pañcatattvasthitaḥ śive \|\| 41 \|\|*

*ūrdhve 'gniradha āpaśca tiryaksaṃsthaḥ prabhañjanaḥ \|*  
*madhye tu pṛthivī jñeyā nabhaḥ sarvatra sarvadā \|\| 42 \|\|*

*ūrdhve mṛtyuradhaḥ śāntistiryak coccāṭayetsudhīḥ \|*  
*madhye stambhaṃ vijānīyānmokṣaḥ sarvatra sarvage \|\| 43 \|\|*

40-43. Incantations, endued with the mystic virtue of destroying life, should be practised during the ascendency of the principle of fire, rites of pacification during the predominance of the water-principle, charms for distracting human mind during the predominance of the wind, spells for benumbing the faculties of one's adversary during the ascendency of the earth principle, while penances for the emancipation of one's own self, should be practised during the predominance of the principle of the sky or ether.

## Chapter 68

## \|\| 68.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*parikṣāṃ vacmiratnānāṃ balo nāmāsuro 'bhavat \|*  
*indrādyā nirjitāstena vijetuṃ tairna śakyate \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Suta said: — Now I shall discourse on the method of testing the genuineness of gems and precious stones. There lived in ancient time a demon, named Bala. Bala conquered the god Indra and his celestials, and reigned supreme and invincible in the universe.

## \|\| 68.2 \|\|

*varavyājena paśutāṃ yācitaḥ sa surairmakhe \|*  
*balo dadau sa (sva) paśutāmatisattva surairhataḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. The gods, on the occasion of a religious sacrifice, jocularly asked him to play the part of the animal of the sacrifice.

## \|\| 68.3-4 \|\|

*paśuvatsa viśastastaiḥ svavākyāśaniyantritaḥ \|*  
*balo lokoparāya devānāṃ hitakāmyayā \|\| 3 \|\|*

*tasya sattvaviśuddhasya viśuddhena ca karmaṇā \|*  
*kāyasyāvayavāḥ sarve ratnabījatvamāyayuḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

3-4. This Bala consented to do and pledged his word for the performance of the part and suffered himself to be bound at the sacrificial stake. Whereupon the gods turned the jest into earnest and killed the invincible Bala in that mockery of a religious sacrifice. Thus Bala yielded up his ghost for the good of the universe and the welfare of the gods, and, behold, the severed limbs and members of his sanctified body, were converted into the seeds of gems.

## \|\| 68.5-6 \|\|

*devānāmatha yakṣāṇāṃ siddhānāṃ pavanāśinām \|*  
*ratnabījaṃsva(jama)yaṃ grāhaḥ sumahānabhavattadā \|\| 5 \|\|*

*teṣāṃ tu patatāṃ vegādvimānena vihāyasā \|*  
*yadyatpapāta ratnānāṃ bījaṃ kracana kiñcana \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. Then the gods and the Yaksas and the Siddhas and the Nagas eagerly rushed to collect those seeds of gems and there were mighty flutterings of celestial pinions and rustlings of celestial garments in heaven. The gods came riding in their aerial cars, and carried away the seeds of gems for their-own use, some of which dropped down of earth, through the violent concussion of the air.

## \|\| 68.7 \|\|

*mahodadhau sariti vā pavarta kānane 'pi vā \|*  
*tattadākaratāṃ yātaṃ sthānamādheyagauravāt \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Wherever they dropped, whether in oceans, rivers, mountains or wildernesses there origined mines of those gems through the celestial potency of their, respective seeds.

## \|\| 68.8 \|\|

*teṣu rakṣoviṣavyālavyādhighnānyaghahāni ca \|*  
*prādurbhavanti ratnāni tathaiva viguṇāni ca \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Of the gems and precious stones, some are endued with the virtues of expiating all sins or of acting as a prophylactic against the effects of poison, snake bites, and diseases, while there are others which are possesed of contrary virtues.

## \|\| 68.9-10 \|\|

*vajraṃ muktāmaṇayaḥ sapadmarāgāḥ samarakatāḥ proktāḥ \|*  
*api cendranīlamaṇivaravaidūryāḥ puṣparāgāśca \|\| 9 \|\|*

*karketanaṃ sapulakaṃ rudhirākhyasamanvitaṃ tathā sphaṭikam \|*  
*vidrumamaṇiśca yatnāduddiṣṭaṃ saṃgrahe tajjñaiḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. Gems, such as the Padmaraga, the Emerald, the Indranlla, the Vaidurya the Pusparaga, the Diamond, the peral, the Karketana, the Pulaka, Rudhiraktya (blood stone) the crystal, and the coral, should be carefully collected, subject to the advice of experts on the subject.

## \|\| 68.11 \|\|

*ākāravarṇau prathamaṃ guṇadoṣau tatphalaṃ parīkṣā ca \|*  
*mūlyaṃ ca ratnakuśalairvijñeyaṃ sarvaśāstrāṇām \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. First the shape, colour, defects or excellences of a gem should be carefully tested and then its price should be ascertained in consultation with a gem expert who has studied all the books dealing with the precious stones.
