20\. By casting obsequious cakes to his depaned manes in the front of the divine images of Gana, Purusottama and the sun god, a man is sure to lead their spirits to the region of Bramha.

## \|\| 86.21 \|\|

*natvā kapardivighneśaṃ sarvavighnaiḥ pramucyate \|*  
*kārtikeyaṃ pūjayitvā brahmalokamavāpnuyāt \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. By devoutly making an obeisance to the god KapardI Vighnea a man is sure to mount over all obstacles in life. The man who worships the god Kartikeya, is sure to be translated to the region of Bramha.

## \|\| 86.22 \|\|

*dvādaśādityamabhyarcya sarvarogaiḥ pramucyate \|*  
*vaiśvānaraṃ samabhyarcya uttamāṃ dīptimāpnuyāt \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. A worship of the twelve Aditayas, duly performed, is sure to prove curative in cases of all bodily distempers. A worship of the god of fire, imparts a healthful glow to the complexion of the worshipper.

## \|\| 86.23 \|\|

*revantaṃ pūjayitvātha aśvānāpnotyanuttamān \|*  
*abhyarcyendraṃ mahaiśvaryaṃ gaurīṃ saubhāgyamāpnuyāt \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. By worshipping the god Revanta a man becomes the possessor of a splendid stud of horses. The moongod, duly propitiated, grants the boon of unbounded wealth to the worshipper. A worship of the goddess Gauri confers affluence upon her votaty.

## \|\| 86.24 \|\|

*vidyāṃ sarasvatīṃ prārcya lakṣmīṃ saṃpūjya ca śriyam \|*  
*garuḍaṃ ca samabhyarcya vighnavṛndātpramucyate \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. A worship of the goddess Sarasvatl brings on wisdom to her suppliant, whereas the goddess LaksmI in creases the pecuniary resources of the man who duly supplicates her favour.

## \|\| 86.25 \|\|

*kṣetrapālaṃ samabhyarcya grahavṛndaiḥ pramucyate \|*  
*muṇḍapṛṣṭhaṃ samabhyarcya sarvakāmamavāpnuyāt \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. By worshipping the lord of the celestial birds (Garuda) one is sure to get over all impediments in the way to success, while the god Ksetrapala, duly propitiated, relents to nullify the evil influences cast by the malignant planets. The man who worships the sancturay of the Mundaprstha hill, lives to witness the realisation of all his desires.

## \|\| 86.26 \|\|

*nāgāṣṭakaṃ samabhyarcya nāgadaṣṭo vimucyate \|*  
*brahmāṇaṃ pūjayitvā ca brahmalokamavāpnuyāt \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. A man bitten by a serpent, is made sound and whole by worshipping the Nagastakam. The man who worships the god Brahma, is translated to the region of Brahma after death.

## \|\| 86.27 \|\|

*balabhadraṃ samabhyarcya balārogyamavāpnuyāt \|*  
*subhadrāṃ pūjayitvā tu saubhāgyaṃ paramāpnuyāt \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. A worship of the god Valabhadra imparts health and strength to the votary, whereas a propitiation of the goddess Subhadra brings good fortune in its train.

## \|\| 86.28 \|\|

*sarvānkāmānavāpnoti saṃpūjya puruṣottamam \|*  
*nārāyaṇaṃ tu saṃpūjya narāṇāmadhipo bhavet \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. By worshipping the god Puruspttama the best wishes of a man are sure to be realised. The man who worships the god Narayana is sure to extend his sway over the entire earth, and to become the undisputed monarch of the whole human race.

## \|\| 86.29 \|\|

*spṛṣṭvā natvā nārasiṃhaṃ saṃgrāme vijayī bhavet \|*  
*varāhaṃ pūjayitvā tu bhūmirājyamavāpnuyāt \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. By touching, and making obeisance to, the image of the Nrsimha (man-lion) manifestation of Visnu, one is sure to win victory in battle. The man who worships the image of the boar manifestation of Visnu at Gaya, is sure to be crowned as a king and to acquire proprietory rights in lands.

## \|\| 86.30 \|\|

*mālāvidyādharau spaṣṭvā vidyādharapadaṃ labhet \|*  
*sarvānkāmānavāpnoti saṃpūjyādigadādharam \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. By touching the image of Vidyadharl, one is sure to acquire the status of a Vidyadhara (celestial musician). By worshipping the image of the original club-wielding deity, a man is enabled to witness the realisation of all his desires.

## \|\| 86.31 \|\|

*somanāthaṃ samabhyarcya śivalokamavāpnuyāt \|*  
*rudreśvaraṃ namaskṛtya rudraloke mahīyate \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. A worship of the god Somanatha leads his votary to the region of Shiva. By making obeisance to the god Rudresvara, a man is sure to be glorified in the region presided over by the Rudras.

## \|\| 86.32 \|\|

*rāmeśvaraṃ naro natvā rāmavatsupriyo bhavet \|*  
*brahmeśvaraṃ naraḥ stutvā brahmalokāya kalpyate \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. The man who makes an obeisance to the image of Ramesvara, becomes endeared to the people like the illustrious prince (Rama) after whom the god is named. The man, who hymnises the god Brahmesvara, should be regarded as arleady a fit inmate for the region presided over by that divinity.

## \|\| 86.33-39 \|\|

*kāleśvaraṃ samabhyarcya naraḥ kālañjayo bhavet \|*  
*kedāraṃ pūjayitvā tu śivaloke mahīyate \|\| 33 \|\|*

*siddheśvaraṃ ca saṃpūjya siddho brahmapuraṃ vrajet \|*  
*ādyai rudrādibhiḥ sārdhaṃ dṛṣṭvā hyādigadādharam \|\| 34 \|\|*

*kulānāṃ śatamuddhṛtya nayedbrahmapuraṃ naraḥ \|*  
*dharmārtho prāpnuyāddharmamarthārtho cārthamāpnuyāt \|\| 35 \|\|*

*kāmānsaṃprāpnuyātkāmī mokṣārtho mokṣamāpnuyāt \|*  
*rājyārtho rājyamāpnoti śāntyartho śāntimāpnuyāt \|\| 36 \|\|*

*sarvārtho sarvamāpnoti saṃpūjyādigadādharam \|*  
*putrānputrārthinī strī ca saubhāgyaṃ ca tadarthinī \|\| 37 \|\|*

*vaṃśārthinī ca vaṃśānvai prāpyārcyādigadādharam \|*  
*śrāddhena piṇḍadānena annadānena vāridaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

*brahmalokamavāpnoti saṃpūjyādigadādharam \|*  
*pṛthivyāṃ sarvatīrthebhyo yathā śreṣṭhā gayā purī \|\| 39 \|\|*

33-39. By worshipping the god Kalesvara, a man becomes invicible to decay. A worshipper of the Kedara manifestation of Shiva, is glorified in the region sacred to thats divinity. The man who worships the god Siddhesvara, is sure to achieve penitential succes and is belauded in the region of Brahma. The man, who sees and touches the image of the original club-wielding deity at Gaya (Adi Gadadhara) succours the souls of a hundred generations of his departed manes and is translated to the region of Brahma. By worshipping the same deity, a seeker of sovereignty is sure to acquire a kingdom, a suppliant for peace would enjoy divine tranquillity in his soul, a worker for the liberation of his self would undoubtedly see his labours crowned with success, a lover of virtue would be strengthened in his love, and a solicit or of creature comforts would have enough of good things in life. In short there is not a single blessing which the human wish can name, which is not promised to a votary of the club wielding divinity. Similarly a female votary of the god woul be blest with the pleasures of maternity, or would be rewarded with the undying love of her husband as her supplication might be. The man who having worshipped the image of the club wielding deity, makes a gift of water, or of boiled rice or of obsequious cakes at Gaya, is sure to ascend to the region of Brahma after death. Gaya is the most sacred of all the sanctuaries on earth, and the club-wield,ing god, transformed into stone at Gaya, is the foremost of all the deities that deign to visit our mortal globe.

## \|\| 86.40 \|\|

*tathā śilādirūpaśca śreṣṭhaścaiva gadādharaḥ \|*  
*tasmindṛṣṭe śilā dṛṣṭā yataḥ sarvaṃ gadādharaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. He who has seen the club wielding god (maintainer of order and equity in the universe symbolised by his club or mace, has also seen his stone manifestation at Gaya, since He is the Universal Spirit who is all and runs through all.

## Chapter 87

## \|\| 87.1-2 \|\|

*hariruvāca \|*  
*caturdaśa manūnvakṣye tatsutāśca sukādikān \|*  
*manuḥ svāyambhuvaḥ pūrvamagnighrādyāśca tatsutāḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1-2. Said the God Hari: — I shall enumerate the names of the different law-givers of the world (Manu) who flourished in the different cycles of time, as well as their sons and progenies such as 6uka, etc., Sayambhuva was the name of the first law-giver of the world. He had seven sons named Marlci, Atri, Angira, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu, and Vasosth, who formed the brotherhood of the seven holy sages known as the Saptarsis.

## \|\| 87.3-4 \|\|

*jayākhyāśācamitākhyāśca śukrā yāmāstathaiva ca \|*

*viśvabhugvāmadevendro bāṣkalistadarirhyabhūt \|*  
*sa hato viṣṇunā daityaścakreṇa sumahātmanā \|\| 4 \|\|*

3-4. Twelve Ganas (regents or tutelary gods of the different quarters of the sky and of the physical phenomena as well) of that cycle of time, were named Jaya, Amita, Shukra, Yama, the four drinkers of the expressed juice of the Soma-plant, ViSvabhuk, and Vamadeva. The latter was elected the lord of the celetisals at the time. The Demon Vaskali invaded the kingdom of the then lord of the gods and the god Visnu killed him with his own discus.

## \|\| 87.5-7 \|\|

*manuḥ svārociṣaścātha tatputro maṇḍaleśvaraḥ \|*

*bṛhadguṇo nabhaścaiva mahābalaparākramaḥ \|*  
*ūrja stambastathā prāṇa ṛṣabho niścala (ra) stathā \|\| 6 \|\|*

*datto (mbho) liścāvarīvāṃśca ṛṣyaḥ saptakīrtitāḥ \|*  
*tuṣitā dvādaśa proktāstathā pārāvatāśca ye \|\| 7 \|\|*

5-7. After him Svarocisa became the Manu or the law-giver of the world. His sons were named Mandalesvara, Caitraka, Vinata, Karnanta, Vidyata, Ravi, Vrhatguna, and Nabha. The seven holy sages who sanctified that particular age with their holy lives, were called Urja, Stambha, Prana, Rsbha, Niscala, Dambholi and Arvariva. The race of Paravatas then habited this terrestrial globe. The guardian deities of heaven were twelve in number.

## \|\| 87.8 \|\|

*indro vipaściddevānāṃ tadripuḥ purukṛtsaraḥ \|*  
*jaghāna hastirūpeṇa bhagavānmadhusūdanaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Vipascit reigned as the lord of the celestials in that age and the demon Purukrtsara was his antagonist. The god Hari assumed the shape of an elephant and killed that dreadful demoniac adversary of the contemporary Indra, and restored the moral order of the universe.

## \|\| 87.9-11 \|\|

*auttamasya manoḥ putrā ājaśca paraśustathā \|*

*devo devāvṛdho rudra ! mahotsāhojitastathā \|*

*sutapāḥ śaṅkurityete ṛṣayaḥ sapta kīrtitāḥ \|*  
*vaśavartisvadhāmānaḥ śivāḥ satyāḥ pratardanāḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

9-11. The names of the sons of Outtama, the third Manu or law giver of the world, were Aja, Parusu, Vinita, Suketu, Sumitra, Suvala, Shuchi, Deva, Devavrdha, Rudra, Mahatsaha, and Ajita. The seven sages who flourished in that age, were named Rathouja, Urdhva-vahu, Parana, Aniagha, Muni, Sutapa and 6anku. The sons of Outtama numbered twelve in all. The races of celestials who habited the region of heaven, were five in all and named as the Va$avartis. the Svadharmanas, the Shivas, the Satyas and the Pratardanas.

## \|\| 87.12-13 \|\|

*pañca devagaṇāḥ proktā sarve dvādaśakāstu te \|*

*matsyarūpī harirviṣṇustaṃ jaghāna ca dānavam \|*  
*tāmasasya manoḥ putrā jānujaṅgho 'tha nirbhayaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

12-13. SvaSantI reigned over them all as their Indra or overlord. The demon Pralamba was the antagonist of the Indra of the age and the God Hari in his Fish Incarnation had to kill that enemy of the gods.

## \|\| 87.14 \|\|

*navakhyātirnayaścaiva priyabhṛtyo vivikṣipaḥ \|*

14\. The sons of Tamasa, the fourth Manu, were named Janu, Jangha, Nirbhaya, Nava, Khyati, Naya, Priya-bhrtya, Viviksita, Havu-SkandhI and Prostalaksa.

## \|\| 87.15 \|\|

*jyotirdhāmā pṛthuḥ (dhṛṣṭa) kāvyaścaitraścetāgnihemakāḥ (kau) \|*

15\. The seven holy sages who flourished in that age, were named Jyotidharma, Dhrsta-Kavya, Caitra, Agni and Hemaka. The twenty five clans of celestials who peopled the region of paradies in that are, were named as the Suragas, the Sudhiyasa etc.

## \|\| 87.16-19 \|\|

*harayo devatāmāṃ ca catvāraḥ pañca (sapta) viṃśakāḥ \|*

*vana (la) bandhurniramitraḥ pratyaṅgaḥ parahā śuciḥ \|*

*vedaśrīrvedabāhuśca ūrdhvabāhustathaiva ca \|*  
*hiraṇyaromā parjanyaḥ satyanetraḥ (nāmā) svadhāma ca \|\| 19 \|\|*

16-19. There were four sun gods in those days and 6ivi reigned as their Indra. The demon Bhlmaratha disputed the suzerainty of heaven with the latter and was subsequently killed by Hari in his tortoise incarnation. The sons of Raivata Manu were named as Mahaprana, Sadhaka, Vanavandhu, Niramitra, Pratyanga, Paraha, 6uci, Drdhavrata, and KetuSrnga. The seven holy ages who flourished in that age, were named Deva Sri, Veda Urdhvabahu, Hiranyaroma, Parjanaya, Satyanama and Svadharma.

## \|\| 87.20 \|\|

*abhūtarajasaścaiva tathā devāśvamedhasaḥ \|*  
*vaikuṇṭha (ṇṭhāḥ ścāmṛta (tā) ścaiva catvāro devatāgaṇāḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. The four celestial clans which peopled heaven in that age, were named Abhiita Rasa, DevaSvamedhas, Vaikuntha and Amrtas.

## \|\| 87.21 \|\|

*gaṇe caturdaśa surā vibhuridraḥ pratāpavān \|*

21\. The regents of the sky were fourteen in number, and Vibhu was the Indra or paramoimt soverign of them all. The demon Santa was the antagonist of the contemporary lord of heaven. The god Visnu assumed the shape of a swan and destroyed that molester of celestial peace.

## \|\| 87.22-31 \|\|

*abhimānaḥ sahiṣṇuśca madhuśrīrṛṣayaḥ smṛtāḥ \|*

*aṣṭakasya gaṇāḥ pañca tathā proktā divaukasām \|*

*aśvarūpeṇa sa hato hariṇā lokadhāriṇā \|*

*karūṣaśca pṛṣadhraśca sudyumnaśca manoḥ sutāḥ \|*

*gautamaśca bharadvājo viśāmitro 'tha saptamaḥ \|*  
*tathā hyekonapañcāśanmarutaḥ parikīrtitāḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*ādityā vasavaḥ sādhyāgaṇā dvādaśakāstrayaḥ \|*  
*ekādaśā tathā rudrā vasavo 'ṣṭau prakīrtitāḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

22-31. The sons of Caksusa Manu were named Uru, Puru, Mahabala, Shatadyumna, Tapasvl, Stayavahu, and Krti. The names of the holy sages who practised penances in that age, were Agnisnu, Atiratra, Sudyumna, Nara, Havis- mana, Sutanu, 6rimana, Sadharma, Viraja, Abhimana, Sahisnu, and Madhu-Shri. The five clans of the celestials were named the Aryyas, the Prabhutas, the Bhavyas, the Lekhas, and the Prthukas, and Manojava ruled as their Indra. The demon Mahakala was the enemy of the contemporary king of heaven who, was killed by the god Hari who had to assume the shape of a horse for the purpose. The sons of Vaivasvata Munu were named Iksvaku, Nabhaga, Dhrsti, Sharyati, Lavisyanta, Pansnsunabha, Navista, Karusa, Prsadhra and Sudyumna. The seven sages who sanctified the age with their piety, were named Atri, the god like VaSistha, Jamadagni, Казуара, Goutama, Bharadvaja and Visvamitra. The wind gods (Marut) numbered fortynine in all, and the celestial hierarchy which numbered fifteen in all, was divided into Adityas, Vasus, Sadhyas, Rudras, etc. There were eleven Rudras, Eight Vasus, two Asvins, ten Vi^vedevas, then Angirasas and nine divne Ganas in those days and Tejasvl was the Indra of them all.

## \|\| 87.32 \|\|

32\. The demon Hiranyaksa was the sworn enemy of the them lord of the celestials and met his doom at the hand of the god Visnu, incarnated as the primordial boar.

33\. Now I shall enumerate the names of the sons of Savarnl, the future Manu of the world. Their names would be Vijaya, Arvavlra, Nirdeha, Satyavak, Krti, Varista, Garista, Vacas and Sugatl.

*variṣṭhaśca gariṣṭhaśca vācaḥ saṃgatireva ca \|*

34\. The seven ages, who would grace the age with their advents, would be named Asvathama, Krpa, Vyasa, Galava, Diptimana, Rsasrnga and Rama.

35-36. The gods such as Sutapas Amrtabhas, and Mukhya, etc., would people the ethereal plains of heaven, and Bali, the son of Virocana would reign over them all as their Indra.

## \|\| 87.37 \|\|

*dattvemāṃ yācamānāya viṣṇave yaḥ padatrayam \|*

37\. The god Visnu, incarnate as Dwarf, would beg of him only three foot-measures of land. Bali would gladly grant him his behest, but would be deprived of his kingdom of the three worlds just at the time of ratifying his agreement, when the dwarf manifestation of god would expand into his Infinite the eternal self to the consternation of all the on-lookers. Subsequently Bali would make over his sovereignty to the god and happily descend into the shades of the nether world.

## \|\| 87.39-40 \|\|

39-40. Now hear me enumerate the names of the sons of Daksa Savarnl, the ninth Manu or the law-giver of the world, their names would be Dhrtiketu, DIptiketu, Pancahasta, Nirikrti, Prthusrava, Vrhatdumnya, Rcika, Vrhata and Gana. The demon Kalakaksa would be the enemy of the then lord of the celestials a l would be destroyed by the Padmanabha manifestation of Visnu.

41-42. The names of the twelve sons of Dharmaputra, the tenth Manu, would be Suksetra Uttamouja, Bhurisrenya, VIryavana, Shatanika, Niramrta, Vrsa-sena, Jayadratha, Bhurldyumna, Suvarca, 6antirindra and Pratapavana.

## \|\| 87.43 \|\|

*ayo (po) mūrtirhaviṣmāṃśca sukṛtiścāvyayastathā \|*  
*nābhāgo 'pratimaujāśca saurabha ṛṣayastathā \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. The names of the seven holy sages who would sanctify that age with their holy lives, would be AyomurtI, Havisman, Sukrti, Avyaya, Labhaga, Apratima and 6ourabha.

## \|\| 87.44 \|\|

*prāṇākhyāḥ śatasaṃkhyāstu devatānāṃ gaṇastadā \|*  
*teṣāmindraśca bhavitā śāntirnāma mahābalaḥ \|*

44\. The inmates of heaven would be divided into a hundred clanships at that cycle of time and would be called the Prana, etc. The demon Bali would dispute the suzerainty of heaven with the then lord of the celestials, and the god Hari would slay him with one stroke of his mighty mace weapon.

## \|\| 87.45-48 \|\|

*rudra putrasya te putrānvakṣyāmyekādaśasya tu \|*

*viṣṇuścaivāgnitejāśca ṛṣayaḥ sapta kīrtitāḥ \|*  
*vihaṅgamāḥ kāmagam nirmāṇarucayastathā \|\| 47 \|\|*

*ekaikastriṃśakasteṣāṃ gaṇaścaindraśca vai vṛṣaḥ \|*  
*dhasagrīvo ripustasya śrīrūpī ghātayiṣyati \|\| 48 \|\|*

45-48. Now hear me enumerate the names of the sons of Rudraputra, the eleventh Manu. They would be called Sarvatraga, Susarma, Devanika, Pururguru, Ksetravarna, Drdhesu, Ardraka and Patraka. Havisman, Havlsya, Varuna, Visva, Vistara, Visnu and Agniteja, would be the names of the seven holy sages who would flourish in that age. The inmates of heaven would be divided into different clanships, such as the Vihangamas (sky-coursers), Kamagamas (going any where they like), Nirmanas and the Rucis Members of the celestial family of Ruci would rule over each of the other clans of heaven, and Vrsa would be the overlord of them all. The demon Dasagriva (ten-necked one) would contest the sovereignty of heaven with the then lord of the celestials and would ultimately fall at the hands of the Shrirupa manifestation of Visnu.

## \|\| 87.49-50 \|\|

*manostu dakṣaputrasya dvādaśasyātmajāñchṛṇu \|*  
*devavānu padevaśca devaśreṣṭho vidūrathaḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

*mitravānmitradevaśca mitrabinduśca vīryavān \|*  
*mitravāhaḥ pravāhaśca dakṣaputramanoḥ sutāḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

49-50. Hear me enumerate the names of the sons of Dak§aputra, the twelfth Manu of the world. They would be named as Devas, Anupadeva, DevaSrestha, Viduratha Mitravana, Mitradeva, Mitravindu, VIryavan, Mitravahu and Pravaha.

## \|\| 87.51 \|\|

*tapasvī sutapāścaiva tapomūrtistaporatiḥ \|*  
*tapodhṛtirdyutiścānyaḥ saptamaśca tapodhanāḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Tapasvl, Sutapa, Taporati, Tapodhrti, Dyuti and another, would be the names of the seven holy sages whose glorious advent would sanctify that particular cycle of time.

## \|\| 87.52-53 \|\|

*svadharmāṇaḥ sutapaso harito hohitāstathā \|*  
*surārayo gaṇāścaite pratyekaṃ daśako gaṇaḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

*ṛtadhāmā ca bhadre (tatre) ndrastārako nāma tadripuḥ \|*  
*harirnapuṃsakaṃ bhūtvā ghātayiṣyati śaṅkara \|\| 53 \|\|*

52-53. The gods would be divided into different clans such as the Svadharmans, Sutapasas, Harltas, Rohitas, etc., and Rtadhama or Bhadra would be their Indra or overlord. The demon Taraka would invade the territories of the then lord of the celestials. О Sankara, the god Hari, incarnate as a eunuch, would destroy that fell perace-breaker of the universe.

## \|\| 87.54-56 \|\|

*trayodaśasya raucyasya manoḥ putrānnibodha me \|*  
*citraseno vicitraśca tapodharmarato dhṛtiḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

*sunetraḥ kṣetravṛttiśca sunayo dharmapo dṛḍhaḥ \|*  
*dhṛtimānavyayaścaiva niśārūpo nirutsukaḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

*nirmohastattvadarśo ca ṛṣayaḥ sapta kīrtitāḥ \|*  
*sva (su) romāṇaḥ sva (su) dharmāṇaḥ sva (su) karmāṇastathāmarāḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

54-56. Now hear me enumerate the names of the sons of the thirteenth Manu of the world. They would be named as Citrasena, Vicitra, Tapas. Dharmarata, Dhrti, Ksetravrtti, Dharmapa, and Drdha. О thou possessed of hand some eyes, the seven holy sages who would grace the world with their advent in that age, would be called Dhrtimana, Avyaya, Nisarupa, Nirutsaka, Nirmana, and TattvadarsT.

## \|\| 87.57-59 \|\|

*trayastriṃśadvibhedāste devānāṃ tatra vai gaṇāḥ \|*  
*indro divaspatiḥ śatrustviṣṭibho nāma dānavaḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

*māyūreṇa ca rūpeṇa ghātayiṣyati mādhavaḥ \|*  
*caturdaśasya bhautyasya śṛṇu putrānmanormama \|\| 58 \|\|*

*ururgabhīro dhṛṣṭaśca tarasvīgrā (gra) ha eva ca \|*  
*abhimāni pravīraśca jiṣṇuḥ saṃkrandanastathā \|*  
*tejasvī durlabhaścaiva bhautyasyaite manoḥ sutāḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

57-59. The celestials would be dided into thirty- three different clanships, such as the Svaro- manas, the Svadharmanas, the Svakarmans, etc. and the god Divaspatl would be the overlord of them all. The demon Trsthubha would dispute with him the suzerainty of heaven, and the god Madhava would kill him in the shape of a peacock. Now hear me enumerate the names of the sons of Bhoutya, the fourteenth Manu of the world. They would be named as Uru, Gabhlra, Dhrsta, Tarasvl, Graha, Abhimanl, Pravlra, Visnu, Sankrandana, Tejasvl and Durlabha.

## \|\| 87.60 \|\|

*agnīdhraścāgnibāhuśca māgadhaśca tathā śuciḥ \|*  
*ajito muktaśukrau ca ṛṣayaḥ sapta kīrtitāḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. The seven holy sages who would flourish in that age, would be named Agnidhra, Agni- viihu, Magadha, Suci, Ajita, Mukta and Sukra.

## \|\| 87.61-64 \|\|

*cākṣuṣāḥ karmaniṣṭhāśca pavitrā bhrājinastathā \|*  
*vacovṛddhā devagaṇāḥ pañca proktāstu saptakāḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

*śucirindro mahādaityo ripuhantā hariḥ svayam \|*  
*eko devaścaturdhā tu vyāsarūpeṇa viṣṇunā \|\| 62 \|\|*

*kṛtastataḥ purāṇāni vidyāścāṣṭādaśaiva tu \|*  
*aṅgāni caturo vedā mīmāṃsā nyāyavistaraḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

*purāṇaṃ dharmaśāstraṃ ca āyurvedārthaśāstrakam \|*  
*dhanurvedaśca gāndharvo vidyā hyaṣṭādaśaiva tāḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

61-64. The gods would be divided into five clanships, each consisting of seven sub-groups, or families, such as the Caksisa, the Karma- nisthas, the Pavitras, the Bhrajinas, and the Vacavrthas, and the god Shuci, would be then Indra or paramount ruler. The demon Maha-daitya would inimically intrude upon the rights of the then lord of the celestials, and the god Hari would slay him with his own hands. The god Visnu, incarnate in the shape of the holy Vyasa, would divide the one and the entire Veda, into four different parts, and subsequently compose the Puranas and the eighteen different branches of learning. The Vedas with their four kindred branches of study, the schools of philosophy known as the MImamsa, etc., the Puranas, the Dharrna- Shastra, the Ayur-Vedas (science of medicine) the Arthasastrakam, the Dhanur- Veda (science of archery) the Gandharva-Vidyas (music and fine arts), etc., form the eighteen diffemt branches of learning.

## Chapter 88

## \|\| 88.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*harirmanvantarāṇyāha brahmādibhyo harāya ca \|*  
*mārkaṇḍeyaḥ pitṛsto traṃ krauñcukiṃ prāha tacchṛṇu \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Suta said: The God Hari related all about the different ages or cycles of time to the gods Нага, Brahma, etc. Now hear me nattate the Hymn known as the Pitr-Stotram which the holy Markandeya heard of yore from the lips of Krouncaki.

## \|\| 88.2 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca \|*  
*ruciḥ prajāpatiḥ pūrvaṃ nirmamo nirahaṅkṛtiḥ \|*  
*atrasto 'mitamāyī ca cacāra pṛthivīmimām \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Markandeya said: — Once in days of yore, the patriarch Ruci, who was shorn of all vanity and attachment to world and its concerns, started out on a journey, free and friendless, with a view to see the different countries of the world.

## \|\| 88.3 \|\|

*anagnimaniketaṃ tamekāhāramanāśramam \|*  
*nimuktasaṃgaṃ taṃ dṛṣṭvā procuḥ svapitaro munim \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. The departed Manes of the patriarch viewed him from their abodes, trudging the land houseless and alone, and passing his nights in. bleak and unsheltered wildernesses without fire or friends to share in the perils of his journey. To him did they address as follows: —

## \|\| 88.4 \|\|

*pitara ūcuḥ \|*  
*vatsa kasmāttvayā puṇyo na kṛto dāra saṃgrahaḥ \|*  
*svargāpavargahe (se)tutvādvandhastenāniśaṃ (nimiṣaṃ) vinā \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. "О son, why hast thou foregone the pleasures of blessed matrimony, and why dost thou roam about cheerless and disconsolate without being bound in holy wedlock with an eligible bride?

## \|\| 88.5 \|\|

*gṛhī samastadevānāṃ pitṝṇāṃ ca tathārhaṇam \|*  
*ṛṣīṇāmarthināṃ caiva kurvallo kānavāpnuyāt \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. By duly propitiating the gods and one's departed Manes, and by attending to the wants of the needy and the holy sages, a householder, О son, becomes entitled to an elevated station after death.

## \|\| 88.6 \|\|

*svāhoccāraṇato devānsvadhoccāraṇataḥ pitan \|*  
*vibhajatyannadānena bhṛtyādyānatithīnapi \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. By uttering the Svaha Mantras (casting libations of clarified butter in fire) a householder is enabled to appease the gods, and a repetition of the Svadha Mantra leads to the propitiation of his departed Manes. Practice of free and hearty hospitality endears him to his guests, while servants and dependants eating his bread, look upon him as the mainstay of their lives.

## \|\| 88.7-8 \|\|

*sa ttvaṃ daivādṛṇādvandhamimamasmadṛṇādapi \|*  
*avāpto 'si manuṣyarṣe bhūtebhyaśca dinedine \|\| 7 \|\|*

*anatpādya sutāndevānasantarpya pitṝstathā \|*  
*akṛtvā ca kathaṃ māṇḍyaṃ svargatiṃ prāptumicchasi \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. О thou holy one among mortals, from day to day, thus thou hast been incurring more and more debts to the gods. Thy obligations to us, thy departed Manes, are getting heavier, and thy debts to the beings at large, as an inmate of the created universe, stand undischarged even up to the present moment. Where is the chance of thy working up to a better life, О my son, if you fail to marry and porpagate children and to take to the life of an anchorite afterwards, as laid down in the books of the Sastra.

## \|\| 88.9 \|\|

*kleśabodhaikakaṃ putra anyāyena bhavettava \|*  
*mṛtasya narakaṃ tyaktvā kleśa evānyajanmani \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Thy present conduct, therefore, brings thee nothing but misery and dooms thee to the pangs of successive re-births even after the cessation of the torments of that particular hell to which the souls of the "sonless are consigned".

## \|\| 88.10 \|\|

*ruciruvāca \|*  
*parigraho 'tiduḥ khāya pāpāyā dhogatestathā \|*  
*bhavatyato mayā pūrvaṃna kṛto dārasaṃgrahaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. To which Ruci thus replied: — Marriage is the parent of sin and misery, О fathers, and serves only to lower a man in the world to come.

## \|\| 88.11 \|\|

*ātmanaḥ saṃśayopāyaḥ kriyate kṣaṇamantraṇāt \|*  
*svamuktiheturna bhavatyasāvapi parigrahāt \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. This thought alone has therefore desisted me from being united with a wife. In a moment, it makes a man doubtful of his own spiritual life and therefore serves as a stumbling block in the way of his own salvation. Thinking of this I have hitherto refrained from marrying a wife.

## \|\| 88.12 \|\|

*prakṣālyate 'nudivasaṃ ya ātmā niṣparigrahaḥ \|*  
*mama tvapaṅkadigdho 'pi vidyāmbhobhirvaraṃ hi tat \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. It is better that an unwedded person, though fondly attached to life and its cares, should wash his soul daily with the water of pure knowledge than that he would marry and forget all about his spiritual self, and become of the earth and earthly.

## \|\| 88.13 \|\|

*anekabhavasaṃbhūtakarmapaṅkāṅkito budhaiḥ \|*  
*ātmā tattvajñānatoyaiḥ prakṣālyo niyatendriyaiḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. It is imperatively obligatory on a man. to subjugate his senses, aftd to constantly cleanse his soul of the mire, which his multifarious acts and promiscuous contact with a large concourse of created beings deposit upon it."

## \|\| 88.14 \|\|

*pitara ūcuḥ \|*  
*yuktaṃ prakṣālanaṃ kartumātmano 'pi yatendriyaiḥ \|*  
*kiṃ tu nopāyamārgo 'yaṃ yatastvaṃ putra vartase \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. To which the spirits of his fathers thus replied: — О son, certainly it is incumbent on all of us to wash our souls of all impurities by subduing our senses, still the way thou treadest, О darling, is not the proper road to salvation.

## \|\| 88.15-16 \|\|

*pañcayajñaistapodānairaśubhaṃ nudatastava \|*  
*phalābhisandhirahitaiḥ pūrvakama śubhāśubhaiḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*evaṃ na bandho bhavati kurvataḥ kāraṇātmakam \|*  
*na ca bandhāya tatkarma bhavatyanatisannibham \|\| 16 \|\|*

15-16. The effects of good or evil deeds done by thee in a previous existence, would not fetter thy soul in the event of thy performing the five daily sacrifices perculiar to a householder (Pancayajna) and practising pemincesand charities without any regard to their ulterior effects, and simply as a passive and involuntary instrument for the discharge of thy duties and for the absolution of thy daily sins.

## \|\| 88.17 \|\|

*pūrvakarma kṛtaṃ bogaiḥ kṣīyate hyaniśantathā \|*  
*sukhaduḥ khātmakairvatsa puṇyā puṇyātmakaṃ nṛṇām \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. The effects of good or bad deeds done by a person in a prior existence, are constantly worn away by his actual experiences of pleasure or pain in this life.

## \|\| 88.18 \|\|

*evaṃ prakṣālyate prājñairātmā bandhācca rakṣyate \|*  
*rakṣyaśca svavivekairna pāpapaṅkena dahyate \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Wise men thus absolve their soul and protect it from being any way fettered with the bonds of Nescience. The soul thus guarded, can never be soiled with the mire of sin. "

## \|\| 88.19 \|\|

*ruciruvāca \|*  
*avidyā pacyate vede karmamārgātpitāmahāḥ \|*  
*tatkathaṃ karmaṇo mārge bhavanto yojayanti mām \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Ruci said: — "Acts have been condemned in the Vedas by the celestial Brahmana as the direct resultants of Nescience, and wherefore, О fathers, — do you knowingly direct me to the path of action?"

## \|\| 88.20 \|\|

*pitara ucuḥ \|*  
*avidyā sarvamevaitatkarmaṇaitanmṛṣā vacaḥ \|*  
*kiṃ tu vidyāpariprāptau hetuḥ karma na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. To which the spirits of his fathers thus replied: — All is illusion in the universe and this universe itself is an illusion, О darling, and it is wrong to say that Nescience proceeds from action alone.

## \|\| 88.21 \|\|

*vihitākaraṇānartho na sadbhiḥ kriyate tu yaḥ \|*  
*saṃyamo muktaye yo 'nyaḥ pratyutādhogatipradaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. On the contrary action primarily leads to the expansion or true knowledge and this brooks no contradiction. The good and the honest shun the evil incidental to the omission of a good act, and this self-imposed restraint leads to salvation.

## \|\| 88.22 \|\|

*prakṣālayāmīti bhavānyadetanmanyate varam \|*  
*vihitākaraṇodbhūtaiḥ pāpaistvamapi dahyase \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. A restraint of a contrary nature tends to degenerate a soul. Thou hast considered it better to cherish pure thoughts in a pure soul, but it avails thee nothing, my son, so long as any charge of neglect or omission of duty may be laid at thy door.

## \|\| 88.23 \|\|

*avidyāpyupakārāya viṣavajjāyate nṛṇām \|*  
*anuṣṭhānā bhyupāyena bandhayogyāpi no hi sā \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Nescience, like an active poison., has its utility in the universe, which, being judiciously employed, rather serves to unfold the spirit than to tighten its shackles.

## \|\| 88.24 \|\|

*tasmādvatsa kuruṣva tvaṃ vidhivaddārasaṃgraham \|*  
*ājanma viphalante 'stu asamprāpyānyalaukikam \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Therefore do thou lawfully take a wife, О son. Otherwise in the absence of any provision for the future world, thy whole life would prove a miserable failure."

## \|\| 88.25 \|\|

*ruciruvāca \|*  
*vṛddho 'haṃ sāmprataṃ ko me pitaraḥ sampridāsyati \|*  
*bhāryāntathā daridrasya duṣkaro dārasaṃgrahaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Ruci said: — "I have grown old, О fathers, and who shall marry his daughter to an old man? Moreover marriage is a luxury which the poor can hardy afford to indulge in."

## \|\| 88.26 \|\|

*pitara ūcuḥ \|*  
*asmākaṃ patanaṃ vatsa bhavataścāpyadhogatiḥ \|*  
*nūnaṃ bhāvi bhavitrī ca nābhinandasi no vacaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. The Manes said "Our descent into the lower regions as well as the degradation of thy own Self, it certain, О son, if thou dost not profit by our advice."

## \|\| 88.27 \|\|

*ityuktvā pitarastasya paśyato munisattama \|*  
*babhūvuḥ sahasādṛśyā dīpā vātahatā iva \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Saying this the spirits of his (Ruci's) fathers vanished in the air like a lamp light suddenly blown out by the wind.

## \|\| 88.28 \|\|

*muniḥ kraiñcukaye prāha mārkaṇḍeyo mahātapāḥ \|*  
*rucivṛttāntamakhilaṃ pitṛsaṃvādalakṣaṇam \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. The holy sage Markandeya of mighty penance, narrated the entire discourse between

## \|\| 88.29 \|\|

*no sanskrit verse \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Ruci and his departed Manes to Krouncakl.'

## Chapter 89

## \|\| 89.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*pṛṣṭaḥ kraiñcukinovāca mārkaṇḍeyaḥ punaśca tam \|*  
*sa tena pitṛvākyane bhṛśamudvagnamānasaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Suta said: — Having again requested by Krouhcaki the holy sage Markandeya resumed the thread of the narrative and related as follows: — "The holy sage of Brahmanic extraction being this agitated by the words of his departed Manes, roamed over the whole earth in quest or a bride.

## \|\| 89.2 \|\|

*kanyābhilāṣī viprarṣiḥ paribabhrāma medinīm \|*  
*kanyāmalabhamāno 'sau pitṛvākyena dīpitaḥ \|*  
*cintāmavāpa mahītamatīvodvagnamānasaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. But a bride he could not secure anywhere. The words of his father's spirits were burning like living fire in his heart. So he easily fell in that mood in which a man often holds colloquy with himself and began be discourse as follows:

## \|\| 89.3 \|\|

*kiṃ karomi kra gacchāmi kathaṃ me dārasaṃgrahaḥ \|*  
*kṣipraṃ bhavenmatpitṝṇāṃ mamābhyudayakārakaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. "Where can I secure a suitable bride for myself and thus ensure an elevated station to my fathers and to my own self in the next world?"

## \|\| 89.4 \|\|

*iti cintayatastasyamatirjātā mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*tapasārādhayāmyenaṃ brahmāṇaṃ kamalodbhavam \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Then having indulged in a similar strain of thought for a considerable time the high-souled one resolved to realise his end by practising penance, and accordingly began to propitiate the lotus-origined Bramha with his austerities.

## \|\| 89.5 \|\|

*tato varṣaśataṃ divyaṃ tapastepe mahāmanāḥ \|*  
*tatra sthitaściraṃ kālaṃ vaneṣu niyamasthitaḥ \|*  
*ārādhanāya sa tadā paraṃ niyamamāsthitaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. For a hundred years thereafter, the magnanimous sage practised austere penance in that forest, and meditated upon the self of his tutelary deity in perfect mastery over senses.

## \|\| 89.6 \|\|

*tataḥ pradarśayāmāsa brahmā lokapitāmahaḥ \|*  
*uvācātha prasanno 'smītyucyatāmabhivāñchitam \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Then Bramha, the progenitor of the different worlds with their inmates, manifested himself in his presence and asked him to name his wished-for, boon as he had been highly pleased with his penances.

## \|\| 89.7 \|\|

*tato 'sau praṇipatyāha brahmāṇaṃ jagato gatim \|*  
*pitṝṇāṃ vacanāttena yatkartumabhivāñchitam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. The holy sage laid himself prostrate at. the feet of that appeased divinity and told the progenitor of the universe his intended course of action according to the directions of his departed Manes.

## \|\| 89.8-9 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*prajāpatistvaṃ bhavitā sraṣṭavyā bhavatā prajāḥ \|*  
*sṛṣṭvā prajāḥ sutānvipra samutpādya kriyāstathā \|\| 8 \|\|*

*kṛtvā kṛtādhikārastvaṃ tataḥ siddhimavāpyasi \|*  
*satvaṃ yathoktaṃ pitṛbhiḥ kuru dāraparigraham \|\| 9 \|\|*

8-9. Brahma said: — "You shall be honoured as a patriarch in the world. You shall be the progenitor of a mighty race of offsprings, О Brahmana, it shall be your portion in this life to celebrate many a religious sacrifice and to rule the country in all the glory 'of a patriarchal sovereign, and then your penitential labours will be crowned with success. Be united with a handsome damsel in holy wedlock as your Manes had enjoined you to be.

## \|\| 89.10 \|\|

*kāmaṃ cemamabhidhyāya kriyatāṃ pitṛpūjanam \|*  
*ta eva tuṣṭāḥ pitaraḥ pradāsyanti tavepsitam \|*  
*patnīṃ sutāṃśca santuṣṭāḥ kiṃ na dadyuḥ pitāmahāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Worship and propitiate the spirits of your departed forefathers, and marry in fulfilment of their pleasant command. Your fathers, perfectly appeased, would grant you the fruition of all your desires. What is it that is not in the gift of one's departed Manes? Fathers, duly propitiated, bless their descendants with wives and children."

## \|\| 89.11-12 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca \|*  
*ityṛṣirvacanaṃ śrutvā brahmaṇo 'vyaktajanmanaḥ \|*  
*nadyā vivikte puline cakāra pitṛtarpaṇam \|\| 11 \|\|*

*tuṣṭāva ca pitṝnvipraḥ stavairebhirathādṛtaḥ \|*  
*ekāgraprayato bhūtvā bhaktinamrātmakandharaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12. Markandeya said: — Having heard these words of the divine Brahma, the eldest offspring of the Phenomenal Evolution, the holy sage offered libations of water to his separted Manes at the open and spacious foreshore of a river, and with his head bent down in devotion, and in a spirit, earnest, humble and contrite, he propitiated them with a hymn which runs as follows:

## \|\| 89.13 \|\|

*ruciruvāca \|*  
*namasye 'haṃ pitṝn bhaktyā ye vasantyadhidevatam \|*  
*devairapi hi tarpyante ye śrāddheṣu svadhottaraiḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Ruci said: — With deep and unbounded devotion I make obeisance to the spirits of my fathers who sit beside the gods, and whom even the heaven-borns worship and propitiate with the Svadha-ending Mantras in the course of a Sraddha ceremony.

## \|\| 89.14 \|\|

*namasye 'haṃ pitṝn svarge ye tarpyante maharṣibhiḥ \|*  
*śrāddhairmanomayairbhaktyā bhuktimuktimabhīpsubhiḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. I make obeisance to the Pitrs, whom even the great sages who are seekers after both salvation and earthly enjoyment, adore in heaven and propitate with rites of purely mental Shraddha worship.

## \|\| 89.15 \|\|

*namasye 'haṃ pitṝnsvarge siddhāḥ santarpayanti yān \|*  
*śrāddheṣu divyaiḥ sakalairupahārairanuttamaiḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. I make obeisance to the Pitrs, whom the Siddhas propitiate in heaven with offerings of celestial produce in the course of a 6raddha ceremony.

## \|\| 89.16 \|\|

*namasye 'haṃ pitṝn bhaktyā yer'cyante guhyakairdivi \|*  
*tanmayatvena vādhadbhiḥ ṛddhimātyantikīṃ parām \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. I make obeisance to the Pitrs, whom the Guhyakas worship in heaven with their whole soul merged in the contemplation of the former with a view to acquire infinite beatitude and unparalleled and most exulted divine- privileges.

## \|\| 89.17 \|\|

*namasye 'haṃ pitṝnmartyairarcyante bhuvi ye sadā \|*  
*śrāddheṣu śraddhayābhīṣṭalokapuṣṭipradāyinaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. I make obeisance to the Pitrs, who are worshipped in this mortal globe with the offerings of a 6raddha ceremony and who, when properly propitiated, bless its performer with a long line of sons and grandsons.

## \|\| 89.18 \|\|

*namasye 'haṃ pitṝnviprairarcyante bhuvi ye sadā \|*  
*vāñchitābhīṣṭalābhāya prājāpatyapradāyinaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. I make obeisance to the Pitrs, who are worshipped even by the twice-born ones in this world with a view to obtain their wished-for boons and who confer on their votaries the glories of an illustrious patriarch.

## \|\| 89.19 \|\|

*namasye 'haṃ pitṝnye vai tarpyante 'raṇyavāsibhiḥ \|*  
*vanyaiḥ śrāddhairyatāhāraistaponirdhūtakalmaṣaiḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. I make obeisance to the Pitrs, who are worshipped by the forest dwellers of regulated diet, with fruits and flowers-the simple, though godly, offerings of the forest tress, sanctified with the occult energy of their well-practised Yoga.

## \|\| 89.20 \|\|

*namasye 'haṃ pitṝnviprairnaiṣṭhikairdharmacāribhiḥ \|*  
*ye saṃyatātmabhirnityaṃ santarpyante samādhibhiḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. I make obeisance to the Pitrs, who are worshipped and propitiated with the sacred energy of their Samadhi Yoga by Brahmanas exercising a perfect control over their senses, and the propulsions of whose minds have become one with the principles of virtue.

## \|\| 89.21 \|\|

*namasye 'haṃ pitṝñchrāddhai rājanyāstarpayanti yān \|*  
*kavyairaśeṣaividhivallokadvayaphalapradān \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. I make obeisance to the Pitrs, who are worshipped by crowned heads and potentates with various victuals of costly manuncture and who when duly propitiated, bless their votaries with blessings which take effect both in this world and the next.

## \|\| 89.22 \|\|

*namasye 'haṃ pitṝnvaiśyairarcyante bhuvi ye sadā \|*  
*svakarmābhiratairnnityaṃ puṣpadhūpānnavāribhiḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. I make obeisance to the Pitrs whom the Vaisyas (members of the trading caste) who are always mindful of their own work, worship with flowers, incense-sticks, bolied rice and water.

## \|\| 89.23 \|\|

*namasye 'haṃ pitṝñchrāddhe śūdrairapi ca bhaktitaḥ \|*  
*santarpyate jagatkṛtsnaṃ nāmnā khyātāḥ sukālinaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. I make obeisance to the Pitrs, who are worshipped even by the Shudras and are known as the Sukalinas.

## \|\| 89.24 \|\|

*namasye 'haṃ pitṝñchrāddhe pātāle ye mahāsuraiḥ \|*  
*santarpyante sudhāhārāstyaktadambhamadaiḥ sadā \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. I make obeisance to the Pitrs whom the great demons worship in the nether worlds, foregoing the pleasures of wine, bestial food, boisterousness and animalism.

## \|\| 89.25 \|\|

*namasye 'haṃ pitṝñchrāddhairarcyante ye rasātale \|*  
*bhogairaśeṣairvidhivannāgaiḥ kāmānabhīpsubhiḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. I make obeisance to the Pitrs whom the various serpents worship in the nether world with a variety of costly oblations for the fruition of their heart-felt objects.

## \|\| 89.26-27 \|\|

*namasye 'haṃ pitṝñchrāddhaiḥ sarpaiḥ santarpitānsadā \|*  
*tatraiva vidhivanmantrabhogasampatsamanvitaiḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*pitṝnnamasye nivasanti sākṣādye devaloke 'tha mahītale vā \|*  
*tathāntarikṣe ca surāripūjyāste vai pratīcchantu mayopanītam \|\| 27 \|\|*

26-27. I make obeisance to the Pitrs whom the snakes worship with the gift of their incantations, etc. I make obeisance to the Pitrs who dwell in my presence, or on earth, or in the welkin, and to those who ramble in the glorious fields of heaven, adored by the lord of the celestials. May they deign to accept the offerings which I have made at this place.

## \|\| 89.28 \|\|

*pitṝnnamasye paramārthabhūtā ye vai vimāne nivasantyamūrtāḥ \|*  
*yajanti yānastamalairmanobhiryogīśvarāḥ kleśavimuktihetūn \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. I make obeisance to the Pitrs, who live in heaven as embodied beings, and who form the highest object of thought and contemplation, and whose satisfaction is the summum bonum of human existence and whom the adepts in Yoga worship in a pure and unspotted heart for exemption from pain and miseries of successive re-births.

## \|\| 89.29 \|\|

*pitṝnnamasye divi ye ca mūrtāḥ svadhābhujaḥ kāmyaphalābhisandhau \|*  
*pradānaśaktāḥ sakalepsitānāṃ vimuktidā ye 'nabhisaṃhiteṣu \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. I make obeisance to the Pitrs who dwell as embodied bemgs in heaven, living upon the libations of clarified butter cast in the course 6raddha the accompaniment of the Svadha Mantras, and who are capable of granting all wished-for boons to their votaries; crown with success all ceremonial rites undertaken for the fruition of any definite object; and are the liberators from all undesirable situations.

## \|\| 89.30 \|\|

*tṛpyantu te 'sminpitaraḥ samastā icchāvatāṃ ye pradiśanti kāmān \|*  
*suratvamindratvamito 'dhikaṃ vā gajāśvaratnāni mahāgṛhāṇi \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. May my fathers in heaven be propitiated in the present 6raddha ceremony. May my Pitrs, who grant all sorts-of boons to persons soliciting them, and in whose gifts are the sovereignty of heaven, horses, elephants, cars,, gem- studded dwellings and other paraphernalia of riches, be pleased with the present Sraddha ceremony celebrated for their satisfaction.

## \|\| 89.31 \|\|

*somasya ye raśmiṣu yer'kabimbe śukle vimāne ca sadā vasanti \|*  
*tṛpyantu te 'sminpitaro 'nnatoyairgandhādinā puṣṭimito vrajantu \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. May the spirits of my departed forefathers, who float in the moon-beam and ride on the white rays of solar light, be pleased with the present ceremony, and may they thrive on the offerings of flowers, perfumes, etc., offered in the course hereof.

## \|\| 89.32 \|\|

*yeṣāṃ hute 'gnau haviṣā ca tṛptirye bhuñjate vipraśarīrasaṃsthāḥ \|*  
*ye piṇḍadānena mudaṃ prayānti tṛpyantu te 'sminpitaro 'nnatoyaiḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. May the souls of my departed ancestors, who take delight in a well-kindled sacrificial fire blazing with the libations of clarified butter, and who, by temporarily residing in the bodies of the Brahmanas invited on the occasion, partake of what is offered to them in the course of a 6raddha ceremony, be pleased with the offerings of boiled rice and libations of water offered to them in the present ceremony.

## \|\| 89.33 \|\|

*ye khaḍgamāṃsena surairabhīṣṭaiḥ kṛṣṇaistilairdivya manoharaiśca \|*  
*kālena śākena maharṣivaryaiḥ saṃprīṇitāste mudamatra yāntu \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. May the Pitrs whom the gods worship with the flesh of a rhinoceros and the offerings of black sesamum of celestial origin, and whom the holy sages propitiate with dishes of cooked and prepared pot-herbs, known as the Kala бака, be pleased with the present ceremony undertaken for their propitiation.

## \|\| 89.34 \|\|

*kavyānyaśeṣāṇi ca yānyabhīṣṭānyatīva teṣāṃ mama pūjitānām \|*  
*teṣāñca sānnidhyamihāstu puṣpagandhāmbubhojyeṣu mayā kṛteṣu \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. In the present ceremony I invoke the presence of the revered souls of my departed ancestors, who are extremely fond of obsequious cakes, in order they might receive the offerings of boiled rice, and perfumes, and libations of water to be offered to them at its close.

## \|\| 89.35 \|\|

*dinedine ye pratigṛhṇater'cāṃ māsāntapūjyā bhuvi ye 'ṣṭakāsu \|*  
*ye vatsarānte 'bhyudaye ca pūjyāḥ prayāntu te me pitaro 'tra tuṣṭim \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. May my departed Manes, who receive our loving homage every day and are worshipped every month on the occasion of an Astaka ceremony and at the close of each year under the auspicies of a Vrddhi 6raddha, be pleased with the present ceremony.

## \|\| 89.36-37 \|\|

*pūjyā dvijānāṃ kumudendubhāso ye kṣattriyāṇāṃ jvalanārkavarṇāḥ \|*  
*tathā viśāṃ ye kanakāvadātā nīlīprabhāḥ śūdrajanasya ye ca \|\| 36 \|\|*

*te 'sminsamastā mama puṣpagandhadhūpāmbubhojyādinivedanena \|*  
*tathāgnihomena ca yānti tṛptiṃ sadā pitṛbhyaḥ praṇato 'smi tebhyaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

36-37. May the departed Manes of the Brahmanas, who shine with the cool and mellow lustre of the moon-beam, and the departed Manes of the Ks atriyas, who shine With the dazzling effulgence of the noon-day sun, and the departed Manes of the Vaisyas whose complexions are as the colour of molten gold, and the departed Manes of the 6udras whose complexions are deep blue, combinedly grace the present ceremony with their august presence, and be pleased with the offerings of flowers, perfumes, and edibles, etc., and the sweet exhalations of clarified butter cast in the sacrificial fire. Perpetually do I make obeisance to the Pitrs.

## \|\| 89.38 \|\|

*ye devapūrvāṇyabhitṛptihetora śranti kavyāni śubhāhṛtāni \|*  
*tṛptāśca ye bhūtisṛjo bhavanti tṛpyantu te 'sminpraṇato 'smi tebhyaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. May the Pitrs, who partake of the obsequious cakes just after they had been eaten by the gods, and who, when duly appeased, confer prosperity upon their votaries, be pleased with the present ceremony. I make obeisance to them.

## \|\| 89.39 \|\|

*rakṣāṃsi bhūtānyasurāṃstathogrātrirṇāśayantu tvaśivaṃ prajānām \|*  
*ādyāḥ surāṇāmamareśapūjyāstṛpyantu te 'sminpraṇato 'smitebhyaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. May the Pitrs, the mighty members of the celestial hierarchy, imd revered by the gods, destroy the demons, and the monsters and the evil spirits and all other baneful visitations in the universe. I make obeisance to the Pitrs.

## \|\| 89.40 \|\|

*agniṣvāttā barhiṣada ājyapāḥ somapāstathā \|*  
*vrajantu tṛptiṃ śrāddhe 'sminpitarastarpitā mayā \|\| 40 \|\|*

40May the different clans of the Pitrs, such as the Agnisvattas, the Varhsadas, the drinkers of clarified butter, and the drinkers of the expressed juice of the Soma-plant, be propitiated in the ptesent 3raddha ceremony.

## \|\| 89.41 \|\|

*agniṣvāttāḥ pitṛgaṇāḥ prācīṃ rakṣantu me diśam \|*  
*tathā barhiṣadaḥ pāntu yāmyāṃ me pitaraḥ sadā \|*  
*pratīcīmājyapāstadvadudīcīmapi somapāḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. I have propitited the souls of my departed forefathers May the members of the Agni- Svatta clan of the Pitrs, guard my person in the east. May the members of the Varhisada clan of that celestial order, protect me in the south. May the drinkers of sacrificial clarified butter protect me in the west, and the drinkers of the expressed juice of the Divine Soma plant, defend me in the east.

## \|\| 89.42 \|\|

*rakṣobhūtapiśācebhyastathaivāsuradoṣataḥ \|*  
*sarvataḥ pitaro rakṣāṃ kurvantu mama nityaśaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. May the Pitrs perpetually guard me against the malignam influences of ghoSts, demons, monsters, and Pisacas.

## \|\| 89.43 \|\|

*viśvo viśvabhugārādhyo dharmo dhanyaḥ śubhānanaḥ \|*  
*bhūtido bhūtikṛd bhūtiḥ pitṝṇāṃ ye gaṇā nava \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. The nine clans of Pitrs are named as the Visvas, the Visvabhugs, the Aradhyas, the Dharmas, the Dhanyas, the Shubhananas, the Bhutidas, the Bhutikrds, and the Bhutis.

## \|\| 89.44 \|\|

*kalyāṇaḥ kalyadaḥ kartā kalyaḥ kalyatarāśrayaḥ \|*  
*kalyatāheturanghaḥ ṣaḍime te gaṇāḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. The six other clans of the same celestial order, are known as the Kalyanas, the Kalyadas, the Kartas, the Kalyatarsrayas, and the Kalyatahetu.

## \|\| 89.45 \|\|

*varo vareṇyo varadastuṣṭidaḥ puṣṭidastathā \|*  
*viśvapātā tathā dhātā saptaite ca gaṇāḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. The seven other clans of the same divine order, are called the Varas, the Varenyas, the Varadas, the Tustidas, the Pustidas, the Visvapatas, and the Dhatas.

## \|\| 89.46 \|\|

*mahānmahātmā mahito mahimāvānmahābalaḥ \|*  
*gaṇāḥ pañca tathaivaite pitṝṇāṃ pāpanāśanāḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. The five clans of the same order, are named as the Mahan, the Matmas, the Mahitas, the Mahimavanas and the Mahabalas.

## \|\| 89.47-48 \|\|

*sukhado dhanadaścānyo dharmado 'nyaśca bhūtidaḥ \|*  
*pitṝṇāṃ kathyate caiva tathā gaṇacatuṣṭayam \|\| 47 \|\|*

*ekatriṃśatpitṛgaṇā yairvyāptamakhilaṃ jagat \|*  
*ta evātra pitṛgaṇāstuṣyantu ca madāhitāt \|\| 48 \|\|*

47-48. The four remaining clans of the same order, are called the Sukhadas, the Dharmadas, and the Bhutidas, thus making thirty-one clanships in all, who guard thwdifferent approaches of the heaven, and are distributed all over the universe for the good of its inmates. May all of them be pleased with the present ceremony, duly inaugurated for their propitiation.

## \|\| 89.49 \|\|

*mākraṇḍeya uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ tu stuvatastasya tejasorāśirucchritaḥ \|*  
*prādurbabhūva sahasā gaganavyāptikārakaḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Markandeya said: — While Ruci was thus devoutly hymnising his departed Manes, a vast column of light suddenly shot across the heaven, and, behold, the universe stood entranced, wrapped in that mystic glow.

## \|\| 89.50 \|\|

*taddṛṣṭvā sumahattejaḥ samācchādya sthitaṃ jagat \|*  
*jānubhyāmavanīṃ gatvā ruciḥ stotramidañjagau \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Ruci looked up and beheld that glorious phenomenon in mute wonder, and began to recite the following hymn on bent down knees.

## \|\| 89.51 \|\|

*ruciruvāca \|*  
*arcitānāmamūrtānāṃ pitṝṇāṃ dīptatejasām \|*  
*namasyāmi sadā teṣāṃ dhyānināṃ divyacakṣuṣām \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Ruci said: — Ever do I make obeisance to the Pitrs, who are resplendent and disembodied spirits, endued with the faculty of spiritual vision, and always absorbed in the contemplation of the supreme Bramha.

## \|\| 89.52 \|\|

*indrādīnāṃ ca netāro dakṣamārīcayostathā \|*  
*saptarṣoṇāṃ tathānyeṣāṃ tānnamasyāmi kāmadān \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. I make obeisance to the Pitrs, who are the leaders of such celestial potentates as Indra, etc., and direct such holy sages as Daksa, Marlci, etc., who constitute the holy fraternity of the seven sages, in the pawof truth and light, and who confer all boons upon their suppliants.

## \|\| 89.53 \|\|

*manvādīnāṃ ca netāraḥ sūryācandramasostathā \|*  
*tānnamasyāmyahaṃ sarvānpitṝnapyudadhāvapi \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. I make odeisance to the Pitrs who are the leaders of such mighty law-givers as Manu, etc., and who direct the sun and the moon in their path of heavenly duty.

## \|\| 89.54-56 \|\|

*nakṣatrāṇāṃ grahāṇāṃ ca vāyvagnyornabhasastathā \|*  
*dyāvāpṛthivyośca tathā namasyāmi kṛtāñjaliḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

*prajāpateḥ kaśyapāya somāya varuṇāya ca \|*  
*yogeśvarebhyaśca sadā namasyāmi kṛtāñjaliḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

*namo gaṇebhyaḥ saptabhyastathā lokeṣu saptasu \|*  
*svāyambhuve namasyāmi brahmaṇe yogacakṣuṣe \|\| 56 \|\|*

54-56. I make obeisance to the Pitrs, who contro the movements of the wind, guide the stars and planets in their orbits and sojourns, uphold the welkin, make the fire bum with its natural hel and glare, and fill in the earth and heaven and the space lying between them. With blended palms, I make obeisance to Prajapati, to Kasyapa to Soma, to Varima, to the lord of all religion sacrifices I make obeisance to the seven clans of the Pitrs, who dwell in the seven regions or worlds. I make obeisance to the self- begotten Bramha whose vision is the light of Yoga (divine communion).

## \|\| 89.57 \|\|

*somādhārānpitṛgaṇānyogamūrtidharāṃstathā \|*  
*namasyāmi tathā somaṃ pitaraṃ jagatāmaham \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. I make obeisance to the Soma-drinking Pitrs who are possessed of astral bodies. I make obeisance to the Moon God and the father of the universe.

## \|\| 89.58-59 \|\|

*agnirūpāṃstathaivānyānnamasyāmi pitṝnaham \|*  
*agnisomamayaṃ viśvaṃ yata etadaśeṣataḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

*ye ca tejasi ye caite somasūryāgnimūrtayaḥ \|*  
*jagatsvarūpiṇaścaiva tathā brahmasvarūpiṇaḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

58-59. I make obeisance to the fiery-bodied Pitrs, as. well as to those whose persons are composed of the cooling principle in the universe. The two fundamental principles (fiery and cooling) rim through all objects, and hence either they are fiery (heat making.) or cooling (watery, albuminous) in their potencies. With a controlled hean I make obeisance to all the Yogins and the Pitrs, who form the illuminating principle of light, and manifestly shine in the sun, in the moon and fire, and who are the models of creation and are identical with the Self of Supreme Bramha.

## \|\| 89.60 \|\|

*tebhyo 'khilebhyo yogibhyaḥ pitṛbhyo yatamānasaḥ \|*  
*namonamo namaste 'stu prasīdantu svadhābhujaḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. May the Pitrs who live upon the sweet exhalations of clarified butter cast in the sacrificial fire in the accompaniment of the Svadha Mantras, be pleased with the performance of the present ceremony.

## \|\| 89.61-62 \|\|

*mākraṇḍeya uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ stutāstatastena tajaso munisattamāḥ \|*  
*niścakramuste pitaro bhāsayanto diśādaśa \|\| 61 \|\|*

*nivedanañca yattena puṣpagandhānulepanam \|*  
*tadbhūṣitānatha sa tāndadṛśe purataḥ sthitān \|\| 62 \|\|*

61-62. Markandeya said: — Having been thus propitiated by Ruci, the best of the holy sages appeared to him in quick succession, illumining the ten quaners of heaven with the effulgence of their own spiritual bodies, and decked with the same sandal pastes and garlands of flowers which he had offered to them in the course of that Shraddha ceremony.

## \|\| 89.63-64 \|\|

*praṇipatya rucirbhaktyā punareva kṛtāñjaliḥ \|*  
*namastubhyaṃ namastubhyamityāha pṛthagādṛtaḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

*tataḥ prasannāḥ pitarastamūcurmunisattamam \|*  
*varaṃ vṛṇīṣveti sa tānuvācānatakandharaḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

63-64. Then Ruci, having again made obeisance to them, addressed them for the second time as follows: — "With blended palms I make obeisance to each of you, О you Pitris!" Whereupon the Pitris!, appeased by his devotion and humility, asked him to name his boon, to which Ruci, with his head hung down in deep humility, replied as follows: —

## \|\| 89.65 \|\|

*ruciruvāca \|*  
*prajānāṃ sargakartṛtvamādiṣṭaṃ brahmaṇā mama \|*  
*so 'haṃ patnīmabhīpsāmi dhanyāṃ divyāṃ prajāvatīm \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. "I have been directed by the god Brahma to beget children and propagate my species. Accordingly most fervently do I pray for a noble and fruitful wife of celestial origin."

## \|\| 89.66-67 \|\|

*pitara ūcuḥ \|*  
*atraiva sadyaḥ patnī te bhavatvatimanoramā \|*  
*tasyāñca putro bhavitā bhavato munisattama ! \|\| 66 \|\|*

*manvantarādhipo dhīmāṃstvannāmnaivopalakṣitaḥ \|*  
*ruce ! raucya iti khyātiṃ prayāsyati jagattraye \|\| 67 \|\|*

66-67. The Fathers replied:-"0 you, the best of the holy sages, this very day you shall be united with an extremely handsome wife. By her you shall have a son, О Ruci, who would be named Roucya after your honoured self, and who would rule the universe as a patriach and lawgiver.

## \|\| 89.68-79 \|\|

*tasyāpi bahavaḥ putrā mahābalaparākramāḥ \|*  
*bhaviṣyanti mahātmānaḥ pṛthivīparipālakāḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

*tvaṃ ca prijāpatirbhūtvā prajāḥ sṛṣṭvā caturvidhāḥ \|*  
*kṣīṇādhikāro dharmajñastataḥ siddhimavāpsyasi \|\| 69 \|\|*

*stotreṇānena ca naro yo 'smāṃstoṣyati bhaktitaḥ \|*  
*tasya tuṣṭā vayaṃ bhogānātmajaṃ dhyānamuttamam \|\| 70 \|\|*

*āyurārogyamarthaṃ ca putrapautrādikaṃ tathā \|*  
*vāñchadbhiḥ satataṃ stavyāḥ stotreṇānena vai yataḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

*śrāddheṣu ya imaṃ bhaktyā tvasmatprītikaraṃ stavam \|*  
*paṭhiṣyati dvijāgryāṇāṃ bhuñjatāṃ purataḥ sthitaḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

*stotraśravaṇasaṃprītyā sannidhāne pare kṛte \|*  
*asmābhirakṣayaṃ śrāddhaṃ tadbhaviṣyatyasaṃśayam \|\| 73 \|\|*

*yadyapyaśrotriyaṃ śrāddhaṃ yadyapyupahataṃ bhavet \|*  
*anyāyopāttavittena yadi vā kṛtamanyathā \|\| 74 \|\|*

*aśrāddhārhairupatairupahāraistathā kṛtaiḥ \|*  
*akāle 'pyatha vā deśe vidhihīnamathāpi vā \|\| 75 \|\|*

*aśraddhayā vā puruṣairdambhamāśritya yatkṛtam \|*  
*asmākaṃ tṛptaye śrāddhantathāpyetadudīraṇāt \|\| 76 \|\|*

*yatraitatpaṭhyate śrāddhe stotramastatsukhāvaham \|*  
*asmākaṃ jāyate tṛptistatra dvādaśāvarṣikī \|\| 77 \|\|*

*hemante dvādaśābdāni tṛptimetatprayacchati \|*  
*śiśire dviguṇābdāni tṛptiṃ stotramidaṃ śubham \|\| 78 \|\|*

*vasante ṣoḍaśa samāstṛptaye śrāddhakarmaṇi \|*  
*grīṣme ca ṣoḍaśaivaitatpaṭhitaṃ tṛptikārakam \|\| 79 \|\|*

68-79. Не shall be the fore-runner of a mighty race of kings, high souled and victorious, who would governthe whole Earth. You in your old age, would retire from the world, decked with the full glory of a pious and revered patriarch, and shall attain your penitential success and salvation.

## \|\| 89.71 \|\|

*āyurārogyamarthaṃ ca putrapautrādikaṃ tathā \|*  
*vāñchadbhiḥ satataṃ stavyāḥ stotreṇānena vai yataḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. Blessed is the man who recites the aforesaid hymn for our satisfaction, for he will be blest with sons and a long life, of progeny, and all the creature comforts in this life.

## \|\| 89.72 \|\|

*śrāddheṣu ya imaṃ bhaktyā tvasmatprītikaraṃ stavam \|*  
*paṭhiṣyati dvijāgryāṇāṃ bhuñjatāṃ purataḥ sthitaḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. A suppliant for health, longevity and the blessings of fatherhood, shall do will to propitiate us with a recitation of the aforesaid hymn.

## \|\| 89.73-74 \|\|

*stotraśravaṇasaṃprītyā sannidhāne pare kṛte \|*  
*asmābhirakṣayaṃ śrāddhaṃ tadbhaviṣyatyasaṃśayam \|\| 73 \|\|*

*yadyapyaśrotriyaṃ śrāddhaṃ yadyapyupahataṃ bhavet \|*  
*anyāyopāttavittena yadi vā kṛtamanyathā \|\| 74 \|\|*

73-74. A recitation of the hymn at the close of a Shraddha ceremony and before an assembly of Brahmanas sitting down at their meals, would bear 'immortal fruits through our intercession.

## \|\| 89.75-76 \|\|

*aśrāddhārhairupatairupahāraistathā kṛtaiḥ \|*  
*akāle 'pyatha vā deśe vidhihīnamathāpi vā \|\| 75 \|\|*

*aśraddhayā vā puruṣairdambhamāśritya yatkṛtam \|*  
*asmākaṃ tṛptaye śrāddhantathāpyetadudīraṇāt \|\| 76 \|\|*

75-76. Verily does it recitation make a Sraddha ceremony, endearing to us, even if it is not attended by Brahmanas well-versed in the Vedas (6rotriyas), or is any way vitiated as to its precedure, or is celebrated with ill-gotten gain, or is attended by men who should not be invited on such an occasion, or performed at an improper place or time, or out of a spirit of bravado.

## \|\| 89.77 \|\|

*yatraitatpaṭhyate śrāddhe stotramastatsukhāvaham \|*  
*asmākaṃ jāyate tṛptistatra dvādaśāvarṣikī \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. The satisfaction which we derive from a 6raddha ceremony, in the course of which the hymn is recited, lasts us, О child, for a continuous period of twelve years.

## \|\| 89.78 \|\|

*hemante dvādaśābdāni tṛptimetatprayacchati \|*  
*śiśire dviguṇābdāni tṛptiṃ stotramidaṃ śubham \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. A single recitation of the hymn in the forepart of winter (Hemanta) gives us a satisfaction which lasts for twelve years. A single recitation of the hymn in winier gives us a satisfaction which continues for twice as many number (twenty-four) of years.

## \|\| 89.79 \|\|

*vasante ṣoḍaśa samāstṛptaye śrāddhakarmaṇi \|*  
*grīṣme ca ṣoḍaśaivaitatpaṭhitaṃ tṛptikārakam \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. The aforesaid hymn, recited in the course of a Shraddha ceremony performed in spring, furnishes us with a sense of repletion which lasts for a continuous period of sixteen years.

## \|\| 89.80 \|\|

*vikale 'pi kṛte śrāddhe stotreṇānena sādhite \|*  
*varṣāsu tṛptirasmākamakṣayyā jāyate ruce \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. O Ruci, a Sraddha ceremony, otherwise vitiated, or made defective as to its procedure, may be remedied by a single recitation of the hymn under discussion. О Ruci, infinite is the pleasure which we derive from a recitation of the hymn during the rainy season.

## \|\| 89.81 \|\|

*śaratkāle 'pi paṭhitaṃ śrāddhakāle prayacchati \|*  
*asmākametatpuruṣaistṛptiṃ pañcadaśābdikīm \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. The satisfaction which we derive from a recitation of the hymn in autumn, lasts us for fifteen years.

## \|\| 89.82 \|\|

*yasmin gehe ca likhitametattiṣṭhati nityadā \|*  
*sannidhānaṃ kṛte śrāddhe tatrāsmākaṃ bhaviṣyati \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. We grace a Sraddha ceremony with our presence in the event of its being performed in a room in which the hymn stands transcribed.

## \|\| 89.83 \|\|

*tasmādetattvayā śrāddhe viprāṇāṃ bhuñjatāṃ puraḥ \|*  
*śrāvaṇīyaṃ mahābhāga asmākaṃ puṣṭikārakam \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. Therefore, О you of mighty heritage, you shall recite the hymn before an assembly of Brahmanas invited on the occasion of a 6raddha ceremony and seated at their meals, whereby you would ensure infinite and eternal satisfaction to us, your departed Manes."

## Chapter 90

## \|\| 90.1-2 \|\|

*mākraṇḍeya uvāca \|*  
*tatastasmānnadīmadhyātsamuttasthau manoramā \|*  
*pramlaucā nāma tanvaṅgī tatsamīpe varāpsarāḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*sā covāca mahātmānaṃ ruciṃ sumadhurākṣarakam \|*  
*prasādayāmāsa bhūyaḥ pramlocā ca varāpsarāḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

1-2. Markandeya said: — The tranquil bosom of that lonely pool was stirred for a moment, and, behold, there appeared to Ruci, Pramloca, the selender-waisted water nymph of celestial beauty.

## \|\| 90.3 \|\|

*atīvarūpiṇī kanyā matprasādvarāṅganā \|*  
*jātā varuṇaputreṇa puṣkareṇa mahātmanā \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. The nymph solaced him with many a sweet and encouraging words and addressed him as follows: — Puskara, the son of Varuna, the Ocean God, has begot on me a handsome daughter of uncommon beauty.

## \|\| 90.4 \|\|

*tāṃ gṛhāṇa mayā dattāṃ bhāryārthe varavarṇinīm \|*  
*manurmahāmatistasyāṃ samutpatsyati te sutaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Do you take her as thy lawful bride at my hands, О sage. By her you shall have a son of rare talents who would be the future law-giver of the universe.

## \|\| 90.5-6 \|\|

*mārkaṇḍeya uvāca \|*  
*tatheti tena sāpyuktā tasmāttoyādvapuṣmatīm \|*  
*uddadhāra tataḥ kanyāṃ māninīṃ nāma nāmataḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*nadyāśca puline tasminsa munirmunisattamāḥ \|*  
*jagrāha pāṇiṃ vidhivatsamānīya mahāmuniḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. Markandeya said: — Then Ruci, having consented to her proposal, drew that beautiful virgin out of the water of that lonely pool and duly married her on its geen-clad bank.

## \|\| 90.7 \|\|

*tasyāṃ tasya suto jajñe mahāvīryo mahādyutiḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. By her he had a son, named Roucya after his honoured self, who had been a Manu (lawgiver) of the universe, as narrated before.

## Chapter 91

## \|\| 91.1-2 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*svāyambhuvādyā munayo hariṃ dhyāyanti karmaṇā \|*  
*vratācārārcanādhyānastutijapyaparāyaṇāḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*dehendriyamanobuddhiprāṇāhaṅkāravarjitam \|*  
*ākaśena vihīnaṃ vai tejasā parivarjitam \|\| 2 \|\|*

1-2. Suta said: — The Manus, such as Svayam- bhuvas, etc., observe the rules of penance, worship, contemplation prayer, etc., recite the Mantras sacred to the God Hari, and meditate upon His eternal Self, which is shorn of body senses, mind, intellect, vitality and the sense of egoism. The sky does not constitute His Self, nor does heat (light) enter into its composition.

## \|\| 91.3 \|\|

*udakena vihīnaṃ vai taddharmaparivarjitam \|*  
*pṛthivīrahitaṃ caiva sarvabhatavivarjitam \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Water does not enter into the composition of His Supreme Self, nor do the attributes which characterise. that material element, affect that eternal entity. Similarly, it is above all the fundamental principles of the earth matter, and it necessarily beyond the operative zone of virtues which specifically belong to that essential substance.

## \|\| 91.4 \|\|

*bhūtādhyakṣaṃ tathā baddhaniyantāraṃ prabhuṃ vibhum \|*  
*caitanyarūpatārūpaṃ sarvādhyakṣaṃ nirañjanam \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Controller of all beings and becomings, he is the ever enlightened, ever wakeful One, the director and lord of all, the fmal receptacle of all force and energy, shorn of all illusion, and identical with ure consciousness.

## \|\| 91.5 \|\|

*muktasaṅgaṃ maheśānaṃ sarvadevaprapūjitam \|*  
*tejorūpamasattvaṃ ca tapasā parivarjitam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. He is One, and without a second or companion, the supreme God, represented by light though void of fundamental quality of illumination (Sattva) and is hence beyond the necessity of practising any austerity.

## \|\| 91.6 \|\|

*rahitaṃ rajasā nityaṃ vyatiriktaṃ guṇaistribhiḥ \|*  
*sarvarūpavihīnaṃ vai kartṛtvādivivarjitam \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. He is shorn of the quality of Rajas, and the three fundamental qualities of Sattva, Rajas and Tamas, do not affect his Supreme Self. He has no shape, is devoid of all action and desire, and is pure and incapable of sin and evil.

## \|\| 91.7 \|\|

*vāsanārahitaṃ śuddhaṃ sarvadoṣavivarjitam \|*  
*pipāsāvarjitaṃ tattaccho kamohavivarjitam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Hankerings cannot assail him, nor griefs and ignorance can disturb the infinite serenity of His eternal Self.

## \|\| 91.8 \|\|

*jarāmaraṇahīnaṃ vai kūṭasthaṃ mohavarjitam \|*  
*utpattirahitaṃ caiva pralayena vivarjitam \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. He knows no old age, death or decay. With out end or origin, he lies inherent in all, the eternal witness of the process of phenomenal evolution and from whose vision nothing lies hidden or veiled and which nescience itself can not clouden.

## \|\| 91.9 \|\|

*satyaṃ sarvācārahīnaṃ niṣkalaṃ parameśvaram \|*  
*jāgratsvapnasuṣuptyādivarjitaṃ nāmavarjitam \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. He is the perfect and absolute truth, the Supreme God, one and indivisible, beyond all rules of ethics, nameless, and knows no sleep, nor dream, nor wakening.

## \|\| 91.10 \|\|

*adhyakṣaṃ jāgradādīnāṃ śāntarūpaṃ sureśvaram \|*  
*jāgradādisthitaṃ nityaṃ kāryakāraṇavarjitam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. He is the only real factor in individual consciousness that makes the sattes of wakening, etc., possible. He is the personified peace, the lord of the gods and the celestials. He is real, and, as such, underlies the states of wakening, etc., void of the necessary categories of cause and effect.

## \|\| 91.11 \|\|

*sarvadṛṣṭaṃ tathā mūrtaṃ sūkṣmaṃ sūkṣmataraṃ param \|*  
*jñānadṛk śrotravijñānaṃ paramānandarūpakam \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. He is imaged in the phenomenal universe, and is accordingly seen by all. He is the most invisible of all invisible entities, and, as such, can be only perceived by means of pure knowledge, or through scriptural learning.

## \|\| 91.12 \|\|

*viśvena rahitaṃ tadvattaijasena vivarjitam \|*  
*prājñena rahitañcaiva turīyaṃ paramākṣaram \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. He is the highest felicity, beyond all material process of creation or construction. He is shorn of intellect, and is beyound the process of intellection, and is identical with the fourth stage of pure consciousness (Turlya).

## \|\| 91.13 \|\|

*sarvagoptṛ sarvahantṛ sarvabhūtātmarūpi ca \|*  
*buddhidharmavihīnaṃ vai nirādhāraṃ śivaṃ harim \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. He is the protector and destroyer of all. Beyond all virtues and attributes, he is the soul of all created beings. Without any receptacle to hold him in, he directs the universe in the path of light and benediction; He is Siva (the blissful one, the highest bliss). He is Hari, the remover of all sin and misery.

## \|\| 91.14 \|\|

*vikriyārahitaṃ caiva vedāntairvedyameva ca \|*  
*vedarūpaṃ paraṃ bhūtamindriyebhyaḥ paraṃ śubham \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. He suffers no change, nor knows any modification. He is known only through the teachings of the Vedanta philosophy. He is personified knowledge, the real sub.stantial substratum whose attributes and senses inform us of.

## \|\| 91.15-16 \|\|

*śabdena varjitañcaiva rasena ca vivarjitam \|*  
*sparśena rahitaṃ devaṃ rūpamātravivarjitam \|\| 15 \|\|*

*rūpeṇa rahitaṃ ñcaiva gandhena parivarjitam \|*  
*anādi brahma randhrāntamahaṃ brahmāsmi kevalam \|\| 16 \|\|*

15-16. He is without the faculties of hearing, taste, touch, vision and smelling. He is without any origin, and lies inherent in the topmost cavity of the human brain, dawning upon the individual consciousness only to establish its identity with his eternal Self, a fact which the human mind interprets in its experience of "I am He."

## \|\| 91.17 \|\|

*evaṃ jñātvā mahādevadhyānaṃ kuryājjitendriyaḥ \|*  
*dhyānaṃ yaḥ kurute hyevaṃ sa bhavedbahma mānavaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. О thou, the supreme god, having realised this experience in mind, and having cast his whole self in the thought-mould of "I am He" a man should meditate upon the self of the supreme Brahman,

## \|\| 91.18 \|\|

*iti dhyānaṃ samākhyātamaśvirasya mayā tava \|*  
*adhunā kathayāmyanyatkintadbrūhi vṛṣadhvaja \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. He, who does this, is no other than the supreme One. I have disclosed to you the mode of contemplating the self of the supreme God. Now tell me, Rudra, whatever else you want me to speek about.

## Chapter 92

## \|\| 92.1 \|\|

*rudrauvāca \|*  
*viṣṇordhyānaṃ punarbrūhi śaṅkhacakragadādhara \|*  
*yena vijñātamātreṇa kṛtakṛtyo bhavennaraḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Rudra said: — "Relate to me, О thou, the wielder of lotus, mace, discus! and conch shell, the mode of meditating upon the divine self of Visnu, a knowledge whereof leads to salvation.

## \|\| 92.2-3 \|\|

*hariruvāca \|*  
*pravakṣyāmi harerdhyānaṃ māyātantravimardakam \|*  
*mūrtāmūrtādibhedena taddhyānaṃ dvividhaṃ hara \|\| 2 \|\|*

*amūrtaṃ rudra kathitaṃ hanta mūtta bravīmyaham \|*  
*sūryakoṭipratīkāśo jiṣṇurbhājiṣṇurekataḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

2-3. Said the god Hari: — Yes, I shall describe to you the mode of contemplating the divine self of Visnu, which is of tWo sorts, according as the embodied or disembodied self of the god is meditated upon. О Rudra, in the preceding chapter I have discoursed on the latter mode, now hear me describe the process of contemplating the imaged or the embodies self of that deity. A seeker of salvation should meditate upon the god as burning with the combined effulgence of a million of suns, and moving about in the infinite space with the dignity of unquestioned prowess and unobstructed energy.

## \|\| 92.4-5 \|\|

*kundagokṣīradhavalo harirdhyeyo mumukṣubhiḥ \|*  
*viśālena susaumyena śaṅkhena ca samanvitaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*sahasrādityatulyena jvālāmālograrūpiṇā \|*  
*cakreṇa cānvitaḥ śānto gadāhastaḥ śubhānanaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. The complexion of his divine body should be contemplated to be white as the hue of a Kunda flower. In the alter native, the god should be contemplated as burning with the combined effulgence of a thousand suns, and dreadful to look at through an excess of light, and as wielding a large and beautiful conch shell, a discus, a lotus flower, and a mace in his four hands, his face beaming with the calmness of divine peace.

## \|\| 92.6 \|\|

*kirīṭena mahārheṇa ratnaprajvalitena ca \|*  
*sāyudhaḥ sarvago devaḥ saroruhadharastathā \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. The crown or the head-gear of the god, should be contemplated as shining with the scintillations of a myriad of gems, and his attendants should be likewise contemplated as waiting upon his gracious divinity.

## \|\| 92.7 \|\|

*vanamālādharaḥ śubhraḥ samāṃso hemabhūṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*suvastraḥ śuddhadehaśca sukarṇaḥ padmasaṃsthitaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. The mental picture, in the present instance, would not be complete without decorating the central figure with a garland of full-blown wild flowers.

## \|\| 92.8 \|\|

*hiraṇmayaśarīraśca cāruhārī śubhāṅgadaḥ \|*  
*keyūreṇa samāyukto vanamālāsamanvitaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. The image should be placed mentally on a full-blown, lotus flower, decked with bracelets, necklace, etc., of celestial manufacture.

## \|\| 92.9 \|\|

*śrīvatsakaustubhayuto lakṣmīvandyekṣaṇānvitaḥ \|*  
*amimādiguṇairyuktaḥ sṛṣṭisaṃhārakārakaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The diamond Koustubha should be imagined as dangling over the region of his breast, grown over with the peculiar ringlets of hair, known as the Shrivatsam.

## \|\| 92.10 \|\|

*munidhyeyo 'suradhyeyo devadhyeyo 'tisundaraḥ \|*  
*brahmādistambaparyantabhūtajātahṛdisthitaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. The imaginary person of this creator and destroyer of the universe, whom the gods and ihe holy sages contemplate in their celestial and sylvan retreats, should be contemplated as composed of the beatific attributes of Anima, etc., the different grades of conscious animalism, from the minutest animalculum to the mightiest Brahma, as having had their seats in the cardiac region of the image.

## \|\| 92.11 \|\|

*sanātano 'vyayo medhyaḥ sarvānugrahakṛtprabhuḥ \|*  
*nārāyaṇo mahādevaḥ sphuranmakarakuṇḍalaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Thus the mental picture of the god should be completed, and the votary should worship it with the knowledge that the deity imaged in his heart, is but the reflection of that primal light, the god of the gods, the absolute purity, the lord of all, and the only being equally compassionate towards all created life.

## \|\| 92.12 \|\|

*santāpanāśano 'bhyarcyo maṅgalyo duṣṭanāśanaḥ \|*  
*sarvātmā sarvarūpaśca sarvago grahanāśanaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. He is the ever blissful lord, the regenator of the the human soul, and the destroyer of the threefold misery. He punishes the wicked, exhorts the good in the path of lightousness, is the soul of all, allpervading, and the appeaser of all malignant stars.

## \|\| 92.13 \|\|

*cārvaṅgulīyasaṃyuktaḥ sudīptanakha eva ca \|*  
*śaraṇyaḥ lasukhakārī ca saumyarūpo maheśvaraḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. The beautiful circles of light which serve to relieve the darkness of the night, are his finger- rings. He is the primary source of all forms, and all shapes lie inherent in his disembodied spirit. He is the supreme god, the perfect beauty, the grand and final resort or all, the fountainhead from which equal felicity flows to all.

## \|\| 92.14-15 \|\|

*sarvālaṅkārasaṃyuktaścārucandanacarcitaḥ \|*  
*sarvadevasamāyuktaḥ sarvadevapriyaṅkaraḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*sarvalokahitaiṣī ca sarveśaḥ sarvabhāvanaḥ \|*  
*ādityamaṇḍale saṃstho agnistho vārisaṃsthitaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

14-15. His body is decked with all sorts of ornaments, and is smeared with sandalpaste. The gods wait upon him in the spirit of loving servitude, and he does what the gods approve of. He does what is beneficial to them. He is Vasudeva, the lord of the universe. He looks after the universe. He looks after the good of all beings. He it is that shines in the sun. He it is that forms what is so wholesome in water. He is the only subject contemplated by all, the supreme or dainer in the universe, the supreme Visnu, whom the seekers of salvation meditate upon.

## \|\| 92.16-17 \|\|

*vāsudevo jagaddhātā dhyeyo viṣṇurmumukṣubhiḥ \|*  
*vāsudevo 'hamasmīti ātmā dhyeyo harihariḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*dhyāyantyevaṃ ca ye viṣṇuṃ te yānti paramāṃ gatim \|*  
*yājñavalkyaḥ purā hyevaṃ dhyātvā viṣṇuṃ sureśvaram \|\| 17 \|\|*

16-17. "I am Vasudeva, I am He, the supreme soul," should be the form of thought in all who meditate upon the self of Visnu. Those who contemplate him in this way, acquire the most exalted station after death. For having thus meditated upon the self of Visnu, the holy Yajnavalkya, was. honoured with the office of laying down the rules of conduct of his age.

## \|\| 92.18-19 \|\|

*dharmopadeśakartṛtvaṃ saṃprāpyāgātparaṃ padam \|*  
*tasmāttvamapi deveśa ! viṣṇuṃ cintaya śaṅkara ! \|\| 18 \|\|*

*viṣṇudhyānaṃ paṭhedyastu prāpnoti paramāṃ gatim \|\| 19 \|\|*

18-19. Therefore, О Sankara, О you, the lord of the celestials, always meditate upon the Self of Visnu. Even he, who reads the present chapter, acquires the most elevated spiritual existence after death.

## Chapter 93

## \|\| 93.1 \|\|

*maheśvara uvāca \|*  
*yājñavalkyena yatpūrvaṃ dharmaṃ proktaṃ kayaṃ hare ! \|*  
*tanme kāthaya keśighna ! yathā tattvena mādhava ! \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Mahesvara said: — Tell me, О Hari, О Madhava, О you who have destroyed the demon KesI, what is it that led tbe holy Yajnavalkya, to lay down the rules of conduct in days of yore?

## \|\| 93.2 \|\|

*hariruvāca \|*  
*yājñavalkyaṃ namaskṛtya mithilāyāṃ samāsthitam \|*  
*apṛcchannṝṣayo gatvā varṇadharmādyaśeṣataḥ \|*  
*tebhyaḥ sa kathayāmāsa viṣṇuṃ dhyātvā jitendriyaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Said The God Hari: — Once on a time, the holy sages visited, in a body, the venerable Yajnavalkya in his hermitage at Mithila; and having duly made obeisance to him, they asked him about the rules of conduct to be observed by members of the different orders of society. Whereupon the self controlled Yajanavalkya, meditating upon the self of Visnu, replied as follows.

## \|\| 93.3-6 \|\|

*yājñavalkya uvāca \|*  
*yasmindeśe mṛgaḥ kṛṣṇastasmindharmānnibodhata \|*  
*purāṇanyāyamīmāṃsādharmaśāstrāṅgamiśritāḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*vedāḥ sthānāni vidyānāṃ dharmasya ca caturdaśa \|*  
*vaktāro dharmaśāstrāṇāṃ manurviṣṇuryamo 'ṅgirāḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*vasiṣṭhadakṣasaṃvartaśātātapaparāśarāḥ \|*  
*āpastambośanovyāsāḥ kātyāyanabṛhaspatī \|\| 5 \|\|*

*gautamaḥ śaṅkhalikhito hārīto 'trirahaṃ tathā \|*  
*ete viṣṇuṃ samārādhya jātā dharmopadeśakāḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

3-6. Yajanavalkya said: — Pious is.the country where herds of black deer are found to roam about. Knowledge is in the Vedas, in the Puranas, in the different schools of philosophy such as the Nyaya, the Mlmansa, etc., in the Dharma 3asttas (Ethics and Social Economy) and in the books of money-making and temporal sciences: Manu, Visnu, Yama, Angira, Vasistha Daksa Samvarta, 3atatapa, Parasara, Apastamba, Usana, Vyasa, Katyayana, Brhaspati, Goutama, Shankha, Likhita Harlta, and Atri, are the names of the fourteen holy sages, who, having worshipped the god Visnu, were enabled to become the ethic dictators and law-givers (Dharma-Sutrakaras) of the ages in which they lived.

## \|\| 93.7 \|\|

*deśakāla upāyena dravyaṃ śraddhāsamanvitam \|*  
*pātre pradīyate yattatsakalaṃ dharmalakṣaṇam \|\| 7 \|\|*
