## \|\| 138.8 \|\|

*viviṃśācca khanīnetro vibhūtistatsutaḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*karandhamo vibhūtestu tato jāto 'pyavikṣitaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Vimsa and another son named Khaninetra, and Khaninetra had a son named Vibhuti. Vibhuti begat Karandhama, and Karandhama begat Abiksita.

## \|\| 138.9-10 \|\|

*marutto 'vikṣitasyāpi nariṣyantastataḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*nariṣyantāttamo jātastatobhūdrājavardhanaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*rājavardhātsudhṛtiśca naro 'bhūtsudhṛteḥ sutaḥ \|*  
*narācca kevalaḥ putraḥ kevalāddhundhumānapi \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. Abiksita had a son named Marutta, and Marutta was the father of Narisyanta. Tamas begat Rajvardhana, Rajvardhana begat Sudhrati, and Sudhrti begat Nara. Nara had a son named Kavela who was the father of Dhundhumana.

## \|\| 138.11 \|\|

*dhundhumato vegavāṃśca budho vegavataḥ sutaḥ \|*  
*tṛṇabindurbudhājjātaḥ kānyā cailavilā tathā \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Dhundumana begat Vegavan, who was the father of Budha. Afterwards Budha begat a son named Trnavindu and a daughter named Ailavila.

## \|\| 138.12 \|\|

*viśālaṃ janayāmāsa tṛṇabindostvalambusā \|*  
*viśālāddhemacandro 'bhūddhema candrācca candrakaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. The said Trnavindu begat on Alamvusa a son named Visala. Visala had a son named Hemcandra who in his turn begat Candra.

## \|\| 138.13 \|\|

*dhūmrāśvaścaiva candrāttu dhūmrāśvātsṛñjayastathā \|*  
*sañjayātsahadevo 'bhūtkṛśāśvastatsuto 'bhavat \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Candra begat Dhaumrasva who begat Srnjaya; and Srnjaya had a son named Sahadeva who was the father of Krsasva.

## \|\| 138.14 \|\|

*kṛśāśvātsomadattastutato 'bhūjjanamejayaḥ \|*  
*tatputraśca sumantiśca ete vaiśālakā nṛpāḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. The name of the son of Krsasva was Somadatta who begat Janamejaya. Janamejaya was the father of Sumantri. All these princes ruled in the city of Visala.

## \|\| 138.15 \|\|

*śaryātestu sukanyābūtsā bhāryā cyavanasya tu \|*  
*ananto nāma śāryate ranantādrevato 'bhavat \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Saryyati had a daughter who was married to the holy Cyavana. Saryyati had a son named Ananta, and Ananta was the father of Devaka.

## \|\| 138.16 \|\|

*raivato revatasyāpi raivatādrevatī sutā \|*  
*dhṛṣṭasya dhārṣṭar (ta) kaṃ kṣetraṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ (śyakaṃ) tadvabhūva ha \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Afterwards Revata had son who was called Raivataka and a daughter named Revati. The son begat by Dhr$ta, the son so Manu, was called Dharstaki who though born a Ksatriya, took to the life of a VaiSya.

## \|\| 138.17-18 \|\|

*nābhāgaputro neṣṭho hyambarīṣo 'pi tatsutaḥ \|*  
*ambarīṣādvirūpo 'bhūtpṛṣadaśvo virūpataḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*rathīnaraśca tatputro vāsudevaparāyaṇaḥ \|*  
*ikṣvākostu trayaḥ putrāḥ vikukṣinimidaṇḍakāḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

17-18. Ambarlsa was the son of Nabhaga, a son of Manu. Ambarlsa begat Virupa, Virupa begat Prsadasva, Prsadasva begat Rathlnara, who was firmly devoted to Vasudeva. Of the three sons of Iksvaku, the first was named VikuksI, the second was called NimI; and the third Dandaka.

## \|\| 138.19 \|\|

*ikṣvākujo vikukṣistu śaśādaḥ śaśabhakṣaṇāt \|*  
*purañjayaḥ śaśādācca kakutsthākhyo 'bhavatsutaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. VikuksI the son of Iksvaku ate the hare kept for sacrificial purposes and hence he was called the here-eater (Sasada). This Masada had a son named Puranjaya who, begat Kakutstha.

## \|\| 138.20 \|\|

*anenāstu kakutsathācca pṛthuḥ putrastvanenasaḥ \|*  
*viśvarātaḥ pṛthoḥ putra ārdre 'bhūdviśvarātataḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Kakutstha had a son named Anena, and the son of Anena was named Prthu. Prthu had a son maned Visvarata who was the father of Ardra.

## \|\| 138.21-22 \|\|

*yuvanāśvo 'bhavaccārdrācchāvasto yuvanāśvataḥ \|*  
*bṛhadaśvastuśāvastāttatputraḥ kuvalāśvakaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*dhundhumāro hi vikyāto dṛḍhaśvaścatato 'bhavat \|*  
*candrāśvaḥ kapilāśvaśca haryaśvaśca dṛḍhaśvataḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

21-22. Ardra begat Yuvanasva who begat 6rovanta. Sravanta had son named Vrhadasva, who was the father of Kuvalyasa va, who had a son called DrdaSva, and who was better known by the epithet of Dhundumara. This Drdhi^va had three sons, viz., Candrasva Kapilagva and Haryasva.

## \|\| 138.23 \|\|

*haryaśvācca nikumbo 'bhūddhitāśvaśca nikumbhataḥ \|*  
*pūjāśvaśca hitāśvācca tatsato yuvanāśvakaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Haryasva begat Nikumbha. Nikumbha begat Hitasva who was the father of Piljasva. POjasva had a a son named Yuvanasva.

## \|\| 138.24 \|\|

*yuvanāśvācca māndhātā bindumatyāstato 'bhavat \|*  
*mucukundo 'mbarīṣaśca purukutsastrayaḥ sutāḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. The son of Yuvanasva was called Mandhata who had a son named Bindu Matya. Vindu Matya had three sons named Mucukunda, Ambarlsa and Purukutsa.

## \|\| 138.25 \|\|

*pañcāśatkanyakāścaiva bhāryāstāḥ saubharermuneḥ \|*  
*yuvanāśvo 'mbarīṣācca harito yuvanāśvataḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. The aforesaid Bindu Mahya had fifty daughters who become the wives of the holy sage Sauvarl. Ambarlsa begat Yuvanasva who begat Hanta.

## \|\| 138.26 \|\|

*purukutsānnarmadāyāṃ trasadasyurabūtsutaḥ \|*  
*anaraṇyastato jāto haryaśvo 'pyanaraṇyataḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. The son begotten on Narmada by Purukutsa was called Trasadasyu. Anaranya was the son to Trasadasyu, and the son of Anaranya was called Haryyasva.

## \|\| 138.27 \|\|

*tatputro 'bhūdvasumanāstridhanvā tasya cātmajaḥ \|*  
*trayyāruṇastasya putrastasta satyarataḥ sutaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Vasumanah was the son of Haryyasva and Tridhanva; was the son of Vasumana. Tridhanva had a son named Trayaruna who was the father of Satyarata.

## \|\| 138.28 \|\|

*yastriśaṅkuḥ samākhyāto hariścandro 'bhavattataḥ \|*  
*hariścandrādrohitāśvo harito rohitāśvataḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. This Satyarata become famous by the name to Trisanku the son of Trisanku was named Haricandra, who was the father of Rohitasva. Harita was the son of Rohitasva.

## \|\| 138.29 \|\|

*haritasya sutaścañcuścañcośca vijayaḥ sutaḥ \|*  
*vijayādruruko jajñe rurukāttu vṛkaḥ sutaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. And Cancu was the son of Harita. Caficu begat Vijaya, and Vijaya begat Ruruk, and Ruruk begat Vrka.

## \|\| 138.30-31 \|\|

*vṛkādbāhurnṛpo 'bhūcca bāhostu sagaraḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*ṣaṣṭiḥ putra sahasrāṇi sumatyāṃ sagarāddhara \|\| 30 \|\|*

*keśinyāmeka evāsāvasamañjasasaṃjñakaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

30-31. Bahu was the-son of Vrka and he become a king. Sagara was the son of Prthu who had sixty thousand sons by his wife Sumati, and a son named Asamanjasa by his wife Kesini.

## \|\| 138.32 \|\|

*tasyāṃśumānsuto vidvāndilīpastatsuto 'bhavat \|*  
*bhagīratho dilīpācca yo gaṅgāmānayadbhuvam \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Amsumana was the son of Asamanjasa and Dillpa was the son of Amsumana. Bhagiratha was the son of Dillpa, and he brought down the Ganges on earth.

## \|\| 138.33 \|\|

*śruto bhagīrathasuto nābhagaśca śrutātkila \|*  
*nābhāgādambarīṣo 'bhūtsindudvīpo 'mbarīṣataḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. $ruta was the son of Bhagiratha, and the son of gruta was named Nabhaga. Nabhaga had a son named Ambarisa who was the father of Sindhudvipa.

## \|\| 138.34 \|\|

*sindudvīpasyāyutāyurṛtuparṇastadātmajaḥ \|*  
*ṛtuṣarṇātsarvakāmaḥ sudāso 'bhūttadātmajaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Ayutayu was the son of Sindhudvipa, and the son of Ayutayu was Rtuparna. Sarvakama was the son of Rtuparna, and Sudasa was the the son of Sarvakama.

## \|\| 138.35 \|\|

*sudāsasya ca saudāso nāmnā mitrasahaḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*kalmāṣa pādasaṃjñaśca damayantyāṃ tadātmajaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. The son of Sudasa become famous by the name of Mitrasaha. Sudasa begat a son on his wife Damayanta who was called Kalmaspada.

## \|\| 138.36 \|\|

*aśvakākhyo 'bhavatputro hyaśvakānmūla(nmṛccha) ko 'bhavat \|*  
*tato daśaratho rājā tasya cailavilaḥ sutaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Kalmasapada begat Asvaka, and Asvaka begat МШака, and Mulaka begat Dasaratha who was the father of Ailavila.

## \|\| 138.37 \|\|

*tasya viśvasahaḥ putraḥ khaṭvāṅgaśca tadātmajaḥ \|*  
*khaṭvāṅgaddīrghabāhuśca dīrghabāhorhyajaḥ sutaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. The son of Ailavila was named Vipasaha, who was the father of Khatvanga. Khatvanga had a son named Dirghabahu who was the father of Aja.

## \|\| 138.38 \|\|

*tasya puttro daśarathaścatvārastatsutāḥ smṛtāḥ \|*  
*rāmalakṣmaṇaśatrughnabharatāśca mahābalāḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. The son of Aja was Dasaratha who had four sons, viz., Rama, Bharata, Laksmana and Shatrughna. All of them become famous in history for prowess and glorious achievements.

## \|\| 138.39-40 \|\|

*rāmātkuśalavau jātau bharatāttārkṣapuṣkarau \|*  
*citrāṅgadaścandraketurlakṣmaṇātsaṃbabhūvatuḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

*subāhuśūrasenau ca śatrughnātsaṃbabhūvatuḥ \|*  
*kuśasya cātithiḥ putro niṣadho hyatitheḥ sutaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

39-40. Kusa and Lava were the sons of Rama. Bharata's sons were named Tarksa and Puskara. Citrangada and Candraketu were the sons of Laksmana, while the sons of Shatrughna were named Subahu and Shurasena. Kuga had a son named Atithi who was the father of Nisada.

## \|\| 138.41 \|\|

*niṣadhasya nalaḥ putro nalasya ca nabhāḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*nabhasaḥ puṇḍarīkastukṣemadhanvā tadātmajaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Nala was the son of Nisada, and Nabhasa was the son of Nala. Pundarika was the son of Nabhaga, and Ksemdhanva was the son of Pundarika.

## \|\| 138.42-44 \|\|

*devānīkastasya putro devānīkādahīnakaḥ \|*  
*ahīnakādrururyajñe pāriyātro ruroḥ sutaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

*pāriyātrāddalo yajñe dala putraśchalaḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*chalādukthastato hyukthādvajranābhastato gaṇaḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

*uṣitāśvo gaṇājjajñe tato viśvasaho 'bhavat \|*  
*hiraṇyanābhastatputrastatputraḥ puṣpakaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

42-44. Devanika was the son of Ksemadhanva, and Ahlnaka was the son of Devanika. Ahinaka begat Ruru, and Ruru begat Paripatra begat Dala, and Dala begat Chala. Vuktha was the son of Chala and Vajranabha was the son of Hyuktha. The sor of Vajrandbha was Gana who was the father of Usitasva who was the father of Visvasaha. Hiranyanabha was the son of Visvasaha, and Puspaka was the son of Hiranyanabha.

## \|\| 138.45 \|\|

*dhruvasandhirabhūtpuṣpāddhruvasandheḥ sudarśanaḥ \|*  
*sudarśanādagnivarṇaḥ padmavaṇo 'gnivarṇataḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. The son of Paspaka was Dhruvasandhi who was to father of Sudarsana. Sudarsana, ana begat Agnivama who was the father of Padmavama.

## \|\| 138.46 \|\|

*śīghrastu padmavarṇāttu śīghrātputro marustvabhūt \|*  
*maroḥ prasuśrutaḥ putrastasya codāvasuḥ sutaḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Padmavama begat 6ighra, and 6lghra begat Maru, and Mam begat Pragmta who was the father of Udavasu,

## \|\| 138.47 \|\|

*udāvasornandivardhanaḥ suketurnandivardhanāt \|*  
*suketordevarāto 'bhūdvṛhadukthastataḥ sutaḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Nandivardhana was the son of Udavasu. Suketu was the son of Nandivardhana. Suketu had a son named Devarata who was the father of Brhaduktha.

## \|\| 138.48 \|\|

*bṛhadukthānmahāvīryaḥ sudhṛtistasya cātmajaḥ \|*  
*sudhṛterdhṛṣṭaketuśca haryaśvo dhṛṣṭaketutaḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Brhaduktha had a son named Mahavirya who was the father of Sudhfti. The son of Sudhrti was Dhrstaketu who was the father of Haryyasva.

## \|\| 138.49 \|\|

*haryaśvāttu marurjāto maroḥ pratīndhako 'bhavat \|*  
*pratīndhakātkṛtiratho devamīḍhastadātmajaḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. The son of Haryyasva was Maru who was the father of Pratindhaka. Pratindhaka begat Krtiratha, and Krtiratha begat Devamldha.

## \|\| 138.50-51 \|\|

*vibudho devamīḍhāttu vibudhāttu mahādhṛtiḥ \|*  
*mahādhṛteḥ kīrtirāto mahāromā tadātmajaḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

*mahāromṇaḥ svarṇaromā hrasvaromā tadātmajaḥ \|*  
*sīradhvajo hrasvaromṇaḥ tasya sītābhavatsutā \|\| 51 \|\|*

50-51. Vibudha was son of Devatidha. The son of Vibudha was Mahadhrti who was the father of Kirtirata. The son of Kirtirata was Manoroma who was the father of Svarnaroma, whose son was Hrasvaroma, whose son was SIradhvaja who had a daughter named Sita.

## \|\| 138.52 \|\|

*bhrātā kuśadhvajastasya sīradhvajāttu bhānumān \|*  
*śatadyumno bhānumataḥ śatadyumnācchuciḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. Kusadhvaja was the brother of SIradhvaja who had a son named Bhanuman. fsatadyumna was the son of Bhanuman and guci was the son of Satadyumna.

## \|\| 138.53 \|\|

*ūrjanāmā śuceḥ putraḥ sanadvājastadātmajaḥ \|*  
*sanadvājātkulirjāto 'nañjanastu kuleḥ sutaḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Shuci begat Urja. Urja begat Sanadhvaja whose son was Kuli.

## \|\| 138.54-55 \|\|

*anañjanācca kulajittasyāpi cādhinemikaḥ \|*  
*śrutāyustasya putro 'bhūtsupārśvaśca tadātmajaḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

*supārśvātsṛṃjayo jātaḥ kṣemāriḥ sṛjayātsamṛtaḥ \|*  
*kṣemāri tastvanenāśca tasya rāmarathaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

54-55. The son of Kuli was Ananjana who was the father of Kulajit. The son of Kulajit was AdhinemI who was the father of Shrutayu. The son of Srutayu was Suparsva who was the father of Ksemari. Ksemari begat Anena who was the father of Ramaratha.

## \|\| 138.56-57 \|\|

*satyaratho rāmarathāttasmādupaguruḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*upagurorupaguptaḥ svāgataścopaguptataḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

*svanaraḥ svāgatājjajñe suvarcāstasya cātmajaḥ \|*  
*suvarcasaḥ supārśvastu suśrutaśca supārśvataḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

56-57. Ramaratha begat Satyaratha; and Satyaratha, Upaguru Upaguru begat Upagupta whose son was Svagata. Svagata had a son named Svanara, who begat Suvarca, who begat Suparsva, who begat Susruta.

## \|\| 138.58 \|\|

*jayastu suśrutājjajñe jayāttu vijayo 'bhavat \|*  
*vijayasya ṛtaḥ putraḥ ṛtasya sunayaḥ sutaḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. The son of Susruta was Java who was the father of Vijaya. Vijaya begat Rta, and Rta begat Sunaya.

## \|\| 138.59-60 \|\|

*sunayādvītahavyastu vītahavyāddhatiḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*bahulāśvo dhṛteḥ putro bahulāśvātkṛtiḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

*janakasya dvaye vaṃśe ukto yogasamāśrayaḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

59-60. And Sunaya begat Vitahavya, who was the father of Dhrti. The son of Dhrti was Bahulasva who was the father of Krti. The different races sprang from Janaka who were all addicted to Yoga.

## Chapter 139

## \|\| 139.1 \|\|

*hariruvāca \|*  
*sūryasya kathito vaṃśaḥ somavaṃśaṃ śṛṇuṣva me \|*  
*nārāyaṇasuto brahmā brahmaṇo 'treḥ samudbhavaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Hari said: — I have finished describing the solar race, now hear me narrate the genealogy of princes who were the descendants of the Moon-God. Brahma, the son of Narayana created the holy Atri.

## \|\| 139.2 \|\|

*atreḥ somastasya bhāryā tārā suraguroḥ priyā \|*  
*somāttarā budhaṃ jajñe budhaputraḥ purūravāḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. From Atri sprang the Moon God who became the consort of the beautiful Tara, the favourite wife of Brhaspati, the preceptor of the celestials. The Moon-God begat on the person of his beloved Tara a son named Budha, who in his turn begat Pururava.

## \|\| 139.3 \|\|

*budhaputrādathorvaśyāṃ ṣaṭ putrāstu śrutātmakaḥ \|*  
*viśvāvasuḥ śatāyuśca āyurdhomānamāvasuḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. The son of Budha begat on the nymph UrvasT six sons who were named 6rutatmaka, Visvavasu, 6atayu, Ayu, Dhiman, and / Amavasu.

## \|\| 139.4 \|\|

*amāvasorbhomanāmā bhīmaputraśca kāñcanaḥ \|*  
*kāñcanasya suhotro 'bhūjjahruścābhūtsuhotrataḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Bhima was the son of Amavasu, Kancana was the son of Bhima, Kancana's son was Suhotra who was the father of Janhu.

## \|\| 139.5 \|\|

*jahnoḥ sumanturabhavatsumantorapajāpakaḥ \|*  
*balākāśvastasya putro balākāśvāt kuśaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Janhu's son was Sumanta and Sumanta's son was Apajapaka. The son of Apajapaka was Balakasva, who was the father of Kusa.

## \|\| 139.6 \|\|

*kuśāśvaḥ kuśanābhaścāmūrtarayo vasuḥ kuśāt \|*  
*gādhiḥ kuśāśvātsaṃjajñe viśvāmitrastadātmajaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Kusa's had four sons named Kusasva, Kusalabha, Amurtaraya and Vasu. The son of Kusasva was Gadhi who was the father of the celebrated Visvamitra.

## \|\| 139.7 \|\|

*kanyā satyavatī dattā ṛcīkāya dvijāya sā \|*  
*ṛcīkājjamadāgniśca rāmastasyābhavatsutaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Gadhi had a daughter named Satyavati, who was give in marriage to the holy sage Rcika. The son of Rcika was Jamadagni, who was the father of Parasurama.

## \|\| 139.8 \|\|

*viśvāmitrāddevarātamaducchandādayaḥ sutāḥ \|*  
*āyuṣo nahuṣastasmādanenā rajirambhakau \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. The sage Visvamitra had a large family of sons such as Devarakta, Madhuchanda, etc. Ayu (a son of Budha) had a son named Nahusa who had four sons named Anena, Raji, Rambhaka and Katra Vrddha.

## \|\| 139.9 \|\|

*kṣattravṛddhaḥ kṣattravṛddhātsuhotraścābhavannṛpaḥ \|*  
*kāśyakāśaugṛtsamadaḥ suhotrādabhavaṃstrayaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The son of Ksatra Vrddha was Suhotra who had three sons, viz., Kasya, Kassa, and Grtsamada.

## \|\| 139.10 \|\|

*gṛtsamadācchauna ko 'bhūtkāśyāddīrghatamāstathā \|*  
*vaidyo dhanvantaristasmātketumāṃśca tadātmajaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. $aunaka was the son of Grtsamada, and DIrghtama was the son of Kasya. The son of Dirghatama was Dhanvantari who look the profession of a physician.

## \|\| 139.11 \|\|

*bhīmarathaḥ ketumato divodāsastadātmajaḥ \|*  
*divodāsātpratardanaḥ śatrujitso 'tra viśrutaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Dhanvantari had a son named Ketuman who was the father of Bhlmaratha. Divodasa was the son of Bhlmaratha, and Pratardana known to history as Shatrujit (conquerer of enemies) was the son of Divodasa.

## \|\| 139.12 \|\|

*ṛtadhvajastasya putro hyalarkaśca ṛtadhvajāt \|*  
*alarkātsannatirjajñe sunītaḥ sannateḥ sutaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. The son of Pratardana was Rtadhvaja, who was the father of Alarka. Alarka's son was Sannati and Sunita was Sannati's son.

## \|\| 139.13 \|\|

*satyaketuḥ sunītasya satyaketorvibhuḥ sutaḥ \|*  
*vibhostu suvibhuḥ putraḥ suvibhoḥ sukumārakaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. The son of Sunita was Satyaketu who was the father of Bibhu. The son of Bibhu was Subibhu, the father of Sukumara.

## \|\| 139.14 \|\|

*sukumārāddhṛṣṭaketurvotihotrastadātmajaḥ \|*  
*vītihotrasya bhargo 'bhūdbhargabhūmistadātmajaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Sukumara begat Dhrstaketu, and Dhrsta- ketu begat Vitihotra who had a son named Bharga. The son of Bharga was Bhargabhumi.

## \|\| 139.15 \|\|

*vaiṣṇavāḥ syurmahātmāna ityete kāśayo nṛpāḥ \|*  
*pañcaputraśatānyāsanrajeḥ śakreṇa saṃhṛtāḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. All these magnanimous princes were firmly devoted to Visnu and ruled in Kasi. Raji (a son of Nahusa) had five hundred sons who were killed by the God-Indra.

## \|\| 139.16 \|\|

*pratikṣattraḥ kṣattravṛddhātsaṃjayaśca ta dātmajaḥ \|*  
*vijayaḥ saṃjayasyāpi vijayasya kṛtaḥ sutaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Ksatra Vrddha (a son of Nahusa) had another son named Pratiksatra who was the father of Sanjaya. Sanjaya begat Vijaya whose son was Krta.

## \|\| 139.17 \|\|

*kṛtādvṛṣadhanaścābhūtsahadevastadātmajaḥ \|*  
*sahadevādadīno 'bhūjjayatseno 'pyadīnataḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Krta begat Vrsdhana, and Vrsadhana begat Sahadeva whose son was Adina who begat Jayattsena.

## \|\| 139.18 \|\|

*jayatsenātsaṃkṛtiśca kṣattradharmā ca saṃkṛteḥ \|*  
*yatiryayātiḥ saṃyātirayātirvikṛtiḥ kramāt \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. The latter had a son named Satkrti whose son was Ksatradharma. Nahusa had a family of another five sons who were called Yati, Yayati, Samyati, Ayati and Krti.

## \|\| 139.19 \|\|

*nahuṣasya sutāḥ khyātā yayāternṛpatestathā \|*  
*yaduṃ ca turvasuṃ caiva devayānī vyajāyata \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Out of these, Yayati begat on his wife Devayam two sons who were named Yadu and Turvasu.

## \|\| 139.20 \|\|

*druhyuṃ cānuṃ ca pūruñca śarmiṣṭhā vārṣapārvaṇī \|*  
*sahasrajītkroṣṭumanā raghuścaiva yadoḥ sutāḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. And three sons on his wife Sarmistha who were called Drahyu, Anu and Puru. Yadu had three sons named Sahasrajit, Krostumana and Raghu.

## \|\| 139.21 \|\|

*sahasrajitaḥ śatajittasmādvai hayahaihayau \|*  
*anaraṇyo hayātputro dharmo haihayato 'bhavat \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. The son of Sahasrajit was Satajit who was the father of Haya and Haihaya. The son of Haya was Anaranya who was the father of Dharma.

## \|\| 139.22 \|\|

*dharmasya dharmanetro 'būtkuntirvai dharmanetrataḥ \|*  
*kunterbabhūta sāhañjirmahiṣmāṃśca tadātmajaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Dharma's son was Dharmanetra, whose son was Kunti. Kunti's son was Sahanji whose son was Mahisman.

## \|\| 139.23-26 \|\|

*bhadraśreṇyastasya puttro bhadraśreṇayasya durdamaḥ \|*  
*dhanako durdamāccaiva kṛtavīryaśca jānakiḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

*kṛtāgniḥ kṛtakarmā ca kṛtaujāḥ sumahābalaḥ \|*  
*kṛtavīryādarjuno 'bhūdarjunācchūrasenakaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*jayadhvajo madhuḥ śūro vṛṣaṇaḥ pañca savratāḥ \|*  
*jayadhvajāttālajaṅgho bharatastālajaṅgataḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*vṛṣaṇasya madhuḥ puttro madhorvṛṣṇyādivaṃśakaḥ \|*  
*kroṣṭorvijajñivānputtra āhistasya mahātmanaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

23-26. Mahisman's son was Bhadrasrenya whose son was Durdama. Durdama's son was Dhanaka who had four sons named Krtavirya, Krtagni, Krtakarma and Krtauja. All of them were of mighty prowess. Krtavirya had a son named Arjuna whose sons were Urasena, Jayadlivaja, Mahu, 6ura and Vrsna. All these five sons of Krtavirya were princes of excellent conduct. Jayadhvaja's son was Talajangha whose son was Bharata. Madhu was the son of Vrsna, and from him (Madhu) sprang the race of Vrsni. Ahi was the son of Krosta and his son was Asanku.

## \|\| 139.27-28 \|\|

*āheruśaṅkuḥ saṃjajñetasya citrarathaḥ sataḥ \|*  
*śaśabinduścitrarathātpatnyo lakṣañca tasya ha \|\| 27 \|\|*

*daśalakṣañca putrāṇāṃ pṛthukīrtyādayo varāḥ \|*  
*pṛthukīrtiḥ pṛthujayaḥ pṛthudānaḥ pṛthuśravāḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

27-28. The son of Asanku was Citraratha whose son was Shasabindu. Shasabindu had two wives. By his first wife he had a hundred thousand sons, while by his second he had ten hundreds of thousands, such as Prthuklrti, etc. Prthuklrti had three sons, viz., Prthujaya, Prthudana and Prthusrava.

## \|\| 139.29-30 \|\|

*pṛthuśravaso 'bhūttama uśanāstamaso 'bhavat \|*  
*tatputraḥ śitagurnāma śrīrukmakavacastataḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*rukmaśca pṛthurukmaśca jyāmaghaḥ pālito hariḥ \|*  
*śrīrukmakavacasyaite vidarbho jyāmaghāttathā \|\| 30 \|\|*

29-30. Prthusrava begat Tama, Tama begat Usna Usna begat Sitayu, and Sitayu begat Rukmakavaca. Rukmakavaca had five sons viz., Rukma, Prthurukma, Jayamagha, Palita and Hari.The son of Jayamagha was Vidarbha whose wife's name was Saibya.

## \|\| 139.31 \|\|

*bhāryāyāñcaiva śaibyāyāṃ vidarbhātkrathakauśikau \|*  
*romapādo romapādādbabhrurbabhrordhṛtistathā \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Vidarbha begat on his wife Saibya three sons whose names were Krutha, Kamsuka, and Romapada, Romapada's son was Babhru, and Babhru's son was Dhrti.

## \|\| 139.32-33 \|\|

*kauśikasya ṛciḥ putraḥ tataścaidyo nṛpaḥ kila \|*  
*kuntiḥ kilāsya putro 'bhūtkuntervṛṣṇiḥ sutaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

*vṛṣṇeśca nivṛtiḥ putro daśārhe nivṛtestathā \|*  
*daśārhasya suto vyomā jīmūtaśca tadātmajaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

32-33. The son whom Kausika begot was named Rci whose son was Caidya. Caidya begat Kund, and KuntI begat Vrsni and Vrsni begat Nivrti, who was the father of Dasarha. The son of Dagarha was Vyoma whose son was Jimata.

## \|\| 139.34-35 \|\|

*jīmūtādvikṛtirjajñe tato bhīmaratho 'bhavat \|*  
*tato madhuratho jajñe śakunistasya cātmajaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

*karambhiḥ śakuneḥ putrastasya vai devavānsmṛtaḥ \|*  
*devakṣattro devanato devakṣattrānmadhuḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

34-35. The son of Amrta was Vikrti, who was the father of Bhlmaratha. Bhimaratha begat Madhuratha whose son was Sakuni, who begat Karambhi, who was the father of Devamata. The son of Devamata was Devaksatra whose son was Madhu, whose son was Kuruvamsa.

## \|\| 139.36-39 \|\|

*kuruvaṃśo madhoḥ putro hyanuśca kuruvaṃśataḥ \|*  
*puruhotro hyanoḥ putro hyaṃśuśca puruhotrataḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

*sattvaśrutaḥ sutaścāṃśostato vai sāttvato nṛpaḥ \|*  
*bhajino bhajamānaśca sātvatādandhakaḥ sutaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

*mahābhojo vṛṣṇi divyāvanyo devāvṛdho 'bhavat \|*  
*nimivṛṣṇī bhajamānādayutājittathaiva ca \|\| 38 \|\|*

*śatajicca sahasrājidbabhrurdevo bṛhaspatiḥ \|*  
*mahābhojāttu bhojo 'bhūttadvṛṣṇeśca sumitrakaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

36-39. Kuruvamga begat Anu. Anu begat Puru- hotra, who begat Amsu whose son was Sattvagruta, who was the father of Sattvata. Bhajina, Bhajamana, Andhaka, Mahabhoja, Vrsni, Divya, Aranya, and Devavrta were the sons of Sattvata, Nimi, Vrsni, Ayutajit Satajit, Sahasrajit, Vabhru, Deva, and Brhaspati were the sons of Bhajamana. Bhoja was the son of Mahabhoja, and Sumitra was the son of Vrsni.

## \|\| 139.40-41 \|\|

*svadhājitsaṃjñakastasmādanamitrāśinī tathā \|*  
*anamitrasya nighno 'bhūnnighnācchatrājito 'bhavat \|\| 40 \|\|*

*prasenaścāparaḥ khyāto hyanamitrācchibistathā \|*  
*śibestu satyakaḥ putraḥ satyakātsātyakistathā \|\| 41 \|\|*

40-41. Svadhajit was the son of Sumitra, and 6ini and Animita were the sons of Svadhajit. Nighna was the son of Anamitra, and Satajit, was the son of Nighna. The other two sons of Anamitra were Prasena and Siva. Satyaka was the son of Sivi, and the son of Satyaka was Satyaki.

## \|\| 139.42 \|\|

*sātyakeḥ sañjayaḥ putraḥ kuliścaiva tadātmajaḥ \|*  
*kuleryugandharaḥ putraste śaibeyāḥ prakīrtitāḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Sanjaya was the son of Satyaki, and the son of Sanjaya was Kuli who was the father of Yugundhara. All these princes were the votaries of the God Siva.

## \|\| 139.43 \|\|

*anamitrānvaye vṛṣṇiḥ śvaphalkaścitrakaḥ sutaḥ \|*  
*śvaphalkāccaivagāndinyāmakrūro vaiṣṇavo 'bhavat \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Vrsni, Svaphalka, and Citraka were the sons that gracede the line of Anamitra. Svaphalka begat on the person of Gandhini a son named Akrura, who was firmly devoted to the God Visnu.

## \|\| 139.44 \|\|

*upamadgurathākrūrāddevadyotastataḥ sutaḥ \|*  
*devavānupadevaśca hyakrūrasya sutau smṛtau \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Upamudga was the son of Akrura, and the son of Upamudga was Devadyota. Akrura had two other sons who were called Devayana and Upadeva.

## \|\| 139.45 \|\|

*pṛthurvipṛthuścitrasya tvandhakasya śuciḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*kukuro bhajamānasya tathā kambalabarhiṣaḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Prthu and Viprthu were the sons of Citraka, who was of the race of Anamitra, aned Suci was the son of Andhaka the son of Sattvata. Kukkura and Kambala Barhisa were the sons of Bhajamana.

## \|\| 139.46 \|\|

*dhṛṣṭastu kukurājjajñe tasmātkāpotaromakaḥ \|*  
*tadātmajo vilomā ca vilomnastumburuḥ sutaḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Kukkura had a son named Dhrsta, and Kapotaromaka was the son of Dhrsta. Viloma was the son of Kapotaromaka, and Tumburu was the son of Viloma.

## \|\| 139.47 \|\|

*tasmāccadundubhirjajñe punarvasurataḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*tasyāhukaścāhukī ca kanyā caivāhukasya tu \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. The sons of Tumburu was Dundubhi who was the father of Punarvasu. Punarvasu had a son named Ahuka, and a daughter named Ahuki.

## \|\| 139.48-49 \|\|

*devakaścograsenaśca devakāddevakī tvabhūt \|*  
*vṛkadevopadevāca sahadevā surakṣitā \|\| 48 \|\|*

*śrīdevī śāntidevī ca vasudeva uvāha tāḥ \|*  
*devavānupadevaśca sahadevāsutau smṛtau \|\| 49 \|\|*

48-49. The sons of Ahuka were Devaka and Ugrasena. The daughters of Devaka were named DevakI, Vrkadeva, Upadeva, Sahadeva, Suraks ita, ArldevI, and AantidevI, who were all married to Vasudeva. Sahadeva had two sons named Deva and Upadeva.

## \|\| 139.50 \|\|

*ugrasenasya kaṃso 'bhūtsunāmā ca vaṭādayaḥ \|*  
*vidūratho bhajamānācchūraścābhūdvidūrathāt \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Ugrasena had several sons named Kansa, Soluma and Cavata. Viduratha was the son of Bhajamana, a son of Andhaka.

## \|\| 139.51 \|\|

*vidūrathasutasyātha sūrasyāpi śamī sutaḥ \|*  
*pratikṣattraśca śaminaḥ svayambhojastadātmajaḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. The son of Viduratha was Sura, who was the father of gams. Pratiksatra was the son of Sami, and the son of Pratiksatra was Svayambhoja, who was the father of Hrdika.

## \|\| 139.52 \|\|

*hṛdikaśca svayambhojātkṛtavarmā tadātmajaḥ \|*  
*devaḥ śatadhanuścaiva śūrādvai devamīḍhuṣaḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. The son of Hrdika was Krtarma, the son of Aura, the son of Viduratha, were Deva, Aatadhanu, and Devamidusa.

## \|\| 139.53-54 \|\|

*daśa putrā māriṣāyāṃ vasudevādayo 'bhavan \|*  
*pṛthā ca śrutadevī ca śrutakīrtiḥ śrutaśravāḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

*rājādhidevo śūrācca pṛthāṃ kunteḥ sutāmadāt \|*  
*sā dattā kuntinā pāṇḍostasyāṃ dharmānilendrakaiḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

53-54. Sura had another wife named Marisa who became the mother of five daughters named Prtha, Arutadeva. Arutakirti, Arutasrva and Rajadhidevi and of two sons such as Vasudeva, etc. Prtha was filiated to Kuntlraja who married her to Pandu.

## \|\| 139.55 \|\|

*yudhiṣṭhiro bhīmapārtho nakulaḥ sahadevakaḥ \|*  
*mādrayāṃ nāsatyadastrābhyāṃ kuntyāṃ karṇaḥ purābhavat \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. The God of Virtue begat on the person of Prtha, a son named Yudhisthira, while the Wind-God and Indra successively begot on her two sons named Bhimasena and Arjuna. The king Pandu had another queen named Madri, who became the mother of two sons named Nakula and Sahadeva, begot on her person by the Asvins Nasatya and Dasra. KuntI had another son before marriage who was named Karp.

## \|\| 139.56 \|\|

*śrutadevyāṃ dantavakro jajñe vai yuddhadurmadaḥ \|*  
*santardanādayaḥ pañca śrutakīrtyāñca kaikayāt \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. Srutadeva was the mother of Dantavakra who was valiant in battles. The king of Kekaya begat on the person of Arutakirti five sons such as Aantardhana. etc.

## \|\| 139.57 \|\|

*rājādhidevyāṃ jajñāte vindaścaivānuvindakaḥ \|*  
*śrutaśravā damaghoṣātprajajñe śiśupālakam \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. Rajadhidevi had two sons named Vindhu and Anuvindha. Damaghosa begat on the person of Arutasreva a son named Aisupala.

## \|\| 139.58 \|\|

*pauravī rohīṇā bhāryā madirānakadundubheḥ \|*  
*devakīpramukhā bhadrā rohiṇyāṃ balabhadrakaḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. Vasudeva had several wives named Pauravl. RohinI, Madira and DevakI, etc. Of these RohinI became the mother of Balarama.

## \|\| 139.59-60 \|\|

*sāraṇādyāḥ śaṭhaścaiva revatyāṃ balabhadrataḥ \|*  
*niśaṭhaścolmuko jāto devakyāṃ ṣaṭ ca jajñire \|\| 59 \|\|*

*kīrtimāṃśca suṣeṇaśca hyudāryo bhadrasenakaḥ \|*  
*ṛjudāso bhadradevaḥ kaṃsa evāvadhīcca tān \|\| 60 \|\|*

59-60. Balarama begat on his wife Revatl several sons such as Sarana, Aatha, Nisatha, and Ulmaka, etc. Devaki became the mother of six sons, who were named KIrtimana, Susena, Udarya, Bhadrasena, Rjudasa, and Bhadradeva. King Kamsa destroyed all these six sons of Devaki.

## \|\| 139.61-62 \|\|

*saṃkarṣaṇaḥ saptamo 'bhūdaṣṭamaḥ kṛṣṇa eva ca \|*  
*ṣoḍaśastrīsahasrāṇi bhāryāṇāñcābhavanhareḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

*rukmiṇī satyabhāmā ca lakṣmaṇā cāruhāsinī \|*  
*śreṣṭhā jāmbavatī cāṣṭau jajñire tāḥ sutānbahūn \|\| 62 \|\|*

61-62. Samkarsana or Balarama was the seventh son of Devaki, and Krsna was her eighth. Krsna had sixteen thousand wives, of whom RukminI, Satyabhama, Laksmana CaruhasinI, and Jambavatl were the eight principal ones. Krsna had a large family of sons by these wives.

## \|\| 139.63 \|\|

*pradyumnaścārudeṣṇaśca pradhānāḥ sāmba eva ca \|*  
*pradyumnādaniruddho 'bhūtkakudminyāṃ mahābalaḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. Pradyumna, Carudesna, and Samba were famous. Pradyumna begat on his wife Rati a son of mighty prowess who was named Aniruddha.

## \|\| 139.64 \|\|

*aniruddhātsubhadrāyāṃ vajro nāma nṛpo 'bhavat \|*  
*pratibāhurvajrasutaścārustasya suto 'bhavat \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. Aniruddha had by his wife Subhadra. A son named Vajra. The son of Vajra was Prativahu, and the son of Prativahu was Caru.

## \|\| 139.65 \|\|

*vahnistu turvasorvaṃśe vahnerbhargo 'bhavatsutaḥ \|*  
*bhargādbhānurabhūtputro bhānoḥ putraḥ karandhamaḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. Vahni was scion of the race of Turvasu. The son of Vahni was Bharya, whose son was Bhlma, the father of Karandhama.

## \|\| 139.66-68 \|\|

*karandhamasya maruto druhyorvaṃśaṃ nibodha me \|*  
*drahyostu tanayaḥ seturāraddhaśca tadātmajaḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

*āraddhasyaiva gāndha ro gharmo gāndhārato 'bhavat \|*  
*ghṛtastu gharmaputro 'bhūddurgamaśca ghṛsya tu \|\| 67 \|\|*

*pracetā durgamasyaiva anorvaṃśaṃ śṛṇuṣva me \|*  
*anoḥ sabhānaraḥ putrastasmā kālañjayo 'bhavat \|\| 68 \|\|*

66-68. Karandhama's son was Maruta. Now hear me describe the race of Druhya. Druhya's son was Setu, whose son was Arandha, whose son was Gandhara, whose son was Gharma. The son of Gharma was Ghrta, whose son was Durgama who was the father of Praceta. Now hear me describe the progeny of Anu, whose son was Svabhanara. The son of Svabhanara was kalanjaya.

## \|\| 139.69-70 \|\|

*kālañjayātsṛñjayo 'bhūtsṛñjayāttu puruñjayaḥ \|*  
*janamejayastu tatputro mahāśālastadātmajaḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

*mahāmanā mahāśāladuśīnara iha smṛtaḥ \|*  
*aśīnarācchibirjajñe vṛṣadarbhaḥ śiveḥ sutaḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

69-70. Kalankaya's son was 3rnjaya, whose son was Puranjaya. The son of Puranjaya was Janamejaya, whose son was Mahasala, who was the father of Mahamana better known by the appellation of Uslhara. The son of Uslnara was Shivl, whose son was Vrsadarbha.

## \|\| 139.71-72 \|\|

*mahāmanojāttitikṣoḥ putro 'bhūcca ruṣadrathaḥ \|*  
*hemo ruṣadrathājjajñe sutapā hemato 'bhavat \|\| 71 \|\|*

*baliḥ sutapaso jajñe hyaṅgavaṅgakaliṅgakāḥ \|*  
*andhaḥ paiṇḍraśca bāleyā hyanapānastathāṅgataḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

71-72. Mahamana had another son named Titiks u whose son was Rudraratha. The son of Rudraratha was Hema, whose son was Sutapa, whose son was Bali. This Bali was the father of several sons who were called Anga, Varied, Kalinga, Andhra, and Paundra.

## \|\| 139.73-74 \|\|

*anapānāddivirathastato dharmaratho 'bhavat \|*  
*romapādo dharmarathāccaturaṅgastadātmajaḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

*pṛthulākṣastasya putraścampo 'bhūtpṛthulākṣataḥ \|*  
*campaputraśca haryaṅgastasya bhadrarathaḥ sutaḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

73-74. The son of Anga was Anapala, whose son was Diviratha, who was the father of Dharma ratha. The son of Dharmaratha was Lompada, whose son was Caturanga, whose son was Prthulaksya, who was the father of Campa. The son of Campa was Haryaksa, whose son was Bhadraratha.

## \|\| 139.75-77 \|\|

*bṛhatkarmā sutastasya bṛhadbhānustato 'bhavat \|*  
*buhanmanā bṛhādbhānostasya putro jayadrathaḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

*jayajrathasya vijayo vijayasya dhṛtiḥ sutaḥ \|*  
*dhṛterdhṛvrataḥ putraḥ satyadharmā dhṛtavratāt \|\| 76 \|\|*

*tasya putrastvadhirathaḥ karṇastasya suto 'bhavat \|\| 77 \|\|*

75-77. Whose son was Vrhatkarma, who was the father of Vrhadbhanu. The son of Vrhadbhanu was Vrhatmana, whose son was Jayadratha, whose son was Vijaya, who was the father of Dhrti. The son of Dhrti was Dhrtavrata, whose son was Satyadharma, whose son was Adhiratha who was the father of Kama.

## \|\| 139.78 \|\|

*vṛrṣasenastu karṇasya puruvaṃśyāñchaṇuṣva me \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. The son of Kama was Vrsasena. Now I shall describe the race of Puru.

## Chapter 140

## \|\| 140.1 \|\|

*hariruvāca \|*  
*janamejayaḥ puroścābhūnnamasyurjanamejayāt \|*  
*tasya putraścābhayadaḥ sudyuścābhayadādabhūt \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Hari said: — The son of Риги was Janamejaya, whose son was Manusya, whose son was Ahayada whose son was $ambhu, who was the father of Bahugati.

## \|\| 140.2 \|\|

*sudyorbahugatiḥ putraḥ saṃjātistasya cātmajaḥ \|*  
*vatsajātiśca sañjāteḥ raudrāśvaśca tadātmajaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. The son of Bahugati was Samjati, whose son was Vatsagati, who was the fattier of RaudraSva.

## \|\| 140.3 \|\|

*ṛteyuḥ sthaṇḍileyuśca kakṣeyuśca kṛteyukaḥ \|*  
*jaleyuḥ santateyuśca rodrāśvasya sutā varāḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Raudrasva had several sons, who were named Rteyu. Sthandileyu, Kakseyu, Krteya, Jaleyu, and Santateyu.

## \|\| 140.4 \|\|

*ratināra ṛteyośca tasya pratirathaḥ sutaḥ \|*  
*tasya medhātithiḥ putrastatputraścainilaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Of these the son of Rteyu was Ratinara, whose son was Pratiratha. The son of Pratiratha was Medhatithi whose son was Ainila.

## \|\| 140.5 \|\|

*ainilasya tu duṣyanto bharatastasya cātmajaḥ \|*  
*śakuntalāyāṃ saṃjajñe vitatho bharatādabhūt \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. The son of Ainila was Dusyanta, who by his wife Shakuntala, had a son named Bharata. The son of Bharata was Vitatha.

## \|\| 140.6 \|\|

*vitathasya suto manyurmanyoścaiva naraḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*narasya saṃkṛtiḥ putro gargo vai saṃkṛteḥ sutaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Vitatha son was Manyu, whose son was Nara, whose son was Samkrti, who was the father of Garga.

## \|\| 140.7 \|\|

*gargādamanyuḥ putro vai śiniḥ putro vyajāyata \|*  
*manyuputrānmahāvīryātsuto 'bhavadurukṣayaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. The son of Garga was Amanyu, whose son was Mini. The mighty Nara, the son of Manyu had another son named Uruksaya.

## \|\| 140.8 \|\|

*urukṣayāttrayyāruṇirvyūhakṣatrācca manyujāt \|*  
*suhotrastasya hastī ca ajamīḍhadvimīḍhakau \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. The son of Uruksaya was Tray arum, whose son was Vyuhaksetra, whose son was Suhotra, who had three sons Hasti, Ajamlhha and Dvimlda.

## \|\| 140.9 \|\|

*hastinaḥ purumīḍhaśca kaṇvo 'bhūdajamīḍhataḥ \|*  
*kaṇvānmedhātithirjajñe yataḥ kāṇvāyanā dvijāḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The son of Hasti was Purumida, and the son of Ajamlda was Kanva. Medhatithi sprange from this Kanva, who was the progenitor of the Kfmvayana clan of Brahmanas.

## \|\| 140.10-11 \|\|

*ajamīḍhādvṛhadiṣustatputraśca bṛhaddhanuḥ \|*  
*bṛhatkarmā tasya putrastasya putro jayadrathaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*jayadrathādviśvajicca senajicca tadātmajaḥ \|*  
*rucirāśvaḥ senajitaḥ pṛthusenastadātmajaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

10-11. Ajamidha had another son named Vrhadisu, who was the father of Vrhatdhanu. The son of Vrhatdhanu was Vrhatkarma, whose son was Jayadratha, whose son was Visvajit, whose son was Senajit, whose son was Rucirasva, who was the father of Prthusena.

## \|\| 140.12 \|\|

*pārastu pṛthusenasya pārāddvīpo 'bhavannṛpaḥ \|*  
*nṛpasya sṛmaraḥ putraḥ sukṛtiśca pṛthoḥ sutaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Риги was the son of Prthusena, whose son Dvlpa, whose son was Samara. Prthusena had another son named Sukrti.

## \|\| 140.13 \|\|

*vibhrājaḥ sukṛteḥ putro vibhrājādaśvaho 'bhavat \|*  
*kṛtyāṃ tasmādbrahmadatto viṣvaksenastadātmajaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. The son of Sukrti was Vibhraja, whose son was Asvaha. The said Asvaha had a son by this wife Krti, named Brahmadatta, whose son was Visvaksena.

## \|\| 140.14 \|\|

*yavīnaro dvimīḍhasya dhṛtimāṃśca yavīnarāt \|*  
*dhatimataḥ satyadhṛtirdṛḍhanemistadātmajaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Dvimidha, the son of Suhotra had a son named Yavina. The son of Yavina was Dhrtimana, whose son was Satyadhrti, whose son was Drdhamuni.

## \|\| 140.15-16 \|\|

*dṛḍhanemeḥ supārśvo 'bhūt supārśvātsannatistathā \|*  
*kṛstu sannateḥ putraḥ kṛtādugrāyudho 'bhavat \|\| 15 \|\|*

*ugrāyudhācca kṣemyau'bhūtsudhīrastu tadātmajaḥ \|*  
*purañjayaḥ sudhīrācca tasya putro vidūrathaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

15-16. The son of Drdhamuni was Supar^va, whose son was Sannati. The son of Sannati was Kratu, whose son was Ugrayudha, whose son was Ksema, whose son was Sudhira, whose son was Puranjaya, who was the father of Viduratha.

## \|\| 140.17-18 \|\|

*ajamīḍhānnalinyāñca nīlo nāma nṛpo 'bhavat \|*  
*nīlācchāntirabhūtputraḥ suśāntistasya cātmajaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*suśānteśca pururjāto hyarkastasya suto 'bhavat \|*  
*arkasya caiva haryaśvo haryaśvānmukulo 'bhavat \|\| 18 \|\|*

17-18. Ajamidha had a wife named NalinI, who gave birth to Nila. The son of Nila was Santi, whose son was SuSanti, whose son was Puru, whose son was Arka, whose son was Haryagva, who was the father of Mukula.

## \|\| 140.19 \|\|

*yavīnaro bṛhadbhānuḥ kampillaḥ sṛñjayastathā \|*  
*pāñcālānmukulājjajñe śaradvānvaiṣṇavo mahān \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. This Mukula became the ruler of the country of Pancala. He had five sons named Yuvanira, Vrhadbhanu, Kampilla, 6rnjaya and 6aradvana. This Saradvana was firmly devoted to Visnu

## \|\| 140.20 \|\|

*divodāso dvitīyo 'sya hyahalyāyāṃ śaradvataḥ \|*  
*śatānando 'bhavatputrastasya satyadhṛtiḥ sataḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Saradvana begat a son on Ahalya, who was called Divodasa, the second. Divodasa had a son named Satananda. Satyadhrti was the son of Satananda.

## \|\| 140.21 \|\|

*kṛpaḥ kṛpī satyadhṛterurvaśyāṃ vīryahānitaḥ \|*  
*droṇapatnī kṛpī jajñe aśvatthāmānamuttamam \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Satyadhrti lost control over his senses at the sight of the nymph UrvasI, and a son named Krpa and a daughter named Krpi were born out of his emitted seed. Krpi was married to Dronacarya, and Asvatthama was the fruit of this union.

## \|\| 140.22 \|\|

*divodāsānmitrayuśca mitrayoścyavano 'bhavat \|*  
*sudāsaścyavanājjajñe saudāsastasya jātmajaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. The son of Divodasa was Mitrayu, whose son was Gyavana; whose son was Sudasa, who was the father of Saudasa.

## \|\| 140.23 \|\|

*sahadevastasya putraḥ sahadevāttu somakaḥ \|*  
*jantustu somakājjajñe pṛṣataścāparo mahān \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. The son of Saudasa was Sahadeva, whose son was Somaka, who had two sons named Jantu and Prsata.

## \|\| 140.24 \|\|

*pṛṣatāddrupado jajñe dhṛṣṭadyumnastato 'bhavat \|*  
*dhṛṣṭadyumnāddhṛṣṭaketurṛkṣo 'bhūtajamīḍhataḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. The son of Prsta was Drupada; through whom Dhrstadyumna came into being. The son of Dhrstadyumna was Dhrstaketu. The aforesaid Ajamidha had a son named Rksa.

## \|\| 140.25 \|\|

*ṛkṣātsaṃvaraṇo jajñe kuruḥ saṃvaraṇādabhūt \|*  
*sudhanuśca pīkṣicca jahnuścaiva kuroḥ sutāḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. The son of Rksa was Samvarana, who was the father of Kuru Sudhanu, Pariksit and Jahnu.

## \|\| 140.26 \|\|

*sudhanuṣaḥ suhotro 'bhūccyavano 'bhūtsuhotrataḥ \|*  
*cyavanātkṛtako jajñe tathoparicaro vasuḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. The son of Sudhanu was Suhotra, whose son was Cyavana, who was the father of king Krtaka. The son of Krtaka was Uparicayavasu.

## \|\| 140.27-28 \|\|

*bṛhadrathaśca pratyagraḥ satyādyāśca vasoḥ sutāḥ \|*  
*bṛhadrathātkuśāgraśca kuśāgrādṛṣabho 'bhavat \|\| 27 \|\|*

*ṛṣabhātpuṣpavāṃstasmājjajñe satyahito nṛpaḥ \|*  
*satyahitātsudhanvābhūjjahruścava sudhanvanaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

27-28. The father of Brhadratha, Pratyagra, Satya and others. The son of Brhadratha was Kusagra, whose son was Rsabha, whose son was Puspanabha, who was the father of king Satyahita. The son of Satyahita was Suddhanva, whose son was Jahnu.

## \|\| 140.29-30 \|\|

*bṛhadrathājjarāsandhaḥ sahadevastadātmajaḥ \|*  
*sahadevācca ca somāpiḥ somāpeḥ śrutavānsutaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*bhīmasenograsenau ca śrutaseno 'parājitaḥ \|*  
*janamejayastathānyo 'bhūjjahnostu suratho 'bhavat \|\| 30 \|\|*

29-30. The said Brhadratha had another son named Jarasandha. The son of Jarasandha was Sahadeva, whose son was Somapi, who was the father of Bhlmasena, Ugrasena, Srutasena and others. The abovesaid Jahnu had a son named Suratha.

## \|\| 140.31 \|\|

*vidūrathastu surathātsārvabhaumo vidūrathāt \|*  
*jayasenaḥ sārvabhaumādāvadhītastadātmajaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. The son of Suratha was Viduratha, whose son was Sarvabhauma, whose son was Jayasena, who was the father of Avadhita.

## \|\| 140.32 \|\|

*ayutāyustasya putrastasya cākrodhanaḥ sutaḥ \|*  
*akrodhanasyātithiśca ṛkṣo 'bhūdatitheḥ sutaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. The son of Avadhita was Ayutayu, whose son was Akrodhana, whose son was Atithi, who was the father of Rksa.

## \|\| 140.33-34 \|\|

*ṛkṣācca bhīmaseno 'bhūddilīpo bhīmasenataḥ \|*  
*pratīpo 'bhūddilīpācca devāpistu pratīpataḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

*śantanuścaiva bāhlīkastrayaste bhrātaro nṛpāḥ \|*  
*bāhlīkātsomadatto 'bhūdbhūrirbhūriśravāstataḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

33-34. The son of Rksa was Bhlmasena, whose son was Dillpa, whose son was Pratlpa, who was the father of Devapi, Santanu, and Vahllka. Somadatta owes his paternity to King Vahlika. The son of Somadatta was Bhuri, whose sons were Bhurigrava and Shala.

## \|\| 140.35 \|\|

*śalaśca śantanorbhoṣmo gaṅgāyāṃ dhārmiko mahān \|*  
*citrāṅgadavicitrau tu satyavatyāntu śantanoḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Shantanu begot on the person of Ganga, a son named Bhlsma, who was noted for his piety. The said 6antanu had two other sons named Citrangada and Vicitravirya.

## \|\| 140.36 \|\|

*bhārye vicitravīryasya tvambikāmbālike tayoḥ \|*  
*dhṛrāṣṭraṃ ca pāṇḍuñca taddāsyāṃ vidurantathā \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Vicitravlryya had two wives named Ambika and Ambalika. The holy Vyasa begot on Ambika, a son named Dhrtarastra; on Ambalika, a son named Pandu; and on the person of a slave girl, a son named Vidura.

## \|\| 140.37 \|\|

*vyāsa utpādayāmāsa gāndhāgī dhṛtarāṣṭrataḥ \|*  
*śataputraṃ duryodhanādyaṃ pāṇḍoḥ pañca prajajñire \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Dhrtarastra had by his wife Gandhari, a hundred sons named Duryodhana, etc, while Pandu had five sons named Yudhisthira, etc.

## \|\| 140.38 \|\|

*pratibindhyaḥ śrutasomaḥ śrutakīrtistathārjunāt \|*  
*śatānīkaḥ śrutakarmā draupadyāṃ pañca vai kramāt \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. By their common with DraupadI, Yudhisthira had a son named Prativindhya; Bhlma, a son named 6rutasoma; Arjuna, a son named 6rutakirti. Nakula, a son named &atanlka; and Sahadeva, a son named 6rutakarma.

## \|\| 140.39-41 \|\|

*yaudheyī ca hiḍimbā ca kauśī caiva subhadrikā \|*  
*vijayā vai reṇumatī pañcabhyastu sutāḥ kramāt \|\| 39 \|\|*

*devako ghacotkacaśca hyabhimanyuśca sarvagaḥ \|*  
*suhotro niramitraśca parīkṣidabhimanyujaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

*janamejayo 'sya tato bhaviṣyāṃśca nṛpāñchṛṇu \|\| 41 \|\|*

39-41. Yudhisthira and his five brothers had a number of wives; such as Yaudhayl, Hidimba, Каиё1, Subhadra, Vijaya and Renumati, who respectively became the mothers of Devaka, Ghatotkaca, Abhimanyu, Sarvaga, and Suhotra. Abhimanyu was the father of Parlksit, whose son was Janamejaya. Now hear nine enumerate the names of kings who came after Janamejaya.

## Chapter 141

## \|\| 141.1 \|\|

*hariruvāca \|*  
*śatānīko hyaśvamedhadattaścāpyadhisomakaḥ \|*  
*kṛṣṇo 'niruddhaścāpyuṣṇastataścitraratho nṛpaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Hari said: — The son of Shatanika was Asamedhadatta, whose son was Adhisomaka, whose son was Krsna, whose son was Aniruddha, whose son was Usana, whose son was Citraratha.

## \|\| 141.2 \|\|

*śucidratho vṛṣṇimāṃśca supeṇaśca sunīthakaḥ \|*  
*nṛcakṣuśca mukhābāṇaḥ medhāvī ca nṛpañjayaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. The son of Citrarath was iSucidratha, whose son was Vrsnimana, whose son was SuSena, whose son was Sunitha, whose son was Aricaksu, whose son was Mukhavana, whose son was Medhavl, who was the father of Jaya.

## \|\| 141.3 \|\|

*pāriplavaśca munayo medhāvī ca nṛpañjayaḥ \|*  
*bṛhadratho haristigmo śatānīkaḥ sudānakaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. The son of Nrpanjaya, Pariplava, whose son was Sunaya, whose son was Medhavl, who was the father of Nrpanjaya, The son of this Nrpanaya was Hari, whose son was Tigma, whose son was Brhadratha, whose son was 6atanika who was the father of Sudanaka.

## \|\| 141.4 \|\|

*udāno 'hninaraścaiva daṇḍapāṇirnimittakaḥ \|*  
*kṣemakaśca tataḥ śūdraḥ pitā pūrvastataḥ sutaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. The son of Sudanaka was Udana, whose son was Ahninara, whose son was DantapanT, whose son was Mimittaka’ whose son was Ksemaka who was the father of Shura.

## \|\| 141.5-6 \|\|

*bṛhadbalāstu kathayante nṛpoścaikṣvākuvaṃśajāḥ \|*  
*bṛhadbalādurukṣayo vatsavyūhastataḥ paraḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*vatsavyūhāttataḥ sūryaḥ sahadevastadātmajaḥ \|*  
*bṛhadaśvo bhānurathaḥ pratīcyaśca pratītakaḥ \|*  
*manudevaḥ sunakṣatraḥ kinnaraścāntarikṣakaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. Now hear me narrate the genealogy of princes, who would grace in future the life of Brhadbala of the race of Iksvaku. The son of Brhadbala would be Uruksaya, whose son wuld be Vatsavyuha, whose son would be Vrhadasva, whose son would be Bhanuratha, whose son would be Prativya, whose son would be Pratilaka, whose son would be Manudeva, whose son would be Sunaksatra, whose son would be Kinnara, whose son would be Antariksaka.

## \|\| 141.7 \|\|

*suparṇaḥ kṛtajiccaiva bṛhadbhrājaśca dhārmikaḥ \|*  
*kṛtañjayo dhanañjayaḥ saṃjayaḥ śākya eva ca \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Antariksaka would beget Suparna, who would beget Krtajit who would beget the pious Brhadbhraja, who would beget Krtanjaya, who would beget Dhananjaya, who would beget Sanjaya, who would beget бакуа.

## \|\| 141.8 \|\|

*śuddhodano bāhulaśca senajitkṣudrakastathā \|*  
*sumitraḥ kuḍavaścātaḥ sumitrānmāgadhāñchaṇu \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Sакуа would beget Suddhodana, who would beget Bahula, who would beget Senajit; who would beget Ksudraka, who would beget Samitra, who would beget Kudava, who would beget Sumitra.

## \|\| 141.9 \|\|

*jarāsandhaḥ sahadevaḥ somāpiśca śrutaśravāḥ \|*  
*ayutāyurniramitraḥ sukṣatro bahukarmakaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Now hear me narrate the genealogy of the princes of Magadha. The son of Jarasandha was Sumapi, whose son was Srutasrava whose son was Ayutayu, whose son was Niramitra, whose son was Svaksetra, whose son was Karmaka.

## \|\| 141.10-11 \|\|

*śrutañjayaḥ senajicca bhūriścaiva śucistathā \|*  
*kṣemyaśca suvrato dharmaḥ śmaśrulo dṛḍhasenakaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*sumatiḥ subalo nīto satyajidviśvajittathā \|*  
*iṣuñjayaśca ityete nṛpā bārhadrathāḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

10-11. The son of Karmaka was 6rutanjaya, whose son was Senajit, whose son was Bhurl, whose son was 6uci, whose son was Ksemya, whose son was Suvrata, whose son was Dharma, whose son was 6masruma, whose son was Drdhasenaka, whose son was Sumati, whose son was Suvala, whose son was Nita, whose son was Satyajit, whose son was Visvajit, whose son was Isunjaya. All these princes were of the race of Vrhadratha.

## \|\| 141.12 \|\|

*adharmiṣṭhāśca śūdrāśca bhaviṣyanti nṛpāstataḥ \|*  
*svargādikṛddhi bhagavānsākṣānnārāyaṇo 'vyayaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. After this, impious Shudra kings, who would stick at nothing to gain their ends, would be the rulers of the world, and oppression, buplicity and falsehood would be the only recognised principles of state craft. The eternal Narayana, who suffers no change nor decay is the creator, protector and disintegrator of the cosmic Universe.

## \|\| 141.13-14 \|\|

*naimittikaḥ prākṛtikastathaivātyantiko layaḥ \|*  
*yāti bhūḥ pralayaṃ cāpsu hyāpastejasi pāvakaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*vāyau vāyuśca viyati tvākāśau yātyahaṅkṛtau \|*  
*ahaṃ buddhau matirjove jīvo 'vyakte tadātmani \|\| 14 \|\|*

13-14. This Pralaya or dissolution of the cosmos admits of being gouped under three different heads; such as, the Naimittika (accidental or contingent, and conditional); Prakrtika (physical and cosmic); and lastly, Atyantika (final, and without any chance of the re-integration and recombination of its molecules). The different categories of cosmic evolution will merge in one another in the inverse order of their enumeration, viz., the soilds will dissolve into the liquids; the liquids will be absorbed in the gaseous or the heat, the heat will die away in the ether, the ether will be merged in the etherine, the etherine, in the category of Ahamkara (Egoism); the Ahamkara in the principle of intellection, (Buddhitattva); the Intellection in the Self or JIva, and the JIva in the untnanifest Brahma.

## \|\| 141.15 \|\|

*ātmā pareśvaro viṣṇureko nārāyaṇo naraḥ \|*  
*avināśyaparaṃ sarvaṃ jagatsvargādi nāśi hi \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Visnu, the Soul of the Universe, is the only deathless Reality in the Universe, which makes itself patent in the shape of Nara Narayana (the Divine Man). The universe is transient and illusory.

## \|\| 141.16 \|\|

*nṛpādayo gatā nāśamataḥ pāpaṃ vivarjayet \|*  
*dharmaṃ kuryātsthiraṃ yena pāpaṃ hitvā hariṃ vrajet \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Many kings there had been in the world and many more will come and pass away as fitful shadows. There fore walk ye not in the piths of the unrighteous. Abjure sin and work out the purity of thought, for in such thoughts consists the salvation of a man and such thoughts lead to the blissful Hari.

## Chapter 142

## \|\| 142.1 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*viṃśādīnpālayāmāsa hyavatīrṇo hariḥ prabhuḥ \|*  
*daityadharmasya nāśārthaṃ vedadharmādiguptaye \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Brahma said: — The God Hari incarnated on earth and protected the seed of the Aryyas. His advent on this fleeting world was for the destruction of the kingdom of the Asuras and the propagation of the religion of the Vedas.

## \|\| 142.2-3 \|\|

*matsyādikasvarūpeṇa tvavatāraṃ karotyajaḥ \|*  
*matsyo bhūtvā hayagrīvaṃ daityaṃ hatvājikaṇṭakam \|\| 2 \|\|*

*vedānānīya manvādīnpālayāmāsa keśavaḥ \|*  
*mandaraṃ dhārayāmāsa kūrmo bhūtvā hitāya ca \|\| 3 \|\|*

2-3. His several incarnation were in the forms of Fish, Tortoise, etc. The God Kesava incarnated himself as the Fish in the primordial ocean, carried the immutable. Vedas on his back, killed the demon Hayagriva, and protected the patriarch Manu and others.

## \|\| 142.4 \|\|

*kṣīrodamathane vai dyo devo dhanvantarirhyarbhūt \|*  
*bibhratkamaṇḍaluṃ pūrṇamamṛtena samutthitaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Incarnated as a Tortoise, he carried the Mount Mandara on his back, were with the gods and demons churned the primordial ocean for ambrosia. As the fruit of that churning, Dhanvantarl, the first of the propounder of the medical science came out of its troubled waters, carrying the pitcher of divine ambrosia in his hand.

## \|\| 142.5 \|\|

*āyurvedamathāṣṭāṅgaṃ suśrutāya sa uktavān \|*  
*amṛtaṃ pāyayāmāsa strīrūpī ca surānhariḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Dhanvantarl related to Susruta the science of Ayurveda with its eight subdivisions, and the God Hari, assuming the shape of a girl of fascinating beauty, doled out the ambrosia to the gods.

## \|\| 142.6 \|\|

*avatīrṇo varāho 'tha hiraṇyākṣaṃ jaghāna ha \|*  
*pṛthivīṃ dhārayāmāsa pālayāmāsa devatāḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Incarnated as the Divine Boar, the God Hari killed the demon Hiranyaksa, lifted up the submerged earth on his tusks from beneath the waters of the enshrouding ocean, and protected the gods and patriarchs.

## \|\| 142.7 \|\|

*narasiṃho 'vartorṇo 'tha hiraṇyakaśipuṃripum \|*  
*daityānnihatavānvedadharmādīnabhyapālayat \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Incarnated as the redoubtable Nrsiihha (halfman, half-lion), the God Hari destroyed the demon HiranyakaSipu with his sinful allies, and vindicated the religion of the Vedas.

## \|\| 142.8-9 \|\|

*tataḥ paraśurāmo 'bhūjjamadagnerjagatprabhuḥ \|*  
*triḥ saptakṛtvaḥ pṛthivīṃ cakre niḥ kṣattriyāṃ hariḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*kārtavīryaṃ jaghānājau kaśyapāya mahīṃ dadau \|*  
*yāgaṃ kṛtvā mahābāhurmahendre parvate sthitaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

8-9. After that, the lord of the universe was incarnated as Parasurama, a son of Jamadagni. For twenty-one times in succession he extirpated the race of the wicked Ksatriyas, killed the dreadful Karttavlryarjuna, made a gift of the whole earth to KaSyapa, and finally settled himself on the summits of the Mount Mahendra.

## \|\| 142.10-13 \|\|

*tato rāmo bhaviṣṇuśca caturdhā duṣṭarmadanaḥ \|*  
*putro daśarathājjajñe rāmaśca bharato 'nujaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*lakṣmaṇaścātha śatrughno rāmabhāryā ca jānakī \|*  
*rāmaśca pitṛsatyārthaṃ mātṛbhyo hitamācaran \|\| 11 \|\|*

*śṛṅgaveraṃ citrakūṭaṃ daṇḍakāraṇyamāgataḥ \|*  
*nāsāṃ śūrpaṇakhāyāśca cchittvātha kharadūṣaṇam \|\| 12 \|\|*

*hatvā sa rākṣasaṃ sītāpahārirajanīcaram \|*  
*rāvaṇaṃ cānujaṃ tasya laṅkāpuryāṃ vibhīṣaṇam \|\| 13 \|\|*

10-13. After that, the subduer of the wicked divided his divine self into four parts and came into the world as Rama, Bharata, Laksmana and &atrughna, the four sons of king Dasaratha, JanakI was the wife of Rama, who, for flue good of his step mother Kaikeyi, and for the performance of a promise made her by his father, resorted, as a voluntary exile, to the forest of Dandaka. Cut the nose of Shiipanakha, killed the monsters Khara and Dusana, and destroyed the dreadful Ravana, who had carried, away his wife Sita.

## \|\| 142.14-16 \|\|

*rakṣorājye ca saṃsthāpya sugrīvanumanmukhaiḥ \|*  
*āruhya puṣpakaṃ sārdhaṃ sītayā patibhaktayā \|\| 14 \|\|*

*lakṣmaṇenānukūlena hyayodhyāṃ svapurīṃ gataḥ \|*  
*rājyaṃ cakāra devādīnpālayāmāsa sa prajāḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*dharmasaṃrakṣaṇaṃ cakre hyaśvamedhādikānkratūn \|*  
*sā mahīpatinā reme rāmeṇaiva yathāsukham \|\| 16 \|\|*

14-16. After the fall of Ravana, Rama installed Vibhlsana, a brother of Ravana, on the throne of his kingdom Lanka, and returned to his own capital in the aerial car, Puspaka, in the company of Hanumana, Sugrlva and his faithful Sita. In the bliss of his consort's love, Rama ruled his kingdom for the good of his people and the gods, and performed a Horse-Sacrifice to commemorate his suzerainty over the earth.

## \|\| 142.17-18 \|\|

*rāvaṇasya gṛhe sītā sthitā bheje na rāvaṇam \|*  
*karmaṇā manasā vācā sā gatā rāghavaṃ sadā \|\| 17 \|\|*

*pativratā tu sā sītā hyanasūyā yathaiva tu \|*  
*pativratāyā māhātmyaṃ śṛṇu tvaṃ kathayāmyaham \|\| 18 \|\|*

17-18. Sita, though passed a long time in the house of Ravana, did not betray his lord either in deeds or thoughts. Sita was as chaste as the virtuous Anasuya, the beloved wife of Atri. Now hear me narrate the excellence of Sid's chastity and the exalted station which virtuous and faithful wives occupy in the ecomy of the universe.

## \|\| 142.19 \|\|

*kauśiko brāhmaṇaḥ kuṣṭhī pratiṣṭhāne 'bhavatpurā \|*  
*taṃ tathā vyādhitaṃ bhāryā patiṃ devamivārcayat \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Once on a time there lived in the city of Pratisthana, a leper Brahmana whose name was Kausika. His wife, who was firmly devoted to him, used to adore and worship her lord as god without even thinking for a moment that he was afficited with such a foul and loathsome disease. But Kausika was a cross and peevish husband, and never missed opportunities to abuse his wife, who though often chastised, never ceased to pay him god-like veneration and love. One day, Kausika took a fancy to visit a courtezan in the city, and expressed that desire to his wife. Whereupon she took him on her shoulders and safely carried him to that house of ill fame. Nor did she gorget to take with her a considerable amount of money which the courtezan might ask of her nefarious trade.

## \|\| 142.20-23 \|\|

*nirbhartsitāpi bhartāraṃ tamamanyata daivatam \|*  
*bhartroktā sānayadveśyāṃ śulkamādāya cādhikam \|\| 20 \|\|*

*pathi sūle tadā protamacauraṃ cauraśaṅkayā \|*  
*māṇḍavyamatiduḥ khārtamandhakāre 'tha sa dvijaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*patnīskandhasamārūḍhaścālayāmāsa kauśikaḥ \|*  
*pādāvamarśaṇatkruddho māṇḍavyastamuvāca ha \|\| 22 \|\|*

*sūryodaye mṛtistasya yenāhaṃ cālitaḥ padā \|*  
*tacchrutvā prāha tadbhāryā sūryo nodayameṣyati \|\| 23 \|\|*

20-23. Now it happened that the Sage Mandavya was then undergoing punishment on the top of a pointed mace, as he was unjustly sentenced by the authorities on a false charge of theft. The faithful wife, on her way to the house of the courtezen, touched with her feet the body of that afflicted sage, who, is his agony, cursed her with the pangs of widowhood on the break of day. The wife, on the other hand, forbade the Sun to rise in order that the curse of the Sage might not take effect. The Sun-God, overpowered by the energy of conjugal chastity, was afraid to show his face, and creation was enshrouded in a pall of darkness.

## \|\| 142.24-27 \|\|

*tataḥ sūryodayābhāvāda bhavatsatataṃ niśā \|*  
*bahūnyabdapramāṇāni tato devā bhayaṃ yayuḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*brahmāṇaṃ śaraṇaṃ jagmustāmūce padmasambhavaḥ \|*  
*praśāmyate tejasaiva tapastejastvanena vai \|\| 25 \|\|*

*pativratāyā māhātmyānnodgacchati divākaraḥ \|*  
*tasya cānudayāddhānirmartyānāṃ bhavatāṃ tathā \|\| 26 \|\|*

*tasmātpativratāmatreranasūyāṃ tapasvinīm \|*  
*prasādayata vai patnīṃ bhānorudayakāmyayā \|\| 27 \|\|*

24-27. Ages past without the Sun in the sky. The frightened gods resorted to Brahma for help and advice. Brahma said, "It is the energy of chastity that has overpowed the energy of asceticism, and obstructed the advent of the Sun.

## \|\| 142.28 \|\|

*taiḥ sā prasāditā gatvā hyanasūyā pativratā \|*  
*kṛtvādityodayaṃ sā ca taṃ bhartāramajīvayat \|*  
*pativratānasūyāyāḥ sītābhūdadhikā kila \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Go, ye gods, to Anasuya, and she will plead, on your behalf, to the wife of Kausika." The gods did as Dev were told to do. The gods propitiated Anasuya, the grant Pativrad of that time. She was pleased and went to the wife of Kausika to request her for the rise of the sun. and honoured by Anasuya for piousness of Sun. The wife of Kausika when requested by Ansuya and promised that by the rise of the sun her husband will not die as cursed by Mandaya. Then there was Suryodaya in the sky and her husband Kausika was also alive. Sid was very much loved and honoured by Anasuya for piousness of SIta.

Rama being victorious married the daughter of Janaka. Laksmana married Urmila and Bharata was married with Madvl as well as Sati ughna was married to 3rutakirti, both daughter of Kusdhvaja then along with parents all the sons accompanied with their wives went to Ayodhya and enjoyed the life. 8-9. And Shatrughna went with him to his Capital. In the meantime king Dasaratha decided. О appoint Rams as Yuvaraja of Ayodhya to install his favourite Rama as the Crown-Prince of his dominion, when his consort Kaikeyl asked him to send Rama in exile for a period of fourteen years.

## \|\| 143.10-11 \|\|

*caturdaśasamāvāso vanerāmasya vāñchitaḥ \|*

10-11. For the spiritual edification of his father, Rama renounced the kingdom as a thing of little consequence and went out as a voluntary exile, in the company of his beloved Sita and Laksmana, to the city of 3rngabera. He renounced the use of his car, and travelled on foot to the city of Prayaga from whence he sojourned to the Mount of Citrakuta.

## \|\| 143.12 \|\|

*rāmasya tu viyogena rājā svargaṃ samāśritaḥ \|*

12\. King Dasaratha, in agony of separation and in bitter remorse for what he had done, died and ascended to heaven. Prince Bharata performed the funeral rites of his father Dasaratha, and then went to Rama with a large army to welcome him back to his kingdom and heritage.

## \|\| 143.13 \|\|

14\. Whereupon Bharata justly ruled the kingdom in the name of his sovereign Rama. Thus dismissed by Rama, Bharata did not return to Ayodhya, but fixed his residence in the town of Nandigrama, while Rama thereafter sojourned to the hermitage of Atri from the Mount Citrakuta.

## \|\| 143.15-16 \|\|

*rāmo 'pi citrakūṭācca hyatrerāśramamāyayau \|*

*nikṛtya karṇo nāse ca rāmeṇāthāpavāritā \|\| 16 \|\|*

15-16. Thence having made obeisance to Sutiks na and Agastya, Rama entered the forest of Dandaka, where the Monstress 6urpanakha attempted to devour (Sita). Rama disgraced her by cutting her ears and clipping away her nose.

## \|\| 143.17 \|\|

*tatpreritaḥ kharaścāgāddūṣaṇastriśirāstathā \|*

17\. Thus disfigurede and insulted, Shurpanakha prevailed upon the Monsters Khara, Dusana, and Trsira to attack Rama simultaneously from three different sides. The three Raksasa heroes, with an army of fourteen thousand Raksasa soldiers drawn up in a battle array, attacked Rama in battle.

## \|\| 143.18 \|\|

*rāmo 'pi preṣayāmāsa bāṇairyamapurañca tān \|*

18\. But Rama with the help of his deadly shafts, consigned them all to the mansion of death. Ravana, through the investigation of this RaksasI (6urpanakha), resolved to carry away SIta by fraud.

## \|\| 143.19-20 \|\|

*mṛgarūpaṃ sa mārīcaṃ kṛtvāgre 'tha tridaṇḍadhṛk \|*

*mriyamāṇaḥ sa ca prāha hā sīte ! lakṣmaṇoti ca \|*

19-20. And for that end, he despatched before him a Raksasa named Marlca to lure away Rama in the forest in the magic guise of a golden stag. Site entreated Rama to chase the golden deer and to secure that golden query for her. Rama chased and killed that magic deer with his arrow, and the disguised Monster expired shouting, "Help, О SIta, help, О Laksmana!" Laksmana importunated by SIta, ran to the rescue of Rama, and beheld him in the forest.

## \|\| 143.21 \|\|

*uvāca rākṣasī māyā nūnaṃ sītā hṛteti saḥ \|*

21\. Rama said, "O Brother, these are the wicked charms which the Raksasas practise in this dense and lonely forest, and surely they have carried away SIta by fraud." In the meantime, Ravana appeared before the cottage of Rama, and carried away the beloved bride of Rama vainly struggling on his lap.

## \|\| 143.22 \|\|

*jaṭāyuṣaṃ vinirbhidya yayau laṅkāṃ tato balī \|*  
*aśokavṛkṣacchāyāyāṃ rakṣitāṃ tāmadhārayat \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. The mighty Jatayu, the king of the birds, assailed the dark souled miscreant on the way, but Ravana was more than a match for him. So in the battle that ensued Ravana completely detated the bird-king Jatayu, and returned victor with his beautiful prize to his capital at Lanka, and kept her well gurded in a shady garden of Asoka trees.

## \|\| 143.23 \|\|

*āgatya rāmaḥ sūnyāñca parṇaśālāṃ dadarśa ha \|*  
*śokaṃ kṛtvātha jānakyā mārgaṇaṃ kṛtavānprabhuḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Rama and Laksmana returned to their forestretreat, their hearts foreboding all sorts of dire mishaps, and found it lonely and deserted. Oh, the first stifled sobs of widowed love that almost broke the all-conquering soul is called Pddaddha of Rama in their repression! Laksmana wept like a child in the first gloom of a dire calamity in which suspense metamor- phises itself into a torrid noon of burning shame, and a robust stream of molten affection suddenly broke forth, in his heart, into a deathless volcano of vengeance of retaliation,for the consummation of which all eternity expanded its bloated bosom and hypothecated itself to the prospective realisa-tion of that spiritual wrath. Rama and Laksmana followed the rail of their stolen goddess-sombre and ominous like a summer thunder cloud.

## \|\| 143.24 \|\|

*jaṭāyuṣañca saṃskṛtya tadukto dakṣiṇāṃ diśam \|*

24\. On and on they went, weary and footsore, and traversed many a mile of that sylvan solitude when they stumbled upon the wounded body of the brave though dying Jalayu. That gallant bird king narrated the whole history of SIta's forcible carrying away by the benighted Ravana, and breathed his last in the presence of the divine brothers (Rama and Laksmana). They collected the cast off leaves and twigs of the forest, exhumed the dead body of the godly Jatayu, performed the last earthly rites to his mortal remains, and trended their way to the South.

## \|\| 143.25 \|\|

*sapta tālānvinirbhidya śareṇānataparvaṇā \|*

25\. While there, Rama entered into a friendly compact with Sugrlva, the brother of the monkeyking Vali, and showed his skill in archery by shooting through the trunks of seven Tala trees. Then he killed Vali and made over the sovereignity of the monkey-land Kiskindha to his brother Sugriva.

## \|\| 143.26-28 \|\|

*sugrīvaṃ kṛtavānrāma ṛśyamūke svayaṃ sthitaḥ \|*

*sītāyā mārgaṇaṃ kartuṃ pūrvādyāśāsu sotsavān \|*

26-28. And quartered himself with his beloved Laksmana in the outskirts of the Mount Rsyamuka. Then Sugriva commissioned the leaders of his monkey-troops to search for SIta in all directions, and the huge monkey-generals, with their bodies mountain high, went out north, south, east and west in quest of the sunny bride of the solar race. In vain did they search every stream or river bank, hill or dale, forest or hamlet, and at last while deliberating suicide in despair they saw Sampan.

## \|\| 143.29 \|\|

*jānakīnte hyapaśyanto maraṇe kṛtaniścayāḥ \|*

29\. Hanuman, the greatest of the monkey generals, having got the information from Sampan, leapt over the sea, which is hundreds of miles wide, wide, and forms the abode of monsters.

## \|\| 143.30-31 \|\|

*śatayojanavistīrṇaṃ pupluve makarālayam \|*

30-31. Не saw the lovely JanakI imprisoned in the forest of Asoka trees, chastised by its female guards who had been pressing her hard to share the bed of Ravana, and harshly rousing her up from her revery of Rama's company.

*aṅgulīyaṃ kapirdattvā sītāṃ kauśalyamabravīt \|*

*yathā rāmo nayecchīghraṃ tathā vācyaṃ tvayā kape \|*

*hatvākṣaṃ rākṣasāṃścānyānbandhanaṃ svayamāgataḥ \|*  
*sarvairindrajito bāṇairdṛṣṭvā rāvaṇamabravīt \|\| 35 \|\|*

32-37. The monkey-general dropped down to SIta the signet ring of Rams, and asked her about her health. "Do not be dejected, О Maithill," observed that gallant monkey, but rather give me something of yours which my master RAM might cherish as a sweet mement of love. Do nor be frightened, О Maithill, for I am the servant of Rama. Whereupon SIta unfastened a jewel from her chignanon, made it over to Hanuman, and asked him to request Rama to succour her immediately after his return to Rama's residence (at Rsyamuka). Hanumaa gladly ascented to her request, and thereafter began to destroy the pleasure garden of Ravana, killing prince Aksa and many a Raksasa soldier in the act. A Brahmastra cast by Indrajita hit him hard and left him a captive in the hands of Raksasas, who dragged him in fetters to the presence of Ravana. Hanuman said, "I am a servant of Rama. Return to him, О miscreant, his faithful Maithill. Ravana, madly infuriated by these observations ordered to burn the tail of the monkey general, and Hanuman, by wildly lashing his burning tail against the thatched roofs of Lanka, instantaneously set the whole city on fire. Having consumed Lanka with fire, then monkeygeneral returned to the side of Rama and reported to him of his having eaten mango and of the general conflagration that broke out in Rama through his own instrumentality.

## \|\| 143.38-40 \|\|

*jagdhvā phalaṃ madhuvane dṛṣṭā sītatyavedayat \|*

*sasugrīvaḥ sa hanumānsāṃgadaśca salakṣmaṇaḥ \|*  
*vibhīṣaṇo 'pi samprāptaḥ śaraṇaṃ rāghavaṃ prati \|\| 39 \|\|*

*laṅkaiśvaryeṣvabhyaṣiñcadrāmastaṃ rāvaṇānujam \|*

38-40. He made over to him the head gem of SIta, and Rama with Laksmana, Hanuman and his monkey-army with its generals and officers, marched in the direction of Lanka. Meanwhile Vibhlsana sighted by his brother Ravana, went over to Rama's side and made a common cause with him. After that, Rama caused a bridge to be built across the ocean with the help of the monkey-general Nala, and crossed over with his whole army and officers to the Isle of Lanka.

## \|\| 143.41-45 \|\|

*suvelāvasthitaścaiva purīṃ laṅkāṃ dadarśaha \|*

*dhūmradhūmrākṣavīrendrā jāmbavatpramukhāstadā \|*  
*maindadvividamukhyāste purīṃ laṅkāṃ babhañjire \|\| 42 \|\|*

*vidyujjihvañca dhūmrākṣaṃ devāntakanarānta kau \|*  
*mahodaramahāpārśvāvatikāyaṃ mahābalam \|\| 44 \|\|*

*kumbhaṃ nikumbhaṃ mattañca makarākṣaṃ hyakampanam \|*

41-45. He viewed the splendid prospect of the Island from the summit of the Hill Suvela, where he fixed his quarter for the day. Then the monkeygenerals Nila, Angada, Nala, Dhuma, Dhomraksa, Jambavana, Munda, Dvividha and others set to demolish the fortifications of the city (Lanka) and killed many leaders of the Raksasa-army. Rama and Laksmana destroyed, with the help of their monkey-army,-many an eminent Raksasa hero of gigantic stature and black as the sable collyrium of death, such as Vidyut- jihva, Dhumraksa, Devantaka, Narantaka, Mahodara, Mahaparsva, Atikaya, Kumbha, Nikumbha, Matta, Makaraksa, and Akampana.

## \|\| 143.46 \|\|

*rāvaṇiṃ lakṣmaṇo 'cchinta hyastrādyai rāghavo balī \|*  
*nikṛtya bāhucakrāṇi rāvaṇantu nyapātayan \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. After that, Laksmana defeated and killed in a single combat, the redoubtable Indrajita, and Rama having severed with his arrows the twenty arms of Ravana, subsequently killed him in battle.

## \|\| 143.47 \|\|

*sītāṃ śuddhāṃ gṛhītvātha vimāne puṣpake sthitaḥ \|*  
*savānaraḥ samāyāto hyayodhyāṃ pravarāṃ purīm \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Sita gave ample proof of her chastity, and came unscathed out of an Ordeal of Fire. SIta, thus purified by Fire, ascended the aeriel car with her beloved consort, and the whole monkey-army, jubilant, and elated with victory, followed its gracious leader to his capital at Ayodhya.

## \|\| 143.48 \|\|

*tatra rājyaṃ cakārātha puttravatpālayanprajāḥ \|*  
*daśāśvamedhānāhṛtya gayāśirasi pātanam \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. Rama ruled the country for eleven thousand years, and protected his subjects with paternal love and care. He undertook and accomplished the celebration of ten Horse Sacrifices in succession, and offered oblations to his departed manes at the shrine of Gaya-sirsa.

## \|\| 143.49-51 \|\|

*piṇḍānāṃ vidhivatkṛtvā dattvā dānāni rāghavaḥ \|*  
*putrau kuśalavau dṛṣṭvā tau ca rājye 'bhyaṣecayat \|\| 49 \|\|*

*ekādaśasahasrāṇi rāmo rājyamakārayat \|*  
*śatrughno lavaṇaṃ jaghne śailūṣaṃ bhatastataḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

*agastyādīnmunīnnatvā śrutvotpattiñca rakṣasām \|*  
*svargaṃ gato janaiḥ sārdhamayodhyāsthaiḥ kṛtārthakaḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

49-51. He was blessed with two sons named Lava and Kusa. It was in his reign that the holy Sage Bharata first organised dramatic performances, and Satrughna killed the demon Lavana. Rama heard the origin of the Raksasas narrated to him by the holy Agastya. Having made over the sovereignty to his sons Lava and Kusa, Rama made his exit from the world at the close of a glorious though chequered life, dedicated exclusively to the furtherance of good therein.

## Chapter 144

## \|\| 144.1-2 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*harivaṃśaṃ pravakṣyāmi kṛṣṇamāhātmyamuttamam \|*  
*vasudevāttu devakyāṃ vāsudevo balo 'bhavat \|\| 1 \|\|*

*dharmādirakṣaṇārthāya hyadharmādivinaṣṭaye \|*  
*kṛṣṇaḥ pītvā stanau gāḍhaṃ pūtanāmanayatkṣayam \|\| 2 \|\|*

1-2. Brahma said: — Now I shall narrate the family history of Hari which teems with the his sanctified exploits of Krsna. Vasudeva begot Krsna and Baladeva on the person of Devaki for the edification on the righteous and annihilation of the wicked. The eternal God was incarnated on this mortal globe in the shape of Krsna. The Monstress Putana was engaged by the tyrant Kamsa to put an end to his life, in infancey, with the pretext of suckling him.

## \|\| 144.3 \|\|

*śakaṭaḥ parivṛtto 'tha bhagnau ca yamalārjunau \|*  
*damitaḥ kāliyo nāgo dhenuko vinipātitaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. But Krsna sucked her poisoned nipples with a force that verily killed her on the spot. The mighty prowessed Krsna overturned the cardemon, felled the two tree-monsters named Yamala and Arjuna, and destroyed the serpent Kallya and the moster Dhenuka.

## \|\| 144.4-5 \|\|

*dhṛto govardhanaḥ śaila indreṇa paripūjitaḥ \|*  
*bhārāvataraṇaṃ cakre pratijñāṃ kṛtavānhariḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*rakṣaṇāyārjunādeśca hyariṣṭādirnipātitaḥ \|*  
*keśī vinihato daityo gopādyāḥ paritoṣitāḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. At this time, he supported the mount Govardhana on the tip of his finger, and was honoured and worshipped by the God Indra for this exploits. He relieved this sinful earth of its weight of sin, and pledged himself to protect the five sons of Pandu in their days of trouble and distress. The demon Arista fell an easy victim to his prowess, and he cheered the Gopas and Gopa-maidens of Bmdavqanby slaying the monster KesL

## \|\| 144.6-8 \|\|

*cāṇūro muṣṭiko mallaḥ kaṃso mañcānnipātitaḥ \|*  
*rukmiṇīsatyabhāmādyāḥ hyaṣṭau patnyo hareḥ parāḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*ṣoḍhaśa strīsahasrāṇi hyanyānyāsa mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*tāsāṃ putrāśca pautrādyāḥ śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*rukmiṇyāñcaiva pradyumno nyavadhīcchaṃbarañca yaḥ \|*  
*tasya putro 'niruddho 'bhūduṣābāṇasutāpatiḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

6-8. He dragged do the demon Kamsa from the platform, and killed the wrestlers Canura, Mustika and Malla, who guarded the person of that detestable tyrant. Krsna had eight principal wives, such as RukminI, Satyabhama, etc., besides a seraglio of sixteen thousand other wives. By them he got hundreds, and thousands of sons and grandsons. By RukminI he' had a son named Pradyumna, who killed the demon 3ambara. The son of Pradyumna was Aniruddha, who married Use, the daughter of king Bona.

## \|\| 144.9 \|\|

*hariśakarayoryatra mahāyuddhaṃ babhūva ha \|*  
*bāṇabāhusahasrañca cchinnaṃ bāhudvayaṃ hyabhūt \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. There ensued a deadly conflict between Krsna and the God Sankara, when the elopement of Usa with Aniruddha was detected and made known to the world. Krsna cut down the thousand army of king Bana with the exeption of two.

## \|\| 144.10 \|\|

*narako nihato yena pārijātaṃ jahāra yaḥ \|*  
*balaśca śisupālaśca hataśca dvividaḥ kapiḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Once upon a time, he killed the demon Naraka and carried the flower Parijata from the garden of heaven. Shisupala, Bala, and the monkey, named Dvibida, were also among the victims, who fell at the stroke of his mighty discus.

## \|\| 144.11 \|\|

*aniruddhādabhūdvajraḥ sa ca rājā gate harau \|*  
*sandīpaniṃ guruñcakre saputrañca cakāra saḥ \|*  
*mathurāyāṃ cograsenaṃ pālanaṃ ca divaukasām \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. The son of Aniruddha was Vajra, who become the king of Mathura, when Krsna as translated to heaven. In order to please his preceptor Sandlpani, Krsna brought back the soul of his son from the mansion of death, and brought back to life the son of that holy sage. For the furtherance of the divine cause, he installed Ugrasena as king on the throne of Mathura.

## Chapter 145

## \|\| 145.1 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*bhārataṃ saṃpravakṣyāmi bhārāvataraṇaṃ bhuvaḥ \|*  
*cakre kṛṣṇo yudhyamānaḥ pāṇḍavādinimittataḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Brahma said: — Now hear me narrate the story of the Mahabharatam. It is so called (Bharatam) from the fact of Krsna's espousing the. cause the Pardavas in battle, for relieving the earth of its weight of sin (Bhubhara).

## \|\| 145.2 \|\|

*viṣṇunābhyabjato brahmā brahmaputro 'triratritaḥ \|*  
*somastato budhastasmādilāyāṃ ca purūravāḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Brahma sprang out of the lotus navel of Hari. The son of Brahma was Atri. The son of Atri was the Moon-God, and in the line that sprang from him was born Purtra.

## \|\| 145.3 \|\|

*tasyāyustatra vaṃśe 'bhūdyayātirbharataḥ kuruḥ \|*  
*śantanustasya vaṃśe 'bhūdgaṅgāyāṃ śantanoḥ sutaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Pururava begot on the nymph UrvasI a son, named Ayu. Yayati, Bharata, Kuru, and Santanu were of the race of Ayu. The divinely wise Bhis ma was the son of Shantanu by his wife Gang.

## \|\| 145.4-5 \|\|

*bhīṣmaḥ sarvaguṇaiyukto brahmavaivartapāragaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*śantanoḥ satyavatyāṃ ca dvau putrau saṃbabhūvatuḥ \|*  
*citrāṅgadantu gandharvaḥ putraṃ citrāṅgado 'vadhīt \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. This Snntanu had two other sons named Citrangada and Vicitravlrya by his wife Satyavatl. This Citrangada was killed in battle by a Gandharva of the same name.

## \|\| 145.6 \|\|

*anyo vicitravīryo 'bhūtkāśīrājasutāpatiḥ \|*  
*vicitravīrye svaryāte vyāsāttatkṣetrato 'bhavat \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. The second son Vicitravlrya married Ambika and Ambalika, the daughters of the king of Kasl. After the death of Vicitravlrya, the holy Vyasa begot sons on the wives of Vicitravlrya.

## \|\| 145.7-9 \|\|

*dhṛtarāṣṭo 'mbikāputraḥ pāṇḍurāmbālikāsutaḥ \|*  
*bhujiṣyāyāntu viduro gāndhāryāṃ dhṛtarāṣṭrataḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*duryodhanapradhānāstu śatasaṃkhyā mahābalāḥ \|*  
*pāṇḍoḥ kuntyāñca mādyāṃ ca pañca putrāḥ prajajñire \|\| 8 \|\|*

*yudhiṣṭhiro bhīmaseno hyarjuno nakulastathā \|*  
*sahadevaśca pañcaite mahābalaparākramāḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

7-9. Ambika became the mother of Dhrtarastra; Ambalika, of Pandu; and Bhujisya of Vidura. Dhrtarastra had a hundred sons by his wife Gandharl such as Duryodhana, etc., while the five sons who were begotten on KuntI and Madri, the two wives of Pandu, were Yudhisthira, Bhlm, Arjuna, Nakala and Sahadeva.

## \|\| 145.10 \|\|

*kurupāṇḍavayorvairaṃ daivayo gādbabhūva ha \|*  
*duryodhanenādhīreṇa pāṇḍavāḥ samupadrutāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. By a preordinance of fate there sprang up a bitter animosit between the Kurus (sons of Dhrtarastra) and the Pandva (sons of Pandu). Duryodhana, a man of fickle temperament and unstable principles, was not slow to devise means for harrassing the Pandavas.

## \|\| 145.11 \|\|

*dagdhā jatugṛhe vīrāste muktāḥ svadhiyāmalāḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. He attempted to kill them by burning them down in a house of shellac.

## \|\| 145.12 \|\|

*tatastadekacakrāyāṃ brāhmaṇasya niveśane \|*  
*viviśuste mahātmāno nihatya bakarākṣasam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. The guileless Pandavas, saved through the merit of their faith and innocence, sojourned to the village of Ekacakra, and took shelter in the house of a Brahmana. These mighty Pandavas stayed for a while in the house of that Brahmana, and while there, the redoubtable Bhlmasena killed the monster Baka.

## \|\| 145.13 \|\|

*tataḥ pāñcālaviṣayedraupadyāste svayaṃvaram \|*  
*vijñāya vīryaśulkāntāṃ pāṇḍavā upayemire \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Thence they went to the country of Pancala and married Draupadi, the princess of that country, whose hands had to be on by a competition in skilful archery, and by showing matchless proficiency in that art.

## \|\| 145.14 \|\|

*droṇabhīṣmānumatyā tu dhṛtarāṣṭraḥ samānayat \|*
