*rūkṣamya snedṛnaṃ kāryamabhisnigdhasya rūkṣaṇam \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Measures calculated to restore the deranged Vayu to its normal condition should be resorted to with the help of any emulsivesubstance in respect of patients of good diges tive capacity. Diaphoretic measures should be employed in respect of person of extremely parched temperament, while parchifying measures should be adapted in cases of over-dose of an oil or Ghrtam.

## \|\| 173.33 \|\|

*śyāmākakoradoṣānnatakrapiṇyākasakubhiḥ \|*  
*vātaśleṣmāṇi vāte vā kaphe vā sveda iṣyate \|*  
*na svedayedatimthūlarūkṣadurvalamūrchitān \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. A compound of Samaka, Koradusa, or boiled rice, or Pinyakam, pasted with whey and made warm, should be used in fomenting the body of the patient, in diseases of the deranged Vayu and Kapham, or in those of the deranged Vayu, or in those of the deranged Kapham. Extremely corpulent, or weak patients, as well as those of parched temperament, or suffering form epileptic fits should not be fomented at all.

## Chapter 174

## \|\| 174.1-2 \|\|

*dhanvatariruvāca \|*  
*ghṛtatailādi vakṣyāmi śṛṇu suśruta roganut \|*  
*śaṅkhapuṣpī vacā somā brāhmī brahmasuvarcalā \|\| 1 \|\|*

*abhayā ca guḍūcī ca aṭarūpakavāgujī \|*  
*etairakṣasamairbhāgairghṛtaprasthaṃ vipācayet \|\| 2 \|\|*

1-2. Dhanvantari said: — Hear me, О Susruta, who art well conversent with the nature of diseases, discourse on the preparations and efficacies of different medicinal oils and Ghrtas. Cook a Prastha measure of clarified butter with an Aksa measure of each of the following drugs, viz., Shankhapuspl, Vaca, Soma, Brahml, Brahma, Suvarcala, Abhaya, GuducI, Ataru- saka and Vaguci, in combination with a Prastha measure of the expressed juice of Kantakari and the same quantity of milk.

## \|\| 174.3-4 \|\|

*kaṇṭakāryā rasaprasthakṣīraprasthamamanvitam \|*  
*etadbrāhmīghṛtaṃ nāma śrutimedhākaraṃ param \|\| 3 \|\|*

*triphalācitrakabalānirguṇḍī nimbavāsakāḥ \|*  
*punarnavā guḍūcī ca bṛhatī ca śatāvarī \|\| 4 \|\|*

3-4. This Ghrtam is called Brahml Ghrtam. It improves the intellect and memory. Cook a Ghrtam with Triphala, Citrakam, Vala, Nirgundi, Nimba, Vasaka, Punamava, GuducI, the two kinds of Vrhatl and Shatavari, or with as many of them as are available.

## \|\| 174.5-6 \|\|

*etairghṛtaṃ yathālābhaṃ sarvarogavimardanam \|*  
*balāśatakaṣāye tu tailasyārdhāḍhakaṃ pacet \|*  
*kalkairmadhūkamañjiṣṭhācandanotpalapadmakaiḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*sūkṣmailāpippalīkuṣṭhatvagelāgurukesaraiḥ \|*  
*gandhāśvajīvanīyaiśca kṣīrāḍhakasamāśritam \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. This Ghrtam may be used with benefit in all forms of disease. Cook half an Adakam of oil with a decoction of a hundred Valas and a paste of Madhukam, Mafiji$tha, Candana, Utpalam, Padmakam, Suk$maila, Pippall, Ku$tham, Tvak, Ela, Aguru, Kesara, ASva- gandha, and drugs of the Jivanlya group, cook it over a gentle fire, and keep it in a silver pitcher after cooking.

## \|\| 174.7-9 \|\|

*etanmṛdvagninā pakvaṃ sthāpayedrājate śubhe \|*  
*sarvavātavikārāṃstu sarvadhātvantarāśrayān \|\| 7 \|\|*

*tailametatpraśamayedvalyākyaṃ rājavallabham \|*  
*śatāvarīrasaprasthaṃ kṣīraprasthaṃ tathaiva ca \|\| 8 \|\|*

*śatapuṣpaṃ devadāru māṃsī śaileyakaṃ balā \|*  
*candanaṃ tagaraṃ kuṣṭaṃ manaḥ śilā jyotiṣmatī \|\| 9 \|\|*

7-9. This Ghrtam, which is named as Rajaballabham, proves highly efficacious in all diseases of the deranged Vayu, no matter what fundamental principle of the organism it might have affected, as well as in diseases of the deranged Kapham. Cook a Prastha measure of clarified butter with a Prashtha measure of the expressed juice of Satavari and a Prastha measure of milk, as well as with the addition of the paste of a Karsa of each of the followings drugs, viz., Shatapu?pa, Devadaru, Mimi, Saileyakam, Vale, Vala and Tagaram.

## \|\| 174.10-12 \|\|

*etaiḥ karṣasamaiḥ kalkaiḥ ghṛtaprasthaṃ vipācayet \|*  
*kuvjavāmanapaṅgūnāṃ badhiravyaṅgakuṣṭhinām \|\| 10 \|\|*

*vāyunā bhagnagātrāṇāṃ ye ca sīdanti maithune \|*  
*jarājarjaragātrāṇāṃ cādhmānamukha śoṣiṇām \|\| 11 \|\|*

*tvaggatāścāpi ye vātā śirāsnāyugatāśca ye \|*  
*sarvāṃstānnāśayatyāśu tailaṃ rogakulāntakam \|\| 12 \|\|*

10-12. Hanchbacks, dwarfs, maimed persons, deaf ones, or those suffering from Vyanga or Kustham, as well as those who suffer from distortions of limbs in consequence of the enargement of the bodily Vayu, or meet disappointment during the middle part of an act of sexual congress, persons suffering from the imbecilities, of old age, or from tympanites or dryness of the mouth, or from diseases affecting the skin, veins and ligaments have got a splendid remedy in this Narayana Pailam, the killer of all diseases, the recipe of which was formerly disclosed by Visnu himself.

## \|\| 174.13-15 \|\|

*nārāyaṇamidaṃ tailaṃ viṣṇunoktaṃ rugardanam \|*  
*pṛthaktailaṃ ghṛtaṃ kuryātsamastairauṣadhaiḥ pṛthak \|\| 13 \|\|*

*śatāvaryā guḍūcyā vā citrakai gocanānvitaiḥ \|*  
*nirguṇḍyā vā prasāraḥ syātkaṇṭakāryā rasādibhiḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*varṣābhūvālayā vāpi vāsakana phalatrikaiḥ \|*  
*brāhayā caigṇḍakenāpi bhṛṅgarājena kuṣṭinā \|\| 15 \|\|*

13-15. Oils or Ghrtas may be separately cookes in admixture with each of the following drugs, viz. Satavari, GuducI, Citrakam, VyoSa, Nimba, the expressed juice of Nirgundl, PrarinI, or Kantakarl, Var§abhu, Vala, Vasaka, Phala- trikam, Brahml, Eranda, Yasthika, Bhrngaraja, Musal, Dagamulam, Khadira and Vata.

## \|\| 174.16-19 \|\|

*musalyā daśamūlena khadireṇa vaṭādibhiḥ \|*  
*vaṭikā modako vāpi cūrṇa syātsarvaroganut \|\| 16 \|\|*

*ghṛtena madhunā vāpi adbhiḥ khaṇḍaguḍādibhiḥ \|*  
*lavaṇaiḥ kaṭukairyuktaṃ yathālābhaṃ ca geganut \|\| 17 \|\|*

*citrakārkatrivṛdvāpi yavānīhayamārakam \|*  
*sudhāṃ ca bālāṃ gaṇikāṃ saptaparṇasuvarcikām \|\| 18 \|\|*

*jyotiṣmatīñca saṃbhṛtya tailaṃ dhīro vipācayet \|*  
*etanniṣyandanaṃ tailaṃ bhṛśaṃ dadyādbhagandare \|\| 19 \|\|*

16-19. Confection, pills, or pulverised compounds of the foregoing drugs, taken with honey, sugar, and clarified butter, or with water, prove curative in all diseases. The intelligent one should cook a medicinal oil in combination with Citrakam, Trivrt, Patha, Malapum, Haya- marakam, Sudha, Vaca, Langalakim, Sapta- parnam, Suvarcika, and Jyotismali. This oil is called Syandanam Tailam and should be employed for the purpose of asepsising and healing ulcers, and especially in fistula in ano.

## \|\| 174.20-22 \|\|

*śodhanaṃ gepaṇaṃ caiva sarvavarṇakaraṃ param \|*  
*citrakādyaṃ mahātailaṃ sarvarogaprabhañjanam \|\| 20 \|\|*

*ajamodaṃ sasindūraṃ haritālaṃ niśādvayam \|*  
*kṣāradvayaṃ phenayutamārdraka sara (śavaḥ lodbhavam \|\| 21 \|\|*

*indravāruṇyapāmārgakadalaiḥ syandanaiḥ samam \|*  
*ebhiḥ sarṣapajaṃ tailamajāmūtraiścayojitam \|\| 22 \|\|*

20-22. The medicinal oil of great efficacy, which is called Citrakadyam Tailam, cures all diseases; cook mustard oil in combination with Ajamoda, Sindura, Haritalam, the two kinds of Nisa, the two kinds of Ksara, Phena, Ardrakam, Sarala, Indra-Varuni, Apamarga, Kadala and Kandala taken in equal parts with the addition of the usual quantity of goat's urine.

## \|\| 174.23-24 \|\|

*mṛdvagninā pacedetgavyakṣīreṇa saṃyutam \|*  
*ajamodādikaṃ tailaṃ gaṇḍamālāṃ vyapohati \|\| 23 \|\|*

*vidagdhastu pacetpakvaṃ caiva viśodhayet \|*  
*ropaṇaṃ mṛdubhāvaṃ ca tailenānena kārayet \|\| 24 \|\|*

23-24. This Tailam should be cooked over a gentle fire and with the admixture of cow-milk. The oil thus cooked and prepared is called Ajamoda Tailam, which proves highly efficacious in scrofula and scrofulous sores. It induces satisfactory suppuration in indurated or partially suppurated sores, and cleanse the suppurating ones. Healing, granulation and softening of ulcers may be brought.about with the help of this Ajamoda oil, which is one of the most efficacious of medicinal oils, and cures a host of bodily distempers.

## Chapter 175

## \|\| 175.1 \|\|

*rudra uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ dhanvantarirviṣṇuḥ suśrutādīnuvāca ha \|*  
*hariḥ punarharāyāha nānāyogānrugardanān \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Rudra said: — Thus the holy Dhanvantari, who is an incarnation of Visnu, discoursed on many a medicinal compound of infallible potency, which (Hari) formerly disclosed to Нага.

## \|\| 175.2 \|\|

*hariruvāca \|*  
*sarvajvareṣu prathamaṃ kāryaṃ śaṅkara laṅghanam \|*  
*kvathitodakapānaṃ ca tathā nirvātasevanam \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Hari said: — О Sankra, in all types of fever the patient should bemade to fast and kept in a room protected from the wind. Boiled water should be given to him for drink.

## \|\| 175.3 \|\|

*agnisvedājjvarāstvevaṃ nāśamāyāntihīśvara \|*  
*vātajvaraharaḥ kvātho guḍūcyā mustakena ca \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Dry formenatitons prove efficacious in all forms of fever; a decoction of Musta and Guduci proves antidotal to the Vataja type.

## \|\| 175.4 \|\|

*durālabhaiścaiva ghṛtaṃ pittajvaraharaḥ śṛṇu \|*  
*śuṇṭhīparpaṭamustaiśca bālakośīracandanaiḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. A decoction of Duralabha cures Pittaja fever, and hear that, a decoction of SunthI, Parpata, Musta, Valaka, Usira and Candana proves remedial in the same type.

## \|\| 175.5 \|\|

*sājyaḥ kvāthaḥ śleṣmajaṃ tu saśuṇṭhiḥ sadurālabhaḥ \|*  
*savālakaḥ sarvajjvaraṃ saśuṇṭhiḥ sahaparpaṭaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. A decoction of the 6unthi and Duralabha taken with ghrtam proves curative in the Kaphaja type or fever. A decoction of sunthi, Valakam and Prapatam proves curative in all forms of fever.

## \|\| 175.6 \|\|

*kirātatiktairnārīguḍūcīśuṇṭhimustakaiḥ \|*  
*pittajvaraharaḥ syācca śṛṇvanyaṃ yogamuttamam \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. A decoction of Takta, Eranda, Guduci, Sunthi, and Mustaka cures Pittaja fever; now hear me enumerate the other medicinal compounds of infallible efficacy.

## \|\| 175.7 \|\|

*vālakośīrapāṭhābhiḥ kaṇṭakārikamustakaiḥ \|*  
*jvaranucca kṛtaḥ kvāthastathā vai suradāruṇā \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. A decoction of Valaka, Usira, Patha, Kanta- kari, Mustaka, and Devadaru acts as a good febrifuge remedy.

## \|\| 175.8 \|\|

*dhanyākanimbamustānāṃ samadhuḥ sa tu śaṅkara \|*  
*paṭolapatrayuktastu guḍūcītriphalāyutaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. О Sаnкаrа, decoction of Dhanyakam, Nimba and Musta taken with honey, or a decoction of Triphala, GuducI, and Potola leaves, internally administered.

## \|\| 175.9-10 \|\|

*pīto 'khilajvaraharaḥ kṣudhākṛdvātanuttvidam \|*  
*harītakīpiplīnāmāmalīcitrakodbhavam \|\| 9 \|\|*

*cūrṇaṃ jvaraṃ ca kvathitaṃ dhānya (dhanyā) kośīrapaparpaṭaiḥ \|*  
*āmalakyā guḍūcyā ca madhuyuktaṃ sacandanam \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. Acts as an appetising, Vayu-subding, and febrifuge medicine. Powders of Harltaki, Pippall, Amala and Citrakam taken with a decoction of Dhanyakam, Usira and Parpatam, or a decoction of Amalaki, Gudcl, and Candanam taken with honey proves curative in all forms of fever.

## \|\| 175.11-13 \|\|

*samastajvaranucca syātsannipātaharaṃ śṛṇu \|*  
*haridrānimbatriphalāmustakairdevadāruṇā \|\| 11 \|\|*

*kaṣāyaṃ kaṭurohiṇyā sapaṭolaṃ sapatrakam \|*  
*tridoṣajvaranuccasyātpītaṃ tu kvathitaṃ jalam \|\| 12 \|\|*

*kaṇṭakāryā nāgarasya guḍūcyā puṣkareṇa ca \|*  
*jagdhvā nāgabalācūrṇaṃ śvasakāsādinudbhavet \|\| 13 \|\|*

11-13. No hear me, discourse on the medicinal compounds, which have the efficacy of subduing the Sannipatika forms of fever. A decoction of Haridra, Nimba, Triphala, Mustakam, Devadaru, Katurohini and Patola leaves destroys Sannipatika fever. Powders of Nagavala, taken with a decoction of GuducI, Puskara, Nagaram and Kantakarl subdues cough, asthma, etc. Hot water should be given for the alleviation of thirst in fever due to the action of the deranged Vayi and Kapham. Cooked 6ali rice reduced to the consistency of a soup, rice gruel, or Mudga soup should be given to a fever patient for the subsidence of fever.

## \|\| 175.14-15 \|\|

*kaphavātajvare deyaṃ jalamuṣṇaṃ pipāsine \|*  
*viśvaparpaṭakośīramustacandanasādhitam \|\| 14 \|\|*

*dadyātsuśītalaṃ vāri tṛṭchardijvaradāhanut \|*  
*bilvādipa pañcamūlasya kvāthaḥ syādvātike jvare \|\| 15 \|\|*

14-15. Water boiled with Visva, Parpatakam, Usira, and Candanam, and subsequently cooled down, should be given for the alleviation of fever thirst and vomiting. A decoction of the drugs of the Pancamulam group proves remedial to Vataja fever.

## \|\| 175.16 \|\|

*pācanaṃ pippalīmūlaṃ guḍṛcīviśvabheṣajam \|*  
*vātajvare tvayaṃ kvātho dattaḥ śāntikaraḥ paraḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. A decoction of Pippall-mulam, GuducI, and Visva-bhesajam conquers Vataja fever.

## \|\| 175.17 \|\|

*pittajvaraghnaḥ samadhuḥ kvāthaḥ parpaṭanimbayoḥ \|*  
*vidhāne kriyamāṇe 'pi ysaya saṃjñā na jāyate \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. A decoction of Nimba and Parpatakam, taken with honey, proves curative in Pittaja fever.

## \|\| 175.18 \|\|

*pādayostu lalāṭe vā dahellauhaśalākayā \|*  
*tiktā pāṭhā parpaṭāśca viśālā triphalā trivṛt \|*  
*sakṣīro bhedanaḥ kvāthaḥ sarvajvaraviśodhanaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. The forehead and soles of the feet of a fever patient, who can not be restored to consciousness even with the employment of ordinary restorative measures, should be cauterised with an iron rod. A purgative decoction consisting of Tikta, Patha, Parpata, Visala, Triphala, and Trivrt, taken with boiled milk, proves curative in all forms of fever.

## Chapter 176

## \|\| 176.1 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca \|*  
*saptarātrātprajāyante khalvāṭasya kacāḥ śubhāḥ \|*  
*dagdhahastidantalepātsājākṣīrarasāñjanāt \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. The Deity said: — Plasters of the ashes of elephant's tusks and Rasanjanam pasted with goat's milk and applied for seven days in succession, contribute to the growth of beards and mustachios.

## \|\| 176.2-3 \|\|

*bhṛṅgarājarasenaiva caturbhāgena sādhitam \|*  
*keśavṛddhikaraṃ tailaṃ guñjācūrṇānvitena ca \|\| 2 \|\|*

*elāmāṃsīkuṣṭhamurāyuktamabhyaṅgataḥ śivam \|*  
*guñjāphalaṃ samādeyaṃ lepanaṃ candraluptanut \|\| 3 \|\|*

2-3. Oil, cooked with its quarter part of the expressed juice of Bhrngaraja and Gunja helps the growth of hair. For the cure of baldness (alopacea), first rub the scalp with a paste of Ela, Mansi, Kustham, and Mura, and then apply a plaster of pasted Gunja berries over it..

## \|\| 176.4-5 \|\|

*āmrāsthicūrṇalepādvai keśāḥ sūkṣmā bhavanti ca \|*  
*karañjāmalakailālalākṣālepo 'ruṇāpahaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*āmrāsthimajjāmalakalepātkeśā bhavanti vai \|*  
*baddhamūlā ghanā dīrghāḥ snagdhāḥ syurnotpatanti ca \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. Applications of plasters of the powdered pulps of mongo stones impart a thickness and silky gloss to the hairs and prevent their falling off.

## \|\| 176.6-7 \|\|

*viḍaṅgagandhapāṣāṇasādhitaṃ tailamuttamam \|*  
*sacaturguṇagomūtraṃ manasaḥ śilameva vā \|\| 6 \|\|*

*śiro 'bhyaṅgācchirājanmayūkālikhyāḥ kṣayaṃ nayet \|*  
*navadagdhaṃ śaṅkhacūrṇaṃ ghṛṣṭasīsakalepitam \|\| 7 \|\|*

6-7. Anointment of the head with a medicinal oil cooked with Vidanga, Gandh-pasana, and Manah-Shila and with the admixuture of cow's urine, four times its own weight, destroys lice and dandruff. О thou bull-riding deity, applications of freshly burnt conch-shell powders mixed with rubbings of lead and water to the scalf impart a raven like blackness to the hair.

## \|\| 176.8-9 \|\|

*kacāḥ ślakṣṇā mahākṛṣṇā bhavanti vṛṣabhadhvaja \|*  
*bhṛṅgarājaṃ lohacūrṇaṃ triphalā bījapūrakam \|\| 8 \|\|*

*nīlī ca karavīraṃ ca guḍametaiḥ samaṃ śṛtam \|*  
*palitānīha kṛṣṇāni kuryāllepānmahauṣadham \|\| 9 \|\|*

8-9. A hair dye composed of Bhrngaraja, irondusts, Triphala, Vljapurakanl, Nil! and Karavlram boiled with an equal quantity of treacle make the grey hairs of old men black again.

## \|\| 176.10 \|\|

*āmrāsthimajjā triphalā nī (tā) lī ca bhṛṅga rājakam \|*  
*jīrṇaṃ pakvaṃ lohacūrṇaṃ kāñjikaṃ kṛṣṇakeśakṛt \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Pulps of mango-stones, Triphala, NIlI, Bhrngaraja, steel-powders, dissolved in Kanjika make a good hair-dye.

## \|\| 176.11 \|\|

*cakramardakabījāni kuṣṭhameraṇḍamūlakam \|*  
*atyamlakāñjikaṃ piṣṭvā lepānmastakaroganut \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Plasters of Cakramards-seeds, Kustham and Eranda-roots pasted with warm Kanjikam and applied to the scalp.prove curative in all diseases of the head (cephalagia).

## \|\| 176.12-14 \|\|

*saindhavaṃ ca vacā hiṅgu kuṣṭhaṃ nāgeśvaraṃ tathā \|*  
*śatapuṣpā devadāru ebhistailaṃ tu sādhitam \|\| 12 \|\|*

*gopurīparasenaiva caturbhāgena saṃyutam \|*  
*tatkaṇabharaṇādugrakarṇaśūlaṃ kṣayaṃ nayet \|\| 13 \|\|*

*meṣamūtrasaindhavābhyāṃ karṇayorbharaṇācchiva \|*  
*karṇayoḥ pūtināśaḥ syātkṛmistrāvādikasya ca \|\| 14 \|\|*

12-14. A medicinal oil cooked with its quarter part of cow's urine and with the addition of rock salt, Vaca, Hihgu, Kustham, Nagegvaram, Shata- and Devadaru, poured into the ears, relieves earache. Similarly, ear-drops composed of rock salt and lamb's urine prove beneficial in otalgia with a fetid discharge, and germination of parasites in the tympanum.

## \|\| 176.15 \|\|

*mālatīpuppadalayo rasena bharaṇāttathā \|*  
*gojalenaiva pūreṇa pūyastrāvo vinaśyati \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Pourings of the expressed juice of the Malati leaves, and cow's urine arrest fetid discharges from the ears.

## \|\| 176.16 \|\|

*kaṣṭhamāṣamarīcāni tagaraṃ madhu pippalī \|*  
*apāmārgo 'śvagandhā ca bṛhatī sitasarṣapāḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Rubbings of a plaster composed of Kustha, Masa, Maricam, Tagaram, Pippall, Apamarga, Agvagandha, the two kinds of Vrhati, and mustard,

## \|\| 176.17-18 \|\|

*yavāstilāḥ saindhavaṃ ca pādikodvartanaṃ śubham \|*  
*liṅgabāhustanānāṃ ca karṇayorvṛddhikṛdbhavet \|*  
*kaṭutailaṃ bhallātakaṃ bṛhatī phaladāḍimam \|\| 17 \|\|*

*valkalaiḥ sādhitairliptaṃ liṅgaṃ tena vivardhate \|\| 18 \|\|*

17-18. Yava, and Tilam pasted with honey and rocksalt remove the numbness of the penis and the arms. Mustard oil cooked with the admixture of Bhallatakam, the two kinds of Vrhati, and the fruit and barks of Dadima trees should be prescribed for the purpose of getting the male reproductive organ elongated.

## Chapter 177

## \|\| 177.1 \|\|

*hariruvāca \|*  
*sobhāñjanapatrarasaṃ madhuyuktaṃ hi cakṣuṣoḥ \|*  
*bha (ca) raṇādrogaharaṇaṃ bhavennāstyatra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Hari said: — The expressed juice of the leaves of Shobhanjanam mixed with honey, and poured into the eyes, undoubtedly relieves all forms of occular affections.

## \|\| 177.2-3 \|\|

*aśītitilapuṣpāṇi jātyāśca kusumāpi ca \|*  
*uṣānimbāmalāśuṇṭhīpippalītaṇḍulīyakam \|\| 2 \|\|*

*chāyāsuṣkāṃ vaṭīṃ kuryātpiṣṭvā taṇḍulavāriṇā \|*  
*madhunā sahasā cākṣṇorañjanāttimirādinut \|\| 3 \|\|*

2-3. Make a pill with the flowers of black sesame, Jati flowers, Usa, Nimba, Amala, SunthI, Pippall, and Tanduliyakam pasted together with ricewashings and dried in the shade. Rub this pill with honey and reduce it to a paste, apply this paste to the eyes in the manner of a collyrium. It cures blindness (Timira).

## \|\| 177.4-5 \|\|

*bibhītakāsthimajjā tu śaṅkhanābhirmanaḥ śilā \|*  
*nimbapatramarīcā ni ajāmūtreṇa peṣayet \|\| 4 \|\|*

*puṣpaṃ rātryandhatāṃ hanti timiraṃ paṭalaṃ tathā \|*  
*caturbhāgāni śaṅkhasya tadardhena manaḥ śilā \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. Take Bibhutaki, Sankha, Manah-^ila, black pepper and Nimba leaves, reduce them to a paste with the addition of goat's urine. It cures Timira, Patalam and night-blindness.

## \|\| 177.6-7 \|\|

*saindhavaṃ ca tadardhenatvetatpiṣṭvādakena tu \|*  
*chāyāśuṣkāṃ tu vaṭikāṃ kṛtvā nayanamañjayet \|\| 6 \|\|*

*timiraṃ paṭalaṃ hanti piciṭaṃ ca mahauṣadham \|*  
*trikaṭu triphalāṃ caiva karaṃ jasya phalāni ca \|\| 7 \|\|*

6-7. Take four parts of powdered conch-shell, two parts of realgar and one part of rock-salt, reduce them to a paste with the addition of cold water, make them into pills, and dry them in the shade. A pill, thus prepared, and pasted with water and applied along the eyes in the manner of a collyrium cures loss of sight, Patalam and agglutination of the eyes with slimy mucous (Picchitam).

## \|\| 177.8 \|\|

*saindhavaṃ rajanīdve va bhṛṅgarājarasena hi \|*  
*piṣṭvā tadañjanādeva timirādivināśanam \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. A plaster composed to Trikatu, Triphala, Karadja seeds, the two kinds of Rajani, and rock salt pasted with the expressed juice of Bhrhgaraja and applied in the manner of a collyrium cures loss of vision, etc

## \|\| 177.9 \|\|

*āṭarūṣakamūlaṃ tu kāñjikāpiṣṭameva tu \|*  
*tenākṣibūmilepācca cakṣuḥ śūlaṃ vinaśyati \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Atarusaka roots pasted with Kannjikam and thickly plastered over the eyelids relieve aching sensations in the eyes.

## \|\| 177.10-11 \|\|

*satakraṃ badarīmūlaṃ pītaṃ vākṣivyathāṃ haret \|*  
*saindhaṃvaṃ kaṭutailaṃ ca apāmārgasya mūlakam \|\| 10 \|\|*

*kṣīrakāñjikasaṃghṛṣṭaṃ tāmrapātre tu tena ca \|*  
*añjanātpiñjaṭasyaiva nāśo bhavati śaṅkara \|\| 11 \|\|*

10-11. Decoctions of Satadkram, and Vadari roots internally administrated relieve pain in the eyes. An Anjanam composed of mustard oil, rock-salt and Apamarga roots pasted together with milk and Kanjikam and prepared in a copper vessel, and applied to the eyes in the manner of a collyrium, removes, О бапкага, the agglutination of the eyelids with mucous.

## \|\| 177.12 \|\|

*oṃ dadru sara kroṃ hrīṃ ṭhaḥ ṭhaḥ dadru sara hrīṃ hrīṃ oṃ uṃ ū sara krīṃ krīṃ ṭhaḥ ṭhaḥ \|*  
*ādyā hi vaśāmāyānti mantreṇānena cāñjanāt \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. This Anjanam (eye-salve) applied by reciting the Mantra, Om, Dadru Sara, Krim, Hrim, Than, Than, Dadru Sara, Harim, Hrim, Om, Um, Um, Sara, Kram, Krim, Thah, Thah, brings the Adaya under the control of the applier at all.

## \|\| 177.13 \|\|

*bilvakanīlikāmūlaṃ piṣṭamabhyañjanena ca \|*  
*anenāñjitamātreṇa naśyanti timirāṇi hi \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. The application of eye-salve composed of BiJavam, and Nill-roots pasted together with water instantly cures the loss of vision.

## \|\| 177.14 \|\|

*kaṭukaṃ (pippalī) tagaraṃ caiva haridrāmalakaṃ vacā \|*  
*khadirapiṣṭavāttaśca añjanānnetraroganut \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. A stick made of Pippall, Tagaram, Haridra, Amalakam, Vacera and Khadira pasted together with water and applied to the eyes, proves curative in occular affections.

## \|\| 177.15 \|\|

*nīrapūrṇamukho dhauti bṛhanmānena yo 'kṣiṇī \|*  
*prabhāte netrarogaiśca nityaṃ sarvaiḥ pramucyate \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Dash cold water over the eyes while holding water in the mouth at morning, each day. "his measure cures many an occular affection.

## \|\| 177.16 \|\|

*śuklairaṇḍasya mūlena patreṇāpi prasādhitam \|*  
*chagadagdhasekamauṣṇyāccakṣuṣorvātaśalanat \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Fomentations of the eyes with vapours of warm goat's milk cooked in combination with the roots and leaves of white Eranda prove curative in the Vataja form of eye-diseases.

## \|\| 177.17-18 \|\|

*candanaṃ saindhavaṃ vṛddhapālāśaśca harītakī \|*  
*paṭalaṃ kusumaṃ nīlī ca (va) krikāṃ harate 'ñjanam \|\| 17 \|\|*

*guñjāmūlaṃ chāgamūtre ghṛṣṭaṃ timiranucca tat raupyatāmrasuvarṇānāṃ hastaghṛṣṭaśalākayā \|\| 18 \|\|*

17-18. A compound of Candanam, Saindhava, Vrddha, Palasa, HaritakI, Patola flowers, and Cakrika pasted together with water, or Guhja- pasted with goat's urine and applied to the eyes in the manner of a collyrium removes blindness (Timram).

## \|\| 177.19 \|\|

*ghṛṣṭamudvartanaṃ rudra kāmalāvyādhināśanam \|*  
*ghoṣāphalamapāghrātaṃ pītakāmalanāśanam \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Lubrication of the body of a Chlorosis- patient with clarified butter containing rubbings of gold, silver and copper rods tends to bring about a cure. Smelling or eating of Ghosaphalam proves curative in chlorosis.

## \|\| 177.20 \|\|

*dūrvādāḍimapuṣpaṃ tu alaktakaharītakī \|*  
*nāsārśavātaraktanunnasyādvai svarasena hi \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Errhines composed of a soluble compound of Haritaki, Alaktakam, Durva and Dadima- pasted with their own expressed juice cure nasal polypi and Vataraktam.

## \|\| 177.21 \|\|

*āpiṣṭvā jāṅgalī mū (tū) laṃ tadrasena vṛṣadhvaja \|*  
*nasyādārādvinaśyeta nāśārśo nīlalohita \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. О Thou blue and red bodied one, О Thou bull-riding deity, errhines composed of Jingali- pasted with their own expressed juice lead of the falling off of nasal polypi.

## \|\| 177.22 \|\|

*gavyaṃ ghṛtaṃ sarjarasaṃ rudra dhanyākasaindhavam \|*  
*dhuttūrakaṃ gairikaṃ ca etaiḥ sādhitasikthakam \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. A medicinal oil prepared with the admixture of Siktham saturated with the expressed juice of Dhuturam and Dhanyakam, and mixed with Sarjarasa, Gairikam, rock-salt and Ghrtam made out of cow butter proves remedial in ulcers, as well as in sloughing and splintering of the lips.

## \|\| 177.23 \|\|

*satailaṃ vraṇanutsyācca sphuṭitoddhaṭitādhare \|*  
*jātīpatraṃ ca carvitvā vidhṛtaṃ mukharoganut \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Jatipatram unmixed with Ghrtam should be chewed by one, for the alleviation of the diseases of one's mouth; chewing of Kosa-seeds imparts a firmness even to loose teeth.

## \|\| 177.24-26 \|\|

*bhakṣātkesarabījasya dantāḥ syuścalitāḥsthirāḥ \|*  
*muṣṭakaṃ kuṣṭhamelā ca yaṣṭikaṃ madhuvālakam \|\| 24 \|\|*

*dhanyākametadadanānmukhadurgandhanuddhara \|*  
*kaṣāyaṃ kaṭukaṃ vāpi tiktaśākasya bhakṣaṇāt \|\| 25 \|\|*

*talayuktasya nityaṃ syānmukhadurgandhatākṣayaḥ \|*  
*dantavraṇāni sarvāṇi kṣayaṃ gacchantyanena tu \|\| 26 \|\|*

24-26. Chewing of a compound consiting of Mustakam, Kustham, Ela, Yastikam, Valakam, Dhanyakam and honey removes fetour in the mouth. Daily ingestions of bitter, pungent, or astringent &akas fried with oil remove the bad smell from the mouth and prove beneficial in cases of ulcerated gums.

## \|\| 177.27 \|\|

*kāñjikasya satailasya gaṇḍūṣakavalāsthitiḥ \|*  
*tāmbūlacūrṇadagdhasya mukhasya vyādhinucchiva ! \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Gargles of Kanjikam mixed with oil, as well as those containing ashes of burnt betel lives prove curative in affections of the mouth.

## \|\| 177.28-31 \|\|

*parityaktaśleṣmaṇaśca śuṇṭhīcarvaṇato yathā \|*  
*mātuluṅgadalānyelā yaṣṭī madhu ca pippalī \|\| 28 \|\|*

*jātīpatramathaiṣāṃ ca cūrṇaṃ līḍhvā tathā kṛtam \|*  
*śephālikajaṭāyāśca carvaṇaṃ galaśuṇṭhinut \|\| 29 \|\|*

*nāsāśirāraktakarṣānnaśyecchaṃśakara jihvikā \|*  
*rasaḥ śirīṣabījānāṃ haridrāyāścaturguṇaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

*tena pakvena bhūteśa nasyaṃ mastakaroganut \|*  
*galarogā vinaśyanti nasyamātreṇa tatkṣaṇāt \|\| 31 \|\|*

28-31. Chewing of 5unthl, as well as eating of a compound of Matuluga leaves, Ela, Yastimadhu, Pippall and Jatipatram pounded together, leads to the secretion of mucous from the mouth. Chewing of the clustered sprouts (Jata) of Shephalika proves curative in Goitre; О Sankara, errhines of the expressed juice of Jihvika arrest haemorrhage from the nose or the brain. A medicinal oil cooked with the admixture of the expressed juice of Sirisa seeds, and Haridra, four times as much as that juice, should be employed as errhines for the extinction of diseases of the head and throat.

## \|\| 177.32-34 \|\|

*dantakīṭavināśaḥ myādguñjāmūlasya carvaṇāt \|*  
*kākajaṅghāsnuhīnīlīkavāyo madhumojitaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

*dantākrāntāndantajāṃśca kṛmīnnāśayate śiva \|*  
*ghataṃ karkaṭapādena dugdhonmiśreṇa sādhitam \|\| 33 \|\|*

*tena cāmyaṅgitādantāḥ kuryuḥ kaṭakaṭānna hi \|*  
*liptvā karkaṭapādena kevalenāthavāśiva \|\| 34 \|\|*

32-34. Chewing of Gunja-roots leads to the extinction of worms in the teeth. A decoction of Kaka-Jangha, Snuhl, and Nffi, sweetened with the addition of honey, kills worms that might have originated in, or invaded the teeth. Rubbing of the teeth with a Ghrtam cooked in combination with milk and the expressed juice of Karkata-pada prevent their gnashing (destroys the tendency of gnashing the teeth).

## \|\| 177.35 \|\|

*trisaptāhaṃ vāḥ piṣṭāni jyotiṣmatyāḥ phalāni hi \|*  
*śuklābhayāmajjalepāddantasyāṅkakalaṅkanut \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. As an alternative, О Siva, a paste of Karkata- pada alone should be applied to the teeth, or Jyotismatl fruits pasted with water alone should be applied to them for three weeks in succession or the pith (marrow) of white myrbalans pasted with water should be applied for removing the black or yellow colour (tan or tartar) of the teeth.

## \|\| 177.36 \|\|

*lodhrakuṅkumamañjiṣṭhālohakā leyakāni ca \|*  
*yavataṇḍulametaiśca yaṣṭī madhusamanvitaiḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. A cosmetic composed of Lodhra, Kumkum, Manjistha, Loha, Kaleyakam, barley, rice, and Yasthimadhu pasted together with water should be used by ladies for beautifying their complexion.

## \|\| 177.37-38 \|\|

*vāripiṣṭairvaktralepaḥ strīṇāṃ śobhanavaktrakṛt \|*  
*dvibhāgaṃ chāgadugdhena tailaprasthaṃ tu sādhitam \|\| 37 \|\|*

*raktavandanamañjiṣṭhālakṣāṇāṃ karṣakeṇa vā \|*  
*yaṣṭīmadhukuṅkumābhyāṃ saptāhānmukhakāntikṛt \|\| 38 \|\|*

37-38. Cook a Prastha measure of oil with two parts of goat's milk and a Karp of each of the following drugs, viz., Rakta-Candanam, Manjistha, Laksa, Yastimadhu, and Kumkum. This Tailam is highly possessed of cosmetic properties; a week's application will impart a beautiful tint to one's complexion.

## \|\| 177.39 \|\|

*śuṇṭhīpippalicūrṇaṃ tu guḍūcī kaṇṭakārikā \|*  
*ebhiśca kvathitaṃ vāri pītaṃ cāgniṃ karoti vai \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. A decoction of Sunthi, powdered Pippall, GuducI, and Kantakarika, acts as a good digestant and stomachic remedy, and tends to allaviate, О Thou, the lord of benighted spirits, the aching (rheumatic) pain brought about through the agency of the deranged Vayu.

## \|\| 177.40-41 \|\|

*vātaśūlakṣayaṃ caiva kageti prathameśvara \|*  
*karañjaparpaṭośīraṃ bahatī kaṭurohiṇī \|\| 40 \|\|*

*gokṣuraṃ kvathitaṃ tvabhirvāri pītaṃ śramāpahan \|*  
*dāhaṃ pittaṃ jvaraṃ śoṣaṃ mūrchāṃ caiva kṣayaṃ nayet \|\| 41 \|\|*

40-41. A decoction of Karanja, Karkata, Usiram, the two kinds of Vrhatl, Katu-Rohinl, and Goksuram, internally administered, tends to relieve the sense of exhaustion or fatigue, and proves curative in Pthisis, consumption, Epileptic fits and Pittaja fever with a burning sensation in the body.

## \|\| 177.42 \|\|

*madhvājyapippalīcūrṇaṃ kvathitaṃ kṣīrasaṃyutam \|*  
*pītaṃ hṛdrogakāsasya viṣamajvaranudbhavet \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Milk cooked with powdered Pippali and taken in combination with honey, sugar and clarified butter cures cough, heart disease, and chronic intermittent fever.

## \|\| 177.43 \|\|

*kvāthaupadhīnāṃ sarvāsāṃ karṣārdhaṃ grāhyameva ca \|*  
*vayo 'nurūyato jñeyo viśeṣo vṛṣabhadhvaja \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. A Karsa measure of the combined drugs should be taken in preparing all kinds of df ugdecoction; О thou bull-riding one, the does of such decoctions should be determined in consideration of the age of the patient under treatment.

## \|\| 177.44 \|\|

*dugdhaṃ pītaṃ tu saṃyuktaṃ gopurīṣarasena ca \|*  
*viṣamajvaranutsyācca kākajandhārasastathā \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. The expressed juice of Kaka-Jangha, as well as the serous fluid extrected from cow-dung, taken with warm milk, proves curative in chronic, intermittent fever.

## \|\| 177.45 \|\|

*maśuṇṭhi kvathitaṃ kṣīgmajāyā jvaranudbhavet \|*  
*yaṣṭīmadhukamustaṃ ca saindhavaṃ bṛhatīphalam \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Milk cooked with Sunthi acts as a good febrifuge. Errhines composed of Yastimadhu, Musta, Brhatlphalam and rock salt pounded together is possessed of highly soporific properties.

## \|\| 177.46 \|\|

*etairnasvapridānācca nidrā syātpurupasya ca \|*  
*marīcapradhvaśvalālānasyānnidrā bhavecchiva \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Similarly, errhines composed of Магаса pasted with honey, О Shiva, are possessed of the virtue of inducing sleep.

## \|\| 177.47-48 \|\|

*mūlaṃ tu kākajaṅghāyā nidrākṛtsyācchirasthitam \|*  
*siddhaṃ tailaṃ kāñjikena tathā sarjarasena ca \|\| 47 \|\|*

*śītodakasamāyuktaṃ lepātsantāpanāśanam \|*  
*śoṇitajvaradāhebhyo jātasantāpanuttathā \|\| 48 \|\|*

47-48. - O Siva, Kaka-Jungha roots are possessed of good soporific properties, and a medicinal oil cooked in combination with Kanjikam and Sarjarasa, applied with the admixture of cold water, instantly allays heat and burning sensation, and shold be employed in alluviating the burning sensation of the body which characterises fever of contaminated blood (fever induced through bloodpoisoning or Septecimia).

## \|\| 177.49-50 \|\|

*śṛkaśaivālamanthaśca śuṇṭhīpāpāṇabhedakam \|*  
*śauvāñjanaṃ gokṣuraṃ vā varuṇacchannameva ca \|\| 49 \|\|*

*saubhāñjanasya mūlaṃ ca etaiḥ kvathitavāri ca \|*  
*dattvā hiṅguyavakṣāraṃ pītaṃ vātavināśanam \|\| 50 \|\|*

49-50. A decoction of 3ali, 6aivala Agnimantha, Shunthi, Pasana-Bhedakam, janam, Gok$uram, Shobhanjanam roots, or Varuna and Channam taken with Yavaksara and Hingu, proves antidotal to diseases of the deranged Vayu.

## \|\| 177.51 \|\|

*pippalī pippalīmūlaṃ tathā bhallātakaṃ śiva \|*  
*vāryetaiḥ kvathitaṃ pītaṃ varaśūlāpahārakṛt \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. О Shiva, a decoction of Pippali, Pippali- mulam, and Bhallatakam, internally administered, proves curative in coilc and convulsions.

## \|\| 177.52 \|\|

*aśvagandhāmūlakābhyāṃ siddhā valmīkamṛttikā \|*  
*etayā mardanādrudra ūrustambhaḥ praśāmyati \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. External applications of a plaster composed of the earth of an ant-hill cooked in combination with Asvagandha, Mulakam and water alleviate the form of rheumatism known as Urustambha.

## \|\| 177.53 \|\|

*bṛhatīkasya vai mūlaṃ saṃpiṣṭamudakena ca \|*  
*pītaṃ saṃghātavātasya vipāṭanakṛdeva ca \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Decoctions of Vrhatl root internally administered cure Sanghata-Vatam.

## \|\| 177.54 \|\|

*pītaṃ takreṇa mūlaṃ ca ārdrasya tagarasya ca \|*  
*haret jhiñjinīvātaṃ?vai vṛkṣamindrāśaniryathā \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. The expressed juice of the roots of Ardrakam and Tagaram, taken with whey, cures the front of neuresthesnia whose specific trait is a tingling sensation, О Shiva, as the thunder bolt of Indra cleaves a tree.

## \|\| 177.55 \|\|

*asthisaṃhāramekena bhaktena saha vāditam \|*  
*patiṃ māṃsarasenāpi vātanuccāsthibhaṅganut \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. The expressed juice of Asthi-SamhArakam taken with a single meal, each day, or with meat soup cures nervous diseases and brings about the setting of broken bones.

## \|\| 177.56 \|\|

*ghṛtaliptaṃ saśuṣkaṃ ca chāgīkṣīreṇa saṃyutam \|*  
*tallopātpādayārnaṃśyetsakṣepye cātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. Powders of fried barley com reduced to a paste with the addition of goat's milk and clarified butter, and applied to the soles of the feet, tend to ally the burning sensation of those localities.

## \|\| 177.57-58 \|\|

*madhvājyasaindhavaṃ sikthaṃ guḍakairikaguggulaiḥ \|*  
*sasarjarasasphuṭitaḥ klomaśuddhiśca lepanāt \|\| 57 \|\|*

*kaṭutailena lipto vai vidhūmāgnau pratāpitaḥ \|*  
*mṛttikārakhāditaḥ pādaḥ samaḥ syādvṛṣabhadhvaja \|\| 58 \|\|*

57-58. Plasters composed of honey clarified butter, rock salt, treacle, Gairikam, Guggulu and Sarja rasa prove beneficial in cases of cracked soles of women and children О thou bull-riding deity, clayeasten soles of feet should be lubricated with mustard oil and heated over a smokeless fire.

## \|\| 177.59 \|\|

*sarjarasāḥ sikthakaṃ ca jīrakaṃ ca harītakī \|*  
*utsādhitaghṛtābhyaṅgo hyagnidagdhavyathāpanut \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. A medicinal Ghrtam, cooked with the admixture of Sarjarasa, Siktham, Jlrakam and Haritaki, and applied to scalds or burns alleviates the incidental pain.

## \|\| 177.60-62 \|\|

*tilatailaṃ cāgnidagdhaṃ yavabhasmasamanvitam \|*  
*agnidagdhavraṇaṃ naśyedbrahuśaḥ kṛtalepataḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

*navanītaṃ māhiṣaṃ ca dagdhapiṣṭatilāni ca \|*  
*sabhallākaṃ vraṇaṃ naśyeddhṛcchūlaṃ nasyalepanāt \|\| 61 \|\|*

*karpūragavyasarpirbhyāṃ prahāraḥ pūrito hara \|*  
*śastrodbhavaḥ sabaddhaśca śuklavarṇena śaṅkara ! \|*  
*pākaṃ ca vedanāṃ caiva saṃspṛśedvṛṣabhadhvaja \|\| 62 \|\|*

60-62. Sesamum-oil saturated with the ashes of burnt barely com proves remedial to belbs, blisters caused by a burn or scald. Plasters of Tilam, and Bhallatam pasted with milk and mixed with buffalo butter, prove beneficial in ulcer cases; applied over the chest, or employed as errhines they alleviate angina pectoris and cardiac colic. О Sankara, bruises caused by blows of one's enemies are remedied by bandaging the spots with strips of clean linen saturated with cow-butter and powdered camphor.

## \|\| 177.63 \|\|

*āmra (tasya) mūlarasenaiva śastraghātaḥ prapūritaḥ \|*  
*ḍhaukate śastraghātābhyāṃ nirvraṇo ghṛpūritaḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. Sword cuts and arrow wounds, filled with the expressed juice of Amra-roots, are adhesioned and united by the first instance without producing any pain, pus, or inflammation. Similarly, sprays of clarified butter poured into freshly made swordcuts or wounds bring about their adhesion and asepsision.

## \|\| 177.64 \|\|

*śarapuṅkhā lajjālukā pāṭhā caiṣāṃ tu mūlakam \|*  
*jalapiṣṭaṃ tasya lepācchastraghātaḥ praśāmyati \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. Cuts and wounds are healed by applying plasters of Sarapuhkha, Lajjaluka, Patha, Casa (the Bengal edition reads Vasa) and Mulakam pasted with water.

## \|\| 177.65 \|\|

*mūlaṃ ca kākajaṅghāyāstrirātreṇaiva śoṣitaḥ \|*  
*pākapūtiṃ vedanāṃ ca hanti vai rohito vraṇe \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. The expressed juice of Kakajangha, poured four three nights in succession in a granulating ulcer, brings about it asepsision and alleviates the inflammation, and prevents the production of of Pus in its cavity.

## \|\| 177.66-67 \|\|

*sajalaṃ tilatailaṃ ca apāmārgasya mūlakam \|*  
*tatsekadānānnaśyecca prahārodbhavavedanā \|\| 66 \|\|*

*abhayāṃ saindhavaṃ śuṇṭhīmetatpiṣṭvodakena tu \|*  
*bhakṣayitvā hyajīrṇasya nāśo bhavati śaṅkara ! \|\| 67 \|\|*

66-67. Rubbing of the body with water and the expressed juice of Apamarga instantly alleviates the bruised pain caused by thrashing. О Sankara, a compound of Abhaya, Shunthi, and rock salt pasted with water and internally administered cures all forms of indigestion.

## \|\| 177.68-69 \|\|

*kaṭibaddhaṃ nimbamūlamakṣisūlaharaṃ bhavet \|*  
*śaṇamūlaṃ satāmbūlaṃ dagdhamindriyakasya (lpa) hṛt \|\| 68 \|\|*

*annasvinnaharidrā ca śvetasarṣapamūlakam \|*  
*bījāni mātuluṅgasya eṣāmudvartanaṃ samam \|*  
*saptarātraprayogeṇa śubhadehakaraṃ bhavet \|\| 69 \|\|*

68-69. Nimba roots tied round the waist relieves an aching pain in the eyes; dry Haridra, white Sarsapa, Mulakam and Matulunga seeds, pounded together, should be used in cleansing the skin of all its impurities, a week's use of this compound imparts a brighter hue to the colour of the skin.

## \|\| 177.70 \|\|

*śvetāparājitāpatraṃ nimbapatrarasena tu \|*  
*nasyadānāḍḍākinīnāṃ mātṝṇāṃ brahmarakṣasām \|*  
*mokṣaḥ syānmadhusāreṇa nasyācca vṛṣabhadhvaja \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. Errhines composed of the expressed juice, white Aparajita leaves and Nimba leaves should be employed for the purpose of delivering patients from the influences Dakinls, Matrikas and other malignant spirit О thou bull-ensigned deity, errhines of Madhuka pitha are possessed of the same efficacy.

## \|\| 177.71 \|\|

*mūlaṃ śvetajayantyāśca puṣyarkṣe tu samāhṛtam \|*  
*śvetāparājitārkasya citrakasya ca mūlakam \|*  
*kṛtvā tu vaṭikāṃ nārī tilakena vaśī bhavet \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. Cull the roots of white JayantI, or white Aparajita, Arka, Chitrakam or Mulakam under the influence of the asterism Pusya, reduce them to a paste with the addition of water and divide the mass into pills, A pills thus prepared and applied as a Tilaka mark on the forehead of a man has the magical virtue of enthralling the hearts of young maidens.

## \|\| 177.72-73 \|\|

*pippalīlohacūrṇaṃ tu śuṇṭhīścāmalakāni ca \|*  
*samāni rudra jānīyātsaindhavaṃ madhuśarkarā \|\| 72 \|\|*

*udumbarapramāṇena saptāhaṃ bhakṣaṇātsamam \|*  
*pumāṃśca balavānsa syājjīvedvarṣaśatadvayam \|*  
*oṃ ṭha ṭha ṭha iti sarvavaśyaprayogeṣu prayuktaḥ sarvakāmakṛt \|\| 73 \|\|*

72-73. Learn, О Rudra, that powders of “ killed iron, Pippall Shunthi, Shmalakam, rocksalt, sugar and honey, taken in equal parts, pasted together, and made into pills, to the seize of an Audmabara, should be taken for seven days in succession by a man, desiring a healthful life of a hundred years. The Mantra, Om, Tha, Tha, Tha, should be employed in connection with all acts of charming.

## \|\| 177.74 \|\|

*saṃgṛhya vidvānkākasya nilayaṃ pradahecca tat \|*  
*citāgnau bhasma tacchatrordattaṃ śirasi śaṅkara \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. Collect the nest of a cow from a tree, burn that nest in the fire of a blazing funeral pile. The ashes of this burnt crow's nest cast on the head of a person makes him distracted and comples him to abandon his hearth and home. О Sankara, hear me enumerate such other measures of black migic.

## \|\| 177.75-76 \|\|

*tamuccāṭayate rudra śṛṇu tadyogamuttamam \|*  
*niḥ kṣiptaṃ ca purīṣaṃ vai vanamūṣikacarmaṇi \|\| 75 \|\|*

*kaṭitantunibaddhaṃ vai kuryānmalanirodhanam \|*  
*kṛṣṇakākasya raktena yasya nāma pralipya ca \|\| 76 \|\|*

75-76. Let a man cast the excreta of his enemy on the skin of a wild rat and tie that skin round his waist, thereby he will be able to cause a suppression of his stool. A man or woman whose name is written on a mango-leaf with the blood of a raven.and is cast amidst heaps of filthy substances is sure to be devoured by crows.

## \|\| 177.77-78 \|\|

*cyutadale madhyamadhye tato niḥ kṣipyate hara ! \|*  
*sa khādyate kākavṛndairnārī puruṣa eva ca \|\| 77 \|\|*

*śarkarāmadhvajākṣīraṃ tilagokṣurakaṃ samam \|*  
*sa śatruṃ nāśayedrudra ! uccāṭitamidaṃ hara ! \|\| 78 \|\|*

77-78. О Hara, a compound consisting of goat's milk, Tilam, Goksuram sugar and honey taken in equal parts and internally administered, proves curative in cases of loss of manhood and virile impotency:

## \|\| 177.79 \|\|

*ulūkakṛṣṇakākasya bilvasyātha samicchatam \|*  
*rudhireṇa samāyuktaṃ yayornāmnā tu hūyate \|*  
*tayormadhye mahāvairaṃ bhavennāstyatra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. A hundred Bilva twigs soaked with the blood of a raven and an owl and cast in the fire by uttering the names of two different persons are sure to create a bitter animosity between them.

## \|\| 177.80 \|\|

*bhāvitaṃ ṛkṣadugdhena matsyasya rohitasya ca \|*  
*māṃsaṃ tatsādhitaṃ tailaṃ tadabhyaṅgācca roganut \|*  
*candanodakanasyāttu romotthānaṃ bhavetpunaḥ \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. A medicinal oil cooked with the addition of the flesh of a Jhasa and Rohita, treated with the milk of a she-bear in the manner of a Bhavana, may be prescribed for anointing the body of the patient in any kind of disease. Solutions of Candanam, employed as errhines, facilitate the re-appearance of hairs.

## \|\| 177.81 \|\|

*haste lāṅgalikākandaṃ gṛhītaṃ tena lepitam \|*  
*śarīraṃ yena sa pumānvṛddherdarpaṃ vyapohati \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. He, who holds a Langalika bulb in his hand, or smears his body with a paste of that plant, is sure to break the arrogance of the strongbodied ones even in his old age.

## \|\| 177.82 \|\|

*mayūrarudhireṇaiva jīvaṃ saṃharate śiva \|*  
*jvalatāṃ tu bhujaṅgānāṃ bilasthānāmapīśvara \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. О Thou blissful one, peacock's blood is fatal even to snakes residing in their holes. Burn down to ashes the dead body of an Ajagar (Boa constrictor) in the fire of a cremation ground.

## \|\| 177.83 \|\|

*dehaścitāgnau dagdhaśca sarpasyājagarasya hi \|*  
*tadbhasma saṃmukhe kṣiptaṃ śatraṇāṃ bhaṅgakṛdbhavet \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. By casting these ashes before one's enemies one is sure to confound them, almost instantaneously.

## \|\| 177.84 \|\|

*mantreṇānena tatkṣiptaṃ mahābhaṅgakaraṃ ripoḥ \|*  
*oṃ ṭha ṭha ṭha cāhīhicāhīhi svāhā \|*  
*oṃ udaraṃ pāhihi pāhihisvāhā \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. The Mantra, which should be recited on the occasion, runs as Om, Tha, Tha, Tha, Cahi, Cahlhi, Svaha, Om, Udaram, Pahi Pahi Svaha.

## \|\| 177.85 \|\|

*sudarśanāyā malaṃ tu puṣyarkṣe tu samāhṛtam \|*  
*niḥ kṣiptaṃ gṛhamadhye tu bhujaṅgā varjayanti tat \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. Sudarsana roots culled under the influence of the asterism Pusya and kept in a chamber drive the serpents from its inside and bar their reoccupation of the same site.

## \|\| 177.86 \|\|

*arkamūlena raviṇā arkāgnijvalitā śiva \|*  
*yuktā siddhārthatailena vartirmārgāhināśinī \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. Torches made of linen soaked with the expressed juice of Arka plants and lighted to illumine a road way serve to drive away all snakes from that road side.

## \|\| 177.87 \|\|

*mārjārapalalaṃ viṣṭhā haritālaṃ ca bhāvitam \|*  
*chāga mūtreṇa tallipto mūṣiko mūṣikānharet \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. Smear the body of a rat with Haritalam soaked in the serum of a cat's excrta and pasted with goat's urine. The sight of such a rat is sure to scare away all its kindreds from that house.

## \|\| 177.88-89 \|\|

*mukto hi mandire rudra nātra kāryā vicāraṇā \|*  
*viphalārjunapuṣpāṇi bhallātakaśirīṣakam \|\| 88 \|\|*

*lākṣā sarjarasaścaiva viḍaṅgaścaiva gugguluḥ \|*  
*etairdhūpo makṣikāṇāṃ maśakāṇāṃ vināśanaḥ \|\| 89 \|\|*

88-89. For the extinction of mosquitos in a chamber, fumigate it with the vapours of a compound consisting of Triphala, Arjuna, Bhallatakam, 6irisham, Vidanga, shellac, resin, and bdellium pounded together and cast in a smokeless fire.

## Chapter 178

## \|\| 178.1 \|\|

*hariruvāca \|*  
*brahmadaṇḍīvacākuṣṭhaṃ priyaṅgarnāgakeśaram \|*  
*dadyāttāmbūlasaṃyuktaṃ strīṇāṃ mantreṇa tadvaśam \|*  
*oṃ nārāyaṇyai svāhā \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Hari said: — Let a woman administer a compound of Brahmadandi, Vaca, Kustham, and Nagakesaram, with a prepared betel leaf to a man she loves by repeating the Mantra, Om NarayanI Svaha.

## \|\| 178.2 \|\|

*tāmbūlaṃ yasya dīyeta sa vaśī syātsumantrataḥ \|*  
*oṃ hariḥ hariḥ svāhā \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. The man to whom such a betel is given becomes the slave of its beautiful giver. After giving it (betel)let the woman recite the Mantra, Om, Hari, Hari, Svaha.

## \|\| 178.3 \|\|

*godantaṃ haritālañca saṃyuktaṃ kākajihvayā \|*  
*cūrṇokṛtya yasya śire dīyate sa vaśī bhavet \|*  
*śvetasarṣapanirmālyaṃ yadgṛhe tadvināśakṛt \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. The man on whose head is cast powders of dried crow's tongue and Godanta Haritalam is sure to be under the influence of their giver. This influence is neutralised by keeping a garland of white mustard seeds hung in the chamber of such a hypnotised man.

## \|\| 178.4 \|\|

*vaibhī takaṃ śākhoṭakaṃ mūlaṃ patreṇa saṃyutam \|*  
*sthāpyate yadgṛhadvāre tatra vai kalaho bhavet \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. By placing Sakotnka and Vaibhataka branches with their leaves unstripped off at the door of one's house you can create dissensions, О Rudra, among its inmates.

## \|\| 178.5 \|\|

*khañjarīṭasya māṃsaṃ tu madhunā saha peṣayet \|*  
*ṛtukāleyonilepātpuruṣo dāsatāmiyāt \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Powders of dried Khahjarita's (a kind of bird) flesh pasted with honey should be applied as a plaster to her own re-productive organ during the menstrual period by a woman, desiring to enslave her love.

## \|\| 178.6 \|\|

*aguruṃ gugguluṃ caiva nīlotpalasamanvitam \|*  
*guḍena dhūpayitvā tu rājadvāre priyo bhavet \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. By fumigating one's body with the vapours of a compound consisting of Aguru, Guggulu, Nilotpalam and treacle one can become a favourite in a royal court.

## \|\| 178.7 \|\|

*śvetāpa rājitāmūlaṃ piṣṭaṃ rocanayā yutam \|*  
*yaṃ paśyettilakenaiva vaśī karyānnṛpālaye \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. With a Tilak mark, on his forehead composed of white Aparajita roots pasted with Gorocana a man is sure to domineer the mind of the person he sees in a royal court.

## \|\| 178.8 \|\|

*kākajaṅghā vacā kuṣṭhaṃ nimbapatraṃ sukuṅkumam \|*  
*ātmaraktasamāyuktaṃ vaśī bhavati mānavaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. A totem on the forehead composed, of Kakajangha, Vaca, Kusnham, Nimba leaves and Kumkum pasted together with one's own blood gives one a gift of fascination.

## \|\| 178.9 \|\|

*āraṇyasya biḍālasya gṛhitvā rudhiraṃ śubham \|*  
*karañjataile tadbhāvyaṃ rudrāgnau kajjalaṃ tataḥ \|*  
*pātayetpadmapatreṇa hādṛśyaḥ syāttadañjanāt \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Take a few drops of the blood of a wild cat, mix it with Karanja Tailam in the method of a Bhabana. Prepare a collyrium therewith on a lotus leat over the fire of a burning funeral pile (Rudragni). By applying this collyrium to the eyes one can remain invisible to others.

## \|\| 178.10 \|\|

*oṃ namaḥ khaḍgavajrapāṇaye mahāyakṣasenāpataye svāhā \|*  
*oṃ rudraṃ hrāṃ hrīṃ varaśaktā tvaritāvidyā \|*  
*oṃ mātaraḥ stambhayasvāhā \|*  
*sahasraṃ parijapyāttu vidyeyaṃ cauravāriṇī \|*  
*mahāsugandhikāmūlaṃ śukraṃ stambhetkaṭau sthitam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. The Mantra to be recited in connection with this charm reads as follows: Om obeisance to the Commander in Chief of the Yaksas who wields a sword and a thunder bolt in his hands. Om Rudram, Hram, Hrim, the science of Tvarita, the repository of all spiritual and occult power. Am, may the Matris stupefy you all. Maha- root tied round the waist arrests the emission of semen.

## \|\| 178.11 \|\|

*oṃ namaḥ sarvasattvebhyo namaḥ siddhiṃ kuru kuru svāhā \|*  
*saptābhimantritaṃ kṛtvā karavīrasya puṣpakam \|*  
*strīṇāmagre bhrāmayacca kṣaṇādvai sā vaśe bhavet \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Karavira flowers seven times enchanted with the recitation of the Mantra, Om Namah SarvaSattavebhyo Namah, Siddhim Kuru Kuru Svaha. These flowers whirled round before a woman are sure to hypnotise her.

## \|\| 178.12 \|\|

*brahmadaṇḍīṃ vacāṃ patraṃ madhunā saha peṣayet \|*  
*aṅgalepācca vanitā nānyaṃ bhartāramicchati \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. A compound of Brahmadandl, Vaca and Patram pasted together with honey, and applied, as a plaster to one's reproductive organ during an act of coitus will enthral the affections of the woman to such an extent that she will desire no other husband.

## \|\| 178.13 \|\|

*brahmadaṇḍīśikhā vaktre kṣiptā śukrasya stambhanam \|*  
*mūlaṃ jayantyā vaktrasthaṃ vyavahāre jayapradam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Clumps of Brahmadandl kept in the mouth arrests the emission of semen. JayantI root kept in the mouth imparts victory to a man in respect of an act of sexual congress.

## \|\| 178.14 \|\|

*bhṛṅgarājasya mūlaṃ tu piṣṭaṃ śukreṇa saṃyutam \|*  
*akṣiṇī cāñjayitvā tu vaśī karyānnaraṃ kila \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Bhrngaraja roots pasted with semen and applied along the eye-lids in the manner of a collyrium exercises a fascinating influence.

## \|\| 178.15 \|\|

*aparājitāśikhāntu nīlotpalasamanvitām \|*  
*tāmbūlena pra (dānā) dadyācca vaśīkaraṇamuttamam \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Aparajita clumps given with Nilotpalam to a man. through the medium of a prepared betel leaf serve to exercise of good fascinating (hypnotising) effect.

## \|\| 178.16-17 \|\|

*aṅguṣṭhe ca pade gulphe jānau ca jaghane tathā \|*  
*nābhau vakṣasi kukṣau ca kakṣe kaṇṭhe kapolake \|\| 16 \|\|*

*oṣṭhe netre lalāṭe ca mūrdhni candrakalāḥ sthitāḥ \|*  
*strīṇāṃ pakṣe site kṛṣṇe ūrdhvādhaḥ saṃsthitā nṛṇām \|\| 17 \|\|*

16-17. Toes, legs, calves of legs, knee-joints, thighs, umbilicus, breasts, sides of the abdomen (groins), arm-pits, neck, cheeks-lips, eyes, forehead, and head are the regions where the Candrakala (erotic centres) are located in the organism. They are located in the right side of a male body and in the left side of a female one. By exciting these centres by tickling, etc., one can rouse up erotic propulsions. The different centres from the head downward should be respectively excited on the different days of a light fortnight, whereas the centres from the toes upward should be respectively excited on the different, days in a black one.

## \|\| 178.18 \|\|

*vāmāṅge dakṣiṇāṅge ca kramādrudra dravādikṛt \|*  
*catuḥ ṣaṣṭi kalāḥ proktāḥ kāmaśāstre vaśīkarāḥ \|*  
*āliṅganādyā nārīṇāṃ kamārīṇāṃ vaśīkarāḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Sixty-four measures of fascination have been enumerated in the Kama 6astra (Erotic Science). Virgins of maidens may be fascinated by an embrace.

## \|\| 178.19 \|\|

*rocanāgandhupuṣpāṇi nimbapuṣpaṃ priyaṅgavaḥ \|*  
*kuṅkamaṃ candanañcaiva tilakena jagadvaśet \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. A totem composed of Rocana, Gandha- puspa, Nimba leaves, Priyangu, Kumkum and Candana pasted together with water and put on the forehead is potent enough to fascinate the whole world.

## \|\| 178.20 \|\|

*oṃ hrīṃ gauri devi saubhāgyaṃ putravaśādi dehi me \|*  
*oṃ hrīṃ lakṣmi ! devi saubhāgyaṃ sarvaṃ trailokyamohanam \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. The Mantra to be recited in connection with this chaim runs as, Om Hrim, О Thou, Goddess Gourl, grant me good fortune and secure me the obedience of sons, Om, Ham, О thou goddess, Laksmi, grant me all good fortune and the power to fascinate the three worlds.

## \|\| 178.21 \|\|

*sagandhasya haridrāyāḥ kuṅkamānāṃ ca lepataḥ \|*  
*vaśayedrudra dhūpaśca tathāpuṣpasugandhayoḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Smearing of the body with a paste of Sugandha, Harida, and Kumkum, О Rudra, as well as its fumigation with the vapours of burning Sugandhi flowers gives one the power of fascinating other people.

## \|\| 178.22 \|\|

*durālabhā vacā kuṣṭhaṃ kuṅkumañca śatāvarī \|*  
*tilatailena saṃyuktaṃ yonilepādvaśī naraḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. By applying a plaster of Duralabha, Vaca, Kustham, Kumkum, 6atavarl, pasted together with sesamem-oil, to her vaginal canal a woman is sure to enthral the affection of her lover.

## \|\| 178.23 \|\|

*nimbakāṣṭhasya dhūmena dhūpayitvā bhagaṃ vadhūḥ \|*  
*subhagāsyātsāti rudra patirdāso bhaviṣyati \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. By fumigating her private part with the vapours of burning Nimba wood, a woman is enabled to become a favourite with her husband, and to captivate his affection for good.

## \|\| 178.24 \|\|

*māhiṣaṃ navanītañca kaṣṭañca madhuyaṣṭikā \|*  
*saubhāgyaṃ bhagalepātsyāt patirdāso bhavettathā \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Similarly, a plaster composed of Yasti- madhu and Kustham pasted together with buffalo-butter and applied to the same organ brings good luck to a girl.

## \|\| 178.25 \|\|

*madhuyaṣṭiśca gokṣīraṃ tathā ca kaṇṭakārikā \|*  
*etāni samabhāgāni pibeduṣṇena vāriṇā \|*  
*caturbhāgāvaśeṣeṇa garbhasambhavamuttamam \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Taka Yasthimadhu, Goksuram, and Kantakarika in equal parts and boil them with water. This decoction boiled down to its quarter part should be taken by a woman desiring concep-tion inasmuch as it is one of the most potent remedies that accelerate pregnancy in a woman.

## \|\| 178.26 \|\|

*mātuluṅgasya bījāni kṣīreṇa saha bhāvayet \|*  
*tatpītvā labhate garbhaṃ nātra kāryā vicāraṇā \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Soak Matulunga seeds in milk, by drinking this milk a woman is sure to conceive.

## \|\| 178.27 \|\|

*mātuluṅgasya bījāni mūlānyeraṇḍakasya ca \|*  
*ghṛtena saha saṃyojya pāyayetputrakākṣiṇī \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. A woman desiring the birth of male child should take Eranda-roots and Matulunga seeds in combination with clarified butter.

## \|\| 178.28 \|\|

*paśvagandhā mṛta dugdha kvathitaṃ mutrakārakam \|*  
*palāśasya tu bījāni kṣaudreṇa saha peṣayet \|*  
*rajasvalā tu pītvā syātmuṣpagarbhavivarjitā \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Milk cooked in combination with a decoction of Asvagandha (acts an an agent) that leads to the conception of a male-child. A woman, desiring to get rid of menstruation and pregnancy, should take Palasa-seeds pasted with honey, during the period of her monthly flow.

## Chapter 179

## \|\| 179.1-2 \|\|

*hariruvāca \|*  
*haritālaṃ yavakṣāṃraṃ patrāṅgaṃ raktacandanam \|*  
*jātihiṅgulakaṃ lākṣāṃ paktvā dantānpralepayet \|\| 1 \|\|*

*harītakīkaṣāyeṇa mṛṣṭvā dantānpralepayet \|*  
*dantāḥ syurlohitāḥ puṃsaḥ śvetā rudra na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

1-2. Hari said: — Take Haritalam, Yavaksara, Patranga, Rakta-Candanam, Jati-flowers, Hingulakam, and Laksa; pound them together and reduce the compund to the consistency of paste with the addition of boiled oil. First rinse the teeth, О Rudra, with a decoction of Haritaki, and after that, apply this plaster to the teeth whereby they would be tinged red.

## \|\| 179.3 \|\|

*mūlakaṃ svidya mandāgnau rasaṃ tasya prapūrayet \|*  
*karṇayoḥ pūraṇāttena karṇastrāvo vinaśyati \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Scorch a Mulakam in a slow fire, and squeeze out its juice. This juice poured into their cavities tends to arrest the discharge from the ears.

## \|\| 179.4 \|\|

*arkapatraṃ gṛhītvā tu mandāgnau tāpayecchanaiḥ \|*  
*niṣpīḍya pūrayetkarṇau karṇaśūlaṃ vinaśyati \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Take Arka leaves, and warm them over a gentle fire. The juice squeezed out of these Arka leaves, being poured into the ears, cures earache.

## \|\| 179.5 \|\|

*priyaṅgumadhukā caiva dhātakyutpalapāṅktibhiḥ \|*  
*mañjiṣṭhā lodhralākṣābhiḥ kapitthasvarasena ca \|*  
*pacettailaṃ tathā strīṇāṃ naśyetkledaḥ prapūraṇāt \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. A medicinal oil cooked in combination with Priyangu, Yastimadhu, DhatakI, Utpalam- leaves, Manjlstha, Lohram, Laksa and the expressed juice of Kapittha, and employed as vaginal enemetas, arrests leucorrhic discharges.

## \|\| 179.6-10 \|\|

*śuṣkamūlakaśuṇṭhīnāṃ kṣāro hiṅgumahauṣadham \|*  
*satapuṣpāvacā kuṣṭhaṃ dāru śigra rasāñjanam \|\| 6 \|\|*

*sauvarcalaṃ yavakṣāraṃ tathā sarjakasaindhavam \|*  
*tathā granthirviḍaṃ mustaṃ madhuyuktaṃ caturguṇam \|\| 7 \|\|*

*mātuluṃ garasastadvatkadalyāśca raso hi taiḥ \|*  
*pakvatailaṃ haredāśu strāvādīṃśca na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*karṇayoḥ kṛmināśaḥ syātkaṭutailasya pūraṇāt \|*  
*haridrā nimbapatrāṇi pippalyo maricāni ca \|\| 9 \|\|*

*viḍaṅgabhadraṃ mustañca saptamaṃ viśvabheṣajam \|*  
*gomūtreṇa ca piṣṭvaiva kṛtvā ca vaṭikāṃ hara ! \|*  
*ajīrṇahṛdbhaveccaikaṃ dvayaṃ viṣūcikāpaham \|\| 10 \|\|*

6-10. A compound of the ashes of dry Millakam and 6unthl, Hingu, Mahausadham, $atapuspa, Vaca, Kustham, Daru, 6igru, Rasayanam, Sauvarcalam, Yavaksara, Sarjakam, Saindhavam, Granthi, Vidam, Mustatakam, with four times as much honey, as well as a medicinal oil cooked in combination with the expressed juice of Matulunga and Kadali, undoubtedly arrests all kinds of discharge. Pourings of mustard oil into the ears tend to destroy the local parasites. О Нага, take Haridra Nimba-leaves, Pippali, Visvabhesajam, Maricam, Vidanga, Bhadram and Musta, pound them together, reduce them to the consistency of a paste with the addition of cow's urine, and divide the mass into pills. One pill of this compound is potent enough to cure indigestion, two of these pills cure cholera.

## \|\| 179.11 \|\|
