## \|\| 183.11 \|\|

*gaḍūcīpadmakāriṣṭadhānyākaṃ raktacaṃndanam \|*  
*pittaśleṣmajvaracchardidāhatṛṣṇāghnamagnikṛt \|*  
*oṃ huṃ nama iti \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. A decoction of Guduci Padmaka, Aristham, Dhanyakam and Rakta Candanam proves curative in the Pittaja type of fever, attended with thirst, vomiting and a burning sensation in the body,

## \|\| 183.12-13 \|\|

*śrotre baddhvā śaṅkhapuṣpīṃ jvaraṃ mantreṇa vai haret \|*  
*oṃ jambhinī stambhinī mohaya sarvavyādhīnme vajreṇa ṭhaḥ ṭhaḥ sarvavyādhīnme vajreṇa phaṭ iti \|\| 12 \|\|*

*puṣpamaṣṭaśataṃ japtvā haste dattvā nakhaṃ spṛśet \|*  
*cāturthiko jvaro rudra anye caiva jvarāstathā \|\| 13 \|\|*

12-13. Sankhapuspi, maystically dynamised with the recitation of the Mantra, Om, Hum, Namah, and tied round the ear of a fever-patient, acts as a sure febrifuge remedy. О Rudra, put into the hands of a fever-patient eight hundred flowers, each consecrated with the maystic formula, Om Jambhinl, StambhinI (destroying and paralysing goddess), Mohaya (make spell bound) Sarva Vyadhin (all diseases) Me (or mine), Vajrena Thah Thati Sarva Vyadhin Vajrena (dissipate with the thunder, like mystic potency of "Tha" Mantra the morbi-fic energies of all diseases), Phat (obeisance), and touch the tips of his finger-nails. All forms of fever and specially quotidian ague may be destroyed by practising this fever-charm.

## \|\| 183.14 \|\|

*jmbūphalaṃ haridrā ca sarpasyaiva tu kañcukam \|*  
*sarvajvarāṇāṃ dhūpo 'yaṃ haraścāturthikasya ca \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Fumigation of the body of the patient with the vapours of a burning febrifuge-stick composed of Jamboline fruits, Haridra and the cast off skip of a snake, pasted together and dried, proves curative, О Rudra, in all froms of fever, and in quotidian ague in special.

## \|\| 183.15 \|\|

*karavīraṃ bhṛṅgapatraṃ lavaṇaṃ kuṣṭhakarkaṭe \|*  
*caturguṇena mūtreṇa pacettailaṃ harecca tat \|*  
*pāmāṃ vicarcikāṃ kuṣṭhamabhyaṅgāddhi vraṇāni vai \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. A medicinal oil cooked in combination with Karavira, Bhrnga-leaves, rock salt, Kustham. Karkatam, and cow's urine, four times, as much as its (oil's) actual weight, proves remedial to ulcers and Pama, Vicarcika and other kindred diseases of the skin.

## \|\| 183.16 \|\|

*pippalīmadhupānācca tathā madhurabhojanāt \|*  
*plīhā vinaśyate rudra tathā sūraṇasevanāt \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. О Rudra, Pippalis taken with honey, or the use of Surana and other sweet articles of diet would prove beneficial in cases of splenic enlargement.

## \|\| 183.17 \|\|

*pippalīñca haridrāñca gomūtreṇa samanvitām \|*  
*prakṣipecca gudadvāre arśāṃsi vinivārayet \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. A compound of Pippall and Haridra pasted together with cow's urine and inserted into the rectum leads to the falling off of rectal haemorrhoids (piles).

## \|\| 183.18-19 \|\|

*ajādugdhamārdrakañca pītaṃ plīhādināśanam \|*  
*saindhavañca viḍaṅgāni somarājī tu sarṣapāḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*rajanī dve viṣañcaiva gomūtreṇaiva peṣayet \|*  
*kuṣṭhanāśaśca tallepānnimbapatrādinā tathā \|\| 19 \|\|*

18-19. Goat's milk admixtured with the expressed juice of Ardrakam should be prescribed for the cure of splenic enlargement. Plasters of Nimba leaves pasted with cow's urine, or of those composed of Saindhavam, Vidanga, Somayaji Sarsapa, Visam and the two kinds of Rajani Haridra and Daru-Haridra) pasted together with cow's urine, and applied to the skin, prove highly beneficial in all forms of cutaneous affections.

## Chapter 184

## \|\| 184.1 \|\|

*hariruvāca \|*  
*rajanīkadalīkṣāralepaḥ sidhmavināśanaḥ \|*  
*kuṣṭhasya bhāgamekantu pathyābhāgadvayaṃ tathā \|*  
*uṣṇodakena saṃpīya kaṭiśūlavināśanam \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Hari said: — Plasters of Rajani and the ashes of plantain bark pasted together with water, or one part of Kusfham and two parts of Pathya taken with hot water relieve an aching pain about the waist and sacrum.

## \|\| 184.2 \|\|

*abhayā navanītañca śarkarāpippalīyutam \|*  
*pānādarśoharaṃ syācca nātra kāryā vicāraṇā \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Abhaya taken with water, or Pippall taken with sugar, cures rectal haemorrhoids.

## \|\| 184.3 \|\|

*āṭarūṣakapatreṇa ghṛtaṃ mṛdvagninā pacet \|*  
*cūrṇaṃ kṛtvā tu lepo 'yaṃ arśarogaharaḥ paraḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Cook a Ghritam with powders, and the expressed juice, of AjarOsakam leaves. Plasters of this Ghrtam are highly beneficial in cases of rectal haemorrhoids.

## \|\| 184.4 \|\|

*guggulutriphalāyuktaṃ pītvā naśyedbhagandaram \|*  
*ajājīśṛṅgaverañca dathā maṇḍaṃ vipācayet \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Potions of Triphala-decoctions taken with Guggulu will bring about the cure in a case of fistula in ano, The cream (surface layer) of milk curd cooked in combination with Ajaji and Srngaveram and taken with salt removes strangury.

## \|\| 184.5 \|\|

*lavaṇena tu saṃyuktaṃ mūtrakṛcchravināśanam \|*  
*yavakṣāraṃ śarkarā ca mūtrakṛcchravināśakṛt \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Solutions of sugar and Yava-Ksaram (impure carbonate of potash) prove remedial in strangury and suppression of urine.

## \|\| 184.6 \|\|

*citāgniḥ khañjarīṭasya viṣṭhā pheno hayasya ca \|*  
*saubhāñjanaṃ vāsanetraṃ nara etaistu dhūpitaḥ \|*  
*adṛśyastridaśaiḥ sarvaiḥ kiṃ punarmānavaiḥ śiva \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Make a collyrium with the excreta of a Khafljana, Sobhahjanan, and the foam of a horse's mouth over the fire of a cremation ground, By applying this colyrium to his eyes, a person remains invisible to the celestials, not to speak of purblind human beings.

## \|\| 184.7 \|\|

*tilatailaṃ yavāndagdhvā maṣīṃ kṛtvā tu lepayet \|*  
*tenaiva saha tailena agnidagdhaḥ sukhī bhavet \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Plasters of burnt barley corn pasted with seasam oil relieve the burning sensation in cases of scald or burn. Plasters of Lajjalu and 6arapunkha pasted together with clarified butter relieve the heat in cases of scald or burn.

## \|\| 184.8-11 \|\|

*lajjāloḥ śarapuṅkhāyā lepaḥ sājyo 'gnināśanaḥ \|*  
*oṃ namo bhagavate ṭha ṭha chindhi chindhi jvalanaṃ prajvalitaṃ nāśaya nāśaya huṃ phaṭ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*kare baddhaṃ tu nirguṇḍyā mūlaṃ jvaraharaṃ drutam \|*  
*mūlañca śvetaguñjāyāḥ kṛtvā tatsaptakhaṇḍakam \|\| 9 \|\|*

*haste badhvā nāśayecca arśāṃsyeva na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*viṣṇukrāntājamūtreṇa cauravyāghnādirakṣaṇam \|\| 10 \|\|*

*brahmadaṇḍyāstu mūlāni sarvakarmāṇi kārayet \|*  
*triphalāyāstu cūrṇaṃ hi sājyaṃ kuṣṭhavināśanam \|\| 11 \|\|*

8-11. These plasters should be applied by reciting the mystic formula running as, Om Namo Bhagavate, Tha, Tha, Chidhni Chindhi Jvalanam Prajvalitam Nasaya Kenya, Hriim Fut, Nirgunditied round the wrist destroy fever. A root of white Gunja divided into seven pieces and tied round the arms of a patient undoubtedly cures rectal haemorrhoids. Smearing of the body with a plaster composed of Visnukranta pasted with goat's urine gives an immunity from the attacks of thieves and tigers. All magical acts may be practised with the help of a Brahmadandl — a root. Triphala taken with clarified butter relieve all forms of cutaneous affections.

## \|\| 184.12 \|\|

*ājyaṃ punarnavābilvaiḥ pippalībhi sādhitam \|*  
*hareddhakkāṃ śvāsakāsau pītaṃ strīṇāñca garbhakṛt \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Powders of Punamava. Bilva and Pippall pounded together and taken with clarified butter remove cough/ hiccough and asthma; administered to women they facilitate conception.

## \|\| 184.13 \|\|

*bhakṣayedvā narībījaṃ payasājyena pācitam \|*  
*ghṛtaśarkarayā yuktaṃ śukraḥ syādakṣayastataḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. The foregoing drugs, cooked in combination with milk or clarified butter and taken with the same adjuncts, acquire a splendid spermato- poetic property.

## \|\| 184.14 \|\|

*viḍaṅgaṃ madhukaṃ pāṭhāṃ māṃsīṃ sarjarasaṃ tathā \|*  
*rahidrāṃ triphalāñcaiva mapāmārgaṃ manaḥ śilām \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Take Vidanga, Madhukam, Pate, Mansi, Sarjarasam, Haridra, Triphala, Apamarga, Manah&la.

## \|\| 184.15 \|\|

*udumbaraṃ dhātakīñca tilatailena paṣeyet \|*  
*yoniṃ liṅgaṃ ca mrakṣeta strīpusoḥ syātpriyaṃ mithaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Audumbara, and Dhatakl. Pound them together and reduce this pulverised compound to the consistency of a paste with the addition of sesame oil. By plastering their own reproductive organs with this paste, a man and a woman became extremely enamoured of each other.

## \|\| 184.16 \|\|

*namaste īśavaradāya ākarṣiṇi vikarṣiṇi mugdhe svāhā iti \|*  
*yonilaṅgasya tailena śaṅkara mlakṣaṇāttataḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. The lubrication of the organs should be followed by the recitation of mystic formula running as, Namaste Isa Vardaya AkarsinI, VikarsinI Mugdha svaha (obeisance to the god who is the grantor of boons, obeisance to the goddess who attracts draws and fascinates every creature).

## \|\| 184.17-18 \|\|

*punarnavāmṛtā dūrvā kanakañcaindravāruṇī \|*  
*bīje naiṣāṃ jātikāyā rasena rasamardanam \|\| 17 \|\|*

*mūṣāya madhyagaṃ kṛtvā rasaṃ māraṇamīritam \|*  
*madhvājyasahitaṃ dugdhaṃ valīpalitanāśanam \|\| 18 \|\|*

17-18. Such enamoured pairs shall rub the palms of their hands with a compound of the seeds of Punarnava, Amrta, Durva, Kanakam, and IndravarunI, pasted together with the expressed juice of Jatika. The killing of Rasa (mercury) consists in rubbing the mineral with the seeds of the foregoiong drugs pasted together with the expressed juice of Jati as described in the preceding line, and then in boiling it in closed crucible. Milk taken in combination with honey and clarified butter arrests the advent of premature old age.

## \|\| 184.19 \|\|

*madhvājyaṃ guḍatāmrañca kāravellarasastathā \|*  
*dahanācca bhavedraupyaṃ suvarṇakaraṇaṃ śṛṇu \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Copper, burnt in combination with honey, clarified butter, treacle and the expressed juice of Karavella, is soon converted into silver. Now hear me describe the method of converting a base metal into gold.

## \|\| 184.20 \|\|

*pītaṃ dharattūpuṣpañca sīsakañca palaṃ matam \|*  
*lāṅgalikāyāḥ śākhā ca svarṇañca dahanādbhavet \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. A Palam weight of lead burnt in combination with a Palam weight of yellow Dhatora flower and twigs of Langalika is easily converted into pure gold.

## \|\| 184.21 \|\|

*dhattūrabījatailena dīpaprajvalanāddhara \|*  
*samādhāvupaviṣṭantu gaganastho na paśyati \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. By burning Dhastura oil in a lamp while seated in Samadhi Yoga, a Yogin can remain invisible even to the sky-scaling divinities.

## \|\| 184.22 \|\|

*vṛṣasya mṛnmayasyaiva yukto bheko nigṛhyate \|*  
*śaṅkarāvayavairyukto dhūpaṃ ghrātvā ca garjati \|*  
*vismayaṃ kurute caiva vṛṣavannātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. A clay figure of a bull, moulded in the attitude of killing a frog, О Sankara, will commence to bellow as a living one, on being fumigated with the vapours of the aforesaid Dhustura oil.

## \|\| 184.23 \|\|

*rātrau ca sārṣapaṃ tailaṃ kīṭaṃ khadyo tanāmakam \|*  
*tābhyāṃ dīpaḥ prajvalito vāgmijvālakalāpavat \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Mustard oil burned in a lamp tends to destroy fire-flies. Fire-flies and mustard oil burnt together ina lamp will produce a glaring light like a conflagration.

## \|\| 184.24 \|\|

*cūrṇaṃ chucchundarīdhaṃ dagdhvā rudra pralepayet \|*  
*tapyate takṣaṇāddagdho yadi samyakpralepayet \|*  
*candanena bhavenmokṣaḥ pānāllepātsukhī bhavet \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Burn down the powders of the cropse of a deat rat; plaster any part of the body with this burnt powder, and it will be found to be burnt in its turn, which may be alleviated with plasters or potions of pasted sandal wood.

## \|\| 184.25 \|\|

*kuñjarasya madāktasya svayaṃ netre śivavāñjayet \|*  
*yuddhe vijayate so 'pi mahāśūraśca jāyate \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. О Shiva, by personally applying a collyrium to the eyes of an infuriated elephant, a man is sure to win a victory in battle and turn out a valorous hero.

## \|\| 184.26 \|\|

*dantaṃ ḍuṇḍubhasarpasya mukhe saṃgṛhya vai kṣipet \|*  
*tiṣṭhate ca jalāntastu nirvikalpaṃ sthale yathā \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. By retaining the skin of a Dundubha snake in his mouth, a person can stay under water as canfortably as on land.

## \|\| 184.27 \|\|

*kumbhīranetradaṃṣṭrāśca asthīni rudhiraṃ tathā \|*  
*vasātailasamāyuktamekatra tanniyojayet \|*  
*ātmānaṃ mlakṣayettena jale tiṣṭheddinatrayam \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. By smearing his body with a compound of the teeth, bones and eyes of a crocodile pasted with the blood and fat of that animal, a person may comfortably stay under water.

## \|\| 184.28 \|\|

*kumbhīrakasya netrāṇi hṛdayaṃ kacchapasya ca \|*  
*mūṣikasya vasāsthīni śiśumāravasā tathā \|*  
*etānyekatra saṃlepājjale tiṣṭhedyathā gṛhe \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. By smearing his body with a compound consisting of the eyes of a crocodile, the heart of a tortoise and the bones of a rat pasted together with rat's lard and that of a tortoise, a man can stay under water as easily as in a chamber of his own house.

## \|\| 184.29 \|\|

*lohacūrṇaṃ takrapītaṃ pāṇḍurogaharaṃ bhavet \|*  
*taṇḍulīya kagokṣūramūlaṃ pītaṃ payonvitam \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Powders of iron taken with whey prove curative in jaundice. Roots to Tandullyakam and Goksuram, pasted together and administered through the medium of milk, cure chlorosis and affections of the mouth.

## \|\| 184.30-31 \|\|

*kamalādiharaṃpitaṃ mukharogaharaṃ tathā \|*  
*jātīmūlaṃ takrapītaṃ kolamūlaṃ tvajīrṇanut \|\| 30 \|\|*

*satakraṃ kuśamalaṃ vā markaṭī mūlameva vā \|*  
*kāñjikena ca vākucyā mūlaṃ vai dantaroganut \|\| 31 \|\|*

30-31. Jati roots or Kola roots, taken with whey, reileve indigestion. Kusa roots or Vakuci roots taken with Kanjikam relieve diseases of the teeth.

## \|\| 184.32 \|\|

*tathendravāruṇīmūlaṃ vāripītaṃ viṣādihṛt \|*  
*surabhikāmūlapā nādvā tannāśo bhavecchiva \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Roots of Indra-Varum taken with water exercise an antitoxic virtue; the roots of Surabhika prove remedial to diseases of the nervoeus system.

## \|\| 184.33 \|\|

*śirorogaharaṃ lepādguñjācūrṇaṃ sakāñjikam \|*  
*balā cātibalā yaṣṭī śarkarā madhusaṃyutā \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Plasters of Gunja-powders pasted with Kanjikam and applied to the scalp prove remedial to diseases of the head (cephalagia). By a taking a compound (decoction) of Vala, Ativala, and Yas ti, sweetaned with the addition of Sugar and honey, even a sterile woman is sure to conceive.

## \|\| 184.34 \|\|

*vandhyāgarbhakarī pītā nātra kāryā vicāraṇā \|*  
*śvetāparājitāmūlaṃ pippalīśuṇṭhikāyutam \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. A plaster composed of white Aparajita roots, Pippall and 6unthi, pasted together with water and applied to the scalp, proves curative m Cephalagia (head-ache).

## \|\| 184.35 \|\|

*paripiṣṭaṃ śirolepācchiraḥ śūlavināśanam \|*  
*nirguṇḍikāśikhāṃ pītvā gaṇḍamālāṃ vināśayet \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. О thou blissful one, Gunja-roots pasted with Kanjikam and applied to the scalp, relieve headache, Aratnika roots boiled with water impart a pleasant colour to the palate. Decoctions of clustered sprouts of Nirgundika prove curative in scrofula:

## \|\| 184.36 \|\|

*ketakīpatrajaṃ kṣāraṃ guḍena saha bhakṣayet \|*  
*takreṇa śarapuṅkhāṃ vā pītvā plīhāṃ vināśayet \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Ashes of burnt Ketaki leaves taken with treacle, or 6arapunkhas taken with whey, cure splenic enlargement.

## \|\| 184.37 \|\|

*mātulaṅgasya niryāsaṃ guḍājyena samanvitam \|*  
*vātapittajaśūlāni hanti vai pānayogataḥ \|*  
*śuṇṭhī sauvarcalaṃ hiṅgu pītaṃ hṛdayaroganut \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Exudations of Matuluga taken with treacle and clarified butter relieve the type of colic (Gastralia) due to the actions of the deranged Vayu, and Pittam. Decoctions of SunthI taken with Sauvarcala and Hingu prove antidotal to diseases of the heart.

## Chapter 185

## \|\| 185.1 \|\|

*\|*  
*hariruvāca \|*  
*āṃ gaṇapataye iti ayaṃ gaṇapaternmantro dhanavidyāpradāyakaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Hari said: — Om, Ayam Ganapataye Svaha (obesiance to the lord of the Ganas)

## \|\| 185.2 \|\|

*imamaṣṭasahasrañca japtvā baddhvā śikhāṃ tataḥ \|*  
*vyavahāre jayaḥ syācca śataṃ jāpānnṛṇāṃ priyaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. By eight thousand times repeating this Mantram; and by tying up the tuft of hair on one's crown in a knot subsequent to that, one is sure to come victorious out of a royal court of justice and to be a favourite with kings.

## \|\| 185.3 \|\|

*tilānāṃ tu ghṛtāktānāṃ kṛṣṇānāṃ rudra homayet \|*  
*aṣṭottarasahasrantu rājā vaśyastribhirdinaiḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. О Rudra, a thousand and eight libations of clarified butter containing black sesame should be cast in the fire with the recitation of this opulencegiving (Ganapati) Mantra for acquring a mastery over the minds of kings and ladies.

## \|\| 185.4 \|\|

*aṣṭamyāñca caturdaśyāmupoṣyābhyarcya vighnarāṭ \|*  
*tilākṣatānāṃ juhuyādaṣṭottarasahasrakam \|*  
*apājitaḥ syādyuddhe ca sarve tañca siṣevire \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Having fasted, and worshipped the lord of impediments under the auspices of the eighth or the fourteenth day of a lunar month, one should cast a thousand and eight oblations of sesame and white mustard seeds in fire, whereby oen would be invincible in battle, and all the inmates of the world would be brought under one's control.

## \|\| 185.5 \|\|

*japtvā cāṣṭasahasrantu tataścāṣṭaśatena hi \|*  
*śikhāṃ baddhvā rājakule vyavahāre jayo bhavet \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Having tied up the tuft of hair on his crown into a knot after eight thousand and eight hundred times repeating the Mantram sacred to this divinity, a man would return victorious from a royal court or tribunal.

## \|\| 185.6 \|\|

*hrīṅkāraṃ savisargañca prātaḥ kāle narastu yaḥ \|*  
*strīṇāṃ lalāṭe vinyasya vaśatāṃ nayati dhruvam \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. The man, who repeats the Hrmkara Mantra appended with a Visarga, each morning, by psychically projecting and locating it in the forehead of a woman, is sure to bring her under his control.

## \|\| 185.7 \|\|

*susamāhitacittena vinyasya pramadālaye \|*  
*sotkāmāṃ kāminīṃ kuryānnātra kāryā vicāraṇā \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. By psychically projecting and locating the same Mantram in the reproductive organ of a woman, one can make her made with amorous propulsions.

## \|\| 185.8 \|\|

*juhuyādayutaṃ yastu śuciḥ prayatamānasaḥ \|*  
*dṛṣṭimātre sadā tasya vaśyamāyānti yoṣitaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. He, who in a pure and tranquil mind casts ten thousand libations of clarified butter in fire by repeating this Mantram, is sure to bring a woman under his control at the first sight.

## \|\| 185.9 \|\|

*manaḥ śilāpatrakañca sagorocanakuṅkumam \|*  
*kṛta ebhiśca tilake vaśyamāyānti yoṣitaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. A Tilaka mark composed of realgar, saffron, ox-gall and Patrakam pasted together and put on his forehead by a man enables him to fascinate the members of the softer sex.

## \|\| 185.10 \|\|

*bhṛṅgarāṭ sahadevā ca vacā śvetāparājitā \|*  
*tenaiva tilakaṃ kṛtvā trailokyaṃ vaśatāṃ nayet \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. A Tilaka mark composed of white Aparajita, Bhrhgaraja, Vaca and Sahadeva, pasted together and put on his forehead by a man enables him to charm the three worlds.

## \|\| 185.11 \|\|

*gorocanā mīnapittamābhyāñca kṛtavartikaḥ \|*  
*yaḥ pumāṃstilakaṃ kuryādvāmahastakaniṣṭhayā \|*  
*sa karoti vaśe sarvaṃ trailokyaṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. A Tilaka mark composed of fishes gall and ox gall pasted together and put on his forehead by a man with the tip of his left small finger, enables him to fascinate the three worlds.

## \|\| 185.12 \|\|

*gorocanā mahādeva ! dhātuśoṇitabhāvitā \|*  
*etairvaitilakaṃ kṛtvā sā naraṃ yaṃ nirīkṣate \|*  
*tatkṣaṇāttaṃ vaśe kuryā nnātra kāryā vicāraṇā \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. A Tilaka mark composed of ox-gall treated with her catamenial blood in the manner of a Bhavana and impressed on her forehead by a woman enables her to fascinate a man at the first sight..

## \|\| 185.13 \|\|

*nāgeśvarañca śaileyaṃ tvakpatrañca harītakī \|*  
*candanaṃ kuṣṭhasūkṣmailāraktaśālisamanvitā \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. О thou supreme deity, a fumigation of the body with the vapours of a (burning) fumigating compound composed of Nagesvaram, Saileyam, Tvak, Patram, Haritaki, Candanam, Kustham, red Shali and small Ela pounded together gives a man the power of fascination.

## \|\| 185.14-15 \|\|

*etairdhūpo vaśakaraḥ smarabāṇaiḥ smārārdanaḥ \|*  
*ratikāle mahādeva pārvatīpriya śaṅkara \|\| 14 \|\|*

*nijaśukraṃ gṛhī tvā tu vāmahastena yaḥ pumān \|*  
*kāminīcaraṇaṃ vāmaṃ liṃpetsa syātstriyāḥ priyaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

14-15. О thou supreme deity, О thou beloved of Parvati, let a man, during an act of sexual congress, take his own seed, and smear the left leg of the woman therewith with his left hand, whereby he is sure to bring her under his control.

## \|\| 185.16 \|\|

*saindhavañca mahādeva pārāvatamalaṃ madhu \|*  
*ebhirlipte tu liṅge vai kāminīvaśakṛdbhavet \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. О thou supreme deity, the application of a plaster composed of pigeon's dung and rock-salt pasted together with honey by a man, before an act of coitus, to his own reproductive organ, enables him to bring the woman under his control.

## \|\| 185.17 \|\|

*puṣpāṇi pañcaraktāni gṛhītvā yāni kāni ca \|*  
*tattulyañca priyaṅguñca peṣayedekayogataḥ \|*  
*anena liptaliṅgasya kāminīvaśatāmiyāt \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Take five red flowers of different species, and Priyangu, equal in weight with these flowers and paste them together. The plastering of his reproductive organ with this paste, before an act of sexual union, given a man the power of fascinating the woman.

## \|\| 185.18 \|\|

*hayagandhā ca mañjiṣṭhā mālatīkusumāni ca \|*  
*śvetasaṣarpa etaiśca liptaliṅgaḥ striyāḥ priyaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. A plaster composed of Asvagandha. Manjlstha, Malati-flowers and white Sarsapa pasted together and applied as the preceding one makes its applier endeared of women.

## \|\| 185.19 \|\|

*mūlantu kākajaṅghāyā dugdhapītantu śoṣanut \|*  
*aśvagandhānāgabalāguḍamāṣaniṣeviṇaḥ \|*  
*rūpaṃ bhavedyathā tadvannavayauvanacāriṇām \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Kakajangha roots taken with milk prove curative in pulmonary consumption. By regularly taking a compound of Asvagandha. Masa pulse and treacle, an old man may be young over again.

## \|\| 185.20 \|\|

*lauhacūrṇasamāyuktaṃ triphalācūrṇameva vā \|*  
*madhunā sevitaṃ rudra pariṇāmākhyaśūlanut \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. О Rudra, powders of Triphala and iron, taken with honey, relieve the type of Gastralgia known as Parinama 3ula.

## \|\| 185.21 \|\|

*kvathitodakapānantu śambūkakṣārakaṃ tathā \|*  
*mṛgaśṛṅgaṃ hyagnidagdhaṃ gavyājyena samanvitam \|*  
*pīta hṛtpṛṣṭhaśūlānāṃ bhavennāśakaraṃ śiva \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Use of boiled water containing alkalis made of burnt 6ambuka (a species of mollusc) shells, or of the ashes of a burnt stag-horn through the vehicle of clarified butter, proves efficacious, О 3iva, in cases of aching (neuralgic) pain at the chest and back.

## \|\| 185.22 \|\|

*hiṅgu sauvarcalaṃ śuṇṭhī vṛṣadhvaja mahauṣadham? \|*  
*ebhistu kvathitaṃ vāri pītaṃ vai sarvaśūlanut \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. О thou bull-ensigned deity, water boiled with Hingu, Sauvarcalam 6unthl, and Mahausadham relieves and forms of cloic.

## \|\| 185.23-25 \|\|

*apāmārgasya vai mūlaṃ sāmudralavaṇānvitam \|*  
*āsvādi tamajīrṇasya śūlasya syādvimardanam \|\| 23 \|\|*

*vaṭarohāṅkuro rudra taṇḍulodakagharṣitaḥ \|*  
*pītaḥ satakro 'tīsāraṃ kṣayaṃ nayati śaṅkara \|\| 24 \|\|*

*aṅkoṭamūlaṃ karṣārdhaṃ piṣṭaṃ taṇḍulavāriṇā \|*  
*sarvātīsāragrahaṇīṃ pītaṃ harati bhūtapa \|\| 25 \|\|*

23-25. Apamarga roots taken with sea-brine cures all forms of indigestion and colic. О Rudra, О thou blissful one, sprouts of a Vata tree rubbed with the washings of rice should be administered for the purpose of curing any form of dysentery. A half Karsa measure of Ankata roots taken with the washings of rice relieves all forms of dysentery.

## \|\| 185.26 \|\|

*marīcaśuṇṭhikuṭajatvakcūrṇañca guḍānvitam \|*  
*kramāttaddviguṇaṃ pītaṃ grahaṇīvyādhināśanam \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. A compound consisting of Maricam, Sunthi, twice as much as Maricam, and Kutaja twice as much as Sunthi, taken with treacle, tends to allevite all froms of dysentery.

## \|\| 185.27 \|\|

*śvetāparājitāmūlaṃ haridrāsikthataṇḍulāḥ \|*  
*apāmārgatrikaṭukameṣāñca vaṭikā śiva \|*  
*viṣūcikāmahāvyādhiṃ haratyeva na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. О Siva, pills composed of Haridra, Tandulam Apamarga, Trikatu, and the roots of white Aparajita pasted together with Siktham, undoubtedly alleviate all forms of cholera.

## \|\| 185.28-30 \|\|

*triphalāguru bhūteśa śilājatu harītakī \|*  
*ekaikameṣāṃ cūrṇantu madhunā ca vimiśritam \|*  
*pītaṃ sarvañca mehantu kṣayaṃ nayati śaṅkara \|\| 28 \|\|*

*arkakṣīraprasthamekaṃ tilatailaṃ tathaiva ca \|*  
*manaḥ śilāmarīcānāṃ sindūrasya palaṃ palam \|\| 29 \|\|*

*cūrṇaṃ kṛtvā tāmrapātre tvātapaiḥ śoṣayettataḥ \|*  
*pītaṃ snuhīgataṃ dugdhaṃ saindhavaṃ śūlanudbhavet \|\| 30 \|\|*

28-30. A compound consisting of Trikatu, Triphala, 6ilajatu, and Haritaki pounded together and taken with honey, proves curative, О Sankara, in all forms of urinary complaints (Meha). 'fake one Palam of Manah-sila, one Palam of Maricam, and one Palam of SindCiram; pound them together and keep them soaked in a Prastha measure of sesame oil and the milky exudations of Arka plants in a copper vessel. Dry this compound in shade; this compound, as well as rocksalt taken with the milky exudations of a Snuhl plant, would be found to be highly efficacious in relieving all forms of colic (and neuralgic pain as well).

## \|\| 185.31-32 \|\|

*trikaṭutriphalānaktaṃ tilatailaṃ tathaiva ca \|*  
*manaḥ śilā nimbapatraṃ jātīpuṣpamajāpayaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*tanmūtraṃ saṅkhanābhiśca candanaṃ gharṣayettataḥ \|*  
*ebhiśca vartikāṃ kṛtvā tvakṣiṇī cāñjayettataḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

31-32. Take Trikatu, Triphala, Alaktam, sesame oil, Realgar, Nimba leaves, Jati flowers, goat's milk, sankha-nabhi, Candana, and goat's urine, mix them together and make the mass into a stick. An application of this stick, pasted with water, to the eyes in the manner of a collyrium, cures loss of vision, cataract, and kindred occular affections.

## \|\| 185.33-34 \|\|

*naśyate paṭalaṃ kācaṃ puṣpañca timirādikam \|*  
*vibhītakasya vai cūrṇaṃ samadhu śvāsanāśanam \|\| 33 \|\|*

*pippalītriphalācūrṇaṃ madhusaindhavasaṃyutam \|*  
*sarvarogajvaraśvāsaśoṣapīnasahṛdbhavet \|\| 34 \|\|*

33-34. Powders of Vibhfaka seeds taken with honey relieve all forms of asthma; a compound of Triphala, Pippall and rock-salt pounded together and taken with honey proves beneficial in all forms of fever, cough, catarrh, asthma (brounchites) and Pthisis.

## \|\| 185.35 \|\|

*devadārośca vai cūrṇaṃ ajāmatreṇa bhāvayet \|*  
*ekaviṃśativāraṃvaitvakṣiṇī tena cāñjayet \|*  
*rātryandhatā paṭalatā naśyennirlomatā tathā \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Soak Devadaru.powders with goat's urine, and dry them in shade, to this twenty-one times in succession; the application of this medicine to the eyes in the manner of a collyrium proves, curative in night-blindness, loss of vision, and falling off of the eye-lashes.

## \|\| 185.36 \|\|

*pippalīketakaṃ rudra haridrāmalakaṃ vacā \|*  
*sarvākṣirogā naśyeyuḥ sakṣīrādañjanāttataḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. О Rudra, a compound consisting of Pippall, Ketakam, Haridra. Amlakam and Vaca pounded together and applied to the eyes with the addition of milk proves beneficial in all forms of occular affections.

## \|\| 185.37 \|\|

*kākajaṅghāśigrumūle mukhena vidhṛte śiva \|*  
*carvitvā dantakīṭānāṃ vināśo hi bhaveddhara \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. O Siva, roots of Sigru and Kakajangha kept in the mougth or chewed together tend of relieve all diseases of the teeth.

## Chapter 186

## \|\| 186.1-2 \|\|

*hariruvāca \|*  
*pītaḥ sāro guḍūcyāśca madhunā ca pramehanut \|*  
*pītaṃ gohālikāmūlaṃ tiladadhyājyasaṃyutam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*niruddhamūtraṃ kvathitaṃ nivartayati śaṅkara \|*  
*tathā hikkāṃ haretpītaṃ sauvarcalayutañca vai \|\| 2 \|\|*

1-2. Hari said: — The expressed juice, or sulphate of, GuducI, taken with honey, cures all forms of Meha (urethral or urinary complaints). A decoction of Gohalika roots and sesame, taken through the vehicle of milkcurd and clarified butter, tends to set flow the suppressed urine. The same docoction taken with Sauvarcala salt

## \|\| 186.3 \|\|

*gorakṣakarkaṭīmūlaṃ piṣṭaṃ śītodakena ca \|*  
*pītaṃ dinatrayeṇaiva nāśayedrudra śarkarām \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Roots of Goraksa and Karkati pasted with Vasya water and taken for three days in succession relieves caries of the teeth and Danta-6arkara.

## \|\| 186.4 \|\|

*piṣṭvā vai mālatīmūlaṃ grīṣmakāle samāhitam \|*  
*sādhitaṃ chāgadugdhena patiṃ śarkasyānvitam \|*  
*harenmūtranirodhañca haredvai pāṇḍuśarkarām \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. MalatJ roots (called in summer) and pasted, with goat's milk should be administered for inducing urination, as well as for the cure of Chlorosis and urinary concretions.

## \|\| 186.5 \|\|

*dvijayaṣṭyāśca vai mūlaṃ piṣṭaṃ taṇḍulavāriṇā \|*  
*gaṇḍamālāṃ harellepādasādhyaṃ galagaṇḍakam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Plasters of Brahmadandl pasted with ricewashings should be applied to scrotal tumours, scrofulous glands, and goitres.

## \|\| 186.6 \|\|

*rasāñjanaṃ harītakyāścūrṇaṃ tenaiva guṇṭhanāt \|*  
*nāśayetpuruṣo vyādhīnnātra kāryā vicāraṇā \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. This plaster mixed with the powders of Harltaki and Rasanjanam should be applied tothe genitals in cases of loss of manhood, or of virile impotency.

## \|\| 186.7 \|\|

*karavīramūlalepādvai lepātpūgaphalasya ca \|*  
*puṃvyādhirnaśyate rudra yogamanyaṃ vadāmyaham \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. О Rudra, a plaster composed of Puga Phalam and Karavira roots pasted together withester would remove virile impotency.

## \|\| 186.8-9 \|\|

*dantīmūlaṃ haridrā ca citrakaṃ tasya lepanāt \|*  
*bhagandaravināśaḥ syādanyaṃ yogaṃ vadāmyaham \|*  
*jalaukājagdharaktañca bhagandaramumāpate \|\| 8 \|\|*

*triphalājalaghṛṣṭañca mārjārāsthi vilepitam \|*  
*tato na prastravedraktaṃ nātra kāryā vicāraṇā \|\| 9 \|\|*

8-9. A plaster composed of Danti roots, Haridra, and Citrakam pasted together should be employed for the cure of fistula in ano. In treating a case of fistula in ano, first apply leeches to the affected part, then wash it with a solution of Triphala, and then apply a plaster of pasted cat's bone to it, whereby the discharge of blood from the locality would be undoubtedly arrested.

## \|\| 186.10 \|\|

*haridrānekavārañca snuhīkṣīreṇa bhāvitā \|*  
*vaṭikār'śovināśāya tallepādvṛṣabhadhvaja \|*  
*ghoṣāphalaṃ saindhavañca piṣṭvā cārśoharaṃ param \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. О thou bull-ensigned diety, soak Haridra with the milky exudations of Snuhl plants and dry them in shade, do this may times in succession. Applications of plasters of such Haridras pasted with water to the polypi prove curative in cases of rectal haemorrhoids. A plaster composed of Haridra and Ghost- phalam pasted together proves highly, efficacious in removing rectal haemor rhoids.

## \|\| 186.11 \|\|

*gavyājyaṃ sādhitaṃ pītaṃ palāśakṣāravāriṇā \|*  
*triguṇena trikaṭukaṃ arśāṃsi kṣapayecchiva \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. О thou blissful one, Trikalukam taken with thrice as much ashes or Alkali treated with clarified butter and dissolved in water speedily leads to the falling off of rectal polypi.

## \|\| 186.12 \|\|

*bilvasya ca phalaṃ dagdhaṃ raktārśaḥ pravināśanam \|*  
*jagdhavā kṛṣṇatilāneva navanītayutānapi \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Pulps of burnt Bilva fruits prove highly efficatious in cases of bleeding piles. Black sesame taken with butter proves efficacious in the same disease.

## \|\| 186.13 \|\|

*śuṇṭhīcūrṇaṃ yavakṣārayuktaṃ tulyaguḍānvitam \|*  
*agnivṛddhiṃ karotyeva pratyūṣe vṛṣabhadhvaja \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. О thou bull-ensigned deity, a lambative composed of Yavaksara, 6unthi powders and treacle, taken in equal parts and pasted together, and licked, each morning, improves the digestive capacity.

## \|\| 186.14 \|\|

*śuṇṭhyā ca kvathitaṃ vāri pītaṃ cāgniṃ karoti vai \|*  
*harītakīṃ saindhavañca citrakaṃ rudra pippalī \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. О Rudra, decoctions of 6unthl, or of Citrakam, Pippali and Harltaki, taken with rocksalt, proves as a good digestant and stomachic remedy.

## \|\| 186.15 \|\|

*cūrṇamuṣṇodakenaiṣāṃ pītaṃ cātikṣudhākaram \|*  
*sājyaṃ sūkaramāṃsaṃ vai pītaṃ cātikṣudhākaram \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Powders of the foregoing drugs taken with water, as well as bacon cooked with clarified butter tends to give an acute appetite.

## Chapter 187

## \|\| 187.1-2 \|\|

*hariruvāca \|*  
*hastikarṇapalāśasya patrāṇi? cūrṇayeddhara \|*  
*sarvarogavinirmuktaṃ cūrṇaṃ palaśataṃ śiva \|\| 1 \|\|*

*sakṣīraṃ bhakṣītaṃ kuryātsaptāhena vṛṣadhvaja \|*  
*naraṃ śrutidharaṃ rudra mṛgendragativikramam \|\| 2 \|\|*

1-2. О Thou dissipator of woes, take Hastikarna roots, and reduce them to powder. О Thou blissful one, a hundred Palam weight of powdered Hastikarna roots, taken with milk in the course of a week, will make its user a prodigy of memory and enable him to cope with a lion in prowess and swiftness of motion.

## \|\| 187.3 \|\|

*padmarāgapratīkāśaṃyuktaṃ daśaśatāyuṣā \|*  
*ṣoḍaśābdākṛtiṃ rudra satataṃ dugdhabhojanāt \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Taken with milk, for sixteen days in succession, these powders will impart a ruby like glow to the complexion of their user and enable him to live for a thousand-years.

## \|\| 187.4 \|\|

*madhusarpiḥsamāyuktaṃ dugdhamāyuṣkaraṃ bhavet \|*  
*tajjagdhaṃ madhunā sārdhaṃ daśavarṣa sahasriṇam \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Taken with honey and clarified butter, they tend to increase the duration of life; taken only in combination with honey, these powers make their users extremly endearing to woman and enable them to live up for another ten thousand years.

## \|\| 187.5-9 \|\|

*kuryānnaraṃ śrutidharaṃ pramadājanavallabham \|*  
*dadhnā nityaṃ bhakṣitantu vajradehakaraṃ bhavet \|\| 5 \|\|*

*keśarājisamāyuktaṃ naraṃ varṣasahasriṇam \|*  
*tacca kāñjikasaṃyuktaṃ naraṃ kuryācca bhakṣitam \|\| 6 \|\|*

*śatavarṣaṃ divyadehaṃ valīpalitavarjitam \|*  
*jagdhaṃ triphalayā kṣaudraṃ cakṣuṣmantaṃ karoti vai \|\| 7 \|\|*

*andhaḥ paśyettu cūrṇasya sājyasyaiva tu bhakṣaṇāt \|*  
*mahiṣīkṣīrasaṃyuktastallepaḥ kṛṣṇakeśakṛt \|\| 8 \|\|*

*khalvāṭasya ca vai keśā bhavanti vṛṣabhadhvaja \|*  
*tailayuktena cūrṇena valīpalitanāśanam \|\| 9 \|\|*

5-9. Taken with milk curd they impart a thunder-like hardness to the muscles; taken with the expressed juice of Kesaraji, they enable their users to live for a thousand years. By using these powders through the medium of Kanjikam, a man is enabled to live for a century without anywise suffering form the ravages of time. Taken with Triphala, they tend to improve the eye-sight; by taking them through the vehicle of clarified butter even blind persons may regain their sight. A plaster of these powders pasted with buffalo milk and applied to the head, imparts a sable colour to the hair. О thou bull-ensigned deity, applications of these powders with oil to the head remove baldness and help a luxurious growth of hair.

## \|\| 187.10 \|\|

*tadudvartanamātreṇa sarvarāgaḥ pramucyate \|*  
*sacchāgakṣīracūrṇena dṛṣṭiḥ syānmāsato 'ñjanāt \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Rubbing of the body with these powders pasted with oil removes wrinkles of the skin and premature greyness of the hair, and grants a sort of immunity from disease. These powders pasted with goat's milk and applied to the eyes, in the manner of a collyrium, for a month, improve the eye-sight.

## \|\| 187.11-12 \|\|

*palāśasya ca bījāni śrāvaṇe vituṣāṇi ca \|*  
*gṛhītvā navanītena teṣāṃ cūrṇaṃ ca bhakṣayet \|\| 11 \|\|*

*karṣārdhamekaṃ seveta natvā nityaṃ hariṃ prabhum \|*  
*purāṇaṣaṣṭidhānyasya pathyamambu pibanhara \|*  
*jīvedvarṣasahasrāṇi valīpalitavarjitaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12. Gather Palasa seeds in the month of Sravana. Reduce these seeds of powder, with their capsules off, and take this powder for six months, living on a rice and milk regimen, and abjuring the use of water. By taking this powder in the way as prescribed, a man is enabled to live for a thousand years, free from disease and decay.

## \|\| 187.13 \|\|

*bhṛṅgarājasya vai mūlaṃ puṣyarkṣe tu samāhṛtam \|*  
*vidhāya tasya cūrṇaṃ vai sasauvīrañca bhakṣayetaṃ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Cull Bhrnga-raja roots under the auspices of the asterism Pusya. Take a Vioapadam weight of this root with barley-wine for thirty days in succession.

## \|\| 187.14 \|\|

*māsamātraprayogeṇa valīpalitavarjitaḥ \|*  
*śatāni pañca jīvecca naro nāgabalo bhavet \|*  
*bhavecchrutidharo rudra puṣyarkṣe caiva bhakṣaṇāt \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Thereby a man will be able to live for five hundred years in the possession of an elephantlike strength of the body and free from disease and premature decay, and a prodigy of memory.

## Chapter 188

## \|\| 188.1 \|\|

*hariruvāca \|*  
*nirvraṇaḥ syātpūyaṃhīno prahāro ghṛpūritaḥ \|*  
*apāmārgasya vai mūlaṃ hastābhyāñca vimarditam \|*  
*tadrasena prahārasya raktastrāvo na pūraṇāt \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Hari said: — A cut, or a lacerated wound, filled with melted butter, will-heal up at the first instance without producing any pus or inflammation. The juice of Apamaga, squeezed out with finger and poured into the cavity of a cut or wound will at once arrest the bleeding.

## \|\| 188.2 \|\|

*rudra lāṅgalikāmūlaṃ cekṣudarbhastathaiva ca \|*  
*tena vraṇamukhaṃ liptaṃ śalyaṃ niḥ sa rati vraṇāt \|*  
*cirakālapraviṣṭo 'pi tena mārgeṇa śaṅkara \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. О Rudra, a plaster of Hijjala roots and Langalika roots pasted together and applied to the mouth of a wound will spontaneously expel any foreign substance, through the passage of its penetration, that might have been lodged therein, no matter how long it might have remained thus imbedded.

## \|\| 188.3 \|\|

*bālamūlaṃ meṣaśṛṅgīmūlaṃ vā vārigharṣitam \|*  
*tena liptaṃ ciraṃ jātaṃ vraṇaṃ nāḍyāḥ praśāmyati \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Applications of plasters composed of Vana roots and Mesasrhgl roots pasted together with water will bring about the healing of sinuses.

## \|\| 188.4 \|\|

*jagdhaṃ māhiṣapadhnā ca yuktaṃ kodravabhaktakam \|*  
*hiṅgumūlasya vai cūrṇaṃ dattaṃ nāḍīvraṇāpaham \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. A sinus may be healed by dusting it with powders of Kanku-roots; the patient shall be enjoined to live on curdled buffalo milk and cooked Kodrava grain during the period of treatment.

## \|\| 188.5 \|\|

*brahmayaṣṭiphalaṃ piṣṭaṃ vāriṇā tenalepitam \|*  
*tena ghṛṣṭaṃ raktadoṣaḥ praṇaśyati na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Plasters of Brahmadandl seeds pasted with water prove remedial to skin diseases due to the vitiated condition of the blood.

## \|\| 188.6-8 \|\|

*yavabhasma viḍaṅgañca gandhapāṣāṇameva ca \|*  
*śuṇṭhireṣāñcaiva cūrṇaṃ bhvitaṃ rudhireṇavai \|\| 6 \|\|*

*kṛkalāsasya talliptaṃ vidradhiṃ nāśayecchiva \|*  
*saubhāñjanasya bījāni tvatasīmasinā saha \|\| 7 \|\|*

*saurasarṣapayuktāni sarvāṇyetāni śaṅkara \|*  
*piṣṭānyanamlatakreṇa granthikaṃ nāśayeddhi vai \|\| 8 \|\|*

6-8. Take ashes of burnt barley corn, Vidanga, Gandhapasanam and Shunthi; pound them together, and soak this pulverised compound with lizard's (Krkalasa) blood and dry it in the sun in the manner of a Bhavana saturation. Apply this plaster, О diva, to abscesses and carbuncles and wonder at the result. Take Sobanjanam roots, burnt linseed, and white mustard seeds; pound them together, О Sankara, and reduce the compound to the consistency of a paste with the addition of whey, which is not acid in its flavour. Plasters of this pasted compound prove curative in Granthikam.

## \|\| 188.9 \|\|

*śvetāparājitāmūlaṃ piṣṭaṃ taṇḍulavāriṇā \|*  
*tena nasyapradānātsyādbhūtavṛndasya vidravaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. For the exorcism of a maligant spirit, an errhine composed, of white Aparajita roots pasted with rice-washings should be given to the possessed person.

## \|\| 188.10 \|\|

*agastyapuṣpanasyaṃ vai samarīcaṃ tu śūlahṛt \|*  
*bhujaṅgacarma vai hiṅgu nimbapatraṃ tathā yavāḥ \|*  
*gaurasarṣama ebhiḥ syāllepo bhūtaharaḥ śiva \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Errhines of the expressed juice of Agastya flowers, saturated with the powders of black pepper, relieve colic pain. О diva, plasters of snake-skins, Hingu, Nimba-leaves, Yava, and white Sarsapa pasted together have the virtue of exercising ghosts.

## \|\| 188.11 \|\|

*gorocanā marīcāni pippalī saindhavaṃ madhu \|*  
*añjanaṃ kṛtamebhiḥ syādgrahabhūtaharaṃ śiva \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Anjanams composed to Gorocana, Maricam, Pippali and rock salt, pasted together with honey have the virtue of warding off the influnces of malignant stars and spirit.

## \|\| 188.12 \|\|

*guggulūlūkapucchābhyāṃ dhūpo grahaharo bhavet \|*  
*cāturthikajvarairmukto kṛṣṇavastrāvaguṇṭhitaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. For relieving quotidian ague and warding of the influences of maliganant, planets, the patient should be wrapped with a black cloth and fumigated with the vapours of a compound consisting of Guggulu, and owl's feathers pounded together.

## Chapter 189

## \|\| 189.1 \|\|

*hariruvāca \|*  
*śvetāparājitāpuṣparasenākṣṇośca pūraṇe \|*  
*paṭalaṃ nāśamāyāti nātra kāryā vicāraṇā \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Hari said: — The expressed juice of the white Aparajita flowers dropped into the eyes tend to destroy the eye disease known as Patola- raga.

## \|\| 189.2 \|\|

*mūlaṃ gokṣurakasyaiva carvitvā nīlalohita \|*  
*dantakīṭavyathā naśyetsurāsuravimardan \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. О thou blue end red bodied one, О thou, the destroyer of the demon of darkness, by chewing Goksura roots, a man may destroy the parasties lodged in his teeth and may get rid of tooth-ache in consequence.

## \|\| 189.3 \|\|

*nārī puṣpādine pītvā gokṣīreṇopavāsataḥ \|*  
*śvetārkasya tu vai mūlaṃ tasyāstadgulmaśūlanut \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. By applying a plaster composed of white Arka roots pasted with cow-milk to her private parts, while observing a fast, durign er flow, a woman may get rid to th pain of Gulma.

## \|\| 189.4 \|\|

*śvetārkapuṣpaṃ vidhinā gṛhītaṃ pūrvamantritam \|*  
*ṛtuśuddhā ca lalanā kaṭau baddhvā prasūyate \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. О thou bull-ensigned deity by wearing a white Arka flower consecrate with the aforesaid Mantra round her waist during an act of sexual congress, after the suppression of her monthly flow, a woman is sure to conceive a male child.

## \|\| 189.5 \|\|

*hastabaddhaṃ palāśasya apāmārgasya vā hara \|*  
*mūlaṃ sarvajvaraharaṃ bhūtapretādinudbhavet \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. О Нага, Palasa-roots or Apamarga roots, tied round the wrist of a patient, act as good frebrifuge remedies and tend toward off the evil influences of malignant ghosts.

## \|\| 189.6 \|\|

*pītaṃ vṛścikamūlañca prātaḥ paryuṣitāmbunā \|*  
*sārdhaṃ vināśayeddāhajvarañca parameśvara \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. О thou supreme divinity, Vrscika roots pasted with water collected over night and given to a fever-patient instantaneously allay, the heat, and burning sensation in his body.

## \|\| 189.7-9 \|\|

*śikhāyāñcaiva tadbaddhaṃ bhavedaikāhikāhinut \|*  
*pītaṃ paryuṣitādbhiśca bhavetsarvaviṣāpahṛt \|\| 7 \|\|*

*yasya lajjālukāmūlaṃ dīyate ca svaretasā \|*  
*sārdhaṃ sa vairaṃ saṃyāti pumānstrī vā na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*piṣṭvā gavyaghṛtenaiva pāṭhāmūlaṃ pibettu yaḥ \|*  
*sarvaṃ viṣaṃ vinaśyecca nātra kāryā vicāraṇā \|\| 9 \|\|*

7-9. The same roots tied with the tuft of hair on the crown of a patient proves curative in daily intermittent fever; taken with Kanjikam they prove efficacious in fever and in the type of Kutham, due to the vitiated condition of blood. Taken with Vasyam water they exercise an antitoxic virtue. A bitter animosity is created between him and one, whether male or female, to whom he administers Lajjaluka roots pasted with his own seed. By taking Patha roots pasted with melted cow-butter one is relived of all effects of a poison.

## \|\| 189.10 \|\|

*mūlaṃ paryuṣitodena śirīṣasya yathā tathā \|*  
*raktacitrakamūlasya rasasya bharaṇāddhara \|*  
*karṇayoḥ kāmalāvyādhināśaḥ syānnātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Shirisa roots taken in combination with Vasyam water act as good antitoxic remedies. The expressed juice of the roots of red Chitrakam poured into the ears (of patient) proves curative in Clorosis.

## \|\| 189.11-12 \|\|

*śvetakokilākṣamūlaṃ chāgīkṣīreṇa saṃyutam \|*  
*trisaptāhena vai pītaṃ kṣayarogaṃ kṣayaṃ nayet \|\| 11 \|\|*

*nārikelasya vai puṣpaṃ chāgakṣīreṇa saṃyutam \|*  
*pibecca trividhastasya raktavāto vinaśyati \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12. The expressed juice of white Kokilaksa roots taken with goat's milk for three days in succession tends to cure Pthisis. Cocoanut flowers taken in combination (pasted) with goat's milk prove remedial to the three types of Vata Raktam.

## \|\| 189.13-14 \|\|

*kuryātsudarśanāmūlaṃ mālyena susamāhṛtam \|*  
*kaṇṭhabaddha tryāhikādigrahabhūtavināśanam \|\| 13 \|\|*

*puṣpaṃ dhavalaguñjāyā gṛhītaṃ mūlameva ca \|*  
*mukhe tu nihitaṃ rudra harennānāviṣaṃ bahu \|\| 14 \|\|*

13-14. A garland of Sudarsana roots tied round the neck proves curative in tertian ague and tends to ward off the influences of malignent Ghosts and planets. Roots of white Gunja plants culled under the auspices of the asterism Pusya, and kept in the mouth, act as a good prophylaxis against a variety of poisons.

## \|\| 189.15 \|\|

*haste baddhaṃ kāṇḍayuktaṃ kaṇṭhe baddhaṃ grahādihṛt \|*  
*kṛṣṇāyāntu caturdaśyāṃ kaṭibaddhaṃ samāhṛtam \|*  
*siṃhādiśvāpadādbhītiṃ harecca nīlalohita \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Tied around the wrist or the neck, the same roots tend to ward off the influences of malignant planets. О thod red and blue bodied one, these roots tied round his waist by a man under the auspices of the fourteenth day of the moon's wane grant an immunity from attacks by lions and other wild beasts.

## \|\| 189.16 \|\|

*viṣṇukrāntāmūlamīśa karṇabaddhantu dhārayet \|*  
*paṭṭasūtreṇa bhūteśa makarādibhayaṃ na vai \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. О thou supreme deity, Visnukranta roots, tied round the ears by a person act as prophylasis against attacks by crocodiles.

## Chapter 190

## \|\| 190.1 \|\|

*hariruvāca \|*  
*aparājitāyā mūlañca gomūtreṇa samanvitam \|*  
*pītañcāśu haratyeva gaṇḍamālāṃ na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Hari said: — Pasted Aparajita roots taken with cow's urine cure scrofula.

## \|\| 190.2 \|\|

*athendravāruṇīmūlaṃ vidhinā pītamīśvara \|*  
*jiṅgiṇyairaṇḍakaṃ rudra śūkaśimbyā samanvitam \|*  
*śītodakañca tatryastaṃ bāhugrīvāvyathāṃ haret \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. О Rudra, Indra-varuri roots taken with cold water, as well as errhines of solutions of Eranda, Jinganl and Shuka Slmbi pasted together tend to alleviate the pain in the neck and the arms.

## \|\| 190.3 \|\|

*māhiṣaṃ navanītañca aśvagandhā ca pippalī \|*  
*vacā kuṣṭhadvayaṃ lepo liṅgasrotastanārtihṛt \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. An application of a plaster composed of Asvagandha or Pippall, or of Vaca and Kustam. Рasted together with buffalo butter, alleviates pain in the mammae and the urethral canal.

## \|\| 190.4 \|\|

*kuṣṭhanāgabalācūrṇaṃ navanītasamanvitam \|*  
*tallepo yuvatīnāñca kuryādvṛttojakau śubhau \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. A plaster composed of Kustham and Nagavala pasted together with butter and applied to the breast acts as a good breast- developer and. imparts a graceful contour to the breasts of youthful maidens.

## \|\| 190.5 \|\|

*indravāruṇikāmūlaṃ yasya nāmnā sudūrataḥ \|*  
*niḥ kṣipyate samutpāṭya tasya plīhā vinaśyati \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. The patient, by mentioning whose name an IndravarunI root is thrown from a distance, is sure to be relieved of his splenic enlargement.

## \|\| 190.6 \|\|

*punarnavāyāḥ śuklāyā mūlaṃ taṇḍulavāriṇā \|*  
*pītaṃ vidradhinutsyācca nātra kāryā vicāraṇā \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Roots of white Punarnava taken pasted with rice washings undoubtedly prove curative in abscess.

## \|\| 190.7 \|\|

*kadalīdalakṣārantu pānīyena prasādhitam \|*  
*tasyādanādvinaśyanti udaravyādhayo 'khilāḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Ashes of burnt plaintain barks administered through drinks relieve all forms of Ascites, ill

## \|\| 190.8 \|\|

*kadalyā mūlamādāya guḍājyena samanvitam \|*  
*agninā sādhitaṃ jagdhamudarasthakrimīnharet \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Plantain roots cooked in combination with treacle and clarified butter over a gentle fire act as good vermifuge remedies.

## \|\| 190.9 \|\|

*nityaṃ nimbadalānāñca cūrṇamāmalakasya ca \|*  
*pratyūṣe bhakṣayeccaiva tasya kuṣṭhaṃ vinaśyati \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Daily use of a compound of Nimba leaves and Amlakam poimded together, in the morning, undoubtedly cures Kustham (cutaneous affection).

## \|\| 190.10 \|\|

*harītakīviḍaṅgañca haridrā sitasarṣapāḥ \|*  
*somarājasya mūlāni karañjasya ca raundhavam \|*  
*gomūtrapiṣṭānyetāni kuṣṭharogaharāṇi vai \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. A plaster composed of Haritaki, Vidanga, Haridra, white Sarsapa, Somaraja-seeds (roots according to Benares Edition), Karaja seeds and Saindhavam, pasted together with cow's urine, proves efficacious in all forms of cutaneous affections.

## \|\| 190.11 \|\|

*ekaśca triphalābhāgastathā bhāgadvayaṃ śivā \|*  
*somarājasya bījānāṃ jagdhaṃ pathyena dadrunut \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. One part of Triphala and two parts of Somaraja seeds taken in combination with powdered Pathya cure ring-worms.

## \|\| 190.12 \|\|

*amlatakraṃ sagomūtraṃ kvathitaṃ lavaṇānvitam \|*  
*kāṃsyaghṛṣṭaṃ kharaṃ lepātkuṣṭhadadruvināśanam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. A plaster composed Kharam rubbed in a vessel of Indian bell metal, pasted with cow's urine, cooked in combination with rock-salt and acid whey (Takram), prove curative in all forms of cutaneous affections.

## \|\| 190.13 \|\|

*haridrā haritālaśca dūrvāgomūtrasaindhavam \|*  
*ayaṃ lepo hanti dadruṃ pāmānaṃ ca garaṃ tathā \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. A plaster composed of Haridra, Haritalam, Durva grass and rock-salt pasted together with cow's urine proves remedial in cases of Pama and ring-worm.

## \|\| 190.14 \|\|

*soma rājasya bījāni navanītayutāni ca \|*  
*madhunāsvāditāni syuḥ śuklakuṣṭhaharāṇi vai \|*  
*takrānnapānato rudra nātra kāryā vicāraṇā \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Somaraja seeds taken in combination with butter and honey prove curative in all forms of leucoderma. О Rudra, the cure is almost certain through the administration of the foregoing compound, but the patient must live on a whey rice regimen during the period of treatment.

## \|\| 190.15 \|\|

*śvetāparā jitāmūlaṃ vartitaṃ cāsya vāriṇā \|*  
*tallepo rudra māsena śuklakuṣṭhavināśanaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Plasters, composed of white Aparajita roots pasted with Sariva and applied to the affected region, for a month, tend to cure all forms of leucoderma.

## \|\| 190.16 \|\|

*māhiṣaṃ navanītañca sindūraṃ samarīcakam \|*  
*pāmā vilepanānnaśyeddur nāmā vṛṣabhadhvaja \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. О thou bull-ensigned deity, applications of plasters composed of Maricam and Sindaram paster together with buffalo-butter would certainly cure Pama and dyspnoea.

## \|\| 190.17 \|\|

*viśuṣkagāmbhārīmūlaṃ pakvaṃ kṣīreṇa saṃyutam \|*  
*bhakṣitaṃ śuklapittasya vināśakaramīśvara \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. О thou supreme diety, dry Gambharl roots cooked in combination with milk prove antidotal to Shukla-Pittam.

## \|\| 190.18 \|\|

*mūlakasya tu bījāni hyapā mārgarasena vai \|*  
*piṣṭāni tena lepena sidhmakaṃ rudra naśyati \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Plasters of Mulaka seeds pasted with the expressed juice of Apamarga and applied to the affected part, prove, efficacious in Shilhika.

## \|\| 190.19 \|\|

*kadalīkṣārasaṃyuktaharidrā sidhmakāpahā \|*  
*rambhāpāmārgayoḥ kṣāra eraṇḍena vimiśritaḥ \|*  
*tadabhyaṅgānmahādeva ! sadyaḥ sidhma vinaśyati \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. О thou supreme deity, ashes of burnt plantain bark and Apamarga twigs pasted together with the expressed juice of Eranda and applied to the affected patches prove curative in Siddhma.

## \|\| 190.20 \|\|

*kūṣmāṇḍanālakṣāraśca sagomūtraśca tattvataḥ \|*  
*jalapiṣṭā haridrā ca siddhā mandānalenahi \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. О thou supreme deity, О thou bullensigned one, burn the ashes of a Kusmanda creeper, mixed with the bark of its stem pasted with cow's urine, and Haridra pasted with water, in a closed crucible luted and plastered with buffalo-dung.

## \|\| 190.21-22 \|\|

*māhiṣeṇa purīṣeṇa veṣṭitā vṛṣabhadhvaja \|*  
*asyā udvartanaṃ kuryādaṅgasauṣṭhavamīśvara \|\| 21 \|\|*

*tilasarṣapasaṃyuktaṃ haridrādvayakuṣṭhakam \|*  
*tenodvartitadehaḥ syāddurgandhaḥ surabhiḥ pumān \|\| 22 \|\|*

21-22. By rubbing his body with this burnt compound, a man is sure to acquire a brilliant complexion. Rubbing of the body with a compound consisting of Haridra, Daru-Haridra, and Kustham pasted together with water tends to impart a brilliant glow to the complexion and a fragrant smell to the skin.

## \|\| 190.23 \|\|

*manoharaścānudinaṃ dūrvāṇāṃ kākajaṅghāyā \|*  
*arjunasya tu puṣpāṇi jambūpatrayutāni ca \|*  
*salodhrāṇi ca tallepo dehadurgandhatāṃ haret \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Plastering of the body with Durva, Kakajangha, leaves of Arjuna and Jambu and Lodhram pasted together with water tends of remove the bad odours of the skin.

## \|\| 190.24 \|\|

*yuktaṃ lodhrabhavairnoraiścūrṇantu kanakasya ca \|*  
*tenodvartitadehasya na syādgrīṣmaprabādhikā \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Solutions of Lodhram saturated with the powers of Kumkam form the most cooling and agreeable paste for smearing the body in summer.

## \|\| 190.25 \|\|

*dugdhenoṣasi sekaśca gharmadoṣaśca naśyati \|*  
*kākajaṅghodvartanantu hyaṅgarāgakaraṃ bhavet \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Washing of the body with milk, in the morning, tends to remove the evils of perspiration; rubbing of the body with pasted Kakajangha acts as an agreeable cosmetic plaster.

## \|\| 190.26 \|\|

*madhuyaṣṭī śarkarā ca vāsakasya raso madhu \|*  
*etatpītaṃ raktapittakāmalāpāṇḍuroganut \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. The expressed juice of Vasaka and Yasti- madhu, taken with honey and sugar, proves curative in Jaundice, Chlorosis, Haemoptisis, and Haemorrhage.

## \|\| 190.27 \|\|

*raktapittaṃ haretpīto vāsakasya raso madhu \|*  
*prātaḥ kāle toyapānātpīnasaṃ dāruṇaṃ haret \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Even a most acute attack of catarrh may be cut short by taking cold water in the morning.

## \|\| 190.28 \|\|

*bibhītakasya vai cūrṇaṃ pippalyāḥ saindhavasya ca \|*  
*pītaṃ sakāñjikaṃ hanti svarabhedaṃ maheśvara \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. О thou, supreme deity, a pulverised compound of Pippall, rock salt and Vibhitakam pounded together and taken with Kanjikam removes hoarsness.

## \|\| 190.29-30 \|\|

*cūrṇamāmalakaṃ sevyaṃ pītaṃ gavyapayo 'nvitam \|*  
*manaḥ śilā balāmūlaṃ kolapaṇa ca gugguluḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*jātipatraṃ kolapatraṃ tathā caiva manaḥ śilā \|*  
*ebhiścaiva kṛtā vartirbadaryagnau maheśvara \|*  
*dhūmapānaṃ kāsaharaṃ nātra kāryā vicāraṇā \|\| 30 \|\|*

29-30. Amalakam-powder administered through the vehicle of clarified butter, or a compound consisting of Manah-sila, Vala roots, Kola- leaves and Guggulu pasted together, or inhalation of the vapours of a fumigation stick, composed of Jatipatram, Kola leaves and Manah-sila pasted together and burnt in a fire of Kola-wood charcoal would undoubtedly relieve cough.

## \|\| 190.31 \|\|

*triphalāpippalīcūrṇaṃ bhakṣitaṃ madhunāyutam \|*  
*bhojanādau hi samadhu pipāsājva(tva)ritaṃ haret \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Triphala and Pippall powders taken with honey, before the midday meal, relieve thirst and fever.

## \|\| 190.32 \|\|

*bilvamūlañca samadhuguḍūcīkvathitaṃ jalam \|*  
*pītaṃ harecca trivadhaṃ chardiṃ naivātrasaṃśayaḥ \|*  
*pītā dūrvā chardinutsyātpiṣṭātaṇḍulavāriṇā \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. The expressed juice of Bilva foots or a decoction of GuducI taken with honey arrests the three types of vomiting. Durva pasted with ricewashings proves antidotal to vomiting.

## Chapter 191

## \|\| 191.1 \|\|

*hariruvāca \|*  
*punarnavāyā mūlañca śvetaṃ puṣye samāhṛtam \|*  
*vāri pītaṃ tasya pārśva bhavaneṣu na pannagāḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Hari said: — Serpents leave the house of him, who takes Punamava roots pasted with water under the auspices of the asterism Pusya.

## \|\| 191.2 \|\|

*tārkṣyamūrtiṃ vahedyo vai bhallūkadantanirmitām \|*  
*sa pannagairna dṛśyeta yāvajjīvaṃ vṛṣadhvaja \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. О thou bull ensigned deity, he, who carries an image of Garuda, made of bear's teeth, on his person, remains invisible to snakes all through his life.

## \|\| 191.3 \|\|

*pibecchalmalimūlaṃ yaḥ puṣyarkṣe rudra vāriṇā \|*  
*tasminnapāstadaśanā nāgāḥ syurnātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. О Rudra, snakes avoid the presence of one, who takes Shalmali roots pasted with water under the auspices of the asterism Pusya.

## \|\| 191.4 \|\|

*puṣye lajjālukāmūle hastabaddhe tu pannagān \|*  
*gṛhṇīyāllepato vāpi nātra kāryā vicāraṇā \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. By tying Lajjaluka roots his hands, or by smearing them with pasted Lajjaluka, a man is enabled to catch hold of snakes without anywise imperiling his life.

## \|\| 191.5 \|\|

*puṣyeśvetārkamūlantu pītaṃ śītena vāriṇā \|*  
*naśyetu daṃśakaviṣaṃ karavīrādijaṃ viṣam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Roots of white Arka plants, taken pasted with water, under the auspices of the asterism Pusya, prove antidotal to Dank" (a large kind of mosquito) poison; Karavlra roots similarly taken are found to exercise a similar antotoxic virtue.

## \|\| 191.6 \|\|

*mahākālasya vai mūlaṃ piṣṭaṃ tatkāñjikena vai \|*  
*voḍrāṇāṃ ḍuṇḍubhānāṃ ca tallopo harate viṣam \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Plasters of Mahakala roots pasted with Kanjikam tend to neutralise the poison of Dundubha or Bodra (Boa) snakes.

## \|\| 191.7 \|\|

*taṇḍulīyakamūlaṃ ca piṣṭaṃ taṇḍulavāriṇā \|*  
*ghṛtena saha pītantu haretsarvāviṣāṇi ca \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Tandully aka-roots taken pasted with rice= washings through the medium of clarified butter (honey according to others) prove antidotal to all kinds of poison.

## \|\| 191.8 \|\|

*nīlīlajjālukāmūlaṃ piṣṭaṃ taṇḍulavāriṇā \|*  
*pītaṃ taddaṃśakaviṣaṃ naśyedekena vobhayoḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Either Nil! roots, or Lajjaluka roots taken pasted with rice-washings prove remedial to Dansaka-poison.

## \|\| 191.9 \|\|

*kūṣmāṇḍakasya svarasaḥ saguḍaḥ sahaśarkaraḥ \|*  
*pītaḥ sadugdho hanyācca daṃśakasyaviṣaṃ ca vai \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The expressed juice of a Kusmanda creeper taken with the admixture of treacle, sugar and milk tends to neutralise the poison of a Danska.

## \|\| 191.10-12 \|\|

*tathā kodravamūlasya mohasya hara eva ca \|*  
*yaṣṭīmadhusamāyuktā tathā pītā ca śarkarā \|\| 10 \|\|*

*sadugdhā ca trirātreṇa mūṣakānāṃ viṣaṃ haret \|*  
*culukatrayapānācca vāriṇaḥ śītalasya vai \|\| 11 \|\|*

*tāmbūladagdhamukhasya lālāstrāvo vinaśyati \|*  
*ghṛtaṃ saśarkaraṃ ṣītvā madyapānamado na vai \|\| 12 \|\|*

10-12. Yastimadhu taken with its own weight of sugar through the medium of milk proves antidotal to mole-poison. Gargles of cold water attest salivation due to the irritation of the mucous membrane of the mouth through chewing beetal leaves. Clarifed butter taken with suger relieves the intoxication of wine.

## \|\| 191.13 \|\|

*kṛṣṇāṅkolasya mūlena pītaṃ sukvathitaṃ jalam \|*  
*tato naśyadgaraviṣaṃ trirātreṇa maheśvara \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. О thou supreme deity, potions of black Ankata roots boiled with water, or errhines of decoctions of black Ankota roots prove remedial, within three days, to any slow poison retained in the system.

## \|\| 191.14 \|\|

*uṣṇaṃ gavyaghṛtaṃ caiva saindhavena samanvitam \|*  
*nāśayettanmahādeva vedanāṃ vṛścikodbhavām \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Warm clarified butter, taken with the admixture of rock salt, relieves, О thou supreme deity, the pain of a scorpion-bite.

## \|\| 191.15 \|\|

*kusubhaṃ kaṅkumañcaiva haritālaṃ manaḥ śilā \|*

15\. О thou bissful one, a compound consisting of Kusumbham, Kumkum, Haritalam, Manah- Karanjam, and Arka roots pasted together, and internally administered, proves antidotal to all kinds of poison.

*viṣaṃnṛṇāṃ vinaśyettu eteṣāṃ bhakṣaṇācchiva \|*

О Rudra, a fumigation of the seat of the bite with the vapours of burning bdellium is sure to neutralise the poison in a case of centipede-bite.

Plasters composed of Nages- varam, Maricam, Sunthi, and Tagarpaduka pasted together with water would prove antidotal to beestings, or the seat of the sting should be otherwise plastered with Ssatapuspa and rocksalt pasted together with clarified butter. Plasters composed of $ iris a seeds cooked with milk would certainly destroy the poison, О thou supreme deity, in cases of Durdura (poisonous rats) bites.

## \|\| 191.20 \|\|

*dhattūrakarasonmiśraṃ kṣīrādyaguḍapānataḥ \|*

20\. О thou moon-crested one, the.,expressed juice of Dhusturam administered with the admixture of milk and treacle proves curative in cases of bites by rabid dogs (Hydophobia).

## \|\| 191.21 \|\|

*vaṭanimbaśamīnāñca valkalaiḥ kvathitaṃ jalam \|*

## \|\| 191.22 \|\|

*lepanāddevadārośca gairikasya ca lepanāt \|*

22\. Plasters of Devadaru and Gairikam pasted together with witer, or of Nagesvaram, Haridra, Daru-Haridra and Manjlstha pasted together with water prove remidial to spider-poisons.

## \|\| 191.23-24 \|\|

*karañjasya tu bījāni varuṇacchadameva ca \|*

*ghṛtaṃ kumārīpatraṃ vai dattaṃ salavaṇaṃ hara \|*

23-24. Plasters composed of Karanja seeds, Varuna bark, Tilab and Sarsapa pasted together would undoubtedly destroy all kinds of poison

13-14. Ashes of dry Mulakam and ^urithi/ Hihgula and Nagaram and Shukntam combination with oil, four times as much, should be employed in curing deafness, otalgia and germination of varmins in the ears, as well as for the purpose of arresting fetid discharges from the ears.

15-16. A medicinal oil cooked with the admixture of ashes of dry Mulakam and SunthI, Hingulam, Nagaram, 6atapuspa, Vaca, Ku§fham, Daru, $igru, Rasanjanam, Sauvar- calam, Yavaksara Samudram and Saindhava salt, Granthikam, Vida, Mustam, Madhu, and 6uktam, four times as much.

17-18. And the expressed juice of Matulunga and Kadali, should be employed, О Нага, for the purpose of removing diseases of the ears, such as deafness, noise in the ears, otalgia, fetid discharges from the ears.

*sadyo vināśamāyānti śaśāṅkakṛtaśekhara \|*

19\. The effect of this oil is almost instantaneous, and О thou moon-crested deity, this is the foremost of all Ksaratailas (alkaline oils) in respect of its efficacy, and instantly cleanses the teeth and the mouth of all impurities.

*candanaṃ kuṅkumaṃ māṃsī karpūraṃ jātipatrikā \|*

By using this oil, a man becomes a favourite with the fair sex, and is enabled to visit a hundred woman, each day. It is possessed of a great spermatopoetic virtue; by using this oil even a sterile woman is blessed with the pleasured of motherhood.

24\. Take a Prastha measure of melted cow- butter, cook it, in the usual way, with the admixture of eight Prasthas of water, Yamani, Citrakam, Dhanyam, Tryusanam, Jlrakam, Sauvarcalam, Pippalimulam, Vidanga, and Rajikam,

32-34. With a decoction of Patola leaves, Krataka, Manjistha, 6arlva, Jisa, Rid, Sami, Nimba leaves, and Madhukam. External applications of this Ghrtam alleviate pain and arrest secretions of ulcers.

36\. By taking, for three days in succession, a compound of Apamarga, Guduci, Kustham, Satavari, Vaca, SanakhapuspI, Abhaya, and Vidanga taken in equal parts and pounded together with the admixture of melted cow- butter, one is enabled to learn eight hundred books by heart.

37-38. Taken with water or clarified butter, Vaca enables a person to learn a thing at the first hearing. One Palam weight of Vaca taken with milk under the auspicies of a solar or lunar eclipse, tends to make its user a profoundly intelligent person.

## \|\| 192.39-41 \|\|

*bhūnimbanimbatriphalāparpaṭaiśca śṛtaṃ jalam \|*

*visphoṭakāni raktañca nātra kāryā vicāraṇā \|*  
*katakasya phalaṃ śaṅkhaṃ saindhavaṃ tryūṣaṇaṃ vacā \|\| 40 \|\|*

*phenī rasāñjanaṃ kṣaudraṃ viḍaṅgāni manaḥ śilā \|*

39-41. Water boiled with Bhunimba, Nimba, Triphala, Parpata, Patola, Mustakam, and Vasaka immediately destroys Visphotas (carbuncles). Sticks (Vartls) made of Ketaku fruits, 6ankha, Saindhava, Tryusanam, Vaca, Phena, Rasanjanam, Vidanga and Manah-sila pasted together with honey prove curative in cough, loss of vision and the type of eyedisease known as Patola.

## \|\| 192.42 \|\|

*prasthadvayaṃ māṣakasya kvāthaśca droṇamambhasām \|*

42\. Cook two Prastha measures of a decoction of Masa pulse with a Drona Measure of water, and take it down with its quarter part left.

## \|\| 192.43-44 \|\|

*kāñjikasyāḍhakaṃ dattvā piṣṭānyetāni dāpayet \|*  
*punarnavā gokṣurakaṃ saindhavaṃ tryūṣaṇaṃ vacā \|\| 43 \|\|*

*lavaṇaṃ suradāruśca mañjiṣṭhā kaṇṭakārikā \|*  
*nasyātpānāddharatyeva karṇaśūlaṃ sudāruṇam \|\| 44 \|\|*

43-44. Cook a Prastha Measure of oil with the admixtue of this decoction in the usual way, add to it an Adakam measure of Kanjikam and a compound of Punarnava, Goksura, Sain- dhavam, Tryusanam, Vaca, salt, Devadaru, Manjistha, and Kantakarika. Internally administered, or employed as errhiness, this oil cures the most acute type of earache; used as an unguent, it removes deafness and proves beneficial in hosts of other bodily distempers.

## \|\| 192.45-46 \|\|

*bādhiryaṃ sarvarogāṃśca hyabhyaṅgācca maheśvara \|*  
*paladvayaṃ saindhavañca śuṇṭhī citrakapañcakam \|\| 45 \|\|*

*sauvīrapañcaprasthaṃ ca tailaprasthaṃ pacettataḥ \|*  
*asṛgdarasvaraplīhāsarvavātavikāranut \|\| 46 \|\|*

45-46. Take two Main weights of rock-salt, five Palas of each of Shunthi and Citrakam, five Prasthas of Sauvlram, and one Prastha of oil. Cook it in the usual officinial way. This oil proves curative in cases of splenic enlargement, leucorrhoea, and all diseases of the nervous system.

## \|\| 192.47-48 \|\|

*udumbaraṃ vaṭaṃ plakṣaṃ jambūdvayamathārjunam \|*  
*pippalī ca kadambañca palāśaṃ lodhratindukam \|\| 47 \|\|*

*madhūkamāmrasarjañca badaraṃ padmakeśaram \|*  
*śirīṣabījaṅkatakametatkvāthena sādhitam \|*  
*tailaṃ hanti vraṇāṃllepāccirakālabhavānapi \|\| 48 \|\|*

47-48. A medicinal oil cooked in combination with a decoction of Audumbara, Vata, Plaksa, the two kinds Jumbu, Arjuna, Pippali, Kadamva, Palasa, Lodhram, Tinduka, Madhukam, Amram, Sarja, Vadaram, Padmakesaram, Shirisa seeds and Kataka brings on graunlation even in old or long-standing sores, and facilitates their speedy healing.

## Chapter 193

## \|\| 193.1-2 \|\|

*hariruvāca \|*  
*palāṇḍujīrake kuṣṭhamaśvagandhājamodakam \|*  
*vacā trikaṭukañcaiva lavaṇaṃ cūrṇamuttamam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*brāhmīrasairbhāvitañca sarpirmadhusamanvitam \|*  
*saptāhaṃ bhakṣitaṃ kuryānnirmalāñca matiṃ parām \|\| 2 \|\|*

1-2. Hari said: — A compound consisting of two kinds of Rajanl, Path, Kustham, Asvagandha Ajamodakam, Vaca, Trikatu and common salt pounded together and treated with the expressed juice of Brahml in the manner of a Bhavana saturation, and taken for a week, tends to highly improve the intellect.

## \|\| 193.3-5 \|\|

*siddhārthakaṃ vacā hiṅgu karañjaṃ devadāru ca \|*  
*mañjiṣṭhā triphalā viśvaṃ śirīṣo rajanīdvayam \|\| 3 \|\|*

*priyaṅgunimbatrikraṭu gomūtreṇaiva gharṣitam \|*  
*nasayamālepanañcaiva tathā codvartanaṃ hitam \|\| 4 \|\|*

*apasmāraviṣonmādaśoṣālakṣmījvarāpaham \|*  
*bhūtebhyaścabhayaṃ hanti rājadvāreṣu yojanāt \|\| 5 \|\|*

3-5. Errhines, plasters, or pastes of Siddharthak, Vaca, Hingu, Karanjam, Devadaru, MahjTstha, Triphala, Visvam, Shirisa, the two kinds of Raja, Priyangu, Nimba and Trikatu pounded together and mixed with cow's urine prove curative in hysteria, poisoning, insantiy, discolouring of the skin, and diseases due to the influences of malignant ghosts.

## \|\| 193.6 \|\|

*nimbaṃ kuṣṭhaṃ haridre dve śigru sarṣapajaṃ tathā \|*  
*devadāru paṭolañca dhānyaṃ takreṇa gharṣitam \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Take Nimba, Kustham, the two kinds of Haridra, 6igru, Sarsapa, Devadaru, Patolam and Dhanyam; pound them together and rub this pulverised compund with whey (Takram).

## \|\| 193.7 \|\|

*dehaṃ tailākta gātraṃ vai nayedudvartanena ca \|*  
*pāmāḥ kuṣṭhāni naśyeyuḥ kaṇḍūṃ hanti ca niścitam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Rubbing of the body with this paste, or with this paste, mixed with oil, destroys Pama, itches and allied diseases of the skin.

## \|\| 193.8 \|\|

*sāmudraṃ saindhavaṃ kṣāro rājikā lavaṇaṃ viḍam \|*  
*kaṭuloharajaścaivaṃ trivṛtsūraṇakaṃ samam \|*  
*dadhigomūtrapayasā mandapāvakapācitam \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Take Samudram salt, Saindhava salt, Ksara, Rajika, common salt, Vid salt, Kate, iron rust, Trivrt and Shuranakam in equal parts, Cook them over a gentle fire, with the addition of milkcurd, cow's urine and water.

## \|\| 193.9 \|\|

*balāgnivardhakaṃ cūrṇaṃ pibeduṣṇena vāriṇā \|*  
*jīrṇe 'jīrṇe tu bhuñjati māṃsyādighṛtamuttamam \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. This pulverised compound, which is called Agnivala Curnam, instantaneously relieves all form of colic, whether intestinal, renal, or splenic, or brought about through the enlargement of intestinal glands (gulma).

## \|\| 193.10 \|\|

*nābhiśūlaṃ mūtraśūlaṃ gulmaplīhabhavañca yat \|*  
*sarvaśūlaharaṃ cūrṇaṃ jaṭharānaladīpanam \|*  
*pariṇāmasamutthasya śūlasya ca hitaṃ param \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. It should be taken through the vehical of warm water, and the patient should be advised to take Masa pulse with melted butter after the digestion of his ingested food. This is almost a specific for all forms of coilc, inclusive of the one known as Parinama Shula.

## \|\| 193.11 \|\|

*abhayāmalakaṃ drākṣā pippalī kaṇṭakārikā \|*  
*śṛṅgī punarnavā śuṇṭhī jagdhā kāsaṃ nihanti vai \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. A compound of Abhaya, Amalakam. Draksa, Pippall Kantakarika, 6rngl, Punamava, and Shunthl boiled together with water, or pounded together, may be given with advantage in all forms of Cough.

## \|\| 193.12 \|\|

*abhayāmalakaṃ drākṣā pāṭhā caiva vibhītakam \|*  
*śarkarāyā samaṃ caiva jagdhaṃ jvaraharaṃ bhavet \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Abhaya Amalakam, Draksa, Patha, Vibhl- takam, and sugar, taken in equal parts and internally administered, act as a good febrifuge remedy.

## \|\| 193.13 \|\|

*triphalā badaraṃ drākṣā pippalī ca virekakṛt \|*  
*harītakī soṣṇānīralavaṇañca virekakṛt \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Triphala, Vadarm Draksa and Pippall combinedly exercise a purgative virtue, Abhaya taken with salt and warm water acts as a good purgative.

## \|\| 193.14-17 \|\|

*kūrmamatsyāśvamahiṣagośṛgālāśca vānarāḥ \|*  
*viḍālabarhikākāśca varāholūkakukkuṭāḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*haṃsa eṣāñca viṇmūtraṃ māṃsaṃ vā roma śoṇitam \|*  
*dhūpaṃ dadyājjvarārtebhya unmattebhyaśca śāntaye \|\| 15 \|\|*

*etānyauṣadhajātāni kathitāni umāpate \|*  
*nighnanti tāśca rogāṃśca vṛkṣamindrāśaniryathā \|\| 16 \|\|*

*auṣadhaṃbhagavānviṣṇuḥ saṃsmṛto roganudbhavet \|*  
*dhyāto 'rcitaḥ stuto vāpi nātra kāryā vicāraṇā \|\| 17 \|\|*

14-17. Flesh, blood, excrementitious matter (stool and urine) of female tortoises, fishes, mares, cow buffalos, cows, female monkeys, she- ackals, female cats, female crows, female owls, and she bears should be given for relieving fits of fever and insanity. Fumigations with the vapours of burning hairs or feathers) of any of these animals likewise prove beneficial in the foregoing maladies. The god Visnu, meditated upon by a person at the time of -taking a medicine, undoubtedly relieves him of the trouble.

## Chapter 194

## \|\| 194.1 \|\|

*hariruvāca \|*  
*sarvavyādhiharaṃ vakṣye vaiṣṇavaṃ kavacaṃ śubham \|*  
*yena rakṣā kṛtā śambhordaityānkṣapayataḥ purā \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Hari said: — О thou self-begotten one, now hear me discourse on the prophylatic formula known as Vaisnava Kavacam, which grants a certain immunity from attacks of maladies.

## \|\| 194.2 \|\|

*praṇamya devamīśānamajaṃ nityamanāmayam \|*  
*devaṃ sarveśvaraṃ viṣṇuṃ sarvavyāpinamavyayam \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Having made obeisance unto the birthless, changeless, undecaying and all-powerful reality, having bowed down unto the all-pervading Visnu, the god of gods, the overlord of the celestials, I shall describe the prophylaxis presently referred to.

## \|\| 194.3 \|\|

*badhnāmyahaṃ pratisaraṃ namaskṛtya janārdanam \|*  
*amoghāpratimaṃ sarvaṃ sarvaduḥ khanivāraṇam \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. I make obeisance to. the eternal spirit of irresistible prowess to the dissipator of all woes and misfortunes.

## \|\| 194.4 \|\|

*viṣṇurmāmagrataḥ pātu kṛṣṇo rakṣatu pṛṣṭhataḥ \|*  
*harirme rakṣatu śiro hṛdayañca janārdanaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. May Visnu protect me in the front, and Krsna, at the back. Hari saves head and heart by Janardana.

## \|\| 194.5 \|\|

*mano mama hṛṣīkeśo jihvāṃ rakṣatu keśavaḥ \|*  
*prātu netre vāsudevaḥ śrotre saṅkarṣaṇo vibhuḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. May Hrslkesa protect my intellect; and Kesava, my tongue. May Vasudeva protect my eyes, and may Sankarsana guard my ears.

## \|\| 194.6 \|\|

*pradyumnaḥ pātu me ghrāṇamaniruddhastu carma ca \|*  
*vanamālī galasyāntaṃ śrīvatso rakṣatāmadhaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. May Pradyumna protect my nose; and Aniruddha, my skin. May Vanamali protect the inside of my throat; and Shrivatsa, the downward portion of my body.

## \|\| 194.7 \|\|

*pārśvaṃ rakṣatu me cakraṃ vāmaṃ daityanivāraṇam \|*  
*dakṣiṇantu gadā devī sarvāsuranivāriṇī \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. May the discus-wielding divinity guard my sides. I consign my left side to the protection of the destroyer of demons and my right side to that of the divine club weapon, that has brought about the annihilation of the Asuras.

## \|\| 194.8 \|\|

*udaraṃ musalaṃ pātu pṛṣṭhaṃ me pātu lāṅgalam \|*  
*ūrdhvaṃ rakṣatu me śārṅgaṃ jaṅghe rakṣatu nandakaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. May the divine Musala weapon protect my belly, may the divine plough guard my back. May the divine bow protect the upper part of my body, may Nandaka protect my knee joints.

## \|\| 194.9 \|\|

*pārṣṇo rakṣatu śaṅkhaśca padmaṃ me caraṇāvubhau \|*  
*sarvakāryārthasiddhyarthaṃ pātu māṃ garuḍaḥ sadā \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. May the divine conch-shell protect my insteps, may the divine lotus flower protect my feet. May the divine Garuda protect me in all concerns of my life.

## \|\| 194.10 \|\|

*varāho rakṣatu jale viṣameṣu ca vāmanaḥ \|*  
*aṭavyāṃ narasiṃhaśca sarvataḥ pātu keśavaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. May the boar manifestation of Visnu protect me in waters, may the dwarf manifestaton of the supreme god protect me on undulating and impassable grounds. May Nrsirhha guard my person in wilderness; may Kesava shield me everywhere.

## \|\| 194.11 \|\|

*hiraṇyagarbho bhagavānhiraṇyaṃ me prayacchatu \|*  
*sāṃkhyācāryastu kapilo dhātusāmyaṃ karotu me \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. May Hiranyagarbha give me gold, may the divine Kapila, the author of the SaOskhya system of philosophy, help me to maintain a normal equilibrium among the different vita principles of my organism.

## \|\| 194.12 \|\|

*śvetadvīpanivāsī ca śvetadvīpaṃ nayatvajaḥ \|*  
*sarvānsūdayatāṃ śatrūnmadhukaiṭabhamardanaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. May the birthless one that preside over the white isle (Shvetadvlpa) lead me to that land; may the destroyer of the demons Madhu and Kaitabha destroy my enemies.

## \|\| 194.13 \|\|

*sadākarṣatu viṣṇuśca kilbiṣaṃ mama vigrahāt \|*  
*haṃso matsyastathā kūrmaḥ pātu māṃ sarvatodiśam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. May the all-pervading Visnu always expel sins from my body; may the swan, fish and tortoise manifestations of Visnu protect me in all the quarters of the heaven.

## \|\| 194.14 \|\|

*trivikramastu me devaḥ sarvapāpāni kṛntatu \|*  
*tathā nārāyaṇo devo buddhiṃ pālayatāṃ mama \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. May he, whose prowess brooks no obstruction in the three regions, dissipate all my inequities.

## \|\| 194.15-16 \|\|

*śeṣo me nirmalaṃ jñānaṃ karotvajñānanāśanam \|*  
*vaḍavāmukho nāśayatāṃ kalmaṣaṃ yatkṛtaṃ mayā \|\| 15 \|\|*

*padbhyāṃ dadātu paramaṃ sukhaṃ mūrdhni mama prabhuḥ \|*  
*dattātreyaḥ prakurutāṃ saputrapaśubāndhavam \|\| 16 \|\|*

15-16. May Narayana protect my intellect, may Mesa grant me that pure knowledge which disples all ignorance, may the god whose mouth is the submarine, volcnic fire, cleanse my spirit of all sin I have committed in the past with my hands, feet, and mouth. May Dattatreya grant me increase of friends, progeny and domestic nimals.

## \|\| 194.17 \|\|

*sarvānarīnnāśayatu rāmaḥ paraśunā mama \|*  
*rakṣoghnastu daśarathiḥ pātu nityaṃ mahābhujaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. May Rama destroy with his battle-axe all my adversaries. May the mighty armed Rama, the destroyer of Raksasas, always guard my body.

## \|\| 194.18 \|\|

*śatrīnhalena me hanyādrāmo yādavanandanaḥ \|*  
*pralambakeśicāṇūrapūtanākaṃsanāśanaḥ \|*  
*kṛṣṇasya yo bālabhāvaḥ sa me kāmānprayacchatu \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. May Rama, the delight of the race of Yadavas, kill my enemise with his invincible ploughshare. May juvinility of Krsna, the destroyer of Pralamba, Kesin, Canura, Putana and Kansa, grant me all my heart disires.

## \|\| 194.19-20 \|\|

*andhakāratamoghoraṃ puruṣaṃ kṛṣṇaṣiṅgalam \|*  
*paśyāmi bhayasantrastaḥ pāśahastamivāntakam \|\| 19 \|\|*

*tato 'haṃ puṇḍarīkākṣamacyutaṃ śaraṇaṃ gataḥ \|*  
*dhanyo 'haṃ nirbhayo nityaṃ yasya me bhagavānhariḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

19-20. Dismayed with fear, utterly terrorstrocken, I see a noose-holding male figure of a blackish, yellow colour, more sable than the primordial darkness and more dreadful to look at than the god of death, hence do I consign myself to the protection of the lotuseyes one that suffers no decay. О my soul, I need not fear since the woe-dissipating lord is mint. I am now indeed an adorable Self.

## \|\| 194.21 \|\|

*dhyātvā nārāyaṇaṃ devaṃ sarvopadravanāśanam \|*  
*vaiṣṇavaṃ kavacaṃ baddhvā vicarāmi mahītale \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Having meditated upon the divine self of Narayana, who guards against all evils and calamities that best human life, I roam about in this world, bearing this Vaisnava prophylaxis on my person.

## \|\| 194.22 \|\|

*apradhṛṣyo 'smi bhūtānāṃ sarvadevamayo hyaham \|*  
*smaraṇāddevadevasya viṣṇoramitatejasaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Since my mind perpetually dwells upon the almighty self of Visnu, melignant spirits dar not assail me. I am a veritable moving pantheon, full of energies of all the divinites.

## \|\| 194.23 \|\|

*siddhirbhavatu me nityaṃ yathāmantramudāhṛtam \|*  
*yo māṃ paśyati cakṣurbhyāṃ yañcaḥ paśyāmi cakṣuṣā \|*  
*sarveṣāṃ pāpaduṣṭānāṃ viṣṇurbadhnātu cakṣuṣī \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. May success attend me in this life sinee I have duly recited this (Vaisnavam) Mantram. May Visnu strike the eye-sight of those sin-perverted beings, that might chance to behold me with their wicked eyes, or whom I might happen to behold.

## \|\| 194.24 \|\|

*vāsudevasya yaccakraṃ tasya cakrasya ye tvarāḥ \|*  
*te hi cchindantu pāpānme mama hiṃsantu hiṃsakān \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. May the discus of Vasudeva, as well as the halo (lit. spokes) that shines round that weapon, sever my sins and strike those that wish me evil.

## \|\| 194.25-26 \|\|

*rākṣaseṣu piśāceṣu kāntāreṣvaṭavīṣu ca \|*  
*vivāde rājamārgeṣu dyūteṣu kalaheṣu ca \|\| 25 \|\|*

*nadīsantāraṇe ghore saṃprāpte prāṇasaṃśaye \|*  
*agnicauranipāteṣu sarvagrahanivāraṇe \|\| 26 \|\|*

25-26. Happening to fall among monsters, and Pisacas, while crossing a lonely waste or a weird wilderness, in quarrels, in contests, while travelling on the kind's high way, in moments of crisis and on apprehension of imminent peril of life, while swiming across a river or to ward off the influences of malignant planets and diseasespirits, at times when attacks by thieves and acts of incendiarism are apprehended

## \|\| 194.27-28 \|\|

*vidyutsarpaviṣodvege roge vai vighnasaṅkaṭe \|*  
*japyametajjapennityaṃ śarīre bhayamāgate \|\| 27 \|\|*

*ayaṃ bhagavato mantro mantrāṇāṃ paramo mahān \|*  
*vikhyātaṃ kavacaṃ guhyaṃ sarpapāpapraṇāśanam \|*  
*svamāyākṛtinirmāṇaṃ kalpāntagahanaṃ mahat \|\| 28 \|\|*

27-28. In thunder, in lightning, on the happening of reasonable causes of terror one should recite this Bhagavatam Mantrama, most sacred of all other Mantras. This renowned Bhagavatam Kavacam, which extinguishes all sin, is the most secret of al secret mantras. I make obeisance to the lotusnaveled one, the seed of the universe, the self without end or origin that lies inacessi- ble within the cycles (Kalpas) of evolution, the emanations of his own Maya.

## \|\| 194.29 \|\|

*anādyanta ! jagadbīja ! padmanābha ! namo 'stu te \|*  
*oṃ kālāya svāhā \| oṃ kālapuruṣāya svāhā \| oṃ kṛṣṇāya svāhā \|*  
*oṃ kṛṣṇarūpāya svāhā \| oṃ caṇḍāya svāhā \| oṃ caṇḍarūpāya svāhā \|*  
*oṃ pracaṇḍāya svāhā \| oṃ pracaṇarūpāya svāhā \| oṃ sarvāya svāhā \|*
