*oṃ sarvarūpāya svāhā \| oṃ namo bhuvaneśāya trilokadhātre iha viṭi siviṭi siviṭi svāhā/ oṃ namaḥ ayokhetaye ye ye saṃjñāpaya daityadānavayakṣarākṣasabhūtapiśācakūṣmāṇḍāntāpasmārakacchardanaduddharrāṇāmekāhikadvyāhikatryāhikacāturthikamauhūrtikadinajvararātrijvarasandhyājvarasarvajvarādīnāṃ lūtākīṭakaṇṭakapūtanābhujaṅgasthāvarajaṅgamaviṣādī nāmidaṃ śarīraṃ mama pathyaṃ tvaṃ kuru sphuṭa sphuṭa sphuṭa prakoṭa laphaṭa vikaṭadaṃṣṭra pūrvato rakṣatu oṃ hai hai hai hai dinakarasahasrakālasamāhato jaya paścimato rakṣa oṃ nivi nivi pradīptajvalanajvālākāra mahākapila uttarato rakṣa oṃ vili vili mili mili garuḍi garuḍi gaurīgāndhārīviṣamohaviṣamaviṣamāṃ mahohayatu svāhā dakṣiṇato rakṣa māṃ paśya sarvabhūtabhayopadravebhyo rakṣa rakṣa jaya jaya vijaya tena hīyate riputrāsāhaṅkṛtavādyato bhayanudabhayato 'bhayaṃ diśatucyutaṃ \|*  
*tadudaramakhilaṃ viśantu yugaparivartasahasrasaṃkhyeyo 'staṃhaṃsamiva praviśanti raśmayaḥ \|*  
*vāsudevasaṅkarṣaṇapradyumnāścāniruddhakaḥ \|*  
*sarvajvarānmamaghnantu viṣṇurnārāyaṇo hariḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Om, to Time (obeisance) Svaha, Om, to the spirit of Time obeisance (Svaha). Om, to Krsna obeisance (Svaha). Om, to the figure of Krsna obeisance. Om, obeisance to Canda, Om obeisance to Candarupa, Om, obesance to Pracanda, Om, obeisance to Pracandarusa. Om, obeisance to Sarva. Om, obeisance to Sarva- rupa. These are the tedts of disease and poison- incantations. May Visnu, may Narayana, may Aniruddha, may Sankarsana, may Vasudeva destroy my all kinds of fever.

## Chapter 195

## \|\| 195.1 \|\|

*hariruvāca \|*  
*salvakāmapradāṃ vidyāṃ saptarātreṇa tāṃ śṛṇu \|*  
*namastubhyaṃ bhagavate vāsudevāya dhīmahi \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Hari said: — Now hear me enumerate the Mantra, which repeated for seven nights in succession by a person enables him to witness the realisation of all his wished-for objects. I make obeisance to the Bhagavan. I meditate upon the self of Vasudeva.

## \|\| 195.2 \|\|

*pradyumnāyāniruddhāya namaḥ saṅgarṣaṇāya ca \|*  
*namo vijñānamātrāya paramānandamūrtaye \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. I bow down into Aniruddha, Sankarsana and Pradyumna manifestations of Visnu.

## \|\| 195.3 \|\|

*ātmārāmāya śāntāya nivṛttadvaitadṛṣṭaye \|*  
*tvadrūpāṇi ca sarvāṇi tasmāttubhyaṃ namo namaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Obeisance to the giver of perfect knowledge, obeisance to the embodied self of pure joy.

## \|\| 195.4 \|\|

*hṛṣīkeśāya mahate namaste 'nantamūrtaye \|*  
*yasminnidaṃ yataścaitattiṣṭhatyagre 'pi jāyate \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Obeisance to the one that delighteth in the soul, obeisance to the embodied quiesism, obeisance to the one who observeth no duality in the universe. This universe is thy image, hence do I make obeisance to thee. Obisance to Hrs ikesa, the great spirit reflected in the universe.

## \|\| 195.5 \|\|

*mṛnmayīṃ vahasi kṣoṇīṃ tasmai te brahmaṇe namaḥ \|*  
*yanna spṛśanti na viduḥ manobuddhīndriyāsavaḥ \|*  
*antarbahistvaṃ carasi vyomatulyaṃ namāmyaham \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. I make obeisance to Brahma from whom all this has come into being, in whom lies this all and from whom many other eternities will originate. Thou supportest this terrestrial globe, I make obeisance to thee. I make obeisance to Him whom the mind, life and the senseorgans cannot reach and who, like this ethereal expanse, lies extended both in the inside and outside of creatures.

## \|\| 195.6 \|\|

*oṃ namo bhagavate mahāpurāṣāya mahābhūtapataye sakalasattvabhāvivrīḍanikarakamalareṇūtpalanibhadharmākhyavidyayā? caraṇāravindayugala parameṣṭhin namaste \|*  
*avāpa vidyādharatāṃ citraketośca vidyayā \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Om, obeisance to the Lord, the great Purusa, the Supreme Lord of the Mahabhutas (primordial matter) whose lotus feet are Citraketu was lifted to the status of a Vidyadhara surrouned by the polens of virtues of heirarchies of beings of Sattva qualities. I make obeisance to the final goal of all. By dint of this knowledge, Citrakatu was lifted to the status of a Vidyadhara.

## Chapter 196

## \|\| 196.1 \|\|

*hariruvāca \|*  
*avāpa japtvā cendratvaṃ viṣṇudharmākhyavidyayā \|*  
*sarvāñchatrūnvinirjitya tāñca vakṣye maheśvara \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Hari said: — О thou, supreme deity, I shall now enumerate the Visnu-Dharma-vidya, by reciting which, Indra was enabled to kill all his adversaries, and was ultimately installed on the throne of heaven.

## \|\| 196.2 \|\|

*pādayorjānunorūrvorudare hṛdyathorasi \|*  
*mukhe śirasyānupūrvamoṅkā rādīni vinyaset \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. The Mantras such as Om, etc., should be psychically located by the reciter in his brain, face, heart, belly, thighs, knee-joints and legs respectively. He should then meditate upon these Mantras located as directed in the preceding line.

## \|\| 196.3-6 \|\|

*namo nārāyaṇāyeti viparyāsamathāpi ca \|*  
*karanyāsaṃ tataḥ kuryāddvādakṣaravidyayā \|\| 3 \|\|*

*praṇavādiyakārāntamaṅgulyaṃ guṣṭhaparvasu \|*  
*nyaseddhṛdaya oṅkāraṃ manuṃ mūrdhni samastakam \|\| 4 \|\|*

*oṅkārantu bhruvormadhye śikānetrādimūrdhataḥ \|*  
*oṃ viṣṇave iti imaṃ mantranyāsamudīrayet \|\| 5 \|\|*

*ātmānaṃ paramaṃ dhyāyeccheṣaṃ yacchaktibhiryutam \|*  
*mama rakṣāṃ hariḥ kuryānmatsyamūrtirjale 'vatu \|\| 6 \|\|*

3-6. . As an alternative, the Mantra running as Namo Narayanaya should be located, as above directed, in the limbs in the inverse order of enumeration. Then the rite of Kara-nyasa should be performed with the twelve-lettered Mantra sacred to the deity (Om Namo Bhagavate Vasudevaya). The votary should recite the Mantra running as Om, obeisance to Visnu, and consider himself as identical with the Sera manifestation of that divinity, attended with the six fold energy. May Hari protect me; may the fish manifestation of Visnu shield my person in water.

## \|\| 196.7 \|\|

*trivikramastathākāśe sthale rakṣatu vāmanaḥ \|*  
*aṭavyāṃ narasiṃhastu rāmo rakṣatu parvate \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. May Trivikrama, who excercises absolute power in the three regions, protect me in the skies; may the dwarf manifestation of Visnu preserve me on land. May the mighty Nrsimha protect me in wilderness; may Rama preserve me on the mountain.

## \|\| 196.8 \|\|

*bhūmau rakṣatu vārāhau vyomni nārāyaṇo 'vatu \|*  
*karmabandhācca kapilo datto rogācca rakṣatu \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. May the boar manifestation of Visnu preserve me on the earth-surface Narayana preserve me inth air. May Kapila protect the worldly concerns of my life; may Dattatreya preserve my yoga.

## \|\| 196.9-10 \|\|

*hayagrīvo devatābhyaḥ kumāro makaradhvajāt \|*  
*nārado 'nyārcanāddevaḥ kūrmo vai nairṛte sadā \|\| 9 \|\|*

*dhanvantīraścāpathyācca nāgaḥ krodhavaśātkila \|*  
*yajño rogātsamastācca vyāso 'jñānācca rakṣatu \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. May Hayagrlva, among the celestials, and Makaradhvaja, among the celestial youths, preserve me May Narada protect me from worshipping any other god. May the tortoise manifestation of Visnu preserve me in the south west; may Dhanvantari protect me from the evil effects of unwholesome food. May Naga protect me from failings of anger and passion May Yajna preserve me from the combined energy of diseases, may Vyasa preserve me from ignorance.

## \|\| 196.11-12 \|\|

*buddhaḥ pāṣaṇḍasaṃghātātkalkī rakṣatu kalmaṣāt \|*  
*pāyānmadhyandine viṣṇuḥ prātarnārāyaṇo 'vatu \|\| 11 \|\|*

*madhuhā cāparāhne ca sāyaṃ rakṣatu mādhavaḥ \|*  
*hṛṣīkeśaḥ pradoṣe 'vyātpratyūṣe 'vyājjanārdanaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12. May Buddha preserve me from the concourse of heretics (Pasnadas), may Kalki preserve me from sin and sinful propensities. May Visnu protect me at non; Narayana, in the morning; the destroyer of demon Madhu, at afternoon; and Madhava, in the evening. May Hrslkesa protect me at the dawn of day; may Janardana protect me at night-fall.

## \|\| 196.13 \|\|

*śrīdharo 'vyādardharātre padmanābho niśīthake \|*  
*cakrakaumodakībāṇā ghnantu śatrūṃśca rākṣasān \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. May Sridhara protect me at mid-night, may the lotus-raveled deity preserve me during the small hours of the night.

## \|\| 196.14 \|\|

*śaṅkhaḥ padmaṃ ca śatrubhyaḥ śārṅgaṃ vai garuḍastathā \|*  
*buddhīndriyamanaḥ prāṇānpāntu pārśvavibhūṣaṇaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. May the discus, club (KaumadakI) and arrows of Visnu kill my enemies and the Raksasa. May the lotus and conch shell of Visnu preserve me from enemies, may the celestial Garuda, and the divine bow end ornaments of Visnu preserve my life, mind, and intellect.

## \|\| 196.15 \|\|

*śeṣaḥ sarpasvarūpaśca sadā sarvatra pātu mām \|*  
*vidikṣu dikṣu ca sadā nārasiṃhaśca rakṣatu \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. May Shesa and Sarva-rupa preserve me everywhere. May Narasimha preserve me in all.

## \|\| 196.16 \|\|

*etaddhārayamāṇaśca yaṃ yaṃ paśyati cakṣuṣā \|*  
*sa vaśī syādvipāpmā ca rogamukto divaṃ vrajet \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. He, who eyes a person with this Kavacam on his person, is sure be fascinated, and such a person enjoys a kind of immuntiy from disease.

## Chapter 197

## \|\| 197.1 \|\|

*dhanvantariruvāca \|*  
*gāruḍaṃ saṃpravakṣyāmi garuḍena hyudīritam \|*  
*kaśyapāya sumitreṇa viṣahṛdyena gāruḍaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Dhanvantari said: — Now I shall enumerate to you the Garudam, as disclosed by Sumitra to Kasyapa. This Garudi Vidya tends to neutralise the effected of all kinds of poison.

## \|\| 197.2-3 \|\|

*pṛthivyāpastathā tejo vāyurākāśamevaca \|*  
*kṣityādiṣveva vargāśca hyete vai maṇḍalādhipāḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*pañcatattve sthitā devāḥ prāpyante viṣṇusevakaiḥ \|*  
*dīrghasvaravibhinnāśca napuṃsakavivarjitāḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

2-3. The five fundamental material principles of earth water, light (heat), air and ether are represented by the different letters of the alphabet as their symbols, which should be regarded as the presiding deities of the occult diagram to be meditated upon at the time of Dhyanam. The deities reside in these five fundamental material principles..

## \|\| 197.4-7 \|\|

*saṣaḍaṅgaḥ śivaḥ prokto hṛcchiraśca śikhā kramāt \|*  
*kavacaṃ netramastraṃ syānnyāsaḥ svasthalasaṃsthitiḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*sarvasiddhipradasyānte kālavahnira dho 'nilaḥ \|*  
*ṣaṣṭhasvarasamāyuktamardhendusaṃyutaṃ param \|\| 5 \|\|*

*parāparavibhinnāśca śivasyordhvādha īritāḥ \|*  
*repheṇāṅgeṣu sarvatra nyāsaṃ kuryādyathāvidhi \|\| 6 \|\|*

*hṛdi pāṇitale dehe karṇe netre karoti ca \|*  
*japāttu sarvasiddhiḥ syāccaturvaktrasamāyutām \|\| 7 \|\|*

4-7. The letters Sa, Sa, and Tha are symboilcal of the energy of Shiva (ether). The rite of Nyasa should be duly performed, and the Caturvaktra Mantram should be psychically located by the votary inside the palms of his hands, in the soles of his feet, as well as in the cavities of his heart and ears. By meditating in this fashion a votary may achieve all kinds of success.

## \|\| 197.8-9 \|\|

*caturaśrāṃ suvistāraṃ pītavarṇāntu cintayet \|*  
*pṛthivīṃ cendradevatyāṃ madhye varuṇamaṇḍalam \|\| 8 \|\|*

*madhye padmaṃ tathāyuktamardhacandraṃ suśītalam \|*  
*indranīladyutiṃ saumyamathavāgneyamaṇḍalam \|\| 9 \|\|*

8-9. First imagine a yellow coloured quadrangle as symbolical of the Earth, of which Indra is the presiding deity. At the centre of this quadrangle should be contemplated the ring of Varuna, at the centre of which is the mystic, translucent lotus upon which the half moon sheds its cool, turquoise-blue beams.

## \|\| 197.10-11 \|\|

*trikoṇaṃ svasthikairyuktaṃ jvālāmā lānalaṃ smaret \|*  
*bhinnāñjananibhākāraṃ svavṛttaṃ bindubhūṣitam \|\| 10 \|\|*

*kṣīrormisadṛśākāraṃ śuddhasphaṭikavarcasam \|*  
*plāvayantaṃ jagatsarvaṃ vyomāmṛtamanuṃsmaret \|\| 11 \|\|*

10-11. Around this should be imagined as transcribed the trianglar Mandalam of fire, crossed by a Svastika mark (cross) and burning with the effulgence of primordial fire. Around this should be imagined the circle of Vayu, sable coloured like the inside of a cut bar of black antimony, and impressed with the mark of the occult Bindu. Encircling this ring of Vayu should be imagined the Vyoma-Mandalam, dreadful in its infinite vastness, lying effulgent and motionless like the ocean of milk (Kslra), or like a sea of molten crystal.

## \|\| 197.12-13 \|\|

*vāsukiḥ śaṅkhapālaśca sthitau pārthivamaṇḍale \|*  
*karkoṭaḥ padmanābhaśca vāruṇe tau vyavasthitau \|\| 12 \|\|*

*āgneye cāpi kulikastakṣaścaiva mahābjakau \|*  
*vāyumaṇḍalasaṃsthau ca pañca bhūtāni vinyaset \|\| 13 \|\|*

12-13. The celestial serpents Vasuki and Shankhapala, should be imagined as residing in the quadrangle of the earth; Karkata and Padma Nabha, in the ring of Varuna; Kulika in the Man dalam of fire; and Takpka and Mahabjaka, in the ring of air.

## \|\| 197.14-15 \|\|

*aṅguṣṭhādikaniṣṭhāntamanulomavilomataḥ \|*  
*parvasandhiṣu ca nyasyā jayā ca vijayā tathā \|\| 14 \|\|*

*āsyādisvapurasthāne nyasyācchivapaḍaṅgakam \|*  
*kaniṣṭhādau hṛdādau ca śikhāyāṃ karayornyaset \|\| 15 \|\|*

14-15. The material principles of earth, water etc., should be imagined by the votary as located in his fingers, starting with the thumb and ending with the small finger, both in the usual and inverse order of enumeration. Likewise, the Jaya and Vijaya Mantras should be located in the bone-joints; the Shiva-Ganga Mantram in the cavity of the mouth; and Hrd Mantra in the arms and the tuft of hair on the crown of the head, and the Vyapakam, in the phalanges of forgers.

## \|\| 197.16-17 \|\|

*vyāpakantu tatvapūrvaṃ kramādaṅguliparvasu \|*  
*bhūtānāñca punarnyāsaḥ śivāṅgāni tathaiva ca \|\| 16 \|\|*

*praṇavādinamaścānte nāmnaiva ca samanvitaḥ \|*  
*sarvamantreṣu kathito vidhiḥ sthāpanapūjane \|\| 17 \|\|*

16-17. The rite of Bhutanyasa should be performed with the Shivanga Mantras preceded by "Om" and followed by "Namah." This rule should be followed in respect of establishing and worshipping all forms of Mantra.

## \|\| 197.18 \|\|

*ādyākṣaraṃ tannāmnaśca mantro 'yaṃ parikīrtitaḥ \|*  
*aṣṭānāṃ nāgajātīnāṃ mantraḥ sānnidhyakārakaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. The first letters of the names of these celestial serpents are the Mantras respectively sacred to each of them, which being duly recited by a votary enables him to draw' any of them to his side.

## \|\| 197.19 \|\|

*oṃ svāhā kramaśaścaiva pañcabhūtapurogatam \|*  
*eṣa sākṣādbhavettārkṣyaḥ sarvakarmaprasādhakaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. The Mantras composed of the names of the five fundamental physical principles coupled with "Om" and "Namah" should be then recited, whereby the celestial Garuda would appear into the votary in all his glory and prowess.

## \|\| 197.20-22 \|\|

*karanyāsaṃ svaraiḥ kṛtvā śarīre tu punarnyaset \|*  
*jvalantaṃ cintayetprāṇamātmasaṃśuddhikārakam \|\| 20 \|\|*

*bījantu cintayetpaścādvarṣāntamamṛtātmakam \|*  
*evañcāpyāyanaṃ kṛtvā mūrdhni sañcintya cātmanaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*pṛthivīṃ pādayordadyāttaptakāñcanasaprabhām \|*  
*aśeṣabhuvanākīrṇāṃ lokapālasamanvitām \|\| 22 \|\|*

20-22. The votary shall again perform the rite of Karanyasa with the help of the vowel letters, and the rite of 3ariranayas thereafter. He shall contemplate his vital energy (Prima) as an unflickering light steadily burning within his heart, and consuming the impurities of his organism, and the BIja Mantra as showering divine ambrosia wherewith his system is being saturated. Thus surcharging his system with the nectarine flow of the BIja Mantra, the votary shall contemplate his self as located in his brain; and the earth teeming with thousands of cities and abodes of men, and guarded by the Lokapalas (protectors of world) and shining with the effulgence of molten gold as located in his lower extermities.

## \|\| 197.23-24 \|\|

*etāṃ bhagavatīṃ pṛthvīṃ svadehe vinyased budhaḥ \|*  
*śyāmavarṇamayaṃ dhyāyetpṛthivīdviguṇaṃ bhavet \|\| 23 \|\|*

*jvālāmālākulaṃ dīptamābrahmabhuvanāntakam \|*  
*nābhigrīvāntare nyasya trikoṇaṃ maṇḍalaṃ raveḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

23-24. The principle of water, clear and smooth, he shall contemplate as occupying the region between his heart and navel, shining with a blue light, and occupying a space, twice as much as that of the earth. The Ravi Mandalam, the seat of heat and light, should be imagined as a triangle occupying the thoracic cavity and resting on an imaginary line across the umbilicus as its base, and extending from the sphere of Bhuvanas (worlds) to Brahma.

## \|\| 197.25-26 \|\|

*bhinnāñjananibhākāraṃ nikhilaṃ vyāpya saṃsthitam \|*  
*ātmamūrtisthitaṃ dhyāyedvāyavyaṃ tīkṣṇamaṇḍalam \|\| 25 \|\|*

*sikhopari sthitaṃ divyaṃ śuddhasphaṭikavarcasam \|*  
*apramāṇamahāvyomavyāpakaṃ cāmṛtopamam \|\| 26 \|\|*

25-26. The Vayu Mandalam, in which is ensconced the image of Self, as permeating the universal space and coloured (deep blue) like broken, black antimony. Over the crown of his head the votary shall contemplate the Divya Mandalam shining with the effulgence of clear, cut crystal, and permeating the boundless expancse of ether, and enshrouding, and enlivening all with divine ambrosia.

## \|\| 197.27-28 \|\|

*bhūtanyāsaṃ purā kṛtvā nāgānāñca yathākramam \|*  
*lakārāntā binduyutā mantrā bhūtakrameṇa tu \|\| 27 \|\|*

*śivabījaṃ tato dadyāttato dhyāyecca maṇḍalam \|*  
*yoyasya kramākhyāto maṇḍalasya vicakṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*tasya taccintayedvarṇaṃ karmakāle vidhānavit \|\| 28 \|\|*

27-28. First the rite of Bhotanyasa should be performed, after that, the one in respect of the celestial serpents, by reciting the BIjas commencing with the letters "La" and coupled with the nasal sign of Bindu, to which the BIjas, sacred to Shiva, should be moreover appended. After this, the votary should meditate upon the Mandalam described before. The intelligent one should meditate upon the Mandalas respectively coloured as aforesaid at the time of practising this incantation.

## \|\| 197.29 \|\|

*pādapakṣaistathā cañcatkṛṣṇanāgairvibhūṣitam \|*  
*tārkṣyaṃ dhyāyettato nityaṃ viṣe sthāvarajaṅgame \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. The feet, pinions, and bills of Garuda should be contemplated as ornamented with rings of black snakes. This figure of Tarksa (Garuda) should be invariably meditated upon in cases of poisoning with any animal or vegetable poison.

## \|\| 197.30 \|\|

*grahabhūtapiśāce ca ḍākinīyakṣarākṣase \|*  
*nāgairviveṣṭitaṃ kṛtvā svadehe vinyasecchivam \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. The figures of malignent spirits, planets, Dakirus, Yaksas, and Raksasa should the votary likewise imagine as located in his limbs, ornamented with black serpents, by an act of Nyasa.

## \|\| 197.31 \|\|

*dvidhā nyāsaḥ samākhyāto nāgānāṃ caiva bhūtayoḥ \|*  
*evaṃ dhyātvā karma kuryādātmatattvādikaṃ kramāt \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Twofold is the rite of Nyasa in this incantation; one is in respect of the fundamental material principles and the other is in respect of the serpents. Having thus contemplated the principles of soul etc., in due succession. The votary should commence practising the charm.

## \|\| 197.32 \|\|

*tritattvaṃ pratham dattvā sivatattvaṃ tataḥ param \|*  
*yathā dehe tathā deve aṅgulīnāṃ ca parvasu \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. First the three fundamental principles of Tritattvas should be contemplated, and after that the, principle of bliss should be meditated upon as located above them.

## \|\| 197.33-34 \|\|

*dehe nyāsaṃ purā kṛtvā hyanulomavilomataḥ \|*  
*kandaṃ nālaṃ tathā padmaṃ dharmaṃ jñānādimeva ca \|\| 33 \|\|*

*dvitīyasvarasambhinnaṃ vargāntena tu pūjayet \|*  
*śaumiti karṇikāmadhye mūrdhni repheṇa saṃyutam \|\| 34 \|\|*

33-34. The rite of Deha-nyasa should be performed by the votary, both in the usual and inverse order, in his limbs as well as in the imaginary figures of the deities meditated upon. The bulb, stem, etc., of the occult lotus, as well as the principles of virtue and wisdom should be worshipped by reciting the BIjas composed of the final letters of the different Vargas appended with the second vowel. The Mantra; "Ksaum" should be imagined as located in the polens of the occult lotus.

## \|\| 197.35 \|\|

*akacaṭatapayaśā vargāḥ pūrvādike nyaset \|*  
*patrāntakesarānte tu dvau dvau pūrvādikau tathā \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. The groups of letters, which are called A, Ka, Ca, Та, Та, Pa, Ya and 6a Vargas, should be imagined as impressed on the eastern petals of this mystic flower, the vowels should be likewise imagined as impressed on the polens of the lotus, two in each, wherein the gods Isa etc., should be worshipped.

## \|\| 197.36 \|\|

*keśare tu svarānnyasyādīśāntānṣoḍaśārcayet \|*  
*vāmādyāḥ śaktayaḥ proktāstritattvantu tato nyaset \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. The goddesses Varna etc., should be considered as the energies of the Rudras worshipped in these polens, after which the votery shall invoke the three fundamental material principles (Tritattvas).

## \|\| 197.37 \|\|

*āvāhayettato mardhni śivamaṅgaṃ tataḥ param \|*  
*karṇikāyāṃ nyaseddevaṃ sāṃgaṃ tatra puraḥ saram \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. The principle of ether he should psychically invoke and locate within his head.

## \|\| 197.38-41 \|\|

*pṛtivī paścime patre āpaścottarasaṃsthitāḥ \|*  
*tejastu dakṣiṇe patre vāyuṃ pūrveṇa pūjayet \|\| 38 \|\|*

*svabījaṃ mūrtirūpantu prāguktaṃ pārakalpayet \|*  
*yaṃ vāyumūlaṃ nairṛtye rephastvanalasaṃsthitaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

*vaṃ ca tvīśe sadā pūjya oṃ hṛdisthañca pūjayet \|*  
*tanmātrānbhūtamātrāṃstānbahireva prapūjayet \|\| 40 \|\|*

*śivāṅgāni tataḥ paścāddhyātvā saṃpūjayettataḥ \|*  
*āgneyyāṃ hṛdayaṃ pūjya śira īśānagocare \|\| 41 \|\|*

38-41. He should worship the principle of earth in the western petal of the lotus; the principle of water, in its northern leaf; the principle of fire (Tejas) in its southern-leaf and the principle of air, in its eastern one.

## \|\| 197.42-48 \|\|

*nairṛtye tu śikhāṃ dadyādvāyavyāṃ kavacaṃ nyaset \|*  
*astrantu bāhyato dadyānnetramuttarasaṃsthitam \|\| 42 \|\|*

*patrāgre karṇikagre tu bījāni paripūjayet \|*  
*anantādikulīrāntā aṣṭau nāgāḥ kramātsthitāḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

*pūrvādikakrameṇaiva tvīśaparyantameva ca \|*  
*pūjayecca sadā mantrī vidhānena pṛthakpṛthak \|\| 44 \|\|*

*hṛdi padme vidhānena śilādau dattamaṇḍale \|*  
*etatkāryaṃ samuddiṣṭaṃ nityanaimittike 'pi ca \|\| 45 \|\|*

*ātmānaṃ cintayennityaṃ kāmarūpaṃ manoharam \|*  
*plāvayantaṃ jagatsarvaṃ sṛṣṭisaṃhārakārakam \|\| 46 \|\|*

*jvālāmālābhiruddīptaṃ ābrahmabhuvanāntakam \|*  
*daśabāhuṃ caturvaktraṃ piṅgākṣaṃ śūlapāṇinam \|\| 47 \|\|*

*daṃṣṭrākarālamatyugraṃ trinetraṃ śaśiśekharam \|*  
*bhairavantu smaretsiddhyai garuḍaṃ sarvakarmasu \|\| 48 \|\|*

42-48. The Tanmatras (essential material principles) and Mahabhutas (gross matter) should be worshipped outside the occult diagram. This procedure should be adapted in all rites of Nitya and Naimittika worship. The votary should contemplate his Self as an expanse of beautifully tinted light, pervading all through the imiverse-its creator, preserver and destroyer-and living the infinite expanse of ether with its own ambrosial energy. Likewise, he should meditate upon Bhairava in the company of the Siddhas and the celestial Garuda in all acts of incantation-the moon crested Bhairava, who is possessed of ten arms and four faces and three eyes, burning with a kind of lurid effulgence, with his diabolical teeth exposed in a dreadful grimace and a weird light emanating from his flame-coloured eyes.

## \|\| 197.49-51 \|\|

*nāgānāṃ nāśanārthāya garuḍaṃ bhīmabhīṣaṇam \|*  
*pādau pātālaṃ saṃsthau ca diśaḥ pakṣāstu saṃśritāḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

*sapta svargā urasi ca brahmāṇḍaṃ kaṇṭhamāśritam \|*  
*pūrvādīśānaparyantaṃ śirastasya vicintayet \|\| 50 \|\|*

*sadāśivaśikhāntasthaṃ śaktitritayameva ca \|*  
*parātparaṃ śivaṃ sākṣāttārkṣyaṃ bhuvananāyakam \|\| 51 \|\|*

49-51. For the destruction of snakes he should contemplate the image of Garuda, dreadful to look at, the tips of his mighty pinions touching the ends of the welkin, the regions of Patala located in his feet, the seven celestial regions lying ensconced in his bosom, the entire universe nestling round his neck, and all the Rudras, from the first to Isa, who is the last in the list of that class of deities, as located within his head, Garuda, who is but another manifesation of Shiva, is the lord of the universe, the gretatest of all the great divinities.

## \|\| 197.52 \|\|

*trinetramugrarūpañca viṣanāgakṣayaṅkaram \|*  
*grasanaṃ bhīmavaktraṃ ca garuḍaṃ mantravigraham \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. His body is made of the energy of the Mantras (mystic formulas); and the votary shall contemplate his in all acts of incantation as effulgent like the fire of universal dissolution and bent on devouring the poisonous snakes. He, whom the votary may contemplate in his mind after performing the rite of Nyasa as above described, shall come under his control and influence.

## \|\| 197.53-54 \|\|

*kālāgnimiva dīptaṃ ca cintayetsarvakarmasu \|*  
*evaṃ nyāsavidhiṃ kṛtvā yadyanmanasi cintayet \|\| 53 \|\|*

*tattadeva bhavetsādhyaṃ naro vai garuḍāyate \|*  
*pretā bhūtāstathā yakṣā nāgā gandharvarākṣasāḥ \|*  
*darśanāttasya naśyanti jvarāścāturthikādayaḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

53-54. By performing this Nyasa, a votary becomes himself a Garuda, ghosts, demons, monsters, Pisacas and the different kinds of fever such as, quotodian ague, etc., fly the presence of him who prectises this incantation.

## \|\| 197.55 \|\|

*dhanvantariruvāca \|*  
*evaṃ sa garuḍaṃ proce garuḍaḥ kaśyapāya ca \|*  
*maheśvaro yathā gaurīṃ prāha vidyāṃ tathā śṛṇu \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Dhanvantari said this GarudI Vidya which was first promulgated by Garuda himself to the holy Kasyapa; now hear me discourse on that which was disclosed by Mahesvara to the goddess Gauri.

## Chapter 198

## \|\| 198.1 \|\|

*bhairava uvāca \|*  
*nityaklinnāmatho vakṣye tripurāṃ bhuktimuktidām \|*  
*oṃ hrīṃ āgaccha devi aiṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ rekhākāraṇam \|*  
*oṃ hrīṃ kledinī bhaṃ namaḥ madanakṣobhiṇā tathā \|*  
*ai yaṃ yaṃ krīṃ vā guṇarekhayā hrīṃ madanāntare ca \|*  
*aiṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ ca nirañjanā vāgati madanāntarekhe khanetrāvalīti ca \|*  
*vegavati mahāpretāsanāya ca pūjayet \|*  
*oṃ hrīṃ kraiṃ naiṃ kraiṃ nityaṃ madadrave krīṃ namaḥ \|*  
*aiṃ hrīṃ tripurāyai namaḥ \|*  
*oṃ hrīṃ krīṃ paścimavaktraṃ oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ ca tathottaram \|*  
*aiṃ hrīṃ dakṣiṇamūrdhvaṃvaktraṃ tu paścimam \|*  
*oṃ hrīṃ pāśāya krīṃ aṅkuśāya aiṃ kapālāya namaḥ \|*  
*ādyaṃ bhayaṃ aiṃ hrīṃ ca tathā śiraḥ tathā śikhāyai kavace \|*  
*aiṃ hrīṃ krīṃ astrāyaphaṭ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Bhairava said: — Now I shall expound the Tripurl Vidya (Science of Tripura) which is known as the Nityaklinna Mantra, which, properly practised, imparts salvation and creature comforts to its votary. Om, Hrim, come О thou, goddess, Om obeisance to Kledeni, the same to the excitress of erotic passions. Am, Hrim, Hrim, obeisance to Narayana. Similarly, the deities Vegavati, Maha-pretasana, etc, should be worshipped. Om, Hram, Hrim, Kraim, Naim, Kraim, obeisance to Madadrava; Aim, Hrim, obeisance to Tripura. Om, Hrim, Krim, obeisance to Pa&mavaktra. Om, Aim, Hrim, obeisance to Uttaravaktra; Aim, Hrim, obeisance to Daksina Vaktra, to Parvavaktra, and to Urdhvavaktra. Krim, obeisance, to the noose of the deity, obeisance of the mace of the deity, Aim, obeisance to the skull which the god bears in his hand. The rite of Nyasa should be performed by reciting the Mantra Adyam, Bhayam, Aim, etc.

## \|\| 198.2-3 \|\|

*pūrve kāmarūpāya asitāṅgāya bhairavāya namo brahmāṇyai \|*  
*dakṣiṇe cai kandāya vai namaḥ rurubhaivāya māheśvaryā vā āvāhayet \|\| 2 \|\|*

*tathā paścime caṇḍāya vai namaḥ \|*  
*kaumāryai cottare colkāya krodhāya namaḥ vaiṣṇavyai \|\| 3 \|\|*

2-3. The deities such as Kamarupa, Asitanga, etc., should be worshipped in the East, the goddess Brahman! and the deity. Visma-nirma should be worshipped in the South. The deities such as Ruru-Bhairava, Kumari, Mahesvari and Candl should be worshipped in the west, the deities such as Ulka, Krodha, and Vaisnavl should be worshipped in the north.

## \|\| 198.4 \|\|

*agnikoṇe aghorāyonmattabhairavāyeti vārāhyai \|*  
*rakṣaḥ koṇe sārāya kapāline bhairavāya māherndyai \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. The Bhairava, Aghora should be invoked and worshipped in south-east corner of the Mandalam; Unmatta Bhairava in its north-west chamber, the goddesses Mahendri Kulantika, and Vilina in the south-west chamber

## \|\| 198.5 \|\|

*vāyukoṇe jālandharāya bhīṣaṇāya bhairavāya cāmuṇḍāyai \|*  
*īśakoṇake vaṭukāya saṃhārañcaṇḍikāñca prapūjayet \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. The god Jalandhara with his accompanying energies of Bhlsana and Camunda should be worshipped in the north-east chamber of the mystic diagram. In the umbilical region of the imaged goddess should be worshipped the god of death and Candl as well as the presiding deities of attachment, pleasure and love.

## \|\| 198.6 \|\|

*ratiprītikāmadevānpañcabāṇānyajedatha \|*  
*dhyānārcanājjapyahomāddevī siddhā ca sarvadā \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. The god of love with his five arrows should be likewise worshipped by reciting the Mantra running as Om, Hrim, Hrim, Hram, Shah, obeisance. Hum, obeisance to Gana, Aksas and Ksetrapalas.

## \|\| 198.7 \|\|

*nityā ca tripurā vyādhiṃ hanyājjvālāmukhīkramāt \|*  
*jvālāmukhīkramaṃ vakṣye sā pūjyā madhyataḥ śubhā \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Thus meditated upon and propitiated with libations of clarified butter cast in the fire in her honour, the goddess Tripura grants the fulfilment of all desires to her votary and bides under his control. The eternal Tripura, worshipped in the manner known as Jvalamukhl-Krama, dissipates all diseases.

## \|\| 198.8-10 \|\|

*nityāruṇā madanāturā mahāmohā prakṛtyapi \|*  
*mahendrāṇī ca kalanākarṣiṇī bhāratī tathā \|\| 8 \|\|*

*brahmāṇī caiva māheśī kaumārī vaiṣṇavī tathā \|*  
*vārāhī caiva māhendrī cāmuṇḍā cāparājitā \|\| 9 \|\|*

*vijayā cājitā caivamohinī tvaritā tathā \|*  
*stambhinī jṛmbhiṇī pūjyā kālikā padmabāhyataḥ \|*  
*jvālāmukhīkramaṃ cārcedviṣādiharaṇaṃ bhavet \|\| 10 \|\|*

8-10. Now hear me discourse on' the process of worship known as Jvakamukhi-Krama. The goddess Jvalamukhl should be worshipped at the centre of the mystic lotus-diagram and her attendent goddesses such as Nitya, Aruna, Madanatura, Mada, Moha, Prakrti, Kalana, Shri, Bharati, AkarsinI MahendranI, BrahmanT, Mahegl, Kaumari, Baisnavl, Varahi, Mahendrl, Camunda, Aparajita, Vijaya, Ajita, Mohanl, and Tvarita should be worshipped in the adjacent chambers within the diagram. The goddess Stambhinl, JrmbhanI, and Kalika should be worshipped outside the diagram. By worshipping the goddess in this manner, a votary is enabled to neutralise the effects of all kinds of poison.

## Chapter 199

## \|\| 199.1-2 \|\|

*bhairava uvāca \|*  
*atha cūḍāmaṇiṃ vakṣye śubhāśubhaviśuddhaye \|*  
*sūryaṃ devīṃ gaṇaṃ soma smṛtvā tu vilikhennaraḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*trirekhā gomūrtrikābhā athavā praśravākyataḥ \|*  
*diśasthānaprasūto vā dhvajādīngaṇayetkramāt \|\| 2 \|\|*

1-2. Now I shall discourse on Cudamani for the ascertainment of auspicious or inauspicious auguries. Having made obeisance of Gana, Soma, and the goddess, the sooth-sayer should obliquely put down three lines on the paper, a stream of cow's urine.

## \|\| 199.3 \|\|

*dhvajo dhūmo 'tha siṃhaśca śvā vṛṣaḥ kharadantinau \|*  
*dhvāṅkṣaśca aṣṭamo jñeyo nāma mantraiśca tānnyaset \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Then the different symbols of calculation such as the banner; camel, lion, dog, bull and the ass should be put down in the different chambers. The crow should be regarded as the eighth symbol in the diagram.

## \|\| 199.4 \|\|

*dhvajasthāne dhvajaṃ dṛṣṭvā rājyacintādhanādikam \|*  
*dhvajasthāne sthito dhūmro dhātucintā ca lābhakṛt \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Banner seen in the chamber of the banner presages thoughts about a kingdom or wealth, haumra (camel) seen in the chamber of the finer presages though about metals and gain.

## \|\| 199.5 \|\|

*dhvajasthāne sthite siṃhe dhanalābhādikaṃ bhavet \|*  
*sthite śunidhvajasthāne dāsīcintāsukhādikam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Lion seen in the chamber of the banner Presages acquisition of wealth and gain. Dog, seen in the chamber of the banner, presages thought female slave and the advent of happiness.

## \|\| 199.6 \|\|

*dhvajasthāne vṛṣaṃ dṛṣṭvā sthānacintā ca lābhakam \|*  
*dhvajasthāne kharaṃ dṛṣṭvā duḥ khakleśādikaṃ bhavet \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Bull seen in the chamber of the banner presages thought about, and acquisition of, landed property. Ass seen in- the chamber of the banner presages misery and sorrow.

## \|\| 199.7 \|\|

*dhvajasthāne gajaṃ dṛṣṭvā sthānacintājayādikam \|*  
*dhvajasthāne tathā dhvāṅkṣe kleśacintā dhanakṣayaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Elephant seen in the chamber of the banner presages victory and acquisition of place by the enquirer. Crow seen in the chamber of the banner presages loss of wealth, and though about pain or misery.

## \|\| 199.8 \|\|

*dhūmrasthāne dhvajaṃ dṛṣṭvā pūrvaṃ duḥ khaṃ tato dhanam \|*  
*dhūmre dhūmraṃ tathā dṛṣṭvā kaliduḥ khādikaṃ bhavet \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Similarly, banner seen in the chamber of the camel, presages pain followed by pleasure. Camel seen in the chamber of the camel presages misery due to evil propensities of the enquirer.

## \|\| 199.9 \|\|

*dhūmrasthāne sthite siṃhe manaścintādhanādikam \|*  
*dhūmrasthāne śuni sthite jayalābhādikaṃ bhavet \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Lion seen in the chamber of the camel foretells an anxiety about, and acquisition of, wealth by the enquirer. Dog seen in the chamber of the camel predicts victory and wealth.

## \|\| 199.10 \|\|

*dhūmrasthāne vṛṣaṃ dṛṣṭvā nārīgo 'śvadhanādikam \|*  
*dhūmrasthāne kharaṃ dṛṣṭvā vyādhiścāpi dhanakṣayaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Bull seen in the chamber of the camel predicats the acquisition of cattle and wives by the enquirer. Ass seen in the chamber of the camel presages disease and loss of wealth.

## \|\| 199.11 \|\|

*dhūmrasthāne gaje dṛṣṭe rājyalābhajayādikam \|*  
*dhūmrasthāne sthite dhvāṅkṣe dhanarājyavināśanam \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Elephant seen in the chamber of the camel augurs the acquisition of wealth and kingdom by the enquirer. Crow seen in the chamber of the camel presages loss of wealth and kingdom.

## \|\| 199.12 \|\|

*siṃhasthāne dhvajaṃ dṛṣṭvā rājyalābhādi nirdiśet \|*  
*siṃhasthāne sthite dhūmre kanyāprāptirdhanādikam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Banner seen in the chamber of the lion predicts the gain of wealth and kingdom; camel seen in the chamber of the lion presages the acqusition of a bride and wealth by the enquirer.

## \|\| 199.13 \|\|

*siṃhasthāne sthite siṃhe jayo mitrasamāgamaḥ \|*  
*kauleyake siṃhagate strīcintā grāmalābhakam \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Lion seen in the chamber of the lion predicts victory and arrival of friends. Dog seen in the chamber of the lion predicts the gain of a village by the enquirer and the fact that he is thinking about a woman.

## \|\| 199.14 \|\|

*siṃha sthāne vṛṣaṃ dṛṣṭvā gṛhakṣetrārthalābhakam \|*  
*siṃhasthāne gajaṃ dṛṣṭvā grāmasvāmitvameva ca \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Bull seen in the chamber of the lion foretells the acquisition of a field, house and money by the enquirer. Ass seen in the chamber of the lion augurs the lordship of the enquirer over his own native village.

## \|\| 199.15 \|\|

*siṃhasthāne gajaṃ dṛṣṭvā ārogyāyuḥ sukhādikam \|*  
*siṃhasthānesthite dhvāṅkṣe kanyādhānyaguṇādikam \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Elephant seen in the chamber of the lion presages good health, joy and longevity to the enquirer. Crow seen in the chamber of the lion predicts the acquisition of a wife, food grain and wealth.

## \|\| 199.16 \|\|

*śunaḥ sthāne dhvajaṃ dṛṣṭvā sthānacintāsukhādikam \|*  
*śunaḥ sthāne sthite dhūmre kalahaṃ kāryanāśanam \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Banner seen in the chamber of the dog indicates the thought about a place and presages the advent of joy and pleasure. Camel seen in the chamber of the dog predicts quarrel and failure in business.

## \|\| 199.17 \|\|

*śunaḥ sthāna sthite siṃhe kāryāsiddhirbhaviṣyati \|*  
*sthite śuni śunaḥ sthāne dhananāśo bhaviṣyati \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Lion seen in the chamber of the dog predicts the success of an undertaking. Dog seen in the chamber of the dog presages loss of wealth.

## \|\| 199.18 \|\|

*śunaḥ sthāne vṛṣaṃ dṛṣṭvā rogī rogādvi mucyate \|*  
*śunaḥ sthāne kharaṃ dṛṣṭvā kalahasya bhayaṃ bhavet \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Bull seen in the chamber of the dog predicts the recovery of a patient from a disease. Ass seen in the chamber of the dog predicts quarrel and danger.

## \|\| 199.19 \|\|

*śunaḥ sthāne gajaṃ dṛṣṭvā putrabhāryāsamāgamaḥ \|*  
*śvasthāne ca sthite dhvāṅkṣe pīḍāsyātkulanāśanam \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Elephant seen in the chamber of the dog foretells the meeting of the enquirer with his wife and children. Crow seen in the chamber of the dog augurs disease and loss of bodily strength

## \|\| 199.20 \|\|

*vṛṣasthāne dhvajaṃ dṛṣṭvā rājapūjāsukhādikam \|*  
*vṛṣasthāne sthite dhūmre rājapūjāsukhādikam \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Banner, seen in the chamber of the bull predicts the honouring of the enquirer by kings. Camel seen in the chamber of the bull predicts royal favour and pleasure to the enquirer.

## \|\| 199.21 \|\|

*vṛṣasthāne sthite siṃhe saubhāgyañca dhanādikam \|*  
*sthite śuni vṛṣasthāne balaśrīkāma īritaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Lion seen in the chamber of the bull augurs happiness and prosperity to the enquirer. Dog seen in the chamber of the lion predicts beauty, strength and gain of creature-comforts to the enquirer.

## \|\| 199.22 \|\|

*vṛṣasthāne vṛṣaṃ dṛṣṭvā kīrtituṣṭisukhādikam \|*  
*vṛṣasthāne kharaṃ dṛṣṭvā mahālābhādikaṃ bhavet \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Bull seen in the chamber of the bull augurs fame, contentment, pleasure. Ass seen in the chamber of the bull predicts great joy and gain for the enquirer.

## \|\| 199.23 \|\|

*vṛṣasthāne gajaṃ dṛṣṭvā strīgajādisamāgamaḥ \|*  
*vṛṣasthāne sthite dhvāṅkṣe sthānamānasamāgamaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Elephant seen in the chamber of the bull augurs the aquisition of wives and elephants. Crow seen in the chamber of the bull presages the gain of place and honour by the enquirer.

## \|\| 199.24 \|\|

*kharasthāne dhvajaṃ dṛṣṭvā rogaśokādikaṃ bhavet \|*  
*kharasthāne sthite dhūmre taskarādibhayaṃ bhavet \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Banner seen in the chamber of the ass augurs sorrow and disease. Camel seen in the chamber of the ass presages terror from thieves and robbers in respect of the enquirer.

## \|\| 199.25 \|\|

*kharasthāne sthite siṃhe pūjāśrīvijayādikam \|*  
*sthite śunikharasthāne santāpadhananāśanam \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Lion seen in the chamber of the ass presages honour, prosperity and:victory to the enquirer. Dog seen in the Chamber of the ass presages loss of wealth and anguish.

## \|\| 199.26 \|\|

*kharasthāne vṛṣaṃ dṛṣṭvā sukhaṃ priyasamāgamaḥ \|*  
*kharasthāne kharaṃ dṛṣṭvā duḥ khīpīḍādi nirdiśet \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Bull seen in the chamber of the ass presages happiness and meeting with dear ones. Ass seen in the chamber of the ass predicts pain and disease.

## \|\| 199.27 \|\|

*kharasthāne gajaṃ dṛṣṭvā sukhaputtrādikaṃ bhavet \|*  
*kharasthāne sthite dhvāṅkṣe kalaho vyādhireva ca \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Elephant seen in the chamber of the ass predicts joy and birth of sons. Crow seen in the chamber of the ass augurs quarrel and disease.

## \|\| 199.28 \|\|

*gajasthāne dhvajaṃ dṛṣṭvā strījayaśrīsukhādikam \|*  
*gajasthānesthite dhūmre dhanadhānyasamāgamaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Banner seen in the chamber of the elephant foretells joy and birth of sons. Camel seen in the chamber of the elephant predicts acquisition of wealth and food grain by the enquirer.

## \|\| 199.29 \|\|

*gajasthāne sthite siṃhe jayasiddhisamāgamaḥ \|*  
*sthite śuni gajasthāne ārogyaṃ sukhasampadaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Lion seen in the chamber of the elephant augurs success and victory. Dog seen in the chamber of the elephant predicts happiness, prosperity and recovery from disease.

## \|\| 199.30 \|\|

*gajasthāne vṛṣaṃ dṛṣṭvā rājamānadhanādikam \|*  
*gajasthāne kharaṃ dṛṣṭvā pūrvaṃ duḥ khaṃ tataḥ sukham \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Bull seen in the chamber of the elephant presages royal favour and wealth. Ass seen in the chamber of the elephant presages the advent of misery to be followed by days of prospertiy.

## \|\| 199.31 \|\|

*gajasthāne gajaṃ dṛṣṭvā kṣetradhānyasukhādikam \|*  
*gajasthānesthite dhvāṅkṣe dhanadhānyasamāgamaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Elephant seen in the chamber of the elephant predicts joy and acquisition of fields and food grain by the enquirer. Crow seen in the chamber of the elephant presages the acquisition of wealth and food frain by the enquirer.

## \|\| 199.32 \|\|

*dhvāṅkṣasthāne dhvajaṃ dṛṣṭvā kāryanāśo bhaviṣyati \|*  
*dhvāṅkṣasthāne sthite dhūmre kaliduḥ khaṃ gamiṣyati \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Banner seen in the chamber of the crow augurs the failure of an undertaking. Camel seen in the chamber of the crow presages misery from gratification of wicked inclinations.

## \|\| 199.33 \|\|

*dhvāṅkṣasthāne sthite siṃhe vigraho duḥ khameva ca \|*  
*dhvāṅkṣasthāne sthite śvāne gṛhabhaṅgabhayādikam \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Lion seen in the chamber of the crow predicts quarrel and mental unrest. Dog seen in the chamber of the crow augurs terror and family dissensions.

## \|\| 199.34 \|\|

*dhvāṅkṣasthāne vṛṣaṃ dṛṣṭvā sthānabhraṃśabhayādikam \|*  
*dhvāṅkṣasthāne kharaṃ dṛṣṭvā dhananāśaparājayau \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Bull seen in the chamber of the crow presags terror and loss of place or home. Ass seen in the chamber of the crow presages loss of wealth and defeat.

## \|\| 199.35 \|\|

*dhvāṅkṣasthāne gajaṃ dṛṣṭvā dhanakīrtyādikaṃ bhavet \|*  
*dhvāṅkṣasthāne sthite dhvāṅkṣe videśagamanādikam \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Elephant seen in the chamber of the crow augurs the advent of fortune and fame. Crow seen in the chamber of the crow predicts a sojourn to a foreign country.

## Chapter 200

## \|\| 200.1 \|\|

*bhairava uvāca \|*  
*vakṣye vāyujayaṃ devi jayā jayavideśakam \|*  
*vāyvagnijalaśakrākhyaṃ maṅgalānāñcatuṣṭayam \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Bhairava said: — Now hear me, О goddess, on the day of Pratipada (first day of a light or discourse on the science of the conquest of the vital air, a knowledge where of enables a person to predict victory or defeat. The four vital airs, which are respectively called Agni, water, Sakra, etc., respectively flow through either of the nostrils.

## \|\| 200.2 \|\|

*vāmadakṣiṇasaṃsthaśca vāyuśca bahulo bhavet \|*  
*ūrdhvavāhī bhavedagniradhastu varuṇo bhavet \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. The breath, which courses in an upward direction through the nostril, is called Agni (fire); that which courses in a down ward direction through the nostril, is called Varuna.

## \|\| 200.3-6 \|\|

*mahendro madhyasaṃsthastu śuklapakṣe tu vāmagaḥ \|*  
*kṛṣṇapakṣe dakṣiṇaga udayasya tryahantryaham \|\| 3 \|\|*

*vahetpratipadādye ca viparīte bhavennatiḥ \|*  
*udayaḥ sūryamārgeṇa candreṇāstamayo yadi \|\| 4 \|\|*

*vardhante guṇasaṃghātā anyathā vighnamaucitam \|*  
*saṃkrāntyaḥ ṣoḍaśaproktā divā rātrau varānane \|\| 5 \|\|*

*yadā ca saṃkramedvāyurardhārdhaprahare sthitaḥ \|*  
*svāsthyāhānistadā jñeyā vāyurbhramati dehiṣu \|\| 6 \|\|*

3-6. The breath, that courses in a middling (neither upward nor downward) direction, is called Mahendra. In the light fortninght the breath-wind courses through the left nostril, while during the dark fortnight it courses through the right. For the period of three days, the breath wind follows the same course after taking a definite direction, changing its course completely dark fortnight). If the breath-wind rises following the course of the sun, and flows out along the passage of the moon, all good qualities of the breather are supposed to increase; contrary is the result if the breath-wind follows a contrary direction. О thou beautiful-faced one, sixteen are the changing periods of the direction of the breathwind in the course of an entire day and night. Impairment of health is brought about when this changing period falls at the close of each two hours and a quarter.

## \|\| 200.7-8 \|\|

*dakṣiṇe ca puṭe vāyurhito bhojanamaithune \|*  
*khaḍgahasto jayedyuddhe ripūnkāmasamanvitaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*vāmeva gamanaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ sarvakāryeṣu bhūṣitam \|*  
*vāyurvahati tatrasthaḥ praśro bhūtasya śobhanaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. Pertaking of a meal, and sexual intercourse are good when the breath-wind flows through the right nostril, and victory in battle attends the man, who enters into it, while his breathwind flows out through the right nostril. A man may safely start on a journey, or undertake any other auspicious act when the breath-wind flows out through his left nostril.

## \|\| 200.9 \|\|

*māhendre vāruṇe vāte ko 'pi doṣo na jāyate \|*  
*anāvṛṣṭirdakṣavāhe vṛṣṭiḥ syādvāmavāhake \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. No evil strikes a man when his breath-wind flows out in directions called Mahendra and Varuna. Men breathe through their right nostrils during a season of drought, while breath flows out of their left nostrils during the rains.

## Chapter 201

## \|\| 201.1-3 \|\|

*dhanvantariruvāca \|*  
*hayāyurvedamākhyāsye hayaṃ sarvārthalakṣaṇam \|*  
*kākatuṇḍaḥ kṛṣṇajihvo vṛkṣāsyaścoṣṇatālukaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*karālo hīnadantaśca śṛṅgī viraladantakaḥ \|*  
*ekāṇḍaścaiva jātāṇḍaḥ kañcukī dvikhurī stanī \|\| 2 \|\|*

*mārjārapādo vyāghrābhaḥ kuṣṭhavidradhisannibhaḥ \|*  
*yamajo vāmanaścaiva mārjāraḥ kapilocanaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

1-3. Dhartvantari said: — Now I shall expound the Ayurveda which deals with the diseases of horses, and the means of keeping them in sound health. Horses that are crow-lipped, black tongued, bearfaced, as well as those that are hot-palated or fierce-toothes, or are possessed of a greater or smaller number of teeth than what they naturally possess, or born with only one testicle, or afflicted with scrotal tumours, or possessed of deformed backs or bifurcated hoofs or teats, or footed like cats, or striped like tigers, or coloured like patches of cutaneous affections, or abscessed, as well as those which are extremely diminutive in size, or are eyed like cats or monkeys, should be regarded as inauspicious and unfit for use.

## \|\| 201.4-5 \|\|

*etaddoṣī hayastyājya uttamo 'śvasturuṣkajaḥ \|*  
*madhyamaḥ pañcahastaśca kanīyāṃśca trihastakaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*asaṃhatā ye ca vāhā hrasvakarṇāstathaiva ca \|*  
*śabalābhāḥ prabhāveṣu na dīnāścirajīvinaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. The best or first-class horses measure upward of four cubits in length, the second or middling class of horses measure half a cubit less than first class horses in length. The last class of horses measure three cubits and a half in length. Horses, that are long-limbed, shorteared, mouse coloured and long-lived, are the best.

## \|\| 201.6-8 \|\|

*revantapūjanāddhomādrakṣyāśca dvijabhājenāt \|*  
*saralaṃ nimbapatrāṇi guggulaṃ sarṣapānghṛtam? \|\| 6 \|\|*

*tilañcaiva vacāṃ higuṃ badhnīyādvājino gale \|*  
*āgantujaṃ doṣajantu vraṇaṃ dvividhamīritam \|\| 7 \|\|*

*cirapākaṃ vātajantu śleṣmajaṃ kṣiprapākakam? \|*  
*kaṇṭhadāhātmakaṃ pittācchoṇitānmandavedanam \|\| 8 \|\|*

6-8. The rite of protection should be done unto horses by worshipping the god, Revanta, and by feeding Brahmanas. For prophylactic purposes, Saralam, Nimba-leaves; bdellium, mustard seeds, sesame Vaca, asafaetida, saturated with clarified butter, should be tied round the neck of a horse. Ulers, which horses are found to be afflicted with, may, be divided into two classes as Agantuja (traumatic, or of extraneous origin) and ^ariraja (idiopathic). Ulcers marked by a late suppuration should be regarded as of a Vataja origin; suppuration speedily sets in ulcers, due to the action of the deranged Kapham while those, due to the deranged Pittam, are marked by a burning sensation in their in side.

## \|\| 201.9-11 \|\|

*āgantujantu śastrādyairduṣṭavraṇaviśodhanam \|*  
*eraṇḍamūlaṃ dviniśaṃ citrakaṃ viśvabheṣajam \|\| 9 \|\|*

*rasonaṃ saindhavaṃ vāpi takrakāñjikapoṣitam \|*  
*tilasaktukapiṇḍikā dadhiyuktā sasaindhavā \|*  
*nimbapatrayutaṃ piṇḍaṃ vraṇaśodhanaropaṇam \|\| 10 \|\|*

*paṭolaṃ nimbapatrañca vacā citrakameva ca \|*  
*pippalīśṛṅgaverañca cūrṇamekatra kārayet \|\| 11 \|\|*

9-11. Thick discharges from ulcers should be attributed to the action of the deranged Kaphah; while those, which are of a Sannipatika origin, exhibit symptoms peculiar to each of the three aggravated Dops. A plaster composed of DantI roots, the two kinds of Haridra, Citrakam. Visvabhesajam, Rasonam, and rock salt pasted together with whey or Kanjikam (a kind of fermented rice or barley grauel) or pastes of sesame, fried barley grain etc, mixed with powdered rock salt and milk curd, or pastes of Nimba-leaves, applied to ulcers in horses, bring about their purification and healing. A medicinal oil cooked in combination with Karavira; Kadall, Arka, Snuhl, Kutaja, Citraka and Bhallataka brings about the healing of sinuses in horses. As an alternative, such a sinus should, be washed with a medicinal Ghrtam cooked in combination with a paste of the five astringent barks. A compound consisting of the two kinds of Haridra, Vidanga, the five kinds of salt, Patolam and Nimba-leaves, Vaca, Citrakam, Pippall, and Shrngavera pounded together and adminis-tered through the medium of water brings about the expulsion of worms from the intestines of horses, and remove their deranged Kapham and somnolence.

## \|\| 201.12 \|\|

*etatpānātkrimiśleṣmamandānilavināśanam \|*  
*nimbapatraṃ paṭo lañca triphalā khadiraṃ tathā \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. A decoction of Nimba-leaves, Patolam, Triphala, and Khadira should be successively given for three days to a horse, after bleeding it, for the cure of any cutaneous affection.

## \|\| 201.13-14 \|\|

*kvāthayitvā tato vāhaṃ sṛtaraktaṃ vicakṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*tryahameva pridātavyaṃ hayakuṣṭhopaśāntaye \|\| 13 \|\|*

*savraṇeṣu ca kuṣṭheṣu tailaṃ sarṣapajaṃ hitam \|*  
*laśunādikaṣāyaśca pānabhuktyupaśāntaye \|\| 14 \|\|*

13-14. Application of mustard oil proves beneficial in cutaneous affections of horses attended with ulcers. A decoction of garlic should be given to a horse for the alleviation of diseases of the deranged Vayu.

## \|\| 201.15 \|\|

*mātuluṅgarasopetaṃ māṃsīnāṃ rasakena vā \|*  
*sadyo dadyāttatra nasyamanyairvātaiḥ susaṃyutaiḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. In disorders of digestion, the expressed juice of Matulunga, or of Mansi should be administered as errhines.

## \|\| 201.16 \|\|

*paladvayaṃ prathame 'hni ekaikapalavṛddhitaḥ \|*  
*yāvaddināni pūrṇāni palānyaṣṭādaśottame \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. One Palam weight of this compound should be administered on the first day, and its dose should be daily increased by a Palam weight until it reaches eighteen Palas.

## \|\| 201.17 \|\|

*adhame 'ṣṭapalāni syurmadhyame syuścaturdaśa \|*  
*śarannidāghayornaivadeyaṃ naiva tu dāpayet \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. The smallest does of this medicine is eight Palam, and its middling dose is fourteen Palas weight. Errhines should not be given of horses in summer or autumn.

## \|\| 201.18 \|\|

*tailena vātike roge śarkarājyapayonvitaiḥ \|*  
*kaṭutailaiḥ kaphe vyoṣaiḥ pitte catriphalāmbubhiḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. In diseases of the deranged and aggravated Vayu, the medicine should be administered through the medium of oil, or in combination with sugar, clarified butter of water. It should be given through the vehicle of mustard oil saturated with Vyosa (Trikatu) powders in diseases of the deranged Kapham, and through a solution, or decoction of Triphala in those of the deranged Pittam.

## \|\| 201.19 \|\|

*śāliṣaṣṭikadugdhāśī hayo hina jugupsitaḥ \|*  
*pakvajambūnibho hemavarṇo 'śvo na jugupsitaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. A horse, that lives on milk, Sali and Shastika grain, is not to be condemned, as well as the one, that is of the colour of a ripe Jamboline fruit, is not to be rejected.

## \|\| 201.20 \|\|

*ardhapraharaṇe dhurye gugguluṃ prāśayeddhayam \|*  
*bhojayetpāyasaṃ dugdhaṃ satvaraṃ susthiro hayaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Bdellium should be given to a horse, after it has been in any way hurt or injured, and milk should be administered to it for the purpose of speedily allaying the agitation.

## \|\| 201.21 \|\|

*vikāre bhojane dugdhaṃ śālyannaṃ vātale dadet \|*  
*karṣamāṃsarasaiḥ pitte madhumudgarasājyakaiḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. In diseases due to the action of the deranged and aggravated Vayu, milk and boiled rice should be given to a horse as food, while in those of Pittaja (bilious) origin, its diet should consist of a Karsa weight of meat soup mixed with honey, Mudga soup and clarified butter.

## \|\| 201.22 \|\|

*kaphe mudgānkulatthānvā kaṭutiktānkaphe haye \|*  
*bādhirye vyādhite grāse tridoṣādau tu gugguluḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. In diseases of the deranged Kapham, Mudga or Kulattha-soup mixed with butter or pungent drugs, should be given to a horse, while in cases of deafness, nervous affections, or in deseases of Sannipatika origin, bdellium should be freely given to it.

## \|\| 201.23 \|\|

*ghāsairdūrvā sarvaroge prathame 'hni palaṃ dadet \|*  
*vivardhayettataḥ karṣamekāhni palapañcakam \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. In all diseases a Palam weight of Durva should be given to a horse on the first day, and the does should be increased by a Karsa measure, each day, till five Palam is reached.

## \|\| 201.24 \|\|

*pāne ca bhojane caiva aśītipalakaṃ param \|*  
*madhye ṣaṣṭiścādhameṣu catvāriṃśacca bhogiṣu \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Eighty Palam is the highest does. Sixty Palam is the middling and forty Palam is the lowest dose.

## \|\| 201.25 \|\|

*vraṇe kuṣṭheṣu khañjeṣu triphalākvāthasaṃyutam \|*  
*mandāgnau śotharoge ca gavāṃ mūtreṇa yojitam \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. In ulcers, cutaneous affections, and lameness, the food of a horse should be made saturated with a decoction of Triphala whereas in impaired digestion, and oedema (dropsical swelling) it should be given saturated with cow's urine.

## \|\| 201.26 \|\|

*vātapitte vraṇe vyādhau gokṣīraṃ ghṛtasaṃyutam \|*  
*deyaṃ kṛśānāṃ puṣṭyarthaṃ māṃsairyuktaṃ ca bhojanam \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. In diseases due to the actions of the deranged Vayu and Pittam, as well as in ulcercases, the food of a horse should be given mixed with Goksura and clarified butter, while a goodly quantity of Masa puls should be given to it whenever a general plumpness of its limbs is desired.

## \|\| 201.27 \|\|

*supiṣṭāyāḥ pradātavyaṃ guḍūcyāḥ palapañcakam \|*  
*prabhāte ghṛtasaṃyuktaṃ śaradgīṣme ca vājinām \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Five Palam weight of Guduci should be given to a horse, each morning, in summer and autumn, through the vehicle of rice-paste treated with clarified butter.

## \|\| 201.28 \|\|

*rogaghnaṃ puṣṭidaṃ cāpi balatejovivardhanam \|*  
*tadevāśvāyadātavyaṃ kṣīrayuktamathāpi vā \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. This food imparts a greater strength and vigour to a horse and acts as a general prophylaxis against disease.

## \|\| 201.29 \|\|

*guḍūcīkalpayogena śatāvaryaśvagandhayoḥ \|*  
*catvāri trīṇi madhyasya jaghanyasya palāni hi \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Guduci may be likewise given of a horse with benefit through the medium of milk. For similar purposes, one, three or four Palam weights of powdered 6atavari and Asvagandha may be given to a horse with Guduci paste.

## \|\| 201.30 \|\|

*akasmādyatra vāhānāmekarūpaṃ yadā bhavet \|*  
*mriyate ca yadā kṣipramupasargaṃ tamādiśet \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. A mortal epidemic is presaged when all the horses in a stud are found to assume one colour.

## \|\| 201.31 \|\|

*homādyai rakṣayā viprabhojanairbalikarmaṇā \|*  
*śāntyopasargaśāntiḥ syāddharītakyādikalpataḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. The visitation may be warded off by the performance of proper prophylactic rites, and Homas, as well as by feeding the pious and learned Brahmanas. The medicine known as HarltakIKalpa may be given with benefit to horses under these circumstances.

## \|\| 201.32 \|\|

*harītakī gavāṃ mūtraistailena lavaṇānvitā \|*  
*ādau pañca tataḥ pañca vṛddhyā pūrṇaśatāvadhi \|*  
*uttamā ca śataṃ mātrāstvaśītiḥ ṣaṣṭireva vā \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. This medicine (Harltakl-Kalpa) consists in giving five Haritakis, each day, to a horse, pasted together with rock-salt and cow's urine. The dose of the medicine should be increased by five Haritakis, each successive day, until it goes up to a hundred Haritakis. The full dose (of this medicine) is a hundred; and the middling, eighty, the smallest dose being sixty Haritakis.

## \|\| 201.33 \|\|

*gajāyurvedamākhyāsye uktāḥ kalpā gaje hitāḥ \|*  
*gaje caturguṇā mātrāstābhirgajarugardanaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Now I shall expound that branch of tire Ayurveda, which deals with the medical treatment of the diseases of elephants. Quardruple of a horse's dose is the dose of a medicine for an elephant.

## \|\| 201.34 \|\|

*gajo pasargavyādhīnāṃ śamanaṃ śāntikarma ca \|*  
*pūjayitvā surānviprānratnairgāṃ kapilāṃ dadet \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Medicines enumerated in connection with diseases of horses may be employed with advantage in those that are found to afflict elephants. The prophylactic, or curative religious rites, in respect of the, alleviation of diseases of elephants, consist in making gifts of jewel-decked Kapila kine to Brahmanas, after worshipping the celestials and Brahmanas.

## \|\| 201.35 \|\|

*dantidantadvaye mālāṃ nibandhīyādupoṣitaḥ \|*  
*mantreṇa mantritānvaidyairvacāsiddhārthakāṃstathā \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. A physician, while observing a fast, shall tie round the tusks of an elephant a consecrated garland of white mustard seeds. The sun-god, Shiva and the goddesses Druga and ЙгТ, duly worshipped, protect elephants from attacks of diseases.

## \|\| 201.36 \|\|

*sūryādiśivadurgāśrīviṣṇvarcā rakṣayedgajam \|*  
*baliṃ dadyācca bhūtebhyaḥ snāpayecca caturghaṭaiḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Offerings should be made to the malignant spirits at the close of the worship, and the body of the elephant should be rubbed with ashes and then washed with four pitcher-fuls of water.

## \|\| 201.37 \|\|

*bhojanaṃ mantritaṃ dadyādbhasmanoddhūnayedgajamam \|*  
*bhūtarakṣā śubhā medhyā vāraṇaṃ rakṣayetsadā \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Food consecrated by reciting the proper Mantras shall be given to an elephant, and the sacred rite of prophylaxis against the influences of malignant spirits serves to grant it an immunity from injury.

## \|\| 201.38 \|\|

*triphalāpañcakole ca daśamūlaṃ viḍaṅgakam \|*  
*śatāvarīguḍūcī ca nimbavāsakakiṃśukāḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Decoctions of parchifying drugs, as well as those of Triphala, Pancakola, Dasamulam, Vidanga, Satavari, GuducI, Nimba, Vasaka, anti Kinsuka should be given for the cure of diseases of elephants.

## \|\| 201.39 \|\|

*gajarogavināśāya hito rūkṣaḥ kaṣāyakaḥ \|*  
*āyurvedadvayoktānāmuktaṃ saṃkṣepasārataḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Thus I have briefly expounded the nature of medical treatment to be employed for the cure of diseases of elephants.

## Chapter 202

## \|\| 202.1 \|\|

*hariruvāca \|*  
*ekaṃ punarnavāmūlamapāmārgasya vā śiva \|*  
*sarasaṃ yoniniḥ kṣiptaṃ varāṅgasya vyathāṃ haret \|*  
*prasūtivedanāñcaiva taruṇīnāṃ vyathāṃ haret \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Hari Said: — A single moist, Punamava root, or Apamarga root, or the expressed juice of either of these roots, introduced into the vagina, relieves the local plain of young wives or 9f Parturient woman.

## \|\| 202.2 \|\|

*bhūmi kūṣmāṇḍamūlaṃ vai śālicūrṇamathāpi vā \|*  
*saptāhaṃ dugdhapītaṃ syātstrīṇāṃ bahupayaskaram \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. The roots of Bhumi Kusmanda taken pasted with rice-washings tend to improve the secretion of milk in parturient women.

## \|\| 202.3-4 \|\|

*rudrendravāruṇīmulaṃ lepātstrīstanavedanā \|*  
*naśyeta ghṛtapakvā ca kāryāvaśyantu polikā \|\| 3 \|\|*

*bhakṣitā sā maheśāna yoniśūlaṃ vināśayet \|*  
*pralepitā kāravellamūlenaiva vinirgatā \|\| 4 \|\|*

3-4. Plasters of pasted Indra Varuni roots, О Siva, relieve the breast pain in females. О thou supreme deity, ingestions of Рака cooked with clarified butter relieve an aching pain in the female reproductive organs. Platers of Karavella roots pasted with water tend to replace a protruded vagina in its natural position.

## \|\| 202.5-8 \|\|

*yoniḥ praveśamāyāti nātra kāryā vicāraṇā \|*  
*nīlīpaṭolamūlāni sājyāni tilavāriṇā \|\| 5 \|\|*

*piṣṭānyeṣāṃ pralepo vai jvālāgardabharāganat \|*  
*pāṭhāmūlaṃ rudra pītaṃ piṣṭaṃ taṇḍulavāriṇā \|\| 6 \|\|*

*pāparogaharaṃ syācca kuṣṭhapānaṃ tathaiva ca \|*  
*vāsyodakañca samadhu pītamantargatasya vai \|\| 7 \|\|*

*pāparogasya santāpanivṛktiṃ kurute śiva \|*  
*ghṛtatulyā rudra lākṣā pītā kṣīreṇa vai saha \|\| 8 \|\|*

5-8. Plasters of Nill, and Patola roots, pasted together with a solution of Tila and applied with the admixture of clarified butter, prove curative in JvalaGardhava. О Rudra, Patha roots taken pasted with rice- washings, as well as Kustha-roots administered in the same way relieve Papa-rogam. Solutions of Vasyam taken with honey alleviate the internal burning sensation in cases of Paparogam. О Rudra, clarified butter taken with as much quantity of Laksa through the vehicle of milk cures leucorrhoea.

## \|\| 202.9-10 \|\|

*pradaraṃ harate rogaṃ nātra kāryā vicāraṇā \|*  
*dvijayaṣṭī trikaṭukaṃ cūrṇaṃ pītaṃ harecchiva \|\| 9 \|\|*

*tilakvāthena saṃyuktaṃ raktagulmaṃ striyā hara \|*  
*kusumasya nibaddhañca taruṇīnāṃ maheśvara \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. О thou blissful one, powders of Dvijayasti and Trikantakam taken with a decoction of sesame prove curative in Rakta Gulmas of women, and act as a good emanagogue remedy.

## \|\| 202.11-14 \|\|

*raktotpalasya vai kandaṃ-śarkarātilasaṃyutam \|*  
*pītaṃ saśarkaraṃ strīṇāṃ dhārayedgarbhapātanam \|\| 11 \|\|*

*raktastrāvasya nāśaḥ syācchītodakaniṣevaṇāt \|*  
*pītantu kāñjika rudra kvathitaṃ śarapuṅkhayā \|\| 12 \|\|*

*hiṅgustraindhavasaṃyuktaṃ śīghraṃ strīṇāṃ prasūtikṛt \|*  
*mātuluṅgasya vai mūlaṃ kaṭibaddhaṃ prasūtikṛt \|\| 13 \|\|*

*apāmārgasya vai mūle garbhavatyāstu nāmataḥ \|*  
*utpāṭyamāne sakale puttraḥ syādānyathā sutā \|\| 14 \|\|*

11-14. Bulbs of Raktotpalam, taken with sugar or with cold water, relieve menorrhagia. A decoction of Sarapunkha taken with KanjTkam, Hingu and rock salt tends to bring about a speedy parturition. A Matulunga root, if it can be culled out entire, by mentioning the name of an ancient presages the birth of a male child, if otherwise (pulled out split or served) it predicts the birth of a female one.

## \|\| 202.15-16 \|\|

*apāmārgasya vai mūle nārīṇāṃ śirasi sthite \|*  
*garbhaśūlaṃ vinaśyeta nātra kāryā vicāraṇā \|\| 15 \|\|*

*karpūra-madanaphala-madhukaiḥ pūritaḥ śiva \|*  
*yoniḥ subhā syādvṛddhāyā yuvatyāḥ kiṃ punarhara \|\| 16 \|\|*

15-16. An Apamarga root inserted into the chignonon of a pregnant woman, О thou blissful one, or Karpura, Madanaphalam and Madhuka pounded together and introduced even into the reproductive organ of an old woman, produces happy results, not to speak of it being used by young maidens.

## \|\| 202.17 \|\|

*yasya bālasya tilakaḥ kṛto gaurocanākhyayā \|*  
*śarkarā-kuṣṭhapānañca dattaṃ sa syācca nirbhayaḥ \|*  
*viṣa-bhūta-grahādibhyo vyādhibhyo bālakaḥ śiva \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Potions of solutions of- Kustam sweetened with sugar, and impressment of Tilak marks on the foreheads of infants act as a general prophylasix against the influence of malignant planets, ghosts, and diseases.

## \|\| 202.18 \|\|

*śaṅkha-nābhi-vacā-kuṣṭha-lohānāṃ dhāraṇaṃ sadā \|*  
*bālānāmupasargebhyo rudra rakṣākaraṃ bhavet \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. An infant should be made to wear on its person, О Rudra, Shankha Nabhl, Vaca, Kustham and bits of iron for prophylactic purposes.

## \|\| 202.19-20 \|\|

*palāśacūrṇaṃ samadhu gavyājyāmalakānvitam \|*  
*saviḍaṅgaṃ pītamātraṃ naraṃ kuryānmahāmatim \|\| 19 \|\|*

*māsaikena mahādeva jarā-maraṇavarjitaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

19-20. Powders of Palasa seeds, or powdered Amalakam and Vidanga taken with the admixture of honey and melted cow-butter tend to improve the intellect. Its effect is almost instantanecous; by taking this compound for a month, О thou, supreme deity, a person is enabled to conquer death and decay,

## \|\| 202.21 \|\|

*palāśabījaṃ saghṛtaṃ tila-madhvanvitaṃ samam \|*  
*saptāhaṃ bhakṣitaṃ rudra jarāṃ nayati saṃkṣayam \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Powders of Palasa seeds and Tilam, taken for a weak, through the vehicle of honey and clarified butter, would undoubtedly remove, О Rudra, the effects of old age.

## \|\| 202.22 \|\|

*rudrāmalakacūrṇaṃ vai madhu-taila ghṛtānvitam \|*  
*jagdhvā māsaṃ yuvā syācca naro vāgīśvarī bhavet \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. By taking, for a month, О Rudra, powders of Amalakam in combination with honey and oil, a person would verily become a lord of speech.

## \|\| 202.23 \|\|

*śivāmalakacūrṇaṃ vai madhunā udakena vā \|*  
*balāni kuryānnāsāyāḥ pratyūṣe bhakṣitaṃ śiva \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Water containing powders of Shiva and Amalakam, sweetened with honey and drunk through the nostrils, each morning, would act as the best strength-giving medicine.

## \|\| 202.24 \|\|

*kuṣṭhacūrṇaṃ sājya-madhu prātarjagdhvā bhavennaraḥ \|*  
*sākṣātsurabhideho vai jīvedvarṣasahasrakam \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. By taking Kustham-powders, each morning with the admixtrue of honey and clarified butter, a man would be able to witness a thousand summers in the full possession of all his faculties in a healthy and fragnant-smelling frame.

## \|\| 202.25-26 \|\|

*māṣasya vidalānye vituṣāṇi maheśvara \|*  
*ghṛtabhāvitaśuṣkāṇi payasā sādhitāni vai \|\| 25 \|\|*

*samādhvājyapayobhiśca bhakṣayitvā ca kāmayet \|*  
*strīṇāṃ śataṃ mahādeva tatkṣaṇānnātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

25-26. By regularly consuming huskless Masa pulse, soaked with clarified butter in the manner of a Bhavana. or cooked with milk, in combination with honey and milk, a man would be able to visit a hundred women, each night. Mercury is purfied by rubbing it with sulphur and castor oil.

## \|\| 202.27 \|\|

*rasaścairaṇḍatailena gandhakena śubho bhavet \|*  
*trikālodakasaṃghuṣṭo balakṛdbhakṣaṇādbhavet \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. A dose of such purified mercury taken with water, thrice a day, acts as a good tonic medicine.

## \|\| 202.28 \|\|

*dugdhaṃ vituṣamāṣaiśca śimbābījaiśca sādhitam \|*  
*apāmārgasya tailena pītaṃ strīśatakāmakṛt \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. By taking milk, that has been cooked with huskless Masa-pulse and Shimb! seeds, in combination with Apamarga oil, one would be able to visit a hundred women, each day.

## Chapter 203

## \|\| 203.1 \|\|

*hariruvāca \|*  
*yā gaurdveṣṭiṃ svakaṃ vatsaṃ tasyā deyaṃ svakaṃ payaḥ \|*  
*lavaṇena samāyuktaṃ tasyā vatsaḥ priyo bhavet \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Hari said: — То a cow, that shuns, or turns hostile to, her own calf, should be given her milk, duly milched and salted, Whereby she would fondly take to her offspring.

## \|\| 203.2 \|\|

*śuno 'sthi kaṇṭhabaddhaṃ hi mahiṣāṇāṃ gavā tathā \|*  
*kṛmijālaṃ pātayati sakalaṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Bits of dog's bones tied round the neck of a cow or a cow-buffalo lead to the expulsion of vermins from her body

## \|\| 203.3 \|\|

*gojaṅganābhipātaḥ syādguñjāmūlasya bhakṣaṇāt \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Gunja roots internally administered would bring about the castings of horns in homed cattle.

## \|\| 203.4 \|\|

*varuṇaphalasyarasaṃ kareṇa mathitaṃ śiva \|*  
*catuṣpāda-dvipadayoḥ kṛmijālaṃ nipātayet \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. External applications of the juice of Vamna-phalas, aqueezed out with the hand, would bring about the expulsion of vermins, О Shiva, from the bodies of biped and quadruped animals.

## \|\| 203.5 \|\|

*vraṇañca śamayedrudra jayāyāḥ pūraṇāt tathā \|*  
*gajamūtrasya vai pānaṃ go-mahiṣyupasarganut \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. О Rudra, pourings of the expressed juice of Jaya would bring about the healing of ulcers in quadrupeds. The urine of a she-elephant internally administered would remove the bodily ailments of horned cattle.

## \|\| 203.6 \|\|

*samasūra śālibījaṃ pītaṃ takreṇa gharṣitam \|*  
*kṣīre go-mahīṣasyaiva goḥ puṃsaśca hitaṃ bhavet \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Lentil seeds and Bali rice pasted with whey (Takram) and administered through the medium of cow or buffalo-milk would prove beneficial to bullocks.

## \|\| 203.7-8 \|\|

*patrañca śarapuṅkhāyā dattaṃ salavaṇaṃ śiva \|*  
*vārisphoṭaṃ hayānāñca kesarāṇāṃ vināśayet \|\| 7 \|\|*

*ghṛtakumārīpatrameva dattaṃ salakṣaṇaṃ hara \|*  
*turagama-kesarāṇāṃ kaṇḍūnaṃśyenna saṃśayaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. 3arapurikha leaves given with salt would cure the belbous eruptions (Vari-sphotam) in horses and bullocks, Ghrtakumarl leaves given with salt would relieve itches in horses and bullocks.

## Chapter 204

## \|\| 204.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*evaṃ dhanvantariḥ prāha suśrutāyaca vaidyakam \|*  
*ata nāmāni vakṣyāmi oṣadhīnāṃ samāsataḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Sata said: — Dhanvantari thus narrated the science of Ayurveda to SuSruta. New I shall briefly enumerate the different names of the Ayurvedic drugs.

## \|\| 204.2 \|\|

*sthirā vidārigandhā ca śālapaṇyaśumatyapi \|*  
*lāṅgalī kalasī caiva kroṣṭupucchā guhā matā \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Sthira, Vidarigandha and Amsumati are the names of 6alaparnl (Desmodium Gangeticum). Larigali, Kalasi, and Krostu- are the names of Guha (Mucuna Pruriens).

## \|\| 204.3 \|\|

*punarnavātha parṣābhūḥ kaṭhilyā kāruṇā tathā \|*  
*eraṇḍaścoruvūkaḥ syādāmardo vardhamānakaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Varsabhu is called Punamava (Spreading hogneed, Boerhaaria Diffusa). Karavellah is another name of Katillaka (Hairy Momardica Charantea). Eranaa (castor-oil plant. Riconus Comamnis) Uruvaka, Amarda and Vardha- manaka are synonymous.

## \|\| 204.4 \|\|

*jhaṣā nāgabalā jñeyā śvadaṃṣṭrā gokṣuro mataḥ \|*  
*śatāvarī varā bhīru pīvarīndīvarī varī \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Nagavala is called Jhasa (Sida Spinosa). 6vadanstra is called Goksura (Tygophylleae Tribulus terestris). Satavari, Vara, Bhiru, Pivari, Varl,and Indivarl (Asparagus Racemosus) are synonymous.

## \|\| 204.5 \|\|

*vyāghrī tu bṛhatī kṛṣṇā haṃsapādī madhustravā \|*  
*dhāmanī kaṇṭakārī syātkṣudrā siṃhī nidigdhikā \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Vyaghri, Vrhati, Krsna, HanspadI, Madhusrava, Dhamani, Ksudra, Simhl and Nidigdhika are the names of Kantakari (Solanum Janthocarpum).

## \|\| 204.6 \|\|

*vṛścikā tryamṛtā kālī viṣaghnī sarpadaṃṣṭrikā \|*  
*markaṭī cātmaguptā syādārṣeyī kapikacchukā \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Vrscikali, Amrta, Kali, Visaghnl, Sarpa- danstrika, Markati, Atmagupta, and Arseyl and the names of Kapikacchuka (Mucuna Pruriens).

## \|\| 204.7 \|\|

*mudgaparṇo kṣudrasahā māṣaparṇo mahāsahā \|*  
*tyajā parā ca mahā jñeyā daṇḍayonyaṅkasaṃjñayā \|*  
*nyagrodhastu vaṭo jñeyaḥ aśvatthaḥ kapilo mataḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Ksudra-Saha is Mudgaparnl (Phaseous Trilobus), while Masapami is called Mafia-saha (Teramuns Labialis, Grangea Madraspatna). Nyagrodha is Vata (Banyan tree); Kapila is the name of Asvattha (Ficus Religioasa).

## \|\| 204.8 \|\|

*plakṣo 'tha gardabhāṇḍaḥ syātparkaṭī ca kapītanaḥ \|*  
*pārthastu kakubho dhanvi vijñeyor'junanāmabhiḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Parkati Gardhavada, and Kapitana are the names of Plaksa (Thaspesia Pahulnea). Partha, Kukubha, and Dhanvl are the names of Arjuna (Farminalia Arjuna).

## \|\| 204.9 \|\|

*nandīvṛkṣaḥ prarohī syātpuṣṭikārīti cocyate \|*  
*vañjulo vetaso jñeyo bhallātaścāpyaruṣkaraḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Prarohi, and Pustikari are the names of NandIVrksa (a species of figlatree). Vanjual is Vetasa (calamus rotong), while Bhallataka is called Aruskara (Semecarpus Anacardium).

## \|\| 204.10 \|\|

*lodhraḥ sāravako dhṛṣṭastirīṭaścāpi kīrtitaḥ \|*  
*bṛhatphalā mahājambūrjñeyā bālaphalā parā \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Lodhra is called Saravaka, Dhrsta, or Tirita (Symplocas Racemosa). Bala-phala, and Vrhat- phala are the names of Maha-Jambu (Eugenia Jambolana).

## \|\| 204.11-14 \|\|

*tṛtīyā jalajambūḥ syānnādeyī sā ca kīrtitā \|*  
*kaṇā kṛṣṇopakuñcī ca śauṇḍī māgadhiketi ca \|\| 11 \|\|*

*kathitā pippalī tajjñaistanmūlaṃ granthikaṃ smṛtam \|*  
*ūṣaṇaṃ maricaṃ jñeyaṃ śuṇṭhī viśvaṃ mahauṣadham \|\| 12 \|\|*

*vyoṣaṃ kaṭutrayaṃ vidyāttryūṣaṇaṃ tacca kīrtyate \|*  
*lāṅgalī halinī ca syāccheyasī gaja pippalī \|\| 13 \|\|*

*trāyantī trāyamāṇā syādutsāyā suvahā smṛtā \|*  
*citrakaḥ syācchikhī vahniragnisaṃjñābhirucyate \|\| 14 \|\|*

11-14. Nadeyl and Trtlya are the names of JalaYambQ (wild Jamboline), Капа, Krsna, Upakulya, 6aundi and MagadhI are the names of Pippall (Piper Longum), while its roots are called Granthikam (Piper offcinarum). Usanam is Maricam (Piper Nigrum), while Visvam and Maahausadham are the names of 6unthl (dry gingiber), Vyosam is the name of Trikatu, (3unthl, Pippalt and Maricam) which is also called Tryusanam. Langali, Halini and Shreyasl are the names of Gajapippall (Potties officinalis), Trayamana is called- TrayantI (Thalicturm Fdliolosum), and Utsa is Vahuvaha. Vanhi, Shikhl, and terms signifying fire, are the names of Citrakam (Plumbgo Zeylanica).

## \|\| 204.15-16 \|\|

*ṣaḍgranthogrā vacā jñeyā śvetā haimavatīti ca \|*  
*kuṭajo vṛkṣakaḥ śakro vatsako girimāllikā \|\| 15 \|\|*

*kaliṅgendrayavāriṣṭaṃ tasya bījāni lakṣayet \|*  
*mustakto meghanāmā syātkauntī jñeyā hareṇukā \|\| 16 \|\|*

15-16. Sadgrantha, Ugra, Shveta and Heimavatl are the names of Vaca (Sweet Flag). Vrkska, Sukra, Vastsaka and Girimallika are the names of Kutaja (Wrightia Anti-dysenterica), and Aristam, Indrayava and Kalinga are the names of Kutaja-seeds. KuntI, Harenuka, and terms denoting. Cloud, are the names of Mustaka (Mariscus cyuprus).

## \|\| 204.17-19 \|\|

*elā ca bahulā proktā sūkṣmailā ca tathā truṭiḥ \|*  
*padmā bhārṅgo tathā kāñjī jñeyā brāhmaṇayaṣṭikā \|\| 17 \|\|*

*mūrvā madhurasā jñeyā tejanī tiktavallikā \|*  
*mahānimbo bṛhannimbo dīpyakaḥ syādyavānikā \|\| 18 \|\|*

*viḍaṅgaṃ krimaśatruḥ syādrāmaṭhaṃ hiṅgurucyate \|*  
*ajājī jīrakaṃ jñeyā kāravī copakuñcikā \|\| 19 \|\|*

17-19. Ela (cardemon) is called Vahula, the smaller variety is called Truti. Padma, Bharngi, and Kanjl are called Brahmanas-Yastika (Cleroden- dron Siphonanthus). Tejini, Tiktabalkala and Madhurasa are the names of Murva (Sanse- vieria Zeylancia). Mahanimba, Vrksanimba, and Dipyakas are the names of Jamanl (Ptychotis) Vidanga (seeds of Embelia Ribus) and, Hingu are called Amatham. Ajaji is the name of Jirakan (cumin seeds), Karavl is Upakancika (Nigella Sativa or Indica).

## \|\| 204.20-21 \|\|

*vijñeyā kaṭukā tiktā tathā kaṭukarohiṇī \|*  
*tagaraṃ syānnataṃ vakraṃ cocaṃ tvacavarāṅgakam \|\| 20 \|\|*

*udīcyaṃ bālakaṃ proktaṃ hrīberaṃ cāmbunāmabhiḥ \|*  
*patrakaṃ dalasaṃjñābhiścārakaṃ taskarāhvayam \|\| 21 \|\|*

20-21. Katuka and Tikta are the names of Katu- (Blach Hellibore) Tagaram, Natam, Cakram, Cocam, and Tvacam are the names of Varangakam, (Cinnamon Bark) Hriveram (Pavonia Odorata) is synony mous with Udicyam, and Valakam, and terms signifying water, are also used to denote this plant.

## \|\| 204.22 \|\|

*hemābhaṃ nāgasaṃjñābhirnāgakeśara ucyate \|*  
*asṛkkuṅkumamākhyātaṃ tathā kāśmīrabāhlikam \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Hemabha, and terms denoting elephant, are the names of Nagakesara (Mesua ferrea). Asrik, Kasmlra, and Bahlikam are the names of Kumkum (saffron).

## \|\| 204.23 \|\|

*ayo lohaṃ samuddiṣṭaṃ yaugikairlohanāmabhiḥ \|*  
*puraṃ kuṭanaṭaṃ vidyānmahiṣākṣaḥ palaṅkaṣā \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Compounds signifying Iron denote Ayuguru. Yavista, Pracina, Kalika, SusabI, Tosanasa and Rambha are the names of Kadali (Plantain). Puram, Kutannat, Mahisaksa and Palankasa are the names of Kutannat.

## \|\| 204.24 \|\|

*kāśmarī kaṭphalā jñeyā śrīparṇo ceti kīrtitā \|*  
*śallakī gajabhakṣyā ca patrī ca surabhī stravaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Kasmari and Shriparnl and the names of Katphala (Myrica Sapida), Patri, Sarabhl, Srava and Garbhaksya are the names of SallakI (Bos Wellia Serrata).

## \|\| 204.25 \|\|

*dhātrīmāmalakīṃ vidyādakṣaścaiva vibhītakaḥ \|*  
*pathyābhayā ca vijñeyā pūtanā ca harītakī \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Dhatri is the name of Amalakam (Emblic Myrobalans) Aksa is the name of Vibhltaka (Terminalia Belirica). Pa thy a, Abhaya and Putana are the names of Harltakl (Indian Myrobalans).

## \|\| 204.26-27 \|\|

*triphalā phalamevoktā tacca jñeyaṃ phalatrikam \|*  
*udakīryo dīrghavṛntaḥ karañjaśceti kīrtitaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*yaṣṭī yaṣṭyāhvayaṃ proktaṃ madukaṃ madhuyaṣṭikā \|*  
*dhātakī tāmraparṇo syātsamaṅgā kuñjarā matā \|\| 27 \|\|*

26-27. The group of drugs, known as Triphala or Phalatrikam, consists of Harltakl, Bibhitaka and Amlakam (with their stones removed. Udakirl, and DIrgha-Vmta, are the names of Karanja (Karanjl of the Raja-nighantam); and Yasti, Yastahvayam, and Madhu-Yasti are synony mous with Madhukam (Liquorice-root; Glycyrrhiza glabra). Tamraparni, Samanga and Kunjara are the names of Dhataki (Woodfordia Floribondia).

## \|\| 204.28-29 \|\|

*sitaṃ malayajaṃ śītaṃ gośīrṣaṃ sitacandanam \|*  
*vidyādraktaṃ candanaṃ ca dvitīyaṃ raktacandanam \|\| 28 \|\|*

*kākolī ca smṛtā vīrā vayasyā cārkapuṣpikā \|*  
*śṛṅgī karkaṭaśṛṅgī ca mahāghoṣā ca kīrtitā \|\| 29 \|\|*

28-29. Sitam, Malayajam, Sitam and GoSirgam, are the terms which signify white sandal wood (Santalam albam), while the red species is called Rakta Candanam. Vira, Vayasya, and Arkapuspika are the names of Kakoli, while 6rngi is known by the names Karkata~Shrngi and Mahaghosa (Rhus Succedanea).

## \|\| 204.30 \|\|

*tugākṣīrī śubhā vāṃśī vijñeyā vaṃśalocanā \|*  
*mṛdvikā ca smṛtā drākṣā tathā gostanikā matā \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Tugaksiri, Subha and Vans! are the names of Vamsalocana (Marina of the Bamboo), and Grapes are called by the epithets of Draksa. Gostanika and Mrdvika (Vitis Vinifera).

## \|\| 204.31 \|\|

*syāduśīraṃ mṛṇālañca sevyaṃ lāmajjakaṃ tathā \|*  
*sārañca gopavallī ca gopī bhadrā ca kathyate \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Lamajjka are called by the names of Usiram and Mrnalam (Juncus Odoratus), and Saram, Gopi, and Gopavalli are the names of Bhadra (Hemidesmus Indicus).

## \|\| 204.32 \|\|

*dantī kaṭaṅkaṭerī ca jñeyā dāruniśeti ca \|*  
*haridrā rajanī proktā pītikā rātrināmikā \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. DantI and Katankeri are tie names of Daru- (Cascinium Fenestratum), and Rajanl, PItika, and terms signifying "Night," are the synonymes of Haridra (turmeric).

## \|\| 204.33 \|\|

*vṛkṣādanī chinnaruhā nīlavallī rasāmṛtā \|*  
*vasukoṭaśca vijñeyo vāśiraḥ kāmpillo mataḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Vira-Vrksa is known by the epithets of Virataru and Varataru, while Rasa, Amrta, Nilavalli and Chinna-ruha are the epithes of Vrksadam (Tinaspora Cordifolia). Kapota is another name of Surya bhakta (Cleome Viscosa, Polanisia Icosundra), while Katapam is called Kant habhalla or Kantha-sala, and Kampika, Vasira and Vasukota are all synonymous.

## \|\| 204.34-35 \|\|

*pāṣāṇabhedako 'riṣṭo hyasmabhitkuṭṭabhedakaḥ \|*  
*ghaṇṭākaḥ śuṣkako jñeyo vaco 'tha sūcako mataḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

*suraso bījakaścaiva pītaśālo 'bhidhīyeta \|*  
*vajravṛkṣo mahāvṛkṣaḥ snuhī snukca sudhā guḍā \|\| 35 \|\|*

34-35. Arista, A^va-smit and Katta-bhedaka are the names of Pagana-bheda (Coleus amboinicus). Ghantaka is known by the epithets of Lusaka, Vaca and Sucaka. Sagandha, Chatradi and Chatra are the names of Kusumbha (Cathamul tenctarius), and Pitasala is known by the epithets of Sarasa and Bijaka (Indian Kino tree, Pentaptera tomentosa). Vajravrksa,Mahavrksa, Sudha, Guda, and Sruk are the names of Snuhl (Uphorbia Neraifolia).

## \|\| 204.36 \|\|

*tulasīṃ surasāṃ vidyādupastheti ca kathyate \|*  
*kuṭherako 'pyarjunakaḥ parṇo saugandhiparṇikraḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. 6ala (Shoria Robusta) tree is known by the epithet of Yaksavrksa, while Anisa is called by the name of Tinisa (Indian Jarula tree-Dalbergia Oujeineisis). Upastha, and Surasa are the other names of Tulasi (Holy basil). The second variety of Tulasi is called Sid (Ocimum album). Another species of Tulasi is called Arjunaka, Pami, Saugandhaparnika and Kutheruka (Assimum Bajilicum).

## \|\| 204.37 \|\|

*nīlaśca sindhuvāraśca nirguṇḍīti sugandhikā \|*  
*jñeyā sugandhiparṇoti vāsantī kulajeti ca \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Nila, Nirgundl, Sugandhika, Sugandha- parini, Vasanti and Kulaja are the names of Sindhuvara (Vitex trifolium).

## \|\| 204.38 \|\|

*kālīyakaṃ pītakāṣṭhaṃ katakākhyaḥ punaḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*gāyatrīkhadiro jñeyastadbhedaḥ kandaro mataḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Pita Kastham and Katakaks rya are the names of Kaliyakam (Yellow Sandalwood); Khadira is called Gayatri (Acacia Catechu), while the white variety is called Kandara (Kadara according to others).

## \|\| 204.39-40 \|\|

*indī varaṃ kuvalayaṃ padmaṃ nīlotpalaṃ smṛtam \|*  
*saugandhikaṃ śatadalamabjaṃ kamalamucyate \|\| 39 \|\|*
