*ajavarṇo bhavedūrjo vājikarṇo 'śvakarṇakaḥ \|*  
*śleṣmāntakastathā śelurbahuvāraśca kathyate \|\| 40 \|\|*

39-40. Indivaram, Kuvalayam, Saugandhikam, 6atadalam, Kamalam and Avjam are the synonuymes of Padma (Nelumbium specio- sum), while the blue variety is called Nilot- palam (Nymphaea Stellats). Vajikama and Asvakama are the names of Sarja (Indian Saltree-Shoria Robusta), while its another variety is known by the epithets of Urja and Ajakarna (Beng: — Jhanji Shal). 6elu and Vahuvara are the synonymes of Slesmataka (Cordia myxa, narrow leaved Sepistun). Kulangana, and Mrgccha are the synonymes of Alambu§a.

## \|\| 204.41-42 \|\|

*sunandakaḥ kakudbhadraṃ chatrākī chatrasaṃjñakā \|*  
*kabarī kumbhako dhṛṣṭaḥ kṣudvidho dhanakṛttathā \|\| 41 \|\|*

*kṛṣṇārjakaḥ karālaśca kālamānaḥ prakīrtitaḥ \|*  
*prācī balā nadīkrāntā kākajaṅghātha vāyasī \|\| 42 \|\|*

41-42. Sunandaka, Kukud, Bhadram and ChatrakI are the names of Chatra (Andropogon citratus) Kabarl, Kumbhaka, Karila, Kamamana, and Dhanakrt are the synonyms of Krsnarjaka, Prac, Bala Nadi, Kranta and Vayasi are the names of Kaka-Jangha (Leelahirta).

## \|\| 204.43 \|\|

*jñeyā mūṣikaparṇo tu bhramantī cākhuparṇikā \|*  
*viṣamuṣṭirdrāvaṇañca keśamuṣṭirudāhṛtā \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. While Dravanti is known by the epithets of Akhukarnika and Musika-karna (croton Polyandrum Kesamusti and Visamusti are the names of Dravanam (Melia Azendarach).

## \|\| 204.44 \|\|

*kiṃlihīṃ kaṭukīṃ vidyādantakaścāmlavetasaḥ \|*  
*aśvatthā bahupatrā ca vijñeyā cāmalakyapi \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Kilihl is called Katuka (black Hellebore) while Amla-vetasa is called Dantaka (country SorrelAcido Zeyfolia). Asvattha and (Bhu) Amalaki are the names of Vahupatra (Phyllan- thus niruri?).

## \|\| 204.45 \|\|

*arūṣakraṃ patra śūkaṃ kṣīrī rājādanaṃ matam \|*  
*mahāpatraṃ dāḍimaṃ ca tameva karakaṃ vadet \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Aragukam, Partra^ukam and Kslri are the names of Rajadanam (Mimonsops Hexenbra). Dadimvam is called Mahapatram (pomegranate) which is also called Karaka.

## \|\| 204.46-47 \|\|

*masūrī vidalī śaṣpā kālindīti nirucyate \|*  
*kaṇṭakākhyā mahāśyāmā vṛkṣapādīti vakṣyate \|\| 46 \|\|*

*vidyā kuntī nikumbhā ca tribhaṅgī tripuṭī trivṛt \|*  
*saptalā yavatiktā ca carmā carmakaseti ca \|\| 47 \|\|*

46-47. Vidali, 6aspa Kalindl Masuri, Kantakaksya, Maha-6yaya, VrksapadI, Vidya KuntI, Nikumbha, Tribhangi and Triputi are the names of Trivrt (Impomea tarpethum). Saptala is called 6ankhini, Sukumari, Tiktaksi and Yavatikta (Kalmegh) and is also used to signify Carma, or Carmaksa (Origaum Vulgaris).

## \|\| 204.48-49 \|\|

*śaṅkhinī sukumārī ca tiktākṣī cākṣipīlukam \|*  
*gavākṣī cāmṛtā śvetā girikarṇo gavādinī \|\| 48 \|\|*

*kāmpillako 'tha raktāṅgo guṇḍā rocaniketi ca \|*  
*hemakṣīrī smṛtā pītā gaurī vai kāladugdhikā \|\| 49 \|\|*

48-49. Gavaksi, Amrita and GirikarnI are the names of Gavadani (Colocynth-Citrullus Colocynthus), while Raktanga, Gunda, and Rocanaka are the synonymkes of Kampillaka (Kamila Melloctus Phillipinesis). The yellow species is called Hemaksm (Gamboge thistle, while the black variety is called Kaladugdhika.

## \|\| 204.50-51 \|\|

*gāṅgerukī nāgabalā viśālā cendravāruṇī \|*  
*tārkṣyaṃ śailaṃ nīlavarṇamañjanañca rasāñjanam \|\| 50 \|\|*

*niryāso yaśca śālmalyāḥ sa mocarasasaṃjñakaḥ \|*  
*pratyakpuṣpī kharī jñeyā apāmārgo mayūrakaḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

50-51. Gangeruki is another name of Nagavala (Sida Spinosa), while Visali is a synonym of Indravaruni (colocynth) Rasanjanam (extract of Indian Barbary) is known by the epithets of Arjanam and Tarkasa-Shailam, while the extrect of 6alamali (Bombax Malabaricum) is called Moca-rasa. Pratyakpuspi is another name of Kara, while Mayurka is a synonyme of Apamarga (Achyranthis Aspera).

## \|\| 204.52 \|\|

*siṃhāsyavṛṣavāsākamāṭarūṣakamādiśet \|*  
*jīvako jīvaśākaśca karburañca śaṭīṃ viduḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. Vasaka (Adhatoda Vasaca) is also called by the epithets of Simhasya, Vrsa, and Ataruskam. Rvaka, JIva 6akha and Karcara are the names of SatT (Curcoma Gedoaria).

## \|\| 204.53 \|\|

*kaṭphalaṃ somavṛkṣaḥ syādagnigandhā sugandhikā \|*  
*śatāṅgaṃ śatapuṣpā ca miṃsirmadhurikāmatā \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Somavriksha (Somavalka?), Agnigandha, and Sugandhika are synonymous with Katphalam (Myrica Sapida), Satapuspa (Dillseed-Aurthum gravey is) is also known by the epithets of Katanga, Misi and and Madhu- rika.

## \|\| 204.54-55 \|\|

*jñeyaṃ puṣkaramūlañca puṣkaraṃ puṣkarāhvayam \|*  
*yāso 'tha dhanvayāsaśca duṣparśo 'tha durālabhā \|\| 54 \|\|*

*vākucī somarājī ca somavallīti kīrtitā \|*  
*mārkavaḥ keśarājaśca bhṛṅgarājo nigadyate \|\| 55 \|\|*

54-55. Puskaram and Puskarahvayam are but the diferent names of Puskaramulam (root of Alpotaxis auriculata). Tasa, Dhanvayasa and Dusparsa are the synonymes of Duralabha (Alhagimauronm Fogoina Arabica) VagujI and Somavalll are the names of SomarajI (Serratula Anthelmintica). Markava and Kesaraja are the synonymes of Bhrngaraja (Wedelia Calendu- lacea).

## \|\| 204.56-59 \|\|

*proktastveḍagajastajjñaiścakramardakasaṃjñakhaḥ \|*  
*suraṅgītagaraḥ snāyuḥ kalanāśā tu vāyasī \|\| 56 \|\|*

*mahākālaḥ smṛto belastaṇḍulīyo ghanastanaḥ \|*  
*ikṣvākustiktatumbī syāttiktālaburnigadyate \|\| 57 \|\|*

*dhāmārgavo 'tha koṣātakyatha yāminī \|*  
*vidyātkośatakībhedaṃ kṛtabhedanasaṃjñakā \|\| 58 \|\|*

*tathā jīmūtakākhyā ca khuḍḍāko devatāḍakaḥ \|*  
*gṛdhranakhī gṛdhranakhī hiṅgukākādanī matā \|\| 59 \|\|*

56-59. Edagaja is another name off Cakramarda (cassiatora). Sarngl, Tagara, Vayasi Vela, Tanduliya and Ghanastana are the names of Mahakala. TiktatumbI and Tiktalavu are synonymous with Iksaku (Bottle gourd, wild variety of Langaneri Vulgaris) Kosataki and Yaminy are but the different names of Dhamargava (Laffu Aegyptiaca), Vidyut, which is another species of Dhamargava is also called Krtabhedanam, Jimutaka, Khuddaka, and Devatadaka. Grdhradana is another name of Gidhranakhi, which is also called Kakadanl and Hingu (caparis Sepiaria).

## \|\| 204.60 \|\|

*aśvāriścaiva boddhavyaḥ karavīro 'śvamārakaḥ \|*  
*sindhuḥ saindhavasindhūtthamaṇimanthamudāhṛtam \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. ASvari and Asvamaraka are but the different names of Karavira (sweet scented OleanderNerrium odorum). Tarasi and Ku^aja are the names of Kapitthapatrl (Being Elvaluk) Sindhu, Saindhava, Sindhuttha and Mani- muntha are the synonymes of Rocksalt.

## \|\| 204.61 \|\|

*kṣāro yavāgrajaścaiva yavakṣāro 'bhidhīyate \|*  
*sarjikā sarjikākṣāro dvitīyaḥ parikīrtitaḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Usara, Yavagra and Yavaksara are the terms which denote a kind of impure carbonate of potash lit ashes of burnt barley straw); Sarjika and Sarjkaksara are the names of barilla. 6ikhi- kanthabham Chitrakam. Tuttham etc., are the% terms which denote nitrate of Copper. Kaslsam, Puspakasisam and Netra bhesajam (lit eye-cure) are the terms which signify greet Sulphate of iron.

## \|\| 204.62-63 \|\|

*kāśīśaṃ puṣpakāśīśaṃ vijñeyaṃ nettrabheṣajam \|*  
*dhātukāśīśakāśī ca saṃjñeyaṃ tacca kīrtitam \|\| 62 \|\|*

*saurāṣṭrī mṛttikākṣāraṃ kākṣī vai paṅkaparpaṭī \|*  
*vidyātsamākṣikaṃ dhātu tāpyaṃ tāpyutthasambhavam \|\| 63 \|\|*

62-63. Kaslsa and Dhatu-Kaslsa are also the different names of the foregoing substence. Tapyam and Tapyutha-sambhavam are synonymous with Maksika (iror pyrites).

## \|\| 204.64 \|\|

*śilā manaḥ śilā jñeyā nepālī kulaṭīti ca \|*  
*ālaṃ manastālakaṃ vā haritālaṃ vinirdiśet \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. Naipali, Kulafi and gild are the different nemes of Manah-sila (red sulphate of arsanic), while the terms Alan and Manastalakam signify Haritalam (tri-sulphide of arsenic) Gandha- pasana is but another name of Gandhaka (sulphar while the term Rasa is used of signify Parada (Mercury lit that which bears a person beyond death and disease).

## \|\| 204.65-66 \|\|

*gandhako gandhapāṣāṇo rasaḥ pārada ucyate \|*  
*tāmramaudumbaraṃ śulbaṃ vidyānmlecchamukhaṃ tathā \|\| 65 \|\|*

*adrisārastvayastīkṣṇaṃ lohakañcāpi kathyate \|*  
*mākṣikaṃ madhu ca kṣaudraṃ tacca puṣparasaṃ smṛtam \|\| 66 \|\|*

65-66. Audumbaram, Shulvam and Mleccha- mukham are the different names of Tamram copper), and the terms Adrsaram (lit. essence of rock; Ayas, and Tiksnam are used to denote iron (and steel. KaksI, Panka-parpali, and Mrtti Kaksaram are the names of Saurastra Mrttika. Maksikam, Ksaudram and Pusparasam are the synonymes of Madhu (honey).

## \|\| 204.67 \|\|

*jyeṣṭhantu sodakaṃ tatsyātkāñjikantu suvīrakam \|*  
*sītā sitopalā caiva matsyaṇḍīśarkarā smṛtā \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. Fermented barley-boilings are called Sauvirakam and Kanjikam. SIta, Sitopala, Matsand! are synonym of Sarkara (sugar).

## \|\| 204.68 \|\|

*tvagelāpatrakaistulyaistrisugandhi trijātakam \|*  
*nāgakeśarasaṃyuktaṃ taccaturjātamiṣyate \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. A compound of Cinnamon, Cardemon, and leaves of Lourus Cassia, taken in equal parts, is technically known as Trijatakam or Trisugandhi. This compound, with one part of Naga-KeSharam added to it, constitutes what is technically known as Catirkatam.

## \|\| 204.69 \|\|

*pippalī pippalīmūlaṃ cavyacitrakanāgaraiḥ \|*  
*kathitaṃ pañcakolañca kolakaṃ kolasaṃjñayā \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. A compound consisting of equal parts of Pipall, Pippalimulam, Cavya, Cutrakamulam and Nagar, and combindly weighing a Kolakam (Onetolla) is called Pancakolam. Bhutrilaga, MahaSali, and Nivara are the different species. Malika.

## \|\| 204.70 \|\|

*priyaṅguḥ kaṅgukā jñeyā koradūṣaśca kodravaḥ \|*  
*tripuṭaḥ puṭasaṃjñaśca kalāpo laṅgako mataḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. Priyangu is another name of Kanguka (Panicum stalicum), and Kordusa is called Kodra (Paspalum Scrobicluatum). Kalapa, Larigaka, and Puta are the names of Triputa (Lathyrus Sativus).

## \|\| 204.71 \|\|

*satīno vartulaścaiva veṇuścāpi prakīrtitaḥ \|*  
*picukaṃ pitalaṃ cākṣaṃ biḍālapadakaṃ tathā \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. Sauna, Vartula and Vena are the names of Satina (Pisum Sativum).

## \|\| 204.72 \|\|

*vidyātkarṣaṃ tathā cāpi suvarṇaṃ kavalagraham \|*  
*palārdhaṃ śuktimicchanti tathāṣṭaumāṣakāstviti \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. A Suvarmam of Kavalagraham is equal to one Karsa is weight. A Suktim is equal to a half Palam or eight Masakas in weight.

## \|\| 204.73 \|\|

*palaṃ bilvañca muṣṭiḥ syāddve pale prasṛtiṃ vadet \|*  
*añjaliṃ kuḍavañcaiva vidyātpalacatuṣṭayam \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. A Vilam, or Musti is equal to a Palam weight. Two Palas snake one Prasriti. Four Palas make one Anjali or Kudavam.

## \|\| 204.74-75 \|\|

*aṣṭamānaṃ palānyaṣṭau tacca mānamiti smṛtam \|*  
*caturbhiḥ kuḍavaiḥ prastha prasthāścatvāra āḍhakaḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

*kāśapātrañca saṃprokto droṇaścacaturāḍhake \|*  
*tulā palaśataṃ proktaṃ bhāgo viṃśatpalaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

74-75. Eight Palas make one Palam. Four Kudavas make one Prastha; four Prasthas make one Adakam or Kanspatrah Tour Adakas make one Drona. A hundred Palas make one Tula weight. Twenty Palas make one Bhara.

## \|\| 204.76 \|\|

*mānamevaṃ vidhaṃ proktaṃ prasthadravyeṣu paṇḍitaiḥ \|*  
*dravadravyeṣu coddiṣṭaṃ dviguṇaṃ parikīrtitam \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. The erudite ones have laid down these measures in respect of try weight, while in respect of fluid weight these measures should be taken as double.

## \|\| 204.77 \|\|

*bhadradāru devakāṣṭhaṃ dāru syāddevadārukam \|*  
*kuṣṭhamāmayamākhyātaṃ māṃsīñca naladaṃśanam \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. Valam is another name of Turaskakam, Daru is another name of Devadaru (Pinus Deodara). GranthI is another name of Sthauneyakam. Vasakam is also called Bhumikam trinam. Kustham is also called Amayam, and Nala-dansanam is but another name of Mansi.

## \|\| 204.78 \|\|

*śaṅkhaḥ śuktinakhaḥ śaṅkho vyāghro vyāghranakhaḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*puraṃ palaṅkaṣaṃ vidyānmahiṣākṣañca gugguluḥ \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. &ukti is also called 6uktinakha..nd Sharikha; Vyaghri is also called Vyaghra-nakha. Puram, Palanka^am and Mahlshaksya are but the different names of Guggulu (bdellium).

## \|\| 204.79 \|\|

*raso gandharaso bole sarjaḥ sarjaraso mataḥ \|*  
*priyaṅguḥ phalinī śyāmā gaurī kānteti cocyate \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. Rasa and Gandharasa are the different nemes of Volam (Myrrh), while Sarja is called Sarjarasa (resin), Kurdarakam is also called Kundam (Olibanum), and 6unistakam is also called Davam (Gomeopal Sandazack). Priyangu is also known by the epithets of Phalini, Syama and Gaurikanti.

## \|\| 204.80 \|\|

*karañjau naktamālaḥ syātpūtikaścirabilvakaḥ \|*  
*śigruḥ śobhāñjano nāma jñānamānaśca kīrtitaḥ \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. Artagala is also known by the epithets of Arta, Bhlsana and Vahukantaka. Sahcara and Vana are the synonymes of Saireyakah, (Balaria Crastata). Naktamala, Putika, and Cira-Vilvaka are the names of Karanja (Pongamia Glabra). Shobanjana, Jvala and Mansa are the different epithets of Sigru (Horse radish tree Morin- gaptery Gooperma).

## \|\| 204.81 \|\|

*jayā jayantī śaraṇī nirguṇḍī sindhuvārakaḥ \|*  
*moraṭā pīluparṇo ca tuṇḍī syāttuṇḍikerikā \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. Jaya, JayantI Sharanl. Nirgundl are the names of Sindhuvara. Morata is another name of Pippall-parnI, while Tundi is also called Tundikerika.

## \|\| 204.82 \|\|

*madano gālavo bodho ghoṭā ghoṭī ca kathyate \|*  
*caturaṅgula sampāko vyādhighātābhisaṃjñakaḥ \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. Galava, Vodha, Ghota and Ghotl are the different names of Madana tree (Randia Denmetorum). Sampaka is known by the names of Caturangula and Vyadhighataka (Kamila).

## \|\| 204.83 \|\|

*vidyādāragvadhaṃ rājavṛkṣaṃ raivatasaṃjñakam \|*  
*dantī kākendutiktā syātkaṇṭakī ca vikaṅkataḥ \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. Know that Aragvadham is also called Rajavrkta and Raivata (Cassia Fistula), Vastaka is Atitikta, KantakI is also called Vikankata (Flacourtia romontchi).

## \|\| 204.84-85 \|\|

*nimbo 'riṣṭaḥ samākhyātaḥ paṭolaṃ kolakaṃ viduḥ \|*  
*vayasthā ca viśalyā ca cchinnā chinnaruhā matā \|\| 84 \|\|*

*vaśā dantyamṛtā ceti guḍūcīnāmasaṃgrahaḥ \|*  
*kirātatiktakaścaiva bhūnimbaḥ kāṇḍatiktakaḥ \|\| 85 \|\|*

84-85. Nimba is also called Arista (Melio Azadirachta). Vayastha, ViSva, Chinna, Chinnaruha, Vatsadani and Amrta are the names of Gudud (Tinaspora Cordifolia). Kirata-tikta, and Bhunimba are synonymous with Kandatiktaka. (plant Agathotes Chiraytu).

## \|\| 204.86 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*nāmānyetāni ca hare vanyānāṃ bheṣajāṃ tathā \|*  
*ato vyākaraṇaṃ vakṣye kumāroktañca śaunaka \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. These are the names, of vegetable drugs that are obtained in the forest. Now I shall deal with Grammar, О баипака, as formerly narrated by Kumara.

## Chapter 205

## \|\| 205.1 \|\|

*kumāra uvāca \|*  
*atha vyākaraṇaṃ vakṣye kātyāyana samāsataḥ \|*  
*siddhaśabdavivekāya bālavyutpattihetave \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Kumara said: — О Katyayana, I shall briefly expound the rules of Grammar which will enable infants tai easily comprehend that subject and to understand the formation of word.

## \|\| 205.2-3 \|\|

*suptiṅantaṃ padaṃ khyātaṃ supaḥ sapta vibhaktayaḥ \|*  
*svaujasaḥ prathamā proktā sā prātipadikātmake \|\| 2 \|\|*

*sambodhane ca liṅgādāvukte karmaṇi kartari \|*  
*arthavatprātipadikaṃ dhātupratyayavarjitam \|\| 3 \|\|*

2-3. Terms are either Sup (substantive) or Tiri (verb). A Sup has seven cases. The forms of singular dual and plural inflexions of the subjective case are respectively called Su, Au, Jas. The subjective case-endings are added to the subject of a sentence, to the object in the passive voice, and are used in the case of address, in Pratipadikam, and in cases where the subjective sense is implied even in the absence of any verb (Lingartha). A term, that expresses a complete sense even in the absence of a verb or any caseinflexion, is called a Pratipadikam.

## \|\| 205.4-5 \|\|

*amauśaso dvitīyā syāttatkarma kriyate ca yat \|*  
*dvitīyā karmaṇi proktāntarāntareṇa saṃyute \|\| 4 \|\|*

*ṭābhyāṃbhisastṛtīyā syātkaraṇe kartarīritā \|*  
*yena kriyate karaṇaṃ tatkartā yaḥ karoti saḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. "Am," "Au," and "5ah" are respectively the singular, dual and plural inflexion-forms of the objective case (Dvitlya). That which is done by the subject of a sentence is called its object (Karma). Dvitiya case-endings are used in the objective case, and are added to terms in association with the terms "Antara and "Antarena" Та/' "Bhis" are respectively the singular, dual.and plural inflexionforms of the Trtlya (accusative cast). Trtiya inflexions are used in Karanam (accusative). The instrument of agency through which a subject pertorms an act is called its Karanam (lit. instrument), and he who performs an act is called its Karta (doer).

## \|\| 205.6 \|\|

*ṅebhyāṃbhyasaścaturtho syātsampradāne ca kārake \|*  
*yasmai ditsā dhārayate rocate sampradānakam \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. "Ne," "Bhyam," and "Bhyah" are respectively the singular dual and plural inflexional forms of Sampradanam (Dative case). Dative caseendings are added to persons to which something is intended to be given, or to which something is owed, or to whom something appears likeable or delectable.

## \|\| 205.7 \|\|

*pañcamī syānṅasibhyāṃbhyohyapādāne ca kārake \|*  
*yato 'paiti samādatte upādatte bhayaṃ yataḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. "Nangsl," "Bhyam" and "Bhyah" are respectively the singular, dual and plural inflexionforms of Apadanam (Ablative case). Ablative case endings are added to a term from which anything is meant to be fallen or dis- loged, or from which any fear is apprehended.

## \|\| 205.8 \|\|

*ṅasosāmaśca ṣaṣṭhī syātsvāmisambandhamukhyake \|*  
*ṅayoḥ supo vai saptamī syātsā cādhikaraṇe bhavet \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. "Nah," "Us," and "Am" are respectively the singluar, dual, and plural inflexion froms of the Sasthi (possessive case). Sasthi im plies possession, ownership relationship, or prominence of one among many.

## \|\| 205.9-10 \|\|

*ādhāraścādhikaraṇaṃ rakṣārthānāṃ prayogataḥ \|*  
*īpsitaṃ cānīpsitaṃ yattadapādānakaṃ smṛtam \|\| 9 \|\|*

*pañcamī paryupāṅyoge itararte 'nyadiṅmukhe \|*  
*enayoge dvitīyā syātkarmapravacanīyakaiḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. "Unga," "Usa," and "Sup" are respectively the singular, dual, and plural inflexion-froms of the Adhikaranam (locative case). Adhikaranam implies the location of a thing in another substance, and its inflexions are added to terms signifying that something is contained in them, or denoting agents under the protection of some body. Ablative caseendings are added to terms which signify objects that are either coveted or disliked, as well as to those used in combination with the prefixes Pari, Apa, and Am, or in connection with the terms Itara (other) and those which denote the names of the quarters of the heaven. The objective case endings are added to terms used in combing tion with "Ena." as well as to the objects of a verb.

## \|\| 205.11-12 \|\|

*vīpsetthambhāvacihne 'bhirbhāgenaiva paripratī \|*  
*anureṣu sahārthe ca hīne 'nūpaśca kathyate \|\| 11 \|\|*

*dvitīyā ca caturtho syācceṣṭāyāṃ gatikarmaṇi \|*  
*aprāṇe hi vibhaktī dbe manyakarmaṇyanādare \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12. Terms which are used in connection with the terms Saha (with), Hina (without) or are coupled with the prefixed "Anu," "Pari," "Prati" always have the objective case-endings. Likewise adverbs and terms denoting road are always used with the objective inflexions. Terms implying attempt at going or efforts of locomotion may either, have the objective or dative case-endings. The object of the verb "Mans," implying an act of light or disrespectful comparison, gets the dative inflexion, if it denotes an inanimate object; denoting an animate object, or a sentient creature, it retains its true objective inflexion.

## \|\| 205.13-14 \|\|

*namaḥ svastisvadhāsvāhālaṃvaṣaḍyoga īritā \|*  
*caturtho caiva tādarthye tumarthādbhāvavācinaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*tṛtīyā sahayoge syātkutsiteṅge viśeṣaṇe \|*  
*kāle bhāve saptamī syādetairyoge 'piṣaṣṭhyati \|\| 14 \|\|*

13-14. Terms used in combination with Namah (obeisance), "Svasti" (blessing- to), "Svadha Svaha" "Vassat" (obeisance) and Alam (capable) get the dative case endings. Used to denote a sense like " for that reason," or "for that purpose" they are likewise used in the dative case. Accusative case is used in combination with the term Saha (denoting accompaniment), as well as in respect of objects denoting the loss or defect of any bodily organ. Terms denoting the progress or course of time as well as the happening or contingency of an event are used in the locative case. Possessive case endings may be as well used in respect of the foregoing terms.

## \|\| 205.15-17 \|\|

*svāmīśvarādhipatibhiḥ sākṣidāyādaprasūtaiḥ \|*  
*nirdhāraṇe dve vibhakto ṣaṣṭhī hetuprayogake \|\| 15 \|\|*

*smṛtyarthakarmaṇi tathā karoteḥ pratiyatnake \|*  
*hiṃsārthānāṃ prayoge ca kṛti karmaṇi kartari \|\| 16 \|\|*

*na kartṛkarmaṇoḥ ṣaṣṭhī niṣṭhayoḥ prātipadike \|*  
*dvividhaṃ prātipadikaṃ nāma dhātustathaiva ca \|\| 17 \|\|*

15-17. Both possessive and locative case-endings may be added to terms coupled with "SvamI," Adhipali "Igavara" (lords or master), "Dayada" (heirs), and "Sutakas"), Either the locative or possessive case may be used where the predominence of one object amongst many (Nirdhara) is desired. Possessive case endings are added to terms used with "Hetu" (for that reason). Objects of the root Smr (to remember) always get the possessive inflexion. Similarly, subjects of verbs formed by Krt, as well as substantives used in connection with verbs denoting the import of killing or envying, get the possessive inflexion. Subjects do not get the possessive inflexion in connection with Nistha suffixes (such as Та. etc.).

## \|\| 205.18-19 \|\|

*bhūvāndibhyastiṅo laḥ syāllakārā daśa vai smṛtāḥ \|*  
*tiptasūjhi prathamo madhyaḥ sipthasthottamapūruṣaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*mibvasmastu parasmai hi padānāṃ cātmanepadam \|*  
*tātāñjha prathamo madhya sthāsāthāndhvamathottamaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

18-19. There are two kinds of Pratipadikam, such as the name (substantive) and Dhatu (root). A Dhatu or root may be declined in ten tenses or Dasa Lakaras. "Tip, Tas" "Anti" are the inflexions of third person singular, third person dual, and third person plural, in the present tense (Lat). Sip, Thas, Tha are respectively the forms of inflexion of the second person singular, dual and plural in the present tense; and "Mi" "Vas" and "Mas" are respectively the forms of inflexion of the first person singular, dual and plural in the present tens.

## \|\| 205.20-21 \|\|

*ādeśā iḍbahimahi dhātutotha ṇijādivat \|*  
*nāmni prayujyamāne 'pi prathamaḥ puruṣo bhavet \|\| 20 \|\|*

*madhyamo yuṣmadi prokta uttamaḥ puruṣo 'smadi \|*  
*bhūvādyā dhātavaḥ proktāḥ sanādyantāstathā tataḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

20-21. These forms are used4- only, in the Parasmai-Pada from. In the AtmanepadI from they are respectively. Те, Ate, Ante; Se, Athe, Dhve; and A, Vahe, and Mahe. "I" and its plural denote first person, "You" and its plural indicate second person, names other than these are third person, Bhu (to be) etc., are called Dhatus.

## \|\| 205.22-23 \|\|

*laḍīrito vartamāne smenātīte ca dhātutaḥ \|*  
*bhūte 'nadyatane laṅvā loḍādyāśiṣi dhātutaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*vidhyādāvevānumato loḍvācyo mantraṇe bhavet \|*  
*nimantraṇādhīṣṭasaṃpraśre prārthaneṣu tathāśiṣi \|\| 23 \|\|*

22-23. Lat means the present tense. A verb having the form of present tense signifies the import of a past tense if used in combination with "Sma" Lan is past perfect tense. The tense Lih is used in conferring blessings or making benediction. In cases of direction, permission, advice, prayer, invitation, request, benediction and asking of well being, Lot is the tense in which a verb is generally used. Lit signifies the past tense, and is used to denote events which have happened in the absence of -the speaker (lit., not under the eyes of the speaker, Paroksa). Lun is the name of the tense which is used to denote an event in the past which did not occur at the time of speaking. Ljt indicates simple future.

## \|\| 205.24-26 \|\|

*liṅatīte parokṣe syālliḍ bhūte ḷḍ bhaviṣyati \|*  
*syādanadyatane tadvadbhaviṣyati tu dhātutaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*dātorḷṅ kriyātipattau liṅarthe leṭ prakīrtitaḥ \|*  
*kṛtastriṣvapi vartante bhāve karmaṇi kartari \|\| 25 \|\|*

*sadṛśāstavyatā ṇyadyadanīyāśca tṛjādayaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

24-26. Lut is used to denote a future event which will take place in the presence of the speaker. In case in which the occurrance of an ovent or the performance of an act is being completed, the tense Lrn is used. Sometimes the past tense (Lit) is used in the place of Lot and vice versa The Lrt affixes may be added to a root in either of the three forms or voices, such as the active, passive and neuter. Trn, Ghang, Aniya, Shatri, etc., are the affixes which are usually affixed to the roots.

## Chapter 206

## \|\| 206.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*siddhodāharaṇaṃ vakṣye saṃhitādipuraḥ saram \|*  
*viprāḥ svasāgatā vīdaṃ suttamaṃ syātpitṝṣabhaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Suta said: — Now I shall enumerate the illustrations of Sandhis (unions Of words) etc., as are found to occur in the Samhitas. Vipra and Agram make Vipragram, "Sa" and Agata make Sagata. "Vi" combined with "Idam" makes Vidam, "Su" and "Uttamam" Suttamam.

## \|\| 206.2 \|\|

*ḷkāro viśrutā sevaṃ lāṅgalīṣā manīpayā \|*  
*gaṅgodakaṃ tavalkāra ṛṇārṇaṃ prārṇamityapi \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Pitr and Rsabha make Pitrgabha, Langala and Isa make Langllsa, Mana and Pasya make "Masaya" "Gangs" and "Udakam" make "Gangdakam." To and Lakara make Tavalkara. Rna and Rnam make Rnamam, Prt and Arnam make Prarnam.

## \|\| 206.3 \|\|

*śītārtaśca tavalkāraḥ saindrī saukāra ityapi \|*  
*vadhvāsanañca pitrartho lanubandho naye jayet \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Shlta and Arta make 6itara. Tau and likara make Tavalkara. Sah and Indri make Sanidrl, Sa and Okara make Saukara. Iti and Api make Atyapi. Vadhu and Asanam make Vadhvaanam. Pitr and Artha make Pittartha, Li and Anabandha make Lanubandha. Naye and Jayet make Nayejayet.

## \|\| 206.4 \|\|

*nāyako lavaṇaṃ gāvasta ete na ta īśvarāḥ \|*  
*devīgṛhamatho atra a avehi paṭū imau \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Lu and Anam make Lavanam. Gau and Ava make Gava. The united with ISvara та Та fsvara. Atham and Atra make Atho Atro. Sat united with Iman make Sat Iman.

## \|\| 206.5 \|\|

*amī aśvāḥ ṣaḍasyeti tanna vāk ṣaḍdalāni ca \|*  
*taccarettallu nātīti tajjalaṃ tacchmaśānakam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Amih and Asvah make Ami Ashva, Sat and Agya make SadaShya, Tat and Navak make Tannavak. Tat and Cart make Taccaret. Tat and Lunati make Tallunati. Tat and Jalam make Tajjalam. Tat and Shmasanakam make Tat Shmasanakam.

## \|\| 206.6 \|\|

*sugannatra pacannatra bhavāṃśchādayatīti ca \|*  
*bhavājjhanatkaraścaiva bhavāṃstarati saṃsmṛtam \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Sugan and Atra make Sugannatra: Paean and Atra make Pacannatra. Bhavan and Cadayati Bhavan and Jhanatkar make Bhavan Thanathara. Bhavan and Tarati make Bhavamstarati. Sam and Smrtam combinedly make Samsoritam.

## \|\| 206.7 \|\|

*bhavāṃllikhati tāñcakre bhavāñśete 'pyanīdṛśaḥ \|*  
*bhavāṇḍīnaṃ tvantarasi tvaṅkaroṣi sadārcanam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Bhavan and Lakhati unitedly make Bhavamllikhati. Tan and Shete unitedly make Tamscchete. Bhavan, 6ete Api, Ami and Idoam combinedly make Bhavang Shete\[ua,Idrsam. Tvam and Karosi combinedly make Tvam- karosi.

## \|\| 206.8-10 \|\|

*kaścaretkaṣṭakāreṇa ka kuryātka phale sthitaḥ \|*  
*kaḥśete caiva kaḥṣaṇḍaḥ kasko yāti ca gauravam \|\| 8 \|\|*

*ka ihātra ka evāhurdevā āhuśca bho vraja \|*  
*svabhūrviṣṇurvrajati ca gīṣpatiścaiva dhūrpatiḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*asmāneṣa vrajetsasyādṛksāma sa ca gacchati \|*  
*kuṭīcchāyā tathā chāyā sandhayo 'nye tathedṛśāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

8-10. Tvan and TarasI make Tvanta rasl, Sat and Arohanam make Sadar Ccanam, Kah and Ihatra make Ka Matra. There are six forms of Samasas, such as (I) the Karma dharaya etc., of which the term Sadblja froms an illustrtuion. The term Trivedi furnishes the example of Dvigu Samasa. Tatkrtasca, Tadarthascha, and Vrkabhiti, etc., are the illustrations of Tatpurusa Samasa, whereas the terms Tattvajna, Jnana-dasksa, etc., illustrate the forms of Vahubrlhi Samasa.

## \|\| 206.11-13 \|\|

*samāsāḥ ṣaṭ samākhyātāḥ sa dvijaḥ karmadhārayaḥ \|*  
*dvigustrivedī grāmaśca ayaṃ tatpuruṣaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*tatkṛtaśca tadarthaśca vṛkabhītiśca yaddhanam \|*  
*jñānadakṣeṇa tattvajño bahuvrīhirathāvyayī \|\| 12 \|\|*

*bhāvo 'dhistri yathoktaṃ tu dvandvo devarṣimānavāḥ \|*  
*taddhitāḥ pāṇḍavaḥ śaivo brāhayaṃ ca brahmatādayaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

11-13. Examples of the Avyayibhava Samasa always commence with the interjectional prefixes of Adhi, etc., while the terms such as Devarsi Manava, etc., furnish the instances of the Dvanda Samasa. The terms such as Pandavas, Saiva, Brahma, and Brahmata are the illustrations of the applied Taddhita.

## \|\| 206.14 \|\|

*devāgnisakhipatyaṃśukroṣṭusvāyambhuvaḥ pitā \|*  
*nā praśastāścarā gaurglaurabajantāśca puṃsyapi \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. The terms Devagni, Sakhi, Pati, Am6u, Krastu, Svayambhu, Pita (Pitrl), Nri (Na), Pr^asta (Pra^astr) Ra, Gan, and Glau, though included within the group of Adajanta words belong to the masculine gender.

## \|\| 206.15-16 \|\|

*halantaścāśvayukkṣmābhuṅmarutkravyānmṛgāvidhaḥ \|*  
*ātmā rājā yuvā panthāḥ pūṣabrahmahaṇau halī \|\| 15 \|\|*

*viḍve dhā uśanānaḍvānmadhuliṭ kāṣṭhataṭ tathā \|*  
*banavāryasthivastūni jagatsāmāhanī tathā \|\| 16 \|\|*

15-16. Similarly, the group of Halanta words consisting of the terms Agra, Juk, Ksabhuk, Kravyad, Mrgabedha, Atman, Rajan, Yuvan, Pathin, Pusan, and Brahmahan, 3agin, Vedhas, Usanas, Anudvan, Madhulit and Kasthatat belongs to the masculine gender. The terms Vanam (wood), Vari (water), Asthi bone) Vastu Cthing), Jagat (universe), Saman (the verses of that Veda), Ahan (day), Karma, (act) Sarpis (clarified butter) Bapus (body) and Tejas (energy) belong to the neuter gender.

## \|\| 206.17-20 \|\|

*karmasarpirvapusteja ajjhalantā napuṃsake \|*  
*jāyā jarā nadī lakṣmīḥ śrīstrībhūmirvadhūrapi \|\| 17 \|\|*

*bhrūḥ punarbhūstathā dhenuḥ svasā mātā ca nau striyaḥ \|*  
*vāksragdiṅmutkrudhaḥ prāyo yuvatiḥ kukubhastathā \|\| 18 \|\|*

*dyodivau prāvṛṣaścaiva sumāna uṣṇigastriyām \|*  
*guṇadravyakriyāyogātstrīliṅgāṃśca vadāmi te \|\| 19 \|\|*

*śuklakīlālapāścaiva śuciśca grāmaṇīḥ sudhīḥ \|*  
*paṭuḥ kamalabhūḥ kartā sumato bahavaḥ sunauḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

17-20. The terms Jaya (wife), Jara (old age), Nidi (river), Laksmi (goddess of fortune), Shrl (beauty), Stri (woman) Bhtiim (land), Vadhu (bride), Bhru (eye-brows), Punarbhu (a remarried widow), Dhenu (cow), Svasa (sister), Mata (mother) Nan (boat), Bak (speech), Srag (garland of flowers), Dik (quarter of the heaven), Krudh (anger), Yuvati (maiden) Kukubh, (quarters of the skies), Dyau (effulgence), Dhrti (comprehension), Pravis (rainy reason), Usnik (metre) and Sumanas (flowers) belong to the feminine gender. Now I shall narrate to you the terms which are respectively included within the masculine, feminine and neuter groups according to the nature of their imports, or the nature of the act they signify. Sukla (white), Kilala, 6uci (pure) Gramani (the master of a village), Sudhi (intelligent one) Vahu (arms), Kamalabhu (the lotus-sprung deity), Karta (master or doer), Vahu (many).

## \|\| 206.21-27 \|\|

*satyā nāgnyastathā puṃso hyabhakṣayata dīrghapāt \|*  
*sarvaviśvobha ye cobhau ekonyānyatarāṇi ca \|\| 21 \|\|*

*ḍataro ḍatamo nemastvaḥ samo 'tha simetarau \|*  
*pūrvaścaivādharaścaiva dakṣiṇaścottarāvarau \|\| 22 \|\|*

*paraścāntaramapyetadyattyatkimadasastvidam \|*  
*yuṣmadasmattatprathamacaramālpatayārdhakāḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

*tathā katipayo dvau cetyevaṃ sarvādayastathā \|*  
*śṛṇotyādyā juhotiśca jahātiśca dadhātyapi \|\| 24 \|\|*

*dīpyatiḥ stūyatiścaiva puttrīyati dhanīyati \|*  
*truṭyati mriyate caiva cicīṣati ninīṣati \|\| 25 \|\|*

*sarve tiṣṭhanti sarvasmai sarvasmātsarvanto gataḥ \|*  
*sarveṣāṃ caiva sarvasminnevaṃ viśvādayastathā \|\| 26 \|\|*

*pūrve pūrvāśca pūrvasmātpūrvasminpūrva īritaḥ \|*  
*sūta uvāca \|*  
*suptiṅantuṃ siddharūpaṃ nāmamātreṇa darśitam \|*  
*kātyāyanaḥ kumārāttu śrutvā vistaramabravīt \|\| 27 \|\|*

21-27. Satya (truth), Madhutaksa and Dsrgha-pat (belong to the masculine gender) The terms Sarva (all) Viva (all), Ubha (both), Anya (other), Anyatara (other than that) are terms that are used both in the masculine and feminine genders. Paurva, Apara, Uttara, Daksina Apara, Antara, Tad, Yad, Idam, Asmad and Yusmad are the terms that are used in all the genders.

## Chapter 207

## \|\| 207.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*vāsudevaṃ guruṃ natvā gaṇaṃ śambhuṃ sarasvatīm \|*  
*mātrāvarṇaprabhedena cchando vakṣye 'lpabuddhaye \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Suta said: — With an obeisance to Vasudeva, the preceptor Ganesa, give and Sarasvatl I shall tell the ignorant student about the metres which are classified according to matras or varnas.

## \|\| 207.2 \|\|

*sarvādimadhyāntagalau mnau bhyau jrau stau trikā gaṇāḥ \|*  
*āryā catuṣkalādyantasarvamadhye caturgaṇāḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. According to the position of Guru and Laghu in the beginning, in the middle or in the end;there are eight Ganas namely, Ma-gana, Nagana, Bhagana Yagana, Ja-ganal, Ra-gana, and Ta-gana.

## \|\| 207.3 \|\|

*vyañjanānto visargāntau dīrgho yuktaparo guruḥ \|*  
*sānusvāraśca pādānto vā ityukto dvimātrakaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. A vowel is Guru when it is followed by a consonant, Visarga, or a conjunct. A DIrgha vowel is always Guru. A vowel which is followed by Anusvara or which comes in the and is also Guru. It is of two Matras.

## \|\| 207.4 \|\|

*yadā nāpi kramaṃ yoge laghutāpi kvacidguroḥ \|*  
*ślokacāryādisaṃjñā syādyatirvicchedasaṃjñikā \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. When the order of Laghu and Guru varies, it is called 6loka. When there is pause, it is called Yati.

## \|\| 207.5 \|\|

*jñeyaḥ pādaśca turyāṃśo yuk samaṃ viṣamantvayuk \|*  
*samamardhasamaṃ vṛttaṃ viṣamañca tṛtīyakam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. A quarter is called a Pada. When the quarters are equal, it is caled Sama. When the -quarters are unequal, it is called Visama. Hence it metres are of three types — Sama, Ardha — same, and Visama.

## Chapter 208

## \|\| 208.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*āryālakṣma tvaṣṭa gaṇāḥ sadā jo viṣame na hi \|*  
*ṣaṣṭhe jo nlau vāpi bhavet padaṃ ṣaṣṭhe dvitīyalāt \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Suta said: — Arya is of eight Ganas out of which the odds should not have Ja-gana. The sixth one mate be Ja-gana or Na-gana after the second Laghu.

## \|\| 208.2 \|\|

*āditaḥ saptame hrasvā dvitīyārdhe śare tataḥ \|*  
*trigaṇāṅghriśca pathyā syādvipulā vahnilaṅghanāt \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. The seventh Gana from the beginning consists of Laghu. In the second half of Arya, the foot ends with the fifth Gana, When the foot ends with the first three Ganas in each half, it is called Pa thy a. When the foot ends after the first three Ganas in each half, it is called Vipula.

## \|\| 208.3 \|\|

*gmadhye dvituryau jau capalā mukhapūrvādicāpalā \|*  
*dvitīyārdhe sajaghanā āryājāteśca lakṣaṇam \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. When the second and the fourth ones are Ja-ganas flanked by two Gurus, it is called Capala. When the first half is like Capala and the second half like Arya or Pathya or Vipula, it is called Mukha-Capala. When the first half is like Arya and the second half like Capala, it is called Sajaghana.

## \|\| 208.4 \|\|

*āryā prathamārdhalakṣma gītiḥ syācceddaladvaye \|*  
*upagītirdvitīyārdhādudgītirvyatyayādbhavet \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. When the first half and the second half both are like the first half of Arya, it is called Giti. When the first half and the second half both are like the second half of Arya, it is called Upagiti. When the second half of Arya, it is called Upagiti. When the first half is like the second half of Arya and the second half is like the first half of Arya, it is called Udglti.

## \|\| 208.5 \|\|

*āryāgītiścāntagururgotijāteśca lakṣaṇam \|*  
*ṣaṭ kalā viṣame cetsyuḥ same 'ṣṭau na nirantarāḥ \|*  
*samā parāśritā na syādvaitālīye ralau guruḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. When one more Guru is added after the first half of Arya it is called Aryaglti. When there are six Matras in the odds and eight Matras in the evervfeet and after each feet there is Ragana, Laghu and Guru, it is called Vaitaliya.

## \|\| 208.6 \|\|

*anter yau pūrvavadidamaupacchandasikaṃ matam \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. When after each feet of Vaitaliya, there is Ragana and Yagana, it is called Aupa- chandasika.

## \|\| 208.7 \|\|

*bhādgau syādāpātalikā jñeyātho dakṣiṇāntikā \|*  
*parāśrito dvitīyo laḥ pādeṣu nikhileṣvapi \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. When Bha-gana is followed by two Gurus, it is called Apatalika. When the second Matra is dependent and there is Laghu in all the feet, it is called Daksinantika.

## \|\| 208.8 \|\|

*udīcyavṛttirasame prācyavṛttistu yugmake \|*  
*sapañcamaścaturthāṃśe yugapattau pravṛttakam \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Whenthe secodn is dependent is the odd feet, it is called Udlcyavrtti. When the fourth and the fifth Matras are dependent in the even feet, it is called Pracyavrtti. When both the characteristics are there, it is called Pravrttka.

## \|\| 208.9 \|\|

*udīcyādyaṅghrisaṃyogādyugmapādaikapādikā \|*  
*cāruhāsinyayugmāṅghrau vaitālīyasya saṃgrahaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. When all the feet are even like the even feet or Pravrttaka it is called Ekapadika. When all the feet are like the odd feet of Pravrttaka, it is called Caruhasinl. The aforesaid metres one under the category of Vaitaliya.

## \|\| 208.10 \|\|

*vaktraṃ nādyānnasau syātāṃ caturthādyagaṇo bhavet \|*  
*pathyāvaktraṃ jena same viparītādiranyathā \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. When-N-gana and Sa-gana do not come after the first syllable, and Ya-gana comes after the fourth syllable, it is called Vaktra. When there is Ja-gana after the fourth syllable in the even feet,it is called, Pathya-vaktra. If it is in the odd feet, it is called Viparita-pathya-vaktra.

## \|\| 208.11 \|\|

*usame naśca capalā vipulā laghusaptamā \|*  
*nikhile vā saitavasya mrau ntau cābdhestatpūrvakau \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. When there is Na-gana after the fourth syllabe in the off feet, it is called Capala-vaktra. When the seventh syallable is Laghu in the odd feet, it is called Vipula. In the opinion of Saitava, it is so in all the feet. If there is Ma-gana after the fourth syllable it is called Ma-vipula; if Ragana, Ra-vipula; if Na-gana; Na-vipula and if Ta-gana, Ta-vipula.

## \|\| 208.12-13 \|\|

*ṣoḍaśalo 'caladhṛtirmātrāsamakamucyate \|\| 12 \|\|*

*navamalastathā go 'ntyaḥ jo nlauvāthāmbudheryathā \|*  
*viślokaḥ syāttaccatuṣkadviguṇādvānavāsikā \|\| 13 \|\|*

12-13. When there are sixteen Laghus is each feet, it is called Acala-dhrti. When the ninth syllable is Laghu and thelast one Guru, it is called Matra-sama. If there is Ja-gana or Na-gana with Laghu after the fourth Matra, it is called Vilsok. When there are four Laghus in feet, it is called Vanavasika.

## \|\| 208.14 \|\|

*bāṇāṣṭanavakeṣu syāllaścitrā ṣoḍaśātmikā \|*  
*samamātrāsamādiṣṭaṃ padākulakamīritam \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. When the fifth, the eight and the ninth Matra in each foot is Laghu, it is called Citra of sixteen Matras. A mixture of the metres of even Matras is called Padakulaka.

## \|\| 208.15 \|\|

*vṛttamātrā vinā varṇairlā varṇā gurubhirvinā \|*  
*guruvo lairdale nityaṃ pramāṇamiti niścitam \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. When the number of Varnas in deducted from the total number of Matras in the metre we get the number of Gurus. When the number of Gurus is deducted from total number of Matras in the metre, we get the number of Laghus. When the number of the Laghus is deducted from the total number of Matras in the metre and the resultant is divided by two, we get the number of Gurus.

## \|\| 208.16 \|\|

*aṣṭāviṃśātilā gantā prathamārdhe dvitīyake \|*  
*triṃśadasyāṃ śikhā gantā khañjātadvyatyayādbhavet \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. When there are twenty eight Laghus in the first half and thirty Laghus in the second half, it is called 6ikha. The reverse of this is Khanja.

## \|\| 208.17 \|\|

*ṣoḍaśānaṅgakrīḍā gā dvātriṃśaccarame ca lāḥ \|*  
*saptaviṃśātilā gantā dalayo rucirā dvayoḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. When there are sixteen Gurus in the first half mid thirty-two Laghus in the second half, it is called Ananga-krlda. When there are twenty- seven Laghus in both the halves, it is called Rucira.

## \|\| 208.18 \|\|

*mātrāvṛttāni coktāni varṇavṛttāni vacmi vai \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Thus I have told about the metres based on Matras. Now I shall tell you about those based Varnas.

## Chapter 209

## \|\| 209.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*śrīrukthā gena sā jñeyā utyukthā strī gurudvayam \|*  
*mo nārī ro mṛgī madhyā magau kanyā pratiṣṭhayā \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Suta said: — When there is one Guru in each foot, it is Shri Uktha. When there are two Gurus in each foot, it is called Stri-Atyuktha. The metre which the Ma-gana in each foot is called Nan; which has Ra-gana likewise is Mrgl-Maghyl. When Magana is followed by a Guru, it is called Kanya-pratistha.

## \|\| 209.2 \|\|

*bho gau paṅktiḥ suprātiṣṭhā tanumadhyā tayau smṛtā \|*  
*nayābhyāṃ bālalalitā gāyatrīcchanda eva hi \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. When the same is followed by two Gurus, it is called Pankti-Supratistha. When there is one Tagana and one Ya-gana in each foot, it is called Tanumadhyfi. When there is one Na-gana and one Yagana, it is called Balalalita-Gayatri.

## \|\| 209.3 \|\|

*masagairmadalekhā syāduṣṇikchandaḥ smṛtaṃ budhaiḥ \|*  
*bhau gau citrapadā khyātā vidyunmālā mamau gagau \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. In Madalekha, there is Ma-gang and Sa-gana followed by Guru- Usnik. In Citrapada two Bhaganas are followed by two Gurus. In Vidyumala, two Ma-ganas are followed by two Gurus.

## \|\| 209.4 \|\|

*māṇavakaṃ bhāttalagā mnau gau haṃsarutaṃ smṛtam \|*  
*samānikā rajagalā jaralā gaḥ pramāṇikā \|*  
*ābhyāmanyadvitānaṃ syādanuṣṭupchanda īritam \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. In Manavaka, are Bha-gana, Ta-gana, Laghu and Guru. In Hamsaruta, there are Ma-gana, Na-gana and two Gurus. In Samamka there are Ra-gana Ja-gana, Guru and Laghu. In Pramanika, there are Ja-gana, Ra-gana, Laghu and Guru. Vitana is dissimilar to these two. So these are the Anustup-metres.

## \|\| 209.5 \|\|

*ranasaiḥ syāddhalamukhī nau maḥ śiśubhṛtā bhavet \|*  
*bṛhatīchanda ityuktaṃ smau jagau sa virājitam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Halamukhi has Ra-gana. Na-gana and Sagana. 6isubhrta has two Na-ganas and one Magana-Brhati. Virajita has Sa-gana Ma-gana, Jagana arid Guru.

## \|\| 209.6 \|\|

*paṇavaṃ syānmanayagairmayūrasāriṇī bhavet \|*  
*rajābhyāñca ragābhyāñca rukmavatī bhamau sagau \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Panava has Ma-na-ya-ganas and one Guru, MayurasarinI has ra -ja-ra-ja-ra-ganas and one guru. Rukmavatl has Bha-ma-sa-ganas and one Guru.

## \|\| 209.7 \|\|

*mattā mabhasagairyuktā narajā go manoramā \|*  
*paṅkticchandaḥ samākhyātaṃ jasatā gāvupasthitam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Matte has Ma-bha-sa-galas and Guru, Manorama has na-ra-ja-ganas and Guru. Upasthita has Ja-gana, Sagana and Ta-gana followed by a Guru. Pankti has been told.

## \|\| 209.8 \|\|

*tau jo gāvindravajrā syājjatajgā gupapūrvikā \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Indravajra has two Ta-ganas, Ja-gana, and two Gurus. Upendravajra has Ja-ta-ja-ganas and two Gurus.

## \|\| 209.9 \|\|

*upajātayo 'nyādyantāḥ sumukhī najajā lagau \|*  
*bhabhabhā gau dodhakaṃ syācchālinī matatā gagau \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Upajati begins or ends with any one of the above two metres (i.e. it is a mixture of Indravajra and Upendravajra). SumukhI has Na-ja -ja-ganas and Laghu and Guru. Dodhaka has three Bhaganas and two Gurus, Shalini had Ma-ja-to gangs and two Gurus.

## \|\| 209.10 \|\|

*abdhilokaiśca vicchedo vātorṃmo mamatā gagau \|*  
*śrīrbhatau nanagāḥ proktā pañcabhiḥ ṣaḍūbhireva ca \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Vatormi has ma-bha-ta-gangs and two Gurus and Yati is after the fourth and the seventh syllables. Shri has bha-ta-na-ganas and two Gurus with yati on the fifth and the sixth syllables.

## \|\| 209.11 \|\|

*maganā no go bhramaravilāsitamudāhṛtam \|*  
*rathoddhatār nau ralagāḥ svāgatā ranabhā gagau \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Bhramara-vilasita has ma-bha-na-ganasand Laghuguru. Rathoddhata has ra-na-ra-ganas and Laghu-guru. Svagata has ra-na-bha-ganas and five Gurus.

## \|\| 209.12 \|\|

*vṛttā nanau sagau gaḥ syānnau ralau gaḥ samadrikā \|*  
*rajarā lgau śyenikā syājjasatā gau śikhaṇḍitam \|*  
*triṣṭupchandaḥ samākhyātaṃ piṅgalena mahātmanā \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Vrtta has na-an-sa-ganas and two Gurus. Smadrika (Bhadrika) has na-na-ganas and Laghuguru. 6yenika has raja-ra-gangs and Laghuguru. 6ikhandita has ja-sa-ta-ganas and two Gurus. Thus Tristup-metra had been stated by Mahatma Pihgala.

## \|\| 209.13-14 \|\|

*ranau bhasau candravartma vaṃśasthaṃ syājjatau jarau \|*  
*tato jarāvindravaṃśā vedasaistoṭakaṃ smṛtam \|*  
*nbhau bhrau drutavilambitaṃ puṭaśca syānnanau mayau \|\| 13 \|\|*

*vasuvedaiśca viratirmuditavadanā tviyam \|*  
*nanararaiḥ samākhyātā nayanā yastathā bhavet \|\| 14 \|\|*

13-14. Candravartma has ra-na-bha-sa-ganas. Vamsastha has ja-ta -ja-ra-ganas. Indravamsa has tata-ja-gangs. Totaka has four Sa-ganas. Drutavilambita had na-bha-bha-ra-ganas. Puta has na-na-ma-ya-ganas with yati after the eighth and fourth syllables. Mudita Vadana has na-na-ra raganas. Kusuma-vicitra has na-ya-na- ganas.

## \|\| 209.15 \|\|

*sā tu kusumavicitrā jaloddhatagatī rasaiḥ \|*  
*jasau jasau ca pādeṣu catūraiḥ stragviṇī matā \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Jaloddhatagati has ja-sa-ja-sa-ganas (with Yati after every six syllable). Sragvini has fourra-ganas.

## \|\| 209.16 \|\|

*bhujaṅgaprayātaṃ vṛttaṃ catubhiryaiḥ prakīrtitam \|*  
*prayaṃvadā nabhajraiśca maṇimālā tayau tayau \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. Bhujarigaprayata has four ya-ganas. Priyamvada has na-bha-ja-ra-ganas. Manimala taya-ta-ganas.

## \|\| 209.17 \|\|

*guhavaktraiśca sannidrā lalitā syāttabhau jarau \|*  
*pramitākṣarā sajasasairujjvalā tu nanau bharau \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Lalita has ta-bha-ja-ganas. Pramitaksara has ssa-ja-sa-ganas. Ujjvala has na-na-bha-raganas.

## \|\| 209.18 \|\|

*mamau yayau vaiśvadevī pañcāśvaiśca yatirbhavet \|*  
*mabhau samau jaladharamālābdhyantyairyatibhavet \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. VaisvadevI has ma-ma-ya-ya-gapas with yati on fifth and seventh varnas. Jaladharamala has mabha-sa-ma-ganas with Yati on the fourth and eighth varnas.

## \|\| 209.19 \|\|

*nau tatau gaḥ kṣamāvṛttaṃ turagaiśca rasairyatiḥ \|*  
*praharṣiṇī manau jrau gā vahnibhirdaśabhiryatiḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Ksama has ma-ma-ya-ya-gangs and Guru with yati onon the seventh and sixth varnas. Prahars ini has ma-na -ja-ra-ganas and guru with yati on the third and tenth varnas.

## \|\| 209.20 \|\|

*jabhau sajau go rucirā caturbhiśca grahairyatiḥ \|*  
*mattamayūraṃ matayāḥ sagau devagrahairyatiḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Rucira has ja-bha-sa -ja-ganas and guru with yati on the fourth and ninth varnas. matta- mayura has ma-ta-ya-sa-gangs and Guru with Yati on the fourth and ninth varnas.

## \|\| 209.21 \|\|

*mañjubhāṣiṇī sajsā jgau sunandinī sajasā magau \|*  
*nanau tatau candrikā gaḥ saptabhiśca rasairyatiḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Manjubhasini has sa-ja-sa-sa-ganas and Guru. Sunandini has sa-ja-sa-ma-ganas and Guru. Candrika has na-na-ta-ta-ganas and Guru with with Yati on the seventh and sixth varnas.

## \|\| 209.22 \|\|

*asambādhā matanasā gagau bāṇagrahairyatiḥ \|*  
*nanarāḥ so ladhuguruḥ svaraiḥ proktāparājitā \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Asambadha has ma-ta-na-sa gangs and two gurus with yati on the fifth and ninth varnas. Aparajita has na-na-ra-sa-ganas and Laghuguru.

## \|\| 209.23 \|\|

*nanau bhanau praharaṇakalikeyaṃ lagau tathā \|*  
*vasantatilakā siṃhonnatā tabhjā jagau guruḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Praharana-kalika has na-nabha-na-ganas and laghu-guru. Vasanta-tilaka (Simhonnata) has ta bha -ja-ja-ganas and two Gurus.

## \|\| 209.24 \|\|

*bhajau sanau gagāvinduvadanātha sukeśaram \|*  
*naranā ralagāḥ pāde śarkarī pratipāditā \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Indu-vadana has bha -ja-sa-na-ganas and two Gurus, Sukesara has na-ra-na-ra-ganas and Laghu-guru. Thus Sarkari (Sakvari?) has been described.

## \|\| 209.25 \|\|

*caturdaśalaghuḥ syācca śreṣṭhā śaśikalā sagā \|*  
*rasagrahayatiḥ sraksrā vasuśailayatistathā \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Sasikala has fourteen Laghus and one Guru. If Yati is on sixth and ninth varnas, it is called Srak. If Yati is on the eighth and seventh varnas. it is called Mani-guna-nikara.

## \|\| 209.26 \|\|

*syānmaṇiguṇanikaro mālinī nanamā yayau \|*  
*vasusvarayatiḥ syācca najau bhajrāḥ prabhadrakam \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Malinl has na-na-ma-ya-ya-ganas with Yati on the eight and seventh Varnas. Prabhadraka has na-ja-bha-ja-ra-ganas.

## \|\| 209.27 \|\|

*elā sayau nanau yaḥsyāccitralekhāsvarāṣṭakaiḥ \|*  
*marau mayau yaśca bhavedukteyamati śarkarī \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. Ela has sa-ja-na-na-ya-ganas. Chitralekha has mara-ma-ya-ay-ganas with Yati on the seventh and eighth Varnas. Thus Atisarkari has been described.

## \|\| 209.28 \|\|

*svarātkhaṃ vṛṣabhagajajṛmbhitaṃ bhrananā nagau \|*  
*najabhajarā vāṇinī gaḥ piṅgalenāṣṭirīritā \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Vrsabha-gaja-jnnbhita has bha-ra-na-na- ganas and Guru with Yati on the seventh and ninth varnas. Vanin! has na ja-bha -ja-ra-ganas and Guru. Thus Asti has been defined by Pingala.

## \|\| 209.29 \|\|

*rasarudraiḥ śikhariṇī yamau nasabhalā guruḥ \|*  
*vasugrayatiḥ pṛthvī jasau jasayalā guruḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Jsikharinl has Ya-ma-na-sa-bha-ganas and Laghu-Guru with Yati on the sixth and eleventh varnas. PrthvI has Ja-sa-ja-sa-ya-ganas and Laghu-Guru with Yati on the eighth and ninth varnas.

## \|\| 209.30 \|\|

*daśasvarairvaṃśapatrapatitaṃ bhraunnabhā lagau \|*  
*ṣaḍvedāśvaiśca hariṇī nasamā rasalā guruḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Vamsa-patra-patita has Bha-ra-na-bha- naganas and Laghu-Guru with Yati on the tenth and seventh Varnas. Harini has Na-sa-tna- ra-sa-ganas and Laghu-Guru with Yati on the sixth, fourth and seventh Varnas.

## \|\| 209.31 \|\|

*mandākrāntabdhiṣaḍnagairmabhanāstatagā guruḥ \|*  
*nardaṭakaṃ najabhajā jalau go yatireva ca \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Mandakranta has Ma-bha-na-ta-ta-gangs and two Gurus with Yati on the fourth, sixth and seventh varnas. Narttataka has Na ja-bha ja -jaganas and Laghu-Guru with Yati on the seventh and the tenth Varnas.

## \|\| 209.32 \|\|

*saptartvabdhiḥ kokilakamatyaṣṭiḥ syācca pūrvavat \|*  
*bhūtartvaśvaiḥ kusumitalatā mtau nyau yayau dhṛtiḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. If the Yati is on the seventy, sixth and fourth Varnas, it is called Kokilaka. So for Atyasti. Kusumitalata has Ma-ta-na-ya-ya-ya-gams with Yati on the fifth, sixth and seventh Varnas. So for Dhrti.

## \|\| 209.33 \|\|

*rasartvaśvairyamau nsau rau meghavisphūrjitā ragau \|*  
*śārdūlavikrīḍitaṃ maḥ sūryaśvaiḥ sajsatāstagau \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Merhavisphurjita has Ya-ma-na-na-ra- raganri and Guru with Yati on the sixth and seventh Varna. Shardulavi-kridita has Ma ja-ja-sa-ta-taga4ri and Guru with Yati on the twelfth and seventh Varnas.

## \|\| 209.34 \|\|

*chando hyatidhṛtiḥ proktamata ūrdhvaṃ kṛtirbhavet \|*  
*saptāśvartuḥ suvadanā bhrau manau yabhalā guruḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. So far Atidhrti metre has been told. Now will come Krti. Suvadana has Ma-ra-bha-na-ya- bhaganas and Laghu-Guru with Yati on seventh, seventh and sixth Varnas.

## \|\| 209.35 \|\|

*vṛttaṃ rajau rajau pāde rajau go laḥ kṛtirbhavet \|*  
*trisaptakaiḥ snagdharā syātprakṛtirmnabhanaistriyaiḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Vrtta has Raja-raja-raja-gangs and Guru- Laghu. So far Krti. Sragdhara has Ma-ra-bha- nana-ya-ya-ya-gangs with Yati on the seventh, seventh and seventh Varnas. So far Prakrti.

## \|\| 209.36 \|\|

*digarkairbhadrakaṃ bhrau nrau naranā go yathākṛtiḥ \|*  
*najau bhaśvāśvalalitaṃ jabhau jabhalagā bhavet \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Bhadraka, has Bha-ra-na-m-na-ra-na-ganas and Guru with Yati on the tenth and twelfth Varnas So. far Akrti. Asvalalita has Na ja-bha ja-bha jabhagangs and Laghu-Guru with Yati on eleventh and twelfth Varnas.

## \|\| 209.37 \|\|

*mattākrīḍañcāṣṭabāṇadaśakairmau tanau nanau \|*  
*nalau guruśca vikṛtiśchinnā saṃkṛtirucyate \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Mattakrida has Ma-ma-ta-na-na-ganas and Laghu Guru with Yati on the eighth, eleventh and seventh Varnas. So for Vikrti. Now Sankrti is told.

## \|\| 209.38 \|\|

*pañcāśvārkairbhatau tanvī nasabhā bhanayā gaṇāḥ \|*  
*krauñcapadā bāṇaśaravasuśailairbhamau sabhau \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Tanvl has Bha-ta-na-sa-bha-bha-na-ya- gams with Yati on the fifth and seventh Varnas. Krauncapada has Bha-ma-sa-bha-na-na-na- ganas and Guru with Yati on the fifth, fifth, eighth Varnas.

## \|\| 209.39 \|\|

*nau nau go 'tikṛtiḥ proktā cchando hyutkṛtirucyate \|*  
*vasvīśāśvairmamatanaiḥ syādbhujaṅgavijṛmbhitam \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. So far Atikrti metre has been told. Now Utkrti is being told. Bhujangavijrmbhita has Ma-ma-ta-na-na-na-ra-sa ganas and Laghu- Guru with Yati on the eighth, eleventh and seventh Vamas.

## \|\| 209.40 \|\|

*nanarasairlagayuktaiśca apavāhākhyakaṃ yatiḥ \|*  
*guhaiḥ ṣaḍbhī rasairbāṇairmonāḥ ṣaṭsagagā gaṇāḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Apavaha has Ma-na-na-na-na-na-sa ganas and two Gurus withYati on 9,6,6,5 Varnas.

## \|\| 209.41 \|\|

*caṇḍavṛttiprapāto 'sau daṇḍako nau tato 'garaḥ \|*  
*raphevṛddhāntakādasya vyālajīmūtakādayaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Candavnttiprapata has Na-na-ra-ra-ra-ra- ra-ganas. Many varieties of this Dandaka- metre are formed by the addition of one Ra-gana in each of them.

## Chapter 210

## \|\| 210.1-2 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*sasasalagāśca viṣame pāde yadyupacitrakam \|*  
*same bhau bhagagāḥ syuśca drutamadhyā bhabhau bhagau \|\| 1 \|\|*

*gaḥ pāde viṣame 'nyatra najau jyau ca gaṇau smṛtau \|\| 2 \|\|*

1-2. Suta said: — Upacitraka has Sa-sa-sa-ganas and Laghu-Guru in odd feet, and Bha-bha- bhaganas and Guru-Guru in even feet. Druta- madhya has bhabha-bha-ganas and two Gurus in odd feet and Na-ja - ja-ya-ganas in even feet.

## \|\| 210.3-4 \|\|

*viṣame vegavatī sā gaḥ same bhau bho gagau gaṇāḥ \|*  
*pāde 'same tajau ro gaḥ same masau jagau garuḥ \|*  
*bhavedbhadravirāṭ ketumatī tu viṣame sajau \|\| 3 \|\|*

*sagau same bhrau nagagā ākhyānakī tvathāsame \|*  
*tau jo gagau same pāde jatajā gurukadvayam \|\| 4 \|\|*

3-4. Vegavatl has Sa-sa-sa-gams and Guru in odd feet and Bha-bha-bha-ganas and two Gurus in even feet. Bhadravirat has Ta-ja-ra- ganas and Guru in odd feet and Ma-sa -ja-ganas and two Gurus in even feet. Ketumati has Sa -ja-sa-ganas and Guru in odd feet and Bha-ra-na-ganas and two Gurus in even feet. Akhyanaki has Ta-ta -ja-ganas and two Gurus in odd feet and ja-ta -ja-ganas and two Gurus in even feet.

## \|\| 210.5 \|\|

*viparītākhyānakaṃ syādviṣame jastajau gagau \|*  
*tatau jagau same gaḥ syāt piṅgalena hyudāhṛtam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. The opposite to the same is Viparlta- khyanaka as illustrated by Pingala.

## \|\| 210.6 \|\|

*pāde 'tha viṣame caiva puṣpitāgrā nanau rayau \|*  
*same najau jarau gaśca vaitālīyaṃ vadanti hi \|*  
*vṛttañcāparavaktrākhyamaupacchandasikaṃ param \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Puspitagara has Na-na-ra-ya-ganas in odd feet and Na-ja-ja-ra-ganas and Guru in even feet, aparavaktra is called Vaitaliya and Puspitagra is called Aupacchandasika.

## \|\| 210.7 \|\|

*vāṅmatī rajarā yaḥ syādayugme jarajā ragau \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Vanmati has Ra-ja-ra-ya-ganas in odd feet and Ja-ra-ja-ra-ganas and Gurus in even feet.

## Chapter 211

## \|\| 211.1 \|\|

*sāmānyalakṣaṇaṃ padacaturūrdhvābhiradhasya hi \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Suta said: — Padacaturardha has 8 Varnas is the first foot, 12 in the second, 16 in the third and 29 in the forurth.

## \|\| 211.2 \|\|

*āpīḍaḥ sarvalaḥ proktaḥ pūrvapādāntagadvayaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. When in a Padacatururdhva all the Varnas are Laghu except the last two which are Guru, it is called Aplda.

## \|\| 211.3 \|\|

*dvitīye 'ṣṭākṣaraiḥ pāde kalikā prathamer'kaje \|*  
*lavalī syāttṛtīye 'tha pūrvavaccāṣṭa kākṣare \|*  
*proktā cāmṛtadhāreyaṃ caturaṣṭākṣare sati \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Kalika has 12, 8,16 and 20 Varnas in each foot respectively. Lavali has 12/ 16, 8 and 20 Varnas in respective feet. Amrtadhara has 12, 16,20 and 8 Varn as in its feet.

## \|\| 211.4 \|\|

*(iti padacaturūrdhvaprakaraṇam) \|*  
*sajau salau ca prathame nasajā go dvitīyake \|*  
*tṛtīye bhanabhā gaśca caturthe sajasā jagau \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Udgata has Sa-ja-sa-ganas and Laghu in the first foot, Na-saja-ganas and Guru in the second, Bha-na -ja-ganas and Laghu-Guru in the third and Saja-sa -ja-ganas and Guru in the fourth.

## \|\| 211.5 \|\|

*pūrvavatsyātsaurabhakaṃ tṛtīye 'ghrau ranau bhagau \|*  
*lalitañcādgatāvatsyātṛtīyeṃ'ghrau nanau sasau \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Saurabhaka has Ra-na-ganas and Guru in the third feet ano other feet are like those of Udgata. Similarly, Lalita has na-na-sa-ganas in the third feet, the rest being like Udgata.

## \|\| 211.6 \|\|

*(ityudgatāprakaraṇam) \|*  
*upasthitapracupitaṃ prathame 'ghrau masau jabhau \|*  
*gau dvitīye sanajarā gastṛtīye nanau ca saḥ \|*  
*nau najau yaścaturthe syāccheṣa pādāśca pūrvavat \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Upasthitapracupita has Ma-sa-ja-bha-ganas and two Gurus in the first foot, Sa-na-ja-ra- ganas and Guru in the second, Na-na-sa-ganas in the third and Na-na-na-ja-ya-ganas in the fourth.

## \|\| 211.7 \|\|

*tṛtīrye 'ghrau viśeṣaśca vṛttaṃ syānnau sanau nasau \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Visesa has Na-na-sa-na-na-sa in the third foot, the rest being like Upasthitapracupita.

## \|\| 211.8 \|\|

*ārṣabhaṃ tajarāḥ pāde tṛtīye 'nyacca pūrvavat \|*  
*pūrvavatprathamaṃ śeṣe tajrāḥ śuddhavirāḍbhavet \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Similarly, Suddhavirad, Arsabha had Ta-ja- ra-ganas in the third foot and the rest like Upastitapracupita.

## \|\| 211.9 \|\|

*(ityupasthitapracupitaprakaraṇam) \|*  
*viṣamākṣarapādaṃ vā pañcaṣaṭkādi yāvakam \|*  
*chando 'tra noktā gātheti daśadharṃmādivadbhavet \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. If there are old syllables or odd feet like five or six in a metre, it is known as Gatha like 'Dasadharmam' (Mbh 5. 33.82)

## Chapter 212

## \|\| 212.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*prastāra ādyago 'tho laḥ paratulyo 'tha pūrvagaḥ \|*  
*naṣṭamadhye sameṃ'ke laḥ same 'rdhe viṣame guruḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Suta said: — In Prastara first all Gurus should be noted down: Then Laghu should be noted down below the first Guru arid the rest should be done as before. In Nasta Laghu should be written for even numbers and Guru should be written for odd numbers. The same holds good about the half of numbers.

## \|\| 212.2 \|\|

*pratilomaguṇaṃ lādyaṃ dviruddiṣṭaka ekanut \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. In Uddistaka upon each Varna numbers beginning from one should be written respectively multiplied by two. The number of Laugh should be added and then one should again.

## \|\| 212.3-5 \|\|

*saṃkhyā dvirardhe rūpe tu śūnyaṃ śūnye dvirīritam \|*  
*tāvadardhe tadguṇitaṃ dvirdvyūnantu tadantataḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*pare pūrṇaṃ pare pūrṇaṃ meruḥ prastārato bhavet \|\| 4 \|\|*

*lagasaṃkhyā vṛttasaṃkhyā cādyāṅgulamathordhvataḥ \|*  
*saṃkhyaiva dviguṇaikonācchandaḥ sāro 'yamīritaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

3-5. (The numbers in two holds, zero in zeros repeated by too. Half should multiplied by half only. When full it is fall and called Prastona, the number of hoghus, the mumber of metres first guru and hoghu he upwards. The numbers of Guru of high should be doubted. This is the essence of the chacken.

## Chapter 213

## \|\| 213.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*hareḥ śrutvābravīdbrahmā yathā vyāsāya śaunaka \|*  
*brāhmaṇādisamācāraṃ sarvadaṃ te tathā vade \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Suta said: — Now I shall relate to you the rules of conduct to be observed by Brahmanas, etc., which Brahma first learned from Hari and expounded to the holy Vyasa. and proper performances where of grant all things to their perfromers.

## \|\| 213.2-3 \|\|

*śrutismṛtī tu vijñāya śrautaṃ karma samācaret \|*  
*śrautaṃ karma na ceduktaṃ tadā smārtaṃ samācaret \|\| 2 \|\|*

*tatrāpyaśaktaḥ karaṇe sadācāraṃ caredvudhaḥ \|*  
*śrutismṛtī ha viprāṇāṃ locane karmadarśane \|\| 3 \|\|*

2-3. A twice-born one, having learnt the Vedas and the scriptural law, shall perform acts (rites) enjoined to be performed in the Vedas; unable to perform the Vedic rites, he shall perform those mentioned in the law codes (Smrd). Even incapable of performing either class of these acts, the intelligent one shall perform acts of good conduct. The Shruti and the Smrti are the eyes, as it were, of Brahmanas in resect of detect of detecting the true virtue. Bereft of one of these eyes of Sruti and Smrti, a Brahmana verily becomes a moral oneeyed; bereft of both he becomes morally blind.

## \|\| 213.4 \|\|

*śrutyuktaḥ paramo dharmaḥ smṛtiśāstragato 'paraḥ \|*  
*siṣṭācāreṇa saṃprāptastrayo dharmāḥ sanātanāḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Pieties described in the &ruti and Sastras and the acts of good conduct performed by the pious triply form the eternal virtues (duties eternally obligatory on all).

## \|\| 213.5 \|\|

*satyaṃ dānaṃ dayālobho vidyejyā pūjanaṃ damaḥ \|*  
*aṣṭau tāni pavitrāṇi śiṣṭācārasya lakṣaṇam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Truthfulness, gift making (charity), absence of greed or avarice, knowledge, performances of religious sacrifices, divine worship, and selfcontrol, are the eight sacred constituents of good conduct.

## \|\| 213.6 \|\|

*tejomayāni pūrveṣāṃ śarīrāṇīndriyāṇi ca \|*  
*na lipyate pātakena padmapatramivāmbhasā \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. The body and sense-organs of the pious, effulgent with a kind of sanctified light, do not adhere to sin, like water drops to lotus leaves. Of men of all the four orders virtue forms the main stay of existence.

## \|\| 213.7 \|\|

*nivāsamukhyā varṇānāṃ dharmācārāḥ prakīrtitāḥ \|*  
*satyaṃ yajñastapo dānametaddharmasya lakṣaṇam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Truthfulness, performance of religious sacrifices and austerities (meditation), and charity, are the cardinal duties of householders.

## \|\| 213.8-9 \|\|

*adattasyānupādānaṃ dānamadhyayanaṃ japaḥ \|*  
*vidyā vittaṃ tapaḥ śaucaṃ kule janma tvarogitā \|\| 8 \|\|*

*saṃsārocchittihetuśca dharmādeva pravartate \|*  
*dharmātsukhaṃ ca jñānaṃ ca jñānānmokṣo 'dhigamyate \|\| 9 \|\|*

8-9. Learning (knowledge), opulence, practive of austerities, valour, noble parentage, and absence of disease (sound health) are the factors that lead to the elevation of a man in this world; all these proceed from the practice of virtue. From virtue proceed happiness and knowledge; knowledge leads of the ultimate emancipation of one's own self.

## \|\| 213.10 \|\|

*ijyādhyayanadānāni yathāśāstraṃ sanātanaḥ \|*  
*brahmakṣattriyavaiśyānāṃ sāmānyo dharma ucyate \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Performances of religious sacrifices, endowments for the public good, study of the Vedas, and practice of charily in conformity with the injunctions of the 6astras may be described as the eternal duties, commonly obligatory on Brahmanas, Kstriyas and Vaisyas.

## \|\| 213.11 \|\|

*yājanādhyayane śuddhe viśuddhācca pratigrahaḥ \|*  
*vṛttitrayamidaṃ prāhurmunayaḥ śreṣṭhavarṇinaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Imparting lessons (teaching)to the pure and the body, officiating as priests and the religious sacrifices performed by the pure, and acceptance of gifts from persons not in any way impure or unholy are the three means of earning livelihood, open to Brahmanas, in the opinion of the Munis.

## \|\| 213.12 \|\|

*śastreṇājīvanaṃ rājño bhūtānāñcābhirakṣaṇam \|*  
*pāśupālyaṃ kṛṣiḥ paṇyaṃ vaiśyasyājīvanaṃ smṛtam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Military professions and protection of creature from hurt or injury are the callings of Ksatriya. Rearing of cattle, agriculture, and trade are the means by which Vaisyas shall earn their living.

## \|\| 213.13-14 \|\|

*śūdrasya dvijaśuśrūṣā dvijānāmanupūrvaśaḥ \|*  
*gurau vāso 'gniśuśrūṣā svādhyāyo brahmacāriṇaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*triḥ snātā snāpitā bhaikṣyaṃ gurau prāṇāntikī sthitiḥ \|*  
*samekhalo jaṭī daṇḍī muṇḍī vā gurusaṃśrayaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

13-14. Service of the three twice-born classes, to be made preferentially in the order of enumeration, should be the vocations of §udras. Residence near the preceptor, service of the consecrated fire, study of the Vedas, three ablutions; each day, ritualistic ablutions, wearing of clotted hairs, carrying of staffs, wearing of Mekhalas, living off alms, residence near the preceptor till death, or a clearshaving of the head are the duties which are obligatory on Brahmacarins.

## \|\| 213.15-16 \|\|

*agnihotropacaraṇaṃ jīvanaṃ ca svakarmabhiḥ \|*  
*dharmadāreṣu kalpeta parvavarjaṃ ratikriyāḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*devapitratitibhyaśca pūjādiṣvanukalpanam \|*  
*śrutismṛtyarthasaṃsthānaṃ dharmo 'yaṃ gṛhamedhinaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

15-16. Perfomances of Agnihotra sacrifices, earning of livelihood by means proper to his order, procreation of sons on his own married wife, and on days not interdicted as Parvas, making offerings to the gods and to his departed manes, as well as feeding of all guests (Atithis) to his house, and perusal of the true imports of Srutis and Smrtis are the duties of a house-holdor.

## \|\| 213.17-18 \|\|

*jaṭitvamagnihotratvaṃ bhūśayyājinadhāraṇam \|*  
*vane vāsaḥ payomūlanīvāraphalavṛttitā \|\| 17 \|\|*

*pratiṣiddhānnivṛttiśca triḥ snānaṃ vratadhāritā \|*  
*devatātithipūjā ca dharmo 'yaṃ vanavāsinaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

17-18. Wearing of clotted hairs on the head, performances of Agnihotra sacrifices, lying down on the bars ground, wearing of deer-skin, residence in the forest, living on roots, bulbs, fruit and Nivara grains, etc., abstention from all forbidden acts, daily performance of three ablutions, observance of vow, and propitiation of the gods, Atithis and his departed manes are the duties of a forestdwelling (Vanaprastha hermit).

## \|\| 213.19-21 \|\|

*sarvārambhaparityāgo bhikṣānnaṃ vṛkṣamūlatā \|*  
*niṣparigrahatādrohaḥ samatā sarvajantuṣu \|\| 19 \|\|*

*priyāpriyapariṣvaṅgesukhaduḥ khādhikāritā \|*  
*sabāhyābhyantare śaucaṃ vāgyamo dhyānacāritā \|\| 20 \|\|*

*sarvaidriyasamāhāro dhāraṇādhyānanityatā \|*  
*bhāvasaṃśuddhiretyeṣa parivrāḍdharma ucyate \|\| 21 \|\|*

19-21. Abstention of all acts or undertakings, living on alms, residence under the trees, non-acceptance of gifts, living in harmony with all and sundry (lit. not in conflict with any), practising of equality to all, maintaining equanimity under all painful or pleasurable circumstances, acquisition of mastery over pleasure and pain, purification of both inside and out, practice of silence and meditation, drawing in of all the sense organs from the external world, practice of constant meditation and attempt at being one with the thought, and purification of ideas are the duties which are obligatory on a Parivrajaka to cultivate.

## \|\| 213.22 \|\|

*ahiṃsā sūnṛtā vāṇī satyaśauce kṣamā dayā \|*  
*varṇināṃ liṅgināṃ caiva sāmānyo dharma ucyate \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Truthfulness, forbearance, compassion, purity, abstention of all killing propensities and sacred discourse are the bounden duties of all the four social orders.

## \|\| 213.23 \|\|

*yathoktakāriṇaḥ sarve prayānti paramāṃ gatim \|*  
*ā bodhātsvapanaṃ yāvat gṛhidharmaṃ ca vacmi te \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Those, who strictly conform of the aforesaid laws and duly perform their respective duties, come by a better fate. Now I shall relate to you the duties of a house-holder from the time when he leaves his bed to that when he goes to sleep in the night.

## \|\| 213.24-25 \|\|

*brāhme muhūrte budhyeta dharmārthau cānucintayet \|*  
*kāyakleśāṃśca tanmūlānvedatattvārthameva ca \|\| 24 \|\|*

*śarvaryante samutthāya kṛtaśaucaḥ samāhitaḥ \|*  
*snātvā sandhyāmupāsīta sarvakālamatandritaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

24-25. Rising at the Brahama Muhurta (about half an hour before the dawn) a house-holder shall attend to the calls of nature, and then having carefully washed himself, at the close of the night, shall think of his own good both in this world and the next. Then he shall bathe and altend to the rite of his Sandhya meditation.

## \|\| 213.26-27 \|\|

*prātaḥ sandhyāmupā sīta dantadhāvanapūrvikām \|*  
*ubhe mūtrapurīṣe ca divā kuryādudaṅmukhaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*rātrau ca dakṣiṇe kuryādubhe sandhye yathā divā \|*  
*chāyāyāmandhakāre vā rātrau vāhani vā dvijaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

26-27. He shall perform the rite of his morning Sandhya after having washed his face and cleansed his teeth. One should void stool and urine, looking towards the north, in the day; and towards the south in the night. At the two junctions of the day and night, the rule laid down in respect of urination and defecation in the day should be followed.

## \|\| 213.28 \|\|

*yathā tu samukhaḥ kuryātprāṇabādhābhayeṣu ca \|*  
*gomayāṅgāravalmīkaphālākṛṣṭe śubhe \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. In shade, in darkness in the day or night, as well as in times of danger to life or of illness, a Brahmana can void stool or urine, looking towards any quarter of the sides, best convenient. One shall not void urine on cowung, charcoal, or an anthill, nor inclear pure water, or on the furrowns of a ploughed field.

## \|\| 213.29 \|\|

*mārgopajīvyacchāyāsu na mūtraṃ ca purīṣakam \|*  
*antarjalāddevagṛhādvalmīkānmūṣikasthalāt \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Similarly, urination near the road side, in an assembly, or over writing materials are forbidden. Earth should not be taken from beneath the water, from a temple, from an ant-hill, from about mouse-hole, or from a cremation ground.

## \|\| 213.30 \|\|

*pareṣāṃ śaucaśiṣṭācca śmaśānācca mṛdaṃ tyajet \|*  
*ekāṃ liṅge mṛdaṃ dadyādvāma haste mṛdaṃ dvidhā \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. The residue of earth with which one has purified oneself (cleaned one's person) should be avoided. One Mrttika (half a Prasritiful Earth) should be used in rubbing the external orifice of the urethra, three Mrttikas should be used in rubbing the anus, three Mrttikas in rubbing the palm of the left hand, and a Half Mrttika in rubbing the palms of both the hands, after voiding stool.

## \|\| 213.31-32 \|\|

*ubhayordve ca dātavye mūtraśaucaṃ pracakṣate \|*  
*ekāṃ liṅge gude tistrastathā vāmakare daśa \|\| 31 \|\|*

*pañca pāde daśaikasminkarayoḥ saptamṛttikāḥ \|*  
*ardhaprasṛtimātrā tu prathamā mṛttikā smṛtā \|\| 32 \|\|*

31-32. Now I shall describe the process of purification, after voiding urine. One Mrttika should be applied to the external orifice of the urethra; three, to the anus; ten, to the plam.of the left hand; five, to the soles of feet; and seven of each of the arms. The greatest quantity of Mrttika (clay) which should be used in cleansing the orifices of the external ducts of the body, under these circumstances, is half of what can be contained in the palm of one's hand, outstretched and hollowed.

## \|\| 213.33-34 \|\|

*dvitīyā ca tṛtīyā ca tadardhā parikīrtitā \|*  
*upaviṣṭastu viṇmūtraṃ kartuṃ yastu na vindati \|\| 33 \|\|*

*sa kuryādardhaśaucaṃ tu svasya śaucasya sarvadā \|*  
*divā śaucasya rātryardhaṃ yadvā pādo vidhīyate \|\| 34 \|\|*

33-34. The second is half of that of the former, and the third is half of that of the second. He, who is incapable of voiding stool or urine in a sitting posture, shall perform half of these purifications, after urination or defecation. Half or a quarter part of the purifying measure, enjoined to be performed in the day, shall be performed in the night, after voiding stool or urine. Men in health must unfailingly observe these rules of purification; while sick folks shall observe them as far as they are capable of observing.

## \|\| 213.35-37 \|\|

*svasthasya tu yathoddiṣṭamārtaḥ kuryādyathābalam \|*  
*vasā śukramasṛṅ majjā lālā viṇmūtrakarṇaviṭ \|\| 35 \|\|*

*śleṣmāśradūṣikā svedo dvādaśaite nṛṇāṃ malāḥ \|*  
*manyeta yāvatā śuddhiṃ tāvacchaucaṃ samācaret \|\| 36 \|\|*

*pramāṇaṃ śaucasaṃkhyāyā nādiṣṭairavaśiṣyate \|*  
*śaucaṃ tu dvividhaṃ proktaṃ bāhyamābhyantaraṃ tathā \|\| 37 \|\|*

35-37. Fat, semen, bood, marrow, saliva, stool and urine, and waxy deposits in the ears, as well as mucous, tears, and perspiration are called the excrements of the human body. A man shall try to purify his person as long as he does not think himself pure; the extent of purification can not be precisely laid down for each individual case. There are two kinds of purification viz., external and internal, the first consists in cleansing the body, with clay, water, etc.; the second is the purification of one's thoughts and ideas.

## \|\| 213.38-40 \|\|

*mṛjjalābhyāṃ smṛtaṃ bāhyaṃ bhāvaśuddhirathāntaram \|*  
*trirācāmedapaḥ pūrvaṃ dviḥ pramṛjyāttato mukham \|\| 38 \|\|*

*saṃmṛjyāṅguṣṭhamūlena tribhirāsyamupaspṛśet \|*  
*aṅguṣṭhena pradeśinyā ghrāṇaṃ paścādanantaram \|\| 39 \|\|*

*aṅguṣṭhānāmikābhyāṃ ca cakṣuḥ śrotre punaḥ punaḥ \|*  
*kaniṣṭhāṅgaṣṭhayornābhiṃ hṛdayaṃ tu talena vai \|\| 40 \|\|*

38-40. mouth with water, and after that, thrice sip water with the ball of the thumb. Then repeatedly touch your eyes and ears with the tips of the thumb and the index finger joined together. The navel should be touched with the tips of the thumb and the small finger joined together; and the region of the heart, with the palm of the hand.

## \|\| 213.41 \|\|

*sarvābhistu śiraḥ paścādbāhū cāgreṇa saṃspṛśet \|*  
*ṛco yajūṃṣi sāmāni triḥ paṭhanprīṇayetkramāt \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. The head should be touched with all the fingers united together, and the back of the arms should be touched with the tips of fingers by rounding the hand. A Brahmana, shall thrice sip water in the manner of Acamanam for propitiating the three Vedas, viz., the Rk, the Yajus and the Saman.

## \|\| 213.42 \|\|

*atharvāṅgirasau pūrvaṃ dviḥ pramārṣṭyatha tansukham \|*  
*itihāsapurāṇāni vedāṅgāni vedāṅgāni yathākramam \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Similarly, by twice rubbing the lips he shall propitiate the Atharva Angirasa, as well as the Itihasas., Puranas, and Vedangas in succession.

## \|\| 213.43 \|\|

*khaṃ mukhe nāsike vāyuṃ netre sūryaṃ śrutī (tīrdi) diśaḥ \|*  
*prāṇagranthimatho nābhiṃ brahmāṇaṃ hṛdaye spṛśet \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. He shall touch the principle of either in his mouth; the principle of air, in his nostrils; the sun, in his sight; the quarters of the skies, in the chord of vitality in his umbilicus; and the supreme Brahma, at his heart.

## \|\| 213.44-45 \|\|

*rudraṃ mūrdhnā samālabhya prīṇātyatha śikhāmṛṣīn \|*  
*bāhū yamendravaruṇakuberavasudhānalān \|\| 44 \|\|*

*abhyukṣya caraṇau viṣṇumindraṃ viṣṇu karadvayam \|*  
*agnirvāyuśca sūryendugirayo 'ṅguliparvasu \|\| 45 \|\|*

44-45. The god Rudra is pleased by one touching one's head, while the Rsis are propitiated by one touching the tuft of hair one one's crown, at the time of performing an Acamanam. The lord of death, Indra, Varuna, Kubera, the Earth-goddess and the fire-god are pleased by one touching one's anus, at the afore said time. He shall feel die contact of Visnu and Indra by touching the soles of his feet and that of Visnu alone by touching his arms. О thou twice born one, the the celestial serpents Vasuki etc., are propitiated by the water that one might cast on the ground at the time of performing Acamanam, and the drops of water that he mught cast around tend to propitiate the hosts of spirits. The dities, Agni, Vayu, Sfrya and Indra are situated in the phalanges of one's fingers. The moon-god, with all the sacred pools and sanctuaries, are situated in the palm of one's (right) hand; hence, the (right) hand is always pure.

## \|\| 213.46-47 \|\|

*gaṅgādyāḥ saritastāsu yā rekhāḥ karamadhyagāḥ \|*  
*uṣaḥ kāle tu saṃprāpte śaucaṃ kṛtvā yathārthavat \|\| 46 \|\|*

*tataḥ snānarṃ pkurvīta dantadhāvanapūrvakam \|*  
*mukhe paryuṣite nityaṃ bhavatyaprayato naraḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

46-47. The sacred streams and river such as, the Ganges etc., are situated in the lines, that run across the palm of one's (right) hand. At the approach of dawn, one shall attend to the calls of nature, and cleanse his person; then having cleansed his teeth with a twig, bitten down in 'the shape of a tooth-brush, he shall take an ablution.

## \|\| 213.48-49 \|\|

*tasmātsarvaprayatnena kuryādvai dantaghāvanam \|*  
*kadambabilvakhadirakaravīravaṭārjunāḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

*yūthī ca bṛhatī jātī karañjārkātimuktakāḥ \|*  
*jambūmadhūkā pāmārgaśirīṣodumbarāsanāḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

48-49. A person remains impure, even after clean sing his teeth, after the expiry of the previous night; hence one shall eat the tooth-twig bitten and smashed in the shape of a tooth-brush), each morning. Twigs of Kadamba, Vilva, Khadira, Karavlra, Vata, Arjuna, Yathi, Vrhad, Jati, Karnja, Arka, Atimukta, Jambu, Madhuka, Apamarga, 6irisa, Audumbara, Asana,

## \|\| 213.50 \|\|

*kṣīrikaṇṭakivṛkṣādyāḥ praśastā dantadhāvane \|*  
*kaṭutiktakaṣāyāśca dhanārogyasukhapradāḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Ksirl, and KantakI trees and plants are recommended for the purpose of being used as toothbrushes. Twigs of pungent, bitter, and astringent flavours, used for the purpose of cleansing the teeth, bring health and happiness to the cleanser.

## \|\| 213.51 \|\|

*prakṣālya bhuktvā ca śucau deśe tyaktvā tadācāmet \|*  
*amāyāṃ ca tathā ṣaṣṭhyāṃ navamyāṃ pratipadyapi \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Then having washed the tooth-twig and cleansed his teeth, he shall wash his face, while seated in a pure site. Tooth-twigs should not be used of days, marked by the new moon, as well as on the first, sixth or ninth day of the moon's wane

## \|\| 213.52 \|\|

*varjayeddantakāṣṭhantu tathaivārkasya vāsare \|*  
*abhāve danta kāṣṭhasya niṣiddhāyāṃ tathā tithau \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. Similarly, the use of tooth-twigs is prohibited on Sundays. In the absence of any tooth-twig, as well as on days in which its use is prohibited, one shall gargle one's mouth with twelve handfuls of water.

## \|\| 213.53-54 \|\|

*aṣāṃ dvādaśagaṇḍūṣaiḥ kurvīta mukhaśodhanam \|*  
*prātaḥ snānaṃ praśaṃsanti dṛṣṭādṛṣṭakaraṃ hitam \|\| 53 \|\|*

*sarvamar hati śuddhātmā prātaḥ snāyī japādikam \|*  
*atyantamalinaḥ kāyo navacchidrasamanvitaḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

53-54. A morning ablution, either before or after the apperance of the sun on the horizon, is recommended as wholesome; a pure-should, and pure-bodied morning-bather becomes competent to practise all religious gets of Japa etc.

## \|\| 213.55-58 \|\|

*stravatyeṣa divā rātrau prātaḥ snānaṃ viśodhanam \|*  
*manaḥ prasādajananaṃ rūpasaubhāgyavardhanam \|\| 55 \|\|*

*śokaduḥ khapraśamanaṃ gaṅgāsnānavadācaret \|*  
*adya haste tu nakṣatre daśamyāṃ jyeṣṭhake site \|\| 56 \|\|*

*daśapāpa harāyāṃ ca adatvā dānakalmaṣam \|*  
*viruddhācaraṇaṃ hiṃsā paradāropasevanam \|\| 57 \|\|*

*pāruṣyānṛtapaiśunyamasambaddhābhibhāṣaṇam \|*  
*paradravyābhidhānaṃ ca manasāniṣṭacintanam \|\| 58 \|\|*

55-58. The human body, extremely fully within and provided with nine apertures or external ducts, day and night, exudes impure and unclean secretions, and a morning ablution is the means of briniging about its purification, each day. An ablution in the Ganges imparts a cheerfulness to the mind, and health and a beautiful complexion to the -body. It dissipates grief and misery. "For the extinction of the ten classes of sin, severally committed by receiving what has not been formally given, by doing forbidden acts, by huting or killing any creature, by carnally knowing another man's wife, by using abusive language to, or hurting the feelings of any, by speaking falsehood, by practising niggardliness, by improper speaking, by coveting other man's riches, by wishing evil to others. I take this ablution in the Ganges."

## \|\| 213.59 \|\|

*etaddaśāghaghātārthaṃ gaṅgāsnānaṃ karomyaham \|*  
*prātaḥ saṃkṣepataḥ snānaṃ vānaprasthagṛhasthayoḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. House-holders and forest-dwelling hermits (Vanaprasthas) are only competent to bathe twice a day, viz., at morning and mid-day; while Yatis are privileged to bathe three times, each day. A Brahmacarin shall bathe only once a day.

## \|\| 213.60-61 \|\|

*yatestriṣavaṇaṃ snānaṃ sakṛtta brahmacāriṇaḥ \|*  
*ācamya tīrthamāvāhya snāyātsmṛtvāvyayaṃ harim \|\| 60 \|\|*

*tisraḥ koṭyastu vijñeyā mandehā nāma rākṣasāḥ \|*  
*udayantaṃ durātmānaḥ sūryamicchanti khāditum \|\| 61 \|\|*

60-61. Having performed the rite of Acamanam, and invoked the sacred pools therein, one shall take a bath in the river. Thirty million is the number of the malignant spirits, called Mandehas, who manifest a desire of devouring the sun at day break.

## \|\| 213.62 \|\|

*sa hanti sūryaṃ sandhyāyāṃ nopāstiṃ kurute tu yaḥ \|*  
*dahanti mantrapūtena toyenānalarūpiṇā \|\| 62 \|\|*
