8\. The hands, which do not pilfer other men's goods, which do not hurt or kill any creature, nor grapple dice, are said to be having wellcontrolled hands. He, who does not look upon another's wife with lustful eyes, is said to be a man who has controlled his generative organs.

## \|\| 235.9 \|\|

*alolupamidaṃ bhuṅkte jaṭharaṃ tasya saṃyatam \|*  
*satyaṃ hitaṃ mitaṃ brūte yasmādvāktasya saṃyatā \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. He, who ungreedily eats a moderate quanity of food, is said to be a man who has controlled his belly. He, who speaks only what is true, beneficial, and only when necessary, is said to be man who has controlled his tongue.

## \|\| 235.10 \|\|

*yasya saṃyatānyetāni tasya kiṃ tapasādhvaraiḥ \|*  
*aikyaṃ yadbuddhimanasorindriyāṇāṃ ca sarvadā \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Of what use is the practice of austerities or celebration of a religious sacrifice to one who has controlled these organs? The concentration of the mind, intellect and the senses (cognition) on the supreme lord of the universe is called Dhyanam i.e.) meditation).

## \|\| 235.11-12 \|\|

*sabījaṃ vāpi nirbojaṃ dhyānametatprakīrtitam \|*  
*bhruvormadhye sthitāṃ buddhiṃ viṣayeṣu yunakti yaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*handriyāṇāmuparame manasi hyavyavasthite \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12. He, who joins his intellect, focussed in a point between the eye-browss, to thoughts of the external world, even after the cessation of the functions of the cognitive organs and before the mind has assumed a state of perfect quisence, dreams many dreams both internal and external.

## \|\| 235.13 \|\|

*svapnānpaśyatyasau jīvo bāhyānābhyantarānatha \|*  
*jīvo jāgradavasthāyāmevamāhurvipāścitaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. The individualised Self beholds many such, dreams even in the wakening state,this is the opinion of the erudite ones.

## \|\| 235.14 \|\|

*hṛdi sthitaḥ sa tamasā mohito na smaratyapi \|*  
*yadā tasya kuto veti suṣuptiriti kathyate \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. The state called Susupti (Dreamless sleep) occurs when the Jiva located in the heart and enveloped in the quality of Tamas does not remember 'where' 'when' and 'wherefrom'.

## \|\| 235.15-18 \|\|

*jāgrato yasya no tandrā na moho na bhramastathā \|*  
*utpadyate na jānāti śabdārthaviṣayānvaśī \|\| 15 \|\|*

*indriyāṇi samāhṛtya viṣayebhyo manastathā \|*  
*buddhyāhaṅkāramapi ca prakṛtyā buddhimeva ca \|\| 16 \|\|*

*saṃyamya prakṛtiṃ cāpi cicchaktyā kevale sthitaḥ \|*  
*paśyatyātmāni cātmānamātmanātmaprakāśakam \|\| 17 \|\|*

*cidrūpamamṛtaṃ śuddhaṃ niṣkriyaṃ vyāpakaṃ śivam \|*  
*turīyāyāmavasthāyāmāsthito 'sau na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

15-18. The state called the Turlya (lit., beyond the three states of existence) and in which the self-controlled individual is neither awake nor asleep, neither utterly forgetful nor labouring under delusion, and does not perceive the objects of the senses, occurs when the individualised self, by withdrawing the mind with the cognitive organs from the objects of perception, by merging the sense of egoism in the principle of intellection, by annihi. lating intellection with the principle of Nature (Prakrti), and by annihilating Prakrti with the energy of the psychic force (Cit 3akti) holds its self within its own self, the self-illuminant, the pure knowledge, the immortal purity, the eternal bliss without action, and running through all. This is what is called to be in the Turlya state.

## \|\| 235.19-21 \|\|

*śabdādayo guṇāḥ pañca sattvādyāśca guṇāstrayaḥ \|*  
*puryaṣṭakasya padmasya patrāṇyaṣṭau ca tāni hi \|\| 19 \|\|*

*sāmyāvasthā guṇakṛtā prakṛtistatra karṇikā \|*  
*karṇikāyāṃ sthito devo dehī cidrūpa eva hi \|\| 20 \|\|*

*puryaṣṭakaṃ parityajya prakṛtiñca guṇātmikām \|*  
*yadā yāti tadā jīvo yāti muktiṃ na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

19-21. The five Gunas are sound, touch, taste, smell and sight; the Sattva, Rajas, and Tamas forming a group of three qualities. These eight qualities are the leaves of the eight-leaved lotus (the emblem of evolution) of which Praknti (Nature), representing the state of equilibrium among the three qualities of Sattva, Rajas, and Tamas is the Karnika (the seed-capsule). The deity (self), the embodiment of pure knowledge (psychic energy), is located in the Karnika of this mystic lotus within the human heart; when the individualised self parts company with this eight-leaved lotus and the Prakrti located therein, it becomes a liberated or emancipated Self.

## \|\| 235.22 \|\|

*prāṇāyāmo japaścaiva pratyāhāro 'tha dhāraṇā \|*  
*dhyānaṃ samādhirityete ṣaḍ yogasya prasādhakāḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Pranayama (control of breath), Japa (repetition of a Mantra), Pratyahara (abstraction of the mind from objects of the senses) Dharana (comprehension) and Dhyanam. (meditation) are the six principal auxiliaries of Yoga.

## \|\| 235.23 \|\|

*pāpakṣaye devatānāṃ prītirindriyasaṃyamaḥ \|*  
*japadhyānayuto garbho viparītastvagarbhakaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Control of the senses is sin-absolving in its effect, and brings on the satisfaction of the Devas. A Pranayama is called Sagarbha (pregnant with a thought) when the practiser thinks of any definite deity or repeats any particular Mantra at the time of practising it; otherwise it is called Agarbha (unimpregnated).

## \|\| 235.24-25 \|\|

*ṣaṭtriṃśanmātrakaḥ śreṣṭhaścaturviṃśatimātrakaḥ \|*  
*madhyo dvādaśamātrastu oṅkāraṃ satataṃ japet \|\| 24 \|\|*

*vācake praṇave jñāte vācyaṃ brahma prasīdati \|*  
*(oṃnamo viṣṇave).ṣaṣṭhākṣaraśca japtavyo gāyattrī dvādaśākṣarī \|\| 25 \|\|*

24-25. An act of Pranayama consisting of thirtysix Matras is the best, that consisting, of twentyfour Matras is the intermediate, and that consisting of twelve Matras is the smallest.

## \|\| 235.26 \|\|

*sarveṣāmindriyāṇāṃ tu pravṛtirviṣayeṣu ca \|*  
*nivṛttirmanasastasyāḥ pratyāhāraḥ prakīrtitaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. All the senses evince a strong attachment of the objects of the external world, Pratyahara consists in withholding them from the object of the senses.

## \|\| 235.27 \|\|

*indriyāṇīndriyārthebhyaḥ samāhṛtya hito hi saḥ \|*  
*sahasā saha buddhyā ca pratyāhāreṣu saṃsthitaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. He who withdraws his mind and intellect from the external world and withhold his senses from their respective object, is said to exist in Pratyahara (abstraction).

## \|\| 235.28 \|\|

*prāṇāyāmairdvādaśabhiryāvatkālaḥkṛto bhavet \|*  
*yastāvatkālaparyantaṃ mano brahmaṇi dhārayet \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Dharana means the concentration of the mind on the supreme Brahma for the period of time necessary for prectising a Pranayama, consisting of twelve Matras.

## \|\| 235.29-30 \|\|

*dhyāyanna calate yasya manobhidhyāyato bhṛśam \|\| 29 \|\|*

*prāpyāvadhikṛtaṃ kālaṃ yāvatsā dhāraṇā smṛtā \|*  
*dhyeye saktaṃ mano yasya dhyeyamevānupaśyati \|\| 30 \|\|*

29-30. Dharna means the comprehension of the Brahma in an undistracted state of the mind, in the absence of any other factor, which produces it distraction; Dhyanam (contemplation) means the reposing of the mind in the object meditated upon by one, who is oblivious of the existence of any other object.

## \|\| 235.31-33 \|\|

*nānyaṃ padārthaṃ jānāti dhyānametatprakīrtitam \|*  
*dhyeye mano niścalatāṃ yāti dhyeyaṃ vicintayan \|\| 31 \|\|*

*yattaddhyānaṃ paraṃ proktaṃ munibhirdhyānacintakaiḥ \|*  
*dhyeyameva hi sarvatra dhyātā tanmayatāṃ gataḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

*paśyati dvaitarahitaṃ samādhiḥ so 'bhidhīyate \|*  
*manaḥ saṅkalparahitamindriyārthānna cintayet \|\| 33 \|\|*

31-33. The great Munis, the foremost of the divine contemplators, call that the great meditation in which the mind is permanently and tranquilly reposed in the object of meditation. The state of mind in which the contemplator sees the whole universe, both inside and out, filled with the presence of the object meditated upon, is called Samadhi. He, whose mind is without any cogitation, and whose cognitive senses have been withdrawn from their respective objects of perception, is said to exist in Samadhi (psychic trance)

## \|\| 235.34 \|\|

*yasya brahmaṇi saṃlīnaṃ samādhisthaṃ tadocyate \|*  
*dhyāyataḥ paramātmānamātmasthaṃ yasya yoginaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. The Yogin, whose mind, dwelling upon the supreme Brahma, reposes absolutely therein, is said to exist in the state of Samadhi.

## \|\| 235.35 \|\|

*manastanmayatāṃ yāti samādhisthaḥ sa kīrtitaḥ \|*  
*cittasya sthiratā bhrāntirdairmanasyaṃ pramādatā \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Delusion, hallucination and a distracted state of the mind are the defects which a Yogin must conquer and which are hostile to the successful practice of Yoga.

## \|\| 235.36-37 \|\|

*yogināṃ kathitā doṣā yogavighnapravartakāḥ \|*  
*sthityarthaṃ manasaḥ sarvaṃ sthūlarūpaṃ vicintayet \|\| 36 \|\|*

*tadvrataṃ niścalībhūtaṃ sūyyasthaṃ sthiratāṃ vrajet \|*  
*na vinā paramātmānaṃ kiñcijjagati vidyate \|\| 37 \|\|*

36-37. For the purpose of bringing about the concentration (lit., undistracted state) of the mind, the Yogin shall meditate upon a gross or material object, at the outset, and thereafter concentrate his attention on the sun (solar plexus), after the mind is perfectly settled. Nothing really exists in the universe except the Supreme Brahman.

## \|\| 235.38-40 \|\|

*viśvarūpaṃ tamevaikamiti jñātvā vimuñcati \|*  
*oṅkāraṃ paramaṃ brahma dhyāyedabjasthitaṃ vibhum \|\| 38 \|\|*

*kṣetrakṣetrajñarahitaṃ japenmātrātrayānvitam \|*  
*hṛdi sañcintayetpūrvaṃ pradhānaṃ tasya copari \|\| 39 \|\|*

*tamo rajastathā sattvaṃ maṇḍalatritayaṃ kramāt \|*  
*kṛṣṇaraktasitaṃ tasminpuruṣaṃ jīvasaṃjñitam \|\| 40 \|\|*

38-40. It is the supreme self that is imaged in this universe; he, who knows this, transcends all delusion, Pranava Mantra (Omkara) is the symbol of the supreme Self; he, who meditates upon this Mantra, located in the cavity of his heart, by an act of psychic projection, and as an embodiment of the Self, that is without body or selfconsciousness, transcends all delusion. First let a man meditate upon the self in his heart, which is enveloped in the principle of Nature (Pradhanam), the latter in its turn being successively encircled by the circles of Sattva, Rajas and Tamas, which are respectively coloured black, red and white, and wherein the Purina, denominated as the individualised self (Java), is located.

## \|\| 235.41 \|\|

*tasyopari guṇaiśvaryamaṣṭapatraṃ saroruham \|*  
*jñānaṃ tu karṇikā tatra vijñānaṃ kesarāḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Over that should be contemplated as located the eight-leaved mystic lotus of qualities and attributes, of which knowledge forms the petals; and science and philosophy, the pollens.

## \|\| 235.42-43 \|\|

*vairāgyanālaṃ tatkando vaiṣṇavo dharma uttamaḥ \|*  
*karṇikāyāṃ sthitaṃ tatra jīvavanniścalaṃ vibhu \|\| 42 \|\|*

*dhyāyedurasi saṃyuktamoṅkāraṃ muktisādhakam \|*  
*dhyāyanyadi tyajetprāṇānyāti brahma svasannidhim \|\| 43 \|\|*

42-43. Apathy to worldly concerns forms the stem of that mystic lotus, while the religion of Vishnu forms its bulb. Let the votary meditate upon the Omkara, located in its pollens, with the individualised self as its receptacle, whereby by he would be able to work out his liberation. He, who quits this life, meditating upon the mystic lotus in his heart as above described, ascends to the region of the supreme Brahma.

## \|\| 235.44-51 \|\|

*hariṃ saṃsthāpya dehābje dhyāyanyo gī ca bhaktibhāk \|*  
*ātmānamātmanā kecitpaśyanti dhyānacakṣuṣaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

*sāṃkhyabuddhyā tathaivānye yogenānye tu yoginaḥ \|*  
*brahmaprakāśakaṃ jñānaṃ bhavabandhavibhedanam \|\| 45 \|\|*

*tatraikacittatāyogo muktido nātra saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*jitendriyātmakaraṇo jñānadṛpto hi yo bhavet \|\| 46 \|\|*

*sa muktaḥ kathyate yogī paramātmanyavasthitaḥ \|*  
*āsanasthānavidhayo na yogasya prasādhakāḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

*vilambajanakāḥ sarve vistarāḥ parikīrtitāḥ \|*  
*śiśupālaḥ siddhimāpa smaraṇābhyāsagauravāt \|\| 48 \|\|*

*yogābhyāsaṃ prakurvantaḥ pasyantyātmānamātmanā \|*  
*sarvabhūteṣu kāruṇyaṃ vidveṣaṃ viṣayeṣu ca \|\| 49 \|\|*

*guptaśiśrodarādiśca kurvanyogī vimucyate \|*  
*indriyairindriyārthāṃstu na jānāti naro yadā \|\| 50 \|\|*

*kāṣṭhavadbrahmasaṃlīno yogī muktastadā bhavet \|*  
*sarvavarṇāḥ śriyaḥ sarvāḥ kṛtvā pāpāni bhasmasāt \|\| 51 \|\|*

44-51. A Yogin, by meditating upon the god Hari, ensconced in the cavity of his heart, becomes an emancipated self. Some there are who behold the Self in their persons with the help of the sight of Yoga, others with the help of Sankhya knowledge, others with the aid of Yoga. Knowledge is — that which makes the Brahma visible, and which unfetters the bond of existence; an absolute concentration of the mind in Brahma is called Yoga. The Yogin, who, illuminated with the light of pure knowledge reposes^ in the supreme Brahma by conquering his mind and senses, is said to be an emancipated self. The different kinds of seats and postures are not the real auxiliaries of Yoga, the so-called essential paraphernalias are but so many impediments to its successful practice. Even the evil-souled ^isupala realised his Self through the constant practice of meditating upon Hari; those, who are addicted to the practice of Yoga, behold their selves within themselves. Compassionate to all creatures, and hostilely disposed to the evil-souled, the Yogins, who have conquered hunger and reproductive functions, become emancipted selves. A Yogin, devoid of all sense-perceptions, reposing in the Supreme Brahma, and existing inert like a log of wood is said to be an emancipated self. The intelligent one by reducing to ashes all impureties done by him, incarnated as a female, or a member of any caste whatsoever, with the fire of meditation, becomes an emancipated self, and comes by the highest blicc

## \|\| 235.52-53 \|\|

*dhyānāgninā ca medhāvī labhate paramāṃ gatim \|*  
*manthanāddṛśyate hyagnistadvaddhyānena vai hariḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

*brahmātmanoryadaikatvaṃ sa yogaścottamottamaḥ \|*  
*bāhyarūpairna muktistu cāntasthaiḥ syādyamādibhiḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

52-53. As fire becomes manifest through churning, so the God Hari shows himself through meditaion; the communion which conclusively establishes the oneness of the Supreme and the individualised soul is the best of Yogas.

## \|\| 235.54 \|\|

*sāṅkhyajñānena yogena vedāntaśravaṇena ca \|*  
*pratyakṣatātmano yā hi sā muktirabhidhīyate \|*  
*anātmanyātmarūpatvamasataḥ satsvarūpatā \|\| 54 \|\|*

54\. The beholding of the Supreme Brahma, by dint of Sankhya or Vedanta knowledge, or by practising the rules of Yoga, is called emancipation. The universe is but a series of appearances, of perceptions of the non-soul as soul, and of the unreal as real.

## Chapter 236

## \|\| 236.1 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca \|*  
*ātmajñānaṃ pravakṣyāmi śṛṇu nārada tattvataḥ \|*  
*advaitaṃ sāṅkhyamityāhuryogastatraikacittatā \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Brahma said: — Hear me, О Narada, now discourse on the knowledge of Self (Atma-JIvnam). There are two kinds of Yogas, viz., the Advaita Yoga and the Sankhya Yoga, the absolute concentration of the mind being the essenial factor in both these forms.

## \|\| 236.2 \|\|

*advaitayogasampannāste mucyante 'tibandhanāt \|*  
*atītārabdhamāgāmi karma naśyati bodhataḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Practisers of the Advaita Yoga become free from the shackles of existence. Past, present and future acts^are destroyed through knowledge.

## \|\| 236.3 \|\|

*sadvicārakuṭhāreṇa cchinnasaṃsārapādapaḥ \|*  
*jñānavairāgyatīrthena labhate vaiṣṇavaṃ padam \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. He, who hews down the tree of existence with the axe of right discrimination and takes an ablution in the sacred pool of knowledge and apathy, comes by the bliss of Visnu.

## \|\| 236.4 \|\|

*jāgratsvapnasuṣuptaṃ ca māyā tripuramucyate \|*  
*atraivāntargataṃ sarvaṃ śāśvate nādvaye pade \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. The three states of wakening dream, and dreamless sleep are the three rods of Ne-science, all are included within this Maya; eternal is the secondless Brahma.

## \|\| 236.5 \|\|

*nāmarūpakriyāhīnaṃ sarvaṃ tatparamaṃ padam \|*  
*jagatkṛtveśvaro 'nantaṃ svayamatra praviṣṭavān \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Without name, from and action is that supreme Self; He created this infinite universe and established himself therein.

## \|\| 236.6 \|\|

*vedāhametaṃ puruṣaṃ cidrūpaṃ tamasaḥ param \|*  
*so 'hamasmīti mokṣāya nānyaḥ panthā vimuktaye \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. I am the knower, the embodiment of reality that transcends all illusion, I am He; it is this knowledge which serves as the only road to Emancipation.

## \|\| 236.7 \|\|

*śravaṇaṃ mananaṃ dhyānaṃ jñānānāṃ caiva sādhanam \|*  
*yajñadānatapastīrthavedairmuktirna labhyate \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Practice of knowledge, meditation, hearing of Sastras, celebration of sacrifice, practice of charity and penitential austerities, sojourns to places of pilgrimage, and the study of the Vedas are of no avail as far as the working out of one's salvation is concerned.

## \|\| 236.8 \|\|

*tyāgena kenaciddhyānapūjākarmādibhiryathā \|*  
*dvividhaṃ vedavacanaṃ kuru karma tyajeti ca \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Some acquire knowledge through renunciation; celebrations of religious rites, or performances of Pajas confer no real knowledge. Two kinds of injunctions are found in the Vedas on this subject, one is "do acts" (religious rites), and the other is "renounce acts."

## \|\| 236.9 \|\|

*yajñādayo vimuktānāṃ niṣkāmānāṃ vimuktaye \|*  
*antaḥ karaṇaśuddhyarthamūcurevātra kecana \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Several authorities assert that seekers after Emancipation shall celebrate religious sacrifices for the purpose of purifying their thoughts. They can not confer any other benefit.

## \|\| 236.10 \|\|

*ekena janmanā jñānanmuktirna dvaitabhāvinām \|*  
*yogabhraṣṭāḥ kuyogāśca viprā yogikulodbhavāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Those, who meditate upon deities, can not be liberated, even with the aid of right knowledge, in the course of one existence. Unsuccessful Yogins are reborn as Brahmanas in the families of Yogins.

## \|\| 236.11 \|\|

*karmaṇā badhyate janturjñānānmukto bhavādbhavet \|*  
*ātmajñānantvāśrayedvai ajñānaṃ yadato 'nyathā \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. It is his acts that bind an animal, liberation lies through knowledge; take recourse to the knowledge of self as otherwise Ne-science will assail thee.

## \|\| 236.12 \|\|

*yadā sarve vimucyante kāmā yesyahṛdi sthitāḥ \|*  
*tadāmṛtatvamāpnoti jīvanneva na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Undoubtedly a person comes by immortality the moment the desires in his heart are annihilated.

## \|\| 236.13 \|\|

*vyāpakatvātkathaṃ yāti ko yāti kva sa yāti ca \|*  
*anantatvānnadeśo 'sti amūrtitvādgatiḥ kutaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. As the self is all-pervading, how can man go any where else, or where else shall he go, or who is he that goes?

## \|\| 236.14 \|\|

*advayatvānna ko 'pyasti bodhatvājjaḍatā kutaḥ \|*  
*ekoddiṣṭaṃ yadanyasya mativāggatisaṃsthiti (m) \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. As the self is infmite, there is no space for it to move in, as it is disembodied, how can it have any locomotion? As it is without a second, it has no separate existence; as it is pure knowledge, how can it have any Ne-science?

## \|\| 236.15 \|\|

*kathamākāśakalpasya gatirāgatisaṃsthiti \|*  
*jāgratsvapnasuṣuptaṃ ca māyayā parikalpitam \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. It is like the firmament and hence its movement is like the movement of the firmament i.e. it is stationary. The tree states of waking, dreaming and slumbering are fancied through ignorance.

## \|\| 236.16 \|\|

*vastu taijasakaṃ prājñe yattu puṇyamakhaṇḍakam \|*  
*yathā te priyātmā naḥ sarveṣāṃ ca tathā priyaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. The indivisible constituents of the individual soul are the very constituents of the universal soul. That is why each and every individual is attracted to his or her own soul.

## \|\| 236.17 \|\|

*bodhamārge yathā cittaṃ sarveṣāṃ ca tathā mate \|*  
*sarvadā sarvabhūtānāṃ sarvasya ca mahāmune \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. О Narada, that is why the mind of each and every individual is inclined toward his or her own self.

## \|\| 236.18-19 \|\|

*nāhamatrātmavijñānaṃ tasmātpūrṇaṃ nirantaram \|*  
*jāgratsvapnaṃ tathā vṛttaṃ sauṣuptasukhameva ca \|\| 18 \|\|*

*smaraṇaṃ vismṛtārthasya nāsti cetkasya jāyate \|*  
*satyamastu tathā vāṇu aśarīraṃ paraṃ tathā \|\| 19 \|\|*

18-19. It is the soul, not intellect, that passes through the four states of consciousness. It is the soul, not intellect that being omniscient knows past, present and future.

## \|\| 236.20 \|\|

*nāsti cetsukhaduḥ khānāṃ sarveṣāṃ vedanaṃ katham \|*  
*sadā sarvatra sarvajñaḥ sarvasya hṛdaye na yet \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. If there were no soul in the body of a person he would not feel the thrill of pleasure nor the pang of the pain in the different states of consciousness.

## \|\| 236.21-22 \|\|

*sākṣibhūtaḥ samāśritya ko jānāti viceṣṭitam \|*  
*satya jñānānanta bhinnaṃ syānnasatyaṃ jñānataḥ pṛthak \|\| 21 \|\|*

*nānantyātpṛthagānandaṃ nāpyamānandataḥ pṛthak \|*  
*tvameva paramaṃ brahma satyajñānādilakṣaṇam \|\| 22 \|\|*

21-22. It is the soul, the witness of all activities which is truth, intelligence, eternal principle, not distince from intellect and which is bliss itself.

## \|\| 236.23-24 \|\|

*ahaṃ brahma paraṃ tattvaṃ jñātvā tvakhilavidbhavet \|*  
*yathaikamṛnmaye jñāte sarvametaccarācaram \|\| 23 \|\|*

*yathaikahemamaṇinā sarvaṃ hemamayaṃ bhavet \|*  
*jñānaṃ tathaivamīśena jñānināpyakhilaṃ jagat \|\| 24 \|\|*

23-24. By knowing Brahman one knows every thing, just as on knowing a jar of clay on a knows all the jars or on knowing gold one knows all that is made of gold.

## \|\| 236.25-26 \|\|

*yathāndhakāradoṣeṇa rajjuḥ samyaṅnadṛśyate \|*  
*yathā saṃmohadoṣeṇa cātmā samyaṅnadṛśyate \|\| 25 \|\|*

*sarpadhārādibhirbhedarainyathā vastukalpanam \|*  
*vyomādinā sarūpādyairanyathātmā prakalpyate \|\| 26 \|\|*

25-26. Just as in darkness on a cannot cognize the rope, similarly through ignorance we cannot perceive the soul. We super-impose a snake on what is in fact a rope, we superimpose the elements, ether, etc. and what is in reality the soul.

## \|\| 236.27-28 \|\|

*pratyakṣamapi yaddravyandurdarśamiti bhāṣate \|*  
*vyomādinā sarūpādyairanyathā kalpitaistathā \|\| 27 \|\|*

*tathā hi rajjururagaḥ śuktiḥ kārajataṃ yathā \|*  
*mṛgatṛṣṇāpathāyāmbhastṛptiṃ viṣṇo tathā jagat \|\| 28 \|\|*

27-28. Even the evident reality assumes a different form. The rope becomes a snake; the mother-of- pearls becomes silver. A deer cannot quench its thirst in the mirage; similarly, a man cannot satisfy his desire by indulging in the false pleasures of the senses.

## \|\| 236.29-30 \|\|

*hāhiṣṇodvijā kathi dbhohamitidṛ \|*  
*grahanāśātpunardhyāyanbrāhmaṇyaṃ manyate yathā \|\| 29 \|\|*

*māyāviṣṭastathā jīvo dehohamiti manyate \|*  
*māyānāśātpunaḥ svīyarūpaṃ brahmāsmi manyate \|\| 30 \|\|*

29-30. So long a man has the sense of pleasure, he is called a possessor. But when possession is lost he remains his true self. The individual soul associated with Maya identifies himself with the body but when may a withdraws he realizes his reality as Brahman.

## \|\| 236.31 \|\|

*grahanāśādyathā mānyajanokrūramavekṣate \|*  
*svarūpadarśanāccāyaṃ māyā nāśantayā vinā \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Just as a noble person is not effected by the loss of possession, similarly, the withdrawal of Maya does not effect a person who has realized Self.

## \|\| 236.32 \|\|

*anāditvaṃ samaṃ dvābhyāṃ svarūpaṃ tadvilakṣaṇam \|*  
*ekaḥ satyaṃ tathā bhāgī vicāreṇa paraṃ mṛṣā \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Reality and illusion are both eternal. But Reality is an unassailable truth of his illusion is a mirage.

## \|\| 236.33 \|\|

*ajopi hi sakṛtpretya saṃbhavāmyātmamāyayā \|*  
*māyecchayā dvidhā sa syātpatiḥ patnī sukhaṃ jagat \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Though declared to be unborn he passes through a series of birth and death. Though one, he becomes many in the form of husband, wife, pleasure, universe, etc.

## \|\| 236.34-35 \|\|

*aṣṭāviṃśatibhedaistu traiguṇyaṃ vidyate pṛthak \|*  
*caturaśītirlakṣyante naranāryākṛtīni ca \|\| 34 \|\|*

*eṣuviśvaṃ prabhavati khaṇḍajaṃ māyayā yathā \|*  
*ādāvante ca santyete nāmarūpakriyādayaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

34-35. The three Gunas multiplied by twenty-eight become eighty-four and these contribute to the formation of bodies, male and female and the universe with all its parts, names, forms, and actions from beginningles time to the endless one.

## \|\| 236.36-37 \|\|

*sattāvakalpanaṃ kāle na santi paramārthataḥ \|*  
*yathā rathādayaḥ svapne santo naiva ca satyataḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

*tathā jāgradavasthāyāṃ bhūtāni na tu sannidhau \|*  
*dvairūpyaṃ māyayā yāti jāgratsvapnapadajña (kṣa) yoḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

36-37. The existence of forms, names, etc is assumed and not real just as the chariot, etc which exist in the state of dream are not real. Similarly, things or object which exist in the state of wakefulness do not exist in reality.

## \|\| 236.38-39 \|\|

*evametatparaṃ brahma svapnajāgratpadadvaye \|*  
*suṣuptamacalaṃ rūpamadvayaṃ padamucyate \|\| 38 \|\|*

*māyāvicārasiddhaiva vicāreṇa vilīyate \|*  
*āpātarahitā sāpi kalpanā kālavartinī \|\| 39 \|\|*

38-39. By his association with Maya born of ignorance, Brahma appears to be dual, while by the withdrawal of Maya through knowledge lie remains non-dual.

## \|\| 236.40-41 \|\|

*evaṃ tasyā (dātyā) tmanādityaṃ siddhamekasya satyajā \|*  
*satostitvaṃ vasātitvādastitvāsatyatāṃ tataḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

*jñānaṃ tatopyananto naḥ pūrṇontaḥ śukamātmanā \|*  
*na nityabhāvājjātohamakṛtvādamṛtosmyaham \|*  
*dīpavaddhṛdaye jyotirahaṃ brahmāsmi muktaye \|\| 41 \|\|*

40-41. Thus the non-dual brahman is as the refulgent sun, Reality, Truth, Existence, Knowledge. It is eternal, complete, inward bliss. As external it is unborn, as nondoer it is nectar, as the light of an earthen lamp, it is an inward light. The realization that the individual soul is identical with the Supreme Soul leads one to relaease.

## Chapter 237

## \|\| 237.1-2 \|\|

*śrībagavānuvāca \|*  
*gītāsāraṃ pravakṣyāmi arjunāyoditaṃ purā \|*  
*aṣṭāṅgayogayuktātmā sarvavedāntapāragaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*ātmalābhaḥ paro nānya atmadehādivarjitaḥ \|*  
*hīnarūpādidehāntaḥ karaṇatvādilocanaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

1-2. The God said: — О thou, who art conversant with all - the Vedantas, who hast practised Yoga with all its eight essential components, now hear me discourse on the synopsis of the Gita as formerly narrated to Arjuna. Realisation of self is the Suminum bonum of human life; this self is devoid of body form, egoism, mind and the senses such as, the eyes, etc.

## \|\| 237.3 \|\|

*bijñānarahitaḥ prāṇaḥ suṣuptau hi pratīyate \|*  
*nāhamātmā ca duḥ khādisaṃsārādisamanvayāt \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Bereft of sensations; this receptacle of life (self) appears to be in a state of dreamless sleep.

## \|\| 237.4 \|\|

*vidhūma iva dīptārcirādīpta (ditya) iva dīptimān \|*  
*vaidyuto 'gnirivākāśe hṛtsaṅge ātmanātmani \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. I am Self, not the combination of misery and phenomena. The self, effulgent as a smokeless fire, like a flash of lightning in the sky, burns itself in the cavity of the heart.

## \|\| 237.5 \|\|

*śrotrādīni na paśyanti svaṃsvamātmānamātmanā \|*  
*sarvajñaḥ sarvadarśo ca kṣetrajñastāni paśyanti \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. The senses such as, the ears etc., do not perceive, it is the omniscient, all-seeing, selfconscious, individualised self (Ksetrajna) that perceives through the means of senses.

## \|\| 237.6 \|\|

*yadā prakāśate hyātmā paṭe dīpo jvalanniva \|*  
*jñānamutpadyate puṃsāṃ kṣayātpāpasya karmaṇaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. When through the extinction of sin, the self is reflected on the mind, like a burning flame on a screen, the right knowlledge is originated.

## \|\| 237.7-8 \|\|

*yathādarśatalaprakhye paśyatyātmānamātmani \|*  
*indriyāṇīndriyārthāṃśca mahābhūtāni pañcakam \|\| 7 \|\|*

*manobuddhirahaṅkāramavyaktaṃ puruṣaṃ tathā \|*  
*prasaṃkhyāya paraṃvyāpto vimukto bandhavairbhavet \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. Like images of objects reflected in a mirror, the self witnesses the objects of sense- perception, the five kinds of gross matter, the mind, the intellect, and the sense of Egoism, reflected in itself. When an individualised self sees itself as universal and running through all, it becomes emancipated.

## \|\| 237.9-10 \|\|

*indriyagrāmamakhilaṃ manasābhiniveśya ca \|*  
*manaścaivāpyahaṅkāre pratiṣṭhāpya ca pāṇḍava \|\| 9 \|\|*

*ahaṃ kāraṃ tathā buddhau buddhiṃ ca prakṛtāvapi \|*  
*prakṛtiṃ puruṣe sthāpya puruṣaṃ brahmaṇi nyaset \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. О thou son of Pandu, by merging all the senses in the mind; the mind, in the sense of Egoism; the sense of Egoism, in the principle of intellection; the principle of intellection, in the Prakrti (Nature); the Nature, in the Purusa (self); and the Purusa, in the Atman (supreme Self) that a man becomes emancipated and perceives his oneness with Brahma, the supreme light.

## \|\| 237.11-12 \|\|

*ahaṃ bahma paraṃ jyotiḥ prasaṃkhyāya vimucyate \|*  
*navadvāramidaṃ gehaṃ tisṛṇāṃ?pañcasākṣikam \|\| 11 \|\|*

*kṣetrajñādhiṣṭhitaṃ vidvānyo veda sa varaḥ kaviḥ \|*  
*aśvamedhasahasrāṇi vājapeyaśatāni ca \|*  
*jñānayajñasya sarvāṇi kalāṃ nārhanti ṣocśīm \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12. The intelligent one, who rightly understands the nature of his organism, provided with nine apertures (external ducts of the body), three supports (the fundamental principles of Vata, Pittam and Kapha), five witnesses (the cognitive organs) and lorded over by the self conscious Ego, is the true seer (Kavi).

## Chapter 238

## \|\| 238.1 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca \|*  
*yamaśca niyama.pārtha āsanaṃ prāṇasaṃyamaḥ \|*  
*pratyāhārastathā dhyānaṃ dhāraṇārjuna saptamī \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. The God said: — О Arjuna, О thou the son of Prtha, rules of self control, rules of penitence, posture, Pranayama, abstraction of the mind from the external world, meditation, comprehension.

## \|\| 238.2 \|\|

*samādhiriti cāṣṭāṅgo yoga ukto vimuktaye \|*  
*karmaṇā manasā vācā sarvabhūteṣu sarvadā \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. And Samadhi (psychic trance) are the eight essential components of Yoga, which leads to liberation.

## \|\| 238.3 \|\|

*hiṃsāvirāmako dharmo hyāhiṃsā paramaṃ sukham \|*  
*vidhinā yā bhaveddhiṃsā sā tvahiṃsā prakīrtitā \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Cessation of all killing or hurtful inclinations to all creatures and at all times is the highest virtue; compassion spells as the highest bliss. An animal duly killed on the celebration of a religious sacrifice is not killed at all. Speak what is true and pleasant

## \|\| 238.4 \|\|

*satyaṃ brūyātpriyaṃ brūyānna brūyātsatyamapriyam \|*  
*priyaṃ ca nānṛtaṃ brūyādeṣa dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. Cease to communicate an unpleasant truth, nor a pleasant untruth; this is the eternal virtue.

## \|\| 238.5 \|\|

*yaccadravyāpaharaṇaṃ cauryādvātha balena vā \|*  
*steyaṃ tasyānācaraṇamasteyaṃ dharmasādhanam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Acquisition of a thing by stealing or force is called Steyam, the contrary of this leads to virtue.

## \|\| 238.6 \|\|

*karmaṇā manasā vācā sarvāvasthāsu sarvadā \|*  
*sarvatra maithunatyāgaṃ brahmacaryaṃ pracakṣate \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Renuciation of sexual intercourse at all times and under all circumstances, whether in mind, speech or act, is called Brahmacaryam.

## \|\| 238.7 \|\|

*dravyāṇāmapyanādānamāpatsvapi tathecchayā \|*  
*aparigrahamityāhustaṃ prayatnena varjayet \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Non-acceptance of gifts even in moments of peril and a studious renunciation thereof is called Aparigraha.

## \|\| 238.8 \|\|

*dvidhā śaucaṃ mṛjjalābhyāṃ bāhya bhāvādathāntarāt \|*  
*yadṛcchālābhatastuṣṭiḥ santoṣaḥ sukhalakṣaṇam \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Purification, which is either external or internal, may be effected either with the help of earth and water, or by purifying the thoughts of one's mind. Contentment is resting happy with whatsoever is easily obtained without solicitation.

## \|\| 238.9-10 \|\|

*manasaścaindriyāṇāṃ ca aikāgryaṃ paramaṃ tapaḥ \|*  
*śarīraśoṣaṇaṃ vāpi kṛcchracāndrāyaṇādibhiḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*vedāntaśatarudrīyapraṇavādijapa budhāḥ \|*  
*sattvaśuddhikaraṃ puṃsāṃ svādhyāyaṃ paricakṣate \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. Tapas consists in concentrating the mind and the senses to any particular object, or in bringing about the emaciation or the body by practising Candrayanam, and Krccha Candrayanam penances. The inner purification of a person effected by reciting the Pranava, Sata Rudrlya and Vedanta texts is called Svadhyayam.

## \|\| 238.11-12 \|\|

*stutismaraṇapūjādivāṅmanaḥ kāyakarmabhiḥ \|*  
*aniścalā harau bhaktiretadīśvaracintanam \|*  
*āsanaṃ svastikaṃ proktaṃ padmamardhāsanaṃ tathā \|\| 11 \|\|*

*prāṇaḥ svadehajo vāyurāyāmastannirodhanam \|*  
*indriyāṇāṃ vicaratāṃ viṣayeṣu tvasatsviva \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12. An undiviating faith in the god Hari, with performances of rites enumerated in the (6rutis and Smrtis, is called divine contemplation. Svastikas cross Padmasanam, etc., are the different postures (Asanas) of Yoga; the Vayu which courses in the organism of a person is called Prana (life) and Pranayama consists in checking the out-flow of breath.

## \|\| 238.13-15 \|\|

*no sanskrit verse \|\| 13 \|\|*

*no sanskrit verse \|\| 14 \|\|*

*no sanskrit verse \|\| 15 \|\|*

13-15. О Pandava, Pratyahara consists in restraining the mind and the senses from wandering among the unreal objects of the external world. Meditation (Dhyanam) consists in meditating upon the self of Brahma, whether embodied or disembodied. The embodied Self of Brahma should be meditated upon at the outset of Yoga, while the disembodied Brahma should be contemplated in its later stage, with the acquisition of increased psychic power.

## \|\| 238.16 \|\|

*no sanskrit verse \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. The knowledge that I am the supreme Brahma represents the state of Samadhi, the speech, the knowledge, the perception that T am Brahma' lead to emancipation. Vyasa said: — The Rsis such as Йаипака, etc., having drunk these ambrosial words, pertaining to the glory of Vipu and encompassing the knowledge inculcated in all the 6astras, became extremely happy. This sacred, purifying, sin- absolving Garuda Puranam should be constantly recited, and by hearing it recited one is enabled to witness the fruition of all desires. The hearer of its narration shall make gifts of beddings, etc., as described before, otherwise he will not acquire the merit of hearing it duly narrated. The text of the Puranam should be first worshipped; after that, the reciter shall be propitiated with presents of land, gold, kine, food and Daksina. Mortals, who recite this sacred Puranam or hear it recited by others, ascend to the eternal region absolved of all sin, and freed from the pangs of existence.

## Chapter 239

## \|\| 239.1 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca \|*  
*sannapi brahma tasmātkhaṃ marutkhācca tato 'nalaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Brahma said: — I shall now tell you of Brahmaglta, knowledge of which will release you from the bond of activities. The knowledge derived from the aupanisadic text I am Brahma releases one from, the tangle (of the senses).

## \|\| 239.2 \|\|

*agnerāpastataḥ pṛthvī prapañcākṛtisūtikā \|*  
*tataḥ saptadaśaṃ liṅgaṃ pañcakarmendriyāṇi ca \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. The knowledge of aham and Brahma leads to the knowledge of the meaning of aham and Brahma and it leads to the knowledge of the sentence aham Brahmasmi. The sense of the two words: aham and Brahma is twofold: denotative and indicative.

## \|\| 239.3 \|\|

*vākpāṇipādaṃ pāyuścāpyupasthamatha dhīndriyam \|*  
*śrotraṃ tvakcakṣuṣī jihvā ghrāṇaṃ syātpañca vāyavaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. The denotative sence of the sentence aham Brahmasmi is not so clear as the indicative one. The relationship between the two is like that between the body and the soul.

## \|\| 239.4 \|\|

*prāṇopānaḥ samānaśca vyānastūdāna eva ca \|*  
*manontaḥ karaṇaṃ dhīśca syānmanaḥ saṃśayātmakam \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. The sruti declares that denotatively the world aham refers to the personal self while indicatively it refers to the nondual Brahman.

## \|\| 239.5 \|\|

*buddhirniścayarūpā tu etatsūkṣmasvarūpakam \|*  
*hiraṇyagarbhamātmīyasūtraṃ tatkāryāliṅgakam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Indeclinable, blissful and unmanifested consciousness is denotated by the word Brahma while the personal self manifested in the body is denotated by the word sham:

## \|\| 239.6 \|\|

*pañcīkṛtāni bhūtāni hyapañcīkṛtabhūtataḥ \|*  
*pañcīkṛtebhyo bhūtebhyo brahmāṇḍaṃ samajāyata \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Indicatively the word aham refers to Brahma, while the word Brahma referes to the soul in the body. (The two are indentical).

## \|\| 239.7-10 \|\|

*lokaprasiddhaṃ sthūlākhyaṃ śarīraṃ caraṇādimat \|*  
*pañcīkṛtāni bhūtāni tatkāryaṃ tatsthameva ca \|\| 7 \|\|*

*sarvaṃ śarīrajātaṃ ca prāṇināṃ sthūlamīritam \|*  
*tridhāhri paramātmasthaṃ śarīraṃ procyate budhaiḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*dehadvayābhigāmī ca tvamatho jīva ekataḥ \|*  
*svabhedavākyādbrahmaiva praviṣṭaṃ dehayordvayoḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*jalārkvavadvadaravajjīvaḥ prāṇādidhāraṇaḥ \|*  
*jāgratsvapnasuṣuptīnāṃ sākṣī jīvaḥ sa ca smṛtaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

7-10. The word aham refers to the perceptible entity (Tivatman) and the word Brahma refers to the imperceptible (Brahma). By adopting the, Indicatory process (laksana) the person arrives at the meaning of aham Brahma which leads him to realize the nondual supreme Self. The knowledge of the meaning of the Mahavakya aham Brahmasmi removes ignorance, enlightens the path and effects release.

## \|\| 239.11-14 \|\|

*jāgratsvapnasuṣuptyākhyairvyātiriktaśca nirguṇaḥ \|*  
*nirgātāvayavosaṃgo nityaśuddhasvabhāvakaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*paramātmaiva yajjāgratsvapnādyairyastridhā mataḥ \|*  
*antaḥ karaṇarāśeścaivāntaḥ karaṇaḥsthitaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*jāgratsvapnasuṣuptīśca paśyato vikṛtiḥ sadā \|*  
*phalakriyākārakayorjāgradādīnvadāmyaham \|\| 13 \|\|*

*indriyairatha vijñānaṃ jāgratsthānamudīritam \|*  
*jāgratsaṃskārasaṃbhūtapratyayo viṣayārthinaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

11-14. Lord Hari said: — From the eternal Brahma was originated the ether, from ether the fire, from fire the earth. The subtle body consisting of seventeen parts came into being; viz the five organs of action, viz, hands, feet, mouth, the generating organ, the organ of evacuation, fire organs of intellect, viz. ears, skin, eyes, tongue, organ of smell, and fire winds Prana, Apana, Smana, Vyana, and mind of which the nature is doubting and intellect of which the nature is ascertainment.

## \|\| 239.15-16 \|\|

*svapnaṃ suṣuptiḥ karaṇopasaṃghāte dhiyaḥ (pa) sthita (ti) \|*  
*brahmaṇaḥ kāraṇāvasthāyāṃ sthitiḥ kālakātmanā \|\| 15 \|\|*

*kramatokramato jīvo jāgradādi sa paśyati \|*  
*samādhyāraṃbhakāle tu pūrvamevāvadhārayet \|\| 16 \|\|*

15-16. This is the subtle creation. Hiranyagarbha is an individual soul which is ascertainable only by its actions. From the five subtle elements originated the five gross elements earth, water, fire, wind and ether, from the five gross elements originated the universe.

## \|\| 239.17 \|\|

*mumukṣāvatha saṃjāte antaḥ karaṇakevale \|*  
*vilāpayetkṣetrajātaṃ tatkṣetraṃ pariśeṣayet \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. The body consists of feet, hands, etc is known as the gross body. It originates from five elements and functions as the base of all activities.

## \|\| 239.18 \|\|

*pañcīkṛtebhyo bhūtebhyo bhāṇḍādi vyatiriktakam \|*  
*yathā mṛdo ghaṭo bhinno nāsti tatkāryatastathā \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. The body consisting of organs of action is called gross but has its basis in the Supreme Self.

## \|\| 239.19 \|\|

*pañcīkṛtāni bhūtāni apañcīkṛtabhūtataḥ \|*  
*śaṃsaṃti vyatirekeṇa śiṣṭāḥ sūkṣmaśarīrakam \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. The individual self pervades the subtle as well as the gross body; as the 3rutis declare, the very Brahma has entered the bodies.

## \|\| 239.20 \|\|

*apañcīkṛtabhūtebhyo na liṅgaṃ vyatiriktakam \|*  
*pṛthvyādhāraṃ vinā nāsti vinā nāsti ca tena sā \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Like the Sun in the water, the higher self reflected in the intellect is called JIva (the personal self) which sustains life and functions as the witness of three states, viz, the state of wakefulness, of dream and sound sleep.

## \|\| 239.21-22 \|\|

*tejaśca vāyunā nāsti vāyuḥ khena vinā na hi \|*  
*yadbrahmaṇā ca khaṃ nāsti śuddha brahma vinā ca kham \|\| 21 \|\|*

*śuddhabhāvastadā jāgratsvapnādīnāmasaṃbhavaḥ \|*  
*jīvatvavarjitaḥ prāptātmacaitanyānurūpataḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

21-22. The supreme self is not associated with attributes, is distinct from three states of conciousness, viz., the state of wakefulness, dream and sound sleep. It is not divided in parts, is non-dual, is of eternally pure nature. Seated inside the body and characterize by three states of consciousness, the individual self is no other than the higher self.

## \|\| 239.23 \|\|

*nityaṃ śuddhaṃ buddhamuktaṃ satyaṃ brahmādvitīyakam \|*  
*tattvaṃpadāntau śiṣṭau ca tatkāro brahmavācakaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. A person who is ever intent on three states, viz., the state of wakefulness, of dream and of sound sleep can never realize Brahma. I shall now tell you Something about those activities which are undertaken for the attainment of fruits and about the three states of consciousness jagrat etc.

## \|\| 239.24-25 \|\|

*ukāraśca akāraśca makāroyamṛgadvayaḥ \|*  
*brahmāhamasmyahaṃ brahmajñānamajñānavardhanam \|\| 24 \|\|*

*ayamātmā paraṃ jyotiścinnāmānandarūpakaḥ \|*  
*satyaṃ jñānamanataṃ hi tvamasīti śrutīritam \|\| 25 \|\|*

24-25. The knowledge of an object through the organ of senses is called jagrat. The seeker for the knowledge of an object goes in contact with that very object through the medium of senses. The same is repeated in dream (svapna). In sound sleep there is a total withdrawal of senses. The mind and intellect are concentrated in Brahman.

## \|\| 239.26-28 \|\|

*ahaṃ brahmāsmi nirlepamahaṃ brahmāsmi sarvagam \|*  
*yosāvādityapuruṣasosāvahamanādimat \|*  
*gītāsāror'junāyokto yena brahmaṇi vai layaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*no sanskrit verse \|\| 27 \|\|*

*no sanskrit verse \|\| 28 \|\|*

26-28. Serially or non-serially, the individual soul passes through the three states. In the preliminary state of meditation he is aware of the objective world. As soon as the desire for liberation is created in him he withdraws his senses from the outside world which being emanted from the creator himself appears to be distinct as the jar appears ditinct as the jar appears distinct from clay.

## \|\| 239.29-31 \|\|

*no sanskrit verse \|\| 29 \|\|*

*no sanskrit verse \|\| 30 \|\|*

*no sanskrit verse \|\| 31 \|\|*

29-31. The universe constituted of the five-fold elements is nothing but an aggreagate of five subtle elements which again are nothing but the indivisible Brahma itself. The earth as the substratum of all stationary and living beings has also a substratum in Brahma. There is no fire without wind, no wind without ether, no ether without Brahma and no Brahma without ether.

## \|\| 239.32-33 \|\|

*no sanskrit verse \|\| 32 \|\|*

*no sanskrit verse \|\| 33 \|\|*

32-33. In pure consciousness there is no awareness of the states jagrat svapna etc. and no sense of separateness. The personal soil loses its identity and merges into the eternally pure, intelligent, awakened and non-dual Brahma. Then 'thou' and that' are dropped and what remains is pure Brahma (indicated by asi).

## \|\| 239.34 \|\|

*no sanskrit verse \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Just as in Om, the syllables a, u, m, are merged, losing their identity, similarly all appendages that create a feeling of separateness are merged into the Brahman. The expressions Brahmahamasmi, aham Brahma serve merely to create confusion.

## \|\| 239.35 \|\|

*no sanskrit verse \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. The self is the supreme light, supreme consciousness, supreme joy, supreme truth, eternal knowledge, expressed by the word tvam. So declares the Sruti.

## \|\| 239.36 \|\|

*no sanskrit verse \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. I am Brahma, pure and simple. I am omniscient. That one. is seen in the orb of the sun, that one I amk, eternally. The lord conveyed this essence of Gita to Arjuna who realized the self.

## Chapter 240

## \|\| 240.1 \|\|

*hariruvāca \|*  
*purāṇaṃ gāruḍaṃ rudra proktaṃ sāraṃ mayātava \|*  
*brahmādīnāṃ śṛṇvatāṃ ca bhuktimuktipradāyakam \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Lord Hari said: — О Rudra, I have narrated to you the Garuda Purana, the essence of all knowledge. It brings joy to the listener and brings about his release.

## \|\| 240.2 \|\|

*vidyākīrtiprabhālakṣmījayārogyādikārakam \|*  
*yaḥ paṭhecchṛṇuyādrudra sarvavitsa divaṃ vrajet \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. It confers learning, fame, glory, wealth, victory and health. Rudra, he who reads or hears Brhama said: — О Vyasa, I have heard the Purana from the mouth of Visnu. It surely brings about liberation to the hearer.

## \|\| 240.3-4 \|\|

*brahmovāca \|*  
*iti vyāsa mayā viṣṇoḥ purāṇaṃ muktidaṃ śrutam \|*  
*vyāsa uvāca \|*  
*śrutvaitadgāruḍaṃ puṇyaṃ brahmāsmānityuvāca ha \|\| 3 \|\|*

*dakṣanārada mukhyādin brahma dhyānhariṃ gataḥ \|*  
*mayāpi tubhyaṃ sūtena purāṇaṃ kathitaṃ param \|\| 4 \|\|*

3-4. Vyasa said: — Thus Brahma who had heard the Purana from the mouth of Visnu related it to Daksa, the Purina becomes omniscient and goes to heaven. Narada and others including myself. I had gone to Visnu-loka with my mind set on Brahman. I heard this Purana and later on, imparted the same to Sara. Now you have heard the same from the mouth of Suta.

## \|\| 240.5 \|\|

*yacchrutvā sarvavitprāptakāmo brahma phalaṃ bhavet \|*  
*viṣṇuḥ sāratamaṃprāha garuḍaṃ gāruḍaṃ tataḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. On hearing the Purana the person attains omniscience satiates his desire, reaps the fruits in the form of realizing the self. This Purana, the essence of all knowledge, Visnu related to Garu4a

## \|\| 240.6 \|\|

*mahāsāraṃ dharmakāmadhanamokṣādidāyakam \|*  
*sūta uvāca \|*  
*śaunaka pravaraṃ proktaṃ purāṇaṃ gāruḍaṃ tava \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Suta said: — This Purana contains the essence of all knowledge and confers Dharma, Artha, Kama and Moksa.

## \|\| 240.7 \|\|

*yadabravītpurā vyāsaḥ sāraṃ māṃ gāruḍeritam \|*  
*vyāsaḥ śrutvā brahmaṇaśca purāṇaṃ gāruḍaṃ śubham \|*  
*devaṃ dhyāyanvedamekaṃ caturdhā vyabhajaddhariḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. In olden days, Vyasa narrated to me this Purana which he had heard from Brahma- Vyasa who had divided a single Veda into Vedas.

## \|\| 240.8 \|\|

*aṣṭādaśapurāṇāni tāni māṃ prāha vai śukaḥ \|*  
*idaṃ tu gāruḍaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ mayā te śaunakeritam \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. He divided the single Puna sarhhita into inghteen samhitas. Йика, the son of Vyasa, has narrated tome this fact. And I have related to you this Purana О Йаипака.

## \|\| 240.9-11 \|\|

*munīnāṃ śṛṇvatāṃ madhye pṛcchataḥ sarvavācakam \|*  
*yaḥ paṭhecchaṇuyādvāpi śrāvayedvā samāhitaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*saṃlikhellekhayedvāpi dhārayetpustake nanu \|*  
*dharmārtho prāpnuyāddharmarthārtho cārthamāpnuyāt \|\| 10 \|\|*

*kāmā navāpnuyātkāmī mokṣārtho mokṣamāpnuyāt \|*  
*yadyadicchati tatsarvaṃ gāruḍaśravaṇāllabhet \|\| 11 \|\|*

9-11. Since you have asked me to narrate the Purana to the sages. One who reads or hears or hires the services of a Pandit to recite it to others, or writes it himself or hires the services of a scribe to write it out or keeps the Purana at home, attains Dharma, Artha, Kama or Moksa, whatever may be the choice. He satiates his desire by listening to this Puma.

## \|\| 240.12 \|\|

*brāhmaṇo vedapārasya gantā syānnātra saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*kṣattriyo kṣattriyasyāpi rakṣitā bhavatīha ca \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. If he is a Brahmana he attains the knowledge of the Vedas; if a Ksatriya he is conferred the strength of protection.

## \|\| 240.13 \|\|

*nānyasya śravaṇaṃ hi syātpurāṇaṃ vedasaṃmitam \|*  
*vadedyadi sa mūḍhātmā kīrtihānimavāpnuyāt \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. None of the other classes (Vaisya or Shudra) is authorized to hear the Purana. If, by mistake, he narrates it to an unworthy person, he becomes the object of censure.

## \|\| 240.14 \|\|

*anyasmai ca vadedvidvān brāhmaṇontarito ya di \|*  
*brāhmaṇāntaritai sarvaiḥ śrotavyaṃ gāruḍaṃ tvidama \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. But, if he narrates the Purana from behind the screen, then both the deserving and the undeserving person become worthy to hear.

## \|\| 240.15 \|\|

*yathā viṣṇustathā tārkṣyastārkṣyastotrāddhariḥ stutaḥ \|*  
*gāruḍaṃ vasurājaśca śrutvā sarvamavāpa ha \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. As Visnu is a celebrated deity, Garuda is a venerable celebrity. In praising Garuda we praise Visnu. By singing praise for Garuda, formerly King Vasu stated his desires.

## \|\| 240.16 \|\|

*varuruvāca \|*  
*namasyāmi mahābāhuṃ khagedra harivāhanam \|*  
*viṣṇordhvasaṃsthānaṃ vitrāsitamahāsuram \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. King Vasu Said: — Homage to Garuda, of irresistible might, the Vehicle of Visnu, the emblem in the banner of Visnu and a terror to the Asuras.

## \|\| 240.17 \|\|

*namaste nāgadarpaghna vinatānandavardhana \|*  
*supakṣapāta niddabha dīnadaityanirīkṣita \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. Homage to you, the destroyer of the pride of the Nagas, the nourisher of joy to his mother Vinata, possessed of beautiful wings, guileless, fefuge of the piteous asures.

## \|\| 240.18 \|\|

*parasparasya śāpena supratīkavibhāvasū \|*  
*gajakacchapatāṃ prāptau bhrātaraucaiva saṃyutau \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. \[Now listen to a story\]. Once Supratlka and Vibhavasu, the two brothers, cursed each other and as a result of curese they were born as the elephant and tortoise.

## \|\| 240.19-20 \|\|

*yaducchritau yojanāni jastaddviguṇāyataḥ \|*  
*kūrmastriyojanotsodhā śatayojanavamaḍalaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

*na khādyau tau tvayānīcau caturbhujau ca pakṣipa? \|*  
*parasparakṛtācchāpadoṣācca parimocitau \|\| 20 \|\|*

19-20. They had immense bodity height as well as breadth. In their struggle for superiority over each other, you acted as a judge. You released them from the accursed curse which they had inflicted upon each other.

## \|\| 240.21 \|\|

*niṣādadeśasvādena devaṃ brūsmāniditam? \|*  
*viṣādīśastato muktastatrāpi brāhmaṇastvayā \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. You swallowed the Nisadas in large proportion. When by mistake you swallowed a pious Brahmana, you vomited him alive, immediately on knowing that he was a brahmana.

## \|\| 240.22 \|\|

*vaṭārohiṇavṛkṣasya yojanānāṃ śatāyutā \|*  
*śākhā bhinnā tvayā yatra vālakhilyāḥ samāsthitāḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. You broke the bough of a Banian tree spread over a hundred yojanas, regardless of the fact that it supported the Balakhilya.

## \|\| 240.23 \|\|

*tvayā yatnakṛtā kṛtvānakhasthau gajakacchapau \|*  
*nabhaspapinirālaṃbe sarvataḥ parivāritau \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. With mighty effort you seized the elephant and the tortoise, put them in the navel.of your thumb, while they were fighting in the supportless sky.

## \|\| 240.24 \|\|

*tvayā jitā raṇe devāḥ sarve śakrapurogamāḥ \|*  
*āhṛtaṃ tatpurā somaṃ vāhniṃ nirvāpya kāśyape \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. You conquered the gods, together with their leader Indra. О son of Kasyapa, you extinguished the sacrificial fire and carried away the Soma forcibly.

## \|\| 240.25 \|\|

*nāgau dṛṣṭiviṣau kṛtvā rajasā tu vicakṣuṣau \|*  
*tīkṣṇāgreṇa na sā bhaṅktvāvikravetau manohataḥ? \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. These were two poisonous serpents who could inject poision by their very sight. You made them sightless by your magical skill.

## \|\| 240.26 \|\|

*āhṛtyāpi tvayā somaṃ nītameva na bhaktitaḥ \|*  
*tena viṣṇordhvajasthānaṃ vāhanatvaṃ gato hyasi \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Out of devotion for Visnu you brought Soma from heaven. You did not partake of it yourself. You therefore got a place of honour in the banner of Visnu and became his vehicle.

## \|\| 240.27 \|\|

*tvayā niḥ kṣipya darbheṣu somaṃ nāgāśca vañcitāḥ \|*  
*jahāra cāmṛtaṃ pātraṃ śīghraṃ vai brahmasūdana \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. You concealed Soma in the Darbha grass and deceived the Nagas. You carried nector to the abode of Brahma and distributed the same among the gods.

## \|\| 240.28 \|\|

*yatra jihvādvidhābhūtāḥ pannagānāṃ dvijottama \|*  
*vinatā mocitā dāsyātkadvā pūrvajitā raṇe \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. О best of birds, by you the tongue of the Nagas was split into two. You released your mother from Kadru, the mother of the Nagas who had made her a slave.

## \|\| 240.29-31 \|\|

*uccaiḥ śravāḥ sa kiṃvarṇaḥ śukla ityeva bhāṣate \|*  
*kṛṣṇavarṇamahaṃ manye pūrvadṛṣṭamuvāca ha \|\| 29 \|\|*

*tvayā vajrapahāreṇa pakṣamuktaṃ purā svataḥ? \|*  
*dadhīcavajraśakrāṇāṃ māturarthāya nānyathā \|\| 30 \|\|*

*tasya pakṣasya devendro yadānītaṃ hi dṛṣṭavān \|*  
*tadā tava suparṇoti nāma sthānaṃ jagattraye \|\| 31 \|\|*

29-31. They say that the horse Uccaihsravas is white in comlexion but I believe he is dark (for his glory is diminished). In the interest of your mother you had cut off his wings with the stroke of Indra's thunderbolt. When god Indra say your mighty deed he bhestowed upon you the title of honour-Suparna.

## \|\| 240.32 \|\|

*dhyānamātrādvinaśyettu viṣaṃ sthāvarajaṅgamam \|*  
*paṭhedvā śṛṇuyādyaśca bhuktiṃ muktimavāpnuyāt \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. By merely meditating on you, one destroys the effect of posion of whatsoever gort. One who hears or reads the Purana gets sensuous pleasure and release.

## \|\| 240.33 \|\|

*sūta uvāca \|*  
*vasurājo gāruḍaṃ vai śrutvā sarvamavāptavān \|*  
*garuḍo bhagavānviṣṇudhyāṃyansarvavāptavān \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Suta said: — King Vasu heard the Garuda Puraria and stiated his desire. The venerable Garuda meditated on Vipu and obtained the objects of his desire.

## \|\| 240.34 \|\|

*taduktaṃ gāruḍaṃ puṇyaṃ purāṇaṃ yaḥ paṭhennaraḥ \|*  
*sarvakāmamavāpyātha prāpnoti paramāṃ gatim \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Suta said: — I have narrated to you the sacred treatise, viz, the Garuda Purana. He who reads this Purana achieves the objects of his desire, and ultimately reaches the supreme goal.

## \|\| 240.35 \|\|

*ślokapādaṃ paṭhitvā ca sarvapāpakṣayo bhavet \|*  
*yasyedaṃ vartate geha tasya sarvaṃ bhavediha \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Byreciting even a quarter of verse, one destroys sins. He who keeps the treatise at home obtains everything in this world.

## \|\| 240.36 \|\|

*gāruḍaṃ yasya haste tu tasya hastagato nayaḥ \|*  
*yaḥ paṭhecchṛṇuyādetadbhuktiṃ muktiṃ samāpnuyāt \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. He who possesses this Purana attains all that is just. He who reads and hears this Purana enjoys sensuous pleasure and gets also release from world.

## \|\| 240.37-38 \|\|

*dharmārthakāmamokṣāṃśca prāpnuyācchravaṇāditaḥ \|*  
*putrārtho labhate putrān kāmārtho kāmamāpnuyāt \|\| 37 \|\|*

*vidyārtho labhate vidyāṃ jayārtho labhate jayam \|*  
*brahmahatyādinā pāpī pāpaśuddhimavāpnuyāt \|\| 38 \|\|*

37-38. By listening to this Purana he attains Dharma, Artha, Kama and Moksa. Desiring a son, he obtains son. Desiring an object he obtains the object. Desiring knowledge he obtains knowldge. Desiring Victory he obtains Victory. If he has killed a brahmin he is absolved of that sin.

## \|\| 240.39 \|\|

*vandhyāpi labhate puttraṃ kanyā vindati satpatim \|*  
*kṣemārtho labhate kṣemaṃ bogārtho bogamāpnuyāt \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. A barren women obtains Son; a girl a good husband. Desiring welfare he obtains welfare. Seeking pleassure he obtains plasure.

## \|\| 240.40 \|\|

*maṅgalārtho maṅgalāni guṇārtho guṇamāpnuyāt \|*  
*kāvyārtho ca kavitvaṃ ca sārārtho sāramāpnuyāt \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Desiring auspiciousness, he obtains auspiciousness. Desiring merit, he receives merit. Desiring to be a poet, he becomes a poet. Desiring to learn the secret of knowledge he obtains the secret of knowledge.

## \|\| 240.41 \|\|

*jñānārtho labhate jñānaṃ sarvasaṃsāramardanam \|*  
*idaṃ svastyayanaṃ dhanyaṃ gāruḍaṃ garuḍeritam \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. Desirous of knowledge, he obtains knowledge that puts an end to his cycle of birth. This auspicious narrative of the Garuda Purana narrated by Garuda himself is associated with bliss.

## \|\| 240.42 \|\|

*nākāle maraṇaṃ tasya ślokamekaṃ tu yaḥ paṭhet \|*  
*ślokārdhapaṭhanādasya duṣṭaśatrukṣayo dhruvam \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. By reading even a single verse one escapes an untimely death. If he reads half a verse he achieves the end of his wicked foes.

## \|\| 240.43 \|\|

*sūtācchrutvā śaunakastunaumiṣe munibhiḥ kratau \|*  
*ahaṃ braheti saṃdhyāyanmuktobhūdgaruḍadhvajāt \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. At Naimisa, at the Sacrifice of sages, Shaunaka heard the Purana from Siita. He meditated upon Brahman identifying his self with the Supreme Self and got release.
